The product is larger than my planting pots, but I found it convenient that it can be trimmed to size.Normally when I pot plants that have large drainage holes at the bottom, I often found that the soil leaked out. With this product, I found that none of the soil leaked.The biggest downside to this product is the price. The retail price for this product is $50. Amazon sells the product for a discount at $32.35. Either way, either price is way too much to pay for this product when there are much cheaper alternatives. $50 . . . really?

This is a giant pot scrubber.  It is the exact same material that you buy at the grocer but oversize to fill flower pots.  Does it work?  Yes, water drains easily through it.  It fills the bottom of a pot and is lighter weight than using rocks, however, there are much more cost effective methods for pot fillers.  I cannot recommend this product at this cost.  2 stars only because it does what it claims.

reviewerName: Lonnie E. Holder "The Review's the Thing"
reviewText: Sometimes the problem with getting multiple items of the same type from Amazon Vine is that there is little additional to say about the same type of item.  So, if you think this review looks a lot like my review for the 9.5 inch pot disc, then you would be correct.These 11.5 inch discs seem to be an answer to a problem that most people may not have.  But, more on that in a moment.These discs are much like nylon scrubbing pads.  The discs feature and open mesh that allow water to pass, but seem to discourage soil from passing.  The mesh is quite light, which is an advantage over options that enterprising persons potting plants sometimes use, such as rocks, marbles, Styrofoam, and other similar items.Now that I have provided a bit of description for these discs, I have to throw a bit of rain on the parade, so to speak.  The biggest problem I have is that there are simpler, and possibly cheaper, options for these discs.  We have tried landscaping fabric and had reasonably good success.  You could also take a cheap green scrubbing pad and likely get a similar effect.  Even better would be to use a green, nylon, scrubbing pad that is about ready to hit the landfill.  There are almost assuredly other options.As I noted above, this size is 11.5 inches in diameter, but the discs are easy to cut with sharp scissors so choose the next size larger than your pot and cut-to-fit.If you do not have any green, nylon pads floating about, or landscaping fabric, or any of the other options that people often use to permit water to pass through the bottom hole, or holes, in a pot while retaining the soil, then these discs might well be a good option for you.Good luck!
summary: These discs work well, but are they the BEST option?

reviewText: I've had much better luck after using the Garden Genius products.  I killed many house plants by over-watering, even if I put rocks, etc., in the planter to give the plants drainage.  I've been more careful about watering, but I do notice more of my plants are thriving and not dying since I've been using Garden Genius products.  It's also easier to use than pebbles, rocks and marbles, which I used for drainage, before.I like the fact that it can be reused when I transplant plants to larger pots.  A worthwhile product.
summary: I haven't used this long term, but . . .

reviewText: As pot fillers go, this is arguably a little easier.  But please pardon my cynicism when I suggest that there are plenty of other alternatives.  Basically, this is a pricey alternative to any number of other ways to add a little space at the bottom of a flower pot.  Is it neater?  Yes.  Is it the best alternative?  Not in my opinion.  I can use a lot of other erstwhile non-recyclable material that I don't have to pay for, and get the same result.
summary: It makes the flower pot marginally lighter

reviewText: First, I have to say that I have been looking at these 3M pot fillers, in all their various sizes, for a few weeks, and clearly there was some pricing error, as it was previously listed at least 5 times this normal price.  For 6 bucks or so, it's a no brainer.  Unless you have a ton of plants, it really is not much of an investment.I am not so great with plants.  I have one that is impossible to kill, and have come close to doing so even still.  Problem is watering.  Remembering to water.  Not watering enough.  Or too much.  It's all about irrigation below, on the bottom of the pot.  I usually just put in an inch layer or so of pebbles and then the soil.  But this simple looking thing is in fact "genius".  You kinda feel like you just bought a round grill scrubber, or a fan filter of some type. But, it specifically for plants, made with materials that will not harm the soil or roots.  It's very firm and truly lifts up the soil on a solid cushion of air.This is customizable as well.  It was about an inch too wide, so I simply cut around the edge, and made a perfect fit for my big pot.  The plant I used I have had for many years, and wonder why it's still alive every time I see it.  But with this filler disc, it truly is living a better life.  It is much fuller, and healthier looking.  They really put some major effort into something that we might look at and chuckle over.  But I am buying more as after several weeks of use, I will not only use it for other plants, I might even try buying some more.
summary: For those who grow plants, and those who kill them.

reviewText: I like the product. It definitely helps when you feel the difference between a pot filled with dirt or just partially filled because you are using the disc. Is it worth it? Depending on how much dirt you have to buy and use and how often you move your pots and planters. I wonder it's long term use and reusability. It feels sturdy enough and it feels or gives the illusion like it would let some air into the dirt.It definitely helps the pot drain faster so if you are in hot weather where you need to retain humidity you might just want to use dirt or mulch.

I love the 3M Garden Genius PF11-1T Durable Pot Filler Disk. I found this Pot Filler Disk to be more effective than ricks and gravel. This not add a lot of weight to the pot, therefore much easier to move the pots around. They als provide better drainage and can be used over and over again. The come in a variety of sizes and can also be trimed to fit yor pot as you wish. These are simple, easy to use and lightweight.

I used this in the bottom of a planter that I filled with an indoor outdoor plant. Currently the plant is outside, but by December I'll be bringing it inside, so I'd prefer a lighter pot. I saved about 4 or 5 cupfuls of dirt by placing this about 1/4 of the way up from the bottom of the pot BUT I'm sure it's moved down some from the weight of the soil I placed on top. I did not cut it to fit the planter. I simply wedged it into the planter where there was still air underneath it. It does allow some space underneath the dirt for better drainage.I expected it to be at least twice as think as it is, to ensure more drainage, especially at over $32 for one disc. Had I not received it to review, I would not have purchased it. It's too expensive for my budget. It does what I expected it to do, but if the price point was about 1/2, and if it was thicker, I would pay for it out of my own pocket.
summary: Easy to set up, less backache later, but expensive

reviewText: I have been using this for awhile now, I can say it is great for plants. I use a regular pair of scissors and cut out the size that I need for my pots. This is very easy. I keep my flowers and plants indoors to weather the elements or until they become strong enough to go out of the pot into my garden. I also use this on  a few pots I have in the house, The plus is that you do not have to water a lot, I like to be able to go and not have neighbors come water my flowers. This does well for keeping the plants or flowers Hydrated, but I think for the price there are better alternatives. Great product easy to use.

reviewerName: Mrs. K "From the wilds of the Mojave"
reviewText: This keeps the dirt from coming out of the bottom of a pot pretty well. It also weighs less than a comparative volume of gravel, rocks or broken pottery.I can see a real use for pots kept on patios and decks where you might just let the water drain out through the bottom -- anywhere you'd be concerned about water making a stain.HOWEVER, the cost is a little insane for any other use.

This filler disc is made off a tough spongy material similar to that used in3M Scotch-Brite SC-DH Medium Grit, 4-1/2" x NH Aluminum Oxide Surface Conditioning Disc Maroon. Putting it at the bottom of a pot reduces the amount of soil needed and therefore the overall weight. This is a useful purpose, and this item does it well. I cannot really recommend it, however, because free alternatives exist. For example, the foam peanuts used in packaging serve the same purpose pretty well and recycling through reusing is a lot more sensible environmentally than buying new special-purpose products.

The first thing I notice is the Amazon price on this product. This item should retail at a fairly inexpensive price, so if it is not, do a web search and find it priced properly. Even at a fair price it would still be cheaper to use rocks or broken clay pots. This product does have its niche in the market. It is clean, light and easy to use. The product is similar in material to the scrubbing side you might find on a kitchen sponge.

This is either very cool drainage for potted plants, or the world's largest frying pan scrubber.It's a great idea.  Those green scrubbing things you use on your pots and pans and stovetop drain very well, when they're not attached to a sponge.  They take quite a long time to break down, so I'm going to guess that this disc will last a long time.  (I'll update my review if it breaks down quickly.)  But at its current price, I could go to the supermarket, buy two dozen store brand scrubbers, and have cash left over for potting soil.  (If you do that, watch out for thesoap loaded scrubbers.)  I was able to cut it to size, though it takes a bit of effort because it's so thick.It's true that this will be much lighter than filling a very large pot with rocks for drainage.  If that's a high priority and these are within your budget, go for it.

I've cut this Huge pot filler down to fit into the largest planter I own.  It works to prevent a lot of potting soil from departing through the drain hole.  Then again, so do the old faithful approaches -- a rock or a pot shard.PROS:1. 3M has found a new use for an old product.2.  You can use the leftovers (if you have to cut it down) to scrub old pots before sterilizing and reusing them.CONS:1. While this pot filler allows minimal soil seepage, it does allow some to escape, so I can't give it points on this function.2. 3M touts the reusability of this product.  While I cannot imagine it will decay, who is going to remove as much potting soil as I've put on top of it to fill my pot just to wash and reuse it?  Not likely to be me.3. It's lighter weight than the traditional rock.  I actually checked this out.  My old faithful river rock weighed 2.25 ounces, the pot filler 2 ounces.  Not enough difference to be noticeable, especially in a giant pot.4. This pot filler fails a cost/benefit analysis (at least for me).  It is infinitely more expensive than a rock or pot shard without an infinitely better function.Overall:Am I about to rush out to buy more pot fillers?  Maybe not.  I'll leave this one in the bottom of my pot, but I'll settle for the rock next time.
summary: Pot Filler?  or Giant Pot Scrubber

reviewText: This summer the first season I use pot filler. Normally I put rocks and broken terra cotta pots at the bottom, which have to be cleaned up in Fall or Spring. Pot filler should eliminate the rocks. I transplanted two asters into the pot with pot filler (see submitted photo).I am not sure if pot filler can retain water. If it has this feature, it will be nice so I don't have to water the pot every day in hot summer.

This *seems* like a good idea... I had thought my pots would use less soil and be lighter. These technically make the pots a little lighter, but not enough to justify the cost. Basically, the larger the pot, the more the soil smashes these pot fillers flat, making the soil savings negligable. I am going to continue using rocks to drain my pots.

I love the concept of the Garden Genius pot filler.  Particularly with pots that don't have drainage holes, you need somwhere for the excess water to go.  And more importantly for large pots, I want to reduce the weight by putting something on the bottom that is lighter than the soil.If you are strictly looking for something lighter than gravel to provide drainage in your 16" pot, this should be OK.  It is really light -- as you can tell from the picture, it's like a thicker plastic version of the coco fiber liners sold by garden stores.  But it seems way too thin (about 1" thick) for a 16" pot and I worry that the weight of the soil in that large a pot will compress the pad and you'll lose the benefit of the drainage space.  Not only that but 16" pots are usually quite large and you need much more lighter fill to keep them from being too heavy.The instructions at the back of the package suggest layering them to lighten larger pots but for the price of this particular Amazon catalog listing, I expected it to be much much thicker.As for the price.  Be a smart Amazon shopper.  As of the date I am writing this review, what appears to be the very same item is available for sale by Amazon for a fraction of the price this item is today.  It is a listing for the 9.5 inch one that also has a tab for the 11 inch one for a much cheaper price.  Just put Garden Genius in the Amazon search bar above to look for it.If you get this for your 16" pot (and I suggest you check all the Amazon catalog listings to make sure you get the best price), I suggest you also get one or more of the 9.5 inch size to layer in your pot because the thickness of this one alone will not be enough for a large pot.
summary: For this diameter, the product should be thicker

reviewText: The Garden Genius 11.5 inch  pot filler is an effective drainage replacement for common ineffective alternatives such as gravel or rocks and so better for drainage and soil retention. They are easy-to-use & durable design and can be rinsed and re-used if needed. The pot filler also allows you to use less soil which is great for indoor plants.Overall this is a great gardening tool for anyone who has a green thumb.

3M's Garden Genius Durable Pot Filler Disc is a great idea especially for year-round gardeners like me who live in the Midwest.  I have lots of very large pots that I plant starter seeds and small plants in during the early Spring indoors, then have to drag them out of the house in the summer and then back indoors again before first frost for my indoor herb garden.I was disappointed in the thickness of this product.  To really help with any real weight issue in the pots, I would have to stack at least four of these discs together to make any sort of difference on their own.  What I did do was fill a third of the pot with large pieces of styrofoam, place the disk on top of the styrofoam and THEN add my potting soil.The discs are made out of the same material as an abrasive scrubber pad that you use on pots and pans.Great idea but totally flawed design...
summary: A Garden Genius? Hardly...  Good Idea- However, Highly Flawed Design

reviewText: When used with a saucer the disc lightens the weight of the pot since you don't need rocks or other heavy material to hold things in place. Like the fact that it can be used from season to season.

I liked the idea of the Garden Genius and was excited to get it in the mail.  I do a lot of gardening and this sounded great.  It is very environmentally sound, durable and helps keeps more soil from 'leaching' out of the bottom of the pot.  However, it does look a bit like a low tech mat.  It was also thinner than I expected and very expensive.I do think it would be especially useful for indoor plants where you want to keep the soil from draining out as much. It is also very convenient (different sizes to fit different pots) and easier to work with if you are potting indoors.  However, for outdoor (where you can usually make more of a mess) I can get much cheaper material that might be a little dirtier and harder to work with but essentially does the same thing.  Right now for lightweight drainage I use the biodegradable peanuts I save from my packages on the bottom of my pots and maybe add some type of netting on top of it to keep the soil from filtering through and the peanuts in place. It it isn't at clean to work with but is still very effective and even lighter depending on how many peanuts you add and can save you on soil if you have a large pot.In summary, this is a good product but I would only purchase it on sale or for indoor use.Pros-Environmentally friendly-Lightweight-Reusable and seems durable-Liked the fibrous material is better at holding soil in and preventing it from leaking through the bottom of the pot- will save on soil retention- probably very good idea for indoor plants because will save on more 'messiness' in the future.-Makes potting indoors easier.Cons-Kind of flimsy- only ~ one inch thick, after looking at it I wondered if I could make something similar from material I already had in my tool shed.-Very pricey- would not buy at full price
summary: 3 1/2 stars, great idea and works but expensive at full price

reviewText: I was anxious to get this and try it out. As I have gotten older lifting heavy pots is more difficult. The weight due in part to the layer of stone in the bottom of a pot for drainage. These worked great!! However you will need to learn how much to water as they do not drain as fast as pots with stone in them. They are very durable and thick. Easy to handle. You can cut to size if  needed.  A little pricey but they will last a long time I would  highly recommend these .

The Garden Genius Pot Filler is wonderful. It is lightweight, looks kind of like a Brillo pad prior to use. It is made of a durable, spongy, and airy plastic that allows water and air to pass through so that your plants can drain and breathe. I have the 11 1/2 inch size for a big pot, and it worked great to add drainage without heavy rocks, which would have made it harder to move this big pot around. As long as you put in enough soil on top of the filler so that there is plenty of growth room for the roots, there should be no problems. Also, at the end of the season when you are changing out pots, this Pot Filler can be washed and reused.

I keep a container garden on my patio and this worked wonderful! It keeps me from having to use a lot of extra dirt and makes the pot a little lighter so I can move it easier. I have no complaints! And my flowers came up beautifully. I think it also helps keep it drained so I don't drown plants either.

reviewerName: Valerie J. Wood "Author and Sports Journalist"
reviewText: I've used a few of these items this year and have been pleased with the performance. As I said in other reviews, durable and does the job. Great at the sales price but I would not pay the full price--it just seems to be over-priced for what it is. Still, as far as the product itself, it's lightweight and easy to use. Not much else to say really.NOTE: Since this item came out the price has come down SUBSTANTIALLY, making it a more feasible alternative to heavy stones and messy ...

Made with nylon, about an inch thick, this looks and feels like a large scouring pad. It can be cut to fit, but I have no problem with folding excess size up the sides of a pot.Large pots are handsome and impressive; the trouble with them is that they require so much dirt and are extremely heavy as a result.I don't quite get how this gadget will help very much; sure it will take the place of the rocks that we use for drainage at the bottom of the pot, but you don't need a whole lot of them, and they probably weigh two or three pounds at most.I have used "packing peanuts" and larger chunks of styrofoam for this purpose in whiskey-barrel planters.Recently I have been putting less dirt in large pots leaving five or six inches between the level of the dirt and the top of the pot.Certainly the Pot Filler Disc will help with the weight problem; I just question how much.

This is a good item to put in the bottom of the pot to keep the soil in and still allow excess water to drain out of the pot.  I like that it can fill the entire pot if you buy the right size for your pot.  I don't like that these pre-measured/pre-cut discs make it so that if you want to use it on a smaller pot, you'd can cut away at the excess to make it fit - but then there is a lot of waste.  So either you have to buy several of all different sizes, or better yet, buy a roll so you can just custom cut the size you want/need.Like others have said - I wish it were thicker.  I think it would be more useful if it were thicker and it would be nice to have the option to use it as a filler as well.Other than that, it works as it should to keep soil in and allow water to drain out.  I like function of it better than using rocks. It is pricey enough though that I probably would just use rocks to save money.  To use this product is quite a luxury.

This lightweight product has the look and feel of a nylon scouring sponge, but an inch thick and almost as large as a phonograph record. Rather than filling the bottom of a pot with heavy rocks, this lightweight and permeable material fills the space at the bottom of the pot, provides adequate drainage, adds almost no weight, and can be reused (although I haven't had it long enough to try that.)Many reviewers commented that this is a good product, but not at this price. Since Amazon's guidelines prohibit mentioning prices in reviews, because prices can change literally at any time, I can't tell what price this will be sold at when you shop for it. However, I will say that this product compares favorably to solutions in the under five dollar range.One of the selling points is that this saves soil. This may not the type of product you would buy to save money on soil, but to provide the correct environment without weighing down the pot. Then again, the soil, water, and the pot itself will make up the bulk of the weight in any case. If the manufacturer is touting saving soil as a benefit, then you should consider the price of soil when determining a fair price point for this item.In some ways, this resembles growing medium, but this is not designed to give any nutrition to plants. It appears as if roots will get embedded in some situations, and I'm having a hard time picturing this product being reused in that case.Objectively, this is a good product, but price will determine whether it's a good value.  If this were in a nursery in the "impulse buy" area near the checkout, I could see spending a few dollars more by adding this to your card to do things right. Otherwise,it might not occur to you to buy this, but if the price is right, you might as well save yourself the trouble of lugging home some rocks and order a few of these.
summary: Good alternative to rocks and heavy fillers

reviewText: Amazon sent this to me to review for you. I am a serious gardener so here is my review. I like the idea of it, it is nice and thick and sturdy. It holds the soil from leaking out the bottom all over the floor. It is easy to use. You just get a pot the approximate size and put it in the bottom or you can cut it up and put it in a smaller pot. At the end of the season you can take it out and wash it, dry it, and store for next year which is a good thing.  It is light and I imagine repels bacteria and disease and bugs.So far so good that was the good part, now for the bad part.It is expensive, I would never buy this for that kind of money.  It is too thin, I can bunch up a few newspapers and have the same effect thus recycling. Who wants to fish it out at then end of the year and wash it. I am sure it will have roots tangled in it, too much work for me. If you don't mind the expense this is a nice item but I would buy two since it does not fill the pot , it is only 1  to 1-1/2 inches.

Well, I obviously didn't count, but there were a whole lotta ladybugs in this delivery, and I didn't see a single one that failed to survive the trip.  The aphids in my garden didn't stand a chance, and I'd definitely purchase again when/if I have a need.

My cucumbers were under attack of aphids. I ordered these and they arrived dead thanks to my mailman and wife leaving them in the mailbox. I contacted the seller and they happily replaced my order. I spread these girls out around dusk and misted the garden to give the bugs some hydration. Its been about a week now an there all over the garden still. Make sure you have plenty of plants for them to hang out on. A raised bed with a few small baby plants wont give them much of a habitat. I have a 30x30 garden with over 20 types of fruits and vegetables and these bugs are loving it.
Well, the price is OK, but while I expected some of the ladybugs to be DOA, it looked to me that out of 1500 about 300-400 came dead. I will look for local suppliers in the future.

Promptly delivered, and all the ladybugs were very active and hungry.  I opened the bag near the worst leaves of the affected plants and they instantly went to down chomping on aphids.Edit: Second batch from the same seller: they were just as livley, but *very* thirsty. The plants with water droplets on the leaves were extremely popular (10 ladybugs trying to get at one droplet!), and the dry plants were of no interest.  After they drank, they stayed.
They got here quick. They are all grown and ready to release immediately. Give them a drink of water before release and they will go to work right away.

I have purchased these ladybugs more than once and will keep coming back to them.  They have fast shipping, very few dead bugs arrive, if any, and great customer service. I used these bugs in my greenhouse to cure an aphid problem. I highly recommend them.

More fun than a barrel of monkeys! These arrived happy and healthy on the third business day after ordering. I was worried about the heat in the mailbox but if you follow the tracking info (yes there is tracking with the cheap shipping. Don't believe the notice to the contrary) you can get them right away. They were about as healthy and happy as a bunch of bugs can be! They were downright rambunctious. They have a distinct aroma that reminded me of my childhood and a jars of ladybugs we would collect. The packing was perfect with ample ventilation and some shavings inside to cushion them.  I suggest that you get a batch just for the fun of it.  I released them after sunset and squirted the bug food around. They are self dispensing. All it takes id a small slit in the mesh and they all crown through it. They start eating right away.  In the morning I was able to find seven of them. I am sure there are more somewhere though. Here in Palm Beach County in May it is 82 degrees Fahrenheit at sundown so they aren't slowed down by cool temps and they can still fly. We also have an army of small hungry lizards who welcome anything that moves. I am going to get more bugs! I may try the Coca Cola to glue the wings closed trick so they stay put and hope the lizards aren't the problem. I'll add to the review and let you know if there are any long term bugs.PSNo bugs left at all. It was still worth it for entertainment.
summary: More fun than a barrel of monkeys!

reviewText: I was needing something too help combat my dust mite infestation in my indoor garden.I'm a type of person who loves everything organic as possible.The little workers showed up all alive and eager ta get out once they warmed up.The natures nectar helps a great deal...,I myself put dried raisins in the garden will also go a long ways as well on feeding them.Sponge full of water helps keep them happy and around longer in the garden area.
summary: Live Ladybugs-Hirt's Gardens approximately 1550 plus natures nectar

reviewerName: E. S. Noyes "liza lives to read"
reviewText: WHEN MY CLIMBING ROSE WAS ATTACKED BY APHIDS, WE ORDERED LADY BUGS AND HAVE LET THEM LOOSE TWICE SINCE. THEY SAVED THE ROSE, NO DOUBT. ARRIVED QUICKLY AND ALIVE. A GOOD PRICE.

This was shipped by standard USPS postage, I think it took about 5 days to get here. About half of the bugs were dead. I followed the directions with the nectar, hoping to keep some of the bugs in my garden, but all but a few left in the next couple of days.  I guess I didn't have enough insects for them to eat.  But about a month later, my (down wind) neighbor was telling me about all the ladybugs in her garden.  I was at least happy someone got the benefit.
summary: About half of the bugs were dead

reviewText: First off, please read the instructions. The company selling these does an excellent job of providing healthy, live insects with fast shipping - after that, you need to read the instructions. Once you've read the instructions, you'll refrigerate your little winged buddies and spray them down with sugar water. Right? And you'll remember the time of day it suggests of course, no? If you deviate from the instructions, you'll release a small army of ladybugs that will vanish within minutes without a single aphid eaten.So we tried this twice. The first time was the "don't read the manual" version and they all left. The second time was more procedural but the truth is they don't stay present for long. I don't know if the aphids aren't sufficient as a snack, or if the sugar water wears off, or if they simply refuse to stay on a handful of plants, but the overall effect isn't very impressive.I was really hoping this would work but compared to a dose of Sevin, it's no comparison. The insect battle wages on.
summary: All alive but they don't stick around

reviewText: These came really fast and were packaged as "live ladybugs". Inside they were in a mesh bag with a sponge like thing which I understand is food. From what I could tell most of them were alive and very lively. Very happy with the purchase and speed of shipping.
summary: Got here fast and most all were alive and active.

reviewText: I have released them in the night  but they only stay for one and half day they all checked out or became birds food.

I bought these ladybugs after trying everything to get rid of aphids in my greenhouse.  I wasn't sure how having live bugs shipped to me would work out but it worked out fine.  I kept track of when the package shipped to my PO Box so I  would pick them up the same day they arrived.  They arrived in a good quality box that had some kind of cold pack or something in it to help keep the ladybugs alive and happy until they arrived.  A word of warning, don't open this in your kitchen when you receive it, the ladybugs immediately start coming out the instant you start opening the outer box, and they do arrive hungry.  They helped me with my aphid problem and I will be ordering more in the spring.

Per the instructions I put the newly-delivered box in the refrigerator for a few hours to make the ladybugs groggy.  When it was time to release them I misted all my plants so that water would be available to the parched ladybugs.  Lastly, I released them just after sundown so it would be too dark for them to fly.  I removed the bag from the refrigerator, took it out to my garden and cut a corner of the bag open just as they were all starting to warm back up and get active.  Immediately they stampeded up the stems of my milkweed.  When they reached the top they started gorging themselves on the aphids.  Can't ask for better than that.
summary: Stampeded up the stems and started munching on the aphids

reviewText: This was my original review:All of my ladybugs were alive when I received them!  They were beautiful.  I bought them because I am having a problem with white flies in my lawn, and other aphids on some of my plants.They arrived quickly.  They were packaged well with a refrigerate pack to make sure that did not get too hot.  They came with a sheet of wonderful instructions.  They also came with a small pack of nectar to sprinkle out with them to help keep them nearby.  But, I also ordered the larger bag of it when I order these.I was very happy with this transaction.THIS IS MY ADDITIONAL REVIEW:These lady bugs are Asian lady bugs.  They are not native.  They do bite when their food source gets low; as in late in the year.  They become aggressive.  I had several bites.  I could not believe it!  Then, I did some research on line and found out.  Asian ladybugs also eat the larvae of native ladybugs. You are much much better off getting lacewings.  I bought those too, and they worked great!  And they will not bite you or kill beneficial insects.
summary: These are not native lady bugs and they bite.

reviewText: These are the same things the pros use, and for the price and the amount you get I thought "Why not?!".I've since caught a range of intersects and rodents. Huge spiders, crawler things, mice, and flying things.These work pretty well if you know how to lure them all to the trap.Happy hunting!

We just moved into a house that previously had a mouse issue so I bought these for maintenance after having the house professionally treated.  So far I haven't caught any mice but I haven't seen any signs of them either.  What I have caught is tons of bugs.  I used them to clear up an ant issue around our fireplace and have caught a lot of flies and grasshoppers in the basement and garage.  These are definitely nice to have around even if it is just for bugs.
summary: No mice yet but works great for ants and other bugs

reviewText: These work as advertised. Very sticky. Put them in my garage to catch mice and they do that, but they also catch anything that touches them. So far I caught mice, birds, lizards and a couple of squirrels. The squirrels run off with it but who cares.

I used these inside a building that became a mouse motel, and had just about instant success.Place against the wall in hidden areas and mice will be captured alive. You can then dispatch them by drowning or blunt force trauma. Once a mouse is caught, place follow up traps in a different place, but still along a wall, or other areas that show mouse activity. They work best when placed flat-not folded up into the trap/like box which is outlined on the back of the board.Works equally well for creepy crawlies. Be prepared to replace the traps based on the amount of dust and captured critters however. Glue traps have a finite life, as the more that sticks to it, the less effective it is.Rats will just laugh at these however. If you could make a 'quilt' of 6 sticky boards you'd have a chance to detain a rat long enough to dispose of it-maybe. Rats will do anything to escape, unlike mice that will just give up.Good hunting.

We live on a small ranch and mice can really be a problem. This is the best non poison solution I have found. They hold great. I have never had a critter come off one. We just lay them flat in a line like a sticky moat.These have really helped us. They are an awesome deal.
These pest pro glue boards work. They caught the vermin and now I am free of them. These are much cheaper than the name glue boards.

I use it around the house, hidden behind furniture and things, to catch bugs. It is amazing how many bugs it can trap.This one is better than Gluee Louee brand which has pictures of bugs printed inside, so that makes it look like bugs are caught when it is empty. This Pest Pro boards have no printing inside.

It's rare I give a 1-star review but in this case I have 4 pounds of useless rat poison.  I'm sure if that rats eat this stuff they will die but here in California at least the rats are too smart for this stuff.  I put it in one of their travel paths and they POOPED on this indicating they just walked right over it.  ZERO bite marks on the bait.  Since I have 4 pounds of it I'm thinking of adding peanut butter to it but I really shouldn't have to do that.  I bought some pellet packs at home depot (about $1 each, really cheap) and the rats LOVE those.I also find it interesting that many of the 5-star reviews for this product are either from reviewers who have ONLY reviewed this product or else gave a bunch of other 5 star reviews the same day as they reviewed this product then haven't reviewed anything else since.  Hmmm..Sorry, can't recommend.

Glad it has a holedown the middle as with others use a nail to hold it down and yes th rats nibble on it,  Had a problem wth them starting and now the problem is just about gone,  Havig dogs it is nice to be able to nail them down s rats cannot move them and dogs cannot get at them,  Thank you
Not sure if these are working as this stuff is going fast and the more we put out the more it's all gone.
Kills em dead every time! I mean every time! I had one who kept mouthing off after he ate it. I laughed as he dropped dead... Mid sentence!

Rodents love these bait chunks but beware that bromethalin is a potent neurotoxin with no known antidote.  It does not act immediately.  Rodents ingesting it will move abnormally, making them much more susceptible to capture by owls and other predatory wildlife, who will in turn die when they ingest the unmetabolized toxin.  Since each of those animals kill more rodents than your bait ever will,use this product with extreme caution and only in tamperproof bait stations where  beneficial wildlife is  unlikely to encounter the victims

I think the last time I reviewed something like this, I also used the tired old joke I told my grandson about how baking soda keeps elephants out of the refrigerator.  His response was, "there aren't any elephants in your refrigerator!"  My response was "then it must be working".  So far I haven't seen any critters in my basement, so I guess it is working.  It is disappearing so something is attracted to it.  Whatever it is, along as it stays out of my basement I am satisfied.

These ratchets hold my 40 pound grow light just fine. The only problem I have with these is I'm unable to change the height unless someone else is there to lift the light too. I cannot change the height by simply pulling, pretty frustrating. These will do however until you can get chains for your light.
summary: Unable to adjust height without help

reviewText: I own two sets of these hangers ,and i gotta say they are really nice and easy to use.Can be manipulated into many positions and set ups.The Ratchet system is a tad louder than I expected since its a smaller ratchet, But other than that, these work AWESOME!! And for the sweet price I paid as well.I will prolly own another set or two before long.

I just upgraded from an iPower 600wSuper HPS cooltube to iPower 500w LED Grow/Bloom panel.Well worth upgrading.I needed another pair of these too hang up my 2 iPower 135w LED Ufos in the 36"x20"x5' veg tent with a clip on fan from amazon too help with temp control.
summary: iPower GLROPE Grow light Heavy Duty Adjustable Grow light Ratchet Rope review

reviewText: These are strong and well made. The metal ratching gear make these work smoothly. The cords are long enough to use for several different purposes. I have found a number of different configurations.
this holds lights quite well, it can slip if it gets too much weight, tie a slip knot to secure

I have about at least 6 sets of these now. They are really useful. I've got a few LED and a Fluorescent light on these and they work great for lowing and raising your lights. They are easy to use a pretty strong.

Seem's to be the exact same item as the hydrofarm rope ratchet.  Works as advertised.  These items are a must have in any type of grow.  I was using para cord before and the ratchets make moving the lights so much simpler.
These are excellent for adjusting the lights at the correct height above plants.  Very sturdy and hold the lights securely.

This Fiskars "Deluxe Telescoping Weed Remover" works well to easily remove the Dandelion and Thistle weeds we have plaguing our front yard. This is a very handy tool that adjusts to accommodate my 6'2" son or my 5'4" wife and allows these stubborn weeds to be removed without chemicals or spending hours on the knees.It does work best if the ground is moist and giving it a "wiggle" to either side before removing the weed from the ground makes for a much "cleaner" extraction. Since this is mostly plastic, I do have some concerns with the long term durability of the tool but being aware of it makes it less likely we will overstress the tool.Overall, this is a well designed and very functional tool that has made weeding much easier and fun enough that my teen son will happily use it.Recommended!CFH
summary: Works Well For Our Needs - Recommended

reviewText: I think this tool is mostly for large, well established weeds.  It is a little difficult for an old lady with arthritis to use.  It also leaves a large hole where you removed the weed.

Was apprehensive though the video and description read volumes.  The first time tried, was impressed by its design and features; follow instructions at first, then adjusted to present conditions as needed.  Weeds are gone and in record time; good device!!

I've had this tool for quite some time. You push it around the crown of a weed (centering it as close as you can), then put your foot on the step and pull. The blades will close around the crown of the weed with a good grip and pull the weed out by the roots.Some good points:Keeps your hands away from prickly plants. We have one kind of short, thistle-like weed that is hard to grip with gloves. This keeps my hands away from it and gets it right out of the ground.You don't have to bend over.You can get out tougher weeds, such as dandelions, which have a long, deep taproot.Some not-so-good points:Eventually, when the taproot grows very deep, you will only get the top half, and the weed does eventually spring back.Once your ground gets very hard, this will only pull off the top half of the weed. We live in a relatively arid region (between two bays, so we get wind but the rain drops elsewhere.) If it's a dry spring or if it's summer and we've had no rain for weeks, this is difficult to use. The ground is too hard and the weed is too well imbedded into the soil.Still, it's short work to trundle around the yard with this in early Spring and pull out newly-sprouted dandelions while the ground is still soft. It's a pleasure to use. I can't think of another yard tool quite like it.
summary: Quick work on dandelions and other stubborn weeds

reviewText: This weed puller is amazing. This Telescoping Weed Remover has saved my husband and I tons of time and back aches. It not only removes the weed from the surface, but pulls the roots as well. The handle is a comfortable size and using the tool is simple. It is super durable and works every time! I highly recommend this to anyone who wants a quality tool that will help save time.
For those pesky weeds that are too hard to pull, like dandelions that wont come out of the ground I highly recommend this product.

Works really good, I was surprised to be honest. On some weeds it does have a little trouble getting the entire thing out, but if it can do 80% of the weeds faster then its well worth the price of purchase. Also based on a few other reviews, if it breaks I have read that Fiskars is really good about standing behind their products.
summary: Makes A Painful Thing Much Easier

reviewText: Yes I have used this product for over 10 years.  Yes it takes the "krud" off of the outside walls, window sills, eaves etc of your house. But the ingredient Sporex(R), which they claim is a unique additive which removes the toughest stains from mold, mildew, algae, dirt, grease, oil, sap, oxidation and more, may help remove the "stain" but not the mold, mildew and algae.  You still need to use bleach.  In fact I use the bleach first to kill the mold, mildew and algae in my ACE plastic sprayer which is designed for bleach mix.  After you let that sit for 15 minutes or so you get your pressure washer powered up with Krud Kutter siphoned into the pressure washer stream.  You begin by a low pressure settling to apply the Krud Kutter and let it sit for again about 15 minutes.  Then you go crazy with higher pressure settings (absent the siphon of Krud Kutter).  Doing this method you will have a very clean exterior surface.

I used this to clean my house, which is vinyl sided with wood window frames. It's been about three years since I last washed the siding so it was pretty dirty and had a nice collection of pollen in the nooks and crannies. I have a pressure washer but I used the optional application given on the label and mixed 12 oz of HS01 with one gallon of water in a garden pump can. I wet the siding with a garden hose and then sprayed the Krud Kutter solution, working from the top down, making sure to give it a n even soaking. I waited about 10 minutes then sprayed it off with the garden hose. Some of the shaded areas had mildew growing and I had to lightly scrub these areas with a soft bristled brush on an extension pole. But the over all process with just using the solution did loosen the dirt and pollen and the hose spray washed it all off. I would consider this average results when using this method without using a power washer. After touching up some areas and brushing some of the white trim, I let it all dry. The house looks like it has a fresh coat of paint. It took two and one half gallons of mixture to complete my siding on a 1 1/2 story home that is mostly vinyl finish.Other observations: my front porch is painted concrete and my outside doors are steel. The Krud Kutter cleaned all of this with just a spray down and then hosing it off. The white trim is very bright after cleaning it, however, the white gutters had stains from rain drips and the downspouts have black stain (not mold). This product did not remove the black stains. I didn't try it on my wood deck, as there are products that are made to do that job specifically. I don't like to use my power washer on my vinyl, just a personal preference. I washed a patch of the concrete driveway, in order to use up what was left in the last pump can. the solution lightened the concrete by removing ground-in dirt, but only slightly. Concrete usually requires a power washer for clean anyway. The Krud Kutter cleans the grime from windows, but it does leave some streaking. There was no irritation of my skin, eyes, or sinus'. The smell is ok and dissipates quickly.I've used several similar products to clean the siding over the years, this one cleans a little better than the ones that I have used. I'd definitely use this product again for the same job.

I had high hopes for this product and tried it on vinyl and wood siding and a wood deck. My first disappointment was in the amount of effort it takes just to prepare your chosen surface prior to using the product. I had minimal foliage to be concerned with but if I had, the directions gave even more prep instructions for plants and flowers. In any case, For the vinyl and wood siding surfaces, I followed the instructions and used the Krud Kutter on half of each structure and plain water on the other half. While I did see a slight difference where the Krud Kutter was applied, it wasn't enough to make me want to use it again when the time came to clean my deck. By then, it just wasn't worth the effort for such minimal results. Granted, the sidings and deck probably haven't been properly cleaned in years so perhaps I was just expecting too much. But given the amount of prep work involved - like pre-wetting each surface - this would have to produce some amazing results for me to want to put that much extra effort into pressure cleaning with anything more than just plain water. Too bad since my cleaning skills really could use some help.....
summary: A lot of effort for ok results

reviewText: This will help you to clean using a power washer but I think a more simple (and cheaper) solution of water and bleach actually works better.  If you have an area where you would not be able to use a bleach solution then this is a product you would like.  Otherwise, I recommend making your own solution of bleach with water--50-50 solution.  Now, the one factor that may prove that this is better than bleach is if it is able to inhibit mildew.  I will return to update on this point.

Used a similar product for 15 years. So Krud Cutter was new to me. Pleased results and labeling for instructions.  I live in the upper south and we get lots of mold and mildew built up on sidewalks, driveways, siding and shingles.  I have a spray on applicator on my garden hose I used this product as a presoak and leave it on according to what I am applying it to . Then use my power washer or  just the water hose to finish cleaning depending on how much pressure it needed.  Also used it to presoak and power wash grease stains on driveway, works good.  The spary applicator I use comes from my local hardware store and is meant to be used  with the dial settings for fertilizer application for lawns.  I have not used this enough yet to have a complete comparison with my old product so I am giving it 3 stars until I have used it on all applications.

Not terribly offensive, and doesn't appear to harm anything I sprayed it on.  It's only been a few days though, so I can't really comment on that, nor on the efficacy of their proprietary SPOREX formulation.What I can say is that the pressure washer (thus, just plain water) does the lion's share of the work.  I call into question their claim that pre-soaking or pre-spraying isn't necessary.  Maybe not on materials you can just hammer-down on them with the pressure washer, but for wood, etc. the product didn't seem to do much more than plain high-pressure water.  Pre-soaking might have helped, but that doesn't abide the directions on the bottle.  Other reviewers have noted similar experiences.At least it doesn't smell like Montana Solvent, and is certified to be greener than the stuff I've used in the past.  Some of the cleaners of olden days would about eat through your sneakers.  They would definitely kill vegetation whether you rinsed them down or not.  All in all, if I were doing another deck, coated in mildew and leaf stains, I think I would just cover my plants, dillute a little Clorox and cry 'Havoc'.This stuff seemed to be mostly about peace of mind, with not much cleaning.  My guess is there was moderate, incremental improvement in cleaning, but it wasn't astonishing.  I wish it were otherwise, but I can't endorse this product further than to say it might mildly improve your cleaning job, with the pressure washer still doing all the heavy lifting.

Like to use my pressure washer in the garden and when I tested this concentrated , thinking that just water does a nice job but, thought a soap concentrate would cut the job in half.Honestly, I did not see any striking improvement.  I was disappointed to say the least.  Thinking I did not use enough of the liquid, I tried again.  Still did not notice any sparkling difference.  So, have to say that I would not  recommend this product.
summary: Nothing Special about Krud Kutter Green Pressure Washer Concentrate.

reviewText: Don't expect this to remove the Green Stuff from your siding just with water and spray. You still need to get on a ladder and scrub. I don't see any special results with this cleaner. In fact, I have better results with Simple Green. I can't recommend this.

I didn't use this with the pressure washer, but got good results with the hose. Only noticed one issue.  I mixed the solution in a spray bottle half and half with water.  When I did that I noticed that while there was no odor, the back of my nose felt dry and uncomfortable as though I'd breathed in paint fumes.  It didn't last too long and I wasn't even sure it came from this product until I used it again.I have used other Krud Kutter products and like them because I can clean the red dirt stains off the house and even off my tennis shoes.  I was eager to try this because it supposedly keeps mold from returning to the siding.  One part of my house is shaded and every year is greenish.  While I can go a few years between washings on the rest of the house, that part needs attention every year.While I expect to try the product out in other ways, this time I just hand-sprayed the siding with the diluted product, no prewetting or other prep.  I then went to uncoil the hose and turn it on and got sidetracked with another small chore so I returned to the sprayed siding about 5 minutes later.  I just sprayed it with the hose using the 'jet' setting on the nozzle and all the green mold  and dirt  washed right off leaving a clean white surface.  The area that had not been sprayed was unchanged  after hosing however.After the siding dried, I sprayed the rest and rinsed and the whole side of the house is now clean.  Time will tell if the mold will return as usual, but I'd sure be happy if it stayed away on the treated part for a couple of years.  The plants below the sprayed area don't look any the worse for wear at the moment and I didn't even rinse them off since they are not anything I care about plus I'm curious to see the effects after a couple of days, before using the product on other areas where landscaping below does matter.My only objection so far is that I have the nose/throat issue again following use.  I will definitely wear a mask when  using the product again.  It is worth it to note that my dilution was only half and half so I was using the product in a stronger solution than others may have, or than it might come out of a pressure washer.  In my trial the product delivered perfect results and if the mold stays away, I'll buy it again when needed.

What a let down.  We recently bought a house that's vinyl siding had not been cleaned in ages.  I was excited to try this product, but after carefully following the directions, I could see no difference between using it or powerwashing with plain water.  Save your money.  The only plus was that it is supposedly safe for plants, but what does that matter if it doesn't clean well?

We live in an area where we have a lot of green junk on our siding and gutters. We usually use bleach but it smells and it hurts our shrubs and grass. This stuff is formulated with out bleach and has a substance that prevents mold. It needs to sit on the surface awhile before using a pressure washer to wash it off. It is low priced and when mixed in a pump sprayer it will cover quite a bit of surface. You can see it working if you spray it first and let it sit for a time. It is still caustic to plants so be sure to read and follow directions.

reviewerName: david l. poremba "the past in review"
reviewText: upon reading the instructions, we determined that it would be too dangerous to try and use this product on the house as we have many decorative plants and flowers; also the presence of two dogs makes us too nervous about using it.

reviewerName: Dr A "A reader of biographies, history, and o...
reviewText: We used this cleaning fluid according to its instructions.  It sort of works, but not that great.  To finish the job we had to turn on our powerwasher.
It doesn't clean any better than anything else I've tried. You still need to use a brush or something, even with a powerwasher. But still, better than just water.

I really liked that this was safe for pets and plants. And biodegradable. However, that might be why this cleaner falls short of doing what I need it to do.I used this in our pressure washer and it performed no better than just using water.So, I've decided to use it, at fuller strength, and for that purpose, it does get things clean. I've been using it to clean our sidewalks, deck and things like old hardware and it works fine for that.
summary: It's ok. Not really strong enough

reviewText: I pressure wash my brick deck about once every five years (whether it needs it or not - ha-ha). So when it's time, it's a lot of work. As luck would have it, this Krud Kutter arrived just in time to use on the deck along with my newKarcher North America 1.601-916.0 Electric Pressure Washer with Quick Connects, 2000 PSI. To be honest, I could easily do the pressure washing without the KK, but when I laid down a layer of the chemical and then switched over to the pressure washer, I got a fine spray of soapy, high pressure water that seemed to work better than water alone. Even just putting down the chemical I could see brown and black muck in the foam before I sprayed it off. I also used it on the sides of the deck where the moss built up and left it to foam a while, and that seemed to loosen the moss better than just water. Could I have done the whole job without the additional soap? Yes, certainly. Did it go faster with the soap? Not really. Did it get cleaner with the soap? Yes, I think so. I would say keep your expectations low and give it a try. You might like it, as I did (for the most part).

Krud kutter green pressure washer concentrate house and siding cleaner works well. I have vinyl siding and it got it pretty clean. There were a few spots with algae that I had to use a brush on but overall it works pretty well. My yellow siding looks a lot cleaner, and I am very pleased with the results!!!

I used this with a sprayer attached to a garden hose.  I didn't measure it, just filled the bottle and went to it.  I used it to clean the white metal railings on my front steps.  I still needed a scrub brush, but the dirt and crud cleaned up much easier.

One of my all-time favorite\s cleaners comes in this gallon container.  My first exposure to Krud Kutter (KK) was at the grand opening of one of those huge box stores and a lady encouraged me to buy a gallon and get one free.  After enjoying the results of my first buy, we moved and lost our store to distance and have NOT seen KK in the stores lately.I had to check this out to see if it is any better, worse and so forth.  It is better than the last century cleaner.  I do not recall what the concentration ratio is; however, at 10 to 1,that is a decent way to get 11 gallons of the good stuff that honestly cleaned my surfaces with ease.  The timing could not have been better, either.  A brand new pressure washer begged to get used, so I accommodated it with vigor.  (I have been slovenly in writing this review because we live on a well and septic tank under the ground and, with great thanks, at different ends of the yard.  Water, therefore, is a cherished commodity and we treat its presence with reverence.  It takes our rain water about 6 months to reach the underground water supply and we have had several instances of the well going dry this spring. )I first used a concoction of KK and water in a bucket.  My brush grabbed the cleanser with ease and it took little time to empty the gallon of mixture.  The best part beyond actually cleaning the walls with ease is that there was no real scrubbing on my part.  My routine was so simple it was almost fun.  Watching the winter grime bubble-up and fall to the ground was fun.  After several 'professionals' cleaning the house, I can now and will resist their visits in the coming months.  Who needs them when there is a fantastic product to clean the house.I am so glad KK included a reminder to protect hands and eyes.  The original cleaner had a strong odor, which is missing in the new.  The new does not irritate as much.  Nor does it smell as bad either.  Can you tell that I like this stuff?  I do and highly recommend it.

I used this to scrub and clean my deck in preparation for fresh finish.  I did not have mildew, just dirt, crud & old stain.  I did not use a pressure washer.  I watered/rinsed my deck & then put this Krud Kutter in a bucket so it would be easy to use.  I have a big scrub brush with a broom handle that I dip in to the bucket & then scrub over the deck.  It did a good job but TSP works better.  But this is better for all my plants that surround the deck and easier on the environment.  It prepped my deck for fresh stain.
summary: It Worked OK & No Damage To Nearby Plants/Environment

reviewText: I have a light colored house with vinyl siding, none too new. I scrub it every year or two. I don't own a power washer, so I mixed this up in a bucket and used a long handled brush. There is dust and dirt that will come off with water, even some stuff that will come off with a scrub. Then there is the moldy, black stuff that discolors one side of the house especially badly. That is where Krud Kutter HS01 Pressure Washer Concentrate House and Siding Cleaner works best. I brushed it on and a few minutes later washed it off with a hose. I had the brush in hand to give the areas I missed another go. Just a little more brushing and all the black spots and green mossy marks are gone. I also tried it on faux wood deck steps. I could see the difference and some of the dark spots came up but not all of them.

i used Krud Kutter before but this is the first time I tried the House and Siding cleaner. Spray it on and let it sit for 5-10 minutes to soak and work on the dirt, then rinse off with high pressure.  It worked well with my Troy Bilt gas pressure washer.  I also used it on washing a steel garden cart prepping it before painting.
summary: Works great to cut the grease and dirt

reviewText: I tried this on a variety of surfaces. It gets sticky moss off Sun aging vinyl siding and trim. It cleans my concrete carport floor (not as well, but it does make a noticeable difference). It cleans glass jalousie windows.  The acid test was our bird bath--old, cement, the bottom stained with iron water and red, dead leaf pigments. It didn't restore the concrete bowl to pristine gray, but it cleaned it. Which was more than I can say for Zap! which claims to restore surfaces to their original state. Not even close. It did not damage any surface I tried it on. Used with a pressure washer, it might be even more impressive.
summary: Does what it says itwill do

reviewText: We power wash our house once or twice a year, and usually use bleach to remove mold from the siding on one end of the house.  I mixed this Krud Kutter and sprayed it as directed, but it didn't remove any of the mold, or even do a good job washing off bird poop or bug stains.  It actually didn't work any better than using plain water.  We ended up having to use bleach water and a scrub brush, as usual.I'm all for "going green" with products that work.  I use vinegar in my mop water and it does a great job on my kitchen floors.  I use lemon or vinegar in water for window washing, and they sparkle.  I use vinegar and baking soda to clean and unplug our drains. But when a product sacrifices performance for the sake of being green, I won't buy it again.
summary: Didn't remove mold from our house siding

reviewText: I got this product to try at the right time.  Pollen and other debris from the trees has fallen all over our yard and home, and both needed a good spring cleaning.  First, we power washed the deck and chairs, first using the pressure washer with plain water, then with the cleaner.  Although it did appear somewhat sudsy, we could not see a difference between what was washed with the cleaner and what cleaned with just the power washer.  Next we washed the house, and although a lot of loose dirt came off with the power washer and cleaner, the moldy green stains did not.  My conclusion is that this might be fine for removing light dirt, but if you have mold or dark stains from tree sap and leaf debris, this is not going to do the job sufficiently.
summary: Krud Kutter HS01 for power washing

reviewText: A couple years ago, I washed my siding using another brand that just attached directly to the hose.  It had one of those spray bottle things, and it washed effectively up through the second floor with just the hose.  I thought that the Krud Kutter would do at least as well as that, with the pressure washer.Well, I hadn't used my pressure washer in a bit, and had some trouble with it.  Even so, the Krud Kutter was not doing *anything at all* to the green stuff growing on my siding.  Finally, I gave up on the pressure washer, and used the Krud Kutter stuff in the same hose-end spray bottle that I had used before (with the other brand).  It helped, some.  But it didn't really clean the siding.  It was better than just rinsing with the hose, but not nearly as effective as the other brand had been.

I'm kind of disappointed in this product. I had high expectations for it but it just didn't seem to make a noticeable dent on the water / mildew stains on the wooden eaves area under the gutters.  We live with fairly high humidity for three seasons of the year and while some of the dirt came off I'm not convinced it was due to the krud kutter solution.

I have used other Krud Kutter products that are outstanding.  Consequently, I was eager to try this product on my aluminum house and white vinyl fence.  It caused no change to the surface of the aluminum siding.  It did not do nearly enough to cut the seasonal green mold on the vinyl fence, even full strength with a brush. Letting it sit awhile did not bring a better result.  I expected better, and will keep looking for some application where it eases a cleaning chore.
summary: Even elbow  grease is not enhanced with this product.

reviewText: Both mildew and bird droppings were explicitly called out in the advertising for this cleaner, but it doesn't seem to work any miracles with them. On the plus side, it is a detergent and didn't damage any surfaces, but it also didn't clean as advertised. So it's really a "meh" review, it's okay, but not great, and probably a silly thing to have shipped to you rather than bought locally.
summary: Okay as a general cleaner, but didn't do anything for mildew or bird droppings

reviewText: Using this product with my 2000 gpm pressure washer to clean aluminum siding on a two story house. Decided to clean one section with just the pressure water and the other with the Krud Kutter solution. Noticed a difference with the soap versus just the water. Upon closer inspection I noted that the Krud Kutter did clean better but there was still some dirt residue on the siding that did not wash away. The water only side did come cleaner but some of the heavier soiling was still present whereas the Krud Kutter was able to remove it. All in all this is a good product for the price and the 1 gallon container covered approximately 2000sq.

I tried this to clean off my front porch, and it seems to work okay, however I'm not sure it does much more than just pressure washing on it's own.  When using it on mildew on concrete, I really couldn't tell much of a difference between using this, and just using water with full pressure.  Given that I couldn't tell much of a difference, I think I'd just as soon stick to just water and pressure to clean and skip all the chemicals.

I find that when I use a pressure washer to clean something, the results depend more on the PSI of my washer and my patience in using it than any soap I try.  So to really test this Krud Kutter, I decided to use it somewhere I can't access with my pressure washer and see how effective it was WITHOUT that extra oomph.  I have a roof over my patio that has alternating panels of corrugated metal and clear plastic.  I live in the Pacific Northwest so it is under constant assault from the elements plus moss, mildew,  rotting fir needles and a coating of sticky tree pollen every spring. There is no way to get at it with the pressure washer, short of erecting scaffolding.  My husband usually hauls out a giant ladder and hose clamps a brush to a long pole and scrubs it down by hand.  I ran the hose up to an upstairs window (which is at one side of the patio) and used a simple pressure nozzle to rinse off the bulk of the fir needles.  Then I put on a coating of Krud Kutter using a hose end sprayer.  After it sat for 5 minutes, I hosed it off with less than dazzling results.  It was better in the areas where I could get real close with the hose nozzle to get a real strong spray and less so the farther away it got.  Then I gave it a second dose of Krud Kutter applied with a pump sprayer.  I think the combination of a stronger concentration and a second application worked well because a lot more of the built up gunk came off when I rinsed it off this time.  It is by no means shiny and bright white now, but considering it didn't get scrubbed or pressure washed, I was pretty happy with the result.I also treated some vinyl lawn chairs with the left over spray I had mixed and they cleaned up pretty nicely too.Bottom line, when applied as a pre-treatment and then hosed off, it is moderately effective but don't expect that you are going to restore a heavily soiled item to new condition with that alone.  I expect that when combined with the force of a pressure washer and maybe a scrub brush on the really bad areas, this would be quite an effective cleaning solution.  I especially appreciate that it does not contain bleach, so my clothes were not ruined from the soaking I got during the project and that it is not going to harm my plants.  A gallon is similarly priced to 30 Seconds Outdoor Cleaner, but according to label directions will cover a lot more square footage, making it a more cost effective choice.  Give it a try!

I got this to use when I do my annual siding and driveway power washing because it says it cleans vinyl/aluminum siding, gutters, roofs, stucco, and brick and also contains Sporex to clean off mold and mildew. I have green mildew on some of my vinyl siding and was excited to give this a try to hopefully avoid using a scrubbing brush and make it easier to clean. I used this exactly as directed and while I did like the low odor factor, it did nothing else that plain water and my power washer couldn't do alone.I used this on the mildew and it didn't even come off, even after letting it sit for a few minutes, so I had to use the scrub brush anyway. I also used this on my concrete driveway and sidewalks to try to get rid of some rust colored stains and it didn't make any difference, plus I still had to use a scrub brush to get stains off. Bottom line, save the $11.99 and just use plain water because the results will be the same!
summary: Might As Well Just Use Water...

reviewText: Living in the Great Pacific Northwest has its challenges, including dealing with moss and fungus on your house siding and gutters.  As such, I was looking for an environmentally friendly product that would not hurt plants, people, or animals.  The material advertising on this product sounded like it meet those requirements, so I went ahead and ordered it.When the product arrived, I started reading all of the fine print and immediately became concerned with the requirement to soak all plants that might become contaminated by this product and to then flush with lots of water after use.  I went to the company website and looked up the material safety data sheet on this product and was concerned when it listed that rubber gloves, protective clothing, and a canister respirator should be used when using this product unless you could ensure that particulate count could remain very low and that you would not be in contact with the spray.  Now I do not know about you, but when I use a pressure washer there is NO way to keep from getting some spray on yourself or to control the amount of mist in the air.  So, using this in a pressure washer tank seemed to not be in the cards since I do not own a hazmat suit.The other recommended way of applying this was to use a pump sprayer with a diluted solution, so I opted for that, used rubber gloves, wore a rain jacket, and a respirator.  I also covered all of the plants with a plastic tarp after first soaking the plants and then when I was done, I uncovered the plants and rinsed them again.Ok, so much for the preliminary, here is what I found.I followed the instructions for dilution and sprayed on the material to half of one side of the house.  I then let it soak, but did not let it dry on the siding and gutters before using the pressure washer to remove the material.  I then proceeded to use the pressure washer without any additives to do the second half of that side of the house.  Since the entire side was pretty evenly dirty, I thought this would give me a good comparison to pressure washer versus Krud Kutter and pressure washer.After I let it dry, I then asked my wife to look at it and tell me if she saw any difference between both halves of the house side.  She could not see any difference (as a note, it looked the same to me as well).  I did not tell her which part was washed with what.So, after all of that, I did not see any difference and thus do not see the reason to use this product.  I am also not comfortable with the description of the safety of this product on plants and such after reading the filing with the EPA on the product and also looking up the active ingredients in the product (sodium metasilicate pentahydrate, and alcohol ethoxylate) .  As an additional note, the proprietary formulation that they will not divulge (alcohol ethoxylate) is on the California list of known chemicals that can cause reproductive issues.Thus, I would NOT recommend this product.
summary: Krud Kutter HS01 Green Pressure Washer Concentrate House and Siding Cleaner

reviewText: This stuff isn't exactly magic, but it does what it claims, functioning perfectly efficiently in the detergent dispenser of my Blue Clean AR118.  I sprayed it on some siding mold, gave it a couple minutes, and hit it again.  Voila!  Mold gone.Bear in mind, you are not supposed to be too tough on siding.  Sure, you could probably blast off the mold with water alone, but your siding should last longer with detergent and a gentler spray.

I have never found any cleaner to do anything magical in my pressure washer, just kind of assist. This seems to work as well as any that I have tried (and I've actually tried quite a few). It helped clean off some decking and some of the siding, as well as under the eaves of my house.Since it works as well as others I have used, and it costs about half what the others cost (at least the good ones; I have used some other cheap detergents that did nothing), I will probably keep using this one.

The house is clean and sparkling so when they sent this I thought, 'Oh great, what will I do with it?'  Well a friend of mine in Texas is familiar with this product and was stopping by last weekend and wanted to know all about my Vine membership with Amazon...and of course if could I get him on ( and for all the Vine members out there that here this week in week out...the answer is no btw...it's invitation only as far as I know)...but I was showing him some recent Vine products I was trying out currently and the Krud Kutter was among them and I explained the situation since I had just had the House professionally cleaned, and Bill, that's his name, said, 'Well heck, little buddy (don't ask), this makes a preemo driveway cleaner back home and you should try it'.  Well he and Agnes drove away Sunday which just happened to be a sunny dry day and I thought why not!!  So sure nuff I mixed some up (guessing at this point but got lucky) and darned if it didn't clean that driveway with just two applications.  So...I can 't speak to the house cleaning part other than to say if it could cut the grime on the driveway with a couple of sprays then I'm assuming it'll do a bang up job on the house siding.
summary: A Friend Of Mine Said This Made A Great Driveway Cleaner And Darned If It Don't!!

reviewText: We have to clean our vinyl  siding 2 x a year because we live near a busy street and because we have neighbors that like to have burn pits going in their yards during the summer. That all adds up to some greasy siding.I followed the directions and wasn't happy after the first wash - the grease was still thick in the little fake wood grainy bumps on the siding. I was hoping it was because I used the hose even though we do have really good water pressure. A week later I decided to try it using the pressure washer and while that took a little more off, I still wasn't real pleased with the results. What I have left I'm just going to use for things I can scrub in addition to spraying, like the lawn furniture etc. It does remove grease - it just needs you to scrub too so as a siding wash it was a fail for me.

This product works great with our Husky 1750 pressure washer.  My husband likes that it is a single step process with no rinsing required after cleaning.  One gallon of concentrate cleans up to 3200 sq. feet of exterior siding.  Care should be taken to prevent contact with your eyes and skin during cleaning.  My husband is happy with the Krud Cutter HS01 Green Pressure Washer Concentrate. He highly recommends this product to others for a brighter and cleaner house or building.
summary: This product works great with our Husky 1750 pressure washer

reviewText: I looked forward to using Krud Kutter cleaner to help my house. I have vinyl siding that hasn't been washed in a couple of years. My pressure washer doesn't have a lot of power, so I hoped a good cleaner would help it do a better job.I didn't get the results I hoped for on my siding. My house was cleaner, but it was also clean in the areas where I didn't use the Krud Kutter, and the Krud Kutter didn't help much on my siding. However, it did help get my flat stone patio cleaner. I compared sections with plain water and with the Krud Kutter, and there was a noticeable difference.The product label says it's safe for people, pets, and plants. You must rinse nearby plants before and after using this product. At first that sounded alarming, but it's probably wise to do after using any substance to clean your home if it can get on your plants or in the ground, even detergent.I wore gloves and goggles when I used this, since detergents can be harsh on skin and eyes, and I wasn't sure what else I was dealing with. I did not wear a mask, but I wish I had because I could taste it and it left a familiar burn in the back of my throat. I've experienced this with certain bathroom cleaners. Maybe it's time for me to consider natural cleaners, like vinegar.I'm sorry to say that I was not impressed with this product. It may be better than plain water, but I'm not convinced it's the best product for the job.
summary: Didn't help clean my house, but my patio looks better

reviewText: I was really hoping that this product would work well and I could give it a good review. I followed the directions and applied it to our vinyl siding with low pressure, using the gas power washer. I waited about 3-5 minutes as directed. The siding and plants had been wet with water previously. The problem area of our house is on the north side and we power wash it every year. The problem is dirt, green mildew or mold and black spots from some kind of mold.When I power washed it after the Krud Kutter application, the dirt came off as usual, some of the green stuff came off more easily than usual, but it did nothing to the black spots. In order to remove them I have always had to get within 10 inches of the siding with the power spray, sometimes closer. I had to do this using the Krud Kutter as well.I tried using the Krud Kutter at a stronger solution, but no difference.
