While the bench itself doesn't appear to be extremely sturdy, it can comfortably seat two and an additional child. If this bench was half the price and came with instructions, it would have received a 5 star rating, but it loses a star for each of those detractions.

There were no instructions, but it was apparent how it fit together.  The back is one piece, the seat another, and then the two arms.  The pieces had to be strong-armed to match the screw holes up, and the screw heads get covered by your typical plastic cover that will likely fall off over time.It seems sturdy enough up to a certain weight, though by simply tightening a screw too much you can easily bend the frame, it's not a very thick aluminum.I do like the angle of the back and the depth of the seat.Overall, however, this seems like something you'd pick up at one of the big hardware stores for under a hundred dollars.
summary: Overpriced for this level of quality

reviewText: First, the good parts.  I like the look and feel.  "Silver" powder coating finish over the aluminum frame has a nice contemporary tidy look.  Ditto for the resin slats, which look quite wood-like.  I haven't time-tested this yet, but I suspect that the resin composite will outlast genuine wood.  Slats are spaced pretty close together, which eliminates uncomfortable gaps.  Comfortable slight tilt to back support.  Nice deep seating surface gives good thigh support to tall sitters.  The armrests are rather spartan, consisting of just the aluminum framing, but I suppose this is acceptable (barely) for outdoor furniture.  The assembled item seems sturdy and strong. Thanks to the use of aluminum, it's not too heavy either.Some minimal assembly is required.  It's not much, just requiring the installation of eight screws, which will attach the four sub-pieces: back, seat, and two armrest/legs. A hex wrench is included, which is the only tool needed.Fortunately, assembly steps are fairly obvious, as the product I received did not include any paperwork at all (such as assembly instructions, warranty paperwork, factory contact info, etc).  The provided screws come in three lengths, so some instructions would have been nice.  Also a caution about using the provided washers on all screws. Do it, otherwise the cosmetic plastic screw caps (not shown on the Amazon Product Listing photos example) will not snap onto the screw heads.Second complaint -- the first screw I tightened securing the seat to the front leg stripped out.  Then so did its counterpart on the opposite end of the bench.  I was not using excessive force.  Fortunately, there are two screws used at this location, so I carefully installed #2 (a shorter screw), and was able to tighten it with good results.  The stripped screws remain snugly in place and should still function ok to provide load bearing and alignment tasks satisfactorily.Again, nice design, and these minor frustration items I can easily put behind me, but this is not a "cheap" bench so these quality control problems shouldn't have occurred.This item was manufactured in China.
summary: Nice design. A couple of quality control issues.

reviewText: One of my favorite chairs, it is great for lounging in the sun room and the flat arms work well for holding a drink.

This Strathwood synthetic wicker chair is just what I wanted. UPS delivered right to my door and it was light enough for me to get it inside.The chair is large (and I am six foot tall, 250 pounds) so I needed a big chair. It is sturdy and doesn't creak and moan when I sit in it.  We've had some gorgeous weather lately so I have been able to sit on my patio and try it out. I use the chair without the throw cushion, my back against back cushion and my feet touch the ground. If you are shorter, you will probably need the throw cushion to push you forward so feet touch ground.I love the dark brown color. I do wish the seat cushions were a darker color (so as to not show soiling easily). So I might recover them myself.The cushion covering material is well made, kind of a glossy material that wipes down well, tightly woven, correct size for foam inserts so the cushions lay the way they should, zippers are sewn well.  I did spray the cushions with3m Scotchgard? Fabric Protector  4101Dand actually spilled an iced coffee on the chair (not on purpose). The cushions wiped clean with no sign of spill and I was able to clean wicker easily (it's tightly woven as well).I do wish Strathwood made an ottoman to go with this chair. I do like to put my feet up and didn't want a lounger. And I do wish the chair was made in the U.S. rather than China.
summary: Comfy outdoor chair - just what I wanted

reviewText: After shopping and considering many options I found this furniture to be very good value for the money, light but strong, happy with purchase

Looks great for the prize, arrived in a timely manner. Fully assembled and boxed just like the rest of the Strathwood set. However word of caution, I noticed the plastic wrap in the box had rust round it. So it may rust if used outside and exposed to rain. I will update in three to six months. As off now, I have it indoors. Will take it out when it gets warm outside. With that said, the chair is large but light weight. I was not able to take it through my stair door leading to the sunroom upstairs, it was too wide. So I had to carry it around back to use the back door which is wider. My back gate was locked, so I threw it over the fence, before jumping over( lucky me, just like the chair, I didn't sustain any damage to my body).The chair landed well bounced off the ground well without any damage. So if you have kids, I think it will stand the rough use. The chairs looks as pictured, it is wide and deep. The back support is not the best support for me. I thought it was because of my small frame but my husband is 6'2, 210lbs and he said the chair was very uncomfortable for him.I plan to keep it because it looks good and it's made well for the prize. I just wouldn't be sitting in it for extended periods, I don't think my back will take it well.I plan to move it outside when it get warm. I will update in 3 to 6 months on how well it holds up outside.
Perfect chair for our screen room.  Excellent quality.

Strathwood - a product by Amazon.comThe Strathwood Griffen All-Weather Wicker Chair is comfortable & roomy. It looks much nicer in person than in the photo.Its simple, casual design will withstand changing trends in furniture styles.A note concerning all-weather, resin wicker: It is  meant to look like natural wicker, but is made of a synthetic material that  requires little maintenance. It is  durable, strong, resistant to humidity, water & UV radiation, & somewhat elastic which adds to the chair's comfort. It's easy to clean & can be hosed down (remove the cushions first). The color is part of the fiber & shouldn't fade.The chair arrives carefully packaged in a large box with no assembly required.The Griffen Chair appears to be well-made, with attention to detail. Constructed with an aluminum frame & feet, the chair is lightweight & strong. The aluminum frame & feet are neatly finished with a dark-brown powder coating. The cushions & throw pillow have zippered, 100% polyester, fabric covers; all of them have piping. The back & seat cushions consist of a  2" block of foam covered by polyester fiber which brings the total width of each cushion to 4".  In addition to under-seat webbing which allows the seat to move comfortably,  there's a curved piece of aluminum for additional strength & safety. (see the photo I uploaded)The back has a slight slope to it so you're not sitting straight up & down.  The included throw pillow can be arranged to give your back  lumbar support if you need it. I'm 5' 3" and need to use the pillow so that I don't sit so far back in the chair. My feet even touch the floor when I use the pillow. Because there's a lot of seat depth, I'm assuming a taller person can sit comfortably in this chair too. I will be sure to update my review when one of our taller friends tries it out.Approximate seat measurements:Seat cushion: 25" long (front to back) x 23.5" wide (side to side) x 4" thick.Back cushion: 17" long (up & down) x 23.5" wide (side to side) x 4" thick.Pillow: 17" squareSeating area using both seat cushion & back cushion: 23 1/2" wide x 22" - 21" deep or less depending on how you place the back cushion.Amazon's product description covers cushion care & cleaning so I won't go into that. However, I will remind you that during inclement weather it's recommended  to bring both the chair and the cushions indoors or securely cover them,  and to store them in a dry place when not in use.This is the most comfortable wicker chair I've ever sat in.  It's roomy,  doesn't cut the circulation off in my legs (at the back of my knees), the cushions aren't lumpy, they're comfortable. The chair arms are smooth & not scratchy. I can rest my arms or my elbow on them without causing myself any discomfort.I will update my review if the Strathwood Griffen chair fails to perform as expected.A product guarantee isn't mentioned. However, you may return this item sold by Amazon.com within 30 days of delivery for a full refund. Amazon.com will pay the return shipping cost if the return is a result of their error.UPDATE:I've been using this chair indoors on a protected porch so I can't comment on how it withstands the weather.

We received our Strathwood Griffen All-Weather Wicker Chair about two months ago.  It came in an enormous box, in one piece, with two cushions and a pillow.  Aside from taking it out of the box and getting all of that cardboard to the recycling center, it was in perfect condition and we placed the chair on our front porch.  My mother-in-law then spotted it, and she liked it so much I thought about giving it to her, but then my wife had a better idea."Let's build a deck."So, I got a $225 chair, and we had to build a new deck roughly 50-times that value to have a place to put it.  How I'm going to pay for it all makes me lose sleep, but, hey, the chair looks great on it.Now that the deck is done, the chair has a nice home in the corner of it, and I must say that even with some supremely comfortable deck chairs ("let's get a table and deck chairs" came soon after the building of the deck began), people gravitate to this chair.  It is wide and a very comfy place to sit back and relax.  It is very sturdy, and I'm sure with care it will last for some time, but some of the reviews I have read do make me a little concerned about the longetivity of the piece.  For right now, it is beautiful and my family loves it.I should remark that this chair isn't "real wicker."  It is a woven resin material which looks strikingly like wicker, treated to protect from ultra-violet light and keep its color and elasticity.  It does seem that the material has some give to it, and I hope this doesn't promote fraying such as in the picture posted by Mr. Petersen at the top of this page.The chair, including the pillow and cushions, wieghs in at just over 20 pounds, which I think is amazing.  It is very easy to move about.  I wiegh in at about 275 pounds, and I feel comfortable parking myself on the chair... whereas some inside-the-house chairs creak and complain.  :^)When it rains, I have managed on almost all occasions to bring the cushions and pillow in, but even when I was too late and they get a little wet, they dry out quickly and cleanly.  The cushions are zippered so that you can remove the foam inserts to clean the covers.I am very happy with the chair after two months, and my wife is as well.  She loves how it looks.  Everyone who has sat in in loves it.  You can see other people on the deck plotting to snatch that seat should the current occupant leave.  So for now, I do recommend this chair, and I will try to remember to come back and write an update in a year or so, or less if something happens to dispariage my feelings on it.  Cheers!
summary: So Far, The Strathwood Griffen All-Weather Wicker Chair was a good call

reviewText: What is a chair?  is there an essence of "chairness" that defines what a chair is?Shut your yap, Socrates, and sit yourself down in this Strathwood Griffen.  Comfortable, feels strong, built for in-door and out-door, this is the right chair for me.See, I had this spot, and I wanted this nice chair ($1900) that was shaped like a catcher's mit ($1900) and was just wonderful.  But common sense (my smart wife) and the price (did I mention $1900?) pushed me into a differnet direction, a chair I could open the door on, let the wind come into the 4-season, and just sit down and relax.The chiar is square, this is a square chair, not a sloucher or a glorified bean bag of a chair, but a real deal chair, with some fiber.  Should you get the entire set?  You should get the chair.  The set may or may not follow.I like this chair.  And it does not resemble a catcher's mit and does not cost $1900.
summary: This is a very well built chair!

reviewText: We received these just yesterday so this isn't a long term review.  Overall, we're happy.  The plastic used to make the chairs IS thinner than the higher dollar ones, but that's not hard to believe.  The look is great and the comfort is decent as well.  We plan to get some accent pillows, because brown and beige is a bit to blah for us.  I gave it 4 stars due to the thinner plastic, but that by no means detracts from the usefulness or beauty of the chair.These come exactly as the photo shows.

reviewerName: Bartok Kinski "A casual stroll through the lu...
reviewText: This comfortable, soft bus stop seating arrangement is very cheap and can be nailed to the ground for bus passengers waiting in desolate areas. It is stuffed with sheep's mutton and allows a few years of use before it needs to be upholstered by a union mechanic. Preferable to the "metal seats" which are currently available which cause blisters to the backside.
I originally wasn't going to purchase this piece, but it completed the conversation area in the Carolina Room. I am glad I did. it is a very comfortable couch, and looks great.

Wow, this outdoor sofa is great! It fits perfectly on our front patio, the color is a bit lighter than shown on the pictures in my opinion but still very nice! This sofa sits under a patio roof but will have contact with the sun from noon to sunset. This sofa should be able to handle the elements it receives from our use so I will update this review if anything arises.UPDATE: Added a picture, so far no issues.

I shopped for months, looking for the perfect outdoor furniture but the ones I liked were so expensive, until I came across this one. After reading some horrible reviews. I decided to take my chances with caution. So I started by ordering the ottoman first because it is a smaller item. (See my review of the ottoman). After that, I ordered the chair and side table(also see my reviews on both items).I then took the big leap and ordered the sofa. It arrived in a timely manner. The delivery man was not friendly at all.After he dropped off the very large box. I struggled to open it and pulled out the sofa. I immediately noticed a huge damage to the lower back of the sofa. The back rod that runs across the sofa, which provides supports for the three rear legs was severely bent inward causing the wicker to fold up and also lifting the legs off the ground. I taught it must have been damaged from transit because the box was slightly damaged and I could not believe that a company will knowingly package an obviously damaged furniture and have it shipped out.I immediately called Amazon customer service. The rep was professional and helpful. She arranged for an exchange for another sofa and she told me that the delivery company will pick up the damaged sofa when the deliver the new one( by the way, that information was incorrect) When they called to schedule a delivery of the new one, they told me that they do not pick up.So I had to call Amazon again, and this time the rep told me that he would contact the company that does the pickup to make the arrangement.Eight days later, I received the replacement, but the damaged sofa and the large box it came in  were still sitting in my living room because they had not been picked up.However this time around the second sofa delivery man was very pleasant and professional. He agreed to help me unpack the sofa and inspect it. We both found the same damage on the same spot as the previously delivered sofa. Although the second sofa was not as damaged as the first one. It was still noticeable and the center rear leg was elevated off the floor.I immediately called Amazon again. The rep was professional. He issued a refund plus additional Amazon credit for the inconvenience. He also mentioned that they have had several complaints about the sofa and that they may stop the sells until  the manufacturer resolves the issues. The call was disconnected, so I called back to finalize the call. This time a different rep took my call. She was professional as well. She finalized the return.So I asked her if I could keep the second sofa with less damage for a discount because they may temporary stop sales of the sofa and I really don't want to shop for another sofa, It is really time consuming. She told me that they could only give me eight five dollars discount.I said No, thanks. If I am going to keep a damage sofa and save them the return shipping for a sofa that they can not resale. The least they can do is fifty to seventy percent off.So with that said, I plan to sit both sofa outside for them to be picked up. There is no room in my house for two large damage sofas and a very large box.Overall, the design of the sofa is nice, it looks just as pictured. The cushions are not very comfortable, they may get more comfortable as they age. It is reasonably prized. Customer service is pretty good.It is an ok sofa if you receive one that's not broken.Good luck, shop at your own risk;)
summary: Damaged sofa, not once but twice:(

reviewText: This sofa in comfy, and durable. Stands up to the elements great and it has given me soo much relaxing pleasure out in the great outdoors under the sun, smoking my cigars.

We have put the couch outdoors, as it is not raining anymore.It looks great, and is more comfortable then I thought it was going to be.I put a big umbrella near it so the sun does not ruin  the material.After looking all over, this is really a good price. Outdoor furnature is very expensive,and looks the same as this sofa does. Although other outdoor furnature has seats thatare thicker and more plush..That said, does other ODF last any longer then this sofa is going too?! Do not think so.This outdoor couch is light weight, but has steel bars underneath to keep it strong, and to keep its shape.It can be moved around easely.Although the midldle back leg came smushed, and wobbles, but still there! I think someone else had the same problem!I don't think I'll be moving it around much, as I think the leg will break off.I also noticed the whole bottom of the wicker couch is not level, it seems to be arched up in the middle from looking at it from the front! Or this could be from the Steel Bars underneath.I'm sure nobody will notice this.The wicker is a type of plastic, but looks nice , so it should last a few years.I'll put this in the garage for the winter.It was delivered just as the picture shows. With the 3 bottom cushions, 3 back cushions, and 4 throw pillows.Everything fits together fine.I took 2 throw pillows off, and put in its place two new outdoor pillows, that have red, black and beige strips. It gives it a little more punch of color.The cushions are NOT Cushy, are not soft, and I don't think very thick.That said, this seems to be a comfortable outdoor couch.It is easy to get out of.The weather here is not good enought (has been raining) to put it outside. It is sitting in my living room, so it has been sat on.My teenage grandkids do not think it is comforable, cause the cushions move around, and seem hard etc.The fabric is poly and slick feeling.. I have to keep pushing in the bottom cushions in to keep them in place, and the top ones also.I realize this is not an expensive peice of outdoor furnature. Although it does look good.I have laid down on it, it is ok, Its not a mushy lay around type of couch.It has a more modern look, with streight lines. I like the look.It looks up to-date.Being that it is new, I think I'm more critical of the couch. As we use it more, I'm sure I willnot be thinking about these little things about the couch!!I bought a outdoor rug from costco to set this couch on.I'm going to a use a couple of outdoor chairs on both sides of the table in the middle.I'm excited to use this couch.After we start to use this couch, if there is any changes, I'll up date.
summary: light weight, great price... Up Date.

reviewText: The wicker is really plastic woven to look like wicker.  That's fine and expected.  The pillows are nice and I find them very comfortable.  I received all of the correct pillows.The item arrived in a box and the box was in perfect condition.  It was fairly well packaged.  No assembly - other than removing some plastic and some tags.My problem is that the left arm is pushed inwards towards the seating area about 2 inches and the right arm is pushed in about 8 inches.  It is as if the sofa were dropped on one side, then the other, BEFORE it was put in the box!The bottom is completely open and you can see the metal powder coated frame.  The metal on my arms is visibly deformed.  Maybe the frame was bent before they applied the "wicker"?It is strong enough and heavy enough to withstand most normal elements (we are in the northeast).The colors of mine look exactly like the picture.The cushions are nice, but don't have much life in them.  After taking a nap the cushions remained "pancaked" for several hours after I got up.  I'm not a big guy.  Pretty standard 160 lbs.  I have some concern that the cushions will need to have the stuffing replaced fairly quickly.NOTE:  Amazon was terrific on an exchange for a non-damaged item.  The guy from CEVA came around to my deck and swapped out the original damaged sofa for the new one (which is perfect).  It was no hassle at all.  They gave me a one hour window for the swap (6-7am) and the guy showed up at almost exactly 6:30.
Love it. Great quality.

reviewerName: Modern Blue Argonaut "No I do not have a shoe...
reviewText: I grew up in Southeast Asia with lots of wicker furniture, so much so that I hadn't felt the need to own wicker in a long time. This is NOT the wicker I grew up with at all. It's more "manufactured" and the frame is in fact plastic wicker, but that is a good thing for the outdoors! It seems extremely durable, it's extremely lightweight (easy to move), and easy to clean. It also looks nice. Comfort level is maybe a 4 at best. It's great for kids and occasional use, but do not expect to sit on this for hours on end enjoying the sunshine. Everything fit well (pillows) and the sofa was delivered in under a week with excellent communication every step of the way by the delivery company. Someone must be present to sign for it, but since I wasn't home, my teenager signed for it. I love the look of this sofa but again, it's not wicker of plant origin so it may not be what you are looking for.

Well made, outdoor furniture is expensive.  Well made, outdoor furniture is hard to find.  Well made, outdoor furniture that comes assembled is hard to find.Strathwood's all-weather wicker 3-seater sofa meets all of the above requirements and MORE.This sofa is made of a beautiful, woven resin wicker on a, more importantly, strong, powder-coated aluminum frame. I have had this sofa and have used it almost daily for over a month.  Three people can easily sit comfortably as it measures 32 inches long by 79 inches wide by 30 inches tall; and weighs in at around 70 pounds which makes it easy for me to move around by myself. It also features a flat back which cuts down TREMENDOUSLY on coveted patio space.The cushions and pillows are in a beige 100% polyester fabric which I sprayed with an outdoor, water resistant spray.  My cushions have already been SOAKED to the core in rain and they drain and dry very quickly due to the light, poly fill stuffing in them.There is a matching Griffen chair and coffee table which I am also interested in. Again, there is no assembly required.  The manufacturer states to just spot clean cushions/pillows but they all are zippered, corded and removable. I have washed one pillow cover just to see how it would come out.  The only thing I would caution on is that to be VERY CAREFUL when removing from the covers as I ripped the outside of the inside portion of the pillow that holds the poly fill inside.All in all, I am VERY happy with my outdoor "davenport" (as my Grandma Pat would have called it) and hope it gives me many years of outdoor pleasure!
summary: A SOLID 4 Stars For Strathwood Griffen Outdoor Sofa - Good Value & Great Price!

reviewText: Not exactly the 2nd day Prime shipping like it was supposed to be, but I still got it and it was well packaged and protected.Overall we're VERY happy with this sofa.  We also have the two arm chairs and table, and they all look great sitting on our covered 18'x18' deck.  The pillows are a bit bland, but we plan to get some accent pillows to liven it up a bit.
summary: Well made and came well packaged!

reviewText: I like the coffee table as part of the set. It does the job without attracting attention to itself and is light enough to easily move.

What an amazing outdoor table!  I will list a few of the pros:+ Heavy and sturdy build+ Attractive, tightly woven texture+ Great natural color+ Legs have small round 'bumps' that keep the bottom from scratching any scuffable surface+ Hollow inside supported by metal frame (durable!)+ Weather proofed powder coated aluminum finishI can't really say anything negative about this table.  It is rather large, so it's tight on small patios.  But it makes a great place to serve drinks or snacks (I would keep drinks on a tray).  I even like to cock my feet up on it and use it as an ottoman.  I really don't see this thing needing replacing or repair for a number of years.  With the aluminum finish, I don't expect to see any fading from sun, or any adverse effects from rain.  I would probably keep an eye on the underside for spiders or mold (if those are problems in your are like they are in 'sunny' Oregon), but that is to be expected from a hollow table of this style.  I highly recommend it.-----------------Update:  If you want to have glasses, plates, etc on this table, then you need to get a tray of some sort.  I actually use a side table for my beverage, making this table not much more than a footrest.  Rating reduced.  It's just that there is not really any reinforcement except around the edges and through the center of the table.  The table covering bows any time you put something on it.  It won't even support a stemless wine glass without the glass tipping.But if you don't mind using a tray, then it's good.
summary: Looks great, but not very functional ~

reviewText: fits perfectly in front of the Griffen 3 seater sofa After shopping and considering many options I found this furniture to be very good value for the money, light but strong, happy with purchase

My wife and I were looking all over for an outdoor living set and we finally settled on this one. I tell ya, I'm not wasting my time or money in retail stores anymore. Amazon delivered another great product at a reasonable price. This coffee table is stylish, contemporary, and durable. It compliments the matching sofa perfectly. Originally i thought it might be a little big, but it compliments the sofa perfectly, smaller would look out of place. I'm glad I got this and I am sure I will have some great memories in the back yard this summer sitting around this coffee table
summary: Perfect coffee table to complement a great sofa

reviewText: I believe a table should have a solid top.  This one does not.  The manufacturer did put a slim (about 1/16" thick) piece of hard and brittle plastic on the underside of the weave.  My table arrived with a 6" jagged crack in that plastic.  I do not see that the plastic adds to the support of the table top.  My 5.5 pound cat walked across the table and created an indent with each step she took.If there were stemmed wine glasses on the table and someone put their hand down and leaned on the table the wine glasses would take a tumble.Besides the unstable table top:  The weave is not always straight with the edges on all sides.  The color of the fake rattan does accurately match the other pieces in this line (at least the one other piece that I have).  The feet are brown-paint-coated aluminum and are anchored well.  The packaging has been improved (since the piece I received last month), in that the spots in the box where the feet hit are reinforced.  The table arrived in good shape because it was packed properly, so don't be afraid about the shipping of this item.UPDATE May 4, 2012:  Found a good use for this piece of furniture:  It is very useful for hiding things.  It is so light weight, just lift it up and store unsightly, but necessary patio/outdoor/pool stuff underneath.  We took a lid from a plastic tub and set our bug sprays, glass cleaner, plant food, etc. on the lid, then put the "table" over it.  If this piece of furniture had a sturdy top and a lid, I'd give it five stars....
summary: Top of table has way too much "give"

reviewText: Perfect and very usable.  May be a bit big if you have a confined space.

This "outdoor coffee table" is cleanly designed, attractive but I feel it is a waste of space because it isn't designed to hold or hide items. Another reviewer noted that it can be used for that purpose by simply putting things under it and indeed it can although you have to lift it up to do that, and obviously remember what you put where. Also I was hoping it could support weighty items but it cannot because the fake wicker "gives" although the frame seems strong enough.All in all it pleases the eye but requires storage or covering off-season and doesn't make the best use of space.
summary: Like its looks but design not completely functional.

reviewText: This table looks exactly like the picture, so if you like the appearance of the table you see in the picture, you'll be happy with it.  Be sure to check the dimensions because it is quite larger than I was thinking it would be and takes up a lot of space.  It is stylish, well-constructed and seems durable, especially if you cover it or take it inside during inclement weather like it suggests.

We received this just yesterday so this isn't a long term review.  Overall, we're happy.  The plastic used to make the furniture IS thinner than the higher dollar ones, but that's not hard to believe.  The look is great and the comfort is decent as well.  It could use a glass top as it's not overly stiff and heavy drinks may fall over if the bases of the glasses aren't overly wide.  We plan to use a drink tray and coasters.  I gave it 4 stars due to the thinner plastic, but that by no means detracts from the usefulness or beauty of the table.
We use several things--this is one of them--to keep critters away from our pond and gardens.  We have been pest free for a time now.
summary: Discourages strays as well as nocturnal visitors

reviewText: The cats in my neighborhood love this stuff. I just sprinkle it on the ground, they show up and lay beside it, roll in it, sniff it. Basically this is granulated catnip.Unfortunately I want to get rid of cats, not get more of them.

Well, the squirrel ate more of the garage door after Dad put these around the area.  He said they smelled bad enough, but didn't work. :(  So, he put a phony woodpecker out there, and is waiting for the results of that, but said that the plastic bird worked quite well in the back of the house.  :)

....so I guess it must be working.We had a small skunk floating around. I spread some of this stuff and have not seen the skunk since.ONE WARNING: If you buy this, use it sparingly and DO NOT SNIFF THE CONTENTS! It is the most pungent smell I have experienced save for maybe medical smelling salts. Use sparingly as well.
summary: Well, the rodents haven't been around.......

reviewText: I bought this product to deter squirrels from moving into my attic.  We're used to having one or two over-winter up there but this year there were at least six (I shot 5 of them and one keeps coming around).  They were really rambunctious and gnawed away at the woodwork in the attic.I made up little sachets of the Fox Urine Granules using paper towels.  The squirrels found them offensive but just threw them out under the eaves of the roof.  They weren't scared by the scent at all.  I might try using the granules to scare off the rabbits if they bother my garden but, so far, the product hasn't worked for me.

I real all the reviews before purchasing, and many comments were directed toward the assembly of this cart.  Was afraid it would be a nightmare, but not so.First, I am a girl.  60 yrs old, but still....  I put this together by by myself in just under 2 hrs.  First, prep time:  Poured a glass of wine and read through the directions the night before and looked over the parts to get an idea of what went where.  Next morning, made myself a mug of tea.  Got out the wireless speakers and put on loud rock and roll music (Pandora's Southern Rock station is great working music).  Put up a table to set the parts on during assembly, and a low stool for floor assembly.  Now I was ready.  The directions were easy to follow.  The packet of hardware was very well marked.  The parts were on a cardboard base with plastic "compartments".  Each compartment was labeled step 1, 2 etc, so no need to sort a bag full of parts into piles as I've encountered with other products.  The only "problem" I ran into was getting the rear frame onto the cart.  When I finally figured out I could lay the cart on it's side, then I could reach the bolts on the inside and the nuts on the outside, all while bracing the frame with my knee.  Didn't need that many tools:  a 12 and 13 mm socket, 12 mm wrench.  The allen wrench needed for some of the "dimple screws" was provided with the parts.Only gave it 4 stars because we haven't tried hooking it up to our yard tractor yet, so waiting to see how that will go.  As a hand pulled cart it is awesome.  Turns easily, big wheels work well on rough terrain back in the trees, haven't noticed a wobbling problem as in some other reviews.  The cart is high off the ground so it doesn't catch on stuff.  Love it so far!5/2014.  I just upgraded my review to a 5.  This is a great cart.  I use it all the time.  Yes, yard work, picking up brush, hauling power tools and cords around.  Also use it to cart provisions to and from our travel trailer.  AND we have hooked it up to the yard trailer, easy as pie.  We weren't hauling a lot of heavy yard stuff, but rather several grandkids.  (Yeah, I know, the manufacturer would cringe at hauling kids around, but hey, they loved the ride.)  Tows like a dream.  Highly recommend this.

Been using this cart for hauling fire wood, and my wife hauls her plantsand and things for the green house.  It seems to be a tough made cart.When loaded with fire-wood it is a bit heavy, but i can pull it ok on level or slightly sloaped ground.Good thing is that if it does get to heavy to pull up hills and throughthe woods, it is made to hook up to my ridding mower.I am happy that i own this cart and it is just the right size too.So far so good, and i would buy it again.

I ordered this product about a month ago.  So far it's been attached to my tractor for a total of 3 hours of engine on time.  That time has consisted of moving 70 bags of mulch - 4-5 bags at a time; 20 bags of "pond rocks" at 7-8 at a time, and of course two 30 something women that wanted a ride around the yard.  It has been one of the best purchases I've made since becoming a new homeowner.The assembly process was fairly straight forward and took about an hour to casually yet methodicly assemble it.  I found that a little extra time studying the instructions during assembly really made the assembly easy.  There are a few steps that could use a bit of "bolding" to ensure that you're not re-assembling it, however if the time is spent paying attention to what the illustrations demonstrate it goes together very easily. Initially the basket does have a smell that dissipated in about a week.On its use - as mentioned earlier most of its use for me has been spent hauling heavy items around our sloped yard and for that - it's been exceptional.  The pneumatic tires soften the ride over the gravel/slate rocks and uneven ground, the basket holds 5 bags of mulch (with 1 of the 5 being taller than the top of the basket).  Putting the bags in, I think that it's safe to say I wasn't gentle, but dropped them in from the bed of a truck and it shows no wear or bolts getting loose from my handling.  The dump function works well, and even with a few hundred pounds of dirt/mulch or rock in it, utilizing the dump release requires minimal effort.  As mentioned in an earlier review the back wheels move closer to the front wheels when dumping and as a result the initial location of the dumped material is about the centerline of the back tires before dumping.  (I would imagine that this is also a result of the fact that during the process, it was attached to a tractor which limited it's movement.)Overall - I have no complaints and am very happy with its function, usability, ease of assembly and overall durability.  I would gladly buy again or recommend to a friend.  If there is no update to my review in the next year - assume that it's still as described above.Update 8/29/2013 - Item is still holding strong and I use it about every other week.  I still stand by my earlier recomendation.Update 3/19/2014 - Item is still great - We moved 5 yards (1 yard is 27cu.Ft) of mulch and 1.5y ards of stone this weekend, If I had to guess it was about 5 tons of material.  I built a rail system for it as well.  It didn't take too long and allowed me to load that much more in it for each trip.  I'd guess each trip of stone was in the 600-800lb range of material.  Still would buy again - but I doubt that I'll need to anytime soon.

I have to agree with some of the other reviewers that the assembly of this item requires some patience. The instructions are good, and the parts (nuts & bolts) are shrink-wrapped onto cards so you can see how many of each you have. This helps a lot during assembly.  It took me a little over an hour to get it assembled, and yes, the tires smell bad. I've been using this cart to haul logs from my wood pile, and moving bulky garden items like potting soil, mulch, bricks, etc..  The dump feature on this cart works like a charm, and its easy to steer with the pneumatic tires.

I recently moved into a 50+ year old house that needed a lot of heavy yard work.  I needed to move a ton or more of gravel, dozens of stones weighing over 100 lbs each, lots of bricks, and loads and loads of dirt.  I went to our local big-box home supply store to get a wheelbarrow when I saw this item. It made so much more sense for what I needed to do and even though it cost more that I was planning to spend I got it.I have to be honest and say that putting it together was a pain for me.  I'm not the world's handiest guy and it took me a good 2 hours to assemble it, even with help (this cart is big enough to require 2 people to put it together).  The instructions could have been much better as it contained a lot of charts but few written directions.  However, like childbirth, once you have brought it into the world you forget about the labor (okay, I've never given birth so I am only going by what I have heard from those that have).Once assembled you have to inflate the tires.  It's those pneumatic tires that makes carrying large loads possible.  The cart is rated for 1200 pounds but I am pretty sure that I will never test that claim.  I am not sure how much I have put in it but I have loaded it full with pea-sized gravel many times and it still handles well.  Learning to steer it took some time but it can maneuver well in a small space.  The handle can come off so that you can attach it to a small tractor, lawn mower, or ATV.  I have never pulled it with a powered vehicle so I can't address that feature.  However, I can say that the handle is well made and does what I need it to do.One of my favorite features about the Gorilla cart is that it is so easy to dump.  When you pull the release handle and lift it the wheels move closer together making it easier to dump heavy loads of gravel, soil, or rocks.  Another thing that I like is how tough the bed of the cart is.  Yes, it can be scratched and marred but I see them as badges of honor.  This thing is tough and a pleasure to use.  I have not had any problems with it so I have not tested the company's customer service department.  I am hoping that this cart lasts me for years.  If a problem does come up I will post updates here.
summary: It's sooo much better than a wheelbarrow!

reviewText: I go on summer backpacking and carcamping trips and enjoy my electronics.  This "adventure kit" looks like the perfect device for me.  It can recharge four AA batteries AND recharge a laptop, cellphone or iPhone.  I take a cellphone and a laptop with me on my roadtrips, and place it in my dashboard for quick recharge.The device is quite portable but a bit heavy for an overnight backpacking trip (there are lighter devices out there to recharge cellphones and iPods), but effective enough for carcamping or long-distance driving where multiple pasengers may want to need their electronics recharged.The four AA batteries recharged with no problem within four hours.I haven't had any issues with the solar cells melting.  I like that the panels can be protected during transport with a zipper-lock that keeps the charging panel covered.

Overall a very good product that delivers all that it promises.  However, there seems to be a disconnect on what people expect and what this technology can do.Although I had received this product for a while and even played with it for a bit. It was never a necessary piece of gear for me while camping, RV-ing or hiking.  Quite simply, I don't like to park my RV in a site with full sun nor do I like to set up camp in full sun because it would just be too hot.  I'm also not prepared to leave my phone and this solar recharging kit in someone else's campsite or left unattended for the whole day on a trail.However, during the aftermath of Hurricane Sandy, this product proved really useful and even essential when we would couldn't get gas for our generator.The realities of using this (and any other solar charger) is:1) It takes approximately 8-10 hours to charge anything.  (As the manufacturer commented below, it might take less on full sunny days, but from the brightly-overcast days after sandy and preceding the snow storm, it took 8-10 hours for us to charge an Iphone4)2) Because it trickle charges, the best way to use this with your electronics is to have it charge backup batteries and then charge your phone with the fully recharged backup batteries instead of expecting it to charge your phone directly unless you are willing to leave your phone next to this solar recharger for the number of hours it takes to recharge your phone.3) If your phone is completely drained, there may not be enough "push" to start a recharge.4) Once the limitations of this technology and this unit is understood, it is relatively easy to plan ahead and recharge one set of batteries per sunny day and ration use of electronics.5) One of the most confusing things about this product is that there are different package combos available at different shops, online stores and discount outlets.  Basically, Nomad7 is the solar panel part of the unit shown here and the "Guide10" refers to the battery pack and rechargeable AA batteries shown here.  There are other "Nomad7 + something else" combos available, but the most useful and versatile one is the one shown here.  On another note, The "Plus" refers to the USB output that has been increased in this model (and the newer models) to have an output of 1.0 Amp compared to the older models that only delivered 0.5 Amp from the USB output.  The older models are the ones often seen on online discount merchants' websites.  So buyer beware.  Double-check to make sure you're getting the version you need to charge your electronics.6) This kit comes with a selection of USB and micro usb adapters and of course a car socket  so that it is compatible with any car adapter/car recharger you may already own for your electronic toys.7) When helping clear debris from my neighbour's yard, I was able to attach the Guide 10 to my daypack so that my cellphone's backup battery could continue charging without being left unattended on my front step.  I never thought I would use, or be able to use the loops on the Nomad7 for this. But I have and really appreciated it when I needed it.8) Because the unit is black in colour,  the battery charging did get very warm (borderline hot) to touch when in the sun, but tucking the battery behind a white handkerchief solved the overheating while in the sun problem.Overall recommended once its limitations and abilities are understood.
summary: Trickle charges your phone over 8-10 hours

reviewText: This Goal Zero "Adventure Kit" is perfect for gadget heavy campers! I have been interested in solar chargers for quite awhile, and this one covers all of the charging needs we have.What's Included:* Guide 10 Battery Pack; Use to charge 4x AA or AAA (with included adapter), has USB connector and built in LED light* Nomad 7 Solar Panel; has USB output and can charge the Guide 10 Battery Pack or power devices directly* Ultra Charge Solar Cord* 12V cigarette adapter; used to power device with Car Accessory plugs* AA rechargeable batteries (4 pack)* Manuals & WarrantyPros -+ Quality; these are well made components that will hold up while camping or hiking+ Power When You Need It; can charge directly from the Solar Panels or from the Battery Pack+ Powerful; tested both on a power hungry HTC EVO 4G and Kindle Fire+ Portable; the solar panels connect nicely to a backpack for use on the go+ Convenience; everything fits nicely into the mesh storage section of the Nomad 7Cons -+ No Power Status Indicator; would be nice to know how much juice is left in the battery pack, but this is a minor issueOverall, I am very impressed with this "Adventure Kit"!Highly Recommended!CFH
summary: Power On The Go - Highly Recommended

reviewText: There are usually a couple of good, solid manufacturers for products like these.  This gadget combines folding solar panels and a battery charger - in theory, it's multi-purpose:  charge the batteries (4 AA batteries, must be charged all at the same time) and then use that reserve to charge your devices.  The other purpose would be to plug in your device directly to the solar panel, and let the sun (almost) directly charge your stuff.  The latter didn't work for my mp3 player or my phone - probably just not enough power being supplied.With that said, this Goal Zero really takes portable solar to another level.  Products likeBrunton Restore 2 Solar Panels and 2200 mAh Batterydo roughly the same thing (and it's a bit smaller), but you're getting a lot less solar panel and one quarter the battery "backup" power for not much cost savings.  And this Goal Zero has all the options you'd want:  easy hanging strips, cigarette lighter adapter, and USB adapter.  Even the largerBrunton Solaris Foldable Solar Panelhas a price premium over this, has less options, and while lighter, I didn't factor that in very much. (If you're hiking with a solar panel, you're probably including electronic gadgets, so a few extra ounces likely isn't the most important aspect of your pack.)All in all, this is a great device, well designed, and great for emergencies and hiking where your legs and the sun provide the only power...Highly recommended.
summary: Finishing up where Brunton left off

reviewText: This is a nice compact solar panel with AA battery pack with attachment to charge AAA, plug in a USB, or 12v. Comes with four AA batteries. I have been charging on this for little over a month I have charged a kindle, an Ipad, lg cell phone, a portable fan and supplied batteries as well as other brands of NiMH. I really like it because it's small and can go anywhere. For maximum charging it must be angled with the sun, I usually prop it up anyway because I hide the things I am charging behind it to keep them from heating up. It will still charge from other angles but direct facing is the best. It charges up batteries in a few hours, great for hiking with gps, cell phones still don't reach some areas, so gps stand alone still important to me. Not having to carry lots of extra batteries is relief. I backpack multiple days out and every pound counts some times. I like the notes about charging are written on charger, can't get lost and with having lots of electric gadgets who green and red flashes mean different things it makes it easy to know where your batteries are in the charging stage. The mesh pocket on back is perfect to holds cords and battery pack and with this model keeps them out of the sun. My biggest concern is the small pin that runs from the charger to the battery pack, there is no way to keep stress off it while it's in the mesh bad, and your moving it around, during a hike etc, I worry that will break. I find I get a better stable charge through the battery pack then stand alone charge. Say for example, charging the LG cell phone, if the panel gets shaded, by the sun moving behind a tree or you walk with out your back facing the sun, it will not continue to charge, it beeps and sometimes has to be unplugged and re-plugged for the charging to continue, using the battery pack as a buffer it has no problems. I have first generation Ipad, it will charge it only if the Ipad is off. They put a small loop at every angle you could possibly need one, it's easy to clip it to things to hang. Really looking forward to see how long this thing will last, for as portable it is and how many ways you can hook into it, I really like it.Next generation I would like to see that pin strengthened. This is by no means a fast charger but portability is perfect.Comes withGuide 10 Battery PackNomad 7 Solar PanelUltra Charge Solar Cord12V cigarette adapterAA rechargeable batteries (4 pack)

summary: Nicest solar battery/device charger I've seen.

reviewText: I happen to own the older version of this product.  And now I have the newer version.There are some really great reasons to buy this version.1) It charges the iPad.  On a full charge, the Goal0 4 pack of batteries charged my iPad, the latest version with the retina display, 9%.  It cannot charge the iPad directly from the solar panel, but it can charge the iPad from the 4pack of batteries.  This is not a bad thing:  if you bought two Guide 10s, you could be charging the iPad with one, while the solar panel charged the 4 pack of batteries at the same time.  I also charged my old Original iPad (version 1) and the Goal0 4pack of batteries charged that iPad from a completely dead battery to 14%.  While neither 9% nor 14% are anywhere close to a full charge, it is good that they can charge the iPads.2) The panel has a storage pouch for both versions.  But the new version has a mesh pouch that is as big as one of the panels, so you can store several things in it, like, your ipad USB charger cable.  In the old version, the pouch was not big enough to do anything but to hold the guide10 battery pack.3) Improved instructions on the back of the guide10.  It now has estimates for charge times, which was missing on the old guide10.  Its a bit easier to read, too.Things I don't like:1) The battery pack gets extremely hot while the batteries are charging, even though I didn't leave it in the sun.  But it is very hot outside.  The instructions tell you that this is normal.2) I felt that the instructions should have been consolidated into one page.  Two different instruction sheets are provided:  one for the solar panel, and one for the battery pack.  When you read the solar panel instructions, it says it can't charge tablets, and this can be confusing.  I think a big improvement would be unified instructions.  In fact, I think the instructions could be on a laminated card and stuck into the mesh pouch, where they wouldn't take any space at all...3) You need to have all 4 batteries in the charger when you are doing some charging.  This would be something that would be easy for your buddy or your kid to forget, and, it means that if you are hiking (which I do) then you will actually have to carry 6 to 8 batteries with you if you want to use a device (like a GPS) while other batteries are charging.  The instructions point out that the batteries can be in any state of charge, so there has to be 4.  So, if you want to use a GPS which has 2 batteries, you would want to carry 6 batteries with you - 2 in the GPS and the other 4 in the charger.  When the two in the GPS run out of power, you would take two fresh ones out of the Guide 10 and put the depleted ones in.Things I like:1) It can charge just about anything if you are using the Guide10 battery pack as an intermediary.2) The battery pack charges no matter what position the power switch is in.  You don't have to worry about whether its set to off, or on.  Some products are possible to damage if you forget to turn them off before you charge them (sad but true) and the Goal0 is well designed so that this is not a problem.3) You can use any NiMH batteries.  I prefer to use EneloopsSanyo NEW 1500 eneloop 8 Pack AA Ni-MH Pre-Charged Rechargeable Batteriesbecause they don't lose power even over the course of a whole year.  Other rechargeable slowly lose power after they have been charged, and in a couple of months they can be dead even though you didn't use them.The charge time isn't too bad, about 3 hours was the average for me.Overall its a good product that does what its supposed to.
summary: Many improvements compared to the old version

reviewText: The Guide 10 Plus Adventure Kit may not get daily use, but when that need arises, this solar powered unit is invaluable.  I'm an avid birder/camper who usually travels alone to out-of-the-way places.  It gives me great comfort knowing I have solar power available to charge up a cell phone or GPS should life go awry.The compact unit consists of two pieces--the Nomad 7 solar panel and a Guide 10 Plus battery pack.  Solar power from the two panels can be achieved several ways, via the included battery pack or through the use of USB charging cables or a 12 volt car outlet cable, also included.  Most devices nowadays use USB cables, but before assuming this unit will work with whatever device you may have, please make certain.  If you cannot find that information out via Goal Zero's website, don't hesitate to call the company.  After reading useful comments they have posted after some Amazon reviews, I've no doubt phone representatives are just as helpful.I use this unit primarily one way, by attaching the solar panel to my backpack and charging up the battery pack during the course of a day's walk.  In the evening, the cell phone is then recharged from the battery pack.  There are, however, other ways to use the kit and other reasons consumers might want one.  We live in an area prone to power outages (ice storms come to mind).  The kit won't turn the heat back on, but it will power up gadgets during those type emergencies.  Rustic hunting camps might use this product just as I do, for peace-of-mind back-up should something go wrong.The Guide 10 Plus Adventure Kit is aptly named.  I want my outings to remain fun adventures, not potential life and death situations.  With this kit on board, I'm just a little more prepared for whatever comes my way.
summary: Getting Extra Juice The Solar-Powered Way

reviewText: Previously my teenage son had bought a different brand of solar charger to recharge his smart phone while camping for a week in the mountains with his scout group. His old charger was a big favorite with the other scouts as everyone could charge their phones and iPods without needing electricity. Now, he's completely blown away by this new Goal Zero charger we received to test out from the Amazon Vine program.For about the same price as our previous solar charger, the Goal Zero charging kit has about 4 times the solar gathering power. It comes in a back-packing friendly fold up cover, with handy loops so you can attach it in open position to your pack while you travel. My son was able to charge his phone while actively hiking. The goal zero charger pushes power out through standard USB and the smaller USB plugs, and it even comes with a car-type outlet, so that you can plug-in car-type 12 volt adapters. It also has a battery pack that can hold AA or AAA batteries so that you can charge those, too. The kit happens to come with AA, but you can substitute your own AAA if that's what you need. The whole kit weighs 1.6 pounds, but the solar charger with just the USB is about 1 pound if you don't need the rest. It's a very useful kit to own when you need maximum utility from a lighter-weight addition to your pack.

The first thing I did when I received this product was to label all the cords with id that they belong to this kit.  The USB cord looks like every other one you own, but is for charging the battery pack and I did not want to confuse it with my zillion other cords.  There is a nice zippered pouch for storing all these bits and pieces.I could not find any way to remove the "protective film", I believe that these panels did not actually have any film on them.  If they do, then they are working fine with the film on them.We live in New Mexico at 7300 feet altitude, and that that altitude we get some serious solar energy.  In fact the GoalZero Guide 10 Plus adventure kit was able to charge 4 Eneloop 1900mAh AA batteries from drained to full in 1.75 hours.  The slow green light (50 -80% was actually lit after 50 minutes)  It charged 900mAh batteries AAA from drained to full in about 45 minutes at midday, when laid flat on a cloudless day.Some devices will complain if they sense the charge is too low (notably Apple products), in that case you run the charge through the battery pack (while still being able to charge the batteries).We were able to charge (without sending the power through the battery pack) the following items on a sunny day in New Mexico.Kindle Keyboard2 kinds of Samsung phonesSansa clipBattery pack for a TI InspireCreative Zen mp3 playerTom Tom GPSUsing the battery pack we were able to charge an Ipod 4G.  I tried charging my ASUS laptop (one can dream, right?) by using the cigarette adapter and a plug I have for the car.  That was not successful.I also accidentally left the solar charging panels out in a rainstorm, and they still worked fine after drying out.  (I had the panels outside the patio door with the Kindle inside the house).  You do need to think about this, your device you are charging may not stand up to the rain as well.  The battery pack instructions state that you should "shield it from direct sunlight" and that "unexpected rain storms probably won't harm it".  I do wish the charging cable were a little longer so that shielding it would be easier.Overall, I love this product.  I love knowing  I will be able to charge my cell phone, the batteries for my nieces insulin pump and necessary items (like my Kindle!) even if the power is out for an extended amount of time.I am going to type up some info from the instructions, that might be useful in making a purchase decision and is not listed above in the Amazon page.  Everything below this is from the manuals.Nomad 7 (the solar panels)USB output port: Accepts any standard USB cable for charging USB devices.Solar Output Port: Charges Guide 10 battery pack faster than USB.Car adapter and 12V output port: Connect the car adapter (included) to charge small 12 V devices.*FAQ  from Nomad 7 (solar panel)What will my NOMAD 7 charge?The NOMAD 7 will directly charge most USB and 12 V devices (not tablets).Can I use the USB and 12V ports to charge devices simultaneously?Yes.  The Nomad 7 will split the incoming solar power between the two ports to charge devices simultaneously.  Some devices may not be compatible.Why am I having trouble charging my smart phone?Smart phones require very specific, consistent input.  If your NOMAD 7 is angle perfectly, there should'nt be an issue.  However, most charging issues with a smart phone are made simpler by incorporating a Goal Zero power pack as an intermediary (such as Guide 10 Plus) (*note, this is the battery pack).Is the Nomad 7 waterproof?The nomad 7 is weather resistant and will not be harmed if exposed to rain or snow.What kind of solar cells do you use in the Nomad 7?We use state of the art monocrystalline technology in the Nomad 7 because it delivers more power per square inch than any other solar technology on the market.Can the Nomad 7 be chained with other devices?No.*FROM THE FAQ for the Guide 10 plus (the battery pack)What batteries can be used?Any AA or AAA NiMH can be sued and recharged, we do not recommend other types of batteries.  4 same sized batteries MUST be charged at once, but not all batteries need to be empty.How do I charge?From solar: use GOAL ZERO Nomad 3.5 or Nomad 7 with solar charge cable for fast charging.From USB: Use any USB power source, such as computer or and GOAL ZERO power pack.Is it waterproof?No, but it is weather resistant.  Care should be taken to shield it from direct sunlight and the elements.  Unexpected rain storms probably won't harm it.How is it protected? Usage is plug and play.  The built in battery management system prevents overcharge and over discharging of batteries.  The USB output will only supply the amount of power needed.
summary: Love it!  Well designed, feels solid, has everything you need.

reviewText: ...but I suppose some people do.  (Paper maps may be archaic, but they're certainly lighter!). If you do, though, this works extremely well to provide power when you're off the grid.  The solar cells charge the batteries fairly quickly and the batteries have enough oomph to charge my iPad.  Keeping the solar cells in sunlight help prevent the batteries from discharging.(Actually, I have to confess...I'm using this at home.  There's something viscerally satisfying about powering things from the sun and sticking it to PG&E.;  I guess I'm a bit of an anarchist at heart.)Highly recommended.
summary: I can't imagine taking my iPad backpacking...

reviewText: This is our 3rd B&D; cordless landscape tool having previously purchased the Alligator Lopper and Chain Saw. Enough said! So on to the "pros/cons" as I see it:Pros:1- cordless tools are lightweight [important!] making them much easier to use.2- batteries last a reasonable length of time [good excuse for "break time"] and even longer if you buy extra batteries and keep them charged [no "break time"]!3- you no longer have to be concerned about electrocuting yourself when you accidentally lop, chop or saw the darn cords!4- vs gas powered... no brainer between the weight of the gas engine and trying to fill an infinitesimal gas tank well you get it.Cons:1- batteries are pricey2- run time is usually about 15-20 mins - but then as I said before..."break time" excuse!My thoughts, if your over 40 do yourself a favor and try these lightweight cordless tools...if your under 40 go ahead and build those muscles up using the heavy gas powered tools!
summary: B&D Did It Again- Great Item

reviewText: Pricing on Amazon can vary greatly for the same product at different times.  Now seems to be a great time for lawn care and tool pricing.Do the math before you assume the 3-pc combo is the way to go.  When we bought the B&D; 20v Cordless pieces, we did it as a trimmer/edger and sweeper duo (comes with a charger and two batteries) and the 22in. trimmer separately with a charger and battery.  The sum total was $10.00 less than this 3-pc combo of these B&D; pieces, which includes just ONE charger and TWO batteries.Not only did we spend $10.00 less buying it that way, it gave us THREE batteries and TWO chargers (a battery and charger go for about $40 separately).  Since we already have the two chargers and three batteries, we then bought the "bare tool" 20v Pole Trimmer WITHOUT battery & charger, and saved a bundle ($50.00).  Can't see that we'd ever run through all three batteries and want for more in a day.Quiet, light and efficient for our city lawn.  It's nice that we don't blast the neighbors with noise, but the primary reason we chose these tools was the ease of use; no gas/oil and no cord.  We'll give it a couple years and see if we ever reach for our corded tools again... pretty sure we'll end up giving those away!Also have a B&D; battery-operated lawn mower.  LOVE IT!!  Has already paid for itself in place of hired yard care.
summary: Measure COSTS twice, Get More, PAY LESS

reviewText: I bought this to trim my overgrown hedges. And it didn't hesitate even an instant to cut even the large branches. Actually my petite wife was the one to do the trimming much to my surprise. She couldn't wait to test it.  But the main reason I purchased this particular one was that it uses Black and Decker's interchangeable 20 Volt lithium batteries I've standardized upon recently.  I am almost to my goal of being becoming 100% standardized on Black & Decker's 20 volt lithium battery powered tools.I strongly recommend Black and Decker's series of tools that use 20 volt lithium battery.  But be aware that there are three different 20 volt batteries. One to avoid if possible is the 22 Watt Hour battery.  Get the 30 Watt Hour battery that is almost the same price.  And there is the double sized Black & Decker LB2X4020-OPE battery for about 50% higher price.  But there is an advantage of having multiple 30 Watt Hour batteries.  You can be charging one while using another battery.  You have a choice of buying several tools without the battery for better economy.
summary: Works Just As Well As A Electric Powered

reviewText: This is a great hedge trimmer for my needs.  The portability provided by the battery power is very handy, and it has good power.  I have used it to trim bushes as well as edge my grass along the patio.  Light weight, relatively quiet, and makes quick work of bush trimming.  If only it would pick up the trimmings. :-)

I own four of the Black & Decker 20V Lithium-Ion battery line of products. They are great for a small yard. I just recently used this hedge trimmer and the pole hedge trimmer together for the first time. My yard is small, but I think I have a relatively sizable amount of shrubs and hedges to trim. The trimmer itself worked great. The only issue is that it took me 2.5 batteries to do all of the hedge trimming in my yard. For me it's no problem, because I have four of the batteries, but if you aren't going to be in that situation this could be an issue for you.I would not recommend buying this product if you don't have either a) multiple B&D; 20V products and therefore multiple batteries or b) the intention to buy one or two backup batteries. If you do not intend to do either of these things and have a good amount of hedge-trimming to do, this product will probably drive you mad. Once the battery is dead, it basically needs to recharge overnight again before it is ready.Pros:Light, works just as well as plug-in models. Cordless is great.Cons:The single battery provided with this trimmer is just not adequate for large hedge-trimming jobs.
summary: Great Trimmer, But Beware Battery Life

reviewText: Am astounded how well this hedge trimmer operates.  Best than any others I have used, electric or gas!  Battery pack from my Black and Decker leaf blower also fits this tool.

I had cut down several dozen trees (mostly saplings but some large ones) with a chain saw on part of our property and the stumps keep sending up masses of sprouts. This area also has a lot of viney briars. I tried using a Round-Up type of product on both of these but it has had little or no effect, and loppers take too long, so I got this and it works great. It slices through them quickly and easily.I also volunteer to maintain a local hiking trail 4 times a year. I've always used loppers to cut small limbs back from the trail, but last time I used this trimmer. The trail is 3 miles long, up and down hills, and this trimmer was light enough to carry easily. And most of the time I didn't even have to stop walking when cutting through bunches of small limbs/sprouts. It took about an hour to do the trail and the battery lasted the whole way.When I first looked at this on Amazon, they were saying that to get it without a battery could take up to 4 months, so I got it on eBay for a few dollars more. Now I see that Amazon already has it in stock. I had recently bought a B&D; drill which came with the same battery and charger, so I didn't think I needed another battery. I can use it quite a while before the battery runs down, but even when I run it nearly all the way down, it takes very little time to charge.I have a Worx JawSaw which uses a similar (but different) 20-volt lithium battery. I often use them both on the same trip to the yard. When charging them both afterwards, the B&D; battery is done long before the Worx battery is.The only con is that it makes ragged cuts when pruning small limbs off of trees and it's hard to get the cut close enough to the trunks, so I'll continue to use loppers for that, but that's not what I got this for anyway.

I REALLY LIKE THESE 20 VOLT TOOLS AND AM CHANGING OVER TO THEM AS THE OLD ONES GO BELLY UP. THE BATTERIES HOLD A CHARGE SO MUCH LONGER AND KEEP THE POWER UP WHILE IN USE EVEN IN THE WINTER WHEN IT IS COLD IN THE GARAGE.
The steel blades rust very fast, like less than a 2 months stored in a garage. Still cuts ok, but I imagine rusty blades will dull fast.
this item is great to gather up leaves and trash in your yard. and it is easier than raking them and a whole lot faster

Okay, but only for light jobs I use it to keep the steps and sidewalks clean.It is much easier than sweeping.The battery is the same kind I have from my weed trimmer, so I have 3 bats in totalThe ones from the trimmer are great and hold a charge for enough time to do a large block 1/2 hr of property (in NY ) but the one that came with this unit is a bust.If I did not have the other bats I would send it back.The unit is quiet but effective but a little disappointing.However,I am keeping it for light jobs.I wonder if it will blow away some light snow? I hate shoveling snow.

I have several other B&D; products that use the same battery. Many complain about the short working times between charges, which is true. But since the tools work about as expected, the battery issues is not a big deal to me.The blower itself works fine.
Not as hard as some folks in Washington of coarse. But almost gets to the level of an Obama speech

This little cordless blower does a good job in beds and on the driveway with DRY leaves.  The battery time is OK, not great, but I always have an 18V battery being charged since I used a whole slew of B&D 18V tools.  No, this is does not have the same cyclonic power of my Toro, but for a cordless blower, it does the job without the weight and noise of a gas or corded blower.
Not as powerful as my electric one, but I dont have to cart a cord around the yard to clean up. I love it

After reading reviews I thought I had made a big mistake. Now the blowing power could be better for what I'm using it for as clumps of grass are left behind after mowing. Next to a unit used by the lawn service this doesn't blow but is ten times quieter and much lighter. Have zoysia grass, it's thick and much like think carpet. I follow the track of grass clipping with the blower and it spreads them around so no mounds are left. As for sweeping the patio is does a good job and furniture doesn't need to be moved. The biggest surprise was the time one battery lasted, on a full charge I finished everything even sweep the garage out. Not prefect but for the money it was worth it.

"Elementary my dear Watson, if your men don't have proper tools."Sherlock HolmesVery little is worse or more frustrating than trying to do a job with the wrong tool; trying to force a tool to do something it was not meant to do is a sure set-up for failure, or at the very least, turning out a very sloppy product. Using the wrong tool can make your life much more difficult than it need be.  Sherlock was correct in the wisdom he passed on to Doctor Watson.We live in the woods.  Our home is surrounded by around 100 gigantic oak trees and other lesser trees beyond count.  Leaves we have.  We also have guttering around our home.  Guttering that is in constant need of cleaning we have.Enter this wonderful little leaf blower.Of all the job around the house, yard and garden (we live of five acres) cleaning gutters, for me, is the most loathsome.  I really, really hate it.  The gutters though must be cleaned.  Overflowing gutters can cause great damage to your home, an if the overflowing water washes out your wife's flower gardens...well, life can be pretty miserable.  Now I am no spring chicken let me tell you, and climbing around the roof at least three times a year is a true pain.  I have very powerful gas leaf blowers.  These things are heavy and they are noisy.  An electric leaf blower with a cord is not an option.  Our home is not small and I would need hundreds of feet of cord to do the job.This little battery leaf blower has made my life so much better.  It is not the most powerful blower in the world and I most certainly would not recommend it for large acre yards with a lot of trees.  It simply does not have the power to get the job done. (I have a large lawn tractor with a very, very large raking contraption I pull around to do the yard with.)  But for the gutters this little machine is just perfect.  It is light, weighing only 3.7 pounds.  It is easy to maneuver and is very quiet.  It is powerful enough to remove the leaves that gather in the gutters and it has a nifty little scraper on the end of the blowing tube which is ideal to scrap up and loosen leaves that have become impacted.I use this when the leaves are completely dry.  Oak trees also have little seed things which look like fuzzy worms in the spring time which also gather in the gutters.  I wait for dry days to remove those also.  Once charge of the battery is adequate to do the guttering so there is no running up and down the latter.  The machine is small and light enough that it does not interfere with my balance all that much and I do not feel like I have climbed a mountain our two after using it.I also use this thing on our driveway and our patios.  It does an adequate job.  It is Not powerful enough for heavy yard work though.While I do not use this thing for extended periods of time and only use it two or three times per year, it was well worth every cent I spent on it and it sure works better than the five or six gas powered blowers which are broken and collecting dust in my barn.For the specific job I use this for it is just about perfect.  Keep in mind that I am not what you would call a big fan of Black & Decker product, but in this case they did well.Don BlankenshipThe Ozarks
summary: SHERLOCK HOLMES KNEW OF WHAT HE SPOKE.  Love this little blower for what I use it for.

reviewText: The blower is great. Assembly is simple. Just put the two pieces of the nozzle together, attach to the main unit, then attach the battery pack after it finishes charging.Taking the battery pack on and off is simple and effortless. It is lightweight, easy to hold and maneuver, and feels well balanced even with the battery pack on. And I love the convenience of not having an electric cord

I bought this sweeper for the express purpose of cleaning grass clippings and dirt from my driveway and gutter after mowing and edging my lawn.  Gutter is about 75 feet long and the driveway is about 25x60 feet.  For that use, it's perfect.  I used it for the first time this morning and it gave a good account of itself.  Lots of forceful air movement (for its size) and the battery lasted for the entire job, about 10-15 minutes.  Can't tell how much battery life was left -- lithium-ion batteries go with full power until they just quit (but if you pay close attention, the tool/battery will slow down slightly during the final minute).Anyway, this is perfect for light cleaning on a hard surface, which is all I need it for.  Ergonomics are good, too: small, good air movement, light weight, easy to hold and maneuver, and relatively quiet. The LBXR20 battery is inexpensive, too, which is a pleasant suprise for a Black & Decker lithium-ion battery.If you're not looking for a heavy-duty blower (think moving piles of leaves around on your lawn in the Fall), and 2-cycle gas engines or dragging around a cord are not your thing, take a look at this sweeper.  I was prepared to be disappointed but I'm not.

I have had this product on my wish list and my wife got it for my birthday. I have a very long driveway, and a large deck and lot of trees around my home. This thing works perfectly for cleaning off my deck, garage and driveway of tree debris that accumulates constantly. I'm not a fan of gas blowers and a corded one would not have enough reach and be a pain to use. I haven't used it more than 10 minutes at a time so I can't speak for battery life. I do know with the included charger it takes a while to charge the battery.It's not the most powerful blower but certainly powerful enough to get the job done, and extremely light an convenient. I plan on getting a couple of other Black and decker tools that go with this battery.

Got refurbished from Country Butler and it is GREAT. I have two of these, one for home and one for work. Both work great, have no issues, and use the same batteries as all of our other Black and Decker 20V items (weed eater, hedge trimmer).
summary: Got refurbished from Country Butler and it is GREAT

reviewText: I already own a powerful electric blower and an even more powerful gas blower that can blow heavy piles of leaves in the fall. However, when I had a new patio installed this summer, I wanted a lightweight cordless blower where I didn't have to worry about the electrical cord getting wrapped around the legs of my patio tables and chairs. After some research I purchased this unit and am glad that I did. Here is why I like this.1. Assembly is simple. Just put the two pieces of the nozzle together, attach to the main unit, then attach the battery pack after it finishes charging. A green light blinks during the charging process and turns solid green when charging is complete. You can leave the battery in the charger after charging is complete without harming the battery, so that way you always have a fully charged battery. Taking the battery pack on and off is simple and effortless.2. This is relatively lightweight, easy to hold and maneuver, and feels well balanced even with the battery pack on.
