And I love the convenience of not having an electric cord.3. Of course this does not have the same power as a gas or electric blower. But for my patio it is perfect. Ditto for my driveway. Neither has large accumulations of leaves or dirt, so this unit is just perfect. However for fall cleanup of lots of leaves on your lawn, this is not the unit to use.4. My typical cleanup lasts under 15 minutes, and this unit has plenty of power during that entire time. I have not tested how long the battery will last on a single charge.Bottom line: This unit works well for light duty use to clean leaves and debris off patios and driveways. For your lawn and extended usage times get something else.Update October 18, 2012: Fall is in full swing in New Jersey and the leaves are coming down. This product has been an effortless way for me to clear the leaves off my front walkway, driveway, and patio.Update May 13, 2013: Each spring lots of "stuff" (not leaves) falls down from all the trees on my property and makes a mess of my patio and driveway. This product is great for quickly cleaning it up. It's especially convenient to just aim this at my patio furniture or the cars in my driveway and blow off all the debris.Also, I had forgotten to remove the battery and charge it after the last time I used this product over six months ago in the fall to clean up leaves. Guess what? It started up just fine, though not surprisingly I ran out of a charge after about ten minutes. From now on I make sure to just leave the battery in the charger when I am done.

I bought this since it's compatible with other B&D products that use the same battery. It doesn't blow hard enough though, and only has 1 fan speed. The battery also barely last long enough to 15 minutes of blowing. I will say it's nice and quiet compared to other electric and gas blowers I've used.
summary: Doesn't blow hard enough and battery has poor life

reviewText: Good:Light weight. Handle and length are both adjustable. This could be used comfortably by anyone between 4'10" and 6'5" without any problems.Good battery. I see a lot of complaints about the battery, but I can trim around my 1/2 acre lot (half fenced), several trees, long driveway on one charge with no problems. I don't know how long the battery lasts, because I've never run out. It takes me about 30-40 minutes to trim.Solidly built. My last trimmer was a Toro and it literally fell apart. This is laight weight with many plastic parts, but it feels solid, and I believe it will last a long time.Power. I keep the trimmer on 2-3 by default, and this eats through nearly everything. At full speed it can eat through bricks without a problem. If you like bricks, don't use it at full speed.Charger. It charges in about an hour, doesn't get hot, and doesn't smell. It also doesn't start house fires or make noise. I can't think of anything else good to say about the charger.Bad:It just won't feed line. I've used it a half dozen times now, and I still have to turn it off, take out the battery, pull the feed forward, and put it back together. But, you know what? This is still better than the "bump and pray" method my old trimmer had.If this thing would feed the trim string at all, I'd give it five stars.

This is a great product. I had a previous battery operated by B&D but it did not have the power of this one. I love being able to adjust the power depending on what I'm cutting. It is light weight and adjustable length which is nice. The battery pack is great assets to the trimmer.

Though very satisfied with my first purchase of a battery B&D; 20 volt lithium trimmer two years ago, I found two fully charged batteries barely were up to the task during peak season; granted a medium plus sized lawn.Pros: slightly larger cutting swath, nearly double the run time of course, variable power selection to enhance battery life, better head rotation design for edging, a battery pack with a capacity guage, and FAST charging.Cons: slightly heavier, more expensive, fewer alternate 36 volt products compared to the 20 volt so far, only one battery.Conclusion: for medium sized lawns or moderate plus trimming needs, NO more gas trimmer!
summary: battery capacity and charging greatly improved

reviewText: This little trimmer really eats up the weeds and tall grass.  Much better than any other cordless trimmer that I've tried.  Battery life is above average and charging is fast.  I do have the B&D Blower that uses the same battery so I have a back up should I need it.  I'll edit this review and add to it after I've had the opportunity to use it longer but so far, I am very pleased with the product.
has lots of power, which is controllable by a switch and am very happy with this product so far....I bought an extra battery and that makes sure I get the whole acre cut.

This just keeps going and going.  Bought this for my father who had been running a corded electric for many years and he is very very happy with it.  He has 1/2 acre of land that is very landscaped and this will last the entire time.  Fairly quiet and lightweight and power settings adjustment is nice for only small items vs big weeds.

I've never used a string trimmer before.  This one is surprisingly easy to use and made short work of cleaning the weeds out of my ground cover.  Though my arms were sore the next day from toting it around, it was better than a sore back from bending over to pull weeds.  The battery life is decent.  I ran it for probably an hour before it needed recharged.  So nice not to be tethered to a cord.  I remember the old tap-to-feed models and it's great to have self feeding string.  Overall, it suits my purposes for light use just perfectly!
summary: Where have you been all my life?

reviewText: This is one great weedeater. I have gotten to the point where i just cant stand cords anymore.  I hate the tangles mess and the time it takes to get all setup to do a project with the corded tool.This tool has litium ion which holds a charge a long time and has a built in led power guage to let you know when it needs charged.I had a long move and had this in storage for three months. Thinking I would have to recharge for use I pushed the guage button and all four led's lit up letting me know it was still at full charge. That was impressive.Nice and lightweight as well. The variable speed is cool and will allow you to use as much or as little power as needed for your job instead of high power for everything.Recommended
summary: Light And Powerful Cordless To Attack Your Weeds And Not Trip Over That Cord

reviewText: I love the luxury of professional gardeners.  Still, I couldn't get myself to pay $70 a pop for them to do a bit of pruning and minor grass trimming.On background, I hate yard work and the hot summer sun isn't my thing.  Top that with, I've never cut grass in my life.  I had to weigh my frugality with my inexperience and loathing of sweat.  I'm glad I picked frugality.MY FIRST DAY OF USENight before: charged battery7:45 AM - 7:55 AMPutting this trimmer together was a piece of cake.  Two snap/screw on pieces and it was done.  The battery and charger were like any other.  In fact, Black and Decker says you can leave the battery in the charger even after it's fully charged.8:00 AM - 8:30 AMClothed in tall rubber galoshes, long pants and a windbreaker, I headed out to the yard.  I tried the edger first.  A little experience will go a long way in the future: managed to make one small bald spot, but otherwise not bad.  Edging grass isn't much harder than vacuuming.  Next, tried the trimmer.  Again, a little experience will go a long way.  Let's just say the trimming looks much more natural than with a lawn mower and with more organic shape to it.  (Probably true for all line trimmers v. lawn mowers) My yard is small.  We have one area that's about 12' x 20', one that's about 12' x 12' and a long stretch of approximately 35' x 4'.  Anyhow, after a half hour I was done.  I was going to vacuum / mulch the cuttings, but the cuttings were so fine, I'm tempted to just leave it to mulch as is.  Anyhow 1/2 hour and it's done.  I give this tool 5 stars.REFLECTION:If you have enough yard, this probably isn't the tool.  For many modern urban yards though, this will do.  I had the strength setting at halfway, and the battery was still fully charged (all lights lit) when I finished.  The power was fine.  I felt no need to up it to a higher strength.  Anyhow, now I need to head to the store, get a nice cold beer and congratulate myself on a job well done.  And it's not even 9 am yet.

It worked so well for about six months but unfortunately as many others have already reported there is a definite battery issue.  Black & Decker confirms there was a large batch of faulty batteries (LBXR36) that got released.  I purchased this from Amazon and they were the seller of this product.  However, even Amazon will no longer sell, warranty or even discuss this poor product.  I'm trying now (with little success so far) to get Black & Decker to honor the supposed 3 yr. warranty on this battery, but so far I've been treated with little more than an honorable ignorance.  If I don't hear from them soon this will sadly be my last Black & Decker product.  I would avoid this product folks.
summary: Battery died in less than 6 months as others are reporting

reviewText: Cordless tools have made a massive leap in the past few years, and this Black and Decker cordless string trimmer is just exactly ready for prime time. Lithium ion batteries and effecient electric motors are the leap that have made these tools possible. A few years ago drills that work all day and are as powerful as a corded version were a dream. Today they are a reality.This string trimmer is outstanding. The trimmer, on low power setting and a full charge, will run for around an hour. On the highest power setting, 6, it will trim for about 20 minutes. There is more than enough power to edge along a sidewalk and cut through normal suburban lawn trimming. On a single charge I was able to trim my entire yard and edge the sidewalk and driveway that hadn't been edged for over three years (a total of about 200 linear feet of edging) - I used 100% of the charge. The next trimming won't even nick the battery.Assembly is fairly simple, attach the string guard, the handle, and snap the battery on. A philips head screw driver is required to attach the string guard. The battery charger is a bit on the cheap side. I'm used to my Makita monster XLT battery charger that tells me everything in the world about the battery charging. This Black and Decker has a very dim LED that flashes green or red depending on the battery state. Sadly that dim lamp is not visible at all in dailight.Battery charging takes about 2 hours for a fully flat battery. There is a four LED charge level indicator on the battery pack that is surprisingly accurate. The battery is nowhere near as beefy as I expected. With 36V on tap, I figured this would be a heavy battery. It is surprisingly light. My drill batteries are heavier.The trimmer has an extension control - the wand telescopes. I'm 6 foot 2 and fully extended the trimmer was comfortable to use. The weight of the battery and motor are well balanced, the trimmer feels really good in my hand.The trimmer head rotates 90 degrees to make sidewalk trimming easier. With the press of one button and a twist, the head rotates. This is amazingly easy to do. They also included a sturdy metal guide that flips down and can follow the edge of the sidewalk. This guide makes it very easy to trim a sidewalk.The string autofeeds, so there is no need to bump the trimmer on the ground. In fact I would recommend trying to not touch the string cartridge on the ground at all, the cap is not exactly super sturdy. I'm not sure I really like the autofeed function. It seemed to take a while for fresh string to feed as I was on purpose wearing the string out quickly on concrete. The trimmer uses standard 0.065 inch string. The instruction sheet shows how to wind your own cartridge, but has two paragraphs above it on why that's a bad idea.The trimmer has a really good feel and weight to it. I wish it went to 11, it would be so much more powerful. Most importantly what does this trimmer compete with? Gas powered trimmers are all hard to start, stinky, noisy, hot, expensive, and dangerous. Corded trimmers are nice, but that darn long extension cord has to follow me all over the place, I hate that, and the weight of the cord to drag around. I guess hand trimmers are the next best alternative, they are super green. But my hands get very tired after 10 minutes of using them.A good price, good power, quiet operation, and well balanced; I love this trimmer.This Is Spinal Tap - but does it go to 11?
summary: No More Gas, No Cord, but it doesn't go to 11

reviewText: Black And Decker back on track to Great Quality Trimmers. I was alittle skeptical but have seen Black and Decker products start to go back up in quality over the last few years (ie drills, blowers etc). This trimmer was plenty powerful. Have a corner lot and it worked like a charm. I was surprised how well the edger worked( tip: if have not edged in months, pay someone a few bucks to edge it first professionally). I plan to keep up the edging and may even spray grass killer like Roundup along sidewalks so don't have to edge at all. I bought an extra battery but did not need to use it. Tip: read owners manual for good tips on conserving battery and trimming tips.It helped. Also, I was able to trimmer on power setting 2 or 3 the entire time even on high weeds, only turned up to 6 power setting to edge.Highly recommend. Much better than the Toro Electric trimmer I had bought awhile back and returned the Toro trimmer.
summary: Black And Decker back on track to Great Quality Trimmers

reviewText: This is my first battery operated trimmer and I am impressed. I previously had a plug in one which was quiet but lacked power and of course had the cord to drag around. I upgraded to a gas powered model a few years ago, which gave me power and no cord, but came with the cost of being hard starting, loud, smelly, and a lot of arm numbing vibration. The LST136 is the best of both models, without the drawbacks.Out of the box it is light weight and easy to assemble. Just attach the handle and grass guard and the unit is good to go, along iwht of course the obligatory battery charge. Build quality seems good and it is lighter then my gas model which it achieves by being mostly thick plastic and by not having the motor.It is much quieter then the gas model and I don't need to wear ear muffs anymore with it. Comparable noise to the plug in but of course no cord to drag around. Power is very good and I had it set at the 3 out of 6 setting. There wasn't anything in my yard the 3 didn't blast through. I probably could have turned it down to the 1 or 2 setting for most work around the house. I did turn it up to 6 just to see what was in reserve and again it was much faster then I would need out in the lawn. Also fought off getting jambed in the long grass along a chain link fence much better then my gas model. (The LST136 bogged down only once and was easily cleared, my fault for thrusting it into to much high grass)I ended up getting about 15-20 minutes of runtime out of the unit while on 3. Did the house, detached garage, swing set, 100+ feet of chain link fence, and a raised garden. It wasn't dead yet at that time but all the bars on the battery indicator were out by then. Again I could have run most of the yard at the 1 or 2 setting and likely gotten more run time out of it. I think 30 minutes is doable.My biggest single thumbs up goes to the huge reduction in vibration over a gas trimmer. My arms and shoulders never got numb and painful like they do near the end of my yard while using a gas model. I'm not a little person by any means at 6'3" 210 lbs, but the vibration issue (or lack there of) is a huge postive to this unit.I didn't encounter anything I would consider to be a negative. The two biggest things I will watch going forward are the battery where I am hopeful the lithium model will last for years as most I have gotten with other items do much better then the ni-cd or ni-mh of a few years ago. Also will have to see how the trimmer cord replacement goes. Right now the "auto" feed feature is working like a charm and I like it better then the old bump the bottom method.Very pleased and impressed with the unit and will be doing more trimming this year due to its ease of use and comfort factor.Update: Stored the battery in an unheated garage over the winter. Numerous sub-zero days. Didn't seem to faze it and it worked and charged up well.
summary: good power and run time, very little vibration compared to gas trimmer

reviewText: OK I've had a dual string corded Ryobi for about 20-25 years that was rewindable by hand and whacked through anything.  I did not expect this B&D; to be that powerful, but it is mainly for my wife's use and light and easy to control.  It meets expectations while feeling a bit weak, but seems to chop through everything we've asked so far.Two concerns however:1.  It does seem to go through string a lot faster than expected.  I've used it once and my wife once, and already I'm ordering more cartridges.  I will also order bulk line to see how that works.2.  Instructions say not to store the battery at over 80F!  Ambient in Texas is higher than that more than half the year!  Does that mean I can't use it if it's more than 80 outside?  The battery replacement is $80, so if I have to replace it each year, I would have been better to buy a couple of lower priced trimmers.Operation:That said, it does seem to cut through big 4-o'clocks and little oak tree upshoots fairly well and breezes over grass.  No problem running out of battery yet, but haven't used it more than half an hour at a time.  I will not be using this as an edger, so there will seldom be that much of a load on it.  Doubt it will outlast the Ryobi, but if it keeps the wife happy, that's all that's important.  Sheis happy so far.
summary: good some ways, not so good others...

reviewText: The trimmer is easy to use, and despite warnings against working it too hard, I was able to establish the initial line near the sidewalk pretty easily.  But it did use lots of line in the process!  Now that I use it just to trim up, I can also use the battery to complete the job with the B&D blower too!
summary: Pretty good, but it doesn't hold much string.

reviewText: This year we decided to save some money by doing our own lawn care after our service provider went out of the business. After reading numerous reviews, I opted to try out a cordless string trimmer for the first time. Can't believe I waited this long!As a middle aged female who knows zilch about tools, I've used a trimmer exactly 1x before. The first time was a disaster as I didn't know there were speeds. I hated the smell, smoke, difficulty priming, maintenance and nearly everything else about the entire experience. All said and done, that was the first...and as far as I was concerned...last time.However, I actually enjoy working in the yard so someone told me to try a cordless model since it doesn't have the same maintenance, start-up routine etc...all I can say is WOW! Basically you hold a button and it's off and running. I went to try it out and did the entire yard. Recharge is fast. Weight is comfortable. Powerful enough to do anything I wanted.This is for the 40V version.
summary: Can't believe I waited so long!

reviewText: I received my first Black & Decker corded lawn tool for Christmas about twelve years ago. I've been gas free ever since. I'll be the first to say that switching up to cordless products has had its moments. My only complaint with cordless B&D; lawn products is the battery life. The only reason besides my expanded B&D; lawn tool collection, that I stayed with these guys is the company's outstanding customer service. They are one of the very few companies that back up their products. The crew that mans B&D;'s toll free customer support number are simply outstanding. Moving on, after a two week test run these are my thoughts on the new B&D; LST 136.After a quick inventory, (trimmer, instructions, (1) 36v lithium battery, (1) string spool, three year warranty and a charger) I scanned over the easy to read instructions. Like my last two B&D; trimmers, all I needed was a philips head screwdriver to attach the debris shield. Out of the box, I charged the battery for about three hours. The battery is sweet. Its outfitted with an on board LED power usage meter. The charger is the typical basic no frills, no thrills B&D; charger. Unlike older models it only accepts 36 volt lithium batteries. Before getting started I sprayed the undercarriage and shield with a non stick cooking spray. This will definitely make clean up easier.Now for the test. Even with the battery I found this trimmer to be light weight. The handle has a good ergonomic feel to it. The trigger configuration hasn't changed. A big selling point for this model is the telescoping height extension. Adjustment is easy. Unlike earlier models, this trimmer is outfitted with a thumb dialed power control. From 1 (lowest) to 6 (highest), I was able to easily increase or decrease the head rotation. On the first week I chose the lowest setting (1) and was surprised that I was able to trim all of the front yard and half of the back yard area before I noticed a significant power drop off. I used my older trimmer to complete the job. A week later I trimmed the front yard first on the highest setting (6). I was barely able to finish the job before the battery was exhausted. I got maybe 15-20 minutes. A second battery would have helped the cause tremendously.The 13" trim path is a definite step up from older models. Trimming wise, this model operates smoothly without any hiccups. It does a great job of getting under bushes and around the fence line. The metal guard for edging has stayed much the same design as the original model. Like my older B&D; trimmers, the LST 136 Trimmer does an okay job of edging but won't be replacing my electric edger any time soon. I think most users will agree, the auto line feed system is sweet. Its much nicer then the old bump and feed system. Spools can easily be changed out by using the side snaps on the cap head. On average I found myself using about four of the 30' line spools a year on my older trimmer. Only time will tell if that number drops with this new model. After each use, I clean the unit and coat the undercarriage with non stick cooking oil. Its a good idea to keep the line cutting blade oiled too. Like my other trimmers, I recommend sharpening the blade about once every three months.Overall, I'm quite impressed with the Black & Decker LST 136 trimmer. Its a powerful, quiet, gas free option that will get the job done. With proper maintenance it will last a long time. The only real shortcoming I find with this product, is that for larger yards more then one battery is needed. I do hope the folks at Black & Decker see the light. Still, this trimmer is a workhorse. I recommend it.

This weed whacker cuts through thick and tall grass as well as a gas-powered device; there's no hesitation.  The difference is that it doesn't smell awful.  I really like that you can stop and start so easily as well.The battery lasts for about 20 minutes, so if you have a lot of whacking to do, you'll need two batteries.  The good news is that the battery charges relatively quickly: about an hour from empty to full.Had my original unit worked well, I would have given this device five stars.  But, my first one died within a week (probably 2 hours use in total).  There was a slight smell of something burning and then it totally stopped working.  Amazon replaced it very quickly, and the second unit seems to be working perfectly.

The best part of this unit is the battery. I have lots of curved areas, stone walls, walkways and more which require use of a string trimmer - the battery lasts long enough to get through all of it, and not needing to move an electric cord around has dramatically reduced the time I spend doing the work.However, the unit itself is poorly designed and unwieldy. I wish I never bought it.The "auto feed" does not work, period. Previous (corded) units allowed me to gently hover above the grass or rest the spinning piece on the ground to cut all grass an even height. Not this unit. The options seem to be either 1. Hover and cut nothing, or, 2. Cut everything down to the soil level.Moving along the ground the guard frequently catches and sends the spinning string toward the ground, hacking bald spots into the lawn.There must be other, better units out there. Avoid this one.
summary: Battery is fine, the rest is the problem

reviewText: I own a lot of cordless tools and used to own theBlack & Decker NST2118 12-Inch 18-Volt Ni-Cd Cordless Electric GrassHog String Trimmer/Edger.  This is an excellent replacement.  The 36 volt battery gives a ton of energy to get this thing running strong and it lasts for hours of use (even when left on the 6 setting).I really like the battery gauge (you push a button on the battery and it lights up telling you how much energy is left).  No more wondering if you need to charge before starting out!The trimmer gives you a 0-6 speed setting.  I didn't find this very useful and ended up just using 6 all the time.I also didn't really love the string advance system.  It didn't always work.  It is a no-bump system that is supposed to automatically advance the string.  I found that it didn't always work and I sometimes found myself trimming with a two inch string!It is well balanced, but a tiny bit heavier than my old 18 volt model.So, I give this four stars (not five) because of the string advance system.  It is well powered (easily as powerful as any gas or corded model) and well balanced.
summary: Really strong, but did't like the automatic string advance system

reviewText: I've been using this for approximately 5 weeks now.  As a baseline, I am coming from using a pair of Homelite 2-Stroke trimmers for 20 years. These Gas trimmers were straight shaft, dual .80 lines. They started reasonably well despite some occasional flooding.  But it was always somewhat of a "Special Effort" to use them, an effort that made me tend to skip a week.This 36V BD is just "push the botton and go". It is so easy to use, that I may pick it up anytime during the week...even when I am not specifically mowing the grass.  It does not Rip, Snort, and Tear like the Gas Trimmer. I think mostly because of the single .65 line.  It is a "Kinder, Gentler" trimmer, but it gets the job done.  It takes just a little longer than using the gas trimmer.  A benefit of this Gentler cut is that it does not splatter my shins and shoes with as much debris.  I now feel OK trimming with shorts on.  With the Gas, I always wore Jeans to keep my shins from getting all nicked up. This Gentler cut also is more forgiving for mistakes.This does take a couple of rounds of practice to get used to it, depending on what you were replacing it with.  Took me a couple times to "Edge" straight, but the end results look great.  I think the lower head end is a bit on the heavy side.  The battery at the top helps balance it.So, it performs well.  How about the battery life?  I have 10,000 sq. ft of yard.  But I have to do fences, landscape trimming, sidewalk/driveway edging, etc.  If I "Just Trim", I can get done easily on one charge.  If I try to Trim and do extensive sidewalk and driveway edging at the same time, I tend to need to move into the second battery from my B&D; Blower.  But that's OK by me for the convenience.The charger is fast.  I have two, but only opened the one.  BTW, the Blower is much weaker than the Trimmer.  Convenient, sure, but not very powerful...(read my review)The Trimmer is a great tool (and toy!)

This is  hardworking, lightweight, all purpose trimmer/edger that combines convenience with power without losing time.Let's compare it with my other machines; a B&D; cord, single line electric and my Craftsman, Brushwhacker- 21", double 0.095" line interchangeable with blades, 16 cc gas.Well, it's no contest, the gas wins out, especially out here, 5 acres of high prarie with tons of knapweed and other unssavories plus 1 acre of green yard grass.  yes, one has to mix the gas and oil, load the reel, and put in the earplugs.  No big deal.  It's been doing the job for over 15 years.So, the real question is, how does the B&D; 36v cordless do out here?First, out of the box, it's very easy to set up.  One can adjust the length by sliding and locking the tube.  Nice.  It's very light, and there's a protective guard one can employ with the edger or the trimmer to avoid cutting, in my case, stuff like drip wands or my flowers.  The battery charges in <2 hours by simply slipping it into the charger box and reading the lights which identify the charge status.  To edge, the head changes to the side position and locks.Now the real test, cutting.  It's fairly quiet, and whizzes right through grass.  I flew through the front and back yards.  Now for the pasture and thick weeds around fence, barn and path.  For the most part, I'd say it did a pretty good job, just took longer with it's narrower, single line than the gas unit.It lasted about 45 minutes of hard work.  It's great that one can release the trigger and save power when needed.I love weed whacking, and I love this unit.  As long as the battery's charged, I can grab it and go, and time is of essence- I want to play later with the family, and enjoy the neat yard.  Overall, it covered 90-95% of what my beloved gas machine does.

This tool is awesome,it cuts grass,weed cutter.it does it all. It actually will cut a small branch!. You won't be disappointed with this great tool. I think this one will last several years to come as its made to take the hard work. Thanks Black and Decker for a fabulous tool!

I know all about you suburban lawn-farmers, with your Kentucky bluegrass and your "mums". Hah. I'm an urban street gardener. Jewel weed. Jade plants. Think ground cover baby.The ground cover in my front patch does a great job of catching and dispersing the rain during rainy season, not dieing during dry season, feeding the local bee hive, and making repeated attempts to take over the adjacent sidewalk and front path.Thus, the trimmer (or, rather, the edger).In edge mode, I've found this device to be an excellent ally in the sidewalk wars, eagerly participating in my repeated rebukes of groundcover encroachments. Thick stems are no problem (woody roots, when I've let things go a bit too far, do sometimes need a bit of help).The balance is good, the battery design is appreciated (fast charging, on-board indicator, can be removed with one hand). I particularly like the wire guard for use in edging mode - I can pretty much rest the weight of the trimmer on that as needed, and it keeps the line from getting trashed by the concrete. I'm a petite female (just a hair over five feet tall), and the shaft length adjusted to my height with no problem.My only complaint about this thing is that it can't be hosed off after use (the instructions suggest a soft cloth and soapy water - a wet paper towel works well also). The instructions also have some parts in the wrong place (in particular the screw that attaches the guard), and say things like "disconnect tool before cleaning" and "do not use edger to create edges". So four stars, not five.
summary: An ally in the sidewalk wars

reviewText: [Update:  I've used the weed whacker a few times and I'm extremely happy with its performance.  I found that the lowest setting is still powerful enough for routine lawn maintenance and the lowest setting makes the machine even quieter and allows for a longer lasting battery. When I used used the machine at full power setting non-stop, the battery got hot and I had to wait over 30 minutes for the battery to cool down before the recharger would work.  Remember to wear safety glasses.]After reading all of the negative reviews, I decided to buy this anyway but my expectations were very low.I already own a good gas powered string trimmer, but I can't stand the noise and the maintenance associated with gas powered devices.  I bought the Black & Decker LST136W for the minor jobs.I had expected (from reading the reviews) that the assembly was going to be a bear.  Not at all. I was able to assemble the unit within a minute or two, without having to open the manual.Based upon the negative reviews, I was expecting that the unit would only be able to handle light-weight growth, and the useable battery life would be very short.  Not at all. The weed whacker cut through everything and I was exhausted before the battery finally ran out of power.When I use my gas powered string trimmer, I have to use a face guard since the string guard is so narrow.  Also, the gas trimmer covers my clothing in grass trimmings (I have to shake out my clothing before putting into the washing machine).  The B&D; trimmer's guard is very wide and only a small amount of debris was thrown onto my clothing.  I still use an eye guard.Power:  I was genuinely shocked by the amount of power.  Even though the B&D; has just one narrow string (my gas unit uses two strings and is much thicker), the B&D; string trimmer cut through all of the weeds without any hesitation.Adjustments:  I like the way I was able to adjust the length of the pole so that I don't have to lean over.Based on the negative reviews here, I anticipated that the B&D; would be the backup unit but after having used the B&D; light-weight unit, no motor noise (I can now use the unit early in the morning in suburbia), the convenience of not having to deal with advancing the string, I found that the reverse is true:  The gas unit will be my back-up machine.  Battery powered devices have greatly advanced in the past few years.I wasn't able to find anything negative to say about the machine after one day's use.
summary: Surprisingly powerful, surprising long battery life.  I LOVE IT.

reviewText: I am pleased with this cordless battery operated grass trimmer.  I have a small yard so the charge is sufficient for me to trim.  In fact, according to the battery, I have 75% of power still left.  I use setting 1 (the lowest) and it is sufficient to trim the grass.  I also like that the string advances automatically when it gets below three inches or so.  No bumping on the ground, it just advances by itself.  I like that I don't have to store gasoline.  I just take the battery out and keep it in the charger when not in use.  At setting 1, it is plenty strong, so at higher settings it should be very strong.

I have used this product three times, each time for over thirty minutes.  I have read some reviews that state the battery life is too short but I have not found this to be true.  The battery I am using is over two years old and came with a Black and Decker 36 volt hedge trimmer, so this battery has held up over time and still holds a good charge.  I have not as yet tried the battery which came with the trimmer but the two are identical.  This is a light duty trimmer; for heavier work I still use a gasoline powered trimmer.  However, for a light duty trimmer and edger it is everything I had hoped for.  Really a nice tool, very light weight and easy to use.

I can trim my whole yard on one battery charge and edge my sidewalks too. I bought this with the 40v blower so I have 2 batteries in case I need them but so far 1 has done the job. The only downside to this wonderful trimmer is the handle could be a bit longer. It is adjustable and that is nice but could be just a bit longer for taller people.

I purchased this as a sister product to the 36 volt trimmer, partly, so I would have access to another battery should I need it.Compared to my electric/corded hedge trimmer, aside from the obvious ommission of a cord, it is much quieter and has longer cutting blades. The length makes it easier and faster to trim larger hedges.
Great power and battery life is wonderful.  The cordless tools are really impressing me over the gas-powered models and this one is no different.  No mess No fuss.  Well except for whatever you trim.

I don't love yard work, but I DO get out and help my husband with it as oftenas I can...why should he be punished? LOL  We have several decorative grassesand many bushes and small fruit trees at our home and it seems that one or moreof them always need some trimming, especially those decorative grasses...now Iwill help more often!  This Black and Decker was light enough for me to holdand trim with.  I found that it trimmed some of the fruit trees little off shootswithout any hesitation.  It did GREAT shaping up the decorative grasses and Iwas happy for that...as I actually did that with regular scissors before, NO MORE!

We have two hedges: one is about 24 feet long by the front porch which is easily accessible on both sides and top; the other is about 80 feet long and runs against a four-foot chain link fence which causes problems.For several years I've been using the Black & Decker 18 volt cordless trimmer on the front hedge and that along with the Black & Decker 18 volt cordless alligator chain saw on the back hedge (see links at the end of the review).This hedge trimmer comes ready to use once the battery is charged. Out of the box, the battery was nearly ready to go. Within thirty minutes, I was able to give this a little test to make sure it worked.The smaller hedge was needing normal trimming and this did the job easily, quickly and evenly. The angles I can work at for this hedge make using the trimmer easy to do.The larger hedge was much more work and this trimmer, compared with the 18 volt, made the job much easier (not easy, but easier). This, like the other one, does get heavy. I'm retired and had to take several breaks.The back of the hedge is against a chain link fence and I had to use this vertically between the fence and hedge to get it trimmed. That's one-handed work. Though the specs say the two trimmers are nearly the same weight, this one seemed much heavier for that portion of the job.The battery life is impressive. I did the entire fence side without recharging the battery. The rest of the job did take longer and I did charge the battery after each use. It never took more than an hour (if that) to charge it.I own several of the 18 volt Black & Decker yard tools and saws and have been well pleased with all of them. Some I've used for over six years. This 36 volt trimmer will get a workout. If you have a lot to keep trimmed I think this does it enough faster and cuts enough larger diameter limbs to be worth the price difference over the 18 volt model. Both do the job they are made to do.Black & Decker NHT518 18-Volt 22-Inch Cordless Electric Hedge TrimmerBlack & Decker NLP1800 Alligator Lopper 18-Volt Cordless Chain Saw
this is a great item. i love the cordless end of it and it lasts very long on a charge. cuts through all kinds of items.

This trimmer retired my old B&D; cord trimmer in one afternoon. No longer I have to drag a cord down the other end of my backyard. The trimmer is light enough that my wife now takes the job of trimming down the butterfly vines hedge that seems to take over our back fence. She finished the job in about less than an hour for a 40'+ fence thtat overgrown with vines and the battery seemed still going.The trimmer is very well balanced, heavy enough that you think it could do serious work and light enough to operate for extended time. Battery is fast charging; in a bit over an hour I got a fullk charge the first time. Snap the battery in, take the cover off and you are in business. That simple. The trimmer blades are stainless steel, sharp and machined precision. Of course, you never handle the trimmer by the blade, but I saved the blade cover to put it back after use.A very good product by Back & Decker and reasonably priced. Every household with yard and hedges should have one, and I am glad I do!

Black & Decker LHT2436 36-Volt High Performance Cordless Hedge Trimmer, 24-InchI have been using the corded version of Black & Decker 24-inch hedge trimmer for years.I consider myself pretty careful, but still have cut through cord one time. I am very happy to try out the cordless model of Black & Decker 24-inch hedge trimmer. The clear benefits of using the cordless model are (1) no more hassles of dragging the extension cord, (2) no more worried about cut through the cord.Actually, after using the cordless hedge trimmer for 3 months, I found out one more additional benefit: The cordless hedge trimmer is lighter than the corded one. I can use it for an hour without getting sore.*** CONSTRUCTIONThe construction is high quality and the trimmer is very well balanced.The trimmer blades are stainless steel, sharp and machined precision.*** HANDLINGComparing with the 24-inch corded Black & Decker Hedge trimmer, the cordless hedge trimmer shows the same trimming capability. I am very surprised to see that a cordless trimmer can be on par with the corded trimmer. I guess 36V (instead of 18V or 19.2V) does help.The corded trimmer is more heavier as the cord is dragging behind to add more weight.The cordless hedge trimmer feels lighter. A lot of times, I use only one hand to hold it to reach bushes on the far side.*** BATTERYThe Lithium-Ion battery provides a lot of benefits, (1) Lithium-Ion battery does not have memory effect like the cheaper Ni-Cd battery, (2) Lithium-Ion battery has very low leakage, it can hold charges for half year, (3) Lithium-Ion battery can be charged far faster (but require a fast charger, which is included in this package).I have a cordless blower and the 18V battery can last only 15-minutes blowing operation. Initially, I was very skeptical about how long the 36V battery can last for the heavy duty trimming operation. But I was wrong. The included Lithium-Ion battery has very good capacity. I trimmed about an hour and still had half a charge remaining according the lights on the battery. Excellent!!*** SUMMARY:This cordless trimmer really exceeds my expectations. It does a great job of trimming and shaping scrubs. I highly recommend it.
summary: Strong trimming capability, easy handling, long battery life. Excellent!!

reviewText: I've used it about 3 times now and it is extremely powerful especially compared to the 18 Volt WORX that recently died after only approximately two and a half years.I don't know what the future holds for it, but thus far is perfect!!

Very easy to use.  This was my first house so the first time trimming back bushes.  It was so easy to do and lighter then you would expect.  It does not take much of a charge to do all the trimming I need.  My parents borrowed it and found it very user friendly as well.  I see this on a gift list in their future.

I''ve had other Black & Decker lawn products before and was generally ambivalent about them - they just never seemed very powerful compared to other brand yard tools.  However, when I saw this 36volt trimmer, I decided to give them another chance - and boy am I glad I did. This is powerful enough that I can trim all my shrubs and hedges in less than half the time it used to take me using the Worx 18volt li-ion trimmer.  Comparing this to the Worx, this is considerably more powerful and therefore produces a much cleaner, neater cut.  The Worx would require multiple passes to get a nice straight cut (I think because it was underpowered) whereas this one gets it in one pass..  And this trimmer can go thru larger sized branches than any of the other trimmers I looked at.  I also like that I don't have to charge the battery every single time I use it - I've trimmed all my hedges and shrubs 3 times before needing to recharge the battery.  This trimmer is also much quieter and smoother than my worx was, and even my smaller corded Black & Decker trimmer.  Overall, I really can't find a single flaw with this product and look forward to buying the blower/vac that can use the same battery.
summary: Best Black & Decker yard product I've ever used!

reviewText: I've been using the Black & Decker LHT2436 36-Volt High Performance Cordless Hedge Trimmer, 24-Inch for a couple of weeks now and I'm reasonably happy. I've trimmed a couple of small hedges, cut back some jasmine and vines and even took it to a small section of lawn that had gotten overgrown. All this on one charge. I also have a Black&Decker; Trimmer Hedge Trimmer that's AC Powered and in comparison the Cordless Hedge Trimmer does feel a bit under-powered. Although it didn't have any trouble cutting through my hedges it did hesitate a bit more than the corded model.On the other hand, the lack of a cord is a huge advantage. No more worrying about cutting the power cord or moving the cord out of the way. No more dealing with extension cables and finding a place to plug it in. And on top of all that it's actually pretty well balanced due to the weight of the battery and it felt like I was wielding a sword. Well maybe more like a light saber :-)So overall I'm pretty happy and I think it'll be getting a lot more use than my other (corded) hedge trimmer.

First I let it charge over night then I put it to work. I trimmed a few small things first to get used to it but then put it to work on a 60 foot long by 10 foot high laurel. Half way through the battery check light said it was done but it was still going strong after 2 hours. I decided to charge again over night and finished the other half the next day. I cut 2 to 3 feet off the top of the laurel plus down the sides. If I had two batteries I could have done it in one day easily.It is phenomenal not having a cord attached or having to deal with the loud and smelly gas options. It isn't too heavy and having at times to use only one hand to reach deep wasn't that difficult. Well balanced holding it with the two handles making it easy to control. From leaves to stock about 3/4 inch thick it had no problem.The only problem of course will be the usual maintenance and keeping it sharp.I love this machine. I was having a ball and trimmed a few things for my neighbor. I now have battery operated lawn mower, sweeper, edger and hedger in my yard maintenance arsenal. NO MORE CORDS!

I am very impressed with the battery powered hedge trimmer.  For moderate yard maintenance, it has both the power and capability of a professional unit.  I am pleased with the amount of battery life between charges.  It does a great job of trimming and shaping scrubs!  This 24" Black and Decker is an overall winner!

This is the third cordless hedge trimmer I've owned. The first two (made by Ryobi)were affordable and easy to use, but neither seemed up to the tasks I bought them to do. They frequently ended up being overwhelmed by what I considered a moderate workload and their battery life was, in a word, short (think 10-15 minutes of trimming at a stretch). So after giving up on those models I decided to get the new Black & Decker LHT2436 Cordless Hedge Trimmer and see what a 36-volt battery could do.Quick answer: a 36-volt battery is a game changer. Longer answer: a 36-volt battery provides both the power and the capacity to do at least an hour of varied trimming without a recharge - which is pretty awesome performance at this price point.Aside from my power and capacity requirements, I also wanted a trimmer that could handle more than some light hedge work. The Black & Decker LHT2436 Trimmer is supposed to cut through a 3/4" branch, and I am happy to confirm that that specification is accurate. I was able to cut through both branches and vines that size without too much strain. After a few weeks of regular use, the trimmer seems to be holding up quite well.The other major factor in terms of product satisfaction is ergonomics, and this is where the Black & Decker LHT2436 Trimmer really excels. It's extremely well balanced and the reduction in vibration compared to other models I've used is remarkable. That alone reduces the fatigue factor significantly, and the relatively light weight completes the package. This trimmer is well designed and you can feel it every time you use it.This is definitely a five-star product, and well worth a serious look if you're in the market for a cordless trimmer.
summary: Serious tool built for real-world yardwork

reviewText: Living out in the country you're going to have critter troubles. And as animals lose their natural habitat they are increasingly showing up in suburbia. What to do when a possum takes up residence under the house?With the Havahart trap you can quickly catch them and either call animal control or take them out to the wilds (if you have any) and release.Just bait the trap with whatever goodie appeals to their appetite and wait. Most ramble about evenings. In the morning you will have a possum under arrest. We got ours and let him go way out in the woods. Finally getting the whole place fenced this week, so we shouldn't see him again.It's really nice to have one of these on hand. It's one of those "when you need it, you need it" items. Your neighbors will probably ask to borrow it. Keep it out of the weather as much as possible and it should last forever.

This review is for the Havahart 1064 Large 2-door Easy Set Trap.  This trap is easy to setup, use, and release animals. It can be used as a single door trap or a double door trap.BUILD:  The dimensions of the trap are 12" H x 36" W x 10.5" D.  The largest opening/gap in the steel cage mesh is 1" x 1".  THe door opening for the animals is 12" H x 10.5" W.  THe handle is sturdy. The steel wires of the pulleys are sheathed in plastic. The weight of the cage is about 2 lbs by itself. It's not heavy at all, but when there's an animal in the cage, it can become heavy.  Since there's a single handle, one person can carry it. Two people can carry it if you use wooden poles  in the front and back.  The top of the cage has a metal plate the size of 14" x 10" to protect you when your hand is on the handle.  When the doors are closed, the enclosed area is about 22" W x 12" H x 10.5" D.You can set either one door open or both doors open. To set one door, remove the wire from the black loop/latch on the top of the cage.  To use both doors, put the wire around the loop/latch.  Since the trip plate is connected on only one side, that side requires less pressure for the trap doors to close.  The doors close quickly.  Once an animal is trapped, remove the wire from the black loop/latch so that only the door on the side of the latch will open to releasethe animal.This trap is sturdy, built well, easy to setup, and use. The intrsuctions are in English, French, and Spanish.  They are easy to understand with the text and diagrams.
summary: For small/large animals, use single door or both doors. Easy to use.

reviewText: All too often have I gone out to the garden to find that a raccoon or other animal has gotten over or under the fence and had a party eating my various veggies, fruits and other things I have growing in there.I now have this larger unit and a smaller one that I keep out there and leave some bait in them to catch the pesky critters that get past the main fence of the property. Since I have been using these traps I have had a seriously large reduction in my garden being ravaged. It has made for much bigger yields over the last year or so now. Sometimes they still get into the garden but I do leave one trap in there as well and with the right bait in the traps they will go after the trap before the rest of the plants, at least most of the time.The great thing about these is that I don't want to hurt the wildlife around my home, I just don't want them getting into my plants. This lets me capture them without harm and then I can release them several miles away out in a different area that maybe they will stay to the new area. It seems to be working as not only have my captures gone down substantially but as well have all my garden invasions.Though there have been a couple instances over the last year or 2 since I started this that I had to call animal control to come get some suspicious a raccoon or cat. Turns out 1 of the 2 animals I had them come get tested positive for rabies. I feel good that I have been able to help get rid of those pests in my area that are disease ridden.For those of you wondering about the kind of area that I live in, it's very sparse for houses near me and in fact I am one of only a couple houses within sight of mine. This makes for a nice place to live and also for plenty of animals to live near you.IT's a simple trap that trips easily and keeps even the largest of raccons in it. They haven't been able to do any damage to it yet.
summary: Get those pests out of your garden and land.

reviewText: My Humane Society has the Havahart traps which they lend out to home owners, so I am familiar with this brand. I have had to borrow a trap several times over the years. Now I have my very own Havahart trap. I have used it to catch several feral cats in our neighborhood. I really like the easy handle to set and release the trap, so you do not have to get close to the animal. It works beautifully and does not hurt the animal. I like that. Our humane society offers free spay and neutering to feral animals, so as I catch them, I take them to the humane society and then release them after the operation. This is the trap I needed to do so.

The Havahart 1064 appears to have a very high level of construction with stainless steel.  It is also super easy to use.  There are two plastic handles at the top. One is affixed to the top and that is the handle for carrying the trap.  The other plastic handle is moveable. To set the trap, just lift the handle in a 180 degree arc and press it down on the other side of the cage.  Both doors will then be open. There is a small plate in the floor of the trap that triggers the doors to drop.  To open the door(s) to release an animal, just lift the handle and press it down on the other side of the cage again.  If you only want to open one door, then you just need to remove the cable from the black metal loop on the top (see the photos I uploaded).  Also see the Havahart videos at the top left corner of the webpage for this item.We have had problems with skunks and armadillos in our yard, and the Havahart appears to be perfect for catching them.  If you catch a skunk, just throw a tarp over the trap and pick it up and move it into your truck.  With the tarp and the skunk not seeing you, hopefully you won't get sprayed.
summary: Super easy to use and high quality construction

reviewText: This two door trap is a humane way to catch feral cats or wildlife that needs to be relocated. The cage is sturdy and comes with simple instructions on how to use it with one trap door open or two. You might want to practice opening an closing the trap a couple of times before using it to catch an animal. The handle on top allows for easy release. It comes with a list of what kind of animals you may catch with this trap and what kind of bait to use.  As with catching any live animals, be careful about separating mothers from babies who may die without them. This trap is great for the home user who wants to protect their garden, as well as for people who work with wildlife rehabilitation and animal shelters. Very good quality and easy to use trap.

My husband and I have volunteered at a local cat shelter for about a decade, and we have extensive experience with many different varieties of humane traps (everything from the Havaharts to custom-built drop traps) and this is the one we bring out most often.The trap is simple to use. Simply release a small lever and then lift the doors up into the upright position where they lock into place.There is a small "plate" in the inside center of the trap that you put a treat or some food on, and when the animal puts pressure on that area, the two doors close shut. The trap can only shut IF the animal is in the center of the trap, so there's very little chance that the animal will get hurt by the closing doors.The reason why two doors are beneficial in this sort of trap is because more skittish animals feel safer entering the trap if there are two ways of escape- forward and backward. However, the two door set up can be awkward if you are trying to transfer the animal into a regular carrier- we find that the one door Havaharts are better for situations in which the animal might be transferred into carriers for trips to the vet, etc.Highly recommended.

Haveahart, in my opinion, makes the absolute best humane traps, and this is no exception. Setting the trap is about as easy as it can get - just lock back the single handle at the top, and you're good to go. The trigger plate has enough resistance to avoid false triggers, but is loose enough to trigger it properly when the (usually unwanted) guest decides to take the bait.This has dual doors to make it easy to position for the best chance of success, plus helps with trapping animals that are reluctant to enter something that does not appear to have an escape route. Both doors slam shut at the same time when the trigger is tripped.The challenge with any of these traps is getting the critter to take the bait. That's more of an art than a science, unfortunatly, and it can take some time to come up with the right approach. The instructions offer some bait suggestions for some animails; other suggestions are easily found via an Internet search.I have two other small Haveahart traps, one of which is easily 15 years old, and still works fine and has not rusted even though it has been left outdoors for days on end. I don't have any concerns about this trap not giving me years of service. Highly recommend if you're looking for a larger-size trap.
summary: Super easy to set and use; sturdy build quality

reviewText: Amazing simple to set, one hand lever operation opens and sets both doors at once. Stable mechanism keeps doors open while trigger responds quickly and effectively with a light step.  The see through 2 door design gives cautious creatures a sense of confidence entering the trap while the locking mechanism on the door does a great job of keeping them from backing out when the set off the trigger.To release the animal you simply move a loop from a guide and when you move the operating lever it will only open one side. It would be nice to have the side for release identified on the top of the trap, I added this myself after trying to remember while I was in the middle of releasing a skunk.The cage itself is heavy gauge and the welds are strong. This trap should easily survive the toughest captors such as raccoon, groundhog, etc.As with any trap, you should check regularly, animals can die without access to food or water and can even be the victim of other animals taking advantage of them being trapped.Another opportunity would be an add on item for these traps to provide a wireless alert on capture so you can get to it quickly after triggered.
summary: Fantastic, easy set, heavy duty construction, built to last!

reviewText: I'm so happy every time I see these for vine as I love them. They are some of the sturdiest and long lasting and easy to use traps that I've ever had. So easy to use, even an 8 year old child could use them without help. The stainless steel they are constructed of is a high grade and I've yet to have one rust, not even the ones that got a hole shot in them. The double doors gives your prey the sense they are not walking into a trap because they can see straight through to the other side. If you're real lucky, and I've had it happen once, you can catch two at once but they have to be entering the trap from each side at the same time and be far enough in when one trips the door to catch them both. Spend the extra money for this brand, you'll be glad you did. They never disappoint.

For humane critter traps, this is the best trap we've used yet. Because of the double doors and open ends it is the most effective as cats and raccoons, two particularly wily critters who are good at avoiding corners, so to speak will enter without a second thought. The cage is solid! So once a critter is caught not only does it hold but it is heavy enough that the animal can't thrash it about and hurt itself. And finally it is humane. Because it is a live trap critters can be relocated without any harm done and the doors can be opened so that you, yourself can stand clear.Worth the investment and will give you a clear conscience.
summary: The best, sturdiest HUMANE critter trap out there

reviewText: We had a critter living under the deck - it was driving the dog crazy. We tried to block off the underside with fencing but our "guest" was clever enough to circumvent our barrier. We decided to try capturing and relocating whatever it was.We put a peanut butter covered piece of bread in the trap and in one night, we had a hefty possum trapped, perfectly safe and well fed!I drove it a mile away to the edge of the nearby wetlands and let it go. I wore gloves and was ever so careful not to get attacked by the scared, excited and possibly dangerous guest! This is not a small issue so be careful... The local animal control officer made sure I knew that, while rabid animals would probably not be attracted to food, caution is better than sickness!I have used smaller Havahart traps before and some have been almost impossible to set. This one is much easier and earns a "recommended" rating.
summary: Great for possums and raccoons - just be careful letting the critter out

reviewText: When I first saw it I thought I could catch a walrus in it!  But when the doors close it's considerably smaller, but large enough for a raccoon or cat.  The openness of having 2 doors makes it easier to catch animals who are skittish.  Watching the demo videos are helpful because it recommends putting treats around the cage and under the trip plate, which is pretty effective.  It's so easy that I didn't even need to read the directions to set the trap, but the directions do give some good tips, like effective bait for different critters.

I have been using these types of traps for over 35 years and they just keep getting better and better. This has a very easy, one-hand setting. All you do is slide the handle and it is set. It trips well so you won't have many escapees. This one is large and is suited for raccoon size animals. They have the same style in various size so find the one that is the right size for the varmints you are trying to trap.

Havahart 1064 Large is not only functional, sturdy, and well made, but also aesthetic.  The only serious reservation raises the small size of the handle in the middle-top making it difficult to carry the trap by 2 people side-by-side except by those with small hands - who usually are weaker - but still not conveniently and very close to the middle mesh exposing their thighs to the animal's claws.  The trap also is lacking 2 handles at both ends allowing carrying it by 2 people easier than side-by-side and farther away from its middle mesh important especially when a raging heavy clever animal inside is tilting the trap and is eager to attack through the mesh with long sharp claws.
summary: Small top handle, no handles at both ends

reviewText: Some of the critters are less afraid to enter this 2 door trap when they can see through to the other end.  Some animals don't like to go up against a solid wall.  The trap trigger plate is very sensitive, and the doors slam very fast.  You can configure this to use 1 or 2 doors.  The construction of this trap is solid, so it is durable and will last a long time in the field.

I'm a wildlife biologist, and have used similar traps for mammals of various sizes. This one is sort of middle-of-the-road in build quality. You're not going to use it outdoors every day for years on end without it rusting. That said, it's both lighter and cheaper than the more expensive, thicker-metal powder-coated traps, and it's sturdy enough for fairly regular use. It's decent, and definitely not junk.This is my second trap with this "Easy Set" design from Havahart. It's brilliant. Fast, and simple. Flip the setting handle from one side to the other, and both doors open and the trap is set thanks to a cleverly-rigged cable system. Takes literally only half a second to set the thing. Love that feature. The mechanism is a little finicky on mysmaller trap, so I sometimes found myself having to try it a few times before it held (so the doors didn't just come crashing back down), but it's been perfect on this large one. Still, even if you have try to set it a few times, eventually it'll work, and it's a great way to set a trap. And open one too, since your hands are nowhere near the door or the animal when releasing it. A suggestion from the instruction page that comes with the trap: unhook the 2nd door's loop and open only one door when releasing an animal, so the animal's path is somewhat predictable. Yeah, you can use this feature to use this trap in one-door mode too, which is handy: less likely for the animal to escape, and you can make sure the animal comes in the side most likely to set off the trap. With both doors open, you can't put food on the opposite side of the trigger plate from both directions, so the animal could get off with the bait without putting any pressure on the trigger.This trap is a perfect size for cats (feral or otherwise). Anything about the same size would be fine as well (raccoons, skunks, marmots, armadillos, etc). The box also shows a prairie dog on it (I think someone at Havahart thought it was a marmot), but I'd go with that smaller trap for them, as anything much lighter in weight than a cat might not trigger it properly, and could end up escaping with the bait. With this design, I don't see a way to adjust the pressure required to trigger the trap, and animals probably need to be at least a couple pounds to have reliable success with it.Anyway, it's a decent trap for anything approximately cat sized.
summary: Decent quality, good for cats, raccoons, skunks, and similarly-sized animals.

reviewText: The first evening the trap (Havahart 1064 Large 2-Door Easy Set Trap) went off, the bait was gone & no critter was inside.  Thankfully the second evening the trap worked properly & caught a opossum.  Since then it has been working adequately; not perfectly.The new design is very sensitive which means it can be hard to keep the trap set.  It takes very little to set it off.  Sometimes the action of setting the trap sets the trap off!  Like the older model, determined critters sometimes escape.  Many times it would be set off with no critter inside.  If bait is still inside I am guessing the animal is pawing at the cage rather than entering it & setting off the trap.  If it is set with no bait I believe the critter was able to break out.  If you already have the older style, I wouldn't recommend an upgrade but if you need a new trap then this one is likely to give you nearly the same results as the older model.While I recommend this trap I do not recommend the smaller trap www.amazon.com/Havahart-1062-Rabbits-Skunks-Squirrels/dp/B003QP328I/ref=cm_cr-mr-title.  Both (smaller & larger) traps are identical in design from what I can tell yet one works & the other does not.  I have been setting the smaller trap out every single day/night for over two months & it has never, not once, not ever caught anything!  But it has gone off without a critter inside & the bait gone time & time again.  All I'm doing with the smaller trap is feeding the wildlife.
summary: Works About As Well As The Older Version

reviewText: I live in the woods, we have a lot of critters, some are nice, others not so.This trap is so easy to use, and light weight despite it's size and sturdiness.  With the 2 doors you don't have to worry about getting your fingers bit off when releasing your catch.  Also, if you happen to 'catch' a cat, a chicken, or some other animal not needed to be trapped you can easily free the animal without causing it any harm.I am very happy with this trap and don't see it getting damaged by normal use...it has worked quite well for me, and I would most definitely recommend this trap.There are several different sizes of Havahart traps that you can purchase, so depending on the size of your pests you can go from large to small.

While pursuing feral cats in our neighborhood over the years, to catch spay/neuter and release we've borrowed various traps.One can't help but notice a big difference in quality between brands..Many have thin gage wire, which make them trickier to get the trigger rod set.Some are painted ~ rather than galvanized for rust resistance as Havahart is.Some have had a smaller hand guard, or worse ~ none.When we finally bought our own, ~ Havahart was the clear choice for easy use and reliable function.We've been very satisfied with the Havahart, professional style one door traps we've been using for the past two years.I didn't think that trap  (# 1079 ) could be beat for all around quality and convenience, but now Havahart has out-done them selves!This single movement, "Easy Set" trap is an innovative and ingenious design that has made the use of traps even quicker, easier and safer.There's more to this handle then meets the eye.This design is an impressive, improvement for several reasons ~ even over Havahart's basic style.This multi-task handle is a solid piece of plastic, riveted to the hand guard, so it can't move around.This is more comfortable and offers more control to keep the trap away from your body then the typical (swinging) wire handles.The handle is as smooth as silk to lock/un-lock ~ by the flip of the handle, there-fore ~no more fiddling around with a touchy trigger rod, and/or thinner wire gage trap that the rod is weaker & difficult to keep set.To use both doors simply leave the cable looped around the 'setting loop', (hook)and to use only one door slip the cable out of the 'setting loop' (hook).This two door feature is quite a clever design, and both options work the same ~ with the flip of the handle.Havahart is an easy to use, excellent preforming, quality constructed, durable trap.With heavy gage solid steel, galvanized wire and all smooth/ rounded edges.This five star product is made in America.Footnote: For convenience ~ three sizes of Havahart traps ~Small ~ Ideal for catching chipmunks, rats, squirrels and similar-size nuisance animals7.1" long ~ 2.4" wide ~ 3.5" high.Medium ~ Ideal for catching rabbits, skunks, squirrels and similar-size nuisance animals. (this one)25" long ~ 7" wide ~ 7 1/4" highLarge ~ Ideal for catching raccoons, stray cats, groundhogs (woodchucks), opossums, and similar-size nuisance animals.32" long ~ 10" wide ~ 12" high.(This is the measurements for # 1079, the two door Easy Set  is a bit larger ~ 36" long ~ 10" wide ~ 12 1/2" high)
summary: THE ~ Trap You Can Count On

reviewText: EDIT 6/5/2013: The trap finally caught something...  Our cat!  It never did catch a skunk, and the cat called me some pretty nasty names when I released it.This is fairly easy to set, but it doesn't catch the skunks that are running roughshod over my property and stealing my cat's food (and occasionally spraying the cats).  The first night, the little buggers tripped the trap, but didn't get caught.  Since then, they have figured out how to take the bait without even tripping the trap -- and they've done it twice!I did give it two stars because it really is quite easy to set up.  Maybe your skunks (or other critters) haven't taken lessons from Houdini, like mine did, but this trap didn't work for mine.  :-(Back to the drawing board.  I hope I can find something that works!
summary: My skunks are too smart for this trap!

reviewText: the quality is outrageously good and it is made in america. i like that part a lot. i can use one door the way i like to do it. it is tough and durable. it is so easy to follow just several simple instructions to set it up. i am trapping now armadillos that are doing a lot of damage in the yard. i then transport the live animal to a new home a couple miles down the road. it is so easy to turn the animal loose and there is no chance of getting bitten. i am having really great luck capturing critters that do damage and then transporting them to another area. do you have a favorite bait to use? right now i am using peanut butter and bread. they sure love that combination. i highly recommend this american made piece of work. please give it a try. i don't think there is a chance of regretting it. i used to get so upset looking around the yard and seeing all the damage. now... i am taking control. thank you!

Even though I don't live in the country, "critters" seem to find their way into my yard.  Over the years, I've seen a couple opossums in my yard.  I wouldn't worry about them, but I have a dog.  I know that it wouldn't be an issue if my dog would leave it alone (they aren't creatures to search out trouble), but it is extremely difficult to get a dog to NOT go directly to a strange animal and start barking like a maniac.  In the past I borrowed someone's live trap and caught an opossum.  I'll admit it -- I was too scared to pick up the cage with it inside.  There just didn't seem to be protection (distance) from my fingers to the animal, so I had someone get it for me.  However, the Havahart 1064 trap takes away that fear with the double doors and space on the upper corners where the animal can't reach.  I personally think all of these traps can be a bit tricky to set, but it's pretty easy to figure out with a little bit of thought.

This is a good size trap for those mixtures of animals from cats to racoons.  You can release the ones you didn't mean to catch and get rid of the ones you did.  I like to use a trap of this size to catch pests when I'm unsure of what it is.  Sometimes you think it is one animal and then you find a different visitor.First the trap is sturdy.  It handles well and sets easily.  Once you catch something, it stays there until you're ready.I deal with a lot of groundhogs, raccoons, opossums, etc. even with houses all around.  There is a lot of woods they come out of looking for something to eat.  This allows me the choice of releasing someone's pet versus a wild creature that is going to keep coming back.If you're looking for a solid trap...this is a good one to have.
summary: Safely trap the animals you want to set free again

reviewText: There are plenty of indepth reviews on Amazon so let me just cover a few things about mine. It is tricky to set. I am sure that this is just mine. It may have bent or whatever in delivery. I would have given up if I did not own a smaller one that works just fine. I needed to stretch one of the cables to get the doors to stay open/set. This is definately for home use so it is not as heavy as it could be. I will use mine in an attic space in the garage so it will not be exposed to the eliments. Very pleased with it.

I use my Havahart 1064 Large 2-door easy set trap to catch and release animals that go into my peacock pen and eat their food at night.  So far I've captured two possums.My peacocks rest on their perches at night, but something gets inside their pen some nights, and we needed to find out what animal it was, and how it gets in.  By using this trap and release device, we were able to narrow it down to who is getting in, and found an inconspicuous place on the ground they were squeezing in to.Now that the peahen is laying eggs, we worried that a predator would get them, and this trap brought peace of mind.  The first night, we got a possum and repaired a place it got in.  The second night, another little possum, and we made a second repair.  Since then, nothing has gotten inside the pen and the trap has stayed open all night, with bait intact.My only complaint with the Havahart is that, when you pull the handle on top of the cage back, which triggers the door to open and the trap is set, sometimes the handle won't stay latched and instantly snaps back shut.  So my trap is a bit trigger happy.It's simple to use.  It comes right out of the box ready to operate.  Just put some bait on the center plate inside the trap - follow the instructions on how to loop the cords according to whether you want to have both sides or one side of the trap open, then snap the handle back and you're all set.  I recommend using super-sized marshmallows if you think you might have raccoons, as that is their favorite treat!Even though I recommend trap and release devices, I do not recommend moving the animals far away from where you trapped them, because they could be mothers with young babies waiting for them to come back, which would mean certain death for the babies.  Raccoon babies, for instance, stay with their moms for up to a year.  Of course, an offspring that old will do fine on it's own, but often there are tiny babies in a nest waiting for their mother, who just left to find food.  I have rehabbed baby raccoons that were taken to a wildlife animal rehab organization, because the mother had made a nest for them in an attic and the owner of the house didn't appreciate it, so he shot the mom, and then realized she had four babies in the attic.  He brought the babies to the animal rehab center, which is selfish, as those organizations are under-funded at best, and are desperate for volunteers, which means little training and resources, which reduces the chances of animals being rehabbed correctly and drastically reduces their chances of survival or living as nature intended.  The best person to raise baby raccoons is a mother raccoon.I definitely recommend this trap and release device to be used to trap feral cats, so that they may be spayed.  That's another great thing about this kind of trap.Just make sure you know what you're doing.  Trapping is easy, but the bigger picture isn't always so simple.  One needs to act responsibly.
summary: A bit fast on the trigger, but works as it should

reviewText: This improved version of the Havahart trap allows one door to remain closed when the trap is set.  With the bait (food) placed farther inside the trap near that closed door, there is less chance of the animal escaping as happened frequently with our older version.  This new trap is incredibly easy to set and to release with one hand.  We will be taking the possum that was trapped to a forested area away from our home.  The large size of this trap should ensure that our woodchucks will fit nicely when they smell the bait.

Setting this trap is as easy as lifting up a handle. Releasing what you've caught is just as easy. The paddle sensitivity is right for the larger creatures this trap is meant for. I've not had any luck catching the vegetarians in my yard. I'm talking about groundhogs and rabbits. It seems they are too cautious to enter the trap. I've tried all kinds of fresh veggies (assorted greens, tomatoes, carrots, celery, etc.) without any catches.  Meat-eaters, mainly skunks where I live, are another story. They go right for the left over meat or dog food I use as bait for them.Transporting and releasing a skunk is bit of a chore but is not as difficult as I would have thought. I approach the trap while holding a blanket or similar type of shield. As soon as I'm close enough I drop the blanket over the trap, pick it up by the handle (which is underneath the blanket), and put it in the back of my truck.
