reviewText: We set this in our pasture area where we have a mole problem. The holes can make a real problem for livestock. Unfortunately, the area is surrounded by fields. When the barley was being harvested the trap kept going off because of the near by heavy equipment.We finally moved it to the lawn and it worked great. I caught two little buggers right off. Since it works so well I am looking forward to using it in the pasture after harvest is all finished.

I did not want to use this at all, it really scared me and I was worried about my kids finding it and getting hurt. The mole issue was really getting out of hand though so I gave it a try. I set it along a path and the next day there was a catch. I emptied it, and didn't clean it or anything then put it in another area of the lawn with a path and got another one. I re set it and haven't had another mole.  My kids don't notice it, and it would take some effort on their part to really pull it up and injure themselves, so I consider it fairly safe, and absolutely effective.
summary: Worked, and was easy to use.

reviewText: This mole trap was very difficult for us to set.  Once we got it into position, we struggled to get the catch to hold.  It does not want to come all the way out to hold the spring up in place.  We have to use a screw driver to cajole the catch into position.  So, I don't agree that this trap is "incredibly easy to set" as the box boasts.Once we get it set, it triggers almost immediately.  We went through the process many times before calling it quits.  With the spikes as sharp as they are and the spring as tight as it is, we decided it was the sensible and safe thing to do:  Give up before we got too tired, made a bad move and hurt ourselves.We have very sandy soil at the location where we have the mole problem.  It is almost at sea level and the water table is not far below the surface.  The box says the trap is "triggered by the slightest movement", and we are wondering if the sandy soil makes the ground too sensitive for this trap.But, whatever the reason, this trap is not working for us.
summary: Maybe too sensitive for our sandy soil?

reviewText: This is a mole trap but it doesnt really trap them it kills them dead.  Just so you know if you are looking for some way to trap them without hurting them this is not it.  This trap is very simple to use.  You just find one of their mole tunnels in the yard and push this into the ground and set it.  The mole while running down the tunnel will set off the trap and the spikes slam down into the mole and kill it.  You then dispose of the dead mole and set it up again to get rid of more moles.  Very easy to use and it really works to get rid of your moles.

This follows a tried and true concept to control damage from moles.  It is much sturdier than it looked in the photos and is heavy enough that I should be able to use it for a long time.  I followed the instructions that came with the trap and within the first week I saw my first results.  It may appear to be a pretty gruesome killing machine, but I have not had any luck with the chemical type traps.  As they say until someone builds a better mousetrap . . . . It does the job.
summary: An Answer to My Mole Problem

reviewerName: Jeri Zerr "formerly a Road Warrior of the Nth...
reviewText: First off - my mole issue is very mild, maybe one or two tunnels a year, at most. I learned awhile back that MOLES EAT GRUBS.  As with any critter, eliminate the food source and reduce the problem.  So when I applied MILKY SPORE 3 times a year, for 2 years in a row as stated on the directions, my horrendous grub issue vanished and the moles with them.BUT, IF I still had a mole problem, this Deadset is an absolute Killing Machine.  My stepsister is selling her home so she needs a NOW solution, she doesn't have the luxury to wait for 2 years for the milky spore to work.  So we used this MOLE KILLING MACHINE where it's proven itself.  However, be aware that you will NOT want to use this Deadset Mole Killing Machine near pets or children.  The spikes are rather vicious - they WILL impale a human hand or a human foot or a dogs paw or a cats paw or that pet ferret that got loose, etc. Keep this in mind when deciding WHERE to locate the trap (er.. Killing Machine.)Meanwhile my neighbor's mole ventured a tunnel back into my yard.  Grabbed the Deadset, followed the directions to a T. Within short order...  Well, there's no more mole.. and my neighbor seems pleased his tunnels have suddenly stopped forming. Gee, I wonder why  ;-)The directions per the box:1. Water the lawn and active area (tunnels) thoroughly. A wet lawn keeps the moles food supply (grubs) close to the surface and makes it easy to place the mole trap in the ground.2. Locate the active tunnels. Poke a 1" hole in the raised earth through to the tunnel. Wait 24 hours. If the hole is resealed the tunnel is active.3. Press down on the raised earth with your foot, depressing the tunnel roof. Press the trap into the softened ground, then use FOOT PEGS to firmly set the trap in place.4. Raise and lower the HANDLE until the SPEARS move freely through the ground, making sure that nothing will get in the way of the SPEARS hen the mole trips the trap.5. With feet on FOOT PEGS, raise HANDLE to set the trap.** wrsweeney has some awesome videos regarding the setup of this trap - highly recommend watching them! **
summary: It's a killing machine - when set properly.  Avoid use around kids and pets.  Milky Spore anyone?

reviewText: This trap IS easy to set, it is fairly easy to stick in the ground although the tabs on the side are a bit small and I have rather large feet so I actually struggled getting enough force. Odd I know. I have had this in my yard and I haven't "caught" anything yet even though I know there are moles in the yard. I'll update this review if it turns out I get any. So for now the build quality is good and it looks like it will work so I'll rate it a 4 out of 5.
summary: No catches yet, and my foot is too big to get this in the ground

reviewText: I once captured a mole, not realizing what it was, and took it to the woods for safety.  It ran back immediately to the lawn from where it was "rescued."  I was quite embarrassed to discover that the critter was a pest, a real nuisance, and not a furry life needing saving.Now I'm keenly aware of the ripples in the earth left behind by burrowing moles.  I requested the Sweeney's 9015 Deadset Precision Mole Trap to rid our property of the destructive creatures and it has worked fine thus far.  Although it's largely made of plastic, we've had no difficult setting the trap, inserting it into the ground, or removing it by using a shovel after it has been successful.  I have not used a metal trap in the past, actually this is my first, so I can't make the comparison.  I personally like it's lighter weight and have no concerns about it being effected by rain or a hose.  I do recommend this trap for soils that aren't too hard or soft.  It works for us.

I really like this trap. It's easy to set and relatively safe for my kids and dog because everything above ground is safe. That being said, we haven't caught any moles yet. I've tried the trap in a few locations and followed the directions to the letter. However after more than a month we have yet to get our first mole. I'm keeping it set in hopes that we can get at least one of the pests that are eating up our back yard.
summary: Easy to Set... Haven't killed anything yet

reviewText: Every once in awhile I get critters tearing up my lawn, boring holes, etc.  I've used hoses, smoke bombs, poison, etc.  So I was happy to try out this Sweeney mole trap for my latest critter attack.  I found the Sweeney build quality to be good - appears rugged and should last for years.  Easy to set - plunger up and ready to go.  I warned my kids not to touch.It turns out my latest critter was a gopher (not a mole) - the Sweeney still took care of the problem.  At $21 not cheap but reasonable if it provides years of poison-free use.  Overall, I rate 5-stars in consideration of price/value.
summary: Turns out it works for gophers too

reviewText: We are overrun with gophers this year.  We have fewer moles; maybe the gophers overran them too.  I set the trap in a gopher tunnel where I had seen them popping their heads out & mocking me as they destroyed the soil behind/under my rock walls.  Within an hour of setting the trap, I had a gopher.  I reset the trap & the next day, I had another.I had been using Victor brand rat traps with a dab of peanut butter as bait.  That also works very well but is more tricky to set; you can hurt your fingers if you are not very careful.  This trap is easy to set and is also safer to use if you have dogs/cats outside.  They could get caught in a rat trap.  With this trap, the action takes place underground so unless you have a "digger", they should be okay.The trap seems to be well made and durable so can be used over & over.

Due to some serious construction nearby, our neighborhood has been inundated with critters who moved to seek a more stable environment.Out of the blue, shrubbery's dying, and it turns out to be moles and their tunnels. The mole trap seemed perfect.It wasn't difficult to set, but so far, no victims. I really had high hopes for this device.The next step's a professional exterminator.

I have not had any luck yet, not certain if it isn't easily triggered as advertised or my pest is wise to this deadly trap and is avoiding it. I guess time will tell it is well constructed and is holding up well to the elements outside. It is also easy to set up and use so I will continue to "try" and slay the beast diligence and several traps might be necessary

This is a very well built, heavy duty mole trap.  It is easy to set and the concept is a good one.  We have not caught a mole yet but are very close.  My husband set the trap right over the mole tunnel as instructed.  He said he thought it might work a little better if it were a tad wider.  The mole ran into the post part of the trap that is underground and went to the left of it instead of in between...LOL!  He got lucky that time!  I am sure this trap will catch the moles that we have because the principle of the trap is very sound.  I like the fact that the sharp parts are under ground where pets and children are not at risk of the trap.  The spring is also very heavy duty, with a lot of power and durability.8-15-2013Just wanted to add that this product has done its job very well!  We did get the mole and it works well!
summary: Sure it will do the job!

reviewText: This thing looks like a medieval torture device.  It's pretty heavy duty, designed so that you get in the ground easily, and when a mole comes by - WHAM, impaled.  I caught one mole the first day it was outside.  It's a pretty horrid looking death, but it has to be a LOT more humane than what we have been seeing - our chickens catching the moles and picking them to death.  Hens are worse than cats and will fight a cat for a mole!  It's been a week and we've got 3- one pretty big.  Anyway, we did have a few times the trap went off and no mole, but when we have got them, they've been dead.I like that it can be used again and again, and it seems sturdy.

How long should one wait before declaring a product effective?  Our Sweeney Deadset mole trap repeatedly trips above active tunnels, but I've yet to pull up an impaled mole or even see evidence one has been injured (blood, fur, etc).  The trap is easy to use and triggers at the slightest movement, but so far no luck.We own Jack Russell Terriers, excellent mousers and all-around varmint eradicators.  They effectively catch moles, but also make a mess.  The dogs have been trained not to dig in the yard because they have acres of surrounding woods to investigate.As a test, I let the dogs dig into the same burrows the Sweeney deadset trap is positioned in.  In a month's time, the dogs scored two moles.  Sweeney's scored zero.To be fair, Sweeney's suggests using multiple traps for improved success.  Perhaps that would help, but I hesitate to invest additional time and money into a product that might take an entire season (or longer) to do its job.  Based on the dog/trap test, moles are there, but it's a crapshoot whether or not Sweeney's will catch them.I haven't given up and am still giving the single trap I own a chance to prove itself.  The challenge is on and the dogs are no longer allowed to participate.  When the trap trips and there's actually a mole on the other end, I will happily upgrade my star rating.
summary: Might Work If You Have Time, Patience and More Than One Trap

reviewText: Sweeney's Deadset Mole Trap is the best way to deal with moles invading your lawn.  The device is sturdy, and easy to set. Most importantly, this trap is effective.I have tried pellets and flooding the moles out with little to no success.  When that didn't work I tried killing them with a shovel.  That was gruesome.Sweeney's Deadset Mole Trap gets the job done and saved my lawn.  Really I think this is the best way to get rid of moles when you are doing it yourself.
summary: the best way to get rid of moles when you are doing it yourself

reviewText: Moles are not easy to get rid of. I knew one older homeowner who read she could get rid of moles in her yard by hooking a hose to her car's exhaust and sticking the hose down the mole hole, and running the car on idle for 'a while.'  Given that her yard was riddled with mole hill holes, she had her work cut out for her.  Her efforts didn't seem to make much of a dent on the mole population, but she did burn out the catalytic converter in her car.This trap does seem to be more practical and business like. Also more environmentally correct.  It's impressive.  If I were a mole I'd see this as a sort of guillotine for moles.  I'm setting it as soon as I see evidence of this year's mole population in my yard, but I can't help thinking this may have more flash than real effect.  Sort of like those bug zappers, which make a lot of sparks and zaps, but only really kill a tiny percentage of the bugs in their vicinity.  Perhaps if I catch a mole I should drape its carcass on the trap as a warning to other moles.  Rather like the smell of burnt bugs might just discourage other bugs from getting too close?  I am giving this trap 3 stars for the impression it creates. I'm deducting 2 stars because it is not exactly easy to set.  Let's hope it doesn't stab the neighborhood cats or dogs....
summary: Cumbersome, not to say scary to set up

reviewText: Either we have smart moles, or I can't follow directions, or maybe the weather has been a factor.  I don't know, but the Sweeney Mole trap hasn't caught anything in five weeks here.  The yard is covered with tracks.  I tried to be careful and selective about placing the trap.  I've tried several different locations, all of which seemed to be active trails.  The trap has sprung exactly once, but it was empty.On the other hand, the trap is easy to set up and use.  So, in that respect, I can't complain.  Also, we have had unusually rainy weather here over the last month, so that may have caused behavioral changes for the moles - different trails and such.I don't know the answer, but we haven't caught any moles!

A mole was digging tunnels everywhere on the lawn.  The trap was placed in an active tunnel chosen because it was fairly recent.  It killed the mole in less than three hours.It appeared to have killed the mole quickly though it was certainly a gruesome sight to behold.  It seems the other moles can smell death on the trap because they have avoided it even after thorough washing.I do wish there were a way to get rid of the moles without killing them.  I also think a mole's life is worth more than grass and that killing them just for a pretty lawn is morally wrong.  They are just doing what they are supposed to do and they have their place in the universe and that should be respected.If you do want to kill moles, though, this is certainly an efficient trap.
summary: Killed the mole in just a few hours

reviewText: Living in southeast USA I have problems with these subterranean critters and I have use similar traps that was more effective. Sweeney's 9015 Deadset Precision Mole Trap is fairly well made but it has a lot of plastic. The other mole traps were made of all steel and was easier to use. I'm afraid that I will break the plastic prongs that I push into the ground. I didn't have to worry with the older and smaller mole steel traps.I like it ok but it's difficult to use. Although dangerous, I prefer to dray fumes into the mole hills. I have used gasoline but now I use mole gas that I find at my local Farmers Supply store. It is quicker and moe efficient than a one kill device. I have also used mole or rodent poison pellets. This product is practically useless if you have a large infestation because it will only get one mole per time if you're lucky. If you have a small mole problem, I can see how this could work.

My mom has always had problems with moles in her yard.  Years ago, she tried the typical things -- the little spinning flag things that create vibrations and electronic devices.  Of course, those didn't work.  We have never tried chemical options because of our dogs.  The only time our current dogs are loose in the yard is when we are with them, so the Sweeney's Deadset trap is okay.  (the dogs don't stray far from our sides)  There is NO WAY I would have used this setup with the dogs we had in the past.  It would be extremely easy for a dog or child to get injured (quite severely) if their curiosity took over for even a minute.  Anyhow, setup was not just an easy 2 step procedure.  You want to make sure to read the instructions thoroughly.  There is prep work that goes into placing the "trap" successfully.  If you don't mind trial and sometimes error during the initial setup work, then I highly recommend this trap.  You also can't be too squeamish when emptying the trap.  I won't empty it solely for that reason.  I may not be a good daughter because of this, but I tell my mom it's her yard when it's time to empty the trap.
summary: More of a killing machine than a "trap"

reviewText: Installed this over the largest, most seemingly active, hole, and found it tripped the next day with no mole in the trap. Still, will try again... Trap itself seems well-built and should serve for a good long time. Am iffy on trapping the mole, but do want to prevent large holes close to the house.
summary: Strong mole trap, but I haven't caught one yet

reviewText: My original review was only three stars.  I knew I had an active mole tunnel because after I punched a hole in it, it was repaired the next day.  The problem wasn't with the trap; rather, it was the way I was setting it.I thought I was following the instructions correctly but I was seating the trap deep enough.  The trick for me was to firmly compress the dirt over the tunnel and then place the trap as close to the ground as possible.  You then need to run the spikes up and down a few times to make sure nothing is in the way.After about 3 weeks in the same location, I moved the trap to another active tunnel.  The next day -- by no small coincidence -- I was in the yard and I heard the trap get triggered.  I expected to see some blood on the spikes but there wasn't any.  I know it got the mole because the tunnel has not been repaired since.I repositioned to another active hole and got another one about a week later.  I don't think I have any more active mole tunnels; but, if I do, watch out for the Sweeney Deadset Mole Trap.Crude but effective.  I endorse this product 100%.
summary: I got the mole and I was there!

reviewText: This is much easier to set than the standard traps that I've used in the past, far simpler.  Just determine where to place the trap (there are excellent directions for that for newbie mole hunters), pull the handle a few times to make sure that it will spring effectively; and wait.  With the upper portions of this being non-metal, there should be less rust as well.The only thing that could make this a more attractive buy would be an electronic sensor that could spot the most active mole run for you.  But I shudder at the thought of what that might cost.  :-)
summary: Nice improvement to the basic trap

reviewText: We have a lot of mole holes through our yard, living so close to the woods it is hard to get rid of them.  The Deadset mole trap seems like a great idea and design, but I have yet to actually get a mole.You have to make sure that the tunnel is an active tunnel by poking a hole in the to and coming back in 24 hrs to see if the hole is closed.  If it is then your tunnel is active.  You then poke your trap spears into the hole and raise and lower them several times to be sure they can move freely in the soil.  Then pull your handle up and set it.The handle is a little bit difficult to get to stay up in the ready to go position, but can be done if you are careful.  I will update this review if I ever do get any moles.  It has only been 2 weeks so far, I haven't given up hope yet!

We have moles and voles, always have. I tried everything from Juicy Fruit Gum to milky spore. Well, I HIGHLY recommend this productSt Gabriel 40oz Milky Spore 1/4 Acre Powder RTUover everything else.This trap is rather easy to use and is seriously strong. If you have had luck with other traps, then this should be awesome!!I used the other product, the Milky Spore and it's just like it says. You have to spread it all over, wait a very  long time, but then you get YEARS of mole/vole-free lawn. Totally worth it. Maybe try both at the same time.
summary: A strong trap, rather easy to use, not too effective in my yard.

reviewText: This is a pretty rough looking device.  Actually, I think it is a great design and probably the best available.  It is NOT quite as sensitive as they say it is, though.  You definitely need to bump the metal tab to get it to go off.  If you follow the instructions to a "T", and partially compress the hole with the trap, your chances are better, but still not a guarantee.I also noticed that the spikes are far enough apart that a mole could conceivably escape by being completely inside their perimeter when the trap goes off.  I'm not sure, exactly, why there are not more spikes.  Perhaps the manufacturer thought having additional spikes was overkill.I was interested to see how many other products they sell to get rid of moles.  The chart on the Amazon page shows the differences and mentions this is suitable for use around children.  I know that they are trying to point out it's not poisonous, but I wouldn't leave my kids playing in the yard around these set traps.  Even if they were set off while still in the ground, the spikes alone are dangerous in the hands of small children.Overall, I think it's probably your most solid chance to successfully get rid of moles.
summary: Careful planning determines rate of success.

reviewText: We have a significant mole problem. We've tried spreading chemicals to discourage them, but it doesn't work as well as we'd like. I don't actually mind the moles out in the pasture, but I don't like them near the house. This trap is fantastic. It's easy to set, and if you make sure you have a life tunnel the mole ends up dead. It's important to check for a live tunnel. We have a great many tunnels and some of them are no longer in use. If you make a hole in the tunnel and the mole fills it up the next morning, try to set the trap on that tunnel. It works. I've only caught one mole so far, but it worked on the first try.I had never used a mole trap before, so I have no comparison, but the trap is easy to set, triggers with slight pressure, and best of all, it catches the moles.
It kills, and i'm a tenderheart that doesn't like killing.  But this darn critter was damaging our apartment's community garden, and so I set this up in a recent tunnel, and he is no more.

If points are awarded thusly: 1 point to the moles for each day they evade death and 1 point to me for each mole I kill, the current score is Team Mole: eleven, Me: zero.I have obvious active hills and tunnels in my yard and have followed the directions, watched the video and tried 3 different locations and not had the trap spring even once.Not only is it ineffective but it is hard to use.  I can't be sure if I have a defective unit or if there is a design flaw, but my trap is intermittently impossible to set.  There is a catch that should lock into place when you raise the handle,  to hold the spikes up until they are triggered.  It is a constant fight to get mine to catch.  I'd say it works 1 out of 15 attempts.  Furthermore, I'd think by design, it should take minimal motion to spring the trap, if you will a hair trigger, so you'd have the best chance of impaling the vermin.  If I ever do get mine to lock in the set position, it is virtually impossible to get it to trigger.  The little lever on the side seems to jam so you can't spring it manually to test.  You can jostle it, kick it, drpo it from shoulder height and throw it across the yard (which I have in fact DONE) without springing the trap.I'm going to keep trying to get this to work because I really hate moles and what they are doing to my yard.  If I have any success, I will revise my review but for now, I cannot recommend this product.

Sweeney's deadset precision mole trap is easy to set and highly effective if you can identify an active tunnel. We killed three moles in a month in our yard and there are still more to kill, our yard must be mole-central, but we keep moving the trap to new areas and once we identify tunnels that are still active we do manage to rid ourselves of moles. I would recommend getting more than one trap if your yard is overrun like ours.
summary: Works, but you might need more than one.

reviewText: My experience with this trap:1) Easy setup.  There are a lot of mole traps out there, based on similar designs (a spring-loaded collection of sharp spikes that are sprung when a mole moves below it).  I've had a few different models.  This has been the easiest to set.  A well designed handle and latch allow you to set it up with little chance of getting hurt with those spikes.  Be warned, though...the spikes are VERY sharp.  The trap came well packaged to protect me from the spikes.  However, once opened, you should be very careful in how you handle this.  DEFINITELY KEEP THIS OUT OF THE REACH OF CHILDREN.2) After a couple days, whatever it was that was digging up our front lawn (not sure if it was a mole or sometihng else) set off the trap.  Because the creature gets trapped while underground, I never saw what the animal was.  However, I've yet to see any new lawn damage since that day.But take note:There is some luck and some work involved.  Depending on the extent of your pest problem, your results may vary.  Don't expect to set it and forget it.  The manufacturer does a good job explaining how to prepare for your trap: watering your lawn brings bugs and, therefore, moles to the surface.  Then you need to locate an active tunnel and depress the ground a bit where you plan to put the trap (because the mole pushing the ground back up is what sets off the trap).If you are persistent, and willing to do a little work, this trap is a good way to go.  Good luck!

I got this trap because we were having a huge mole problem in our yard.  We had said we were just going to live in peace with it and no traps until it started running amok in our garden area and actually managed to get up into our raised garden beds (that had protective barrier underneath.) We were seeing new mole hills every day, in and around the garden beds.Two days before the trap arrived, I went to water the garden beds and found a large bloody area, no sign of what caused it though.  After that...no more mole activity.  So something in nature must have taken care of the mole.  We set up the trap, but it remained empty because the mole was already gone.  So I can only review how it was to set up and the quality of it.  It was super easy to set up and use.  It's a solid, well-built trap that was higher quality than I was expecting.  If we have new mole activity, I will update this review to reflect if the trap catches the mole or not.

Having set this trap according to instructions at various locations around the yard over the weeks I have owned it, I have yet to impale a mole.Granted, something sets it off and it penetrates into the ground just fine where the mole *should* be. I really cannot say why I haven't nailed one yet. The trap is plenty sturdy and of quality manufacture. The yard is plagued with the critters and there is no shortage of molehills.In summary, I think I have simply been unlucky, (or rather the moles have been lucky), because there seems to be no logical reason for this trap to not work.I will say that if I had cats around, I would not use this trap. You know how cats can get into things and places where they are not supposed to be and if one dug around the trap with his paw, he might get nailed. But, of course, if I had cats I would likely not have the moles in the first place.I won't say to not try this product but I have to be honest and point out that, in my case, it was not effective.

Pest control is a challenge especially when you are trying to get rid of moles. This year we had a spur in the population of these nasty little critters and I have been using this little machine for the past two weeks. I have been able to trap and kill one and hoping for more success.It is easy to set it up and activate.  The trap is ergonomically designed; with a firm grasp, push the trap into the mole-mound (by first watering the area and rendering it wet). Push the activator plate (situated on the trap) a little harder into the ground using your foot and lift the lever; you are all set. The manufacturer also has a video demonstration of how to use this tool, but it is a simple machine to operate. The triggering system is activated by the slightest movement in the underground and the sharp spears quickly get the mole. The machine sometimes bumps accidentally perhaps due to foraging animals in which case you have to re-set or redeploy the trap.It is easy to clean the trap with water and can be reused. It withstands sun & rain and the quality of the product is excellent. When this is activated or when not in use; keep the kids away from this tool since the spears are very sharp and can harm young children. I have rated four stars for its design, quality and utility.1.P3 International Sonic Mole Chaser P79002.Victor 0610 Easy Set Gopher Trap

It's been over a year and this trap has not killed any mole.  However, we have noticed that since those thousands of 7-year cicadas are not around this summer, the moles have left.  Apparently they came for the cicadas. We had never seen any moles in our 12 years living here until the cicadas started coming out of the ground.The mole tunnels have become prolific during the past week that this trap has been set.  So far, the only thing that seems to work are the 'bombs' we bought at the local hardware store.  We will post any results we have with this trap.
summary: No moles trapped so far update

reviewerName: Richard C. Drew "Anaal Nathra/Uthe vas Bethod...
reviewText: This is really a clever design, fully mechanical and easy to use. It's triggered by the upward movement of the earth as the Mole moves beneath the ground in it's tunnel. There's a trigger plate that rests against the tunnel. Mole passes beneath. Plate moves up. Deadly spikes shoot downward, propelled by a strong spring. Mole gets impaled by the trap. Simple, elegant and deadly. There are also instructions on finding a "live" tunnel vs an unused one, so you don't waste your time setting the trap where it will never be introduced to the Mole.The trap can be used again and again. Plus, since the mole is exterminated beneath the ground, it's already buried. No mess, no fuss. Just a smelly spot in the ground for a few days. Toss on some lime and more dirt, and that will disappear in short order.

As anyone who's ever encountered them will tell you Moles are the baddest of the underground bad for lawns and gardens.  I'm sharing some farmland this summer on my brother's farm to grow some fresh veggies and raise a few cattle and we've had the problem really bad.  My bro's tried and true farm solutions haven't been too successful and so when I saw this on vine I grabbed it (did you ever in a million years think you'd be buying a mole trap on Amazon?????).  I gave it to bro and I watched him set it up.  Took all of five minutes.  Three days later he called me in the city and said deed done...mission accomplished!  So it set's up incredibly easy for a spring trap and it works.  Can't beat the price.  So if you want to keep those insidious mole people from letting your lawn or garden travel through time and end the summer intact this is the tool for you!  My apologies to George Pal.
summary: Easy Set Up and Does The Job

reviewText: It is very easy to use and since the spikes will only go off if the device is tripped from underneath, it is safe to use if you have pets. It seems weather proof as I have had it outside and with sprinklers and I have not seen any signs of rust.I have not however seen any results from the trap. I have not seen any mounds of dirt in the yard either so it is possible that the critters happen to not be active at the moment. Maybe they now know this is installed and waiting for them?  They were causing a lot of havoc and mess in the yard right before we set this up.I will have to wait and see how it performs once I see more activity. If you do keep it in on a lawn you have to remember to remove it to cut the grass.I am going to leave it armed and in place waiting to see how well it works. I am rating this 4 stars because it's very well made and sturdy and it was so  easy to set up.  If I find this works for us, it's a 5 star product for sure and I'll update the review and the rating.

I had high hopes for this trap. We have a ton of moles here and it was easy to find a mole tunnel to set up the trap according to the directions.  Twice the trap was tripped, and no dead mole.  After that, the trap is not even being tripped, I have tried everything with this trap to make it kill these pest moles, but with no luck.  In my book this is an easy to set trap that does nothing to rid your place of mole infestation.  Not a single dead mole to show for the trouble. Not recommended.
summary: Easy to set and doesn't catch a single mole

reviewText: This puncture style mole trap is a plastic version of the older metal ones I have.  It sets easily, but in trials the prongs penetrated the ground between 1 and 2 inches deep.  I would prefer a consistent 2 inches for moles, so this means you have to be very particular regarding where you set this trap, making sure you've set it over the mole run with loose soil.I'd like the spring to be a bit stronger for greater soil penetration.  Now, the set instructions include "Raise and lower trap until spears move freely through the ground."  In other words, make sure you DON'T have a 1 inch penetration.  But these instructions are on the web site, not on the packaging.Moles are a frustrating animal to deal with for many homeowners.  Nothing is more frustrating than to set out traps and watch the mole travel around the yard with seeming impunity.  The usual issues are the trap location and the trap set. The mole is really the most predictable thing!One alternative to mole trapping is developing a "mole garden." Moles are very territorial, so consider developing an area in your lawn where the mole is happy to forage.  Once you've had moles, you'll probably keep having them.  Those deep tunnels probably last years, so a new mole dispersing to a lawn that had a previous mole trapped out is going to find it to his or her liking.  So keep trapping, or find a way to live with them.
summary: Trade off with ease of setting versus a stronger spring

reviewText: Kills moles dead as can be, the Sweeney Deadset Precision Mole Trap triggers reliably and kills the tunneling vermin deader'n the career of a comedian with no sense of humor. The mole trap is easy to set, does it's job, and hasn't broken so far. I'm really not a fan of plastics, I'd prefer if it were metal framed, but in this age that truly seems like asking for too much. As long as the plastic doesn't crack and break from UV exposure, all will be well.

I ordered this device to help with my 'war of the gophers'.  They create small hills all over the yard and I get tired of mowing over them.It was very easy to set and the instructions were very good.  The entire thing is well built and I think it will last a long time. I will post a review update if I am successful in terminating one of the enemy.  Ha.
summary: Easy to set, good quality that should last.

reviewText: This works well, but plan to check it frequently because it goes off constantly.  If you can get past the fact that it goes off 10 times for every successful result, then I highly recommend you try this.
summary: Too sensitive but otherwise it works well.

reviewText: The other mole traps I have tried have always been very difficult to set. This one solves that problem! Consequently I will use it more. I have a never ending invasion of moles in my yard but was always a little nervous when trying to set and reset the traps so I was often lax about trying to hold down the invasion. That said, now all I need is for the varmints to just use the same tunnel twice so I can "nail" them!
summary: Very easy to set mole trap!

reviewText: In the two weeks that I've had this I have already caught 2 moles. Well, I can't say that I actually caught them, but my gardener used this Precision Mole Trap and HE caught them. He followed the directions implicitly and has had great luck. These particular moles were on the lot adjacent to my beach house, which is on the Oregon Coast. We watered the lawn the night before to drum up all the worms and grubs that the moles like to eat and placed the trap on the biggest mole hill. Sure as shoooting, the next morning there was a dead mole in the trap. While I can't stand any animal cruelty whatsoever I'm choosing to believe that this trap kills instantly without any suffering to the poor little moles. He looked pretty peaceful and not tormented so let's hope it was a quick and painless demise. Either way, I'm glad to be rid of those pesky moles so my yard won't be all torn up with big sandy mole hills anymore. I think there were only 2 moles in the yard, but I'm keeping this mole trap on standby in case any more unwanted guests arrive.

This is my second mole trap. The other one that had a scissor trap did not work because the soil here in Georgia is clay - soft and mushy when wet and hard as concrete when dry. The soil grabbed the blades and wouldn't close on the rodent. This Sweeney trap works on a completely different principle. When the mole trips the trap it gets stabbed by four "nails" that shoot at high-speed into the soil. I'm not going to go over the instructions because there's a video posted that shows you how to use the trap. I did find it very easy to set and clean up after. I kept the soil moist in the area so the soil didn't harden too much. It worked perfectly. The trap seems to be well-constructed and should last a long time because living out in the woods means I always have moles coming to feast on my grass so this will get plenty of use.Warning: Make sure if you have little kids that they stay away from this trap.Highly recommended.

I've had this trap for over a month, loaded into 2 different runs. Unfortunately, we've had no success with spearing one of these things. We have voles, not moles, so perhaps that is the issue. The trap never triggered. Perhaps we'll try again when the weather cools.

I'm sure it's a great trap, but it hasn't worked so far.It was kind of a pain to install, so it might help (sorry to sound sexist) if you're a guy.Personally, I didn't find it very user friendly.The instructions really sucked.And it hasn't worked so far (I live in Chicago, YMMV).

With this type of mole trap, dirt has to be soft in order for the spikes to penetrate. So far, we are unable to kill a mole with this trap. In theory, it is well constructed, seems to work perfectly with the mechanism is has, however we have not been able to kill any moles or gophers with this product. I am only giving it two stars because of the type of trap it is, it needs special conditions for it to work properly. Like manicured lawns, with softer dirt than we have. It's built very well, durable, and will last a long time.

Moles invading our lawn are a bane of ours every year so my husband is constantly seeking out ways to eliminate them. This is not one of them. It takes so much pressure to spring the trap that the mole would almost have to jump into it for it to work.

Sweeney's Mole Trap is a terrific, easy-to-set, safe trap. Unlike many of the all-metal mole traps on the market, this one features an ergonomic design, tough plastic parts, a graspable handle, an activator plate that can be pushed into the ground by foot, and a patented triggering system. The trap requires no assembly and is simple to use.The package includes illustrated operating instructions, as well as a mobile scan with access to a detailed instructional video.The trap can be used multiple times. It has a trap release lever to disengage the trap once it's been activated. It is weather resistant. I appreciate the safety and construction of this particular trap.
summary: A Safe Mole Trap! (except for moles)

reviewText: My mole problem isn't in my yard, but rather at a quasi-primitive cemetery in a remote corner at the tree line, where we own a large group of plots and several family members are buried.  The mole activity has not been constant, but has shown up now and then.  This summer, the rainy midwest weather pattern seems to have made him (them) them active in our plot area again.  This Sweeney's Deadset Mole Trap came along at an opportune time.  My experience:This trap has a heavy plastic (or plastic-like composite material) frame, with steel components on the business end (spring, fork tines, etc).  Follow the simple instructions and deployment is a snap.I set the trap and checked daily, and in the first two days I got a couple of false trippings (no kill) but I believe it was due to the track being bumped by foraging deer (or human visitors?) in the evenings. Each time I relocated the trap to another apparent traffic area. (I don't know mole psychology . . . does the tripped trap scare them off, or rather allow them to become desensitized and comfortable with the mechanical intruder?) I also have some thoughts about the accidental bumping problem - what I did to try and deal is described below.After the two falses, on day three I discovered a mole kill.  The trap worked just as it was supposed to.  You can't improve on that. I don't know if the eliminated mole was a lone pest or part of a group - the kill was just a couple days ago. I stamped down the tunnels, and will monitor and redeploy as needed.Now, some added thoughts on the trapped being tripped by being bumped - whether by humans, wildlife, or pets.  The trap frame is black, and is arguably darn near invisible at night.  Working on the assumption that moles, #1 Don't surface to reconnoiter, and #2 Have trouble reading English anyway -- I thought perhaps a light colored flag or tag hanging on the handle would help keep it from being accidentally bumped by surface traffic.  It may be coincidence, but after I hung a tag following my two false trips, there were no more (yet).  And in my case, the trap is deployed in an area accessible to the public including children . . . so I actually labeled my handle tag boldly, "DANGER - Mole Trap, Sharp Spikes, DON'T TOUCH". And in my case, I'll also have to accommodate the mowing routine of the cemetery caretaker, taking down the trap as needed.This thing works, and performed exactly as designed.  Read and follow the simple instructions.

I dislike the heck out of moles, and we have terrible issues with them. My family has a place out in the country and the moles always ravage the lawn, and are a pain to get rid of. We've used all types of methods to control them, from cats to traps; in the past I've used traps like these but made out of metal to great effect. You've probably seen the type, hard to set and hard to use, rusting all the time, a hassle really, so when I saw this I wanted to try it out. The way these are designed and the fact that they are cheap to buy make those old ones somewhat obsolete, but most of all they work well. The spring is strong and the trap is pretty durable; both fears I had when I saw a plastic frame like this. Like another reviewer stated, when they saw the spring they knew this would be a killer. I felt that way when I pulled it back, knowing this thing would do the job fine. I've taken out three moles with one so far too, and plan on getting more to take back control.

I'm a big believer in "live and let live", but when I moved into my new home and spent big bucks on landscaping, the gophers moved in too. Discouraging to find that the reason some plants were looking sickly was that their roots had been eaten right up to the surface level of the ground. This trap is a welcome addition to the numerous Exhart devices I have deployed. For anyone who has gone through the delicate excavation process involved in setting the old fashioned gopher traps, the Sweeney's comes as a pleasant surprise: read and follow the instructions, and it truly is a snap to deploy.

I read a lot of the other reviews before posting mine.My experience with this mole trap was the same as some of the others....  It didn't seem as if the trap was as sensitive as it should have been.I noticed a lot of the reviewers mentioned this aspect of it.It did go off finally but I felt it must have missed many days in which the little critters had gone about their business unharmed.There were a couple of times it was set off and nothing to show for it...  but on the third time it did get its mole.So mine worked after a few misses.My experience seems to be the same as some of the others.Overall I had to approve it because nothing ever works perfectly but if it does the job it's supposed to that's about all I ask of a product.
summary: Easy to set  ---  Very simple instructions provided

reviewText: We've had a problem with knock-out roses suddenly losing their roots lately. One day they're fine, the next day they're wilted. I read somewhere that moles only eat grubs and earthworms, and the voles (those cute little e-wock things with short tails) use the mole burrows to travel in to eat the roots.  Either way, same results.This trap is plastic but very sturdy and easier to set than the metal ones.  Just be sure the trail is active. Stomp a section of the burrow down and wait over-night. If the burrow has popped up again it is being used, so set the trap.  Nature takes it's course.

reviewerName: Y. R. Wu "The will to win is nothing without ...
reviewText: Summary - much easier to set than the Victor brand version.  Don't read any more if you're squeamish.  This is not a humane trap!We have a persistent mole problem.  This is the second plunger trap I've bought - see the picture.You use this type of trap by finding an active tunnel, then setting up a booby trap where a set of six sharp spikes on a plate comes down with great force when the mole tunnels underneath.  Mole-kebab.I have a friend who swears by this type of trap.  He has aVictor 0645 Mole Trap Plunger Styleand I purchased the same.  He had a lot of luck, but I must not have the same  Perhaps my moles are smarter.  My yard is also on a slight slop and I have a lot of sand and clay, which doesn't help.It helps for the soil to be damp when you set the trap.  You also want the plunger to stick into the ground a few times so the spikes can go into the mole and not into the ground.  This trap was MUCH easier to set, and the force of the spring is a LT stronger.  Assuming I can get a good tunnel to set it up on, I'm hoping i'll have good news to report in an update.

They are loose fitting but do not appear stretchable as the advertising suggests. If I use them to train a planted small shrub or tree for instance, I will need to remember to remove them as the tree grows so not to choke growth. Maybe they will break as the trunk or branch they are attached to grows but I'll certainly have a problem removing them at that time and I'd rather not be proven right. So I'm back to my Gardener's Blue Ribbon Stretch tape which I would need to have on hand anyway for any larger staked plant.The one place where the Global Garden Clips are a right solution is with my Desert Rose (Ademium). These like most succulent plants, Jades,giant sunflowers, and euphorbia are top heavy and have a tendency to bend and topple from the top weight. Also clematis and other vines can get top heavy as they grow and start tumbling. The clips can unobtrusively anchor and support the weight to allow the plant or vine to bring me continued joy in my garden.At the time of this review, the per clip cost is just over 50 cents apiece. Ouch!With 20 in a bag, the global Garden Plant Clip is an expensive solution for securing a plant. So unless, the plant is decorative and I want to make a statement at my entrance door or patio or it's a particular favorite vine that I enjoy from a favorite window, I'm back toGardener's Blue Ribbon 150 ft Sturdy Stretch Tie T007A.  What's important to you and your application will determine if this is a right solution in your life.
summary: An Expensive Product with a Found Solution

reviewText: I really like these plant clips, but I find them a little tricky, and a little fussy, to get on my fingers just right.  They are unusable unless positioned just so on the fingers, but once they are, they do work great and make clipping plants to supports a one-handed operation.  They're designed to look like little leaves, which makes them both cute and a little more inconspicuous, and they're also designed to pop open if the stem gets too big for the clip.  I got these late in the season and haven't had a stem outgrow a clip yet, so I can't evaluate how well that works, but I see it coming with next year's tomatoes.  If it works right, it will be a great way to avoid choking and damaging growing stems.  If it doesn't work right, I'll report back to let fellow gardeners know.

These clips are very nice and work well.  However, they are a bit expensive.  They will hold plants/stems/vines on thinner stakes.  In order to work them, you insert a finger into each loop and either close them or pull them apart to open, so it requires a little effort, but it is easy to clip plants or vines or stems into place very quickly and often more easily than when using twine or twist ties,  The green color allows the clips to blend in nicely with the plants.
summary: Nice, Work Well, Easy To Use But a Bit Expensive

reviewText: Ok, before I get lots of hate mail I want to say that the product works . . . that is . . . if the stem of the plant and its stake or pole are of the right diameter.  So if you think you can use these clips to fasten a skinny plant to a skinny pole it will fall down the plant stem until it either falls to the root base or to a stem - kinda like someone trying to wear pants too big.  This device did not work for me with my orchid plant because of that issue.  However this winter I am hopeful to use them successfully with my tomatoes-on-the-vine plants that I have growing in my earthboxes.  I will update then.  But for now I will take a leap of faith and say (based upon my past experience with securing tomatoes to poles) that I am optimistic of success.  I like the look and feel of the product.

These plant clips are the easiest ones I've ever used. My only complaint is that they did not work with all the stakes I had - they work best with thin to medium sized ones. I used them on roses, tomatoes, and snap peas. I can hold the plant with one hand and snap these on with the other. In one case, the rosebuds got too heavy and the clip opened, but it didn't cause the stem to snap. I like that they are made out of recycled materials and that all of them made it to be reused for at least one more year.

The gimmick with these seems to be that you can operate them with one hand, slipping your fingers into the curved side handles and snapping into place. They work okay, look like they will hold up for several seasons. But I really don't see the advantage over a reel of twist ties.These arrived too late in the growing season to put them to use, I'll try them out on my dahlias next summer.I don't know how much they sell for, but at this point my feeling is, I would not buy them.If they show outstanding performance in next year's garden, I'll update this review.

I received this in the winter, so I haven't been able to test it through a growing season. But I did test it on a plant stake and it seems to work really well; therefore 4 stars. I hope so, because it's a pain to find the right kind of ties that will hold a plant without damaging it as it grows. Will update this review in the Spring or Summer after I've been able to test it further.Update: Used them to tie up my roses which are just starting to leaf out and bud, and so far so good! Much quicker to "clip" these than mess with ties. Great little product and if they make it through the season, I'll be ordering lots more. And I mean a LOT. I have so many plants that need staking and this will really help.UPDATE May 2014: I've used these for a number of months now and they work great. I will continue using them and buy more since we have more than 75 roses in our garden, and lots of flowers & vegetables and that need staking. Finally plant holder that is easy to use and doesn't need to be cut, twisted or tied. Reusable, too!They are a bit expensive at 50 each, but I will buy them along with plant stakes and use them season to season. Hopefully they will sell a bulk pack too.

These clips are easy to use. Just snap together to close. They hold securely but are easy to take apart when you need to. I wish the green color was darker so that they would blend in better and be less noticable.They work well for attaching the plant stem to any stake that has horizontal wires. If you just have a plain vertical stake (like in the case of orchids) these clips won’t do anything. They just slide down to the bottom. The opening is one size and you can’t tighten it around the stem/stake.
summary: Good product, but not good for orchids

reviewText: I use pretty much everything to tie/clip up the plants in my garden from twist ties (too fussy) to twine (degrades over time, plus who wants to deal with knots?) to pieces of garden Velcro tape (fine, but not cost effective) to little tiny spring-loaded hairclips that orchid growers use to stake orchids (perfect, but not great for thick stems and the metal bits rust out over time). My favorite have become the little spring loaded clips because they are so easy to use- simply squeeze one end, and the other pops open. Very easy to shift up the length of a stem without much fuss and doesn't damage the plant. I decided to try these because they seemed like a similar product but designed specifically for gardening use.They work a little differently than the spring loaded clips (you put your fingers into loops, snap them closed or pull them apart to open) so they are *little* fussier, but they are much better than twist ties and twines because no tying is required. Once you get the hang of them, they are easy to use. They also DO blend in nicely with the plants - they look like little tendrils of leaves. I like that you can grab a handful and use them on either one plant that needs support and guidance (my 20+ foot passiflora vine needs constant clipping) or as needed throughout the garden (droopy tomato stalk? clip to the trellis and you are done.)I can't yet speak to durability, or if these will survive a season of Florida sun and high temps (things tend to degrade very quickly around here) but I'm excited to see how they do.

These Global Garden Friends Ultimate Plant Clips work well on both Tomato and Bean plants. My sister is the gardener in the family and she keeps a garden all year in the southern part of the country so we tried these out on the plants she had in the ground.The clips attach nicely to the little green garden stakes and it is easy to route the stems through the clips for the needed support. These blend in with the plants and look fairly natural.These are fairly expensive but work as described.Recommended!CFH

I have recently started to plant a few things, I have a black thumb usually.  Receiving this Vine product to review was right up my alley.  I found it to work just as they said it would, I actually found an easier way for my arthritic hands to deal with them.  It might not work for everyone, as it is a two hand application, I just grasped it with my right and left forefingers and thumbs and pulled it gently apart, I came in from the plant's stalk towards the dowel I was using as support for the plant...it worked PERFECTLY!  I was please, it did not break, it stayed in place even without "locking" it together..but I DID lock it in place just to make sure it locked, etc.  I am pleased with this and sure would purchase more and would also recommend to others.

Pros:- The clips are easy to use. I'm 6'2" and in possession of fairly large hands and fingers, and I find it easy to hold and install these clips with one hand.- The clips are green and don't stand out amongst the plants (on the con side, the clips are green and so they're harder to find when you need to move them!)- They're strong and secure enough to helpfully attach my plants to their supporting bamboo posts.Cons:- They're not one-size-fits-all - they're too big for little seedlings and not big enough for large plants...but the spectrum of branch sizes that are a good fit is pretty large.- They clip fairly securely...but not perfectly. Or not completely securely. This isn't really a true "con," however, as this means that the clips are less likely to choke off a growing plant.

This plant clips are quite a bit different than many I’ve seen and the reusable factor is a real plus.  Some of the ones that are circular and open up to clip wear out in time and break at the joint.  The Ultimate Plant Clips are one solid piece of plastic all the way around and have enough give so they won’t snap.  They can be removed and used time after time.The clips themselves are very interesting looking as they themselves are in the shape of a vine with leaves on either end.  They are easy to attach to plants and can either be removed or moved without harming the plant.  These are going to see heavy use with plants such as tomatoes and cukes, but are also good for flowers.  If you’re going to be doing a lot of vertical garden growing, you may wish to pick up a package with more in it.FEATURES:☼  Works with your hand’s natural motion to secure your plants fast and easy☼  It won’t kill your plant’s by choking their stems, the clip has enough give to let them grow☼  Its quality, durable and flexible design keeps your plants secured for years☼  Recyclable plastic☼  Environmentally friendlyGLOBAL GARDEN FRIENDS:Global Garden Friends Ultimate Plant CageGlobal Garden Friends trelc1 Ultimate Trellis KitGlobal Garden Friends Ultimate Plant Clip, 50-PackGlobal Garden Friends 20-Pack Ultimate Plant ClipGlobal Garden Friends plants6 Ultimate Plant StakeGlobal Garden Friends plantc2500 Ultimate Plant Clip, 2500-Pack
summary: A perfect, reusable clips that would work nicely in vertical gardens ...

reviewText: I am a male of average size (5'10" tall) with normal-sized hand (size Large gloves). The pictures show someone with *much* smaller hands.[1] While these clips might be usable by such a person, they are all but unusable by me.The pictures show three different grips. The one I could get to work best was the one with the loop toward my wrists.[2] I could get the other two grips to work if my hands were dry. However, with a little moisture, the inherent slipperiness of the clip combined with its mismatch to the size and contours of my hand would cause it to slide around, even off the hand. This was for closing the clip.For opening it, I could get only the first grip to work, and then not every time. The problem is that the finger "grips" are too slippery and flexible to apply much pressure to the locking mechanism. The lock is designed to open by the sides shearing away from each other. Although it is possible to pop the lock open (sides moving directly away from each other), the finger loops at too flexible to generate the needed force and I couldn't grip the sides strongly enough. The only way I got it to pop was to push the main loop down over my finger until the finger over-filled the loop.The clips were extremely hard to open the first few times that I used them. I found that I needed to open and close them 3-4 times to have any chance of opening them using the finger grips. With more repetitions, it became easier. I would recommend against using these with actual plants without this "conditioning". I have *not* subjected the clips to weathering to know how that affects their operation.[3]My larger hand and finger size reduced the range of orientations of the clip relative to my hand. This repeatedly resulted in me having to contort my wrist and arm to try to get the clip properly oriented with the stake and the plant stem.[4] What I wanted from these clips was the ability to reach into difficult locations and to easily and sure-handedly clip a stem to a stake or other support. Instead of being allowed to contort my wrist and arm as needed, these clips forced me to put my hand into contorted positions even for the simplest applications. I practiced applying them using vines I was about to trim and that convinced me to not even try to use them with tender stems -- the sliding around on my fingers was too much. Finally, I have zero confidence that I would be able to open the snap without damaging a tender stem.----[1] "smaller hands": My thumb and finger fill and/or stretch the loops in the different grips. The pictures show fingers that don't come close to that.[2] The picture showing two hands: one closing and one opening the clips. On the package, this is the only one illustrated.[3] Note: I repeated this experiment on clip after clip in the package with the same result to ensure that I wasn't just testing a bad sample.[4] Notice in the picture with the Sunflower that the hand with the clip is vertical. This is not simply for photo composition, but reflects roughly the position of the hand needed for that grip.-- Douglas B. Moran

These worked great for my rose bush but not for my cherry tomato plants because the clips were too loose on them.  I love that they blend in with the stems, are reusable, and secure.  I would definitely recommend these.  Hopefully they'll in in different diameters in the future.
summary: Much better than twine or twist ties for securing stray branches on bushes.

reviewText: These are very attractive, hard plastic clips that snap together, and the ends look like leaves.  The leaves aren't straight out, but curved somewhat to resemble real leaves.  Easy to use, but if the plant and stake aren't thick enough, it doesn't stay up unless supported by other leaves. I would buy again.

My wife is an avid gardener.  We have huge tomato plants that are supported by the wire cages that are sold everywhere, and do a good job up to certain point.  Tomatoes need support when the fruit starts to mature because of the weight.  She has always used tie ties, like on the packaging for a loaf of bread---just a pain to put on and take off at the end of the season.  These plant clips just make the job so much easier and can be used season after season and they do not cut into the plant--really nice.  She also uses them in the flower garden for holding the stems up to show off the bloom, just attach to the support rod or stick. So simple to use, place the clip around the stem and the support and snap closed; easy to move as the stems get longer.  If grandma only could have got her hands on these, she used string; but, that was a long time ago and these had not been born yet.  If you, like my wife spend a lot of time in the yard gardening I'm sure you would find these very useful too.
summary: Get Rid Of The Tie Ties!

reviewText: The Global Garden Friends 20-Pack Ultimate Plant Clips are an easy way to prop up those branches that are threatening to tip over your planter. The method of securing the branch to the pole/stake with the clip is a bit awkward at first but after your 3rd-4th try it will become second nature to you. The size of the plant clips allows multiple sizes of stems to be propped up. The green color blends in with the plant greenery and does not stick out like a sore thumb. The plastic material of which the plant clip is made allows these to be used inside and outdoors.
summary: Easy Way to Prop Up Plants

reviewText: These are a very clever design for clipping plants of certain sizes. They will easily fit over the typical bamboo stake and the small to medium size plastic coated stakes. They won't work that well with the larger plastic coated stakes though. They provide a broad enough surface area on the plant side so that the plants should not be harmed. It is the wrong time of year to try them on Tomatoes but they seem like they will be ideal for that type of use.
summary: very clever and it works well

reviewText: These are plastic clips designed specifically to attach plants to supports. As shown in the picture on the packaging, they can easily be fastened with just one hand. The clips are sort of W-shaped, with a clasp right in the middle. You put your thumb through one end of the W, your index finger through the other and snap the clasp shut around your plant stem. The clasp is secure enough to hold up ordinary house plants, but if your stem should happen to outgrow the clip, the clasp is designed to open up rather than choke the stem. The clips are bright green, and the tips shaped like small leaves, so they will blend in easily with most plants. According to the package, they are made in the USA.In the past, when I've needed supports for my plants, I've grabbed anything at hand, including especially twist ties. These little clips are easier to attach than twist ties, and they sure look a lot better than twist ties on my house plants. Highly recommended.

reviewerName: Gina Pera "Is It You, Me, or Adult A.D.D.?, a...
reviewText: Before these plant clips arrived, I would use a variety of stick elements combined with twist-ties to stake my dahlias and other flowers.  This method had its downsides, including:1. The twist-ties had usually rusted by the time the dahlias died back, making them hard to remove (required for city composting)2. They typically looked unsightly.These clips go on and come off easily, they look like leaves, and their design accommodates a growing stem.I would happily pay this price for clips I can use and re-use.

I used these on my heirloom tomato plants.But you need skinny bamboo, not thick bamboo.I take a two foot piece of hollow electrical conduit and I hammer that in the ground half way. Then I put the skinny bamboo stick into the hollow conduit.These clips are just the right size for this. The vine and the stick completely fill the loop formed by the plastic clip.
summary: Works good on tomato plants and skinny bamboo

reviewText: Ease of use-  Your fingers fit into the small C on either side of the clip, and squeeze together. It takes a few tries to get used to the motion, but it is relatively simple to adjust to. However, if you have particularly large hands, weak hands, and/or arthritis, this may be difficult to impossible for you.Clip effectiveness- These are advertised as being specifically designed not to cut off plant growth; therefore they are intended to fit loosely around whatever plant and stake you are using. They are not expandable, stretchy, etc. They are easier to move and adjust than twine or tape. However, if they fit too loosely they slide down; if the plant stem or stake is too large they don't fit; and if the plant stem is not strong enough (i.e. sinking down, rather than top heavy), it will simply slither through.However, for certain plants- those that have strong stems, are top heavy, and are of medium thickness- these are the most effective and easy to use clip I've found.Cost- These are approximately $0.50 per clip. If the clips last through a season or two (they are listed as both biodegradable and infinitely reusable; one has to give) they will be worth the money. As of the current writing, they lasted through a few months of North East fall and winter, but I will update if there are any changes.
summary: Still not perfect, but better than many similar products

reviewText: Overall I feel as though this product is weak. It is easy to snap together, but very difficult to pull apart. I messed around with them for some time, thinking there must be a knack to it, but I just couldn't figure it out. I had to pull it really hard to make it snap back open again and I feel as though this would damage a plant stem. Also, the space left for the stem once snapped together was rather large--I imagine an Asiatic lily stem fitting in it snuggly, but the pepper plants that I grow ever year would probably have too thin of a stem to fit securely.The best thing about this product is that it is green and is made in a leaf design so as not to draw attention to it. Otherwise though, I think I'd rather stick with using twine.

I like these clips. Their design is so they blend in and look like leaves. That's kind of neat if this is a requirement that is important to you. For me the aesthetics is not important at all. I have been using the JMK clips20pc Gentle Plant & Flower Clipsfor about 2 years and they are great for large vines like tomatoes and do not smash the vine. These Global clips are smaller and can pinch the vine if it's too large. The great thing about the Global clips is in their 1 piece construction. Because of this they do not break as easily as the JMK's. I break at least 3-5 JMK's a year but I really need them for their large round size. I use both clips now. I use the Global's for my cucumber's, Beans. And I use the JMK's for the tomatoes, Squash, Peppers, and Tomatillo'sDon't forget the netting!Luster Leaf 864 Rapiclip Vine and Veggie Trellis Net, Green
summary: Don't forget the netting for these great clips!

reviewText: I was hoping that these truly would have been the ultimate plant clip, but alas, it turns out that this is not the only clip I will ever need. The Global Garden Friends' Ultimate Plant Clip is an interesting concept at its core. These are certainly fine clips for tomato plants, or for any other small plant in need of a stake, supposing there exists enough girth between the plant and stake to hold the clip in place, or if there is a lateral branch on which the clip may rest; otherwise, these smooth, plastic clips will not hesitate to slide down.These clips have inner dimensions of almost a half an inch across the short length, by barely over one inch across from tip to snap. Closing them is a snap, quite literally, and they open up inch a pinch, also, quite literally.I believe these add a bit of whimsy to any plant on which they can stay in place; the theme is spot on. However, function is of utmost importance, and without friction of some sort to hold a clip in place, an alternate solution oftentimes becomes necessary.I enjoy the clips, but their application is somewhat limited. I eagerly look forward to using these on my next crop of tomatoes, but this did nothing for my poor little Orchid. I recommend these clips for situations in which these will be able to maintain their posts, so to speak, supposing cost is no factor, keeping in mind that they are no replacement for traditional ties. These Ultimate Plant Clips are ideal for those considering them more for either their aesthetics or their novelty, rather than for functional convenience.

reviewerName: Juanita A. Floyd "Life is too short to read b...
reviewText: These are cool clips. They are a lot bigger than most plant clips which is a good thing. I do a lot of orchids and lilies and these are going to be wonderful. A nice amount in the pack, although they do seem a little pricey. Just staked up one of my orchids that is blooming like crazy and these clips allowed me to gather several stems at one time instead of just one. Easy to close and easy to get back open.

I had to wrestle with what I thought of these clips, because I didn't feel like clipping them was particularly "natural". I guess if you have larger fingers (about a ring size 12), these aren't the easiest to use.On the upside, though, they hold well, and I like how they'll accommodate plant growth. That seemed more important to me, but the clips cost so much, it's hard to recommend them to most people.If you have indoor plants and need to color coordinate, these are pretty awesome. I can't say I'd tell anyone to run out and get these for their tomato gardens, though.

These clips seem like a good idea but execution of use is not as easy as you would think.The little leaf ends are supposed to be ergonomically designed for your thumb and forefinger. Any pressure to the outside and they give without accomplishing the task of opening the clip. However, you can close them with one hand but two hands are easier. The clips are big enough for a stake and a stalk up to " but be careful because at that size, it will be tight.They are sturdy enough for smaller stalks but a heavier plant may have issues with the strength of the plastic.Nice that they are made in the USA. That is a big plus in their favor!
summary: Moderately Good, Limiting in Strength and Size

reviewText: I love gardening,but certain things can be cumbersome, like staking and tying plants back. Many times I have tried with and without success. These ultimate plant clips make this job a breeze. The clips are easy to use with one hand. With the index and thumb the clip can be opened or closed in one motion. No more awkward  trying to hold the plan and tying yarn. The clips are economical and reusable. Highly recommend.

Buy looking at these they seem they would serve my purpose quite well.  I've been using wire twine to prop up vines, etc., but this sometimes cuts into the plant, is hard to remove, slips down the prop I'm using . . . You get the picture.  The plastic seems strong and I'm thinking they won't snap or weaken when outside.  I'm eager to sue them.
summary: I haven't had an opportunity to use these, yet . . .

reviewText: Very nice and handy item and not just for the garden.One of the problems when you are tied back you tomatoes is that you only have two hands and most ties need both (and some more than two). These ties are designed so you can use them with only two fingers on one hand. You may need a little practice at first, but once you get the feel for these clips, you will be done in no time.  And they are also good for wires and cables. I used them for cable management when setting up my new TV and entertainment center and they worked great there as well.I will admit they could be made of a better material, more flexible or malleable, but for the price these are great.
summary: Handy clips for your garden shed

reviewText: I'm giving this 3 stars because it's definitely not a one size fits all.  If it would include different sizes, I would probably give it five.The product itself is fairly easy to use.  I have orchids so I gave it a try on them.  The clips are too big.  The only reason it holds the plant is because I forced the stem up and it's really stiff, therefore the plant pulls away from the stick making it a tighter hold.  I've raised tomatoes and although I have no plants now, this would be too big for a young plant.  Maybe, once the tomatoes are established but we need to hold them up as they are growing too.

They do what they say they will do.I have citrus plants and a money tree and the little green clips allow me to easily clip the branches together to keep them from dragging towards the ground (or the floor, in my case). They clip in such a way that as the branches get thicker, you don't have to worry about the clips restricting their growth.Plus, they're green, so they match!
summary: They do what they say they will do

reviewText: I used these or a lot of my plants and flowers. These are easy to clip on and take off. I have used it with new flowers to make them stand better and look better in a flower pot. I have used them as well on my Roses. Overall a good product, great for all your plant needs.

These work well for their intended purpose.  They do a good job of holding up the plant without choking the stem or vine, as could easily happen if it was tied off.  But one does have to take into consideration that the radius of the opening on these are only so big - slender stakes should be used, if you were planning to use a thicker stake, these clips probably won't fit around the stake, let alone accommodate a plant stalk.The opening of the clip is about 3/4 inch wide and 1 1/2 inches long.  Which makes them good for plants of smaller stem thickness and skinny stakes.  Garden plants with thicker stalks, like larger tomato varieties, would "outgrow" these over the course of a summer - especially if you were to use them on the main part of the stalk to secure them to the stake.What would have been really great with this product is a variety pack.  I'd really like to have the option of different sizes.They are definitely more convenient than ties, but not as readily usable on a wide variety of plants.

Like everything else, gardening has changed over the last 70 years.  Clips like these are part of the change.  They will definitely be helpful during growing season.  They give ample room for growth, and are quite simple to use, to dlip on and lock.  The green leaf shape is an added bonus feature for the looks of the addition.  The price for 20 of these clips is reasonable.  This indeed is a recommended purchase for those who love their gardens.
summary: They look nice an work well

reviewText: ... and they are working, so far!  I an give a better review when an entire growing season had passed, but Amazon wants this NOW!

Appearance:  the clip is designed to look like a plant leaf so is fair at camouflaging itself on a plant stem.  It's cute.Utility:  the clip is easy to spread open (as long it's already opened and not in the "clicked" closed position)and close around a plant stem with one hand while the other hand is holding the stem and stake with the other.  It's useful for plants whose stems don't grow more than a couple of centimeters in width.Although the package says it can secure tomato plants, I'm not sure what kind of tomatoes it could possibly mean.  The tomatoes that I grow in my garden can grow upwards of five feet high and the stems can grow to be two inches in diameter.  Although the clip is meant to release rather than "choke" a stem if the stem grows too thick, the  reason I clip a plant to a stake,  for security or stability of the plant, is then lost.
