About three quarters of the way through my dig, I experienced overheating. The unit simply shut down. I pulled the start key and gave the tiller time to cool down. About thirty minutes later I hit the circuit breaker reset button (which is located on the left side of the motor housing) and I was back in business.After completing the dig, I was somewhat surprised to find that I still had juice in the battery. I did notice some drop off in power but not enough to keep me from completing my project. For anyone that operates battery powered gear, that is saying something in itself. Clean up was a breeze. Afterwards I coated the blades with a thin layer of oil. Overall, I found that this Black & Decker Tiller compared well with my older gas powered Mantis. I won't say that it was better, but was equal in getting the job done. That's good enough for me. Believe me, I don't miss the pull cord on my old tiller. For battery powered gear, I find it impressive. Without a doubt its an effective garden tool.

I was thrilled to receive the Black & Decker CTL36 36-Volt Cordless Electric Front Tine Tiller, and although it arrived after I'd already planted half of my community garden plot, I was able to use it today for the remaining half.  The package was in terrible condition when it arrived and part of the handle had deep scratches from metal rubbing against metal in the box.  One of the cable clips was broken as well, but otherwise, the tiller arrived in good condition, as did the battery.  I charged the battery and assembled the tiller a few days later.  The multilingual manual was easy to follow and all the parts were enclosed in the package.  Working at a leisurely pace and needing only pliers, I was able to put the tiller together in less than 30 minutes.This tool is very easy to operate but does require strength as does any tiller.  I was accustomed to my little gas powered Mantis tiller, but had had difficulty lately pulling that darn cord to start her up.  No worries with this Black & Decker because you simply insert the key to activate the electrical connections, then press the button on the side of the handle and immediately after, pull the handle lever back toward the handle.  Be sure you do this in the location you're going to till because the tines immediately start turning and you'll destroy anything else.  Where the Mantis tended to need repeated cleaning of the tines and was very loud, this one required only one untangling and was very quiet by comparison.  There's also no smell of gas!  When the handle lever is not held back, the machine will shut down, so there's no way to regulate the speed of the tines other than on and off.  Since it's so simple to start, having to shut it down periodically is no problem after you get into the rhythm of its operation.The item description states, "The 3-position tine depth is perfect for shallow or deep tilling, and can be adjusted by just a touch."  It's not really just a touch, but you must pull up a springy large plastic pin thing (technical term), then move the handle up or down.  The description also states, "The adjustable handle height allows users to adjust the cultivator for maximum comfort and the soft grip handle provides added comfort during use."  It actually adjusts to two heights, both are tall for my shorter self and I wish there was a shorter option.I also wish the handle was collapsible because it would fit into a car more comfortably.  In a truck it's not a problem, but driving a car and wanting it to remain relatively clean required some advance preparation.  I removed the tines for the ride home and will likely also store it without the tines attached until I need it again in a few months.  Transporting it was easier for me to do in two steps with the battery removed from the tiller.As I reread my review, I wonder why I'm giving it a five star review since there are functions I find lacking.  I guess it's because I found it relatively easy to assemble and operate, and the tilling was superb.  Black & Decker was responsive to my phone call regarding the broken and scratched parts and they are replacing them.  I'd recommend this tiller.
summary: Despite imperfections, it's a five star product

reviewText: Battery Powered Tiller.Yes, they did laugh. They said it wouldn't work. They said it wouldn't have enough power.Well, they can laugh all the way to the bank when they make a withdrawal to pay for their own gas powered tiller that's noisy, a polluter, and ugly.This little tiller (little compared to the big gas powered ones). Does take some time to get used to.So before trying to scorn your friends with all the drawbacks their gas powered tillers have, please, please, take time to practice with this one.Aside from the fact that it's a nicely sized tiller (not too big, not too small), the battery makes this guy pretty heavy. Just try pulling out the battery for the first time.Fortunately, you don't have to remove the battery to charge the tiller, but when you do, be prepared to "lift from the knees."The other thing is that it seems a little unwieldily when you're just trying to get it to the place you want to till because the guider rod gets in the way. You can lift the rod up or simply angle the tiller so the rod doesn't get in the way when moving the tiller around.-- the sound --Yes, it does make a sound. No, it doesn't sound like what you think a tiller should sound like.It's quiet. Quiet compared to gas tillers.You probably won't feel the need for any earplugs.The sound it does make is electric. Reminds me of a large electric toy car.-- Tilling --It's a pretty good tiller. For the price, and size, it does a great job.It jumps around a bit, until you get used to using it. I thought it would pull and drag forward, but if you angle it down too much, it just goes deeper into the soil. Angling it up too much, and the rotator blades can bounce on the soil.Once you practice enough, you get used to how the tiller works and can maneuver it better.The depth of the tilling seemed just right, but can be adjusted if needed.-- Dirt --The soil moisture content makes a difference. I preferred how it handles when the soil is slightly moistened (not wet mind you). Extremely dry soil was harder to till.-- Plants --I tilled over grass that was growing in the garden as a test. Seemed to do okay, but check the blades afterwards (when it's powered down) because grass might get caught in the blades). I just used a broom to sweep it out rather than risk loosing a finger (even when the unit is turned off).-- wishes --I wish that the handle was up a little higher. Seems like you have to stoop down a bit to use.Other than that, it's a great tiller. It's great that it's quiet and doesn't use gasoline.So they can laugh all they want with their noisy, polluting, behemoth tillers.This works just fine.
summary: Let them Laugh all they want

reviewText: I finally made the leap from gas to battery-powered tiller this year, and it's been a revelation in more ways than one. First, a caveat - I am an amateur gardener with about 750sf of tilled garden space. If you're looking for a professional's assessment of this tool, my review probably isn't going to be 100% useful. Having said that, the Black & Decker CTL36 36-Volt Cordless Electric Front Tine Tiller is a very good tool that has many advantages and a couple of minor limitations.First and foremost, it's powered by an electric motor, so there's virtually no maintenance and startup is instant. That was NOT the case with my gas-powered tiller, and it's one of the reasons I made the switch. The motor provides a lot of energy to the tiller tines, and you might be pleasantly surprised by how much soil-moving torgue this model has.It also features a terrific design, and moving this unit through typical northern climate soil (high clay content and lots of small rocks) is pretty easy. Because this is a small tiller, you can expect some issues with large rocks or particularly hard soil, but for the average user this won't be a problem. The machine is well balanced, and is it not nearly as fatiguing to use as a larger tiller. As always, it's a tradeoff in terms of size - performance vs. ease of use - and in the case the Black & Decker CTL36's modest size provides decent performance and exceptional comfort.I can't think of a better investment for a gardener looking for a tiller that's simple to operate and maintain and which offers the environmental and ergonomic benefits of an electric motor.
summary: Honda quality at a great price!

reviewText: These are not likely to be investigated and messed with by a kid or a pet (cat or a dog), can kill multiple mice at once (up to 12), and can be used both indoors and outdoors.I like that these come pre-loaded and are disposable. With this product, you can just kill all the mice and never need to touch the poison.They eat the poison from the station and die elsewhere. The biggest problem with this product and with poisoning mice (besides the inhumane treatment of poisoning mice) is that cats or dogs cat then eat the dead mice and then the pets die that way. Although this product is good at making sure that children and other pets do not get to the poison, the fact that the mice will die somewhere in the house and might be then eaten by your pets who will then die is scary.Also, it should be noted that although 12 seems like a large number, mice tend to exist in large families so one of these stations might not solve the problem in your house or barn.
summary: great for not touching the poison but should be used with caution if other pets are present

reviewText: I am giving this three stars - Bromethalin is an effective mouse toxin. The problem is that it is also toxic to dogs and extremely toxic to cats. So, while my dogs have ignored the bait stations, I am still picking them up during the day when I'm not at home. There is no test and no antidote to this poison, once it is consumed, you have fifteen minutes to make your pet vomit it out. After that, there is little that can be done.If you decide to use this, please make sure that you make certain not only that your pets (especially cats) do not attempt to eat the dead rodents.I suggest before you try this you consider a non-poison alternative in your home. By mixing flour, baking soda, and sugar (equal proportions) you can make a substance that may get rid of your mouse (or rat) problem. Set the dry mix down in something you will later throw away where you have seen mice. The baking soda reacts with the stomach acid of the rodent and creates gas, which the rodent can't pass. Eventually this substance will cause a blockage or rupture the colon killing the mouse.An effective choice ... but even in "pet safe" containers, not 100% safe. Keep away from pets and children.

I have neighbors who fancy themselves farmers They are not. As a result of their ineptitude, I feel like I am living a scene in a cheesy horror movie. Hordes of mice can be seen swarming from their property to ours. Some have made their way into the attached garage and chewed their way into my car. I take no joy at ending any animal's life but after the assault on my Subaru, it was unavoidable.  This bait trap seems to be effective, at least it appears the garage infestation has ended. The design protects you from actually having contact with the poison and although it is supposedly dog and child resistant, I have restricted my pets access to the garage. Additionally, my brother has the job of checking for and removing any carcasses thereby limiting harm to scavengers.This is certainly an effective product but must be used responsibly. Use it when necessary and with respect.

After fighting a very long battle with a mouse that kept outsmarting my efforts, traditional traps, glue traps and bags of bait underneath the house, a friend recommended that I try Motomco Bait Station. I placed these underneath my kitchen sink, in my laundry room and in bathrooms. After a few days I could tell something was eating the bait. I have not seen any evidence of mice in my home since beginning using these.Now, I don't wait until I see the evidence of rodents inside my house before placing traps and poisons. I start outside in the hopes that they never make it inside. I place bait stations underneath my house, in and under my storage shed and inside my tool shed and check regularly and replace if needed.These stations, 2 in the pack, come preloaded with bait. After the bait is gone you just toss and replace. If you don't like handling poisons these are for you. If you, like me, try to avoid tossing plastic into the trash headed for land fills, the company offersMotomco 22478 Tomcat Refillable Tier 1 Mouse Bait Station, 1-Ounce, 8-Pack. I've tried them both and I prefer being able to reload the stations as opposed to tossing them.The company claims these are pet safe and child resistant.  My children are grown and I don't have pets.  I did attempt to pry the top off and was unable to do so.  These are ready to place right out of the package. When the bait is gone simply toss and replace.Motomco Bait Stations work.

This "Tomcat 2 Count Mouse Killer Disposable Bait Station" is used to attract and poison mice, sending them out of the house to die. I should note that we do not have these where children or pets are a concern, so they work well for my needs (your requirements may be different).We can see that critters have been nibbling at the bait in the units we set in our shop, home, and detached garage.Highly Recommended, with the caveats above.CFH
summary: Works Well, Good Value - Highly Recommended

reviewText: This is a single block Tomcat bait trap that will kill up to 12 mice.  It's not a trap that mice will be trapped in, but rather one that they will go into to eat the bait and leave.  It's rather hard to see how much they've eaten at this point in time, but when the block is gone, the trap can be disposed of.  The bait is enclosed in the trap, but the top is clear plastic and it will be easy to see when it needs to be discarded.  Apparently with ingestion of a very small amount the mice will die within a couple of days, but not in the trap itself.We do have pets and obviously we don't want anything around the house that can inadvertently harm them.  These are "Kid & Dog Resistant," but if you have your doubts, take a pass and continue using the old Victor traps if need be.  I've even used the electronic method with some success.  I'm not going to be using any of the Tomcat Mouse Killer traps in any accessible place in the house, but rather in my small barn.Field mice usually are more problematic in the fall when they are heading to shelter, but manage to be busy throughout the year.  I'm using the Tomcats outside.  I do like the concept and like it much better than the d-Con I've tried in the past.  They came in a box and just seemed to attract more mice than they eliminated.  I also was concerned about how the poison seemed to be spread all over the place.  Not enamored with that method.I'm not quite sure how the Tomcat Mouse Killer system will work in the long run, but I definitely like the system.  I will not be using it in any place where animals or children will have easy access to it at all.  My comfort level isn't high when I take any chances, which in the case of bromethain I'm not planning on it.  Better system than the open-boxed d-Con I've used in the past, but how well it works in the long run remains to be seen.
summary: A better alternative to the d-Con open-boxed system I've used in my outbuildings ...

reviewText: Tomcat has several types of Mouse Killer stations. The Mouse Killer version, this one, is a small black box with a clear plastic cover. It is pre-filled with bait (Bromethalin) and has an opening through which the mouse will walk toward the bait. The bait cannot be refilled and there is no need to ever touch the bait. This particular unit is child and dog resistant (it also appears to be cat resistant). There are two bait boxes contained in this particular package. The setup appears similar to the Mouse Killer II package, which has a translucent rather than transparent cover but is otherwise quite similar. The Mouse Killer II packaging indicates that it is only child resistant rather than pet resistant as well. The Mouse Killer I packaging has a bigger bait station and you have to actually place the bait into the container.
summary: Not a mousetrap, but rather a mouse poison station

reviewText: These are pretty nice, they come preloaded with bait, they are resistant to being messed around with by children, and can kill multiple mice.  Better than the poison packs which when they are chewed into can scatter the poison all around.They can kill up to 12 mice, so ideally you could just throw a couple of these down and it should handle your mouse problem without having to keep resetting traps. reviewText: You get 2 little black boxes that are pre filled with mouse bait poison. These are water resistant so it makes them perfect for outdoors, but you can also use these inside.  As these are sealed and refilled, they are perfect to use around children and pets. Each box has a bet that is supposed to kill up to 12 Mice.
summary: Perfect for outside mice problems prefilled water resistant mouse poison bait boxes.

reviewText: Farms have mice. And this last year, the mice seem to have gotten much worse for some reason. I can't just set out some traps, we have to have a focused consistent approach.I loved the Tom Cat mouse killer stations. The bait is attractive to mice. I can see from the top how active mice have been at each station. Every station I have set has had significant action. The poison works quickly. I have actually had two mice die at the station. One thing to be aware of is the active ingredient kills mice but the mice don't have that dead mouse smell. I think this is a huge plus. But it can mean you are surprised with a dead mouse.This disposable station is perfect for a just starting mouse problem or a new siting. This is really easy to set up and you wont have to mess with the traps again.

I have already found a dead mouse in my lawn shed.  I put this in a few weeks ago and went to check again the other day and found a dead mouse.  It seems to be working ok so far and I have noticed a little less activity from the mice in this building.  Will continue to  use and hopefully fully eradicate the mouse population at my house

Although these have not resulted in a "catch" yet, they are used as prevention in a storage shed after a neighbor found vermin. I like the fact that they are pet friendly and can be left out without warning or concern. Good for outdoor (or indoor) areas such as storage sheds etc and for use around pets.

Even considering just Motomco's rodent control products, there's enough to drive a person crazy. Snap traps, glue traps, spin traps, and several different types of bait stations. Of them all, poisons are perhaps the last I'd choose (except maybe the glue traps... I hate to see animals suffer like that). While I'm not a fan of poisons (I prefer snap traps), there are four different, very similar products, and it's hard to keep them straight:Mouse Killer (this product): Disposable, kid and pet safe, and can be used both indoors and outdoors.Mouse Killer I(Best choice!): Refillable, kid and pet safe, and both indoors/outdoors.Mouse Killer II: Disposable. Kid (not pet) safe, and indoors only.Mouse Killer III: Refillable. Kid (not pet) safe, and indoor only.Of the four, Mouse Killer I makes the most sense to me. It's as safe as they get, and refillable (and therefore more cost-effective in the long run). They all come with the same poison, so there's no difference there. This one has an additional covering over the entrance the others don't have, making it a little more tamper resistant, and a bit more attractive to mice, which like such things.The disadvantage of poisons? They don't work right away, and the rodents may go off and die in a place where you can't get to them, but their rotting corpses still stink up your house.My preferred option is stillsnap traps, which are infinitely reusable without purchasing additional products (poisons, etc), and much cheaper, especially when obtained at a local hardware store.
summary: Not the one I'd choose. Here's a summary of them all:

reviewText: Our two basic wooden mousetraps that we have in our garage have caught over 100 mice with just peanut butter on them. I don't see any need for these, especially since they are deadly to humans and pets. Not worth the risk.

Dead mice, plain and simple.  This stuff works just as well as that other brand of poison.  Will continue to use it, because I have 'discovered' the results.  The best part is you never have to touch the bait and it will kill at least 12 mice before having to throw the station away. While this is small and convenient to stick in a corner or along a wall, it is just the right size to entice a mouse inside to the bait that is kept completely away from the opening. We like to use the bait traps outside along the house edge to get them before the come in for the winter.This box contains two non-refillable stations.

I've only tried these outside, as I have pets inside and I don't want the mice to eat the bait and then die in the house, and then risk my dogs messing around with poison dead mice.The mice that were rooting around in my garden seem to be gone, so I guess it's been working.The 2 count station means you have twice the bait of a regular trap - it can kill a dozen mice and then you can whole thing away when the bait is chewed up - no need to mess around with poison replacement bricks.The only benefit over snap traps is really being able to set it and forget it and not have to deal with the dead mice after.  And if it does kill a dozen mice at a time, that's faster and easier then setting a dozen snap traps.

I purchase big containers from a pest control company and use either small bait traps that were purchased on-line or bigger traps that are on a concrete block and purchased from the local branch of a national pest control company.  Mice don't bother with the bait much during the summer, but like it in the other seasons.  It has worked well for me in my country home.  I have never had any problem with decaying mouse odors. reviewText: I live near a river and some woods as a result mice and other wildlife are abundant. Mice will often make it to my outdoor shed, my garage and my basement. My shed has also been home to larger rodents..The Tomcat mouse killer bait stations are nice because they are covered and the poison comes included in the trap so I did not need to wear gloves while handling the poison myself. The bait station is small. I have used larger bait stations. It looks like it is safe if children and pets are around because it is disposable and is not meant to be opened so it would be hard to get into it. In the short time I have had this I have not seen any nibbles but I have used this type of Tomcat mouse poison before and it has been eaten by mice.This is great if you don't want to touch the poison and you have pets or children around that might try to open the bait station. The box does say to keep the station away from children.  Once the poison is gone this can be thrown out.

The design is such that pets and children would have to work to get at the poison.  However, the poison is Bromethalin.  One dose is lethal to rodents, and they die within 24 to 36 hours.  The downside to this is that they may go elsewhere and die, which may be someplace that you do not want a decomposing creature.A persistent dog could chew on this, and it is deadly to dogs (and even more so to cats, but they are less likely to be randomly chewing on plastic, at least from what I have observed!).  There is no antidote, so if you have a rambunctious dog, you might want to consider a snap trap (annoying to a dog, but not lethal).Now, does it work?  In my experience, nope.  I placed these traps along with an electronic trap, and a couple of snap traps along the wall in my garage where I KNOW mice run (we catch about a half dozen a week).  After 10 days I pried the station open (which is not recommended) to be sure the bait had been gnawed.  It had not.I think I would rather go back to my old fashioned snap traps (at least I know where the dead mice are) or my new fangled electrocution chamber (which also kills instantly).

I also use traps (I like JT Eaton 409BULK Jawz Plastic Mouse Trap, For Solid or Liquid Bait (Pack of 24) ). The combination works well for me. I never have had my dogs or any neighbor dogs show any interest in the bait, but something strong at night (raccoons?) have messed with them a few times.The only difference in this product, the Tomcat Mouse Killer 1 and the 6 PACK TOMCAT DISPOSABLE MOUSE KILLER 2, Units Per Package: 2 is that the top of these containers are clear and the 2's tops are cloudy. It is easier to see how much bait is left with this one, but I slightly prefer the 2's as I don't really want to see any more than I have to.
summary: Been using this sucessfully for years

reviewerName: Richard C. Drew "Anaal Nathra/Uthe vas Bethod...
reviewText: I've used glue traps, regular mouse traps and a variety of poisons - those little wedges, bags and more. This is a solution I prefer.  No spillage of the poison, and it's kid/pet resistant. It's also refillable.  Since you're handling poison, you should wear latex gloves or handle the blocks with a disposable towel/cloth.I gave this four stars because I think the blocks should have a way of handling them without having to wear gloves, etc. Maybe a pair of small tongs or a clip.

I live near a river and some woods as a result mice and other wildlife are abundant. Mice will often make it to my outdoor shed, my garage and my basement.  My shed has also been home to larger rodents.The Tomcat mouse killer bait station is nice because it is covered.  It come with 4 refills. It is refillable so you need to wear gloves and touch the poison blocks and place them in the bait station. The trap is on the small size.  It says it is safe from the tampering of dogs and children and looks like it would be hard to get into. While the trap may be safe the bait itself must be stored in a safe place out of the reach of children or pets.  In the short time I have had this I have seen a few nibbles. I have used this type of Tomcat mouse poison before and it has been eaten by mice.You need to touch the poison to load this bait station and while it says the station is safe from the tapering of children or dogs the remaining bait blocks are not so you have to store them in a safe place.

I have a problem with mice around my home, so i have tried many different products to rid my home of them.  This is one of the best that I have tried.  The Tomcat brand has different solutions for various pest problems and all that I have tried have worked well.  This is one of the best mouse killers.  The mice clearly like them and they enjoy the bait.  I used to only use the disposable kind, but this is so easy to refill so I don't find it a problem to use.  It also saves money when you have a lot to get rid of.  I would recommend this to anyone.

I used these on my plants (I have several dozens in my house) and noticed that the leaves were shiny on each plant and that each plant seemed to look even greener than before.Having said that, I am not sure if mineral oil is good for plants. For people, mineral oil is one of the worse things one can put on the skin as it blocks permeability and doesn't allow the skin to breather. It occurs to me that mineral oil might play the same biological role on the plants. This to me would be a sad fact as without being able to breathe in CO2 and breathe out O2, the plants will die (from being unable to photosynthesize).Therefore, I have been afraid of using this product continuously. It adds luster to the plants but I do not want to risk it.
summary: all that glitters is not gold - apply with caution

reviewText: great product!!!!!I really like this product, its not a heavy productshines very well and its very light not heavy on the leavesvery nice shineHighly recommend

I had a few houseplants whose leaves were looking very dull lately. I also had just gotten a few new plants that I used this on as well.I took them all outside because I was concerned with overspray and gave them a generous spritzing with this. It does say you should wipe very dusty plant leaves with a cloth after spraying but I didn't actually do this. It was effective even without this step for me. It made my very dusty plants leaves shine and had a nice effect on the newer ones too.It's amazing what a difference it makes in the home when your plants look healthy and shiny!

I have to admit that it had never exactly occurred to me before that plants were more shiny in the store than they tend to be at home. As it's turned out, this is nice to have when I want to make the house look as polished as I can because company is coming or something. I don't think it's going to be something I use constantly, because I'm content with how leaves naturally look most of the time, but it'll be worth using on the plants in the kitchen area where people come over for dinner and it feels good to make sure things look very polished.

reviewerName: C. Ball "An idea that is not dangerous is unw...
reviewText: You know how that plant looked when you got it from the nursery, all healthy and shiny?  Well you can get rid of the dust and give that look of beauty back to your plants and this is the secret.  It's healthy for the plants and healthy for you with no chemical smell.  It is easy as pie to apply and the directed nozzle keeps the spray on the leaves not all over the room.  All in all a great product and it gives your house that extra mark of beauty with shiny leaves on your plants.

This spray product is easy to apply. It cleans the leaves and leaves more shine than one would achieve using water alone.Normally I place houseplants on the balcony and spray a lot with water.  That works very well. This spray is good for convenience when I don't want to do that whole routine.

This leaf shine comes in a 8 oz. spray bottle that sprays a targeted stream. It gives a nice shine to plant leaves and it's especially noticeable on plants with large leaves. We have a princess tree that has huge leaves on it and it looks very pretty when the leaves are all nice and shiny and healthy looking. It doesn't take much of this product to get a good result so even though it comes in a small 8 oz. bottle it will still last the average person a while. This product is also good for indoor plants that tend to get dusty. You can take them outside and spray them down and wipe them off and they will look amazing. This is a nice product for those that take great pride in their plants.
summary: Great for large leaves and indoor plants. Gives a healthy looking shine.

reviewText: Miracle-Gro leaf shine adds shine to the leaves of your houseplants instantly. It's not a necessary product and doesn't provide any nutrients for you plant like you might think since it's from Miracle-Gro but it does make them look healthier.Houseplants with large leaves need to be cleaned and dusted anyway so it's easy to use the Miracle-Gro leaf shine while you're doing it. You can spray the product directly onto the leaves but to avoid overspray, it is easier just to spray it onto a cloth and wipe the leave with the cloth.

This product does help make your foliage "greener" looking.  It does work with a small odor when sprayed.  You also have to be careful when spraying because it is a wide spray and gets everywhere, especially on smaller leaves.  The main ingredient is mineral oil so be careful not to get it on your skin.  If you want your plants looking shinier, this is for you.

For me, indoor plants are there to provide refreshing natural colors, textures,  and some oxygen.  Most plants, when carefully tended to, will have naturally shiny leaves.  I gave this Leaf Shine spray a try on some potted indoor plants that had a light layer of dust.  Got a slightly shinier surface (wax?) than just misting with water.  The leaves with heavier layers of dust had to be wiped down with a damp cloth after spraying Leaf Shine.  Just feels like extra effort for small increase in shinier leaves.  I'll stick with misting the leaves with water when this Leaf Shine bottle is used up.
summary: Gimmicky spray to make natural leaves look like shiny plastic.

reviewText: I've always liked products like Leaf Shine. I'm not sure of what they used to call this product, but I even used in when I was a child. The Miracle-Gro works really well. The first thing I had to do was unlock the bottle. It's difficult to see where the lock is because the whole top is green. You simply press down on the rectangular button and you're good to go.Now this isn't like one of the clean and shine products I've seen people use for their artificial plants. It comes out in a fine mist and after spraying a leaf, I actually wipe it down with a soft cotton cloth to shine it. If I'm working inside, I put the cloth behind the leaf or leaves before spraying to protect the wall or other items around it.The leaves come out beautifully and really sparkle. I haven't used anything like Leaf Shine in years and I forgot how much I loved it. I've started working on a large philodendron and will probably add it to my spring cleaning repertoire. You can't use Leaf Shine on fuzzy haired plants such as African violets or you'll ruin them. Very pleased with the result.
summary: I love the spring cleaning shine my philodendron got with Leaf Shine ..

reviewText: Miracle Gro has done it again as always. This is an easy to use formula just spray and wipe and your leaves of your house plants look so much better great product for indoor house plants.Renita
summary: Add a little shine to the leaves of your lovely house plants.

reviewText: I have been using Miracle Gro products since my Mom introduced them to me when I was a kid and helped her in the garden planting vegtables and plants. I have tons of Hostas all over my yard and some of them needed a little extra shine and this stuff worked great! It cleaned and shined them all and they look like I just bought them at the store!Thumbs up!

For plants with large leaves that collect dust, Miracle-Gro Leaf Shine is a good alternative to water to make them look clean and shiny. It certainly lasts longer than water at keeping them shiny. I was worried that it would leave a glossy fake-looking shine, but it doesn't. Rather, the plants just look vibrant and healthy. It is easy to apply and the shine lasts for at least a few days. It's like dusting with a spray, probably not something you want to use all the time, but it works well when you do.I am not sure it is worth the price to buy a leaf shine product, but if you are going to buy on, Miracle-Gro works, is easy to apply, and looks good.

I will admit that this does make leaves shine. It uses a mineral oil water based solution, I can't confirm if it's good or bad for the plant.  The price isn't bad at $4.99 as an add-on item as of when I write this. If you have dusty plants, this might be a good way to "clean" them up, but honestly I would rather just use water and clean the leaves then use an oil. Yes it works, but so does water.

This product is very easy to apply & not too messy - just be sure to move your plant to a countertop that can be cleaned or put newspaper under the plant before spraying.  I always rinse/wipe the leaves with a damp cloth before applying.  I use this on my orchids & my Meyer lemon tree.  They look so pretty when the leaves shine.

I used this on my houseplants and it worked great. I sprayed on and used a soft cloth to clean my plants- They stayed shiny and kept the dust buildup away longer then just a normal dusting. A great product if you like your plants to look extra shiny :)

This makes my peace lilies look gorgeous, like they came from the nursery.I don't like the nozzle much though - over half my product was gone when it came in - it must have got mashed a lot against the box and sprayed out, because everything was intact, just soaking wet.I've always just cleaned my plants with a bit of whole milk in a lot of water, or need oil when I have it.  This works better than the milk solution, and about the same as neem..I looked up the MSDS because I am always leary of products like this, but it says that it doesn't harm aquatic life, so the run off would be safe, and it says it is environmentally efficient.  It looks very safe- it seems the only potential problem is eye, skin, and respiratory irritation IF you use it in LARGE concentrated applications.  (I think even water would say that.)  I feel ok using it around my cats.It's easy to use.  Just make sure that you put something under it, because the leaves will drip.  This time of  year I take mine outside and it's not an issue outside.  The plants look very similar in shine to when they come from the nursery.

I take pride in my house plants but forced air heat often makes them look dusty and dull.  Using Miracle-Gro Leaf Shine restores luster without adding too much unnatural looking sheen.  Directions say to protect furniture, walls and floors when spraying, but I try to use this product outdoors when possible.  For those who don't have that option, the bottle has a very small-holed nozzle which puts out just a bit of spray.  Keeping the spray contained is easy to do, and each leaf requires just a teeny spritz for effective results.Using this leaf shine seems to prolong dust/dirt build-up, so a little bottle lasts a long time.  My plants have never looked better.

I'll be honest... I'm far from a green thumb. I ordered this product because my plants get dusty and I thought it might be nice to not just clean off the dust but give them a bit of shine. I really had no idea how important it is to the health of a plant to keep the leaves clean! This product sprays easily onto the leaves with a targeted mist and is easy to wipe off with a cloth or even a paper towel. It left my plants looking beautiful with just the right amount of shine. I love knowing that my plants are so much healthier now as well! Excellent product!
Doesn't smell great.This works, but as with all things miracle grow, my lungs are not in love with it.

This worked well and is easy to apply to my plants. I sprayed it on an wiped with a clean damp cloth. I did see an amazing improvement in the way my houseplants looked. I honestly thought it was going to make them super glossy but it actually is a mild shine but a much healthier appearance. I really liked it.

I was afraid that this spray would make plants look like they were made of plastic, but it instead just makes them look clean and healthy.  I don't think it actually makes the plants healthier, but it doesn't hurt them.  The spray is easy to control without making a mess.  Overall, a nice way to make a plant look more "groomed."

I recently used this to clean my decorative bamboo. It was easy to spray and wiped off nicely, leaving the leaves looking glossy and clean. It did a great job of removing the dust that had accumulated on the leaves.

I have used this product in the past and am very happy to see it works as good as ever. I love the fact that it has a mist sprayer instead of the old spray option which was messy and wasteful. I use it on in the house plants so ones that I can do in the sink get done there but I prefer to spray this on a soft cloth and use that to clean the leaves while adding some shine. Works so nice that it doesn't hurt the plants at all and makes them look like they just came from a greenhouse.

I have a couple of big Spathiphyllum plants that are about ten years old. They are nice and healthy, but the leaves had become dull.  So, I decided to try this product on them.Heeding the advice of another reviewer, I shook the bottle well before applying.  I sprayed the plants in my patio to avoid damage to walls and floors.  I was pleased to see that the shine is delivered as a very fine mist, and did not run or drip.My plants came out looking beautiful.  The product contains mineral oil, and does leave a light oily film on the leaves.  I was afraid that this film would end up being a dust-catcher, with the leaves ultimately being left looking dirty.  However, I found that after a few days the oily feeling disappeared. Two weeks after the initial spraying, the leaves were still looking as clean and shiny as they were on the first day.I like this stuff!
summary: Very fine mist adds a nice shine to plant leaves

reviewText: I chose this to spruce up my indoor (and some outdoor) plants in preparation for selling a house. This takes off the dust but also leaves a light (not overpowering) shine that makes leaves look healthier.The nozzle sprays just the right amount onto the leaf (though directions recommend you hold a cloth to catch overspray) and the whole process is fairly painless (as painless as a process can be when you have a plant with a lot of leaves).The shine has lasted for two weeks now and the product doesn't seem to be collecting dust faster onto the leaves.

If you have plants with dusty leaves then you might like this product. It should only be used on plants with solid sturdy leaves. I work in an office with a huge fichus tree and it is an amazing dust catcher. This type of product will clean the leaves which in the long run is better for the plant.If you follow directions, there is really no mess. You need a soft cloth to hold below the leaf when you spray and definitely make sure you shake the bottle well each time you use it.So this solves that irritation - now if only it could solve other office problems as easily.

Miracle-Gro All Purpose Liquid Indoor Plant Food is easy to dispense from the pump container.  It dispenses as a foam that then dissipates when watered.  The fertilizer NPK Analysis: 1-1-1 (Nitrogen, Phosphorous and Potassium), so it a fairly weak fertilizer, so there is little chance of over-feeding.

I don't generally feed my indoor plants but I certainly will now that I've seen what a difference this makes. I had some plants that were looking pretty pathetic and now they are really coming around.I know some people had issues with the foam application but for me it's great. I love not having to mix anything up with the water; I can just use a few pumps of this and then water as normal. I had no problem applying it on my potted plants. If a tiny bit got on the plant it washed right off in the watering that followed.This makes feeding houseplants really easy and it actually worked. I'm very pleased with the results.
Miracle-gro is the only brand she uses for plant fertilizers, indoor and out.  She loves this liquid for the indoor house plants and says she can note that the plants appear healthier after using it.
summary: My wife swears by this stuff

reviewText: Miracle-Gro's houseplant, liquid fertilizer, USED TO BE GREAT!  I've used it for decades. I knew exactly how much to add to the water and our plants flourished, year after year.  Our 48 year old Christmas Cactus enjoyed the fertilizer between blooming seasons.  Now?  I'm supposed to squirt some foam into the plant's base.  I can't even SEE the base of the 48 year old Christmas Cactus, and even if I could, how does one squirt of foam compare to a few drops of the liquid.  A conversion chart would have been handy, BETTER YET, drop this foamy stuff and bring back the time-tested, good, reliable, dependable, REAL liquid houseplant fertilizer.  In the meantime, I bought another company's liquid fertilizer.  I sure hope I don't do damage to the plants.
summary: Don't Change Things That Are Perfect!

reviewText: We have about 40 houseplants (not counting orchids) that I really enjoy having around the house, especially since my wife takes care of them. She has always been a Miracle-Gro fan, as have I from the earlier version of this product that you add to water, to our annual garden startingMiracle-Gro Gro-ables Vegetable and Herb Garden Kit, 18 Seed Pods (Not Sold in CA). This new version of indoor plant food comes as a liquid with a pump bottle that dispenses the product as foam, much like a foaming hand-soap product.It is very easy to use. You just carry the bottle around with you when watering and pump a few dollops of foam onto the dirt around the plant - two pumps for small plants, three or more for larger plants - then water as usual. This also makes it easy to get the correct quantity of nutrients to most any potted plant. The foam does tend to rise a little if you use a rain type watering can, but it quickly dilutes and soaks in, leaving no visible trace in the pot. It's a great product, works as advertised, and the plants are doing just fine. It does seem to run out a little quicker than the stuff you mix with water, but because it is easier to use, I still think it is a five star product.
summary: Nice iteration of a trusted favorite

reviewText: I'm a certified black thumb and it's probably because I never think about things like liquid food for my indoor plants.  I was excited to try this because this makes it easy ... just a squirt of the foam onto the soil of each plant and I'm done!  My plants are mostly desert varieties (I live in Phoenix) so the soils are not covered and the foam is easy to apply (unlike thicker foliage plants where you might have to dig a little to find the soil).  My orchid especially likes this product - it hasn't flowered in quite some time, and now about a month after my application it has buds!
summary: Foaming plant feed makes it easy!

reviewText: I'm not overly fond of this foam. It's not that it's a bad product, it's actually much simpler to use than a crystal formula that requires dilution beforehand, but the foam is just a bit too messy for my liking. I have some very small potted house plants and therefore the foam doesn't just spray onto the soil, it goes all over the plants too. I'd rather have a liquid form that can be directed with more precision.However if the foam application works for you, then I feel as though this product would work as well as any other Miracle-Gro fertilizer would. I have used Miracle-Gro products for years and have always been pleased with the results.
summary: Not a fan of the foam application

reviewText: This is very nice if you have a few indoor plants that you would like to baby a bit.  It's a foam that comes out a lot like a hair mouse might, from a pump dispenser.It's a very light fertilizer, so it shouldn't burn up a plant - some houseplants can be very sensitive.  I used it on my spider plant, my aloe vera, and a green vine plant, and all have done well with it.Miracle Gro knows what they are doing - by putting it in this foam form, the already low level of nutrients gets delivered more steadily and slowly.  Houseplants can be very sensitive, so this helps keep the ends from getting burnt and brown.
summary: Nice for a few indoor plants

reviewText: I've used Miracle Gro products for decades, and my father used it in our garden when I was growing up in the 70s.  I get great results with my houseplants and in our garden, and in fact I buy Miracle Gro over any other brand.This product, however, isn't a winner.  The idea is to puff a little bit of the "plant food mousse" on the soil before watering and it dissolves into the soil.  I find this awkward to apply, since many of my house plants have leaves and branches that hide the soil. I much prefer adding the liquid or granules to the watering can, and using the long neck of the can to reach inside the branches to water.Sorry, Miracle Gro, I won't be buying this product.

I like this plant food because I find it easy to place the foam evenly in the pots when I feed my plants. The consistency is similar to bubble bath bubbles.  I have gotten spots on my leaves with liquids that you add to water as it splashes on them,  so I find this a better solution.  My plants look good and healthy after several uses and that's the best of all.

"What's this good for," I thought.  "Just a new way to spill fertilizer on my kitchen counter and floor."Then I tried it.  If you've ever tried to fertilize an indoor plant you know that fertilizer smells bad and it can stain.  This stuff can't do that.  Because it's a foam.  It stays put.  It takes real work to spill it - I haven't managed to, yet, nearly the whole bottle has gone into plants around inside my house.It even made a tiny rose I got for Christmas 3 years ago - it's in a 4 inch pot, I thought it had really had it - sprout out with vigorous new life.  It had been making paltry, transparent white leaves - whatever was deficient got corrected and now it looks fit to sprout a bud or two.  I'm amazed - this plant has sentimental value to me - and I think I will be able to repot it at the end of this season, when I was readying myself to put it in the dustbin instead!Highly recommended.
Love Miracle Grow products, they work so well, and the plants really are superior.This product is no exception.  Easy to use, great idea.Only problem, it's a bit costly.Other than that, five stars.

I have two plants I got after my mother's funeral at the beginning of February 2013; I've been working to keep them alive.  One is a wide-leaf plant, one is more succulent and sadly I didn't have the information on how to care for them so I've been winging it.  They've survived but the blooms they had never came back.So I applied this Miracle-Gro All Purpose Liquid Indoor Plant Food to both plants per the instructions on it over the course of four weeks.  After four applications the succulent looks really no different but the wide-leaf plant has grown a great deal, almost doubling in size with the stems more uprise and the leaves darker green.I didn't think to take a before and after photo so I apologize for that.I would strongly recommend this product and I'd continue using it myself though I need to get a larger planter I think.

We've used and enjoyed Miracle-Gro products for years, and they've provided helpful fertilization for our various flowers and plants. If we've had a frustration with the various products, it's that something is needed for one type of plant and another something is needed for another kind of plant. Thus, the "All Purpose" (indoor / outdoor - flowers / vegetables) is a very useful "feature" of this product; we're able to use it on our flowers and vegetables. Rather convenient.Also nice is the simplicity of the shake-on application process. It's a bit approximate, of course, but it's easy and quick. And it feeds plants for up to three months - that's helpful.
summary: A Nice, Low-Key Help for Our Garden

reviewText: I've tried brands other than Miracle Grow to fertilize my plants, and I always return.  This time, I'm staying with Miracle Grow.  Some brands dissolve too quickly, and other brands seem to sit like pebbles on the soil, week after week.  This particular blend of granules works both indoors and outdoors (I find that outdoor use requires more frequent application), and it works for both flowers and vegetables.While this is a quality product, it is a general purpose one, which means that it will fertilize a broad range of plants without being tailored specifically to a particular kind, and it is not organic.  For experienced gardeners:  the formula is 12-4-8.  For less experienced one: These numbers give the percentage of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium, nutrients for plant growth.  Tomato fertilizers are generally 18-18-21, so this adds some nutrients without giving them a full-strength kick.  I find that the general purpose is best for annuals, perennials, and non-acid-loving shrubs.  (I tend to rely on more organic methods with edible herbs and vegetables.) The only thing I'm not wild about is the "shake 'n feed" part, something that's great to broadcast the granules outside but which can make a mess when trying to spread them into pots.If you don't have the time or the memory to fertilizer your plants using organic or water-soluble fertilizers, go with the MiracleGrow.  It may cost more than other brands, but it always performs for me.-- Debbie Lee Wesselmann
summary: The Best Slow-Release Plant Food (5- stars)

reviewText: Miracle-Gro has been our choice for many years when it comes to our flower and vegetable gardens.  It is dependable in terms of assisting healthy plant growth, better veggie crops (more and bigger tomatoes, green peppers, lettuce, watermelon, pumpkins, and green beans), and with the new Shake N' Feed, it is easier to apply.The only Miracle-Gro product I have found unsatisfactory was the Liquid-Feed (a name close to that, not sure exactly what it is called).  Premixed Miracle-Gro in a bottle that you screw into a sprayer.  It worked okay, but super expensive, and I was never certain if enough or too much was being applied.  Much like any hose sprayer, it is less accurate in dispensing the plant food than sprinkling the pellets over the garden surface according to instructions.There is a photo on the container showing exactly the amount to use in comparison to a photo of a dime.  Makes it simple for even the most novice of gardeners.I believe this is basically the same formula as our previous plant food from Miracle-Gro, and I am positive we will, once again, have beautiful flowers, and scrumptious veggies.
summary: You cannot beat this Plant Food in terms of healthy, vigorous growth of flowers and garden plants

reviewText: I have been using miracle-gro products since I was  a child.  Their products are formulated for the home gardener and packaged in a way that makes them easy to use.  Back when, my garden was a handful of cacti and a small kitchen herb garden on mom's windowsill In New York.  Now I have an acre in Hawaii.  I grow fruit, vegetables and herbs.  Most of the  vegetables are in raised beds, though some are being grown in pots as the neighbor's cat often wreaks havoc on the seedlings in my beds.  I am on the windward side of the island, more or less in the rain forest. I use Miracle-gro shake and feed to replace the nutrients which are washed out by heavy rains.  It is a very basic fertilizer which is good for most things in the garden (i.e. not formulated for specific types of plants or to promote flowering).  The lid has small staggered spikes to make it good for broadcasting on beds.I started my seedlings last week, perhaps a bit early (given the amount of rain we have been getting).  I put a few grains in each pot to give them a good start and replace the nutrients lost to heavy rain.  Just 4 days after planting all of my seedlings are up and looking sturdy.  if it were not raining now I would post a picture.  I credit Miracle-gro with giving them a boost and shielding them from environmental stress (strong winds and torrential rain). Another locally produced time-release fertilizer burned all my delicate seedlings last year.  This one is time release and not super concentrated. In my experience it is safe for seedlings .  All of mine are looking sturdy and healthy, and growing very fast.  Miracle-gro says this is not formulated for containers but I have been using it in mine with great success.In the past I have used liquids, powders and spikes.  To my mind, this is the easiest to use because you can adjust the amount to the size of container or plant and it is suitable for just about any kind of plant.  You do not have to worry abut getting the mix right or how to store any excess.  Best of all, it does not expire.It is a nice, flexible, multi-purpose fertilizer.  I am using it for vegetables, young fruit trees in pots, and flower starts.  It is easy to use and unless you get 400 inches of rain a year like I do, you do not have to think about it again for 3 months,
summary: Easy to use and good for most things in your garden

reviewText: I’ve been using various Miracle-Gro products for many years and they have never let me down.  The Shake ‘N’ Feed line is the easiest to use – for established plants, just sprinkle it on top of the soil following the directions for proper amounts, and every time the granules get wet, the Miracle-Gro dissolves a little more and sends nutrients down to the roots.  Every couple of months, shake out a little more around the root-line of the plants.  The All-Purpose product works well for potted as well as ground plants.  With new plantings, I mix Miracle-Gro deep into the potting soil to give the plants a good start.  At first I was unsure but, once I got used to it, I found the newly designed shaker top is easier to manipulate than the old spout design.  With the spout, I sometimes poured more plant food than I intended.  I store my gardening supplies in an outside potting area, so I like that the granules of this particular food continue to be available in a water-proof container.  This ensures the bottom never gets soggy and turns the plant food into a block of unusable stuff.  It doesn’t get any easier than this, and my plants thrive on it.

With Spring arriving, I sprinkled this around all of my favorite plants in the yard.  It is all-purpose so it is good for feeding flowers, shrubs, potted plants and even vegetables and fruit trees.  My plants were badly in need of food and this fit the bill - they are thriving now.  If you are a more serious gardener, you might first consider getting your soil tested to see what its deficiencies are prior to using this product.  As a general pick-me-up for your plants though - Miracle Grow is a solid bet.

I have used Miracle-Gro Shake 'N Feed All Purpose Continuous Release Plant Food in the past.Often.  It never lets me down. This year, nothing is growing in my garden yet, but the plants I have at work were looking a wee bit sad. Maybe more than a wee bit. So I took some of this to work, and over a couple of weeks time, they are looking much more healthy and happy already. I look forward to using this on my outdoor plants if spring should ever arrive! Miracle-Gro is always in use at my house during the growing season. I like this line of products, and don't see myself changing this preference any time soon.

This dispensing system for fertilizer is cleverly designed, with ergomoics and practicalityin mind.  The 4.5 pound package balances nicely in your hand, while enabling even sprinklingof its contents over your plants.The trick is simply to trust the packaging; it does not look as though the sprinkling offertilizer pellets will occur by merely tipping the container.  My first impulse was to cutaway the plastic liner to clear the spout.  That plastic cover actually causes the pelletsto disperse evenly.It is still early in the planting season, so it is difficult to ascertain the benefits ofMiracle-Gro.  I will add further comments as the season progresses.Note added 31 March 2014:  A few weeks into the planting season yielded mixed results.There have been no changes in seed germination or sprout development from MiracleGro vsother fertilization methods.  Thus, it's a matter of personal choice.
summary: Convenient way to tend the garden

reviewText: This is a general purpose fertilizer in granules that can be applied once and releases continuously throughout the growing season.  I have a 200 sq ft bed and I generally get a couple of applications out of it; it poops out visibly around the 8 week mark and I just apply another layer according to the directions, watering it in.The top has a built in spout that pops open; holding the handle, you can wave this across your garden to get a fairly even dispersal of granules.  This is convenient if you don't have a spreader; if you do, you can just unscrew the lid and pour out as much as you want.I use Shake'n'feed every year because it's convenient, well packaged, and it works and saves precious garden time.  So I'd recommend it to anyone who wants their garden to grow!

I received this product through the Amazon Vine program, which requires that a review be written within thirty days.  I was thinking that it would be difficult to review the fertilizer itself in such a short time, as it is a continuous release product.  I tried this out on some planters filled with Spenger asparagus plants, and was very surprised to see some visible greening-up in just a few days.The container itself is a winner.  It's designed to distribute the fertilizer particles in the recommended pattern, making it easier to apply the proper amount of plant food to the target area.  I also like the fact that the container is sturdy, and moisture proof.The only thing that could be improved about the packaging would be to make the NPK rating more visible.  It's in little print on the back of the jug.  When I shop for fertilizer, that's what I am looking for, in big numbers right on the front of the package.  This product has an NPK content of 12% Nitrogen, 4% Phosphorus, and 8% Potassium. meaning that it is better for green plants than for flowering plants or vegetables.  (Flowers or vegetables need a lower nitrogen content and a higher phosphorous content, otherwise you end up with lots of leafy growth and little crop or flower yield.)Update: July 2014I am very happy with this plant food.  My plants are looking very healthy and green, and I've had no problems with fertilizer burn.
summary: The shake-and-feed container is a winner

reviewText: Miracle-Gro Shake 'N Feed All Purpose Continuous Release Plant Food comes in a handy 4.5 pound container.  This plant food lasts up to 3 months and can used for outside or inside plants.  As the name implies, the container has a built in shaker lid, that makes distribution to small areas very convenient.  The formula of 12-4-8 is acceptable to most plants.  This sure beats the regular Miracle-Gro that we have used over the years.  So happy to have such an easy method of fertilizing our plants.

I'm new to Miracle-Gro because I lived for many years in places where I couldn't have a garden and only had a couple of indoor plants. We've made a start on a nice little garden in my new home, but it's too early to know how this fertilizer will work on it.For now I can say I like the ease of use. At first I was confused by the lid, because it seemed like the opening was in the wrong place. After shaking out some fertilizer on the ground, I realized the lid design is actually very clever, because you can distribute the product evenly without spilling too much out in one place. I'm also thinking of using this on my houseplants. They're pretty healthy, but I've never given them any fertilizer in all the time I've had them. I shall report back on any results I get.

The Miracle -Gro Shake and feed is a fantastic alternative to the overly expensive Osmocote.Once you try it you won’t want to go back to Osmocote.  Although I have only been using it for 2 weeks I can already tell the differences.First off, I Immediately liked the built in pouring spout to disperse the fertilizer.  (Osmocote has a cap you have to unscrew –clunky to use.)  Miracle-Gro also doesn’t have the toxic smell of ammonia that you get with Osmocote which sensitive noses with appreciate.  Another thing I found annoying with Osmocote are the round shells left behind when the fertilizer is used up. They look very unattractive and float everywhere when you water.  I have not noticed shells with the Miracle -Gro …yet.  Instead, it appears to come in different sizes granules, I assume to disperse fertilizer at different time lines.And my plants seem to be just as happy with the Miracle -Gro which is a lot cheaper.  This product really impressed me and won me over.  Miracle -Gro has seemed to fix all the issues that have irritated me with Osmcote, I only wish it had tried it sooner!Brief run downMiracle -Gro vs. OsmocoteMiracle-Gro ProsCheaper than OsmocoteDoesn’t appear to leave behind ugly empty ‘shells’ when fertilizer is gone.Pours out easily, easy to disperseDoesn’t have toxic ammonia smell that Osmocote hasMiracle-Gro ConsCan’t think of one yet, will have to see as I use it longer.Miracle-Gro is the clear winner! I like!Brief run downMiracle-Gro vs. OsmocoteMiracle-Gro ProsCheaper than OsmocoteDoesn’t appear to leave behind ugly empty ‘shells’ when fertilizer is gone.Pours out easily, easy to disperseDoesn’t have toxic ammonia smell that Osmocote hasMiracle-Gro ConsCan’t think of one yet, will have to see as I use it longer.Miracle-Gro is the clear winner! I like!
summary: Miracle is Cheaper & has seemed to fixed the issues that have irritated me with Osmcote, I only wish it had tried it sooner

reviewText: With a nickname like 'The Peripatetic Gardener' you know that I've been using Miracle-Gro Shake 'N Feed All Purpose Continuous Release Plant Food for years.We've had great success with the entire line of Miracle-Gro products.  And using this easy to apply fertilizer often signals the start of our gardening year.I'm far from the most energetic gardener out there.  But I enjoy 'waking' our slumbering shrubs, flowers, and trees once the danger of frost has past.  I simply shake the suggested amount of Miracle-Gro around each plant, scratch it in a bit, and water.Later, I'll add a bit to the new annuals as they go in.I like that it continues to act for up to three months.  It's like the 'easy button' for gardeners.
summary: If only everything were this easy....

reviewText: I have used the Miracle-Gro Continuous Release Plant Food for about 10 years. I find that the plants require no additional fertilizer for the entire season. I particularly use it for flowers, but I have caved in a bit on my organic gardening as I have gotten older and use a bit of this fertilizer on some of my vegetables. I still refuse to use any herbicides or pesticides. I still pick off potato bugs, etc. by hand.I started out by using Osmicote fertilizer, but the cost is higher and I have found little or no difference with the Miracle-Gro.I mix my own potting soil for seedlings: 2 parts any top soil which I sieve to remove foreign matter and make fine, one part peat moss, 1/4 to 1/2 part Perlite and a shake or two of Miracle-Gro. IF NEEDED, I add Aluminum sulfate to make the soil more acid for the acid loving plants or lime for those which require an alkaline soil. I have had very good success with this.  The Continuous release plant food prevents any burning or over-fertilizing of the seedlings or plants. This is a good product.

Gardening is one of my hobbies, both flower and veggies, and I'm a long-time user of MiracleGro products. Last year I bought a container of the Shake `n Feed and was pleased with the results, so I jumped on the opportunity to review their product.I find the Shake `n Feed line very easy to use since there's no messy mixing of liquid. Just sprinkle on the pellets in a pattern similar to the illustration on the label and you're good for three months. Note: the directions advise not to pile the product around plant stems or apply to wet foliage. Following this advice, I sprinkled the pellets on the soil in the vicinity of my newly transplanted strawberries, beets, sugar snap peas, kohlrabi and roses. It's too early to see any results, but I feel confident the product will perform as well as it did last year. Its NPK formula of 12% nitrogen, 4% phosphorus and 8% potassium along with a plethora of micro-nutrients helps keep overworked soil nutrient dense, thus promoting new growth. I even use it around my Meyer lemon trees with less yellowing effect.This year we assembled a greenhouse and I've been fertilizing the newly potted plants even before I set them out in the garden. We've been fortunate to have a mild winter (I'm in Zone 8), so already the days are in the high sixties to low seventies. The fertilized plants are looking very perky; I'll provide an update in a few weeks, noting any new growth as well as overall plant health. I plan to continue the use into mid-summer and slack off in Fall when the plants require less nitrogen.My overall thoughts on Shake `n Feed: an easy to use product at a reasonable price and one that gets results.
summary: So easy to use and gets results

reviewText: I'm not going to have time to use this before reviewing it, we still have snow cover here, but I have used the product before and this is a different format. Yes, much more convenient than measuring out a tablespoon of plant food and filling the watering can. Just shake onto plants. I will update later!

Like many (if not most!) home gardeners, I've been using Miracle-Gro products for years.  Their foliar sprays are very fast acting, but short-lived; the Shake’n Feed products incorporate both fast-acting fertilizer and a polymer-coated slow-release component.  The combination provides an immediate boost, plus a long tail.Application – The package says that a single application lasts up to three months.  Because many of the trace minerals are water soluble and not in a time-release form , I prefer to use the recommended amount for the first spring feeding, and then feed roughly 2/3 of the recommended  amount every two months thereafter.  This 4-1/2 pound package will feed roughly 135 sq. ft. if you’re using it in a vegetable garden or flower bed.  For outdoor pots use 1 tbsp. for an 8” pot; 1.5 tbsp. for 10”; 3 tbsp. for 12” and 5 tbsp. for 14” pots.  Indoor plants should get half that amount.Composition – Nitrogen – 12%; Phosphate – 4%; Potash – 8%; Calcium – 1.5%; Magnesium – 1.4%; Sulfur – 4.2%; Copper – 0.05%; Iron – 0.9%; Manganese  - 0.35%; Zinc – 0.1%.A few years ago, my daughter and I were in the back yard planting annuals.  About half way through, she got a little lazy and stopped mixing fertilizer into the bottom of the hole.  Those plants ended up much smaller than the ones that were fertilized...proof that both my soil is lousy and that this stuff really works.Highly Recommended...
summary: Easy to use and works well...

reviewText: My box arrived unscathed and the assembly of the trimmer took about 2 minutes (1 minute being used to find a small phillips screw driver, the only tool you'll need).Overall, the unit looks like it has some ergonomic features, such as a wheel to roll on while edging, fully adjustable angles on the head unit, etc. Trouble is, as other people have noted also, that holding the power-on button is awkward and eventually becomes tiring because of the pressure required to keep it engaged. The trimmer design could be better so that it would not feel as awkward - perhaps the handles could be shaped more like those found on metal detectors? So using this trimmer is great in short bursts, not so great over longer periods.Avoid the temptation to think that the automatic line feed feature is in fact automatic. You can advance the string in small increments manually by pushing a button on the spool and pulling on the trimming line at the same time or stop/start the trimmer over and over to get it to advance 1/4" of line each time you stop and start it.  The latter option appears to be the Greenworks definition of "automatic" though it's a bit annoying in that you need to stop and start the thing over and over while using it to make use of this feature.One potentially serious negative was that the included charger does not properly engage the battery and as such cannot charge it. Thankfully, I had also bought the40V mower, so I could use the battery charger included with that unit. I contacted Greenworks by e-mail and after several weeks of waiting called them to follow up. Allegedly, a new charger is now on it's way to me. Curiously, Greenworks didn't want the old charger back or its serial number. However prompt the current response by telephone is now, it would have been even better if Greenworks could be as responsive regarding e-mails as it is regarding being called.Speaking of the charger, this could be a more intelligent design than it is.  While having a smart charger is a step up from the constant voltage chargers that some lead-acid competitors use, the LEDs on this unit could be put to better use (see included pictures above). The current design of the charger lights is less than helpful since three possible battery conditions are indicated by one combination of lights (left red, green right). Why is this a problem?  Well, one of the states includes a battery pack that is too hot. Good design practice would dictate that the user be alerted to this issue because it can literally be explosive.It's not that hard to make the LEDs behave differently based on the current condition of the battery pack, the designers simply didn't elect to do so. For example, it is trivial to combine red and green LEDs to make a orange color, which might be a good cue for the "battery too hot" condition. Same LED count on the PCB, just a smarter application of the microprocessor running them. According to other customers anecdotes, it appears that a dangerous battery condition is indicated with a orange light - just not not per the manual or the attached tag.Anyhow, while I am pleased overall with the product (other than the less-than automatic) "automatic" line feed, I am quite unimpressed with the company behind the product. Try contacting the company behind the Neuton sometime. I had an e-mail response within 8 hours, offering to sell me a spare mower part that had broken. With this sort of e-mail support (4 weeks and counting) I wonder why Greenworks bothers publishing an e-mail address at all. All it will do is aggravate those seeking support from Greenworks.
summary: Easy to Assemble but Battery Charger DOA

reviewText: Set up was not exactly a breeze.  The manual was a little hard to follow but luckily it wasn't rocket science to get it together.  But I think we mostly just figured it out on our own than rely on the instructions we were given which were not the clearest.The battery (it says) comes uncharged.  It looked to us as if it had half a charge.  When we put it on the charger it looked like it was saying it was fully charged - yet the lights on the tester still indicated half a charge.  We let it go all night and the same thing was there next morning.  I worked with it, took it off and put it on again and then noticed a gray lever and worked with that and then noted that the battery began to charge at that point so we didn't have it on the charger correctly even though it seemed like we did.  So we let it charge fully and a few hours later it was.The trimmer is WAY taller/longer in the handle than our other one.  And I am short.  So for me this is going to take some getting used to.  You hold it differently with the elbow resting just in front of the battery pack.  When I was using this as an edger - my arm got really tired.  My husband used it and could not figure out why my arm was tired since there is a wheel for the bottom part and your arm just rests at the top so he thinks that I am perhaps trying to hold the trimmer up more than I need to.  I agree with his assessment.  This will just take some time to get used to.We both agree the trigger to operate the trimmer makes your fingers tired.  There is no way around that.We both think that the auto feed for the string is not the greatest.  We felt the string is always an inch or two too short.  Sometimes it will kick out a long enough string but 90% of the time it's too short for our tastes, although it is perfectly functional with the size string it has.  But when edging we felt the string would do better if it were longer.  For regular wacking the shorter string I guess is fine... but a longer string would get the job done faster of course.We like the ease of going from wacking to edging and how adjustable everything is... no to mention the battery power of it.  Battery charges very quickly once you figure it out.  The power is just as good as our old corded wacker, I cannot tell a difference there.I can tell you we are dumping our old wacker in favor of this new one... so the problems I outlined above are not serious enough for us to not use it.  We feel it is superior to our old corded wacker which feeds out string better and doesn't make our fingers tired when we use it - so I think that should say something about how much we like this new battery powered wacker even with the negative things we have mentioned.
summary: It has a lot of adjustabilty and options.  Nice power.  String seems short.

reviewText: As the owner of aBlack & Decker LST220 12-Inch 20-Volt Lithium-Ion Cordless GrassHog Trimmer/EdgerI was somewhat reluctant to try another trimmer. Quite honestly, I was happy with the Black & Decker. That is, until I got my hands on the Greenworks 21132A.What I found on the Greenworks trimmer were more options. I'm able to rotate the trimmer head to the best angle for me, turn the head and use its side-wheel to run as an Edger (way better than the metal wire on the B&D;), and reposition the lower handle. The latter is the most important element to me. With the Black & Decker, the lower handle is set in place, making it a short grip for my long arms, whereas the Greenworks adjusts to fit me perfectly. The only thing I don't like about the Greenworks' lower handle is that it feels a little cheap, like it could break in the future, but it's possible they give it some play for a reason. On the upper handle, I appreciate the better grip; much easier to hold.Another great feature is that the shaft is longer on the Greenworks. This, coupled with the larger trimming shield, helps to keep stuff from flying back and hitting me. The wheel on the side works great too--not just for edging, but for guiding the trimmer around trees.The Greenworks is a little heavier (9.6 pounds) than the Black & Decker (9 pounds), but not by much. The Greenworks balances better so the weight difference doesn't significantly affect me. The large 40-Volt, 4Ah Lithium-Ion Battery adds the most weight. Whereas the Black & Decker uses a 20-Volt. At first, I thought I was getting gypped on the Greenworks by not getting two batteries like I did on the Black & Decker, but after looking at the strength and quality of the single battery, I realized that running out of juice before the project is done isn't a concern--one battery basically equals two. Another advantage with the Greenworks is that the battery has an indicator that shows you how full/empty it is. With the B&D;, you have to wait until it stops working.In the end, the Greenworks Trimmer surpasses the Black & Decker on many levels. So much so that I'll be getting rid of my B&D; and happily transition into the Greenworks from this day forward.
summary: Much better than my Black & Decker

reviewText: This string trimmer is equipped with a formidable 40 volt lithium-ion battery and consequently it performs better and lasts longer than most other battery operated trimmers.  Although comparable in power to a gas operated trimmer, the Greenworks eliminates much of the noise and all of the noxious fumes associated with that method.  The battery supposedly arrives discharged (although it appeared to be at least partially charged) and requires about 3 hours to fully charge as instructed.  Greenworks also warns not to allow the battery to run down completely nor to overcharge it. The convenient LED battery indicator keeps you aware of its status so this shouldn't be difficult.  We have yet to use the trimmer long enough in one session to discharge the battery, but according to the manual, it should last for 70  minutes between charges.
