How nice to see a large variety and number of birds feeding simultaneously.Perky-Pet needs to test their products in hard-core squirrel country.  Where there's a will, there's a way, and squirrels around here are experts at draining and destroying.  The cap on this feeder does offer a lock system of sorts, but it is flimsy.  Just a matter of time before I break the little plastic pieces off or the squirrels do.  There's nothing to stop squirrels from lazily wrapping themselves around a tray and gorging themselves either.  That's why I've located the Panorama off an old basketball hoop--no squirrel can reach it.  With a little care on my part, this feeder hopefully will last a long time.If you don't have squirrel problems, I highly recommend this universal feeder.  It does not selectively keep out any bird, is esthetically pleasing to look at and its cost is within every birder's budget.
summary: All The Birds Like This Feeder

reviewText: the birds in my area LOVE this feederit was a little harder to fill than i had hopedbut then again i was trying to be creative and fill it with two different bird seed blends lolit is really easy to take apart for cleaning and that is something i really like about itand it is really easy to fill when i am not trying to get creative with two kinds of seedanother creature that LOVE this feeder...Squirrels ...they hop on it and shake the food out onto the groundi have it on a hook am hoping to go find a pole that it can sit onwe have a pole but it is too wide for the hole on the bottom of this feederi think once i get it on a pole that will prevent them from being able to shake food out of itit is a very nice feeder one f our favorites for watching birds on itso big and we get so many different kinds of birds to feed of it
summary: Perky Pet Panorama Feeder -NOT squirrel proof

reviewText: How exciting to see this bird feeder offered through the vine program!  I can NEVER have too many feeders and it turns out this one is great!I LOVE that it has two compartments that allow you to put two kinds of food in one feeder.I like the construction of the feeder and the overall design as well.The squirrels haven't noticed it (yet!) so I don't know how it will do once the invasion begins and they start digging at the ports.  Will update if they destroy it.Until then, I, and my birds, are enjoying this very nice feeder.UPDATE: After almost a year of constant use, exposure to blazing hot sun and many many hard freezes I can say this is still a 5-star feeder and my favorite.  It has withstood the evil squirrels many attempts to chew/vandalize/sabotage--HOORAY!  Most of all, what I love is that refilling the feeder is a breeze.  I leave it hanging on the shepherd's hook, squeeze button and slide cover up.  Fill the bottom with a songbird blend and the top with a nuts/berries blend, squeeze button and slide cover down til snug.  No need to remove from hook and balance on ground. Quick and Easy.  Buying another one today.  Oh, and this feeder is always covered with birds!

I replaced a problematic bird feeder with the [[ASIN: Perky-Pet birds and berries lantern feeder]].  While the screen printed design didn't interest me, the bird feeder itself did a good job of feeding birds and thwarting squirrels.  Being so pleased with the Perky-Pet bird feeder, I decided to give this more visually appealing option a try.The Perky-Pet 325S panorama wild bird feeder, made in China, is a cylindrical double bird feeder.  In the center of the upper feeder is a tube, which when filled high enough, will drop some seed into the lower chamber.  Once seed falls below the top of the 4.5 inch tube in the 6.5 inch tall chamber, seed no longer falls through to the lower level.  The shallow .75 inch feeding tray has drain holes placed about 2 inches apart to prevent moisture build up, and is encircled by a perch ring 1.25 inches from the edge of the tray for birds to rest on while feeding.A short metal cable runs through the center of the feeder, allowing the top to stay securely in place.  Adding seed up to a maximum of 4.5 pounds requires pressing a button to release the tension and allow the lid to slide up the cable.  The bottom chamber can also be opened up for filling if you would rather not deal with the upper tube or use two different bird seed blends. Fill with seed, align the parts, and press the button again to secure the top back into place.  As the birds feed, the separate compartments will empty independently of each other.When I removed my Perky-Pet 325S panorama wild bird feeder from the box, it was clearly damaged.  All the fastening clips from the upper plastic surround had broken off, leaving sharp jagged edges to cut myself on.  Fortunately the bird feeder still assembles securely without any difficulty.  Even so, I went to Perky-Pet's website to request a replacement part.  They offer live chat, although it wasn't available when I attempted to use it.  Instead I was given the option to send an email.  I received a response three days later indicating I should try to resolve the problem with Amazon.  If I found Amazon unwilling to resolve the problem, Perky-Pet would allow me to file a warranty claim.The Sure Lock Cap system keeps squirrels out of the compartments themselves.  However the shallow feeding trays cause seed to fall over the sides as small sized birds peck and push at the seeds.  Getting into the bird feeder is unnecessary as there is so much seed on the lawn for big birds and squirrels to enjoy.  I'm not sure the Sure Lock Cap system really matters on this bird feeder.When it comes to keeping squirrels away from the seed, the Perky-Pet birds and berries lantern feeder is the better choice.  However, the Perky-Pet 325S panorama wild bird feeder attracts more birds feeding at the same time and brings larger birds to the yard to feed on fallen seed.  The Perky-Pet 325S panorama wild bird feeder is worthy of consideration, although it may not fit everyone's needs or desires.PROS:YouTube channel provides bird feeding tipsWilling to resolve customer issues12-month limited warrantyCONS:May keep squirrels out of the seed compartments, but they will still enjoy the seedSlow customer service response timeArrived damaged
summary: Two Feeders In One: A The Perky-Pet 325S Panorama Wild Bird Feeder By Woodstream Corp. Review

reviewText: Perky Pet 325S Panorama Bird Feeder has a metal top & metal perches/trays with large feeding ports. Another great feature are the trays which have drain holes. To open the bird feeder, press the button on the top, then pull the top up along the hanging cord.When you open the feeder, you'll see the  tube  we used  to fill the bottom part of the feeder. To make filling the bottom half easier, we used a funnel similar to this one, Heath Outdoor Products FS-1 Feed Scoop-Funnel.This feeder is fun because you can fill it with two different types of seeds to attract a wider variety of birds. In the past, I layered different types of seeds in our feeders but still only the birds that liked that seed would visit.  With the Panorama, different types of birds can enjoy their favorite seed at the same time. The feeding ports are fairly large so we can use the seed that gets stuck in our other bird feeders.Our squirrels haven't bothered it yet. The very, very intelligent squirrel that got into all of our feeders last year, is missing this year.  He wouldn't give up until he was victorious. Of course, he irritated me, but I loved watching him spend hour upon hour trying to figure out a solution.  Anyway, he's gone now & none of the other squirrels are as interested in our feeders as he was.  I'm sure that before summer's end, the squirrels will be eating from this feeder too, but they won't be knocking the top off, they'll probably be performing acrobatics using the perches.UPDATE 6/11: The birds are loving this feeder! It took about a week for them to begin using it. Since the birds' discovery,  visits have been increasing daily. I haven't seen any squirrels on it yet, but the seed has been going down fast which makes me wonder. Several squirrels are eating seed off the grass below the feeder.
summary: Metal top & perches... the metal trays have drain holes...birds love this feeder

reviewText: I liked how this bird feeder looked, how sturdy it feels and how big it is. What I didn't like was it was hard to get open. I like something that I can throw up and easily refill with feed. Just makes life a little easier. Other than that, it's a nice feeder and I would recommend it!
summary: It's a middle of the line review...

reviewText: I received this as an amazon vine reviewer and thought it would work nicely to attract different kinds of birds.  It actually does have more space and now the Robins, Blue Jays and Woodpeckers don't look so awkward when feeding on the more sparrow friendly:Droll Yankee B7F 20-Inch Pewter 6-Port Sunflower Wild Bird Feeder.However, the pretty cap does not look so pretty once you put a squirrel proof cap on it.  This one more or leas matches if you hang it 10 inches or more above the bird feeder's built in cap:Woodlink Wrap Around BCBAF22 4 x 4 Baffle, 22 Inch - Bronze Color.You could probably attach the bird feeder to a poll, but there is no way to securely attach it to a poll without some specialized equipement. You need to depend on gravity and better ingenuity to connect to a poll.  You could then try this to keep the squirrels away:Droll Yankees SQPM Pole Mount Squirrel Guard.Overall, the design is very nice.  The push button release takes a bit getting used to.  If squirrels aren't a problem, this is a great bird feeder, especially if you have birds larger than sparrows that you wish to feed.

I was really excited about this feeder. It sounded so promising against the squirrels..but to no luck here. :( It didn't take long at all. The squirrels by us cleaned out the bottom section in a day and had the top section emptied in another two days. I witnessed it, saw them with little trouble feast away.If squirrels aren't an issue in your area than by all means this is a great feeder. Light weight yet quality construction. Easy to fill and hang. And, the best part, I LOVE the design concept of 2 separate feeders in one. I anxiously filled each compartment with a different mix in hopes of attracting multiple species of birds. Now I'm not sure if given the fact the squirrels emptied the bottom first, if they prefered that food or if it was the easier to access....The search for me continues!

This is such a cool feeder. It is fairly large, which makes it possible to have several birds on it at once (and they do!) It feels quite substantial. I was worried the clear plastic would be flimsy and the 'copper' would be thin plastic, but not so. It is heavy and the cord isn't plastic but a metal wire cord.To fill, you must depress the toggle switch (genius!) to release the top. This keeps the top in place during use and makes it difficult for smarty pants squirrels who finagle their way into my other feeders. The top opens with a tug and you are able to fill both chambers from the top. There is a cylinder that runs from the top into the bottom, allowing you to fill both chambers at once or the op differently than the bottom.We have filled it 3 times in the 2 weeks that we've owned it. The birds seem to favor it above the others, even with all containing the same kind of seeds. I enjoy it because it is attractive and I have every indication that it will stand the test of time, use and weather.

The problem is that this product is designed to be sold loose on a shelf. But since Amazon ships everything, it is shipped in the warehouse packaging which is normally shipped on a wrapped palate to stores. As such my first one came broken in a very cheep cardboard box and no foam to protect it. The second one was shipped in a bigger box with padding and arrived undamaged.The second problem is there are no instructions on how to open the damn thing. It took me a bit to figure out exactly how and where to twist the top with out twisting the base off by accident. But once I figured it out, it became a very nice feeder.Unlike your normal Tube-style feeder, this one is basically two feeders in one. so instead of all the birds fighting over the bottom holes, they can feed at all holes till both chambers are empty. Now I especially like the copper finish, almost all my feeders are copper colored. And so far the squirrels have not noticed this one yet and since I give them their own feeder, the birds usually steal from them.Overall, a great feeder, but you should check for damage if it is not shipped in another padded box.

I bought this to replace an older feeder that was damaged during last winter's storms, and after a number of months this appears to be a winner. The construction of the feeder seems sturdy, so I have no fears about it lasting. The design is what makes this a 5-star product. The 360 view means that more birds can hang on and feed, which makes it that much more enjoyable for me. It's deceiving how much bird feed this holds, as well. I don't have to fill it up nearly as much as my last one.
summary: Great design, and appears to be sturdy

reviewText: One the one hand, this feeder holds a ton of seed, and the two chambers allow you to put two different kinds out if you'd like.  On the other hand, this thing is giant and when full it's very heavy.  I know if it ever gets knocked off the hook by acrobatic squirrels, the weight will cause the plastic to shatter when it hits the ground.The small troughs the seed collects in at the bottoms of the sections have a lip that seems like a good height, the birds haven't made as much of a mess with this feeder compared to other models I've had.

I'm a birder.  Have been for decades, although I no longer tromp through the brush every weekend with binocs pressed to my eyes. No, now I sit at the kitchen table chain-drinking coffee and watching the tweets as they flick about the feeders.The last feeder I was fortunate enough to snag wasPerky Pet's  Five Tier Bird Feeder.  At first I was skeptical about the design, but that feeder has become their favorite... and consequently my favorite.This Panorama Feeder is nice though.  In fact, it's far superior as far as appearance, having an antiqued bronze look that would fit into even the neatest garden, be it modern, colonial, or asian in feel.  (at least in my opinion)AND if appearance is important to you, BUY this feeder rather than the 5-Tier, which after some time strikes me as a bit funky.BUT for myself I prefer the 5-Tier, and here's why.  Both feeders are sort of messy to fill, but the birds just love the wire cage.  To my surprise the goldfinches and sparrows, nuthatches and titmice just love hanging from the sides.  They like the Panorama, but they haven't developed the same zeal towards it, which might be because it's rather new, but I think they feel more comfortable hanging sideways to sitting straight up.I really like the Perky Pet Panorama and I do Recommend It.  It's attractive and the birds like it.  It is not as easy to fill as one would think, and the idea of filling the top with one seed, and the bottom section with another is going to take some machinations are your part.  Simple said, it's an over flow system so you must use a funnel and fill the bottom section entirely before you can fill the top with a different sort of seed.SQUIRRELS!  The bane of many a bird feeder, the Panorama offers superior protection when compared to the 5-Tier.  Not that anything is squirrel proof.Enjoy!ps--Let me also note that I am shocked that the birds have all but abandoned my old feeder, a well used, sturdy greenHeritage Farms Bird Feeder.  But they like these Perky Pets.
summary: Very Pretty (a comparison with other feeders)

reviewText: Perky-Pet's Panorama Bird Feeder was received well packaged and fully assembled to use. It took us less than 5 mins to hang this up on a tree filled with bird seeds. To our surprise it took even less time for the birds in our backyard to discover the new bonanza and started feeding on this panorama bird feeder instantly. Very satisfying to see it.The construction is mixed with metal and plastic parts and seems sturdy enough to last few years. It looks very elegant in our backyard. We have had this now for a week and so far my family is liking it. But more so my backyard birds are having a blast!. They love it.Five stars! from me.

I love that you can put two different feeds in this bird feeder to attract the most variety of birds. Filling is simple. The top slides up the cable and their is a brown tube to pour inside for the bottom level. It is designed to empty both chambers evenly and looks great on garden poles. The squirrels are adamant on feeding and right now, they are hilariously loosing the battle by consistently falling off the wide top.  The feeder stands about a foot and half high and a little over a half foot wide and stores a little less than a 5 pound bag. It is suggested that every two weeks a cleaning is needed with mild soap and water.

This is an attractive, fairly large feeder. It says you can use 2 kinds of feed, but I just have mixed seed in it. (I have the Perky-Pet Grandview feeder next to it, filled with sunflower seed.) It's made of metal, with a pretty dark copper color. My wild little friends like it fine. My only complaint is the soft braided hanging wire. If it was more rigid towards the top, it would be much easier to hang.

This is a nice bird feeder, with two tiers that can be filled with different types of seeds, or the same type. The sections lock together firmly, and the perching area is made of metal, not plastic. The top clamps into place on the hanging wire with a spring clamp. I would have preferred the top cover be wider, for better protection from rain, but that is a problem with most all feeders, not just this one. The seed seems to dispense well, and birds from dove size down to finches have not had issues using the feeder. This feeder holds a lot seed too.

I maintain over 10 bird feeders in my backyard.  Each one is designed to attract and feed different species of birds.  I have a thistle feeder for finches, suet feeder for woodpeckers, nectar feeders for hummingbirds, etc.  When I got the opportunity to get this feeder I was very interested in it based on it's ability to distribute two different types of seeds at the same time.The lid of the feeder is removed by pressing on a button and sliding it up a cord.  Looking down the external feeding tube you can see and inner tube that fills the lower section of the feeder.  I liked this feature since I could fill the lower section with a seed that would attract one type of bird and a different type of seed in the top for other birds.  I used a funnel type ofscoopto fill the inner tube that allowed me to put safflower seed in the lower portion of the feeder.  Once that is filled I added sunflower seeds to the top portion.Here is where the feeder failed for me.  Once it was hung it was entirely emptied in less that three hours.  This thing holds over four pounds of seed so for it to be eaten in such a short period of time represents an epic fail for my needs.  I can afford neither the time or the seed to keep this feeder in service.  The reason that it was emptied in such short order has to do with the width of the perch.In the part of Texas that I live (San Antonio) we have an over-abundance of White-winged Doves.  I have found that many other areas have their own version of "pest" birds that will monopolize a feeder to such an extent that no other bird can get a meal from it.  The doves, which are fairly large, can easily perch on the large ring of this feeder and since they are so numerous and travel in flocks they clean out the feeder in short order.  So instead of getting to see a wide variety of colorful birds visiting this feeder through the day I am treated to a hoard of plain colored birds occupying and emptying it within a few hours.  Although the Perky-Pet Panorama Feeder works well (maybe too well for me) I have taken it down since I am not interested in operating a White-winged Dove restaurant.
summary: It works almost too well as a general purpose bird feeder

reviewText: This is a beautiful and stylish feeder.  I've only used it for a few weeks but it seems well-made and sturdy, and the feed doesn't get wet during a heavy downpour of rain.  But the best part of this feeder is the dual compartments that let use two different feeds in the same container.  There is also a hollow tube down the center that allows you easily fill the bottom compartment without disassembling the entire thing.  This is a very nice feature, but I wish the tube extended all the way to the top of the upper compartment.  The tube stops about a 2 inches from the top so you need to be careful when pouring the seed into the tube (they tend to go flying).  In the end I found a funnel that made the job of fill the bottom compartment a lot easier.The only hesitation I have about the feeder is that it attracts doves that monopolize the feeder and scare off the smaller song birds.  The perch encircling the feeder is wide enough for the doves to balance on, so they will sit on the perch and eat and eat and eat until everything is gone.I have a second feeder with a smaller perch and this seems to work much better in my yard.  The smaller birds eat from the feeder and the doves sit on the ground and gobble up whatever falls their way.So if you have a lot of dove or black birds in your area, this might not be the best choice.
summary: Large perch allows Doves to monopolize feeder

reviewText: The Perky-Pet Panorama Bird Feeder arrived well packaged and fully assembled. Set-up was a breeze (it is one of four feeders in our wild bird sanctuary garden and replaced an older feeder that did not keep the squirrels out.It came with instructions about the importance of cleaning the feeder tubes every two weeks but did not give instructions on how to remove the tubes for cleaning. I did not find this information on Perky-Pet's website but finally figured out that if you detach the lid, then press down the plastic tube with one hand and turn the bottom tray with the other, the tube will slide out of the tabs holding it in place. Since it is plastic, I recommend doing this with a gentle hand so as not to break the tabs.The tubes together hold 4.5 pounds of seed and fill easily. Since there are two independent seed compartments that are filled and emptied separately, several birds can feast together. Two different types of seed may be used simultaneously to attract a wider variety of birds.The top is sturdy and has a stop to keep it in place, thus foiling attempts by eager squirrels to get at the grain. I will report back on its effectiveness. So far, the birds like it and it's an attractive and functional addition to our cottage garden.

This feeder comes fully assembled. I like the steel cable that runs through the lid and is attached to the bottom of the feeder. The cable has a built-in loop that makes hanging easy right out-of-the-box. Note that the rest of the feeder is virtually entirely plastic.This feeder fills easily once hung. The lid is attached directly to the steel cable, and held in-place by a spring-loaded button. You simply press the button, and you can slide the lid up the steel cable, out of the way, and have access to the top for filling. I use a cup to pour in the seed. The chambers are segmented in such a way that causes the top chamber to overflow into the bottom chamber, but they are separate chambers, so you can add different types of seed to each chamber if you are careful when filling it, because you don't have direct access to the bottom chamber. However, the benefit is that the chambers empty at their own paces, which means the bottom chamber can actually empty before the top chamber.I use a wild-bird or songbird blend in this particular feeder. Sometimes there are three to four birds perched on each of the two segments' feed trays. Larger birds have also attempted to make use of the feeder (crows, starlings, and jays). Mourning Doves feed off dropped seed on the ground.From a squirrel-proof perspective, I don't think the squirrels in my yard can get to this feeder, either because it is ill-placed for them, or because it proves challenging (or a combination of both). I've been using it for over a month, and I've yet to see a squirrel perched on it or trying to climb down it. I think the smooth plastic presents them with a problem. Disclosure: I have a second feeder in the yard which the squirrels always access, so maybe they are simply distracted and don't need to access this feeder.What I've noticed is that birds have been able to drain this feeder quickly. The seed mix flows quite quickly into the feeding trays. I easily go through a 10-pound bag of mixed seed (no sunflowers) within 4-5 days. There have been days when I can fill this feeder in the morning, and it will be completely empty by the next morning. Granted, there are a lot of birds accessing it, but I wish they couldn't drain it so quickly.In general, I like how this looks, and I like how it is built. It looks good in the yard (even when empty). Birds have no problem accessing it, and it does exactly what it is intended to do -- attract birds and feed them.
summary: Good build, easy to fill, drains fast

reviewText: PRETTY
This is durable and holds many different bird species from small to the large. The sparrows and Mexican parrots love this stand

I hung two of these on a gardman pole feeder.  The cardinals love it.  It holds enough seed that I don't have to fill it every day.  One caution.  These are very well packaged in bubble wrap and tape.  While trying to cut the tape away so I could unwrap it, I nicked the steel hanging cable.  It still works fine, but be careful unwrapping it.

The winter birds that frequent our neighborhood must be awfully hungry, so I decided that I would buy a couple of these to help them keep fed and warm.  I use Black-striped sunflower seeds (thinner shells than regular sunflower seeds).  This particular bird feeder seems quite sturdy, easy to put together and to fill with seeds.  I would say that probably 10-12 birds can fit comfortably on the outer rim to feed on the seeds.  The seeds are released to an area below the chamber that holds the seeds, providing easy access to the seeds.  This bird feeder has a classy look to it and our covered, open-air patio seems  I would definitely recommend this bird feeder to my friends
summary: The winter birds are having a feast!

reviewText: I am using this with a common wrought iron hanger under a tree in our yard. I am on a second course of bird seed and it is fun to see the smaller birds (mainly Finches) feed methodically.  Larger birds (Jays and Doves) attempt to feed but frequently can't support themselves and there is much flapping of wings and bird cries. It is easy to assemble and disassemble and is very attractive in our yard.
The squirrels love it and do not chew it up because they can get plenty to eat. It is supposed to be attractive to Cardinals but they still remain on the ground and eat the droppings.

I just got this feeder to replace an older one that was hard to fill without making a mess. One important point. Its NOT squirrel or raccoon proof as some are. I have this hanging on a tall pole and they can get on the feeder and empty it quickly even with a lube on pole. Ordered the Brome unit to replace this. You get what you pay for.
summary: Easy to fill but NOT Squirrel or Raccoon proof.

reviewText: This feeder looks very pretty in my yard and was easy to fill.  However, birds haven't paid much attention to it yet even though they have emptied out the other feeders I have in my backyard.  My other feeders are brightly colored (one is yellow, the other red), so I am not sure if they are easier to see (I used the same seeds, so that isn't it), but so far the birds in my yard haven't been interested in this feeder and only fly to it and then fly away.  I'll keep an eye out and will update my review it there are any changes.
summary: Very pretty but the birds haven't used it yet

reviewText: Squeeze a knob at the top and lift the cover, pour in the seeds, and slide the cover back down the wire. Voila, refill done!The birds in our yard are having a blast at this feeder.
summary: Easy to refill, works well for small bids

reviewText: I filled it and put it outside on my porch. The small birds don't use it at all. The larger birds have tried several times but they weigh too much and the feeder starts to sway and the birds can't hang on and leave.
summary: So far the birds don't use it

reviewText: First, shipped well packed and quick.  Second, it looks great, better than the photo on AZ.  Third, it has some features I didn't find on more expensive feeders, i.e. the coated cable that holds it goes through the top and then is anchored to the metal base.  I had one this feeder replaced where the cable was just to a bar stuck through the sides of the plastic of the feeder.  The plastic just gave out, the feeder fell and now is in the junk.  Another nice feature is the little button on the beautifully polished copper top which you push and hold to lift off the top and once filled, slide the top back down securely on the plastic portion to lock it.  Well made all the way.  Also like that the seed passes through several ports into the perch mounted feeder tray rather than just spilling into it.  I think this will really cut down the spillage.  Very pleased.  Oh, btw.  Somebody mentioned in another feeder review that you could douse the seed with pepper and oil to deter squirrels.  That's too much bother.  Just get the cheapest economy size container of cayenne pepper you can find and just liberally sprinkle it over your seed when you get it.  Mix it in (maybe sneeze a couple of times) and with this stuff mixed through your seed, no more squirrels.  I've seen a squirrel hit one of my feeders, must have got a snoot full of pepper and down he went, rubbing his head on the grass trying to relieve his 'burn'.  It doesn't hurt the squirrel but he's finished with your feeder (he'll tell his friends) and it's actually good for the birds who don't seem to mind the pepper at all. As long as your feeders are kept well laced with cayenne, you don't need fancy squirrel baffles.

This is a pretty bird feeder and a comfortable place for the visiting birds to feast on their favorite seeds. I have had this feeder for six months and it's been hanging on the tree in front of my house since then. It has seen sunny, rainy, snowy and windy weather, but it held up very well to all of these weather related challenges. I am quite happy with this purchase and so are the birds.
Attractive, functions perfect, nice hanging wire cord and the birds are getting fat while entertaining us.  Really a fair price for an attractive product.

I'd been wanting to get myself a second hose holder for my house for a while, and being able to try this out was great for me.  I've had a hose reel cart for 12 years, but I've grown tired of wheeling it back and forth between the front and back yards.  Because I'm used to the hose reel, I'll be partly comparing this to it.First off, this is a nice looking holder.  As a guy, I opened the box and thought, "looks nice" and didn't give it much more thought...until my elderly neighbor walked by with her dog, started a conversation, and stopped in the middle of a sentence to remark how nice it was.  She seemed to really like it, and I think that she has nice taste in her own stuff.  So, I give it high marks for aesthetics.  It is unquestionably better looking than the hose reel cart that I have (which is like thisAmes cart).  The color is nice, and the embossed pattern is attractive.As for construction, it seems sturdy to me.  The thin walls aren't too flimsy, and they give the benefit of the holder being pretty lightweight.  It's really easy for me to move around with a 50" hose in it.  On the other hand, it's also easy for the holder to move around when I'm trying to pull the hose out - but that isn't too bad and could be helped by putting something heavy under the hose to weight it down.So, why do I rate it as only "OK" given all that?  Two reasons:  ease of use, and value.The ease of use isn't as high as that of my hose reel.  I have a no-kink hose that is fairly stiff.  To get the hose to sit in a circle in the holder, it has to be twisted like it was when I bought it.  However, to use the hose, it has to be untwisted so that it extends out straight.  A good forearm workout, but a bit cumbersome.  That's likely true of all hose holders like this, so perhaps unfair to knock it down a star for it - but it definitely isn't as easy as a hose reel.As for value, I have to say that I'm suprised at the current cost of this.  As of this review, the base alone is $90, and the lid costs extra.  At $40-$50 for both, I'd say it's a good value, but not at $90+.Pros:- Attractive- Lightweight- Pretty sturdy constructionCons:- Cumbersome to get a stiffer hose to wind up into a circle inside of it- Expensive.  At least as of this review, the base alone is over $90.- Traps water.  Even with the drain holes, water pools in the bottom of mine.
summary: Very attractive, but a bit cumbersome with stiffer hoses

reviewText: The bright-green, 50-foot hose I keep on the side of my house has always been an eye sore. The CobraCo is a great solution for your loose hose. It's easy to plop your hose in and keep it out of view and the product looks great next to a house or in the garden.Unlike other reviewers who seem to have problems loading and unloading the hose, I just tilt the container on its side to dump it out to use and then hold the hose above the container and "swirl" it to load it back up. Easy for me, but it may depend on the kind of hose you use. (Mine's pretty thick and doesn't kink easily.)The only thing I don't like about the CobraCo is that the lid doesn't fit. It's not a huge issue, but mine has enough of a gap that water can get in and it might blow off in gusty weather. At this price point, I would expect a much more precise fit.

I have used two types of hose holders in the past, reel types which roll the hose onto a reel and hideaway types like this from CobraCo.I have found pros and cons with both types. Typically the reel types offer you more "automation" in that you can pull hose off the eel, and later rewind it with a handle. These tend to work OK, but not perfectly and I've found myself having to walk back to the reel when the hose becomes caught on it, jammed, etc. The hideaway type storage makes is easy to simply take the hose from the holder, but putting it back can be a nuisance, depending on hose quality and length.I would suggest doing the following when putting a hose in the Cobracoe for the first time. First feed the end of the hose you are connecting to your faucet through the container from the inside through the hole to the outside. Leave the rest of the hose lying on or near the container for now. Leave enough hose on the outside of the hole to reach your faucet and allow a little for adjustment. Next, attach a nozzle to the hose, and then connect the hose to the faucet. Now, turn on the water so the hose fills. Then shut the water. While it may be slightly heavier to work with, the water in the hose will make the hose "more responsive" as you fit it into the container. Working from inside the container, start by the hole and wrap the hose around and around the spindle until you have it all in the container. I used 100 feet of hose and it fit without a struggle, but obviously the longer the hose, the more closely you'll want to wrap around the spindle. I did not go super tight around it and fit the 100' without an issue. I was able to securely close the lid with the house and nozzle inside. Some reviews have noted a problem with the lid's ft. Mine fits perfectly so I can go only by my own experience, but it is worth noting that some people have had this complaint.Although they are sold separately, I got both the CobraCo container and the lid for a finished look. The product is made of steel and is lightweight. The finish on the container has "lattice" embossed on it which look similar to Celtic crosses. The lid has raised circles on it. The finish is that of a verdi gras on my container and lid, more like the greenish photos in the advertisement as opposed to a couple of the photos where the product appears more bronze in color. The verdi gras finish gives the impression of a nice patina on the container and lid.The container is about 17" wide, and a little under a foot tall. The lid fits perfectly and I can feel it "snap" into place when I seat it on the container.I ended up tested the container with two hoses. Both are 5/8" diameter. One is a "no kink" heavy duty hose that is 100 feet long. The other is a less expensive 75 foot hose. I was able to put both in without too much hassle.TIP: If you have a brand new hose, you will find it easier to put the container, simply because it is wound tightly from its manufacturer.As far as functionality, I didn't run into any issues using the hose. I was able to easily pull the hose from the container and put it back later. It is a manual process so you do have to wind whatever hose you take out back into the container. But it's pretty simple. The weight of the container and hose combined make the container stable when pulling/removing hose, unlike some reel hose holders, where the reel snags, or the whole reel and unit even drag along the ground if not mounted to the house.The CobraCo hose holder is not cheap, but it is very nice looking and appears to be of good quality. Based on this product, I would buy from CobraCo again.

This is an attractive container if you want to hide your garden hose. The actual color of the container is a medium green with black streaks (a fake aged look but it looks nice) with a lattice pattern. It's much nicer looking (and a lighter color) than the photo that appears in the Amazon description. The container itself, at a little over 9 pounds, seems lightweight - it's easy to pick up and move, but it's not so lightweight that it falls over. It feels sturdy.It easily holds a garden hose. I had no problem coiling a garden hose into the container - the center post makes it easy to put the hose into the container.The container also has several holes - there is one large hole (approximately 2 inches in diameter) along one side toward the bottom from which you can slide the garden hose and then attach to the faucet (you can see this hole in the Amazon photo). However, I'm not sure why you would want to do that - that seems to defeat the purpose of hiding your hose. There are several small holes to drain water (and also helpful if you want to use the container as a pot for a plant).If you want to use it for other purposes, the center post is easy to remove. I can see using it as a container for magazines or even dog toys.Note that this review (and rating) is for the container only. I also received the lid for this hose holder. The lid looks like the lid of a trash barrel - a top with a lip. Unlike a trash container, this lip should fit on the inside of the holder. Unfortunately it's just a bit off - the lip fits on the inside of 3/4 of the container but not for the entire container. For the price of this container (and lid), this lid should fit perfectly.
summary: A nice looking container but expensive

reviewText: This container looks very stately and elegant. It is one large piece of stamped steel that has been treated to look aged and oxidized. Some of the photos make it look shiny olive drab, but it's not really. Mine looks more blueish-green. From a distance, it takes on the appearance of patinated copper. The color and pattern remind me of a piece of armor from ancient China (like the ones the terracotta soldiers wear). Looking closer, the paint job is very obvious and you can see the paint spray patterns and lines left by the treatment process.The container itself is quite large, with a middle post that can be easily removed by loosening 3 bolts. The bottom has 3 small drainage holes (diameter of a pinky) and the side has one larger hole for the hose to pass through, the size of a golf ball. You can use it for a variety of purposes indoors and out, but I'm using mine for holding small books, knick-knacks, DVD's, and video games. I've chosen to keep the stump in because it acts as a convenient divider so all my DVD cases and books don't slump together in a heap. I arrange items around the stump, like a vertical loading washer. This works quite well.It's not quite as thick as I expected. But with thickness comes weight. The lid is sold separately. It doesn't really fit together exactly. Whether this is by design or an engineering mistake, I don't know. The rim of the lid is slightly too wide to mate with the bottom, so one side of the lid will always stick up a bit. For the price, the container should come with the lid. And the lid should fit better. And it should look more inspired than a normal garbage can lid.Overall, a very attractive looking container for inside or outdoors. It fits in with any decor.

I thought this steel hose holder was going to be really heavy. It turned out to be a light weight enough to be easily manageable. There is a 2 inch diameter hole on the side of the hose holder for the hose to come out to attach to the faucet.It has a removable center column, which is great because it makes this item very versatile. I will be using it all summer long outside for my hose, and will be bringing it inside in the winter to use in the house to store my papers for recycling. It also has drainage holes so it would make a nice planter. I really like the deep green color.Maybe it's just the one that I received, but the lid does not fit perfectly on the pot. When I push it in, it pops back up a little.

When we ordered this hose holder pot, we envisioned it sitting on our patio, storing small garden tools, and etc., and never intended to use it as a garden hose holder.  When it arrived, with lid, we were impressed by the beauty of it, and decided the pot was too nice to use outside.  The metal pot now commands a place in the livingroom, storing our cool-weather wraps and blankets, and it fits in well with the rest of our furnishings.  The shape of the bowl, the lattice design stamped in the metal, and the antiqued green finish are pleasing to the eye. I would describe the design as a cross between East Indian and Oriental...a very soothing look!

A hose holder is one of those things you just don't want to pay money for. Happily, thanks to Amazon Vine, I didn't have to. ;) I had previously had one of those plastic wind-up/hand crank reel ones, and found it to be a miserable experience every time I needed to use my hose. I was eager to try something new.I like that this item has a lid. That being said, it doesn't fit properly on the bowl. Manufacturing defect, I suppose. Also, it rusts, and quite quickly I might add. Unacceptable for an item of this cost. Like many others, I saw rust within the first two weeks.There is drainage in the bottom, but this will still hold water - a little anyway. However, the drainage holes are a welcome addition.The design is nice and goes well with my landscaping. It's actually an attractive piece to have sitting amongst my hostas, bushes and plants. It blends in very nicely with the greenery. It's sturdy, too, esp with the weight of the hose holding it in place.The big issue is that this item doesn't make using your hose any easier. This is especially true if you have a long hose (75 feet long or longer) or one of those heavy duty "no kink" kinds. It's a real struggle to "wind"/lay/coil your hose back into the bowl. My hose is medium duty and just doesn't respond well to be coiled into this holder; maybe that will change as the weather warms up. All that being said - this is no fault of the hose holder. It technically holds my medium-duty, no-kink 75 foot hose, but barely.For the price, this item isn't a good deal. This item should be priced around $35, tops. And, this doesn't make using your hose any easiest, just prettier, in terms of storage. ;) I think this item would make a better indoor plant holder or magazine holder instead.
summary: Sturdy, nice design, but not any easier to access & use your hose

reviewerName: Gertrude, the Innocent "Live well, laugh loud...
reviewText: This is a nice looking container that has made the circuit of my house and yard while I was trying to find the best use for it. I have to say that it is a lot more stable than I would have thought but not as heavy as it looks like it would be.It was a magazine holder but then I threw all the magazines away.A little girl hid in it in a raucous game of hide-and-seek.Then, it was briefly a container for legos.  It made the worst, loudest, container for legos on earth.  It's amazing how many noises legos can make.  The boys had contests to see how far they could throw legos and still land them.  They even had points associated with each distance.  YES, I am still stepping on legos even though I have vacuumed, swept, vacuumed, and swept.Then it had stuffed animals in it until one of the babies asked if we could cook them in it and make animal soup.The longest-lived use of this has been as a stick holder around the outdoor fireplace.Who knows where it will turn up next?Eventually, I'm going to put it in the yard with a hose in it but in the meantime it's just making its way around our house and yard.  My husband has the hose all coiled up on the back deck, ready to go in it.  He rolls his eyes every time I put it somewhere else.I'd like to point out that this does not come with the lid included.  The lid is a separate purchase.6/24/2012 Update:  We did finally try using it for the hose.  It was not a very useful hose holder.  It takes too long to wind it up and put it away.So now I just have a giant bowl with a hole in the side of it.

reviewerName: Jason P. Pumphrey "the movie & music man"
reviewText: I like this hose holder, it's nice and sturdy and keep the garden hose nice and tidy, and it looks neat too.A lid is available for this product, but that must be bought seperately.
summary: keeps that garden hose nice and tidy!

reviewText: While a hose holder might not seem like an exciting item, those that have struggled with infuriating, expensive hose reels or have made do with the unsightly appearance of a hose that never sits in the right place will appreciate the ease of use and attractiveness of this product.As an old married couple that has fought about hoses for years, it never seems like we have a decent solution. We've tried super expensive hose reels that were heavy, cumbersome and broke down after a year. So the spouse then decided to try the super cheap version of a hose reel with the rationale that they are more or less disposable so why spend more...it was a nice thought but within a week it became abundantly clear why they must cost so much because the cheap ones are just like taking money out of your pocket and setting it on fire...with the added privilege of having to struggle with it in the interim. In short, horrid.We then tried those cute little stakes...that was my bad idea. Perhaps they work if you have a 10 foot light duty hose but we don't. Ours are all 75 or 100 feet and big heavy duty hoses. The stake just falls over, gets tangled and eventually gets tossed away or used as a tomato stake.So, we've been comprosiming and just wraping the hose into a little pile and then hanging the handle on the water bib because I detest a muddle hose handle. Actually, I just quite using the hose because if it's not the hose handle, the entire hose is a big dirty mess after wrapping it under the hose bib. You can imagine my delight when this came up for review!First, it's attractive. I can now place the hose anywhere desired without concern over appearances...in fact, this is downright appealing and really looks great with the big vase shaped water barrels etc...Next, it's functional. There are drainage holes and an access point plus these nifty rolling guides (GREAT TOUCH) to help assure the hose goes where its meant to go. Water drains easily so no worry over mosquitoes etc, easy to clean, very attractive. I might have liked a hole in the lid so I could use the hose without removing the lid at times but it would also reduce versatility for other uses.Finally, this appears solid and durable. The coating is thick and seems like it will withstand the test of time. Substantial but not so heavy as to be difficult to move yet not so light as to feel flimsy.Overall, a wonderful addition to the garden, patio or outdoor living space. Very pleased!

Once again, Amazon shipped fast, arrived on time, item undamaged. This CobraCo steel hose holder is perfect for someone looking to take your unsightly looking green hose attached to the side of your house or lying on the ground, and make it look nice and unseen. I placed it on my patio for my garden hose and it looks and works great. The only issue I have is the hole in the bottom. If you dont place your hose through the hole, this could become a welcome hangout for field mice or a garden snake, both of which frequent my back yard. Just a heads up on that.

This looks really classy on my patio.  It seems like it is practically unbreakable - I imagine you'd have to run over it with a truck or bobcat to mess it up.  It's nice and solid, won't rust, well balanced.The lid fits nicely and helps hide my ugly hose.  The hose coils inside and comes in and out the two holds on the bottom/side.  When using a non-kink hose, it allows me to pull out just what I need easily.We tried it at first with a cheap hose we have and that didn't work - the hose kinked and the water wouldn't flow - but that was more a problem with the hose, but that's why I do recommend using a non-kinking hose with this.  We have hoses going in 3 different directions and this keeps the one on the patio nice and neat and out of view.It could be used as a planter, but it's too nice a hose holder for that!  It's pretty enough to use for one though.The petina is very nice - it has a hint of green like weathered copper.  It's very natural, and while pretty, doesn't jump out of the background at you.

Ok this is a very neat looking containerbut honestly it is not too practical for storing your yard hoseours is not very long a 50 footer i thinkand it does not wind around the middle column in the pot too wellsome of it ends up sticking up out of the top making the lid pointlessas far as making this a planter..might work ok if you find a pot large enough to put inside this potyou would not want to plant anything directly into this potit has a large hole on the side for the hose to hook to your outdoor spoutso far we have not yet found a pot to put inside to make this a planterBUT we did manage to find a smaller one and then placed a piece of wood in the bottomand set the plant on the topi have had this outside on the porch since the day it arrivedit has gotten wet though not soaked and has not rusted or shown any signs of wearit seems like stamped tin and not a very strong metalwhich is another reason i would never plant directly into it for fear of too much weight from the soilthe bottom of mine kind of pops out and i can bend it back againfor the price honestly i would not bother for a hose holderi really really wanted to like this for the original intention is was made forthe idea is great but it just does not work out for us
summary: Looks nice enough but not too functional

reviewText: This Cobra Co HLatice steel hose holder is a very nice green metal, though the metal is thin, I also have the cover and it does a nice job of hiding your hose, though I used mine for a long extension cord going outside and it is perfect.  I am not sure how it will be in the rain, it seems to me that water will still get in, but this does a great job of hiding your cords or hoses and making your yard look a bit neater.  I would recommend this product to anyone in a neighborhood or anyone who gardens or just has a hose across their yard! Very easy way to organize and be neat.  The cover does not come with this hose holder but you can order it if you are so inclined as an accessory.

With the lid on this pot, I keep thinking it looks like a Snake Charmer's pot.  I like it - the design is simple and nice, and the color looks good.I was surprised how lightweight it is.  It is said to be steel, obviously with a coating of some sort.  Mine did come with one small scratch, which didn't break the coating.  I suspect it is a little bit like the coating on an enamel coated cast iron cooking pot - it'll be fairly durable and protect from rust until you drop it against something hard, and then it'll just get worse and worse, but certainly more durable than a ceramic pot.  With some care, it should be fine.  I will let you know if it ever does have a problem with the elements - I am good about updating my reviews.The hole can be easily covered up with a small piece of tarp if you want to use this as a planter.  I would put it where the hole can be hidden.  The inner pillar is held on by three decorative coated nuts on three screws, and can be removed easily.  The base sits on three indents, allowing for drainage and to keep the screws from touching the surface.For hose housing it's not bad.  I'd rather have one of those really expensive automatic winders, but they don't look good.  And the manual winders are cheap, but they don't work well and don't look good, either.  If your hose is in a congested area, like mine, you have to carry most of it to where it is stored anyway, so a pot like this is just as efficient as a manual winder.My lid fits well.  If you push down on it at any area on the rim, it may move 1-2mm, but it looks and feels correct.I wouldn't personally use this for a magazine holder, but having a few uses is nice in case you get sick of it one way or just want to change things up.  I just think it's a good looking pot, and it's interesting to be made of steel.  I expect it to hold up nicely.

This is a very beautiful product, and it did include the lid. Made in India, it has a lovely patina finish. I don't know whether I'll use it as a hose holder or not, but it definitely has a place in my home.

I used to have my water hose attached to the wall in the garage which is effective but unsightly.  This hose holder is a quite beautiful green which should go with any garden setting perfectly.  It is quite easy to put in my hose as there is something in the center (which is actually removable if you would like to use this as something else) to wrap the hose around and there is a small opening in the back to attach the hose to a water source.  And as elegant as it looks, the container is surprisingly lightweight (the steel is quite thin) and easy to move around which is nice since I only have one hose that I use for the front and back yards.

I was able to obtain this item for review through the Amazon Vine program.  I have a garden hose that must reside rather near my front door, and had been looking for a hose holder that was nice looking, and did not weigh a ton.  I thought that this item fit the bill nicely.Pros:The hose holder is nice looking, having an embossed pattern in the metal, and being colored an attractive verdigris green.It is lightweight, and therefore easily moved.It can indeed hold at least a 100-foot 5/8 hose(see photo).The central post can be removed in order to use it for something other than a hose holder.I did not have to order the lid separately, as it came with the lid.Cons:The lid showed rust in just two days, simply from sitting outside overnight in cool damp weather. It was not exposed to sprinklers or rain within that time span.  The fact that it started to rust that fast causes me some concern over its long-term durability.Looks like I will have to clean off the rust and coat it with polyurethane or other similar clear coating in order to have it remain good-looking for any length of time, and to avoid rust stains on my concrete.Disappointed.  The listed price at this time is $94.58. For that much money I would expect better quality.  If I had paid for this item, I would be sending it back.
summary: Started to rust in two days

reviewText: The CobraCo HHLATICE-AG steel hose holder has plenty of room for straight or coiled hoses.  You can leave a large spray nozzle on the hose, and have it all fit neatly inside.The product itself is a little thin, but still heavy enough to stay in place.  The color is a little more green than shown in some pictures, and maybe a little less expensive looking.Overall, it still looks good, has plenty of room, and keeps our back yard looking much tidier than before.
summary: Plenty of room inside and keeps backyard looking tidy

reviewText: This CobraCo hose holder would make a nice Mother's Day present for a hard to shop for mom.  It's pretty, it's practical and it's unusual.  Chances are slight she already has one, or one of your siblings will get her the same thing.  It is made to store a garden hose, and it would work with a shorter lightweight hose, including a curly hose likePlastair SpringHose PUWE650B94H-AMZ 50-Foot 3/8-Inch Coil Garden Hose - Green.  I somehow doubt it is big enough for a really long heavyweight hose, however.  That is why I haven't tried it yet for hose storage.  I'm debating if I should or not. I really don't think it was made for that type of hose.This container is made of lattice steel, and I'm also not sure if that would start to rust quickly.  It does have drainage holes in the bottom.  If it's not prone to rusting, you could also use it as a container for canned or bottled beverages for a cookout.  Just keep filling it with ice.  There are actually lots of other things you can do with it, besides hose storage.  You can easily unscrew the center piece, and then use the container to hold a large potted plant, or a small potted tree--both real or artificial, both inside or outside of the house.  You can use it to store things on your patio, such as small garden equipment and garden gloves.  It comes with a pretty matching lid, but the lid does not fit on tightly.  Thus, you might hear it being knocked off at night by a raccoon, hoping the container is a small green trash can.  Inside in a sunroom, away from the raccoons, it could be used to store bird seed, suet and other bird feeding supplies. There are really lots of things this hose holder could be used for, if you don't want to use it for hose storage.  Who knows what ideas your mother might come up with when she sees it.
summary: For The Mother Who Has Everything . . . .

reviewText: Every spring I look for that mythical hose minder that actually works.  I've bought the light weight (hold it down with your foot) windup reels.  I've used the awful `attaches to the side of the house after you coil it up' types.  And even the upscale `bench' models with the storage compartment in the seat.As the weather gets hotter and my fortitude lags, I usually end up throwing the hose somewhere behind a bush near the faucet, and heading for the cool house.So it was with great interest that I ordered the CobraCo Lattice Steel Hose Holder.  It's a large, metallic green lidded jar that is, in theory, large enough to hold 125 feet of a 5/8 inch round garden hose.  And it does hold our smallest hose - but just barely.There are small drain holes in the bottom and a hole on the side for attaching the hose to the faucet.  The lid sits rather precariously atop the jar, but without it, even with the drain holes there might well be enough residual water for mosquitoes to breed.It's not especially easy to use, but it does effectively hide the hose in the kind of jar that I'd always imagined Aladdin's genie uncoiling from.The jar is lightweight, although metal, and can be used as a planter or storage container when the central column is removed.  That's all a matter of personal preference.  And I'm thinking that once I start tossing that hose behind the bushes again, we're looking at a new planter here.As a decorative place to hide the hose, this works.As an easy place to store the hose, it does not.At the price that is currently being asked, I can't see that this is a good buy.I'm updating my review in early May to add that so far the finish is holding up quite well, and to admit that although the price being currently asked may seem high to me, it is on a par with others I've seen.We have it on the street side of the house and it does look far better than the hose 'hidden' behind the bushes.
summary: It holds the hose; getting the hose in the jar is your job....

reviewText: This is a nice, roomy hose holder with an attractive verdigris-like finish.  It's a good, basic design, and holds a lot of hose, has drainage, and a lid which -- in the case of the holder I received, at least -- fits snugly.  I noticed that one review speaks about rust, and I can honestly say I have noticed nothing of the sort, though I'm not suggesting it isn't possible.The only thing I'd quibble about is the price.  $95 is a lot of money for something like this.  Yes it looks very nice in the garden and does the job, but I really think it's over-priced.  YMMV.

Made from painted steel, I'm not sure how long this will look decent when exposed to rain/snow after a couple years.  The center piece can be removed (3 bolts) if using as a container to store your fireplace wood or magazines. You couldn't use this for a plant unless you have a plant in another pot and set it inside this one (because of the hole for a garden hose).I have a 50' garden hose in mine with extra room to spare; but I doubt it will hold a 125' long hose as stated in the description. You know how garden hose gets kinked up after it's used a few times and it becomes harder to get it to coil back?  I think by mid-summer this 50 foot hose will be hard enough to get it all back in so I can put the lid on, let alone trying to stuff a kinky 125 foot hose inside.Speaking of the optional lid:  My main problem with this is the lid (an additional $28 purchase as of this date) - doesn't fit right.  I'm not sure if the hose holder or the lid itself is "out of round" but it won't fit completely inside the rim of the hose holder. Who knows....maybe mine is defective or they are all made like this (imperfect). Picture a pot with a lid you have cooking on the range to let the steam out and that's the same way the lid fits.Made in India.
summary: Better suited as a log holder or for magazine storage

reviewText: I have been in search of a good hose management solution since I bought my house.  I've tried several brands of rolling carts, and they all end up leaking or breaking.  So we ended up with just a balled up hose in the garage.  This holder has solved the problem!  While it's not as convenient as a wheeled cart, it is much nicer looking and smaller.  Rolling the hose up does take a couple of minutes, but that's a small price to pay for the a nice tidy package.  The color is pretty accurate as shown, the cap is very handy too, keeps most of the bugs out.  It appears to be sturdy and well built, I would imagine it will last many years.

I have been searching for a hose holder for my deck to keep our garden hose protected from the heat and sun and from my teens driving their vehicle over the hose.  Local stores only carry the plastic hose holders that don't weather well in the hot southern temperatures or the exterior wall mounted or wheeled hose reels that offer little to no protection from the elements.TheCobraCo Beehive Steel Hose Holder with Copper Finish HHBEESTL-ACalong with the matchingCobraCo LIDBEESTL-AC Beehive Steel Hose Holder Lid(sold separately) offers both protection from the elements and is beautiful sitting on our deck.  It is so pretty that I almost decided to use inside, as suggested by the manufacture, to store miscellaneous items but I really needed a hose holder.The inside bottom of theCobraCo Beehive Steel Hose Holder with Copper Finish HHBEESTL-AChas drain holes to keep water from standing if you don't have or need the cover but if you want to fully protect your hose you will need to purchase theCobraCo LIDBEESTL-AC Beehive Steel Hose Holder Lid.  It adds extra height to the beehive but is really needed to cover and keep water, dust & dirt out of the holder. I'm just not sure why the manufacture didn't offer this as a set instead of selling in pieces.

I am very happy with this hose holder. The lid was a pleasant surprise. I do not have to worry about emptying the holder when it rains. Secondly, I was impressed with the weight and diameter of the holder. It does not tip over easy and is very sturdy. It holds a 20' hose with no issues with the hose becoming tangled with the cone center. The copper color is nice without drawing too much attention to itself.
summary: Nice Yard Piece. No more seeing ugly green hose.

reviewText: This hose holder looks so much better than the old washtub I was using to store my hose, and I've already gotten compliments. I also have the lid to keep the rain and debris out. I have several concerns though, a couple which I hope may turn out to be unfounded.  First of all, it seems very light and thin and I wonder if it may dent easily.  Secondly, I wonder how long the finish will last.  It appears to be painted with a copper finish and then sealed.  The last thing is not technically a concern, but an aggravation.  While I like the look of the design, the top is narrow and it's a bit tedious to feed the hose back in. I'll update if I have any problems with durability.Update:  After a year of use, the finish is shot.  Lot of rust and some holes forming.

This is an extremely nice hose house!  I have a 75' hose in it in my back yard and it looks very presentable - much better than curling my hose on the ground!  The lid makes it a true keeper because it completely hides the hose and stops dirt/moisture from getting inside.  Very solid piece; and has a hole in the back for the hose leader from your spigot.

This is an attractive and sturdy hose holder that I am now using in my front flower/shrub bed to replace a resin (plastic) fake half barrel that had one too many days in the sun.  I have the matching lid to keep out rain and debris, and the 'beehive' easily holds the 60' garden hose that I have wound up in there.  The construction is steel with an antique copper finish and what appears to be a glossy lacquer to help protect it.  The color is almost a bronze, but not quite as brown.I like having the matching lid (sold separately) because the sun in this area gets intense enough that it ages rubber and vinyl hoses and makes them brittle. Plus leaves kept blowing into my last hose holder and eventually plugged the drain holes in the bottom.  Depending on where you plan on putting the hose holder, you may not want or use the lid.  As you can see by the pictures, the product looks good without it, and it is tall enough that you have to be standing almost on top of it to see what is inside.  The center pole helps to wind and unwind the hose in and out of the holder without kinking or tangling, but is removable in case you want to use the container for other purposes or want to try to fit more hose inside.  My only concern with this is the steel construction under the copper finish lasting before the elements take their toll and rust starts to show itself. However, I'm hopeful that the gloss finish and thickness of the steel itself will keep this from being a problem for some time.**Update:  6 months in and the lid is covered in rust.  The base is still in great shape, but I'm not so optimistic as I was now that I see that the lid didn't even last a summer, with the first rust showing after about three months. Down to three stars.
summary: CobraCo HHBEESTL-AC Beehive Steel Hose Holder

reviewText: I adore the CobraCo Beehive Steel Hose Holder!  For years I've considered getting a hose holder to hide the ugly hose in my front yard, but I never could find one I liked.  The CobraCo Beehive Steel Hose Holder has everything I wanted and more.  I really like the lovely copper patina and unique design of the CobraCo Beehive Steel Hose Holder, it fits in well with my garden and landscape style.  The sturdy steel construction is surprisingly light weight and easy to move around the yard (empty, that is, the weight of the hose makes it heavy).  The holder comes with a cute lid (not shown in the picture) that really completes the look of this hose holder.Winding the hose inside the pot is made easy by the installed center post - which is removable if you'd rather use your hose holder for an ornamental container instead of using it to hide an ugly hose.  The wide base and narrower top make winding the hose inside a cinch. And when you're done, just pop the lid on the pot and you have a lovely decorative accent for your landscape instead of an unsightly hose lying around.

It's a nice little container that's stylish and includes a little lid not pictured. It holds a standard garden hose nicely. But there's no mechanism for cranking up the hose, you just have to coil the hose in around the spindle, but the ribbing of the sides holds the hose nicely, and hose dispenses out the top easily.

A coiled up water hose may be expected in the garden, but on your patio it can be a mess or even an accident waiting to happen. This hose holder is perfect for when you need your hose near, but want it out of sight. Run one end thru the hole on the bottom and coil the rest inside. And the best part is the beehive design makes it very easy to coil it back inside.And this hose holder isn't limited to just hoses, the center piece can be removed and it can be use to hold other items; blankets, recyclables or toys. It also can be used as a decorative pot for you larger house plants. Not that there is a matching lid, but it is sold separately.Overall this is a very durable, solid steel storage box with an excellent copper finish.

The CobraCo Beehive hose holder combines a rustic style with a clean modern finish, giving a look that would work well both in a living room and among flower pots.  For outdoor use with a hose, it is plenty big and includes good drainage.  I found the metal a bit thin, and that resulted in it arriving with one side of the base already bent.  However, thick metal with something this big would make it too heavy to easily move around, and with moderate use it should last many years.  I do fear that the steel will begin rusting, and I will update this review if that happens.For indoor use, as the pictures suggest, the central beam can be removed with a screwdriver, leaving the large inner area for storage.  The rustic/modern combo would fit well with both a country look and a more commercial space, such as an office lobby.  It may clash with more minimal or trendy decor.Overall, the Beehive hose holder is a great product indoors and out.  I am struggling to decide which place to keep it long-term.  I want it inside, but then I'll need another way to store my hose!

This is such a nice hose holder that we realized we can't put it in our driveway like we'd intended because junkies would probably steal it to sell it to metal scrappers. We didn't realize how lovely it would be in person. Instead, we put it in our fenced back yard and it looks gorgeous there.The copper looks just great in a garden area, the copper with the greens in nature are stunning. My son loves using it as a seat too, it's just the right size for a little kid to sit on it when the lid is on.This is a well made product and I'd recommend it to anyone looking for a snazzy hose holder.

The manufacturer states “Just a sprinkle of Preen stops weeds before they start, and now, with Preen's new battery-powered spreader cap, weed prevention is faster, more precise and easier than ever. The Preen Battery-Powered Spreader provides better coverage with less fatigue, and customers love it because it's easy to use. Just flip open the cap, turn it on, tilt the container down and move it evenly around the target area. The AAA batteries (included) do the rest, delivering just the right amount of Preen to large or small areas”.  The package contains, a pamphlet detailing precautions, hazards, first aid, directions for using Preen Garden Weed Killer, plus an extensive listing of the annual weeds controlled, use around the types of established plants, in addition to how and when to apply.  No questions that we can see have not been answered.  Just remove the battery strip, turn the power switch on, adjust the angle of the container, apply in an even back and forth motion - thats it.  We used the Preen Garden weed killer following the detailed instructions without incident - recommended.Following are some facts provided by Preen:Can Preen Garden Weed Preventer stain? Yes; Preen Garden Weed Preventer can stain porous surfaces such as concrete, rocks, bricks, landscape blocks, shoes, leather and linoleum.When can people and pets enter an area that was treated with Preen Garden Weed Preventer? They may enter the treated area after it is thoroughly dry from the first rain and/or watering.Can Preen Garden Weed Preventer be applied on top of mulch? Yes. After removing existing weeds and weed roots, rake the mulch to loosen it, and ensure the mulch is 2 – 3 ″ thick. Then, apply Preen Garden Weed Preventer and water thoroughly.Can Preen Garden Weed Preventer be applied around corn? Strawberries? No; Preen Garden Weed Preventer is not labeled for use on corn or strawberries.Can I use Preen Garden Weed Preventer on my lawn or with grass seed or sod? No; turf injury could result. Preen Garden Weed Preventer is not labeled for use on lawns.Can I use Preen Garden Weed Preventer in or near a pond, lake, or other type of waterway? No; Preen Garden Weed Preventer is harmful to aquatic life.Can I use Preen Garden Weed Preventer around, under, or near a swimming pool, sandbox, playground type areas, or under bird feeders? No.
summary: An excellent garden weed killer distribution container

reviewText: I love Preen - use it on my terrace between the cracks and don't have to weed all summer.  This applicator would not be ideal for that purpose as you have to direct it very precisely and this applicator spreads it broadly.  It worked well on my bocce court however but I still had to shake it a bit if I wanted it to come out faster - using just the battery power provided rather sparse coverage.  It was useful and easy to use but I'm not sure if the Power spreader aspect adds that much over just shaking it out by hand, which is why I only gave it four stars..
summary: Preen is great, applicator works fine

reviewText: Preen is a solid way to keep weeds from popping up around flower beds and shrubs. I also use it on my side yard which is mostly mulch. When you get the consistency right it typically works for a full season.So why 3-Stars? I find that when using this "Power" spreader, I lose the control and precision needed to balance coverage and accuracy. The other big issue is you can get 16-pound pail of Preen Weed Preventer for nearly the same price.I would not recommend this combo.
summary: Save your money and spread by hand.

reviewerName: david l. poremba "the past in review"
reviewText: We have used this product for a number of years with great success. The power spreader makes it even easier to use. The spread is much more even and a bit broader for the larger areas. A great product!

you should try this!  I have used pre-emergent for quite some time and always have just grabbed a fist full and spread around my yard with sometimes iffy results.  Go back later and use weed killer in the spots that i missed.  No doubt Preen is a great product and  works very well.  What makes this product a real killer is the built in spreader, It puts down just the right amount and is hassle free!  I know most folks that use this type product use a separate spreader,  while I, do it by hand----me cheap!  After a session using this product and seeing how well it works, well, I'm sold!There is plenty to do a large lot area in a rather short amount of time----when done the weed problem can be kissed good-by.The only problem I encountered was the first time I used this was the plastic strip that is pulled to allow the batteries to make contact, dislodged one of the AAA's-----couldn't get it going until I figured out what went wrong.  Snapped the batteries out, put them back in and I was in business.  The on-off switch is easy as is the whole design of this product-----it deserves all five stars for, innovation, quality of product, and ease of use.

I’ve used Preen products as a fertilizer/weed preventer in my flower gardens for a long time – for initial planting and later in the spring.When planting I mix Preen with the soil before dropping in the plants so it can work at the level of the roots and then sprinkle some along the top of the soil after planting is complete. I still end up weeding but like to think that I spend less time weeding than if I had not applied Preen.The new Preen for 2014 comes with a very nice feature – a battery-powered spread to give a more even, balanced coverage with less strain on the back. All you have to do is flip the cap to the open position, tilt the container down toward the bed and move it evenly across the soil. This really makes it easier to apply makes me love my Preen even more!Preen is formulized to kill 200-plus weeds and is supposed to kill weeds for up to three months. That might be so but I still reapply once a month just to be sure. You can refill the container when it empties by purchasing a 5-, 10- or 30-pound bag and keep using the battered operated spreader. And the batteries are replaceable.Lebanon Seaboard Corporation, which produces Preen, also makes fertilizer, grass seed, turf products, and wild bird seed. Formed in 1947 the company is based in Lebanon, PA.
summary: Preen Improves Usefulness With Battery Operated Spreader

reviewText: I have used preen for years and loved it,but I was never quite sure I was getting the right amount put on. I did'nt want to go overboard with it but sometimes I did. Now it is so easy!  Just install the batteries and go. Now I am not worried about the right amount because the spreader does it for me. It is so awesome get it and try it you will love it!!!

As in any killing product, read the label. In this case a booklet.The ingredients of this product are what is used commonly in residential use gardening. Preen is a known brand, reliable, if used as directed. SMALL garden product. Large truck farm gardeners may want to look at bagged product, using your own applicator, to save $$.A picture in the accompanying booklet of directions and information shows the light amount of granules needed to curb weeds, as compared to a quarter. That is the advantage of the battery powered applicator lid. It sounds crazy, but works. A more uniform distribution with not too much, not too little product. It is worth the extra cost to get the container with this lid for one buy. Then less expensive packaging can be purchased for refills. For me, I likely save the difference by not overly broadcasting the weed presenter granules.My flower beds are a mix of some old-garden standards like lamb's ear, flags, hollyhock, bee balm, wild geranium, Shasta, yarrow, etc which are all included in the list of treatable.
