Same with the list for Shrubs and Veggies. One important note; most veggie beds need treated prior to seed or plants. A few need application after, so read, read, read.I expect I'll be spending more time enjoying my gardens rather than weeding them.THIS IS A GARDEN ITEM--NOT FOR LAWNS.
summary: Good for the garden--but read the fine print

reviewText: I've been using Preen for years, we buy it in the big giant buckets as we have lots of trees at the back of our lot and weeds seem to love growing under them. As a weed preventer (assuming you get it down early enough in the season, and reply as needed) it works fantastically... yes you'll still get some weeds but the difference in the years I've used this vs the couple I didn't was huge. I hate weeding, so using Preen is a no brainer.I wasn't so sure about this container with the power spreader cap, and figured it was a bit of a gimac.... but gave it a shot anyways. I'm very pleasantly surprised. Normally I use a scoop to put Preen into one of those scotts handheld/crank spreaders and it's messy and yes, I often skip the spreader and just try to shake it from the scoop directly (which never goes very well). This container actually did distribute the Preen evenly and easily and since it's refillable (and holds enough product that you can do a good size area w/o having to refill it) I see myself using this every single time I need to reply now as well. I'll continue buying the large value sized containers, but will keep using this one instead of the crank spreader to put it out!
summary: I love Preen and was surprised at how well the electric spreader cap worked!

reviewText: I have been a big believer in Preen for more than 10 years.  My usual method is to put Preen down in all of my beds, directly on the dirt if possible, then cover with mulch, pine straw, etc.  This has served me very well.  I do not have to pull many weeds at all.  Once in awhile near the end of the growing season some weeds will start to show up.  I just pull the weeds and then spot treat the area, and the problem is solved.I tried this product specifically to see how the power spreader cap works.  I have never minded shaking the preen bottle back and forth, so how much better could this be?  Well, it prevents you from having to shake the bottle back and forth, and does a MUCH better job at spreading the Preen around evenly.  I am anxious see if I potentially left fewer spots bare, and consequently have fewer weed breakthroughs later in the season.Anyway, this is a great product that I highly recommend.

I have an almost 100% organic garden and yard and overall I don't have that big an issue with weeds (I use a lot of black plastic mulch in my veggies, for example--you'll never see weeds again), but I have a few areas, like my patio, where they are just out of control. I despise the thought of adding any weed-killing chemicals to my yard for many reasons (I eat a lot of what comes out of my yard, I have a lot of wildlife that has a hard enough time surviving, I worry about harm to pollinators, etc.). But again, for a few areas, I thought this might be a potentially good idea and actually Preen came highly recommended by a local landscaper. After reading the label and precautions, however, I decided to ONLY use it far away from any area where food is grown or where pets might roam (I would not want my pets licking this off their paws sorry).The primary place that I wanted to use the Preen was on my patio which is made of pavers (like 8 x 12"); the weeds grow like wildfire in the cracks between the pavers and it make me nuts. Since no other plants grow there I thought it might be safe to use. The trouble in using a powdered form of Preen, I found, is that the stuff just bounces off of the pavers and there' no way to make sure it goes in the crack. So, that's no fault of the product or spreader, but that experiment was a failure.I did find a few border areas that are largely gravel (weeds seem to love gravel beds) where I tried spreader and it worked (as far as distribution) fine. But since it's still early spring here in New England, I have no idea whether or not this stuff will prevent any weeds. I tried to use it *very* sparingly because, as I said, I have no desire to bomb the yard with any chemicals. The thing is, the power spreader actually does work and you can go through a $25 jug of this stuff PDQ (which is the source of my headline above). What a clever idea: add a battery-powered spreader to make sure that you're blowing through the stuff quickly! Give that guy a raise.Overall, while I can see the convenience value of this to someone who doesn't mind using a weed killer in garden beds and who has no pets, but for me, I felt guilty using it. I think I'll go back to yanking the weeds (or using vinegar to kill them). I don't like the idea of hurting wildlife, I think many weeds are good for the pollinators whose populations are declining, I don't want poison in my yard and this stuff is way too expensive. I would never buy this product, sorry. Please, before you buy it, read the labels and the warnings. If you have a gravel parking area or some other non-natural place where weeds are an issue, perhaps this is a safe product. But in the garden? I don't think so.
summary: I hope they gave a bonus to the person that invented the spreader

reviewText: This will not kill existing weeds or stop weeds that have already taken root, but can help them from spreading via seed (so put it down early, before seeds take hold!). I scatter it in my rock driveway and flower beds and it definitely does make a difference.I'm not sure how much the spreader helps....you still end up sort of shaking/moving the container around to spread the stuff, but I guess it does help disperse it a little more easily - get the power spreader if you can and it's not much more expensive, but it's not as much easier to spread as a hand sprayer would be vs a power sprayer. Definitely love Preen, though!

I have used Preen in my flower beds for a long time and it prevents most of the weeds if you apply before the weeds come out.  It does not kill grass.  The difference in this container of Preen is the power spreader cap.  It does make it easier to give an even spread of the product.  There is not that big a price difference between this power cap Preen and the regular cap Preen and you can buy a bag of Preen that will refill this Preen.  All in all it is worth the price difference to get the Power Spreader Cap.
summary: A New Way to Spread Preen

reviewText: This product is exactly what it says - Weed "Preventer".  If you wait until you have weeds, it will do nothing.  You must put it down before you have any sign of weeds and then reapply about ever 6 weeks or anytime you disturb the soil, like when planting something new or if you rake the soil.  I know the bottle says it will last longer but I'm giving you our real world experience.  My wife and I have used this product for about 9 years now in our flower gardens and it works very well if you apply it before weeds appear and reapply anytime the soil is disturbed.  It creates a barrier that prevents weed seed from germinating.  It is not 100% perfect but it does work very well.There is one weed we get sometimes that Preen does not seem effective against.  I'm not sure what the weed is called but it grows like a vine across the ground.  We get it in our grass sometimes and it will grow across into the garden and the Preen doesn't stop it.  I think that is because it is already a mature weed that is spreading across the ground but for everything else, it has been effective for us.UPDATE:The new packaging includes a motorized spreader built into the nozzle.  It is powered by 2 AAA batteries (included).  It works like a miniature broadcast spreader.  So rather than shaking the product as in the past, you just flip the power switch to on and tilt the container and the product sprays out.  It works very well and makes spreading the product much faster and easier.
summary: Work great providing you put it down BEFORE you have weeds.

reviewText: April 23, 2014 Update:Thank you Deb Balcerlak-Wilson for bringing my error to my attention.  Please excuse me while I wipe the ton of egg off my face for committing a serious error in this review.  I wrote my review for another product completely and not for Preen as received.  The product I used is similar to Preen, but it is for removing weeds in the lawn as well as other places.  Unlike Preen, which works in gardens only and is printed on the outside in a readable red font For use in Garden Only, I just simply used the granular weed killer.  It did not work at all and Preen has not worked yet.  And until the sun wakes up the gardens and the veggies begin to grow, it would be remiss to even consider a worthy review for Preen.  I did, however, use the Preen granules on the garden and other non-lawn areas and look forward to NOT seeing any weeds in those areas.  I am sorry for that senior moment, but the past 6 weeks have been fraught with many suburban terrorists who have made their way into many normal structures of normal lives.As soon as this product arrived, I read the instructions and followed them while carefully placing each grain with what turns out to be a super spreader container.  I made it a point to avoid any areas in the yard that might be populated by our dogs and other neighborhood pets.  No other animals were harmed by the application of Preen's so far as I can tell.Therein lies the rub.  I chose not to give this product a 1 star because I do not know if it will work in a few weeks or not.  I put it on the  lawn after a very cold winter.  To be a fair as I can, I mixed a container of weed-only liquid killer and applied that mixture to one side of my lawn.  The following is not an exaggeration.  The grass is brilliant emerald and right now it is about 5 inches tall thanks to my not being smart enough to fix my mower.  There are zero weeds of any type.  That part of the yard is either green from the fescue or brown from the Bermuda.  On the right side of the lawn, I used the entire container of Preen's and waited for action.  Mine was the classical story of attempting to watch weeds die and grass grow except, in this case, it was watching the weeds and grass grow; NOT one weed died.  The earlier mentioned liquid weed killer wilted the weeds in 2 days and in a week the weeds joined the elements.  I also applied Preen's in different rates in similar weed areas so that in case of one weed being stronger than another I would stand a better chance of success.  What a waste, so far.If by any chance the weeds on the right side of my lawn should die, I will revise this review accordingly; however, if the product does not do any better I will return for a reduction in the rating and additional words.  Shoot, this is the most beautiful time of the year in this Valley and even the weeds add to that beauty.
summary: Still Waiting for Results, Any RESULTS

reviewText: I'm not totally into organics, but I do try to avoid pesticides as much as possible. And I try not to use chemicals where I don't have to. That being said, my feeble attempts at gardening have grown more weeds than produce, so I was quite excited about the possibilities this product posed for my lawn and garden.Unfortunately, the warnings on this product are a bit off-putting. You are cautioned to avoid contact with skin as well as to wear protective eye covering when dispersing this product. If that's the case, I don't think I want it near my food, much less my children. So, we were very careful about where we placed it--on the patio between pavers, and in landscaped areas where the children don't play. Even had it not been for the children, this weed preventer is not supposed to be used on grass, which wasn't clear when we ordered it. Likewise, it does not eliminate existing weeds, just prevents new ones from growing. For me, that was the biggest issue with this product--to have as many warnings as it does, I'd expect it to kill the weeds that already exist.The power spreader cap was actually not something that we found useful. The cap flips open, and the "power" is in the flipped lid. Basically, the product is like pebbles that fall onto the cap and then are dispersed outward. You are supposed to control the flow by tilting the entire bottle up or down, just as you would if you didn't have the power cap. Perhaps it might be different when the bottle isn't near to full, but it's pretty difficult to control the output. And it's not easy to disperse to smaller areas. Effective or not, I can't see myself purchasing this product in the future.
summary: Says it's safe for the veggie garden, but not safe on your skin...

reviewText: We live where the cold persists into May and returns in September so for our brief growing season we really want our yard to look nice.  We have a persistent assault by dandelions every year.  Our yard is now nice and green but a certain percentage of it is due to dandelions and the like rather than grass.  That's where the Preen comes in.  The cap is battery powered and makes for an even distribution of the chemical over the affected area.  The bottle says it will cover 1000 sq ft and that seems right because it is a large bottle.  I'm looking forward to a dandelion-free lawn this summer.

There is NOTHING like Preen to stop a weed.  I have a very large garden, and have experimented with Preen by just doing a small patch and comparing to the areas where Preen was not used.  A HUGE difference, Preen really does stop the weeds....and now they have added a power spreader cap, LOVE IT!  Two AA batteries power the spreader cap, so now instead of having the shake your jug of Preen you now get a nice even spread.I will buy Preen over and over again, definitely worth your money.

I have used Preen Weed Preventer for many years and have always been happy with the product. While it doesn't stop every weed from sprouting it does significantly cut down their number. I use it along several flower borders and a few flower beds consisting of both annuals and perennials, and have not experienced any damage to my plants. I applied Preen a few weeks ago using this bottle and so far the weed count has been low - however the weather has been unusually cool this season so that could change.The addition of a battery powered spreader cap is a nice idea but for me one that works better in theory than actual use. I still had to shake the bottle at times and overall I didn't feel I had as much control. Half of my garden areas are borders and for those, manual application is more precise. For the larger garden beds, the power cap works fine.One other thing to note, with a six pound bottle it was a little weighty to hold until some of the Preen was used up. Also, the battery powered cap will fit on other bottles of Preen, so it can be saved to use again. I tried it on my organic Preen, which I use in the veggie garden, and it fit perfectly.
summary: Significantly cuts down on the number of emerging weeds

reviewText: Preen is great at stopping weeds from growing and this product makes it even easier to spread.  The batteries may have to be placed to make it work .
summary: Preen is great.  Batteries might have to be replaced

reviewText: This battery-operated distribution cap topping the familiar product works great.  The battery is included.  The only learning curve required is to hold the canister almost upside down, as the Preen sifts in a perfect amount on the garden surface. It is also extremely user-friendly for a person with hand/wrist issues. This is a wonderful addition to the cottage/patio/planter garden.
summary: Top-notch distribution of tried and true product

reviewText: This is so helpful, spread and it REALLY prevents weeds.  I have an area about 6 feet by 30 feet where I have planted blueberries and a few tomatoes and such - which has been a weed cultivator !  This year after it was weeded the Preen weed  per-venter went down...  I just checked it out AND I didn't see a weed!! Yea.  I would recommend this product - Jesus' Blessings and Peace
summary: Just checked my garden and no weeds!

reviewText: i do a lot of container gardening for my hobby and this product is what i use to stop cold the new formation of weeds. i always pick out any weeds out of my pots no matter how small or large they are to start with. i mix all of my soils and compost and then place them into the large pots that i use. i then sprinkle my weed preventer on top of the soil and allow the pot to sit until i am ready to use them. it works great. thanks.

I do find this product helps most if you use it in your bed prior to planting your plants.  It does distribute easy.  This product is to prevent weeds, it's not like a weed killer you spray on already mature weeds.  It needs to put sprinkled on a freshly made bed.  I used some in my flower garden, not in my vegetable garden.  As of now, it does seem to help keep the weeds down. Those little cocoa weeds (that's what I've been told they are called) are next to impossible to kill.  The have a hard root at the bottom and nothing seems to kill them.
summary: Easy distribution and helps keep weeds at bay

reviewText: It does kill weeds and stop new growth for about 2 weeks.  This is with the cooperation of Nature.  When heavy rain occurs, the active time is reduced.  Frankly, I prefer a blend of vinegar, water, and salt.  It lasts for about 3 months and is easy to apply.  If you have only a small area to treat, Lebanon Preen could be ideal for you.  It will need to be retreated on a biweekly basis, but has none of the smell of my vinegar concoction.

My beds in the front have mulch, but the weed and unwanted plant growth seem to keep popping up.  I'm tired of having my lawn person that he agreed to keep that bed clear, so I thought I'd give this a try.  I know it won't help with the stuff already growing, but I hope it will prevent more from showing up.  The cap made spreading it easy.  I'll report back to add if it reduced the problem of the volunteers.

Finally had the opportunity to use this as it's been a long Winter as I'm sure most know.First take off the lid and remove the seal on mouth.  Attach lid back to canister and flip top open and you'll see an on/off switch.  Switch to on and the spreader starts.  Tip towards ground and start to spread.I've used Preen before so I believe this will do it's job though I can't attest to that ability yet as I just put it down.  However - this does spread more evenly with the motorized spreader cap than if you were throwing it out by hand.  I would trust that it makes the item more economical too because it's an easy stream of product and only so much room for it to feed through.It's not as user friendly as I would have liked.  It's a bit heavy with a hefty handle to hold especially when you find yourself constantly shaking the bottle to keep the grains flowing from the sprout.  There is a small dial on top to use if you feel the top is clogged.  I don't believe it was clogged like that, I just think you have to shake quite often to keep the grains free-flowing.It still goes fast and now it's empty.  I'm going to get more Preen though and refill to use (at least until the batteries are dead.)Here's to controlling weeds this Spring!

I used this weed preventer in a place that already had weeds, to keep it from getting "weedier." It didn't kill any of the existing weeds, so I wonder if it will be as effective as weed killer is. I suppose time will tell and I can update when I know more.

I use Preen in my yard every spring. The power spreader cap is something I have been unable to try as of yet because we are still waiting for Spring to come in Minnesota. I have to go ahead and do the review before the time limit ends (as a Vine Member), but I will come back and update this review in a few weeks in regard to the Power Spreader Cap - as soon as I am able to use it.  However, I find Preen is an easy way to fertilize and keep the weeds down, though it needs to be repeated during the summer - I use it mostly for a Spring kick-start to my flower gardens.

I have used Preen for many years to prevent weeds from germinating.  The most remarkable thing about this Preen is the battery powered distributor.  The distributor now makes it easier to apply Preen evenly to garden areas.  The directions are so easy to follow and application is smooth and even.  This added touch to Preen makes it "so easy to use" and much better than using Preen without the battery.  This is a buy!!

Preen has been my go-to weed preventer for the past 2 or 3 summers. I have a large tomato garden and Preen helps to keep it virtually weed free. I simply spread the Preen on at the same time, or shortly after I plant my tomatoes, before the weeds have had a chance to germinate. Very few weeds can get through the Preen "iron wall."  I like the new battery-powered spreader cap. The product went on smoothly and evenly. I did not have any problem with battery life as other reviewers have had. I would recommend this product highly and I will use it again in the future.
summary: Easy to Use, Easy to Distribute

reviewText: I am a HUGE fan of Preen and have been using it exclusively for years. This battery-operated spreader is an interesting innovation.I recently applied the entire container to my garden, which consists mainly of perennials, foundation shrubs, ground cover & decorative trees. I liked the spread and distribution of the the integrated power cap. There were periodic gusts of wind, as there often are in the Spring, so sometimes the granules did not go where I intended. However, that is not my concern with this spreader. Rather, I found that sometimes the on-off spreader switch worked, sometimes it didn't. Sometimes the dial cleared the issue, sometimes it didn't. I was constantly checking the spreader, particularly as I had gotten about half-way through the container and the cap & spreader started getting coated in dust from the product.At this price point - and you will pay extra for the cap - it's really up to the consumer to decide whether it is worth the extra money. One option is to get a larger container of Preen, and fill this smaller container with product through the season. However, I probably won't do that, even though I have 3 large containers of Preen set aside for this season. The manual shake & dispense method suits me fine. The checking & rechecking the dispenser, coupled with the excessive dust that developed on the cap, just does not balance out the benefits for me.Regardless, I'll still be using Preen for a very long time.
summary: New spreader cap is good, not great. Is it worth the extra money?

reviewerName: Wendi Barker "Wendi's Book Corner & What Wend...
reviewText: Preen itself is great to help prevent new weeds from growing in my yard once I've weeded and added the Preen to the dirt.The difference with THIS Preen is in the cap - it is battery powered to help spread the Preen evenly and avoid dumping too much Preen in one spot and wasting it.  So far the battery has been a trooper and I haven't had any problems.  I plan to keep using it until it completely dies (I'll refill this bottle).Love the concept but it is not a "need", rather, it is nice to have and helpful.  Thank you Preen
summary: Easy Even Way to Spread Preen

reviewText: Part of our strategy to get rid of weeds was to get rid of the lawn. Last summer, we landscaped the front yard with plants and features, surrounded by weed-preventing sheeting and cedar bark chips. Of course, a few weeds always manage to pop up here and there. Enter Preen Garden Weed Preventer. This is perfect for our purpose. we can spread this product periodically in the areas among the plants, and it prevents new weeds. We try to avoid getting it on the plants we want, of course, but in general it seems pretty safe for most plants that have already become established. If dandelions, for instance, get a head start, I use a natural weed killer that seems to work fine. However, there's no way to keep the seeds from floating over the yard occasionally, since some of our neighbors seem to have dandelion farms.In any case, this product works for me. It seems to keep new weeds from becoming established and allow more time for other, more enjoyable summer activities.

I have been using this set of quick disconnects for a few months now with a garden host that is always on. I am using these along with several different watering wands/nozzles.Pros:-------------+ The seal is excellent, no leaks at all so far.+ Mostly aluminum parts.+ No issues with water flow.+ Price is fair compared to similar products.+ Made in USA.Cons:-------------- The plastic parts will not last forever.
These are high quality made in the usa quick disconnects. Good for the nozzle end at a lower price than brass. these last.
No leaks, but I just installed them. I was worried about not being brass, but so far these don't leak and work just fine. Good value.
I've had a few of these for about 6 months and they still work without leak. I'm happy with them. They also work well with the Dramm brass connectors.
I have a powerwasher and it came with a plastic disconnect, it did not do the job.  Therefore I had bought this and put it on and now I do not have any leaks.

I bought this to hold the soaker hose down near my newly planted Evergreens. They did and still doing a great job. I have no problems of them breaking or cracking and we have seen 95F - 8F temperatures within last year. I have it for almost 2 years and couldn't ask of anything better. Also, I never had any problems with them breaking down when hammering down.

I have been usingOrbit DripMaster 65731 1/2-Inch to 5/8-Inch Loop Stakesto hold down soaker hoses.  This year I decided to give these a try and like them better.  The seem to stay in better without having to be pressed as deep.  Also, the look doesn't press into the hose as much as the loops did.Price being roughly equal I'll be buying these in the future.
summary: I like these much better than the metal loops

reviewText: I use these all over the place for drip irrigation in pots.  I found that they are better than the staples I have been using, and I like the idea of them not rusting on me.  So far they have worked like a charm.  They are large, so they may not be a fit for smaller/crowded pots, but I have not had that problem.

After years of working with metal garden fabric fasteners,  I opted for these Fiskars 5" stakes instead. What a tremendous improvement. Unlike the metal anchors, these thermoplastic (ABS) stakes hold their own in maintaining garden fabric integrity. Measuring in at 5" L x 3/4" W, these stakes are built to last. Not only does this anchor work for my network of garden hoses, it also provides excellent support for edging boundaries. We've even used these stakes for anchoring volleyball net lines. Installation is cut and dry. The only tool I needed was a mallet. Picking up the 50 count pack vice the costlier 12 count unit is a no brainer.

I'm a big fiskars fan so when looking for additional garden stakes I didn't hesitate to purchase these since I got 50 of them at a great price.  They arrived quickly, thanks to my amazon prime, but they are about half as tall as the regular yard stakes I am used to.  I got a chance to use them to hold down some plankets during a couple of freezes and they worked very well, even better than the tall stakes I have since you don't have to push them down as far.  This was a great deal for the price!
summary: small garden stakes, great for holding down plankets and other landscaping materials

reviewText: Lightweight and easy enough for my petite wife to wield.Does an excellent job at trimming our hedges and small, tender saplings.Have never had an issue with Toro branded products and this one is just great!

I've used this perhaps a total two hours since delivery on three occasions.At first I was pretty sure it was less clacketty-clack noisy than the several-years old 22 inch B&D; electric it replaced. Now I'm not as sure. It still cuts more cleanly than the older trimmer it retired, and doesn't leave the foliage looking as if it had been "chewed".The description says this trimmer "easily" cuts through branches up to 9/16 inch diameter. That is untrue. It only cuts smaller twigs.I'm satisfied so far.  Hey, its a $50 hedge trimmer!BTW, looking at the other reviews, there is a provision on the Toro's handle whereby you can loop the supply extension cord, so than it can't unplug.  Another purchaser said there wasn't.
summary: Good, serviceable trimmer, so far so good

reviewText: I love it it is a great cut, it is lightweight it is long it is easy to use and handle it plugs in it is not loud it has a lot of power it is quick and doe the job great. I recommend
summary: bought for my dad and I find myself using this to do all the bushes love it

reviewText: Have to say that I am impressed with this product. I used it to trim 4 hedges and it worked excellent. I would have to say this is an amazing product for the price. The only thing missing is something to hold the cord in place. That gets annoying when it keeps falling out.

I Love this trimmer it does what i want and gets the job Done!! Yeah its electric and you got to drag a cord around but it cuts evenly and it has a 2yr warranty. I enjoy using it, But I have several hedges I need to remove so I wont be using it that much.

I bought this to take mature hedges down several feet. Unlike B&D, I trusted Toro to actually cut the size branches claimed. To my satisfaction, I found that I only needed to use the long handled loppers on a few of the biggest stalks. I owned a 2.5amp B&D trimmer, and it was ridiculous when I stuck it in the middle of the hedge to see what would happen (not much). The Toro carved through until it hit a large branch, then opened up the area to expose it for lopping. Over 20ft of hedges in approx. 1 hour. The hardest part was clean up, just what I had hoped for.

Toro 51494 Cordless 22-Inch 20-Volt Lithium-Ion Hedge TrimmerWhat was I thinking when I filled my yard with flowering shrubs and hedges that need constant maintenance during the growing season, thousands of flowers that need to be dead-headed before they will produce more, gigantic ornamental grasses (Pampas, Cosmopolitan and Japanese) that need to be cut to the ground every winter to be beautiful the next season, butterfly bushes that need to be trimmed back before Spring, or they will not bloom, and roses that stab me when it's time to prune etc. ?  I usually do all this with a hand clipper which takes a good chunk out of my "Me Time", to say the least! :|The Toro 51494 Cordless 22-Inch 20-Volt Lithium-Ion Hedge Trimmer is impressive right out of the box, fully assembled -- nothing to monkey around with, as they say, and comes in one of my favorite colors -- Red.* Electric hedge trimmer with a 22-inch-long cutting bar and a sturdy protective slide cover over cutting bar.* 20-Volt Max* Lithium-Ion Battery* a nice, weighty, Charging base for battery.  Sits on floor, or wherever, and plugs into outlet via electrical cord.* Instructions1st charge up battery, remove plastic cover over cutting bar and oil the top blade with machine oil -- if ya don't have any, buy a little can -- as the top blade needs to be oiled before and after use. I just put a little on a paper towel and wipe the blade.  *makes note to self to buy another can of oil*20-Volt Lithium-Ion Battery slides down a groove, on the charger, and then snaps into place with ease -- the fit is snug, not wobbly.  Plug charger into wall outlet.  2 red lights come on to let you know the battery is charging.  Battery is fully charged when one light is red and the other is green.  It didn't take all that long to charge the 1st time.Slide charged battery into designated slot on hedge trimmer.  *Snap*  Good to go!Gripping the Toro 51494 Cordless 22-Inch 20-Volt Lithium-Ion Hedge Trimmer's dual handles for trimming, and carrying around the yard to the next project, was a very pleasant experience. The handles felt secure, and the trimming did not tire my hands or arms, even after a couple of hours of steady use. :)I was able to trim a variety of hedges, large ornamental grass, various shrubs (rose, butterfly bushes, rosemary), some smaller tree branches, dead-head a lot of flowers with a single swoop of the trimmer, create a lot of "neighbor - envy" -- and a whole lot more.  The blades cut through the vegetation super fast without snagging or slowing down.  There is a lot of power coming from the 20-Volt Lithium-Ion battery! 'nuf said!"The handle rotates 90 degrees in each direction, making trimming vertically easy and comfortable."  This is a very nice feature, and very easy to implement.  Just press the top button with thumb and turn trimmer till you hear a *click*, then it's locked in place. Press it again to return to the original position.The Toro 51494 Cordless 22-Inch 20-Volt Lithium-Ion Hedge Trimmer just put the Fun back into yard work. *wonders what I will do with all that time I just freed up on the weekends*Does the Toro 51494 Cordless 22-Inch 20-Volt Lithium-Ion Hedge Trimmer sound like what you may be looking for? :)  Would make a Fantastic gift!  Highly Recommended!  --Katharena Eiermann, 2012

Forget about the rotating handle, the great blade or the durable battery; the time this device saved us is priceless. We've moved to our current home last fall and the previous owners let the privet hedge go wild. It was too wide and too tall. It also has about 200 ft in length, so you can imagine the amount of work. With this trimmer we could finish it in a little more than an hour!We wanted to try the trimmer as soon as possible, so we started working late one afternoon and we had to stop because it was getting dark. I don't know if the battery would hold for the entire time, but I can say that it did hold for 45 minutes on and off, with no change in potency.The trimmer is not too heavy, it's easy to maneuver, has a nice grip and the rotating handle is extremely practical for formal hedge trimming.The blade was the right size for the work we had and it took care of every branch (in our case, the largest ones were 5/8 in). We didn't expect this amount of power with a 20-Volt battery, so we were pleasantly surprised.The other obvious pro is the cordless feature, which is also time saving, allowing freedom and independence of movement.In conclusion, you cannot go wrong with this device. Me and my husband highly recommend it.

Trimming with this Toro hedge trimmer is fun.  Toro has made the perfect sized trimmer with no fuss or muss and it works like an old-time heavy trimmer.  I charged my battery overnight the first time (2-3 hours after that).  When one of the two lights is red, it is ready to go.  The power is surprising and I was able to swiftly trim my hedges in a matter of minutes.The blade will cut a branch just over " in thickness which is perfect for hedges.  Next came the errant new growth in the far back of my yard.  Trees were trimmed back more evenly and I felt safe at whatever angle I held the blade at.  The blade can be rotated and locked at 90 degrees (two directions).  The handle is very comfortable to handle and control.  Many new tools come with the lithium battery and it is a wonderful invention.  No more dangerous cords.  No more gasoline.  At just under (7) pounds (6.8) you won't get arm fatigue.22-inches is the perfect length for a hedge trimmer.  I'll explain why as I am a landscape architect.  Most hedges should not exceed 24" in height for safety reasons (thieves, burglars, line of site for driving, etc.)  With this length, you never need to reach or go around the back of a hedge unless you have some unique bushes.The battery lasted about 45 minutes, but held its strength.  When the power goes, it's fairly obvious.  Plus, the trimmer is easy to clean and take care of.  Add on the 2-year warranty and I figure for the price, this is one of the better deals on the marker for every homeowner.  Check out Toro'sBlack & Decker LST220 12-Inch 20-Volt Lithium-Ion Cordless GrassHog Trimmer/EdgerandWORX TriVac WG500 12 amp All-in-One Electric Blower/Mulcher/Vacuum.

My previous hedge trimmer was a small corded Black & Decker that worked just fine.  Or so I thought until I got to try out the Toro Cordless.  For starters, how awesome is it not to have to drag out a cord, not to mention not have to worry about getting carried away and "trimming" the extension cord.  The battery may be one of the best features of this tool.  Lithium powered batteries have much more power than the Ni-Cad of days gone by.  They also hold a charge either when left in the charger or when left in the tool so you are always ready to go.  Furthermore-they are SMART!  The battery has a tester built into the back of it to indicate how much charge you've got left.  The charger itself has a set of indicator lights to let you know if it's charging, done charging, too warm to charge or not inserted properly for charging.  If you forget what the various lights mean, there's a sticker on the cord that explains them all.  As for the trimmer itself, it has a nice long blade so you don't have to bend way over to prune low growing shrubs.  The weight is not bad at all for a battery powered tool.  Get this, the handle SWIVELS so you can easily trim the vertical edge of a hedge without having to hold it at an awkward angle the whole time.  I grinned and grunted like Tim the Tool Man when I saw that feature!!!I was hoping the battery & charger would be interchangeable with a Toro weed whacker I have but alas that was not the case. Not a big enough deal to deduct from my 5 star rating but it sure would have been a nice bonus.My only regret is that I don't have more shrubbery in my yard on which I can use this new toy.  But you know, since it's cordless, I may just go out roaming the neighborhood trimming every overgrown hedge as I go.
summary: Is it wrong to love a power tool this much?

reviewText: I absolutely adore the Toro 51494 Cordless 22-Inch 20-Volt Lithium-Ion Hedge Trimmer. I have two other hedge trimmers - theBlack & Decker LHT2436 36-Volt High Performance Cordless Hedge Trimmer, 24-Inchand theBlack & Decker HH2455 24-Inch HedgeHog Hedge Trimmer With Rotating Handle And Dual Blade Action Bladesand the Toro is my favorite.It's not as powerful as the AC powered hedge trimmer or the 36-Volt Black and Decker but it makes up for that in flexibility. I've always found it annoying to change my grip when cutting the right/left side of a bush or holding the trimmer vertically and the 90 degree rotating handle makes that completely unnecessary.On top of that the battery life is pretty good and it's quite well balanced.So to sum it up: if you find yourself annoyed at having to shift your grip and move your hands to cut different sides of a bush then by all means buy the Toro 51494. If you don't care then go for the more powerful and slightly bigger B&D; 24".
summary: Lightweight and neat 90-degree rotating handles for vertical cutting!

reviewText: I already owned theBlack & Decker LHT120 HedgeHog Hedge Trimmer(also 22-Inch, 20-Volt), so this spring's first backyard trim seemed like a good time to compare the two. I found that the Toro had some ergonomic advantages, but was in general heavier and not as well balanced.- Blades. The B&D; blades are notably thicker than the Toro blades, though both are the same length. The B&D; blades are a shiny machine metal, and the instruction booklet included instructions on how to resharpen a broken blade tooth. The Toro blades are powder-coated with no option to resharpen.  The B&D; blades also cut better on the hard-stem blackberry bushes (sorry guys), though both did equally well on softer growth. You do have to let the blades work at their their own speed and not force them forward.- Battery. The B&D; takes many hours to charge, and you really just want to let it go overnight. The Toro charges notably faster, and has a charge indicator on the battery, which is a certainly plus. The B&D; batteries hold a charge for an impressively long time - I haven't had the Toro long enough to do an overwinter 6-month charge test yet.- Ergnonomics/safety.  Both trimmers have a thumb-lock that you have to push down before pushing the actual trigger on the handle (always a good thing), and both will let you let go of the thumblock once the main trigger is down. The Toro thumb lock is just a hair too close to the trigger to fit my hand perfectly, and the B&D; is just a hair too far away. I note I'm a petit female, but with unusually long fingers for my size. The Toro thumblock is, IMHO, just a little too easy to confuse with the button that lets you rotate the blade, but if I trimmed my backyard more often it probably would be less of an issue.- Balance. The B&D; is notably better balanced and generally feels lighter. A big part of this is the size and weight of the Toro battery, which is humongous compared to the B&D.;- Storage. The Toro has a lovely hard plastic scabbard to keep the blade when you're not using the trimmer, with good teeth protection and airflow to make sure you don't trap moisture next to the blade. The B&D; trimmer comes with a soft vinyl sheath to slip the blade into, but it can't compare - the Toro is clearly superior here.- Bells and Whistles. The Toro has the option to rotate the blade in relation to the handle. I was thrilled to have this while sculpting the edges of the camellia bushes - it really did decrease hand and wrist fatigue.Overall, the B&D; is a lighter and more powerful machine than the Toro, but has fewer perks (no scabbard, can't rotate, no battery indicator).  For those of you playing along at home, however, I did choose the B&D; to finish the job.
summary: Comparison with the Black & Decker LHT120

reviewText: I already trimmed my 60 foot hedge with a Black and Decker hedge trimmer so I couldn't test the battery life on this Toro, however, I did have a few things to try it out on.First it is 2 inches shorter then the BD which doesn't seem like a lot until you have to reach and it can make a big difference.Balance felt equal to me. I can hold either with one arm stretched out and both felt light enough.The BD felt like it has a bit more power espcially for thicker material. The BD is a 36 volt, the Toro is 20.One thing I do like about the Toro is the handle rotates 90 degress in either direction which makes it more comfortable when you need to change directions for instance up and down in a tight location.You can't go wrong with this tool especially with the added handle rotation. I have completely switched to battery operated garden tools over gas. This is another great tool in my gardening chest.
This Toro 51496 Cordless 24-Inch 24-Volt Hedge Trimmer is just wonderful. It has a lot of power and the battery holds a long charge. Very easy to use.  I am so glad I bought it.

I have never owned a corded hedge trimmer but this is my second cordless hedge trimmer. I would consider this Toro trimmer to be similar quality to my Black and Decker hedge trimmer. It holds a great charge and holds it for long periods of time. The battery in this trimmer doesn't need to be charged very often at all so it's almost always ready for use. One great thing about this trimmer is how you can push a button and turn the handle. My Black and Decker trimmer doesn't have this option and it's nice to have and makes it easier to make cuts that are at difficult angles or that are up high. For safety this trimmer does have a plastic shield and a hard blade cover that is used to cover the blade when not in use. The blade cover keeps you from getting cut by the blades but it's a little difficult to get in on the blade. The cover also keeps the blade clean. It's also recommended that you oil your blades after each use. I normally oil them after every 2-3 uses. My Black and Decker trimmer also has a blade cover but it's made of vinyl so it really doesn't provide any type of protection but it keeps the blade clean. There are several things about this trimmer that I like better than my Black and Decker trimmer but the most important thing is how it cuts. This Toro trimmer cuts pretty decent but not quite as good as my Black and Decker trimmer. There are times when this trimmer will break the branches instead of giving a nice clean cut. I never had this problem with my other trimmer. I also use my other trimmer to trim large decorative grass which is does really well but this trimmer doesn't do as good with the large grass. Overall I think Toro makes a good trimmer with some nice features.
summary: Toro Hedge Trimmer vs. Black and Decker, just as good overall but with different strengths and weaknesses

reviewText: This Toro trimmer is fantastic.  The swivel action makes trimming hedges on the sides a breeze.  You really do get less fatigue when you don't have to turn your wrists sideways.  The Li-Ion battery is extremely light and holds a charge very nicely.  I was able to trim all my hedges and still had juice left over.  Granted, I trimmed my hedges for about 20 minutes straight and was finished.I also have a 18v NiCad Black & Decker Hedge Trimmer - NHT518 cordless, and this Toro kicks it's butt.  It is stronger, and quieter.  I only wish it came with a sturdier blade cover.  The blade cover is flimsy, but does it's job.  You won't be disappointed in this trimmer.  It comes fully assembled, and all you should do is charge the battery first before using.  5 stars all the way.

This has been a big step up from my old Black and Decker cordless.  For starters the battery last about 2x as long as the B&D; ever did.  I know because I used to trim about half my bushes before I had to drop it on the charger and the Toro can finish my whole yard.  Right there, I'm sold.  It also cuts a little easier which is also helping my trim time come down.  The weight is comparable to the B&D; and much better than my old gas trimmer.The swivel feature is surprisingly nice.  My first thought was "gimmick" but the improved comfort is noticeable.  It's actually a big plus in the usability column.  Overall this is an awesome hedge trimmer with lots to recommend it and no draw backs that I've encountered.  I've got a decent number of bushes to trim and I've never looked back at a gas powered trimmer since I went cordless.  No noise, no mixing gas and oil for the two stroke, and much lighter.

Having used hedge sheers to trim the bushes at the front of my house for years (there's five of them), taking hold of the Toro 51496 was like a dream. First of all, the job finished five times quicker. Secondly, my hands and wrists didn't hurt afterwards.The trimmer has a good even weight from front to back, making the large battery balance well with the cutter blades. The device didn't feel heavy or clunky, either, and I was surprised at how smoothly it operated.There are LED indicator lights on the battery, allowing you to check the remaining charge without having to take it off the trimmer. But it does only come with one battery (and one Charging unit). Thankfully, the battery life lasts quite awhile (more than several jobs worth) and can be recharged within an hour.The rotating handle seemed like a nice feature, but I found that I just didn't have a need for it. What I liked best was the uncommonly wide slots in the cutting blades, which allowed me to tackle thicker branches (up to 5/8-inch, which is just over a half inch, around the size of my pointer finger).It surprises me how many people buy corded trimmers--I'd rather chop away with a hedge sheers than constantly tug and trip over a cord. With how powerful battery operated tools are nowadays, to me, it's a no-brainer.
summary: The perfect tool for my needs

reviewText: This is the best hedge trimmer I own now. I have a collection a large electric a small electric, and 18 volt cordless and now a 24 volt cordless. This 24 volt is by far the best. It came fully assembled all I had to do is charge the battery for about 3 hours. First thing out of the box you know this is quality.I tried it first on a bunch of honeysuckle that is growing over my fence from a wooded area. It didn't hesitate once it was like combing the fence all those twigs and leaves hitting the ground. The unit is sturdy without being to heavy to handle. I have a lot of that to work on this Spring and 9 huge boxwood hedges that are sculpted that I dread each summer to cut. These should have the power I need to get the job done.If you are hesitating on a rechargeable trimmer not to worry these have the power. I worked as long as I could and it didn't run out of power. I then took my Toro mulching mower and ran over the mess of leaves and twigs and poof the area was all cleaned up, it is a bank with an ivy type covering.Highly recommend.
summary: Like a hot knife through butter~Best trimmer yet!

reviewText: This is my favorite of all my electric hedge trimmers.  I have had several in the past - 2 cordless, and 2 with cords.  I strongly favor the cordless since I have a tendency to cut into the cords.Here's what I really like about the Toro 51496 Cordless Hedge Trimmer:1.  It's light in weight.  I am female and can easily lift, carry and use this trimmer even over my head.2.  It cuts nicely.  It cut down our overgrown hedges like a hot knife through butter.  Even cut stems that were up to 1/4 inch in diameter.3.  The safety switch that must be constantly held is very easy on the thumb.  On my other cordless, I had to push the safety switch which really tired my entire hand.  On this hedge trimmer, the safety switch is PULLED back which really saves wear and tear on your thumb.4.  The battery only took about an hour to charge.  I don't yet know how long it will hold a charge but I did get 4 BIG bushes trimmed down to size before it started raining.5.  It has a swivel mechanism.  With the push of a button the cutting apparatus will swivel so that you don't necessarily have to turn the entire hedge trimmer on it's side to cut down the side of a bush or shrub.  I still have to get used to that feature, but I think it's a good one.There's really nothing I can find to complain about concerning this hedge trimmer.  It cuts well, is easy to use, and charges quickly.  Nice little machine!UPDATE:  April 29, 2012I took the Toro 51496 Cordless Hedge Trimmer over to my mother's house and cut back all of her bushes and hedges.  I really like the swivel feature because by pressing the blue button, the motor and cutting blade will rotate together either to the left or right 90 degrees and lock in. I was able to cut the sides of the bushes while still holding the handle of the trimmer in the upright position.  It really made cutting the sides of the bushes and hedges much easier.

Plenty of power and run time on a full battery charge.  I do have a smaller yard with only a handful of bushes but have never even run the battery half way down.  Enough power to trim most bushes in my yard.  Very easy to use.

I really like this trimmer.  It looks like a chainsaw because of the handle and the guard.  It is light-weight and I like the 24v lithium battery and charger it comes with.  This trimmer rotates so it is more ergonomic when having to turn the trimmer based on angles.  The battery comes with a button that when pressed, it gives you the battery status.The length of the trimmer blades is longer than my old Black & Decker so I am able to reach more and finish quicker.  The guard in front is there to protect you against branches as you trim as well as keeping your knuckles away from the blades, which is as we all know, very important.The cons of this unit is there is no lock for the switch.  You have to keep the trigger pulled and can get fatiguing if you are doing a large job.  The battery lasts a long time, but having no trigger lock is a bad thing for large jobs.When running the unit it is very quiet as opposed to some of the other trimmers.  Overall I am satisfied with this unit, but for small jobs.
summary: Like a well oiled machine..for small jobs

reviewText: I hate gas powered machines. I am a techie, but I don't understand gas engines very well. And I certainly don't like dealing with gas and oil, or filters and all the craziness that comes with maintaining a gas engine.I also recently saw someone who bragged about his awesome overpriced gas powered trimmer that always start on the first pull. A few minutes later, he couldn't get this "awesome" machine started for a full 1/2 hour.Enough ranting, here's what happened.I researched for something that would not be too heavy. adjustable height. battery-powered. swivel to do edging. lots of power to cut through tough brush. battery that will hold a charge for a long time. excellent warranty. good brand name.The best option for me was this unit.I can check the battery quickly (without removing it even). The battery pops out, and charges quickly. It pops back in and is ready to go for probably close to 2 hours. It is not too heavy, I don't get fatigued while using it, although I do wish there was a way to have it working without holding down the button, but I see why it has that safety feature.And it is powerful. I was used to a corded trimmer and this thing really holds its own. I can finally edge like a pro!
summary: The exact thing I was looking for...

reviewText: Interesting! The week whacker came in an obviously pre-opened package and I was expecting grass and dirt but all contents looked untouched and new. Instructions were reasonably easy to follow; however the description, and even the mention of the wall bracket was missing from the printed copy and at first I wondered what that part was for. However, I figured it out and confirmed it when I downloaded the manual from the Toro Site. Also, there is nothing in the instructions which tells me which of two possible orientations to install the wire edge guide so I guess I have a 50/50 chance of getting it right. I first installed it with the end pointing down but changed it to point upwards after using it for a while. I see the cost of battery replacement is very high...almost 70% of the cost of the trimmer itself. Hope it lasts for a while. I usually like to keep one or more spare batteries fully charged for the inevitable dead battery experience but not this time...not at those prices.I used it once on my yard, a small lot of about 150 x 60 less the house, with trimming all around both the house and the fence on three sides and gardens. I also used the "edger" mode for the drive, front of the house and the rear patio. This is not really an edger with a blade and all, just the whacker turned 90 degrees so it whacks vertically so it doesn't really do what a blade would do but it''s okay for my purposes. Hard to guide straightly, however, even with the wheel so the edge is somewhat ragged. Having said that, I whacked for about an hour on low power setting (really a blade movement which takes off about an inch of the end of the cord) and still had more to go. Nice not to have fuel fumes or a long cord to deal with.Am reasonably satisfied with this item and would recommend it to a friend.
summary: Excellent Quality Product on First Look

reviewText: This Toro 51486 Cordless 12-Inch 24 Volt Electric Trimmer/Edger is the best. Toro is the best!  I also bought the 24-volt hedge trimmer, so I would always have a charged battery. One battery lasts a long time.  I am very impress.  I would buy it again.

I used a gas trimmer before and there is no difference in power/quality.  If anything, this is much better!  Would definitely recommend spending a little extra to get this one over other similar models if you are comparing.  I have not had to use for more than 45 minutes at a time and the battery handles it perfectly.  The rotator is a nice feature as I can do weeds and as a sidewalk trimmer.

It telescopes out, but not much. To make the cutting head parallel to the ground, the handle/battery has to be about two feet from the ground!! This makes it uncomfortable for a large percentage of the population.I would lose the telescoping feature, a waste of money, and instead have a swiveling cutting head so the user doesn't have to bend over all day to keep the head level. It also needs the front handle to be adjustable up, in addition to the fore and aft adjustment it has now.Seriously, I may rig up some sort of  handle extensions.Why not just return it? Well, it is a good trimmer.I have a big, noisy and vibrating gas trimmer for my bi-annual full yard trimming, one that takes all day. The Toro is the no-excuse device to do the weekly little trims when the wild grasses in my rural yard are growing fast.The Toro trimmed this wild grass, almost 8 inches tall and wet from a shower, probably around 300 square feet, quickly and without drama. Even some errant tough-stemmed ground cover was dealt with nicely.I thought the single small diameter cutting string would just not be enough and that the motor would bog down, but it didn't. It all cut well and quite quickly really. All this only seems to have used maybe 25% of the battery! Pretty impressive. The string did not jamb and it seems to feed out at a decent rate. I thought it might fly out fast in order to sell more string, but it is fine. And I used the long-string option (you can set it so the string is cut off shorter, thus lowering the load on the motor and saving the battery).You obviously slide into heavy wet grass slowly and nibble at it a bit more than you would with a landscaper's gas unit, but I think the Toro would be fine for most residential yards.I do not have a need for the edging setting, and cannot comment on its use, but it seems well thought out for what it does. It would seem that dedicated edgers would be better for that perfect, professional cut along the circular drive and around the pool...
summary: Comes up a bit short for some

reviewText: Disclaimer: I am reviewing a unit I received for free through the Vine program.Well it is a decent string trimmer. Here's what I compare it to/against: I hate gas trimmers, have 2 broken ones that won't start (one 2-cycle, one 4-cycle), cluttering up the garage. I also have a smaller Worx cordless electric trimmer (with 18V NiCad battery; <http://www.amazon.com/WG150-1-10-Inch-18-Volt-Cordless-Electric/dp/B000NKPCDM>), and a broken ancient Black & Decker EdgeHog cordless electric trimmer that died years ago.Pros:* It is cordless electric, not gas. did I mention that I hate gas string trimmers and have 2 broken ones?* It is well balanced, so even with a slightly heavier battery up top, overall it's not too tiring to carry and wave around for a while.* For an electric trimmer, it is relatively "heavy duty" (slightly thicker string, and larger spool holding more string, than the Worx electric trimmer; longer handle too). I was surprised that it was able to whack some pretty thick-stemmed nasty weeds, and some nasty tenacious vines (thanks to global warming, we get more and more nasty vines every year lately).* It comes in the middle price range, for cordless electric trimmers -- more than the $60 Worx GT 18V (http://www.amazon.com/WG150-1-10-Inch-18-Volt-Cordless-Electric/dp/B000NKPCDM) but less than some Black & Decker's.* The 24V lithium battery does last longer than NicCad batteries of lower voltage (in the Worx, where there was actually a recall & free replacement last year, of bad old batteries). or compared to the ancient Black & Decker EdgeHog whose battery died like 7 years ago. We have a few acres although I only need to weed-whack small areas around the house; still it takes over an hour to do a complete job; in the 2 times I've used this Toro electric trimmer so far this season, the battery lasted most of the way, though not all the way (I had to switch to the Worx electric trimmer to finish the job, after this one's battery finally gave out).Cons:* The edge guard was a joke. It snapped off and got lost, after the first 45 seconds of use, in a heavy patch of weeds, and I never found it again!* The automatic string advance doesn't work, not for me at least. Even the manual advance button doesn't work for me either. So I have to take off the cap from the spool, and manually lift the spool up to let out a few turns of string, every time I need to advance some. Now maybe I've got something screwed in the wrong way, I don't know, but I've tried removing the spool and putting it back, twisting this way and that, and still nothing works, neither the automatic advance nor the manual button.(contrast this with the Worx electric trimmer, which has smaller spools and thinner cord, BUT the automatic advance works great there)* The spool refills aren't free (contrast with Worx electric trimmer, which offers free replacement spools for life! you just pay shipping & handling)* It does cost more than the Worx GT 18V, which does have the free lifetime spool replacements, plus you can buy a 2nd battery for the Worx, to make up for its shorter battery life, total still less than this Toro's price. The Worx did have a horrible problem with its batteries going dead after just a few uses, but Worx has a recall + free replacement program now, for the bad batteries, so you might give the Worx a try to save some money.*  It does only have one string outlet from the spool, so there's only 1 piece of cord flying/cutting, which is typical for electric trimmers; gas trimmers, on the other hand, usually have 2. ALthough the trade-off is that with only 1 outlet for 1 length of string, you also don't have double windings of 2 separate cord lengths in the spool/housing, so this one is much simpler than those in gas trimmers.

Yes...I am a woman, AND a woman of a 'certain age' (that's what...over 40??)and I decided I was going to put this together AND use it.  I DID need a bitmore muscle when it came to get the handle in place (I have small hands thatare ALSO of a certain age...) but that was the only help I needed. I love this Toro...we have owned other Toro products over the years but this was the first trimmer we have had of theirs.  That little wheel they have built in, WHAT A STROKE OF GENIUS!! Honestly it made it SO much easier for me to guide it alongto edge the yard, and I did a good job with it if I say so myself.  Its nice it has a low energy level that you can use...or not if you want more energy...but with it having the one battery charged up I think you could do a very sizable lawns trimming and edging with no problems whatsoever.  Plus that wheel, ahhhh!!Really how is it that no one has come up with that before now?  No more big zigs or zags while edging! They even pack it right, came in a thin box probably about4 or so inches deep so it was very compact and tightly packed so nothing was loose and nothing was missing parts or broken from flopping around a too large package.  I am really impressed, and to be honest with you, I think the price Amazon sells it for is a great one, we have paid more for our other line-trimmers/edgers that were not as nice as this one...I talked my husband into donating our other one that is just a season old, as THIS one is THAT much nicer, more power, better features.  WHY would anyone want a gas trimmer/edger in the days of 4.00 gallon gas???  I think THIS would be a great Father's Day or birthday gift to a gardening or lawn mowing Dad  =) I really thought it was a great product, and I do not like yard work, but wanted to be able to review this properly.
summary: Woman does yard trimming...Toro wins her heart!

reviewText: I was really excited about getting this trimmer with all the great reviews. Several problems for me. First I hated the fact that I had to hold down the saftey switch the entire time or it cuts off. My arms were very tired just from having to hold down that stupid saftey switch. Also battery didn't last very long even on a regular sized yard. The charger also kept saying battery too warm even when it wasn't warm. Also didn't find the auto feed helpful. Lastly, very weak power. I returned mine and went and bought a Craftsman 4 cycle gas weedwhacker with electric start(no mixing of oil and gas, electric start so no pulling, starts right up, awesome power, and has a simple no hazzle weed cord that only takes ten seconds to change out and so far have weed eated entire yard and haven't had to change the weed cord yet. Anyway, I don't usually recommend other products in my reviews but in this case I did because I don't think any other brand of gas weedeaters have this electric start and no oil mixing except for the Craftsman 4 cycle weedwhacker.Craftsman gas is alittle heavier but buy a $10 shoulder strap on you will be fine. My arms are less tired using the gas craftsman and took one fifth the amount of time and energy than we I used the toro electric.

It looks good, and you cannot argue the advantages of having no cord.  It has lots of power, and I have found the battery to last an acceptable length of time.But...I am so disappointed that I have to manually adjust the string!  Oh, they say it advances automatically, but in the manual they mention a method to advance the string, and while edging, you must use this method often.  And it's not a bump, rather a thing where you run it, stop it, wait a couple seconds and repeat.  That works, but honestly I just did the edging out front and I had to do that annoying thing approximately every 8-12 seconds in order to have enough line extending to do the job.  It starts out great, but within seconds it needs more line.  Once you get the line it does a great job, but only for seconds at a time!  I find the procedure hard on my hand because I have to do it so often, plus I stop so often that it takes forever to edge!I like the wheel that helps with the edging, and I like the edging guide, but the guide cannot be tucked out of the way while cutting weeds.  If you want it out of the way you must remove it and of course you can imagine it wouldn't take long to lose it.Usually my reviews are favorable because I do so much research before I buy, but if I had it to do over I would not buy this model again.  Putting up with a cord is easier than putting up with this line advancing thing.  Note that I have been using this for months, so I have given it a chance to make me happy, but my disappointment only grows.  They clearly have some kinks to work out.  Too bad because the cordless feature is good and this machine has a lot of power.

This has decent power for a cordless, not great but good. Very lightweight and balanced. Cuts through grass easily and most weeds, even thick ones pretty well too if you take your time and go slow with the thicker weeds.Edging feature works really nice and was a breeze.I did about 30 minutes off trimming and edging and still have two bars left.

I own another trimmer that is an 18 volt that has served me well but it doesn't have the power this baby does. From the moment I unpacked the box I knew I was dealing with real quality. I have a Toro lawn mower that Is really great so I had high expectations and they were met and then some. It is very easy to put together in just a few minutes.It took about 3 hours to charge the battery. There are 2 lights on the charger the left one stays red and the right one turns green when it is fully charged. The manual says it will take less time for each charge as time goes by.I first used it as an edger. It is easy to rotate into position and you can also set it to a lower energy consumption level for edging. It has a wheel on the edge so you just roll it in front of you and it zips along. I did the driveway and whole front walk in about 2 minutes and I have a considerable amount to do. The wheel makes it easy to go a straight line. I am super impressed as I have not edged in over a year. It looks great. Next I flipped it back and did my trimming, I did set it back to full power for this. Worked great. I still had battery power left when I was done and it had not slowed down a bit.I can highly recommend this unit. It is very high quality in construction and operation. It has a full 2 year warranty for use in home conditions.
summary: WOW~This trimmer does the job, easy and FAST!

reviewerName: Mr. Deeds "Opportunity is limited only by ima...
reviewText: I have a little over 4 acres of land around my home in rural Ohio -- most of that land is around the barn and pasture. I've been using this Toro all summer and it has not let me down yet.It's been more than powerful enough to tackle all of the long, hard-to-reach grass and weeds immediately around my house and surrounding trees, shrubs and fence. That task takes around 30-45 minutes minutes.I've never had the battery run out on me -- my arms wear out on me before the battery. That said, even though the Toro 51486 Cordless is light-weight at 8 pounds (relatively speaking compared with gas-powered trimmers), it still gets heavy after awhile. I strung a bit of rope around it and created a makeshift shoulder strap which really helps.The unit is very easy to use. I particularly like the flower-guard, which let's you trim right up next to flowers and other desirable plants without hurting them. My last trimmer didn't have one and I sometimes slipped-up and whacked flowers.The edger feature works well on walkway/driveway sections that already have a nice edge and just need to be cleaned-up a bit. I tried it on the driveway up to the barn, which has never been edged, and it got bogged down a bit.I've never weed-whacked the tall grasses and weeds that grow along the fence to the pasture, but did so just to really put the Toro 51486 Cordless to the test. It did very well, much better then I thought. It took a few extra passes to whack everything down, but it got the job done.In summaryPros:* Very easy to setup and use right out of the box (after charging the battery)* Long battery life. My arms give out before the battery does.* Flower-guard: Let's you trim right up next to flowers and other desirable plants without hurting them.Cons (and these really aren't cons, but might be useful to know):* It's lightweight at 8 pounds, but it gets heavy after awhile. Would be nice if a shoulder strap was included.* Edger is really only good for walkways and driveways that have been previously edged. Gets bogged down a bit when tackling a long-neglected stretch.
summary: Tough enough for most yards + long-lasting battery

reviewText: When I first got this, I wasn't too sure I was going to really like it, but after several months use I really love it.  I had the Worx GT li-ion trimmer edger and I liked it alot, but I really like this Toro better and now use it exclusively.  The reason I prefer this one, is the bigger longer lasting battery - I can go 2-3 weeks of edging and trimming on one battery before I have to recharge - the Worx trimmer battery basically has to be charged after every use and gain, because the toro battery is bigger it has more power than the Worx GT.  Another thing I like is that the head pivots to change from trimmer to edger - and it's very easy to push the button and swing it around.  The worx required me to twist the handle, then step on head and move the arm back and forth to switch from trimmer to edger - and sometimes I wouldn't get it in exactly the right position for either and would have to stop and adjust it - the toro only has the two positions (edging or trimming) so once you swivel it it's always in exactly the right position.  This is a walk behind edger just like the Worx GT which is a must in my book.When I first tried this trimmer/edger, I was a little concerned about the space between the safety and trigger (I am a petite woman with small hands) and whether or not I could easily span it with my hand, but I quickly adapted to it and don't even notice it anymore.  Overall, I couldn't be happier with the quality and function of this trimmer/edger - now I'm anxiously waiting for a hedge trimmer and a blower that can use the same battery!

This Toro Trimmer replaced a first generation Worx GT in my yard care arsenal.  I loved the design of the Worx but the NiCad battery was a gutless wonder.  I was considering upgrading to their new Lithium-ion model when I was offered this Toro to test.  The comparison is night and day.  You can charge up the Lithium battery ahead of time and a week later it will still be ready to go like you just took it off the charger.  It has really good power and cut through all but the most hard core weeds I could find.  My dry run was on what is essentially a vacant lot, untended and overgrown.  I put the trimmer on the "power save" setting (the blade is positioned closer to the center so the cutting swath is less and the motor uses less juice due to the shorter line length)expecting the battery to run out long before I got finished.  I was nearly done with the yard and hadn't noticed any drop off in power so I switched out of power save mode and still had power left after doing the entire lot.  The trimmer easily switches to edger configuration and rolls easily to trim along walkways.  I did not ever see the line auto feed but it is so easy to manually feed it (just push a little button and pull out some more line).  Actually this will probably prevent wasted trimmer line in the long run.  I took off the little wire guard since it seemed to keep me from getting as close to my desired targets as I wanted.The only think I miss from the Worx trimmer is that the head on the Toro is fixed.  The Worx pivots so you can get a better angle to go under shrubs.  On the Toro, you just have to compensate with the angle at which you hold the shaft so it is more something to get used to than a big design flaw.The weight, balance and height adjustment of this tool work great for both me and my husband.  I used to dread edging but now we fight over who gets to do it!

My yard is fairly small; maybe 1/4 of an acre which takes me less than 30 minutes to edge.  This edger has more than enough power and is quiet as well.  I like that the head flips so that i can edge along the sidewalk and driveway. So glad that I found this product.

This looks like a real good one.  Take the parts from the box, and you will need a Phillips screwdriver to assemble.  Takes about 30 minutes of less to assemble.  Charge the battery for about 2 hours on the charger provided.  Shaft is adjustable for the just the right height you need.  Bottom section flips over at the push of a button to use as a trimmer.  Also has a cool little wheel, to help with trimming.  Battery has a test button to show how much life it has left.  Appears to be made of strong plastic and medal parts, so should hold up very well.  Weight is about 8 pounds and is nicely balanced, so as not to wear you out. Uses .065 line, which will come out automatically or manually at the touch of a button.  Comes with a full 2 year warranty for residential use.

This battery powered trimmer is just the device for maintaining a small yard.  It is light weight and trims and edges both horizontally and vertically, however, I would not reccommend it for larger jobs such as cutting weeds.  It is excellent for a regularly maintained yard.  The battery is sufficent for extended trimming.  It is great for edging around scrubs.  Great for edging along the walkways because you can edge the two different ways.

Don't think this will replace a gas-powered trimmer for cutting brush; but it will handle tall weeds and maintain your lawn nicely.  I used it to cut the high grass and weeds around out rural mailbox (which had grown quite high due to balky starting of my gas trimmer) Went all around yard to trim around 12 trees and half dozen posts.  Lasts about 45min of near-continuous use and recharged in the time it took me to cool down with a beer.  Seems well constructed too.

Wow.  This Trimmer is excellent!!  Not flawless, but excellent. I own a Black & Decker model.  Standard model, non-adjustable height.  Can convert easily from edger to trimmer.  But this one by Toro, man it is great.  It swivels with a push of a button.  Only one way because it uses a spring action.  Again.  Only one way.  Battery is a 24 volt lithium battery.  Comes with a charger, battery all you need to get it going.I like the telescoping adjustment for length.  It comes with a power save mode, which is basically just a string trimmer adjustment.  Supposedly you save power if the string is shorter than longer.  I guess.  I keep in long.The edging feature is different.  You press the button and it turns into edging position and has a wheel where you can push from behind to edge.  I found this a bit difficult to get used to since you can't see where you are going and sometimes it wiggles.  Great concept, but there is a learning curve.  I guess I have to get used to it.The other thing I feel is a bit lacking is the string length adjustment.  You have to stop the device.  Wait until you hear a "click" and then start it up again.  This can get a bit frustrating when the string starts to shorten from use.One thing I would like to see is a "guide" to know where to keep the edger straight when edging.  I like edging from the side as opposed to the rear.  That is the only issue with this trimmer.I like the battery because it has a button that you can press to see the power level.  Very nice feature.The trimmer is light so it is not cumbersome to use over a length of time.  I do recommend this unit.  Just remember the learning curve with using the edger.
summary: Nice.  Very nice.  Edger may need getting used to.

reviewText: Our old trimmer recently died. It was probably a decade-old and this Spring just gave up the ghost. We don't have a huge yard in either the front or the back so our goal was to get a decent one that could handle two small yards.  Since we needed one anyway and it matched our criteria, when I saw this one I decided to give it a try. So how did it do?First off, it comes tightly packed in the box that weighs about 13 pounds. The box was relatively easy to get open, just three pieces of tape on the top and three pieces on the bottom. Just a tip, you're probably better off pulling it out of the bottom of the box than the top. The package contains the device, the secondary handle, the guard, battery and charger, and a wall mounting thing with screws. The only real tool you're going to need to assemble the trimmer is a Phillips head screwdriver. From opening the box, to fully assembled unit, took me roughly half an hour. A very good start.Next charging the battery. The battery charges in a unit separate from the device itself. I have a cordless lawnmower, which set a pretty high bar by being able to charge either inside the mower or outside. I'd rather it could charge the battery while still in the trimmer, but it's not a huge deal. It takes a little bit of force to put the battery into its charger, so be ready to push a little bit, because you won't hurt it as long as you have it in the right way. To remove the battery you have to pull up on a little lever on the side that doesn't go into the charger to release.The manual says it takes 3 hours to charge, but my first charge only took about two hours.  According to myBelkin power meter, while charging the battery up to capacity the charger is using 41-42 watts of power dropping to about 27 W as it charged a while; to give you a rough idea, by the power meter's estimate that's roughly $3.43 a month, however it'd obviously be less as you're not going to charging a dead battery for 720 hours straight.
