As a side note, the battery itself has a built in tester so you can see it's charge with the push of a button, which is very cool.To make it last, proper battery treatment is important.  Lithium batteries don't suffer the same "memory" effects (lost capacity from repeated partial charges) that the old Nickel Cadmium batteries used to.  It's actually better for the battery to charge it when it's only 50% drained rather than letting it go dead before charging it.  The charger only uses .5 W maintaining a full charge (roughly $0.58 a year if left plugged in), but you'll prolong the battery's lifespan if you plan ahead and only charge the battery before you're ready to use it instead.  The instruction manual suggests leaving it out of the charger over extended idle periods, but if you're going to leave it sitting out a VERY long time, you might want to just check it and charge it periodically to keep it around half charged since all rechargeable batteries lose a bit of a charge over time and lithium batteries prefer to be stored in a cool place at 40-50% charged.Overall design of the trimmer is excellent. You can adjust the length of the handle a certain amount for more comfortable operation. The placement of the secondary handle can also be adjusted somewhat. I found them to be an excellent position to provide support. The guard allows for a 90 orientation change. By pushing in on a button and rotating it you're able to change the orientation so you can get things that are right along the edge of the fence for example. There's even a perfectly placed wheel to allow it to glide easily along those areas while edging. In addition there's a little power saver knob which shortens the length of the wire and thus prolongs runtime by having less length to spin; basically, it's just a little razor blade that cuts the chord off to 10" instead of the regular 12" length.  The trimmer comes with a full line spool, but when you eventually have to replace that, their instructions suggest using Toro 88532 line, (available on Amazon) so you can check the cost for that, though any .065" (1.6 mm) trimmer replacement line should work.The device feels sturdy. The materials are lightweight, weighing only about 8 pounds, but it doesn't feel flimsy. Even the plastic bits seem to be pretty solid and look like they can take some abuse. If you're reasonably strong individual, using this on even a midsized yard shouldn't be a problem.  When the line inevitably breaks, you can extend it using the auto-advancing line feature or you can manually extend the line yourself using a button on the base of the wire spool.  I only use it for about 20 minutes at a time so I can't speak to maximum battery life, but it cut everything with plenty of power and the battery wasn't drained that much.I think the defining thing I thought of as I was writing this review is how I kept telling my wife "This is so cool!" right after I'd set it up. I like just about everything about the design and it's a trusted brand so I don't have any fears about the battery dying immediately or other parts breaking right way. I think we'll be using this for a long time to come.

My husband and I put this bird feeder up along with 2 others on a timber post we concreted in as a feature in our new backyard this weekend. There all different finishes and at different heights filled with various bird feeds. This feeder contains a songbird mix and boy has it been busy! I like that it sways just a tiny bit when the birds land on the bars along the edges to feed. That way you notice a new feathered freind coming in for a landing out the window.My one complaint is you need to fill this feeder over a container as the open edges with no ledge to speak of below them allow the seeds to fall out at a pretty good trickle as you pour the feed in. Then you can just tip the fallen seeds back into the feeder at the end of filling. But you can make a bit of a mess if you don't realize that at the start.

The Perky-Pet 363 Birds and Berries Lantern Feeder is an attractive addition to our backyard patio.  The feeder is very easy to fill and has 4 u-shaped perches for multiple occupants-although I have only seen one bird at a time on it thus far.  We hung the feeder on a shepherd's crook just off the patio and waited for a few days before we saw our first taker.  Well the word must have spread throughout the Bird Network because we now have a steady stream of finches, cardinals and bluejays enjoying the Wild Bird Seed mix we have provided.  No squirrels have tried to invade the feeder(the openings are probably too small for them and they can't open the top) but they do enjoy the seeds the birds drop to the ground.  All in all-its a lovely feeder that does the job well!

I have had this feeder in front of my house for about a month now but it doesn't seem to be attracting any birds. I previously had a smaller bird feeder in the same place and the bird seed would go faster from that feeder, but the big birds broke the bottom part so I needed to replace it.Maybe it is the bird silhouettes on the sides of the feeder that is making it so no birds come up to it. Or maybe it is the little perches for them to stand on to eat the food. But, whatever it is this feeder is not popular with the birds around my house. I usually get blue birds and finches that come and eat at my feeder, but so far I haven't seen either come to this one.Overall look is very appealing. It is much nicer looking than my old feeder. It is pretty to look at and looks nicer in front of my house. It is a pretty hefty as well, feels nice and solid.

Almost all the birds in our yard are those little brown sparrows. They took to this immediately and drained it in one day. The feeder itself is a nice change to the tube with perches out of the side style that I have.Feeder is very attractive and a nice addition to my yard. It came well-packed and was easy to fill and hang.No complaints here!
summary: Feeder is a hit in our yard

reviewText: Perky-Pet 363 Birds and Berries Lantern Feeder is a real sight.  I got it out of the box, put some seeds in it and minutes later, all the birds in the area started to hang around the feeder.  Finches, jays and black birds started milling around the feeder, fighting each other and loitering.  I enjoy birds so I thought it was a hoot.  The feeder didn't take long to set up and it's very light (but sturdy).  Just hung it from a post, eave or tree and wait for the birds to come.  If you're looking for a backyard bird feeder then I suggest that you try the Perky-Pet Birds and Berries Lantern Feeder.
summary: A sturdy and light feeder that brings in the flocks

reviewText: Perky-Pet 363 Birds and Berries Lantern Feederas the poet e. e. cummings once said:  I would rather learn from one bird how to sing than to teach 10,000 stars how not to dance.Among other things, I'm a nature photographer and an avid bird watcher.  Wild birds need clean water, a bit of shelter and food -- it's that simple. :)  I've gone through my share of bird feeders, over the past 10 years -- some good, some bad.  They are not all alike!Perky-Pet 363 Birds and Berries Lantern Feeder is impressive, right off the bat!a few things I really like about the Perky-Pet 363 Birds and Berries Lantern Feeder, other than it comes in one of my favorite colors -- black:* good sized feeder, holds up to 5lbs of seed.  ( hint:  My own observation:  a huge variety of birds seem to love black oil sunflower seeds ).* sturdy metal housing with see through plastic inserts that slide out for easy cleaning and allows one to see if feeder needs refilling.* small holes in bottom of feeder for drainage, in case rain gets into feeder from angle, but the holes are too small for seeds to drop through.  Don't worry, the metal roof overhangs -- the housing -- to keep most rain out, imo.* Easy to fill:  hold down button on top and finial moves up hanging wire/with loop so lid can be lifted and seed poured in.* good sized, rounded metal stands are just the right size for little song and medium sized birds like Cardinals and Morning Doves.  There are four feeding bays.*  decorative, as well as functional.  ( may create a bit of "neighbor-envy", if ya know what I mean ) :)I find the Perky-Pet 363 Birds and Berries Lantern Feeder to be everything I look for, in a bird feeder -- and the birds flock to it!  *Will upload photos later*Does the Perky-Pet 363 Birds and Berries Lantern Feeder sound like what you may be looking for? :)  Would make a Fantastic gift!  Highly Recommended!  --Katharena Eiermann, 2012

There are several reasons why I like this bird feeder: first, it is very attractive. I love the finish and design of it as it closely matches the exterior door lights on my home. It hangs on a black hook so that everything looks as though they belong together. I also like the outline of the cardinal on the sides, one of my favorite birds. Another reason why I like it is that for some reason, aside from keeping squirrels out, it also keeps deer out. I have two other feeders near this one and the deer always manage to get into the other feeders but not this one. And yet the openings for feeding seem easier to access to me than the others.Usually it takes quite a while for birds to find a newly introduced feeder, but my backyard birds found it right away. Even now as I type there is a wren and a sparrow feeding out of it. If you're looking for a bird feeder that is effective and attractive, this is a good choice.

This is by far the nicest bird feeder I have ever owned, hands down. It came packaged very well and not a scratch on it ! The black bird on all 4 panes is a nice plus and the panes slide out easily for cleaning. It's not heavy, but it has a nice weight to it and it hangs straight from the tree branch.I hung the bird feeder from a leafy tree (see photo) so the metal would not get too hot and burn their feet while they perched; I think leaving it in full sun would be harmful to dainty feet. It's such a lovely design and it looks beautiful, it would make a fabulous gift for anyone who loves nature and appreciates the entertainment which birds give us. Highly recommended !

I have this feeder hanging about 6 feet away from a cylinder-type feeder, and, judging by how fast the seed disappears, the birds seem to like it better. Because the shape is wide, when you lift the top off to fill it, you can pour directly from a bag of seed, without needing a scoop. The side panels slide out for cleaning. The holes the birds feed from are a bit larger than on most other feeders, so you need to pour a bit slowly if you don't want a lot of seed spilling out. Like most feeders, this one is not squirrel-proof. However, you could easily add one of those dome-shaped baffles to the top of it. As for aesthetics, the lantern shape and black cardinal decorations on the side panels make it very attractive.

reviewerName: Lettetia "As Long As I Am Able To Read, I Sha...
reviewText: Perky-Pet 363 Birds and Berries Lantern Feeder is a well constructed and attractive accent to your porch or garden.  "U" shaped perches and easy access to seed make this a favorite for my family.  The style is sleek and contemporary is an aged brownish metal finish.  While the smaller birds in our area [finches, snowbirds, etc. have easy access to feed, the pesky "bird feeder robbers" [jays and black birds] cannot get to the seed.  I am very impressed and will be ordering more for friends and family.
summary: Very attractive and excellent for small birds

reviewText: Thebird feederI bought in 2009 is rusting and looks terrible.  Plus, rainwater collects in the base which sours and ferments the contained bird seed.  While it looked nice out of the box, the old bird feeder was problematic and failed to live up to my expectations.  When I saw the Perky-Pet birds and berries lantern feeder offered, I jumped at a chance for anything better.The Perky-Pet birds and berries lantern feeder, made in China, is largely constructed of powder coated metal in a traditional four-sided lantern style.  Each side includes a transparent scratch resistant plastic panel with a screen printed bird and berries design, and a small U shaped perch.  The center of the base is raised with drain holes at the lower corners which keeps rain exposure to a minimum and allows the seed to move towards the small access openings.  A short metal cable runs through the center of the feeder, allowing the top to stay securely in place.  Adding seed requires pressing a button to release the tension and allow the lid to slide up the cable.  Fill with seed and press the button again to secure the top back into place.While the screen printed design is okay, I would prefer it be less noticeable or not even there.  This is a style preference, and I can see where others would prefer the screen print as is.  However, to me it's a distraction.  Otherwise, the construction and look of this lantern style bird feeder is pleasing.It has rained a couple times since I put the bird feeder out, although we haven't had a downpour or major storm yet.  So far, the contained seed has stayed dry and remained usable.  It appears the design of the Perky-Pet bird feeder protects the contents much better.I've yet to see a squirrel get into the food, nor have I seen a bird eat any either.  The branch I hung the old feeder on has been removed, so the Perky-Pet bird feeder is in a new location. It took awhile for the birds to find the older bird feeder, and I figure it's the same scenario with this one.The Perky-Pet lantern style bird feeder is a huge improvement over the older bird feeder I bought.  Only time will tell if this bird feeder will stand up to the weather.  If you're looking for an attractive bird feeder to feed birds and not squirrels with, then the Perky-Pet birds and berries lantern feeder is worthy of consideration.PROS:Traditional lantern designU shaped perchesHolds up to 5-pounds of seedSure-Lock cap system keeps squirrels outCONS:Screen printed design too much for me
summary: 30 Helens Agree, Birds Prefer U-Shaped Perches: A Perky-Pet 363 Birds and Berries Lantern Feeder Review

reviewText: Really like this--it mostly keeps the squirrels out, but those pesky critters hang on to the feeder with one claw and manage to scarf down as much as they like.  Oh, well.  The birds love it, and it looks lovely hanging in our back yard.  Easy to fill and re-fill.

This birdfeeder is sturdy, attractive, and easy to fill. It also looks like cleaning it is a snap, and the perches are the type preferred by a lot of our Midwestern songbirds. The trick will be keeping the squirrels away from the goods, but we're always working on that here in Chicago.We've had it up for a few days now, and at first we thought the cardinal silhouettes might keep birds away. But they seem to be attractants--"Hey, it looks like that's a popular feeder!"--and we've seen a number of birds coming in to feed. I had hoped this would let me actually see more species in my yard, and it has, although as usual the house sparrows try to monopolize the feeder.Our yard is small and almost every location for the feeder also makes it accessible to the above-mentioned squirrels, which are as agile as the Flying Wallendas, but I guess we'll just have to live with that. If I can figure out another location in the yard that would be bird-but-not-rodent friendly, I would install another one of these feeders.(I added this part to my original review: We figured out how to hang this  so that it's really inconvenient to the squirrels, and I have seen a LOT of different species in my yard...birds I'd only seen once or twice in my life. It's really cool. Also, one morning I heard a racket in the yard, and there was a flock of THOUSANDS of starlings--around the feeder, on the lawn, the deck, the garage, the mew, the neighbor's garage...it was very Hitchcockian. I think they were migrating through and all descended at once. Wow.)
summary: This will have them flocking to your yard!

reviewText: My wife loves to feed the birds and one of her greatest pleasures is seeing a variety of birds come and go. I am always on the lookout for bird feeders that will make her hobby that much more enjoyable so I was interested in trying the Perky Pet 363 Birds and Berries Lantern Feeder. Although it is an attractive feeder it does not suit our needs, the problem being wind.This is an attractive little feeder that at a minimum makes a lovely decorative addition to the yard. The silhouette of a cardinal on the clear plastic wall is not gaudy but actually adds to the appearance of an otherwise rustic-looking lantern style.Filling this feeder is simple and easy.Emptying the feeder is easy too - hang it in a windy area and the seed blows out relatively quickly. The problem is that the hole through which the birds can get to the seed is too wide and as a result the wind can easily disturb the seed within. This is an unfortunate issue. More of a concern, though, is that smaller birds such as chickadees might be able to squeeze into the feeder through the same hole.A creative and industrious person could certainly make an adjustment with some well-placed plastic and a little tape to narrow down the opening. However, this should not be a necessary step just to make this feeder keep its seed. In calm areas where there is little wind, this is actually a nice feeder that attracts the birds. In windier areas, though, it's better suited as a decorative element.
summary: Not Suitable for Open, Windy Areas

reviewText: I have been looking for a bird feeder that would look OK hanging in a front window on the front of our house.  This one fits the bill perfectly.  It is of high quality (real metal, not plastic, real glass).  I'm not certain, but I think the painted bird may be the reason that the birds in our neighborhood tend to flock to this feeder more often than the other feeders I have out.  A very nice gift for a bird watcher.

This feeder is very well constructed. It's easy to refill,even my kids get in on the act.  The bird design on the outside is a nice touch.  We love the perches on the side for the birds to rest on. The holes are just the right size for the seeds and the bird don't seem to scatted them all over the ground.

This is a beautiful bird feeder. It looks great on my front porch. I like the quality of the Perky-Pet products they are functional and yet look really nice. The birds love it and it is great to watch them eat and fly and just hang around because of the feeder. Definitely five stars.

I have been feeding birds a very long time. I've used different feeders - I had one feeder that the squirrels managed to get into and and stay until every seed was eaten. It doesn't appear the squirrels can get into this feeder.It's a cute feeder, but I'm not sure how tough it is. The feeder has glass sides and I am a little concerned about possibly breaking the glass. Or having some inclement weather cause the glass to break (powerful winds could knock it down or cause something to hit the glass). But so far it has survived me, so that's good.It's easy to install and easy to take care of. I'm not sure of the birds' response to the feeder yet as it's only been up one day. I think the smaller birds will really like it, it seems geared to smaller birds. But don't worry, the bigger birds won't go starve - I have another feeding station set up.I do recommend this feeder, especially if you have many small birds to feed. It's just I'm not too fond of the glass sides._enjoy_

This is a great birdfeeder!  It looks really stylish and expensive and it's very well made.  The lid lifts off for easy filling and it holds a lot of seed so that it doesn't have to be filled very often.  There are nice little perches for the birds to stand while eating and the amount that comes out is pretty much perfect.  I really like this a lot!

This adorable lantern is just the thing to have on the patio or garden -- except, without a tray, most of the seed ends up on the ground where few. if any, birds will stop to pick it up.  Here's my take on the Perky-Pet Birds and Berries Lantern Feeder:PROS:1.  This feeder is well-constructed with metal frame, top, and perches.  The sides are clear plastic imprinted with birds, but it's easy to see the seeds through the plastic.2.  The top is secured by a stretchy gizmo that holds it in place.CONS:1.  The design is such that pouring seeds in the feeder results in seeds all over the kitchen because the feeds on the bottom edge of the feeder are open -- to the weather, to the wind, and to the floor as well as to the birds.  A good shake from wind will send seeds flying, and not to the birds.2.  The metal perches are cute, but they get VERY HOT in the summer sun.  What bird wants to burn her feet?3.  The lack of a tray around the bottom edge of the feeder will discourage the squirrel from sharing the bounty, but it also discourages the birds.  Although the feeder has been up three days, I have yet to see a bird enjoying it.OVERALL:Although this is a sturdy feeder that will probably last and last, I would not choose it again.Three Stars!
summary: Cute Feeder, But Designed to Feed the Ground More than the Birds

reviewText: The first thing I noticed when I took this feeder out of its packing is that it's fairly heavy and quite sturdy. It's also somewhat elegant looking.Filling the feeder, I was surprised at how little bird seed was spilled. When I filled up the feeder (with wild bird seed), only a few dozen seeds fell out. (I should add that in order to remove the top, you have to squeeze a button on the cord. I'm not sure why that's there since I've never had problems with similarly styled feeders without the button, but I suppose the top will stay more secure. Perhaps this point is of concern to people who have squirrels that steel from feeders.) I'm used to losing much more than that from my other feeder. Then I hung the feeder under the eave of a porch and watched to see what would happen. The regular feeder stayed up, about three feet away.The birds favor the old feeder by about a two-to-one ratio (based on the amount of seed they have eaten). There are a few possible reasons for this preference. The first is that they're simply used to the old feeder. Another is that the old feeder (which is about the same size) has a ledge all the way around it, allowing multiple birds to alight on one side. I've seen as many as seven birds there. The new one, as the picture shows, has only a single bar on each side, allowing a maximum of four birds. The third possibility is simply that it took the birds a little while to figure out that the new feeder is indeed a feeder.The end result, though, is that they use it well. I do have two concerns about the feeder, though. The first is that it is, even without the seed, rather heavy, and it needs a sturdy support. My porch is sturdy, but if I were to try to hang this from a tree, I might have problems if I could not access a strong branch. The second concern is that the birds' access to seeds seems to have the potential to serve as a trap. When a feeder runs low, birds get greedy, and I've had to rescue one bird that got its head caught in an old feeder (one that is no longer in use, and the bird was fine since I discovered it soon after its predicament arose). This one appears to have that potential, and I shall have to keep a close eye on it, at least for a while.If my fear materializes, I will update this review.
summary: A sturdy and generally quite nice bird feeder

reviewText: EDIT: Okay, it took two months for the birds to really notice this feeder, but now it's their preferred feeder in my yard. I've got this one, a mealworm feeder, and I had one of those seed blocks as well, and the birds basically just ignore everything else and go just for this. Granted, they're all different food types, but I've had no real hits on the mealworm feeder and the seed block was pretty much ignored, whereas this feeder with black oil sunflower seeds is now a huge hit. Since "the awakening" when they finally all noticed it was there I have observed the following species actually feeding from this feeder (I have only stocked it with black oil sunflower seeds): house finch, pine siskin, lesser goldfinch, white-crowned sparrow, song sparrow, dark-eyed junco, western scrub-jay (poking around on the ground looking for fallen seed), and mourning dove, and have observed tons more birds in my yard though not at the feeder at least when I've been looking.Now that I can give a proper review of this feeder, here are some pros and cons:Pros-Easy to fill, just pull back the lid and pour the seed into the top! :-P-Easy to hang, just push the lid all the way down so that the clamp on top tightens around the cord, and you're good to go-Easy to disassemble, just pull back the lid and pull the plastic panels straight out through the top and you can individually clean themCons-Seed has a tendency to get stuck in the corners when it gets low, where it is very difficult for birds to reach-I wish the top were actually removable, as it would make it even easier to clean the metal part if I weren't trying to maneuver around the lid-Cleaning can be a pain sometimes (because of the non-removable lid) but it's not that bad-I wish this had some kind of catch tray on the outside between the perch and the actual food. It varies, but sometimes I can put seed in here and it'll last for several days; other times I put seed in here and it lasts for less than a day. Where has all the seed gone? On the ground below, where the birds just hop around eating it. I just have a feeling that if there were at least a tray on the outside there would be less seed falling everywhere as the birds eat out of the feeder, and it might slow down the emptying process.Note: Please be aware of your obligations if you decide to take up bird feeding and get this (or another) feeder. Unless you are in an area with extreme weather and therefore few areas with suitable forage, then it's probably not necessary to constantly maintain a steady supply of seed. In normal circumstances birds probably know other areas they can feed if they aren't getting new seed from you right away. HOWEVER, it is important for you to make sure that your feeder(s) remains clean and that you periodically clean up the hulls or leftover seed on the ground underneath so as to reduce the risk of transmitting diseases, especially after a rain or a series of foggy days when seed may have a higher chance of molding and going bad. Additionally, be aware that high amounts of bird activity may draw predators into your yard. Since the birds started really going crazy over this feeder I have observed not just the neighbor's cat sitting underneath the feeder in my yard, but I also came home one day to find a Cooper's hawk sitting in my yard in front of the feeder as well. While I was thrilled to find the hawk in my yard, you do need to be aware that songbirds are food for larger animals, and you may get these animals coming into your yard if they see or hear all the activity.ORIGINAL REVIEW: I've got a ton of bird activity in the area surrounding my house, and I really expected them to flock to this feeder. I stocked it with black oil sunflower seed but unfortunately after several weeks I've got no activity whatsoever. I know the seed is fine because I've also spread it on the ground and have found that it gets eaten, but the seed in the feeder is completely ignored. Another reviewer suggested that maybe the birds that are on every side of the feeder are deterring other birds from coming closer, and that could be the case. For now I'll have to rate this down, but since I can't be conclusive I'll leave it at 3 stars.

This feeder is well built, looks great, and is easy to hang up and also refill.  So far, I haven't seen any Squirrels getting to it, and it's too small for the big birds to clean out.  Well worth the money.

The feeder is well constructed, and looks like it will be pretty durable. Arrived well packaged, assembled, and ready to use. A small loop of stranded cable that goes through the lid and attaches to the bottom of the feeder makes up the hanging mechanism. I hung it from a tree branch with some baling wire. The feeder is fairly easy to fill while it is hanging up, but I deducted one star because it would be much easier to fill if the hanging cable was an inch or two longer. To fill, you squeeze a spring clasp and pull the lid straight up; the lid then hangs on the cable about two inches above the top of the base. The limited amount of travel makes it somewhat difficult to fill from a bag, but one can just use a scoop or cup to fill instead. The feeder holds about 4 cups of food. The birds like it very much, and we have had many chickadees. It looks very nice hanging in my yard. Overall, would buy again.As the fall continues, more and more birds use the feeder. I have to refill it every other day, which is impressive because it holds about 3-4 lbs of food. The birds love it.
This feeder is easy to open and fill even when still on the tree. The birds seem to like it. It was a little weird to hang though. It is pretty and elegant.
This birdfeeder is large, and so detailed, I love it. Has room for four birds if they cooperate, lol. Very pretty for your flower garden or to hang on a tree. Love this thing!

The Perky-Pet 363 Birds and Berries Lantern Feeder is easy to assemble and use.Pros:  Attractive.Holds five pounds of seed.Has four easy-to-grip 'U' shaped feeding stations.Sliding lock on cap keeps 'varmints' out.Fairly wind and rain proof.The clear sides make it possible to see the seed levels.Cons:  The sides are plastic.  Heavy glass panels would have been both squirrel proof and would have withstood the sun better.  The plastic sides lower the value and lasting quality of the feeder.We live on a hill top in Tennessee where the wind-driven rains can be pounding and raccoons raid our bird feeders at will.  So far the Perky-Pet feeder has stood up to the challenges of keeping the seed dry and fairly safe from non-bird predators.  But I'm sure that come winter, a hungry critter is going to eat through that plastic and dine on the birds' seeds.  I wouldn't mind that, but it will make the feeder useless.The bottom line: An attractive commodious feeder best used in an area safe from predators and the sun.  For other locations, think twice.

I tried using this as a bird feeder but I have the smartest squirrels on the upper East Coast.  Darn things got right into the food and cleaned it out in one day.  The birds enjoyed what they got of it.  I was watching a Titmouse and Finch and they had no problems getting the food out like some of the other feeders I've had in the past.  This has a nice opening for them to get to and it keeps the rain out.Loading the feeder was a breeze as the top slides up a cable and back down when you are finished filling.  The perches are an excellent size and they are metal like the rest of the framing.  I was hoping their would be glass to view throught but it is plastic painted with a cardinal on it.The weight of the feeder is a nice size so that it doesn't toss around in the wind as easily which I like since I love taking photos of my visitors.  I would have to say though that my best experience with this feeder is that I put some Halloween lights in it after trying it out as a feeder and I really like it better as a hanging light on my front porch.  I will be able to change the lights with the seasons and this is just enough so that you don't have a really bright light but just a little something so you can see where you're going.I have posted to pictures of how the feeder looks with the Halloween lights in it.  It's so much nicer than the photos but at least you can see what I am talking about.  It will be a nice fixture for quite some time for me.

Feeding the birds and *not* feeding the squirrels is always a challenge, so I decided to put the Perky-Pet 363 Birds and Berries Lantern Feeder from the Amazon Vine review program through the test.  I'm happy to say that it passed with flying colors.The design of the feeder makes it quick and easy to load seed of any size.  The locking mechanism has (so far) stood up against the attacks of the tree rats, so that's a good sign.  The perch size seems to attract the smaller birds quite readily, as the placement of the tray and perch works well for them.  It's attractive and blends into the outdoor decor, so it's not a glaring eyesore like some novelty feeders can be.  It's sturdy, easy to hang, and easy to clean when necessary... in short, it's perfect for what I wanted it for.The only thing I can't comment on is how it will hold up over time and weather.  But so far, this bird feeder is a great addition to the local dining options for my feathered friends, and I wouldn't hesitate to open "new locations" using the same model throughout the backyard.Disclosure:Obtained From: Amazon Vine Review ProgramPayment: Free
summary: The birds and I both love it.  The squirrels aren't very happy, however...

reviewText: The Perky-Pet lantern feeder is very attractive. Made with a black powder coated finish, and plastic with detailed screen-printed designs of birds and berries on all four sides, this feeder will not only attract birds, but bird-watchers as well.The bird feeder features a squeeze and pull lock on the cap to keep pests out. It holds up to 5 lbs. of seed and has four feeding stations with U-shaped perches. The feeder comes with a wire and loop so that it's ready to immediately hang and use once you bring it home.The look and design of this feeder will accent any home, deck, or garden.
summary: This Feeder will Make a Beautiful Addition to Your Home or Garden

reviewText: There are many people that actually hate birds and will do what they can to keep them away from their balconies; that is what I have come across in my neighborhood.  One neighbor scatters rice while another actually has thread with needles at the end that precariously sway in the wind.  If only I could reach the lines and cut them down, but I digress... I personally love all birds; even the NYC pigeons.  We have a lot that frequent the area and live on the roof.  I have tried coaxing them over but I believe my dog's barking keeps them at bay or they might just be too polite!When this bird feeder became available I readily snatched it up.  It is a very handsome bird feeder!  I love the matte black finish and decorative styling on the plastic panels.  The plastic panels is what I absolutely hate!  I really do wish that the plastic was a lightweight glass instead.  The glass panels would weather so much better after a couple of seasons and sitting in the sun all day.  Not to mention how disgusting plastic becomes after a while.  The ledges where the birds stand to feed are U-shaped and rather large.  I also found the openings to be a bit large where seed does fall out a bit too readily for my liking.  I have had a few sparrows, but not many more takers.  I have not come across any squirrels on my balcony so I cannot remark on it's rodent-proofness.  When I first opened the feeder I did have a bit of an issue replacing the top properly.  It hangs wonderfully, but I am afraid that when storms hit we will probably lose a lot of seed.Highly recommend if you are in the market for an attractive lantern style bird feeder where you need a bigger than conventional opening.  It will be a lovely addition to any home where you can spend hours just watching our feathered winged friends.

This is really a gorgeous fire tub.  I've received compliments on it from everyone who has seen it, and the copper glow is striking with or without a fire.  The assembly was very easy, just fastening the legs to the base and the handle to the spark guard, then stacking the parts together: base, tub, grate, screen.The vinyl cover fits well and thoroughly protects the tub and spark guard.  We had torrential rain the day after I placed this outside, and it was perfectly dry when I removed the cover the following day.  The cover also serves to disguise the tub so that a casual passer-by will not observe that it's made of high-value (high-theft-temptation) copper.I look forward to enjoying this fire tub for a long time and if, as predicted by some, it ends up as a planter, it will fill that purpose beautifully, as well.

This Fire Tub is simply beautiful. It is 100% copper it is not too large but not too small (26"w  23"h with spark guard cover and the height without spark cover is 14 1/2"). It looks very nice in our deck. Even if we never used it to burn wood in it, just by itself is a beautiful decorative accent.Please keep in mind that this tub is all metal and when you burn wood or charcoal the entire thing gets really hot. So keep your distance and use some type of glove if you have to remove the spark cover to add more charcoal or wood.

This fire pit looks great. I was afraid of the way the copper would look over time but it only gets prettier. It's simple but attractive.It does require some assembly, but nothing too difficult. The only issue is that it says to put sand in the bottom to distribute the heat more evenly but there is a hole in the bottom to allow the fire pit to drain so we were concerned the sand would just fall through. We skipped that step and it still works great. We've considered filling in the hole because we keep it covered anyway, but decided not to because it seems to work fine without the sand.We have the fire pit on our pool deck and it looks great. It is the perfect size. It comes with a poker/lid remover and a vinyl cover. The vinyl cover is good quality. The lid of fire pit really does do a great job of preventing sparks. Overall this is a great fire pit.

This fire tub has been a beautiful addition to our back porch! It has a textured finish that really adds to its beauty. At first, I didn't really understand the high price, but my husband informed me how expensive copper is right now. So, that explains it. This tub is 100% copper. If you're wanting a copper fire tub, I don't hesitate to recommend this one. If copper isn't that important to you, there are cheaper options.This one comes with a spark guard cover, and a vinyl cover for when you aren't using it. We've only used it once so far, since the weather is SO hot right now. As it cools off, we plan on using it a great deal more. We are extremely pleased with it so far, though! No complaints at all!

Nice looking addition to the backyard even without a fire in it.Good size for a cozy fire for two with usable inside dimensions of 23" x 6" if you discount for the 2" tall steel grate to hold the wood off the bottom, then you have another 6" in the screen lid (center) above the copper pit.. of course this slopes down to meet the copper so stack of wood is limited by the lid when used.  Large enough to enjoy a nice low fire...The stand is welded mild steel (not wrought iron) and requires assembly, but only takes about 15 mins to put together with supplied bolts in the threaded holes.  A hex wrench is included.Comes with steel hooked fork with insulated handle to lift the lid when it's hotBottom of copper pot is 7" off the ground so be aware of what you are setting it on to have a fire.  The instructions tell you to put at least one inch of sand in the bottom to help insulate the heat, and then there is a grate supplied to hold the burning wood off the copper by about 2"  There are air vents drilled in the bottom so you will get some sand running out at times I suspect.While this is a nice looking copper pot, I really don't think it's hand formed but might be hand hammered after being stamped to shape to give a nice hand wrought look about it.  Detail on the upper lip is die formed for sure but still looks pretty good.Copper thickness used is about 16 MIL or .016 inches thick (26 gauge) but is strengthened by the hammering ridges to hold it's shape.They approve the use of wood, self lighting fire logs or charcoal in this but in my opinion, I would not want to get the copper over heated if you want it around a long time, best used for the flicker of flames rather than for any heat produced.Comes with a rubber lined nylon cover with heavy elastic band on open end to keep it in place.Hard to say if it's worth the high MSRP as that is something each buyer must determine for themselves.  Copper prices are way up at this point in time, CobraCo also makes a full range of steel fire pits at lower prices.My only negative note is that on this one, the steel lid does not fit into the copper tub and is just a bit too large to fit down in the ledge formed in the copper...Being copper also makes you wonder how visible you want this to be if left outside, seeing as how they steal every kind of valuable metal they can find these days... just a thought.Please don't be a victum of carbon monoxide poisoning, only use outdoors
summary: A nice look and feel for the backyard or patio... (non combustible surface)

reviewText: We live in a very windy are of Colorado and my first concern was that this thing would never withstand the 50 mph gusts we get in our backyard... I was wrong! After a very nasty windstorm this grill with cover stayed in place on our patio. No movement from its original spot at all. The copper is beautiful and the iron cover prevents the embers from flying away into our prairie yard. It is just the right size for a small gathering and a beautifully crafted piece of art. The simplicity of the fire tub is part of the beauty. The construction process (you have to assemble the stand) is easy and all of the tools needed are included. The only thing that would make this perfect was if the manufacturers included the required sand for the bottom of the tub.

This is my first fire tub, so I can't speak for its cost worth in comparison to the many lower priced fire pits offered on Amazon. This one seems to be at the higher end of the price spectrum, which I would mostly attribute to the copper (which is on the expensive side at the moment) tub.The fire pit consists of a stand, the copper tub and a metal spark guard. There is also a grate, a poker and a vinyl cover. The tub stand comes in 6 pieces, the four legs and two circular pieces. The tub stand was easily assembled in my living room with 12 screws and the provided, ever present allen wrench. The handle for the spark guard is also assembled using one screw and the allen wrench.The tub is sturdy, but is not so heavy that I can't move it, at least when it's empty. There is no insulation on the tub, so the entire apparatus gets very hot when it is in use. The poker is multi-use and is designed to lift the grate but can also be used to move the wood around inside the tub. The poker does not help with adding wood to the fire; this must be done by hand. The fire pit is not so large, however, that this is a problem.So far I am very happy with this fire pit. It seems sturdy and works well; it is also beautiful. Time will tell how it holds up to use and the elements.

In Michigan bonfires have long been a favorite pastime - spring, summer and fall. A bonfire is always called for on an evening at the lake for Memorial Day, Fourth of July or Labor Day and for quite a few days in-between.In the suburbs you can no longer light bonfires or burn leaves because of anti-pollution ordinance controls. But you can use bonfire tubs with covers and enjoy companionship around the fire at home anytime.  I started out with one of those traditional, taller black tubs but it wasn't that safe for younger children and the height made it harder for them to roast hotdogs or marshmallows for smores.So recently I updated and acquired CobraCo's Vintage 100% Copper Fire Tub. The antique rose copper finish and hand-crafted hammered texture adds beauty to the tub itself. The heavy duty spark guard cover keeps sparks and ash from blowing, making my city ordinance enforcement officer much more comfortable.The tub sits low to the ground so you can safely reach down to roast dogs or marshmallows. The tub comes with a spark guard removal tool which allows you to remove the mesh cover when it is hot.The fire tub is fairly easy to assemble. I did it in 40 minutes; you can do it in 20. Assembly simply involves putting a handle on the mesh spark cover, screwing four legs onto an outer ring and then screwing an inner ring onto the four legs. The tub rest safely and securely on the inner ring.CobraCo's vintage copper fire tub is a safe, sociable means of getting the family away from the TV, laptops and video games and spending some quality time together. CobraCo, however, does not do anything about the corny jokes Grandpa tells around the bonfire - much to my Grandson's dismay.
summary: Beauty and functionality found in Vintage Copper Fire Tub

reviewText: This is a gorgeous deep fire pit. Perfect for gathering around! The pit looks attractive and functions very well. Even after using it a few times the pit still looks nice and is easy to clean up after use. The copper gets a pretty aged look with use and weathering, but it does not take away from the beauty of the pit at all. I like how deep the pit is, it makes for a more substantial fire. The accessories that come with the pit are functional and well made. We have this on a patio surrounded by chairs and we tend to gather around it even when it's not in use. An excellent find!

This fire tub is very beautiful, even when not in use. The pictures do not do it justice. The design is nice and the construction is solid.Fire tubs are not difficult to use. You put in the kindling and wood, and light it. It obviously gets very hot, so you need to keep young children away. The spark guard works well. There are a lot of un-burnt pieces left after the fire goes out. I don't think this is a problem specific to this tub. It comes with a cover, but it looks better without the cover on. It does collect water in the rain if you don't use the cover. Don't let it fill with water when there are ashes - it makes a mess and it is hard to dump the water when it's full of ashes.I'm hoping it will weather nicely.
summary: This fire tub is very beautiful

reviewText: I was SUPER excited about this fire pit! When it came it was fairly easy to assemble-only took about 10 mins or so with no reading of the directions needed! The grate on top is a nice black color, so as you use it, it maintains the same color.  The texture of the bowl is very nice (a pounded look) and there is a beautiful decorative pattern around the top edge of the bowl as well! It also comes with a weatherproof cover so you can keep it looking nice.One of the MAJOR problems, however, is the copper bowl turned completely  silver/gray after the very first use.  I thought maybe it would turn back after it cooled, but it did not, I'm not sure if that's what heat does to copper, but I would say, skip the spendy "all copper" and just go with a steel model for A LOT less money! Copper prices are super high right now and after one use you can't even tell it's really copper anyway! Overall, it's a decent fire pit, but don't pay extra for the copper that only looks nice if you're never actually going to use this for fire!

I like the way this feeder looks and I'm sure I'll get a couple of good years out of it. It's been in my yard only a few days and already birds have been coming in to feed. While this may not be the case for first-time feeders, I have other feeders already, so the birds are quite used to using them.The copper finish is basically a coated steel, so I'm sure in a few years this will not look as good and the connected points of steel will definitely rust over time. The plastic windows which act as feed control are OK, but would have much rather had glass. In my experience, the plastic will break down over time in the sun and I've had this happen with several other feeders. After a few years, it gets crumbly and breaks easily.For 20 dollars, this is not a bad feeder, but not something you should view as long-term. FYI, I have a glass/wood feeder that was the first one I bought and it has lasted for over 20 years.Three stars, a nice looking feeder with some design/manufacturing flaws.

I think any experienced bird feeding hobbyist could take one look at this feeder and realize it is not squirrel proof, so I'm really not rating it on that aspect.  The cap on which the squirrel-proof claim rests has so far kept squirrels from going in through the top, but only because it's easy enough to access the seed from the feeding ports that they haven't bothered to try lifting the lid.  They can only get a little bit at a time, but my squirrels are oh-so patient and are content taking as long as necessary to empty a feeder.However, I have a more accessible hopper style feeder nearby of which the squirrels are big fans, so I am able to use this one with a fair amount of success.  The birds really do seem to like the U-shaped perches better than the straight perches on my actually squirrel-proof feeders (Brome 1024 Squirrel Buster Plusand Brome's similar peanut feeder), and this feeder is hands-down more attractive.  For twenty bucks it is not, of course, actually made of antique copper, but it does give the appearance and is a pretty yard decoration.  Time will tell whether the copper finish will age nicely, and I have low expectations for the plastic windows which, in my experience, take about one season to become scratched and cloudy.  For now, though, I am enjoying this feeder a lot and the price is reasonable enough that it won't break my heart if it doesn't hold its looks for multiple seasons.  It is sturdy and I expect it will continue to work, so I'll just move it to a less visible spot in the yard if that happens.

I love watching the birds on my patio eating from this bird feeder. Even when the birds aren't around, this feeder looks like a really pretty lantern hanging down. It's easy to use and seems to be quite sturdy.

I love watching the birds (and OK, the squirrels!) in the yard.  This feeder was a very nice addition to the front yard.  It has four feeding docks so several birds can enjoy it at once, and it looks quite nice hanging from a tree.  I like the copper look, though it's a coating and I wonder how long it will last if I leave it out for the birds over the winter.My main issue is the plastic cover for each side.  The instructions say to take it down and clean it often to prevent mold and such in the seed, and I think the panels are meant to slide out for easy cleaning.  For my feeder, this also means quite a bit of hassle and frustration filling it if it's near empty.  The panels slide all over, seed spills out the bottom, and it just doesn't seem very sturdy.  If I'm on the ball and fill it half-way through, the panels are stuck down by the weight of the seed and it works well.  Not sure if this is an issue with just my feeder, i.e. a defective one, of it others have had this problem.Also, this is not a squirrel-proof feeder. I rather like seeing the squirrels, especially when they have to use their ingenuity to break into a feeder, and they had this one down in under two hours.  The knob at the top does not lock firmly, so if they hang from the tree and lift up the lid, enough twisting and prying lifts it enough to grab a paw full of seed.Overall, it's a very nice looking feeder and the birds love it. If not for the weird plastic panels, I'd give it five stars.
summary: Good looking feeder, but not squirrel proof

reviewText: I have all sorts of sparrows, chick-a-dees, purple finches, and juncos landing on the feeder all day.  I have found that the grackles and cardinals are just a hair too large to land on the rungs, so they join the red winged blackbirds and brown headed cow birds on the ground.The feeder is beautiful, and I have it on a Shepards Hook in the backyard.  I suspect in time it will develop an equally beautiful patina.  It seems to be very sturdy, and hangs by a steel cable.No squirrels have tried to raid the feeder as of yet, thank goodness!The picture is a little deceiving as I thought the feeder would be larger.  This is NOT a negative in my opinion, rather it saves me on food costs.  Please read the dimensions carefully.
summary: Beautiful, and the birds LOVED it!

reviewText: We have this hanging on an iron stand with a baffle.  The feeder is easy to fill and holds more seed (2 lbs maybe?) than many feeders.  We get a good variety of birds and are overall satisfied with the purchase.

I hoped that this birdfeeder would not attract larger bird such as starlings and woodpeckers. Generally this has proved true. The bigger birds do occasionally latch on to grab a bite to eat but because it has no collecting plate on the bottom it is extremely hard for them to do so. However the smaller birds can feed freely. I love the copper finish and I'm looking forward to seeing if it will tarnish in the weather. I actually want it to turn green. Time will tell.

The finish is not top notch, with buffed out sections and uneven weld holes.  The plastic is held in place by bendable metal clips.  They are rusting from the inside.  The metal is very thin.  However, it is an inexpensive bird feeder at about $20.  I don't think that it will hold up well to weather, but I will update at a later time.  I am rating it a four star as it is pleasing to the eye and looks quite nice from any distance other than close up, where the flaws can be seen.  I think that it hits its target market pretty nicely.
summary: It is attractive and for the price it is adequate

reviewText: I have received more compliments on this birdfeeder in the short time that I have owned it, than I have on any other feeder, ever.  It is a very sharp looking feeder.  It really stands out.One of the things I like about it is that it holds a lot of food.  The feeder that I replaced was one of those thin long cylinders and I found myself having to refill it every day.  And whenever I was refilling it I happened to notice how much food was lying beneath the feeders.  With this feeder there also seems to be a lot less waste lying underneath it.The chord that it hangs from is a very durable and thick wire; I don't see it breaking very soon.  But what I like the most is the fact that it seems to deter the gluttonous grackles, starlings and various other piggy black birds.  They swoop in too hard and heavy and it sets the feeder spinning - those birds fly off!!I will be purchasing this feeder for the bird lovers in my life - it's a great feeder.Cherise Everhard, May 2013

I received the most wonderful antique copper bird feeder in my mail delivery today...it was from Amazon!!  I live in a wooded area on a lake and have many birds come to my feeders.  The cardinals and blue jays seem especially attracted to this four-station feeder at this time.  The feeder is so easy to fill and lock down...it looks so special in my forested area and I am so pleased to be able to view it from three windows!  You need to get yourself one of these beauties for your feathered friends who come to visit.  Amazon has them at best price and fast shipping.Perky-Pet 365 Antique Copper Lantern Feeder

This is really nice.  I received it already put together (although it is pretty basic).  I did find one of the plastic windows were not in their all the way (probably popped out in shipping).  This is really nice and looks great!  I filled it up with the economy bag of bird seed at Walmart (which makes it pretty heavy) and after the initial "bounce out -- the stuff hitting the bottom of the feeder and bouncing out of the holes; could have avoided this using a cup and not trying to pour straight from a 20 pound bag" it did not lose any seed, it is heavy where the wind will not shake it that much, but even with me swinging it slightly it did not lose any seed (and the economy bag is mostly that little seed with a few sunflower seeds).  I like the top of the bird feeder, where the lid can clamps to the metal hanger and allows it to stay open while hanging, and the metal hanger is nice and means no tear from weather in the future!In the end this is a nice bird feeder, it is a beautiful copper metal hanger with thick plastic windows and a nice perch for birds and the opening holds in my economy bird feed from Walmart without losing any.  The metal hanger is nice and adds to the high quality of this product.  I really like this and hope to attract some nice Cardinals and Blue Jays to my yard with this!--Just to note, this thing holds a lot of seed (5 pounds) and my old hook was not strong enough for it (pulled it down a bit), so you will need a pretty sturdy holder or a hanger on a pole or something.  --Just a note, if you are like me going from a seed bell to a feeder, that you will need a strong support!
summary: Looks great and easy to fill

reviewText: The bird feeder came unassembled in an Amazon box in several pieces with no box or assembly instructions.  This could be because it is a vine shipment, because multi-packs are always deboxed and split up.  Maybe it was deboxed out of habit.  My rating does not reflect the lack of box or disassembly.All but 1 plate was unattached.  It was fairly easy to see how to reattach them, but awkward for large hands. There are 3 bendy clips along each metal corner to hold the plastic face plates in.  They are a little stronger than 1940's Manila Envelope metal clips, but not much.  All of mine were welded on and already covered with rust.  And they want you to wash this with soapy water every 2 weeks. I would assume this will cause it to self destruct within the year.The copper veneer is nice looking, but thin.  It may not stand up well to weather.  There is no detailed screen printed design of birds and berries on all four sides of this feeder!  Look at the first picture.  This is what mine looks like.  The sure lock squirrel proof cap lock does not work on mine.  It barely makes a difference on how fast you can raise the lid whether or not you press the button.This makes a good Squirrel & Bird feeder & seed shaker.  But this is not what it is advertised for.  As a Squirrel proof, small bird, outdoor feeder, I can only give it 2 stars.

This is a bit pricier than the bird feeder I threw away, but it's very well made and attractive.  The copper appearance is very sharp, loading seed into the feeder is very easy, and it's solid, leaving no doubt that it's going to hang fully loaded even in windy weather.  And if it fell, I think it would withstand that fall nicely.Birds have had no trouble enjoying the feeder, and it's a classy addition to my backyard pergola.I highly recommend this and am strongly considering buying a matching extra because it's a pretty good value.
summary: The best bird feeder I've had

reviewText: We live in the mountains, and I love bird watching.  We have over 7 acres of land, and a few birdhouses and bird feeders, already.  When I saw this item, I was excited to try this out.  I set up this feeder on a Shepherd hook in the yard.  I like the ease of opening this particular feeder.  With feed it is stable and stays secure.  As it empties it tends to swing more in the wind.The construction is a copper finish on anodized aluminum.  I like that plastic comprises the windows but I wish it were fiberglass or tempered glass which would be more durable over time.  Filling can be messy and I found it best to fill it right next to the hook.Overall, I'm pleased with having another stylish feeder.  I'm even more pleased with the birds getting fed during the Spring.Two thumbs up!
summary: Classic styling for a bird feeder

reviewText: This is an adorable bird feeder. I love the antique cooper. It looks great in my backyard. The birds also seem to like it. Perfect for your bird feeder needs.

While it's painted to look like copper it is not .I really wish it were real copper.It spins freely in the wind, so far squirrels have not figured out how to hold on and eat out of it. Perches on each side, after heavy rainstorm, seed is damp yet birds are still eating. Was easy to fill but I had to place a bird bath under it to catch the falling seed, birds push seed out while picking through it and it falls out sometimes from just the wind.

Looks to be good quality and really stylish. It looks so nice that I've decided not to hang it out where it can get rained on but to put it on the porch and let the birds come to me. (I know there's going to be a mess eventually but it's really nice looking and I hate to see it get dirty and yucky looking too quick.) It's made so that squirrels can't get into it which has been a real problem with our other bird feeders. Even the deer have jumped up to those and knocked the seed out of them, but the squirrels are the worse. They swing back and forth on the other one like they are doing acrobatics. With this one, only the birds can feed from it. A nice, quality product.

Perky-Pet 365 Antique Copper Lantern Feederas the poet e. e. cummings once said:  I would rather learn from one bird how to sing than to teach 10,000 stars how not to dance.Among other things, I'm a nature photographer and avid bird watcher.  Wild birds need clean water, a bit of shelter and food -- it's that simple. :)  I've gone through my share of bird feeders, over the past 11 years -- some good, some bad.  They are not all alike!Perky-Pet 365 Antique Copper Lantern Feeder is impressive, right off the bat!a few things I really like about the Perky-Pet 365 Antique Copper Lantern Feeder, other than it comes in one of my favorite colors -- copper:* good sized feeder, holds up to 5lbs  of seed.  ( hint:  My own observation:  a huge variety of birds seem to love black oil sunflower seeds ).* sturdy metal housing with see through plastic inserts that slide out for easy cleaning and allows one to see if feeder needs refilling.* small holes in bottom of feeder for drainage, in case rain gets into feeder from angle, but the holes are too small for seeds to drop through.  Don't worry, the metal roof overhangs -- the housing -- to keep most rain out, imo.* hold down button on top and finial moves up hanging wire/with loop so lid can be lifted and seed poured in.* good sized, rounded metal stands are just the right size for little song and medium sized birds like Cardinals, Blue Jays and Morning Doves to stand on, while eating.* decorative, as well as functional.  ( may create a bit of "neighbor-envy", if ya know what I mean ) :)I find the Perky-Pet 365 Antique Copper Lantern Feeder to be everything I look for, in a feeder -- and the birds flock to it!  *Will upload photos later*Does the Perky-Pet 365 Antique Copper Lantern Feeder sound like what you may be looking for? :)  Would make a Fantastic gift!  Highly Recommended!  --Katharena Eiermann, 2013

This "copper" colored/finished metal bird feeder is very nice looking.  I like that it is a moderate size(8 x 10") but holds a lot of seed(5 lbs).  The interior is made nicely with a piece that is at an angle and funnels the seed towards the openings.  It also has four drainage holes.  It has a nice cable lock down that secures the lid well and the bird perches are metal and attractive. Each see-through side is made of hard plastic.  In the sun, the plastic ends up cracking but it takes a few years for that.I don't like the cable that it hangs from that is a pewter color and doesn't match the copper.  The cable is just looped to hang from.  I think they could have made it at least match.I also just noticed that it is already rusting on the bottom after two days of rain!  Guess the didn't take the time to seal the bottom where water drips off!Although I am not happy about a few thins, if you are going for a nice, expensive look, this is your bird feeder.  It really is attractive if you like the copper color and it works well.
summary: Nice Looking~Holds Seed Well~Birds are Happy!

reviewText: I know it if for the birds, but considering how the squirrels keep lining up to gorge like this is their own personal gumball dispenser, maybe a better name would be "Perky-Pest Antique Copper Lantern Feeder." As far as bird feeders go, this one is OK, but nothing special.It is easy to refill and easy to clean, and the various birds we have in our area seem to not mind the fakey copper finish or somewhat cheaply made perches---that is, whenever they can get a turn from the every present squirrels (and our Aussies do a good job chasing off the pests when they are in the backyard).Still, I keep thinking that I would rather spend my money on a USA made feeder from a smaller company or craftsman rather than support the proliferation of yet more imported goods made from who knows what. It works fine, but I won't be filling up the branches and shepherd hooks with Perky Pet products. Here is what one online retailer says about this outfit: "Perky Pet Products had a long history in Denver, where they started out. However, they made low end products that all the big outlets carried at bargain basement prices. Several years ago they moved their operations to China and the quality became even lower."Bottom line: it works but the irony of using a product possibly containing toxins and inferior materials to improve one's backyard enviroment needs to be at least acknowledged. I have to wonder what the real cost of these products are in the grand scheme.
summary: Yes it works fine, but what is the real cost?

reviewText: There are many bird-feeders one the market; multi-tube, squirrel proof, spinning, and in every color and style. But sometimes, just the basics is best.This Perky pet feeder holds about 5lbs of seed, so you don't have to fill it as often. four feeding stations that can handle large or small birds. The top opens far enough to make filling easy and locks in place to keep spills and squirrels at bay. The copper finish is a nice bonus, we will see if it takes on that green finish after a few years, might be nice.

I really like how this antique copper lantern feeder looks, the copper color really makes it stand out.  I also love how easy it is to push a little button and move the top up the string so you can just pour birdseed in.  It is so easy.  This is a nice little bird feeder, that is easy to use, looks nice and is a good value for the price.  I noticed some people wondering if it would make it through winter or bad weather, and it is a bit thin but it is also sturdy.

PROS:-Looks good and is attractive, this copper- like bird feeder is a beautiful addition to any bird lover's backyard.-Looks expensive but is reasonably priced--a good value for the money.-Sturdy, weighing in at 3 lbs and holds 5 lbs of bird seed.-With four perches for birds to stand on, the openings are wide enough for seed to flow easily.-Supposedly squirrel proof, but I have not tested it yet.CONS:-Glass looking panes are actually plastic. It is ultra thin and does not appear durable. I am wondering how this will hold up in the long term.-I am not sure if it can be left out in harsh Northern winter  and whether it will withstand below freezing cold and snow of Michigan, since I feed the birds mostly in the winter, when they need it most.-Aesthetically, it looks really good, but I do not like the silver cord that runs through the feeder and out of the top for hanging. It contrasts with the copper look.-It is not made in America, so if that bothers some folks, then this feeder is not for you.BOTTOMLINE: The feeder looks beautiful and is good value for money.
summary: Attractive & Affordable Feeder But Will It Withstand Harsh Winter

reviewText: The clear panes on each side are made of a heavy plastic.  They lift out individually if needed for cleaning.The top has a very strong twisted wire rope for a hangar. Push the button in on the ball and it will slide along the wire rope, allowing you to lift the lid.  once the lid is back on, slide the ball back to the top and release the button. It will keep the lid in place.The bottom has a raised center with drain holes, which is essential for keeping bird food as fresh as possible.The metal is quite attractive.  This is a very nice feeder, and would make a nice gift!
summary: sturdy and a well thought out design

reviewText: I received this product for free to review from the Amazon Vine program. This birdfeeder is a pretty asset to any backyard. It holds a fair amount of seed, and attracts an ample number of birds. It is a nice looking bronze color that blends in well with our wooden fence and tan and black colored patio furniture.The main problem is that the bird seed spills out pretty easy.  We have two bird feeders in the back yard, and the other feeder stays full a lot longer.  On day one after we put the seed out in this feeder, it was all gone the next day.  At first I thought it was squirrels tilting the feeder from their body weight, so we moved the feeder to a tree branch that made it less accessible to the squirrels.  But my son who is in charge of keeping it filled said that the seed just spills out pretty easy, squirrels or no squirrels, sometimes just from a strong wind or a big bird landing on one side and tilting the feeder.
summary: Attractive Feeder, But Seed Spills Out Easy

reviewText: The Perky-Per birdhouse is a nice birdhouse.  It has a very attractive finish and the clear plastic walls not only allow you to monitor the feed level, but it also adds to the beauty by allowing the colors of the food to be seen.  The U-hook design of each feeding perch allows a single bird to easily stand while feeding.  For the inexpensive price, I think this is a great deal and you won't be disappointed.

I went for the Toro Ultra over the other Toro models because my wife loves to shred leaves for mulch. While the other models do shred leaves this is the only one with metal blades. I've only used this blower/vac for one season, but it has been great.My only complaint is the size of the bag for the vacuum - it fills up after sucking up leaves in a 4'x4' area so I am constantly stopping to dump the shredded leaves.

I'm happy with this overall.  It wasn't all that useful as a vacuum though, at least on the heavy oak and cottonwood leaves I was using it for.  It did mulch them up nicely though. It's pretty heavy-duty and sturdy feeling.  I didn't have any particular trouble with excessive vibration.  I would purchase this again.
summary: It blows better than it sucks.

reviewText: This Toro Electric Blower/Vacuum is perfect for my needs. It's powerful and surely live up to the Toro name. Great price too!

I bought this for the vacuum feature. I have a blower but the leaves just blow back over the yard. This sure beats raking! The bag connector is plastic and my first one arrived broken. I requested just a new bag and a whole new machine arrived in the mail in just a few days. But the machine itself really works great. My second one has not been used yet.
This blower works well, does what I bought it to do. It has good blower power to clean off my patio and driveway.  It does what I bought it to do.
I can verify this is an awsome blower/vacuum.  Very powerful and lightweight.  The one drawback is the noise.  Need ear plugs when using this blower.

GOT TODAY AND WORKS WONDERS ON THE LEAVES AND SMALL TWIGS AND YES IT DOES MAKE SIX BAGS INTO ONE, MULCHES THEM RIGHT UP,  I AM GLAD I FOUNMD THIS/ SHOIPPED AROUND AND FOUND OLDER MODEL.  THE SELLER SHIPS FAST AND THERE WAS NO DELAY,  I THANK YOU AND YES WOULD RECOMMEND THIS TO ALL,  HAVE OVER AN ACRE HERE AND LOTS OF TREES ALSO,

I mainly purchased this product to act as a means of clearing the leaves off of my yard. Before buying this, I raked and raked and raked until I had a huge number of refuse bags full of leaves. I knew there had to be a better way to rid my yard of leaves. The Toro might be the answer, but there are a few things lacking.Note: I've only used the mulcher option, but then again I may decide to only use the mulcher option.The device is fairly easy to assemble and ready to go almost out of the box. It took me about 20 minutes to understand the pictures (bad angles), but I eventually figured things out after some fiddling. Once everything was secured, I was good to go.The mulcher has a dial to change the speed settings. If you don't have it on at least half way, the vacuum seems pretty useless. Right now I'm playing catch up with all the leaves in my yard. It has trouble picking up larger piles of leaves. If there are a few scattered here or there, the machine has a much easier time. This is part of my complaint about it, the sucking power is somewhat lacking. Not to say it lacks total sucking power, but it is not as strong as you would expect. There are times when I had to go over the same spot 3 or more times to grab all the leaves and this was in places where there weren't that many.

I haven't used it on 'suck' mode, but it does great on 'blow' mode.  Plenty of speed, and the variable dial does seem to work, though frankly I'm not sure why I'd ever use it on anything other than MAX.  Has all the parts you'd need and it will allow you to coil your extension cord directly to the blower if you wanted, though I use a reel to manage the cord.The only thing they could do to make it better - give us a little hook to use as a strain relief for the extension cord and prevent any accidental unpluggings.

It does perform as advertised, collects tons of leaves in no time.I have my own theory why grasses around perimeter of the tree always struggles.  Tress wither leaves for many reason, obviously to adapt itself for survival, but I also think by dropping leaves, it hampers the growth of other plant, conserving all nutrient from soil for itself.  Leaves on ground combined with moisture will form a firm barrier to sun light essentially need for photosynthesis process for all plant.  Also, by blocking Sun, it helps to retain constant moisture level, which encourages the growth of fungi and consequently, unwanted fungus will further blocks germination process of other plants.It's all simple process of evolution, come to think of it, but with so much fertilizer applied to trees every spring, they don't need be so greedy; trees and grasses can coexist and thrive, only trees don't seem to realize that, so it's the job of tree grower/planter to remove dead leaves to encourage the growth of the grass around the tree.  I understood this natural process, however, removing leaves, tons of them every week, with rake is pose to be a serious challenge, so it's been ignored all these years.Now, I can blow, vacuum and dump it back onto tree bed as a natural fertilizer.  Include shredder function only helps re-located dead leaves not so susceptible to be blown away by high winds, kept it neatly all winter long, where they need to be, underneath the tree, on its bed.While vacuuming, it picks up not only soft leaves but often other hard unbreakable materials; I can hear it. One with plastic impeller, I would not use it to vacuum, as no plastic parts is made to endure grinding small gravels and stones subject to rapidly spinning chamber.  All blowers seem to made in same factory, marked differently for each manufacturers; some blower selling at less than half the price of this one, but incorporates a plastic impeller.  It's well worth the money to buy more expensive blower incorporating aluminum impeller.I already returned this unit once, due to broken switch mechanism; I can only can hope it won't happen again as returning to manufacturer, dealing with unknown customer service, hopefully not like evil Nikon corporation selling known flawed productNikon D610 24.3 MP CMOS FX-Format Digital SLR Camera (Body Only)to boost its sales, who returns customer patronage with BIG and BIGGEST middle finger I've yet to experienced.  Only if the manufacturer can figure out ways to design and fabricate this handy tool more reliable which I can't see why it can't be done, this would have been perfect tool, in a quest of pleasantly appearing backyard garden, a sanctuary for most of homeowners.

I have/had gasoline blowers but I wanted something I could setup and use fast for my deck that didn't include the requisite struggle and the potential temperamental nature of a gas blower. This unit is perfect for that. Very fast, adjustable airflow moves stuff out of even tight corners. Not as noisy as a gas blower, lighter weight, and...without all the mess. I also liked the idea of a metal impellor. I hope this translates to longevity.Seems to be balanced well without a lot of vibration. I haven't heard any complaints, (I've got everybody using it, wife and daughter. :)

We used to joke about living in Florida... "Palm fronds didn't require raking!"  Well, we recently purchased a home with enormous oak trees that daily fill our yard with their winter droppings (leaves).  One of our wonderful neighbors was helping us by using his blower until ours arrived.  Since this one vacuums and crunches the leaves to fit more into each trash bag (process that my husband claims is slow-going, but saves bags), he's become the envy of the other neighbors :).  So far, with daily use, it's been exceptionally dependable.  My husband said he'd definitely recommend... Toro makes a good product.

Used both as a blower and as a vacuum for yard debris (leaves, very small twigs, pine needles). Has plenty of power on the blower side, a bit less on the vacuum side (you just have to go slower). The metal impeller looks brand new (about 12 uses so far) and does a very good job chopping up whatever goes through it.The true test will come this fall with all the leaves.
This has been a good blower, a little awkward to carry around but generally good, the attachment a somewhat tight and a little troublesome to change.
this thing looks great in the box. its almost time to start using it. I hope it works as well as it looks

I bought a gas blower because of portability and moveability. It was a mistake. The darn thing started sputtering after two seasons, and after three it started spewing oil. I did not appreciate this, and vowed to try electric the next time. Much less mess, and while it does take a bit more planning and sometimes effort, (not to mention untangling), the benefits outweighed the negatives.This is my first electric blower, and have been under the understanding that electric and good "oomph" power did not go hand-in-hand. I was wrong to this this way, because this thing is actually stronger and more consistent than my 2-cycle gas blower! The portion of the blower was a bit hard to get off, and if you want to attach/remove anything to the nozzle of the blower, you have to take this piece off. It's not a huge deal, but it's plastic, and I was a touch uncomfortable I'd break it with the force needed to get it off of the blower. It didn't break, but I'd not recommend taking this on and off constantly.I have NOT used the mulcher portion of the blower. I'm not interested in cleaning it out after-the-fact, and the bags are never really all that large so it's a constant battle of disconnecting/emptying. The power that is emitted for blowing leaves, so I'm sure sucking them up would be just as powerful/good.All in all I am impressed w/ the power and function of this blower and would recommend this to anybody that is on the fence on whether or not to buy it :)Ps- I got a 100ft 15A outdoor cord. Be mindful of the cord you buy for this. They recommend AGAINST a 10A cord (majority of cords), and there is not a 13A rated cord... 10A = power loss / possible damage to blower 15A is OK, but much MUCH heavier than 10A.
summary: Great power, but be mindful on the cord you choose to go with it!
