reviewText: We purchased a new-to-us house about 18 months ago, and it is the first house we have owned that has a significant number of towering trees (oaks, sycamores, poplars, elms, sassafras trees and more). Three-quarters of our one acre property is wooded, so we get a dense blanket of leaves and more than a few acorns come fall.Years ago I had an electric blower that we used to clean the dust and pollen off the deck, front porch and driveway... but that unit's power is insufficient for the needs of this property. Since the noise and fumes from small gas engines is something that our home owners association frowns upon, our research found that this electric blower has a good reputation for strong output and few problems -- so we gave it a chance.Having used it this past fall, I can wholeheartedly confirm that this little blower does indeed pack a good punch. We had more leaves, acorns, gumballs and small branches cover our yard this fall then we could have ever imagined, but this blower just kept on going and moved them all to the Back 40 (down the hill and back into the woods) with ease.  Thankfully we have a slew of commercial grade long extension cords to let me get all the way down the property.The blower is fairly lightweight so I never felt like my arm was going to fall off, even though I would use it two to three hours at a time. The handle is also nicely placed to allow one hand balancing, which surely helped keep the fatigue away.I have only used the blower function and not the vacuum, so highly recommend this unit if you are looking for a lightweight, strong electric-powered blower for jobs similar to what I've noted above. If you are -- go for it, you will not be sorry.
summary: Toro Ultra Electric Blower - Surprised how strong this blower really is - excellent for our leaf blowing needs

reviewText: It is not the easiest tool to handle.  The balance is off a bit and the handles seem to be in the wrong place.  I would prefer it be 4 inches longer because I am 6' 2" and I have to been over just a bit.  Not a deal breaker for me, but if you have any back issues it may be. It is powerful enough but you still need to rake the leaves into a pile.  A blower may get them into a general area, but you don't want to have to walk around too much with this. It is obviously quite loud so I would recommend ear protection.
summary: it does reduce the size of the pile.

reviewText: This unit is easy to use.  Don't be afraid that buying an electric blower means you have a weak or inferior product. It is variable speed so you turn the dial up or down to meet you needs.  No preset speed.We have both this newly purchased electric and a gas powered blower. I can never start the gas one or by the time I do get it going, I am too tired to use it.This is perfect and instantly ready.  Especially since I got the cord and a quick winder to use with it. I see some reviews regarding plastic parts.  I checked first thing when mine came and the part that rotates to generate the air flow is metal.  The part that holds this onto the unit is metal.  If the whole blower was metal, it would probably be heavier, certainly would be more expensive.  So, I have no complaints about the materials of construction.  I also bought one for my daughter and her husband as a wedding gift.  They love theirs too.  He said it is great to quickly blow out the garage to keep it clean.

I needed a garden vacuum to remove leaves from both the front and rear patio areas. In these areas a blower does not fit the bill. There's no where to blow them to. This works very well. My only complaint is that it is a little awkward to use. (I am only 5-6 so that may be an issue). And it's awkward to empty the bag.But it does its job well so overall it's a good product. Remember this is electric and not gas so you need a convenient outlet and an extension cord.

Definitely worth every penny I paid.  It is EZ to put together and to change from blower to vac and back.  It is sturdy and not too heavy at all.  It has a great variable speed dial for control over blowing and suction power - very helpful. It gave me a "I can get this done" attitude from the minute I clicked it on.In vacuum mode, it amazingly left behind all the olives while sucking up all the olive leaves!  It compacted the leaves and debris very well. I empty the bag when about half-full (it gets heavy and my shoulders are bad) 7 or 8 times to fill one large black yard waste trash bag.  The part that shreds is deep up from the actual vacuum "hose" (2 large tubes that can be put together or not) so I didn't have to worry about a rock getting kicked out and hitting my face.

Tis the season for leaf clean up.  I was blowing my leaves into piles and then shredding them.  The shredding is the part that really lights my fire due to the 16x1 compression ratio.  I can get the enormous pile of leaves down to four 50 gallon trash cans and I don't need to bag.  I was thinking to myself how amazing my Toro blower was and how long it has given me good service.  Arrgghh!  I should have realized that was the kiss of death as moments later it died.  Dead, gone to the other side, non-functional!After a suitable moment of silence I left is sit for the afternoon in hope that it had overheated or "something".  Well after testing on multiple outlets in the futile hope that it was the extension cord or outlet, I concluded it was truly dead.I researched blowers.  My boys have gas powered ones that they love.  Alas the infernal combustion engine and I have a bad history.  Every time I have gotten a gas powered tool, it has died over what ever season it spent in disuse.  Adding Stabil, draining the tank, etc, none of my hand held gasoline tools got through a season without taking it in for service.  My Toro Blower on the other hand continued to blow (in a good way) year after year.I discovered that Toro still makes my blower!  It is red not black but I can live with the color change.  The only upgrade I can see is the metal impeller which is a smart upgrade when that is what does your shredding.  My only beef is that none of the parts or accessories from my old one will fit on the new one.  The new one made short work of the balance of my leaves and looks to be as good or better than it's deceased forbearer.When throwing the box away from the original blower I found the UPS shipping date on the box.  November 7, 2001 was the date.  That means that I got just slightly over twelve (count them 12)  years of service for a $70.00 tool with moving parts.  Kudos to Toro for usability and durability.
summary: Previous Model Gave me 12 YEARS of Excellent Use

reviewText: I bought this to handle the leaves in our various gardens which have over hanging trees and on our white marble rock walkways.  There have been complaints about it sucking up rocks and ruining the blade inside.  Hint: do not run it full blast all the time.  I found it easy to find the right amount of speed to suck up the leaves without also sucking up the gravel.  The blower is very powerful and cleans all sorts of debris from our driveway.  I would recommend this machine.

I think the style of this waterer is cute, just like the office water jug.  The molded-in handle makes it easy to carry and maneuver, and while I do lose some water turning it over, it's easy enough to do it quickly so that it's not a major issue.  As others have pointed out, the design is for smaller birds (finches, say) only.  So far, the birds have been only mildly interested in it, but we have had a record-breaking wet spring.  I'll be interested to see if it is more popular during the hot summer months; if so, I'll be back to upgrade it to 5 stars.
summary: Nice little addition to the bird feeding lineup

reviewText: this was a cute idea, and it came packaged quite securely, but the handle had a leak in it and all the water leaked out within seconds.  Not usuable in any way shape or form.  It would've been a great addition to our nature area in our backyard and I am sad it's not going to work.

This seems like a fantastic idea, and I really like the idea of giving water to all the birds I try and attract with many bird feeders.  It's just two pieces, super easy to clean and hang (no junky hook).  It looks pretty good (if a bit industrial) in the yard.But so far, no birds.  It's there amongst the other feeders, and I've yet to see anyone make the leap to try it.  I moved it from a sunny to a shady area to see if that made a difference. No go.  I will revise my review if suddenly they discover it and have a Friends style water party, but otherwise, this concept is over my birds heads.....I'm tempted to use it for grape jam for my orioles, but won't resort to that until this is a complete miss.
summary: I like it, but do the birds?

reviewText: There are two different ways to use this waterer.  I have had it hanging off a Shepards Hook in my backyard for the last few weeks.  It works okay, but I've only seen very small birds (5" and under) perched on it.  I had to use a large 'S' hook I owned to hang it.I think I'll get better traffic when I put it on my deck.  Currently, I'm using an outdated punch bowl to water my birds...and that won't fly when it gets warm enough for mosquito breeding!I can't stress enough that water has to be changed every few days even if it looks like the water level hasn't dropped.  Birds will poo where they eat and drink, if you get my drift.....Also, you might be deceived on size because we all know the size of water jugs.  This is smaller than you realize...so read the dimensions listed above in the product description.Post script....dropping it down one star.  It is hard to clean once you get algae growing inside.  I get about 2 days of clear water before I have to change it.  The same is true for my control, free standing bowl of water; two days of clear water, max.  It is just easier to clean the bowl.
summary: Hang it or set it out

reviewText: Overall I love the construction- it is easy to grip and fill, the perch around the basin makes it easy for birds to sit and drink- but no matter how I manipulate mine it cannot hold water. It all just drains away no matter how I screw or unscrew it. I can assume I have a defective unit. Were it working, it would be the perfect addition to my yard. I will look into replacing it.

Perfect little water cooler for your backyard bird population.  It is simplistic and blends in well with the environment.  Birds do not use it as much as I had hoped but mayber they are still coming to realize that it is even there.  Hubby suggested taking it down and using it as a self-adjusting waterer for the the cat.  Actually, it probably could be used that way as well, though the base might not be as stable as one would want. This is such an easy way to enjoy nature in a basic way.  Recommended.

This is a really cute little waterer for wild birds.  Shaped like one of the 5-gallon water bottles you find on a water cooler, the idea is to put out water on hot summer days for the wild birds who might struggle to find some.  They will be more attracted to stick around if you have both a feeder for them AND a source of water.  While I don't doubt that, in my area there is no shortage of water available for the wild birds, so I didn't need it for that.  Instead I decided to try it for when I am raising chicks - I am always looking for a better way to supply water to them.What I like about this:* the hanging loop is solid and thick enough to support the weight even when the bottle is full of water.  I really like being able to hang the waterer as it keeps the chicks from kicking their food into it, and I can raise it up as they grow* the bottle screws into the base very securely so I don't need to worry about it coming loose if chicks add their own weight by standing on it.  It actually needs to be screwed on and off for quite a few turns - not just half a turn as is so often the case, so I was very pleased with that* the carry handle.  My husband immediately picked it up and said the handle was a ridiculous waste of space and plastic, but the difference between us is that he has huge hands that can easily pick up the full bottle, holding it by the top, and transport it where he wants to go.  My small hands can not accomplish this, so the handle is invaluable to me (I wish they put this on the waterers sold as chick waterers!)The only negative FOR MY USAGE is that the bowl is quite shallow.  For wild birds - i.e, using it for its intended purpose - I'm sure the shallow bowl is fine.  For me it is working but if it were deeper, I'd be even happier.  However since I am using it for a different purpose than intended, I did not feel that warrants removing a star from the rating.  Overall, I am very pleased with this and do recommend it.

Well designed and constructed this waterer is welcomed in drought stricken south Texas. The handle incorporated in the side of the jug makes it easy to transport and stabilize while filling. The ring built into the top of the jug makes it easy to mount and is stable. The jug and tray are extremely easy to keep clean and I am certain it will last for years. bogie

The Perky Pet Waterer for birds is a genius of an idea. It is light weight and easy to fill and keep filled. I have tried to put water out for the birds, but the pan always gets leaves and dirt in it immediately. This waterer is perfect for small birds. They can perch on the edge and the water is right there for them. I love it.

Attracting birds, butterflies, and other melodic/colorful creatures to one's outdoor surroundings is a common goal and the easiest way to achieve this is through a watering device. After all, every living creature needs water and a plentiful supply is bound to attract them.With the Perky Pet water cooler, you get a cute- looking watering container that is small, lightweight- even when filled with water- and easy to fill. The cooler is designed in the shape of an actual cooler used by people and the cuteness factor alone will convince many to give it a try.I like that this water cooler is smaller and easier to use, but it is not without its fault and the first one I experienced was when I tried to hang it up. I have hooks on my back porch, but they are stationary. The loop at the top of this cooler is also stationary and it isn't very large. The stationary factor means the only way to attach is by tilting the cooler and when you do, the water will come pouring out. This is why it is best to hang this on a moving hook or find a flexible hook to attach to the cooler first. Otherwise, you will lose a portion of the water every time you fill it and reattach.I could tolerate the water loss issue, but one thing I could not handle is that this little cooler just doesn't attract any wildlife. I was puzzled at first and even took it moved it to a tree, just to see what would happen. Still, there was no sign of any birds or other creatures trying to get at the water. Days later, the water was still at the same level as before. I checked other reviews and it looks like I am not alone- others have complained of the same problem. And it appears that the main issue is the small size of the base. It is too little to attract anything except the smallest of birds. I do not have any smaller birds in my area, hence a water cooler that remains full and untouched.As I said, this water cooler is cute and it could fulfill the needs of some people, but it is no use for me and I have already taken it down and placed it in permanent storage in the garage. I may try again later but for now I'm going to chalk this up as a good idea with a faulty design.
summary: Cute, but Ultimately it's For the Birds

reviewText: For people who don't want to deal with a bird bath, this is an easy way to offer water to backyard birds.The support ring is sturdy and should hold up a long time, and the water container screws easily onto the base.The ONLY potential downside that MIGHT occur is the base, being made of plastic, getting brittle over time and breaking or cracking in spots.  But --- I imagine that would only occur after many years and only if it were in direct sunlight ALL the time.A good, sturdy watering device for feathered friends. Five stars.

For whatever reason, I envisioned this being a lot...bigger.  I will take the hit on that one, but I would venture to say nothing bigger than a finch or a small sparrow or robin is all that will visit this water cooler.  I did not have leaks like other have mentioned and the basin filled just fine...just not that much.The fact that the base is plastic is nice since it wont corrode over time, but by the same token, it does feels extremely cheap.
summary: For small birds only and it's all plastic

reviewText: This is great.  I have a couple of birdbaths in our yard that I empty, rinse and refill when I water the garden, but they are always nasty.  This simple, but wonderful water cooler will keep the water cleaner and can be hung in the shade of trees to keep it cooler.  I expect the birds to appreciate this thing and it's easy to rinse and refill using the garden hose.The base just twists off and on and with the handy built-in handle, maintaining it will be easy.Why didn't I think of something like this?  I'm glad someone did.

This is a great little bird waterer!  I filled it with water and hung it from a branch in a little tree that I have feeders filled with thistle seeds for the finches.  This waterer is just the right size for the finches to perch on and get a drink of water.  I also love the handle...it makes filling it a lot easier with the handle to hold on to!  Since the weather has turned warmer I know the birds appreciate the clean, fresh water to drink.  I highly recommend the Perky-Pet Water Cooler Bird Waterer to everyone with a tree to hang it from!

This is a great way to provide clean, fresh water to wild birds.  It is easy to clean and fill.  I wish the top loop was a bit larger as hanging it can be a bit tricky.  I did end up spilling some of the water trying to hang it - but not too much. Given the size of the perching area, I think this will only be useful for small birds.

[Revised 2013-06-09 = beginning of week 5 when the chickadees starting to use it regularly]+[Additional updates on progress]My situation: I have a variety of small birds -- chickadees, titmice, bushtits, wrens,... -- that drink out of the ant traps on myHummingbird Feeders, both integral and supplementary (Trap-it Ant Trap for Hummingbird Feeders). I was interested in something better. Because of the leaping ability of the neighborhood cats, I will not locate feeders or this product with less than 5.5 foot (bottom) clearance (higher in many locations).This requirement for hanging at this height requires using a small ladder and made this product inconvenient for me (unless I see some subsequent advice), hence the rating. I currently have it in a location that I would not have otherwise chosen in order to make the use of a ladder practical (although still somewhat inconvenient). Even if you don't have my situation, this product may still be inconvenient for you to hang.It has taken the chickadees 4 full weeks to become accustomed to using this waterer (details below). I have _observed_ none of the other small birds using it, but that may simply be that the chickadees call more attention to themselves. I have just observed the titmice, which are somewhat larger, landing _vertically_ on the perch, but don't seem to know how to access the water tray (yet?). As for the wrens, they may not have the right type of athletic ability to land on the perch.[Update Week 7: The chickadees are now using it enthusiastically, but still none of the other birds that visit the adjacent feeder have been observed using it. The visits of the titmice and wrens to the feeder often overlap those of the chickadees, so it isn't for lack of examples for using the waterer.][Update: In Week 8 which was a very hot spell, the titmice started making occasional, tentative sips. In Week 9, they are becoming somewhat more confident. In Week 11, titmice have become enthusiastic. It is an amazingly slow process, especially compared to the quick adoption of new feeders. The wrens that visit the feeder still haven't tried it, nor have any of the flock of bushtits that daily pass within feet of it.]----The hanging loop is too small and impossible to see from below. Even practicing with the container empty, I couldn't put it on a typical screw-in hanging hook much above eye-level on the first or second try. It has to be tilted at a considerable angle and wiggled about to find the hole. With a full container, I was unable to get it onto the hook without several inches of water pouring down my arm, and usually most of the water in the jug spilled. With the hook at eye-level, putting it on a stationary (screw-in) hook typically spilled about an inch of water. Spill-less hanging seems to require a large S-hook, and since that precludes your holding the container from the side or bottom, that in turn limits how high you can hang with without using a ladder or other device.----Bird use:I hung this close to a popular bird feeder (peanuts) where it would be a convenient perch for birds waiting their turn -- the hanging flower pot that it replaced was used for just that. It was over two weeks before first known use -- I hear the chirping as the birds arrive at the feeder and usually get a secondary alert from my cat. To supplement direct observation, I put newspapers under a quarter-full jug and looked for speckling from the water drips that I expected would happen when birds landed. Note: I switched back to a full jug before observing the first arrival, and that chickadee didn't produce enough movement to spill any water. During weeks 3 and 4, only the larger adult chickadee used the waterer -- the smaller adult (mate?) who feeds second continued to drink from the nearby ant-trap even though it was in a somewhat more exposed location (there are Cooper's Hawks, so they switch off on look-out duties). At the beginning of week 5, the juvenile chickadees started showing up at the feeder and they quickly adopted the waterer and the smaller adult started using it as well.My suspicion is that the perch is just too close to the water jug for even small birds to land comfortably. The adult chickadees that I have seen using it land not head-in, but vertically or sideways on the perch, appearing to also use a connector bar (between the perching circle and the tray). The adult chickadees also drink predominantly sideways -- they duck down and turns their heads sideways to get at the tray. The juvenile chickadees are small enough to drink head-on.This observation screams that the tray-perch is much too small relative to the jug.----Cleaning: questionable adviceThe typical advice for cleaning hummingbird feeders is to use vinegar and to avoid soap. Some claim that hummingbirds hate soap's taste, other that it causes problems with their digestive system (or they may hate the taste because of those problems).Consequently, I was surprised that the advice was to clean with mild soap. Soap and vinegar have very different roles. Detergents such a soaps are molecules that have one end that binds to water and the other to a oil or grease molecule and thus allows water flow to pull off not just that oil/grease but everything else that is attached to it. Vinegar is a weak acid that tears apart or dissolves other types of contaminants. This is why you will find both in many cleaning products. My understanding of the types of problems likely to occur -- minerals and harmful biologics -- are ones dealt with by vinegar and on which soap has little/no effect. There is no mention of bleach (either way).----Apparent theory of operation (beyond the basics):The slots that release the water into the tray are very thin. When I first turned over the feeder, the water released didn't even completely cover the bottom. But rock the feeder even slightly -- as it would in the wind or from birds landing -- and more water is released. This has the potential to do more than just replenish the water in the tray -- the currents _might_ help float debris up and over the sides. I could simulate a little of this by hitting the perch with my finger, but it would take actual birds landing to confirm this speculation.Observation from current use: With evaporation and without periodic rocking, the water in the tray can become very depleted -- not completely covering the bottom -- which might then not provide sufficient attraction for birds to land and providing the rocking to do the replenishment.Suggestion: One might want to periodically give this product a tap to release a bit more water into the tray.-- Douglas B. Moran
summary: Form inhibits function. Birds were slow to adapt, but eventually enthusiastic. Inconvenient for me

reviewText: When it comes to birding, cleanliness is very important.  With the jug handle, this waterer is hard to clean, even with a flexible brush.  I have lots of finches, and with finches, comes conjunctivitis, and being able to clean this properly is very important.  Sure, I could just slosh some bleach around it when cleaning, but I'm not comfortable not being able to scrub each and every inch of this.  If it has been one solid jug, it would've been much easier to clean.I've had it up for a few weeks now and have not noticed one bird on it.  Only small birds can use this, which I have plenty of (sparrows, finches, chickadees, nuthatches, etc).  Initially I did put it up a few feet away from a thistle feeder, and the goldfinches abandoned the feeder.  Once I moved this waterer, the birds came back.  Strange, but not unheard of.  It's now near the bird bath and still, no takers.

Mine works great. It took a few days for the birds to "discover" it, as birds will do. I read some reviews here that say it doesn't work. I am assuming it should NOT be filled right to the top, completely full. Some space needed above the water for air pressure. It's an attractive container, large enough. If TOO large you will need to rinse & fill it more often, and water will not be fresh long. I liked this so much I ordered a second one. UPDATE 5/29/13: I still really like it. It attracts birds medium & small (hummingbirds) and I'm glad to offer them clean water, especially in these hot summer months. They have been using my two daily and I need to fill them every few days. Recommended.
summary: High quality, attractive, leave some air space above the water for air pressure.

reviewText: Birds will flock to this waterer.  In summer, they want safe places to drink and appreciate having a drink well off of the ground.  Only reason for four stars is that it's so small, you have to refill it so often.  I recommend it.
summary: Birds will flock to this waterer

reviewText: I'm really excited about this bird waterer.  It's a perfect size i.e. easy to fill and carry back after filling to hang again.  It's really attracting the birds of all kinds in  my back yard.  I think because it's easy for them to drink from while "hanging on".  Highly recommended. PS.  Also because of the clear glass, it blends nicely into the scenery.

[Note: I am editing this review. The edited portion is at the bottom of this part, which was my original review.]I am a bird feeder from way back. I currently have four feeders in the garden outside my kitchen window - one for hummers, two for standard seed or sunflower seeds and one for niger seed or other finch-type food. I also have a bird bath. Birds know my yard well and we back up to a woods. I get all kinds of perching birds and song birds from Blue Jay and Grackle size to Goldfinches, Chickadees, Sparrows and Wrens and the in-between sizes. I have yet to see a bird on this waterer. I think it's because the perch isn't wide enough. The design is good in that it's well-made and sturdy, but if the birds aren't using it, I can't give it stars for its good looks.It's been up 4 days. I will leave it up and refill it every few days for the foreseeable future, and may also try moving it around, but so far.... just one star. If the birds figure it out and start using it, I'll revise this._____________________________________________Edit: June 17, 2013 - The small birds have found my waterer. I have seen goldfinches, chickadees and today I got some pictures! I am revising this because it does seem to work for small birds. It is also easy to clean and if it does get some mold in it, bleach will of course kill it easily.The larger birds can't use it and the hook loop on the top is much too small.
summary: Editing to say... the little birds found it.

reviewText: I agree with the other reviewers - this is only good for small birds.  My finches like it and I see them drinking from it from time to time (they seem to prefer the birdbath on the other side of the yard, though), but the perch isn't big enough for larger birds like the wrens and robins I have in my yard.It isn't too big or too heavy to hang up on a moderate sized hook, but I had to purchase and extra s-hook to hang it since there is no way to hang it the way it came in the mail.  I probably should have expected that, but it was a minor challenge to find a hook that fit through the loop at the top and I had to take the waterer to the hardware store to make sure it would fit and hang properly.  Other than that, it holds a good amount of water and is easy to fill.

We love feeding the birds in our back yard, but beyond our bird bath, I never gave much thought to providing water for them.  Wow, they love this--can't believe the activity we have seen since hanging this up.  I only wish I had it last Summer in the heat--but they can enjoy it this year.  I would recommend this for all bird lovers!

This looks and works very much like a water cooler; bottle on top, dispenser on the bottom.  I like that I can hang it so I can see it out of the same window where my suction-cup-attached birdfeeder is.  Before I was using a kind of saucer-in-holder water container that was part drinking fountain, part birdbath, part squirrel waterer.  It was always either empty or dirty because it was out of sight.  If this guy is empty, it's right there in my face which helps a little.What I didn't think of is that this needs something to hang from.  It comes with nothing, not even an S hook.  Filled with water it weighs 3 - 4 pounds and that doesn't sound like much, but when I tried to hang it over the side of my wood fence with a coathanger, the coathanger lost.  It became just a limp piece of wire that couldn't even hold the jug upright.  So I bought a sturdy hook to mount onto my fence for more than the water jug cost, found some suitable mounting screws in my extra parts stash, made a hook out of a zip tie and behold, my birdie waterer was up and running!The point here is not to be a dummy like me and just get the jug.I've read other reviews that say that only small birds can enjoy it and I guess that's true.  The other drawback vs. my ground-level saucer/birdbath is that squirrels and rabbits can't get to it.  Some might not consider that a drawback but I will keep using that because my dogs are fascinated by squirrels and the occasional rabbit.  The big plus vs. my ground level thing is that this one gets a lot less dirty.Anyway, a very enjoyable and easy to use item.
summary: Fine birdie water cooler but you need more

reviewText: I have several bird feeders (suet, thistle, seed, etc.) in my yard here in Connecticut and I get a tremendous number and variety of birds. I always feel a bit guilty though that I don't pay enough attention to their water needs and it can get hot and dry here by July. I have a bird bath, but I'm not great at keeping it filled. For those reasons, this little water cooler for birds really appealed to me.I have to say I'm more than pleased with the quality and the design. First, it's very rugged and I don't think that, even if it fell from the hook where I have it hanging, that it would get hurt. Also, its very simple to use--just unscrew the base, fill it with water, re-attach the base and (quickly) flip it right-side up and you're ready to go. It's that easy. And the threads are very strong and the dish part screws on very securely.The loop at the top of the bottle makes it easy to hang. I used one of those elongated s-hooks that are used to hang a hanging pot from a branch or whatever and it works perfectly. A piece of nylon fishing line would work fine, too.I really am very pleased with this and I think it will be a hit with the birds (I just put it out today, so still waiting for the first customers). I'm hanging it next to my screened porch to keep the cats entertained. It's nice to find an affordable product like this that does what it says it will do, is nicely made and serves a good purpose. A great gift for your bird-feeding friends, too. I'll post some photos once the birds belly up to the bar.By the way, a few reviewers have said that they have had it up for a while and no takers yet. I suggest posting a sign nearby, pointing to the waterer. (Kidding.) It takes a little while for birds to feel safe around anything new in your yard. They see it, they know it's there, they'll come. If you want to attract them faster, try letting a hose drip into a bucket nearby for a few hours a day for a few days--birds are extremely attracted to moving water. If they think water is in the area, they will investigate more.
summary: This is a great idea, I love it & so nicely made!

reviewText: It looks like a miniature water cooler. You fill the plastic bottle, screw on the cap which provides the pool for the water from which the birds drink, and hang it up. There is no assembly. This is very easy to use. It works well, but if placed in direct sunlight the water in the bottle heats up. It does a fair job of attracting birds, but not as many as a feeder.

This handy dandy little water source for our feathered friends is a perfect edition to our bird watching area off our back patio.  The birds like having a place to get a drink and this is convenient to fill and hang.  The birds appreciate it and it makes a nice edition to the different feeding options we have put there.  It has been cold up to now here close to the mountains, but Spring has finally sprung and there are flowers blooming to enjoy in our garden and nice green grass and lovely birds visiting.  Recommend!

My Perky Pet Water cooler is too small for all but the smallest of birds to sit on the ledge while drinking.  There is no stabilization so it swings back and forth as soon as a bird does land on it, consequently the bird flies off because it's swinging.  You have to take it completely down to fill and then screw off the bottom which is where the birds poop is. I wouldn't recommend this product just because you have to get it down from the tree, and then touch bird excrement and then the birds don't use it anyway because it sways and is just too small. Mine did not come with a hook to hang it so you'll have to find your own S hook or string to hand it with.
summary: Not easy to fill & only small birds can fit on the perch

reviewText: I was eager to try out this "water cooler" for birds. Its basically a small jug of water turned upside down and attached to a well with a ridge where the birds can perch and drink their water. As the water goes down the jug refills without spilling over. Once its empty, its easy to take down unscrew and with its built in carry handle can easily fill it up and its ready to go with ease. Small birds fit perfect on this... but not sure about larger ones. It looks nice, yes its a jug, but most people that have seen it tell me thats a neat little water jug for birds, or how cool is that.. some even said what a great idea.. so its definitely a big hit. My son loves it also as its easy for him to fill and handle without spilling- so it is kid friendly as well.
summary: Perfect for Small Birds, Easy to Handle, Looks Decent

reviewText: My hopes with this product was to attract insect eating birds that do not usually visit our feeders.The problem is tray. The water holding portion is so narrow, covered by the bottle itself, that the larger birds don't even attempt it. :( This could've been easily resolved with a base of a greater diameter. Larger birds will choose a bird bath, everytime. I liked this concept as a cleaner water option that required less attention than a bird bath which dirties easily.I like that the bottle itself is small, requiring it to be filled more frequently. This helps insure it is refilled with fresh water and not growing green slime. Which, I also put a dash of apple cider vinegar in the waterers to help keep things from getting funky. The smaller bottle also isn't too heavy when filled. It's still plenty easy to lift to a feeding station. A note, you will need a narrow hook to fit the loop, it does not come with one for hanging nor did it fit on my station's hook.Overall, this hasn't been what I had hoped. No new insect eating birds attracted. It does offer a clean water station for small birds, like finches and sparrows though. Not necessarily the birds I was hoping to attract more of though.

Yep, it'll water birds alright! It is super lightweight, being just a thin plastic jug. We opened it, unscrewed the blue plastic "top". Rinsed it well and filled it with water. We went outside and quickly turned it upside down (a little water spilled) and hung it next to the bird feeders.Thus far, I haven't had any takers. But we'll see. My kids enjoy the thought of it and I'm willing to see 1. how long the water lasts until its ucky and 2. how many birds actually want to use it.I did end up making a loop with wire to hang from a shepherd's hook instead of trying to wiggle it on without spilling it all. But an "s" hook would work just as well.

So this is a convenient bird water cooler. Little birds will certainly get the use from it.It has benefits and flaws, depending on what your interests are.Benefits are it's small, easy to re-fill, and will not take up much space. It's small enough that you wouldn't need a crook to hang it from if you have a ledge you could sit it on. I have it on a deck's beam, and it's fine right there.In fact, even full, it could hang from a sturdy branch. Though it might be uneven and the water would spill out - I tried this, but it's not ideal. It IS possible.Because the water basin is screwed to the cooler, it's an easy two-part product to unscrew to refill the water - it's a very simple design.It could be an effective replacement for metal birdbaths that get rusty or dirty over time. Other than rinsing the plastic basin, there won't be much to clean.Flaws are not design flaws, but it depends what you want to get from it.It's not decorative at all. Whether hanging or sitting, it looks like an upside-down water cooler. So it won't add anything visual to your yard, except its utilitarian appeal. It's also not a bird bath, so many birds will still look for other water sources.It's small and when empty, very light. So if you don't hang it from something, a stiff wind would blow it away.Little birds could use it, but it's not for big birds. They could not balance on the basin - unless it sat on a porch ledge, then even bigger birds could dip their beaks. But then it might blow off in the wind.It's perfectly useful and will accomplish providing water for the birds...but it does lack decorative appeal.UPDATE as of August 6: So I've had this all summer and the little birds (chicadees, finches) liked it, while bigger birds (morning doves, cardinals) didn't seem to use it.I'm less impressed then I was. The design makes for difficult cleaning, and the interior gets dirty pretty quickly. The birds aren't going to care, as they can drink pretty much anything, but it can be unsightly.If you're not going to hang it, it needs to be set FLAT or on hot days the reservoir will dry up. Even a little tilt will create a problem.It can't be outside during the winter anyway. I think it works for one spring-to-fall season, and then replace it.I'm not going to drop this a star, but after three months my opinion leans more toward "okay" than "like."
summary: A simple option, but depends what you're going for (updated with some concerns)

reviewerName: N. Ferguson "Two, Daisy, Hannah, and Kitten"
reviewText: Unlike our bird bath, this cooler keeps the water clean!  We love using this in the hot summmer months!  After years of trying to use a bird bath as a drinker, we finally had to accept that it would never stay clean, as droppings from perching birds contaminate the water almost instantly.  The cooler provides a great alternative when hung on a sturdy branch.

This bird water cooler is very easy to fill up and keep clean.Made in the USA with very durable material.  I would like it to be available in different sizes so I could get one for the bigger birds too.You'll need a sturdy chain, hook or something similar to use to hang it.So far birds aren't coming to it, but that would be because we are going through a wet period and there is an abundance of places they can find water right now.I will update this review when it heats up around here.*Update* after a month of it up in the heat of summer, I never saw a bird on it so I ended up taking town and putting a hanging bird bath up and they love that.
summary: Very cute, durable water cooler for the birds

reviewText: Whenever I go looking for pet products I keep my eye open for Perky-Pet.  They are my goto for Hummingbird feeders and other birdie items, so I was pretty happy to find this Bird Waterer.PROS--cute.  This thing looks just like a big 10-gallon water service jug, only smaller.--it's not too heavy.  Water, as I'm sure you all know, is heavy.  This water holder is sized so that even full it's not too heavy to raise about your head.--holds enough water you won't have to fill it but once, maybe twice a week.--has a handle on the side which makes it easy to carryGeneral NOTES--you should fill it with fresh water every week.--Perky Pet folks say you should gently wash it at least every other week.  I think it makes sense to wash it out when you refill it.--it has a loop at the top to hang it by, but it won't fit over the end of your standard metal shepard hooks.  This means you'll need a sturdy chain or rope.CONS--my major concern is that the dish at the bottom is too small for larger birds.  The finches have no problem, but I haven't seen a Cardinal on it.I really like the design.  It's cute, and I like that the whole waterer is lightweight and doesn't create a mess.  I think this will come in very handy in the summer because the water won't evaporate as quickly as it does in my bird baths.  Only minus is that it seems more suited to smaller birds and I love me Cardinals and LadderBacks.Pam T~mom/fur mom/birder

I've been Birding my entire life. Growing up on a farm with fields, virgin prairie, wetlands, streams and forest, about the ONLY birds we never saw were those from the Tropics. I've taught birding classes at many a nature sanctuary and I have over 14 feeding stations on our acre of land with 5 bird baths, too. So, I'm no novice.When offered this water station, I was very excited, hoping that the smaller warblers and finches would find it attractive since they are such skittish birds. I hung this waterer from a pine limb that's dead and very stationary; it is right in the midst of the finch/warbler feeding stations.After a solid week of trial, Not.One.Single.Bird. has either approached it, attempted to approach it or even considered it!!! Now, birds are opportunists and will investigate ANYTHING that is new in their area. I've put out brand new feeders they've never used at 4:00 p.m. and by 4:10 p.m., the feeder is filled with birds. And it's not as if I didn't watch that area for interaction, as it's Spring Migration season Up North and I'm doing Bird Counts of migrants, being able to eyeball the waterer for hours on end.I'll keep it up, and if nothing else, the flying insects will get water from it. I'm sad. There was a lot of promise and hope with this product but zero delivery. I ranked it 3 stars because it is very well made and came with clear instructions. But, just like when you buy a toy for your cat or dog and they NEVER play with it, it doesn't mean the toy is Bad, it just means that it holds no attraction to your individual pet. So it is with this device: I can't rate it as bad in construction and I can't rate it as "bad" for providing water, just MY birds had no desire to even attempt to use it. Sorry. :(
summary: If You Build It, it DOESN'T mean they'll come. :(

reviewText: I live in an extremely dry area, so I would think that the birds I feed would welcome water. After over a week, though, I have yet to see any evidence that they are getting a benefit from this. I recognize two parts of the problem but not the full problem.To begin with, the hook on the top of the container will not fit over many hooks or nails, so I had to use some nylon line to hang the waterer. If you buy one, there is a plastic tie that holds on the tag and instructions (if these can be called instructions), and I recommend you don't cut it off as I did. That little tie should be enough.Filling the plastic bottle with water was easy enough, and attaching the base was easy, too. But that's when I noticed the first problem. Very little water actually came out. The next day, when I went to check, the dish from which the birds are supposed to drink was bone dry. So I shook the bottle a bit and induced some water into the dish. The next day, the dish was dry again. Once again, I jiggled the bottle and managed to get a little bit of water into the dish.I've tried screwing the base on more tightly and doing so more loosely, but water simply does not seem to want to leave the bottle and settle in the dish. That's the first part of the problem.The second part is that the base seems just too small for many birds. In the time I have had this, I must have looked at it forty or fifty times. There have been birds galore on the feeder two feet to the right of the water bottle but never a bird on the water tray.I gave it two stars rather than one in deference to those who love it. Perhaps my bottle is just defective in some way. But, having disassembled it and inspected it (thinking perhaps that the plastic hadn't been cut back sufficiently where the water was supposed to come out--not the problem, I discovered), I cannot recommend this product.

We live in a lake region so no obvious need to provide water for birds. However we do have a few feeders and thought we could add this to the mix. This waterer is sturdy and easy to fill. The loop at the top was perfect for a mini-carabiner to hang from a hook. Small birds (chickadees, finches) have taken to it. It is already popular and it took no time for the small birds to get used to it. Easy to clean and a breeze to refill.Given out water rich environment I'd probably not buy another but if I was in a dryer area a few of these would be great for backyard birders. I've not seen any of our larger songbirds at the waterer so I'd say expect smaller birds.

Like most bird lovers, we have several bird feeders and also have a few areas for water.  Those areas include bird baths, ground level water holders, and a small waterfall in our back yard.  There are a few areas though that do not have water and we thought this might make a good addition.Here is what I liked:1.  Very light weight material with a built in hand hold.  The blue plastic tray and the clear plastic  water holder should not confuse the hummingbirds.2.  The water holder is easy to fill.Here is what I did not like:1.  There is no hook included to use to hang this with.  You will need an s shaped hook to be able to use this.2.  Water does not really fill the bottom tray so much as it has some water on the surface that moves around with the movement of the unit.  This also means that as wind catchs and moves the unit, water spills from the unit onto the ground.  In three days in light winds the unit has spilled half of the water onto the ground.  By light winds, I mean 3 to 5 MPH.3.  Cleaning can be a pain.  Due to the design of the handle and the size of the opening that connects to the base, you cannot get a brush into all of the areas to clean it with.  This makes it basically a bleach water cleaning which also means you need to ensure you get it well rinsed out.4.  After 5 days, no birds have checked it out evern though there are three feeders within 5 feet of the waterer.  Perhaps it just takes more time.Overall, this is probably a good way to add water if you are limited on space, but a small active waterfall or a shallow birdbath still seem to me to be the best options.

I have been using this waterer for the past four weeks and I must say it works well. The big bird baths we have in the yard is open to wind and sun and evaporates within 2 to 3 days on sunny days, and this baby holds water for several weeks with a constant supply for the birds to quench their thirst. The jug with water remains clean and free from leaves, dust or algae.I like the design and the make is reasonable, but the quality of the material is moderate. The jug seems to attach to the bottom part pretty well. The ring built into the top of the jug makes it easy to mount. The perch area at the base of the bath, where birds drink water from is quite small, thus preventing medium and large size birds from using this bath.We have mounted this on a tree in our back yard and it is satisfying to watch (from my kitchen window) the birds get a drink of water on a sunny day.1.First Nature 3004 Globe Style Bird Bath and Waterer2.Hagen Living World Cockatiel Bird Bath, Brown and Topaz

I've had this up for a couple weeks now and have yet to see any birds on it.  The problem seems to be that the perches are quite small and there isn't a lot of drinking space; the design requires that the bird sort of duck under the jug.  We'll see what we'll see, but so far this has been a bust for me - on my wooded property most avian visitors are woodpecker or cardinal -size birds - this seems designed for small finches.The design of the thing is pretty clever, but you WILL lose some water when turning it upside-down.  Once upright the water wicks out somehow - provided you screwed the jug in fully.It's pretty small.  Maybe if you are trying to encourage sparrows and drive pigeons away it would be good?

Before I start my review let me give you an overview of the environment:We have a decently large size backyard with lots of trees and shrubs. We never really needed to attract birds as they love our backyard anyways due to the peace and serenity we tend keep in the backyard. we also do not have a dog or small child to scare the birds away. We generally sit by the patio on pleasant evenings and watch birds with ease as they keep chirping, digging for worms and or merely having fun. Over the years we have seen certain species of birds (we call them the 'usual' suspects) who are not scared of us anymore and go about doing their business chasing each other or just like to dig for worms from the backyard lawn.When Amazon offered me this Perky-Pet Water Cooler Bird Waterer for review I gladly accepted to review it thinking that we will be able to watch these birds drink water from time to time and moreover as summer is around the corner we will be able to provide some thirst relief to the birds in our backyard.The product received for review is cute and well constructed - there is no doubt in that. It Looks good, functions and obeys laws of physics and drips water automatically as designed but sadly does not attract birds of any kinds as of yet. It has been nearly a week and I have not seen a single bird ever drink water from it. They zoom fly past by it never even looking at it once.I personally think the problem is with the base. The base in my opinion is too small for the types of birds in our backyard to land on and drink water thereby avoiding it completely. I am reading other reviewers who have had some degree of success with it. It is possible that those who have had success might be due to small birds in their backyard.Anyways, as the product did not attract birds as expected I am currently rating it with 2 stars. Attractive to humans but not birds is my feedback with the original design. I have plans to make the base a bit wider by attaching a plastic plate underneath the waterer and hang it in the same tree. I will update my review with my findings. Please see the comments section with in next couple of weeks or so with my updated results.

My area has been in a drought for a few years.  When I saw birds trying to get water out of my pool, I knew I needed to provide an easier way for them.  At first, I used old pie plates, but they rusted pretty fast.  I got two silicone baking pans and they have worked out quite well.  Certainly, no rusting.  The birds use them both for drinking and for bathing.When I saw this bird waterer, I thought it would work well with my pans.  The birds could use the pans for bathing and the waterer for fresh water.  They often splash most of the water out of the pans during their baths, so this way there would always be water to drink.I put the waterer out several days ago.  I have yet to see a bird using it, although they are still visiting and using the pans.  I think the problem is the size.  The base is about 6" in diameter with a perch around the outside of it.  The trough for the water doesn't extend out much past the water container at its widest.  The bottle does taper in to where it screws on to the base.  This makes the water accessible to small birds, but doesn't seem to work for the bigger ones, which is what I get.  I rarely see sparrow-sized birds in my yard.  I mostly get cardinals, blue jays, mockingbirds, morning doves, and several varieties of similar-sized black birds.  I don't think there is any way for them to stand on the perch and drink the way a smaller bird would be able to do.  They prefer to either stand on the rim of the pan or just stand in the pan to get their water.  I do have the waterer sitting on my patio next to the pans (I don't have any trees in my yard), so they could probably stand on the patio and get the water that way, but I guess they haven't been desperate enough to bother.  They don't seem to mind drinking water they, or others, have been bathing in!  Since I put this on my patio, I am glad the base is plastic and not metal.I like the design of this waterer.  It is easy to fill and empty.  The water does not just flow out until it is gone.  My backyard friends are just too big for it.  If I had more birds that were sparrow-size or smaller, I think it would work well.ETA:  The waterer is now being used, but not by the birds.  The bees are using it.  I guess they need water, too, so at least it is helping something.

It does okay for the small finches, but I keep having to go out and tip it a little to get the water to come out, I tip it too much and it just runs out, it doesn't self refill. But when the water is there, it works great. I don't see this problem with the other reviewers so maybe it's just an issue with the one I have. I have it on the deck too, so all the birds can use it, not the just the very small ones as hanging it would make it impossible for the larger birds like the doves to drink. They do use it when I remember to tip it so that it can refill, so it is useable, just not self refilling.

I've had this water cooler hanging in my back yard for over a month and I've never seen a bird on it once. I clean it, fill it, I've moved it to see if another spot is more appealing. There are a ton of birds in my yard, but they want nothing to do with this water cooler.

This is a decent little bird waterer that suffers from one major flaw (in my experience): it basically doesn't replenish itself. I have to manually come over and squeeze the "bottle" to get an appreciable amount of water to come out into the dish below. If I don't do that then what comes out is a trickle at best that doesn't even completely cover the entire bottom of the dish. Other than that the waterer is reasonably attractive given that it looks like a water cooler bottle. It is quite small. You will want to have an extra hook or something if you're hanging it from a pole. My feeder pole has two arms that curve upward on the ends to prevent what's on them from falling off; the hole on top of this bird waterer is so small that I spilled a ton of water just trying to fit it over the arm on my feeder pole, and it's not even very wide. A decent waterer that in my case at least is more trouble than it should be.

Provides 1.5 quarts of water to your thirsty birds. The water cooler shape allows your birds to have their own water cooler to gather and gossip. The handle on the bottle makes it easy for filling and carrying. Adding water near a food source, attracts more birds. Birds will seek out water, offering them water in your setting increases your bird population.
summary: Bird gossip around the water cooler

reviewText: I have a large private back yard where I have several water features and feeders for wild birds.  I have purchased Perky-Pet products in the past and have always been happy with the quality and that they are a "made in the USA" company.  This bird waterer is adequate for smaller birds such as finches and house sparrows but the small base does not allow larger birds to perch.If the base were just a touch bigger, I think it would attract more birds.However, I love the design - It features:Unique water cooler design1.5 Qt water capacityErgonomic handle allows easy filling and carrying and inverting so that the water doesn't pour or leak outConstructed of durable plastic and made in the USAI clean and refill my waterer every week so that the birds have fresh H2O!Happy Bird Watching!
summary: Perky-Pet Products - MADE IN THE USA! Great SMALL Bird Waterer

reviewText: The concept behind this waterer is sound. Providing fresh water to birds is an essential part of caring for backyard birds and creating a welcoming environment for them so they can be enjoyed as they visit our yards.Its blue color seems more intent on being colorful rather than blending into an outdoor setting. I'm not big on Fisher-Price colors for outdoor equipment, so if given the choice, I would rather have something dark green, tan, or even black.The water bottle is perfectly-sized. Not too big, not too small. The cap, which serves as the perch and reservoir when in use, screws onto the bottle easily. The hook on the top (when inverted during use) makes it easy to hang, but only if you have an S-hook to hang it on. It's far too small to hang on a shepherd's hook or other kind of outdoor hanger. That hook also keeps you from being able to fill it with water and then set it down on a counter before taking it outside. The handle is nice enough, but it seems to be there to make it look like a large water bottle than for its utility. The bottle isn't large enough to need to be carried like a milk jug, so I think it would be just as useful not to have it, but if it works for some people, so be it.I've replaced the water and cleaned it several times since I started using it three weeks ago, and it's given me the chance to form some opinions regarding cleaning. The neck opening should be larger so that the bottle could be cleaned more easily; at about 2.25" it's much too small for me to get my hand in. That aformentioned handle also creates a situation where that could be difficult to clean if algae were to start growing in there. The bottle is perfectly cylindrical, so be prepared to have it roll around on you while you're cleaning the cap, because you can't set it on its top (the hook is in the way) and if you lay it on its side, it will roll without stopping (a dab of hot glue or something would prevent that pretty easily, but it was something I noticed). The cap is quite easy to clean. It's shallow and it doesn't have any small crevices that make it difficult to clean easily.All those issues aside, the biggest problem I've had with this waterer is that in 3+ weeks of use, I haven't seen a single bird use it. We have plenty of birds in our backyard, with everything from cardinals, orioles, and mourning doves, to chickadees, goldfinches, purple finches, sparrows, and wrens. I think this unit is too small for the larger birds to use, but I would have thought that the finches and chickadees and wrens would have taken advantage of it by now. I've moved it to another location to see if that will help, but after a few days, still nothing. There are other water sources nearby, including a cascading water fountain, so it's possible that a stationary water reservoir just hasn't caught their attention. I would like to see if having a wider cap with the same sized bottle would attract more birds, but as far as I know, that's not available.Overall, this waterer is nicely priced and is decent enough to use for small birds. While I have been unsuccessful in attracting any birds to use it, if you have small birds and no other water sources for them in the vicinity, this may work out for you.
summary: Never saw a bird on it in 3 weeks

reviewText: Really awful design.The product works on the principle of suction, so be careful when flipping it over to hang.  I spilled water all over my kitchen and myself!It does not come with any hanging equipment, so be sure to purchase that if you get this product.I think the perky pet people forgot that this product hangs outside and is frequently going to be pooped on by birds.  The water bottle top and the blue water dish below screw on and off.  The water bottle top needs to be turned right side up to fill.  It cannot be filled while still hanging on the tree.I do not wish to handle a poop laden water cooler every time this product needs refilling.Also, I tried to cut a hole in the bottom of the water bottle so I could fill it with water from the top.  DO NOT do this, the whole thing works on the principle of suction, and once it has a hole in the bottom it won't work anymore.Anyway, the plastic seems like good quality because it took a lot of effort for me to cut a hole through it.  The water dish is of less solid construction.All in all, I would not recommend this product at all.Update: I filled it up with birdseed, but unless you have very tiny granules of seed, it won't work.  The seed just gets stuck and you have to empty it by unscrewing it.  (Which defeats the purpose of cutting a hole in it).

This unit is exactly what it looks like. It is a plastic water jug with a built in handle. Instead of the original cap, a plastic "lid" with narrow slits and a ring of plastic around it screws onto the top of the water jug. A quick flip upside down and gravity causes the water from the jug to fill the shallow reservoir. When the water level reaches the slits, water stops coming out until the level is lowered from evaporation or birds drinking.Pros:  Very eash to fill, the threads on the cap portion easily screw onto the jug. It's a good size.Cons:  The loop on the top is a little bit shallow, meaning it's hard to find a means of hanging that feels strong enough but is small enough to pass through the loop. Not a big problem.It isn't very attractive. It doesn't look very pretty hanging from a tree. This won't matter to the birds, but it might to a homeowner.All in all it will work well for providing the birds fresh water without a birdbath which has to be frequently cleaned due to leaves and other debris. Depending on your climate, it will probably need to be emptied and brought inside for the winter. I don't think the plastic would survive a freeze. It will be important to provide the birds who've become accustomed to having water in a particular location an alternate source of water in the winter.
summary: Fresh water for our feathered friends

reviewText: A reliable source of drinking water is critical in order for birds to survive hot and dry summers.  Bird baths are helpful (birds need to keep their feathers clean and well as keeping themselves hydrated) but the bigger, more aggressive birds tend to dominate the bath and smaller birds (such as Chickadees, finches and Nuthatches) need to look elsewhere in order to get the water that they need.This is my second Perky-Pet waterer.  I accidentally left one behind on my last move.  I really liked it so I was quite pleased to receive this one.  My experience with this product, and with water sources in general, is that birds will have no problem finding what they need when they need it the most.  When natural sources of water are available (ponds, creeks, even puddles) birds will utilize those.  However, in a drought, birds will happily seek out man-made sources.  This bird-cooler is no exception.  Small birds flock to in during the hot, dry South Texas summer months.This waterer is simple, well made and works perfectly.  The water comes out of the holes and fills the tray easily.  My only complaint is that this cooler does not come with any type of hanger.  A simple chain, rope or clip would be helpful and really should be included.  Other than that, this is a great and unique looking item that gives little songbirds the water that they need.
summary: Perfect for getting small birds through our hot, dry summers

reviewText: I thought this would be an interesting and handy take on a traditional bird bath so that I could provide birds with a stable clean water source. While the product assembles easily and seems to work as described, I'm not entirely sure the birds are interested. I've had it up for about three weeks, and most of the water is still in the bottle, and I've yet to see a single bird actually using it.Assembly is easy. The bottle screws onto the base. So the idea is that you can fill the bottle, screw on the base, and then flip it over to hang it from the hook. If you fill it inside your house, do not flip it over until you get it outside. Also, expect to get somewhat splashed regardless of how carefully you flip it over -- the water will spill from the four openings before gravity takes over and the water stops coming out. The unit has a small loop at the top from which you can hang it. I picked-up a medium-sized S-hook so I could loop it through the unit's loop, and then attach it to an existing pole in my yard. The unit is strong enough to hold its own weight, complete with water.So I've noticed a few things. The tray doesn't always have water in it. I suspect this is because it is evaporating, but because the bottle doesn't have a hole (or valve) at the top, it doesn't allow the water to flow naturally. If I slightly tilt the unit, the water will flow and fill the tray. That's fine, because a gentle breeze or a visit by a bird should cause enough movement to move the unit to fill the tray.However, I have yet to see a bird using this. I have it positioned next to a bird feeder, and while there are always birds on the bird feeder, they never seem to use the water bottle. If they were, I would expect there to be far less water in the bottle after about three weeks. Maybe it is only truly useful to certain types of birds, but unless I watch it 24/7, it is really hard to tell how useful it is.It also seems that insects have an uncanny ability to enter one of the four openings at the base of the dish, and then float their way to the top of the bottle, where they usually ultimately drown and die. While I guess this can be expected, it will probably force you to dump the water often and refill it.Ultimately, I view this as an interesting fixture for a yard in which you already attract feathered-friends. If you plan on using to attract feathered-friends, I would pass on this. It does exactly what is says it is designed for...but whether it attracts birds is inconclusive.
summary: Easy to assemble, but doesn't attract many birds

reviewerName: Valerie J. Wood "Author and Sports Journalist"
reviewText: The Perky-Pet Water Cooler Bird waterer is a nice, easy to clean, lightweight waterer. Not too big, either. We have a huge waterer in one area and it is a bit of a pain to clean. This one is light and unscrews easily to wash/refill. Very pleased with this item. Would recommend it!

I was quite excited about it at first when this bird waterer first came out.  Unfortuatly, it doesn't work too well.  First, the device should come with an axilliary hook for hanging it.  If you have a rigid pole with a firm hook at its end, it would be much more convenient to hang this had it came with a  hook to go between the waterer and the pole.  That way you can hang it without turning it sideway to fit it onto the pole.  The device is not too attractive and looks just like what it is, an ugly plastic jug.  The dish on the bottom surrounding the water container is too narrow for birds to have enough of a ledge to land on and to stand up in order to start drinking.  The space is just too tight for anything but the smallest of birds.  Lastly, water does not run out of the jug nicely to fill the dish on the bottom unless aided by a little shaking which is an absurdly inconvenient thing to have to do.  This device has too many problems to work well.

Arrived in a box within a box. No damage at all. It took three minutes to remove it from the box and put it together. The string head snaps into the shaft and you tighten it up with a star knob. Very clear instructions as to its starting procedures. It took 5 or 6 pulls after priming to get it to fire off and start running. Once running, it stayed running and after a few seconds, I set the choke on the recommended position and it never had a hiccup after that. I stopped the motor, waited a few minutes and restarted it just to see if it would start easy. It started several times with just one pull. Quick, high rev and with the .095 diameter string, it makes quick work of the weeds around my yard. It's very well balanced and fairly lightweight. If I had anything to change about it, I'd put a shoulder belt with it that could clip onto the motor housing. That would really make it comfortable in long sessions with the weeds. A complimentary bottle of 2-cycle oil is including, good for a couple of tanks of fuel. This is a good, lightweight trimmer and it does what it's designed to do.

I have a B&D; Electric weed wacker that generally can handle some maintenance for 1 week of growth in my yard.  I picked this up to handle the spring cleanup and when I might go a week or more due to time constraints.It was easy to assemble and use. I thought it was a more noisy and had more vibrations than the electric.  I couldn't complain on the results, and I thought it was very comfortable to use and had more power than the electric.  The trigger throttle was nice to use around my fence.My wife wasn't interested in using as she was fine with the simplicity of the electric.I'm also concerned with the longevity, which remains to be seen. My electric has lasted many many years.

Remington's RM2520 is easy to crank.  I'm a 45+ year old female that has always taken care of my lawn.  This weed-eater has a three step crank instruction printed on the side of the motor.  It's easy enough to crank and has a lot of power once cranked but I was unable to complete my entire yard. After weed eating around my house and sidewalk, not a very large area,  my hands and arms were shaking really bad from the vibrations of the weed eater.  Both my arms were weak and shaky for several hours after this small job.  I asked a male friend to finish for me and he too complained of aching arms and hands from the vibrations.  I have a GreenWorks battery powered weed trimmer that I used most of last year.  It is much easier to use and doesn't cause the weakness and pain in my arms.If you're young and strong this probably won't bother you.  If you're getting older, as I am, and have arthritis you will want to skip this one.

I would consider the Remington Wrangler an entry point gasoline trimmer.  For the price it's not a bad value.  Positives:  Easy to assemble, started easily, does the job.  Negatives:  Handle is not adjustable, tap to feed string as opposed to continuous feed, could use a shoulder strap.  I have a battery powered trimmer that I like much better.  Though it also lacks a shoulder strap, the handle is adjustable to work for the user's height.  Unfortunately, the battery wears out after about 90 minutes of use.  The gas trimmer will keep going after 90 minutes with a quick gas refill, however I think I might wear out first due to the weight and ergonomic issues.

This Remington RM2520 gas trimmer came packaged box within a box. The inner box wasn't packed in place and moved around so that this big box was rather cumbersome to get into the garage and unpack.PROS:*  Easy to assemble*  Good operator's manual; easy to read and tells you what you need to know*  Starts easily if you follow the instructions in the operator's manual*  Lightweight and well balanced*  Good power (we have a 1/4 acre lot and it has plenty of power even for big,  stalky weeds)*  Uses .095 heavy-duty line (still using original length of line; haven't had to "bump" the line to get more length and have used it four separate times so far)*  Adjustable head angle*  Accepts attachmentsCONS:*  Noisy compared to our older Ryobi trimmer*  Vibrates quite a bit so harder to use if you have arthritis or lower hand/arm strength*  2 cycle so have to mix oil and gas*  Don't like the clutch setup in the head - string doesn't spin unless the engine is revved up; harder to control the cutting speed when you're trimming around flower beds or more delicate items.For the price, this is a good trimmer especially as it will accept attachments. If you are willing to pay more, check out 4 cycle trimmers. Then you don't have to mix the oil and gas.

Bottom line: This is made by MTD and is very similar in terms of performance and features to other MTD brand gear (such as Yard Man, Bolens, Troy-Bilt, and several others). It offers decent homeowner-grade performance with the benefit of being attachment capable. Not heavy-duty enough for extensive use, and the bump head is very finicky.Full review: It’s getting tough to find something that isn't made by MTD these days. That’s not necessarily a bad thing since they make some decent gear considering the price. (They also make some really poor stuff as well.)This is one of their decent efforts. The main issue with the Remington, much like everything made by MTD, is that it’s intended for light-duty use. It’s perfectly fine for they typical suburban yard, but if you have a couple of acres to deal with, need something for commercial use, or want something that will last for a couple of decades, look elsewhere (I’d suggest brands such as Stihl or Echo. A lot more money, but a lot more durable as well).Starting/running – fired up pretty quickly right out of the box. It comes with oil and uses a 40:1 ratio (again, typical of most MTD devices). I did have to adjust the idle so it would run smoothly at low RPMs, which is easy to do (outlined clearly in the manual). It has a spring loaded pull rope which I really like. I have that on my Troy-Bilt machines, and it’s a great feature for folks like me with back problems. Rather than have to do a sharp tug to get it started, you pull the rope in a smooth motion. There’s a spring that compresses when you pull, and then releases. It’s hard to explain but easy to use and a great feature for ease of starting. The downside is that when the spring breaks, it’s a major, major pain to fix.Power – This has a decent amount of power (25cc 2-cycle engine) for getting through tough weeds, provided you use good quality line. Although this is attachment-capable, it does not have enough power to effectively run things such as a tiller attachment. It’s fine for most other attachments.Attachments – This has the typical split boom setup and will take attachments made by MTD (and their related brands such as Craftsman). I tried it with attachments from Troy-Bilt and Craftsman (an edger and a straight shaft trimmer head) without any problems.Weight/Balance – Decent on both. The vibration was not too bad – on a par with others in this price range. The grip handle is hard plastic but reasonably comfortable.Controls – straightforward. The build quality on some, such as the choke lever, is not great, so some care is needed to ensure it does not break. I like that the on/off switch is on the shaft near the handle so it’s easy to get to.Bump head – horrible! I didn't have much faith that it would work well since every other MTD bump head I've tried has been poor. This was no exception – feeding is sporadic and the force needed to feed out line puts way too much stress on the drive shaft (e.g., you’ll end up cracking it when bumping the line). If you get this, toss the bump head and get a fixed line head. You can pick one up at a home center store for just a few bucks. Yes, you’ll need to manually put the line in, but it’s very simple and far more reliable than the bump feed. Plus, you can use better quality line, such as Gatorline, which cuts through weeds much better than the standard stuff.Tip: MTD machines hate ethanol in gas – it will kill the fuel lines. I add both Sta-Bil and Sea Foam to my gas, and that has worked great. Zero problems with fuel lines, and all my 2-cycle machines have started and run well over the years.This is a decent choice for light-duty use. It’s not one of those tools that you’ll be able to hand down to the grand kids, but it will get the job done for several years (provided that you maintain it and use additives in the gas). The split shaft allows you to use this for multiple jobs, such as edging, or replace the curved shaft with a straight shaft. In comparison to a Stihl or Echo it’s quite poor, but, for the price charged, it’s a pretty decent choice. 5 stars since it delivers a good level of performance for the price.
summary: A decent value in an MTD-brand trimmer

reviewText: I was excited to get a new hedge trimmer to try out. First off this is gas powered, and you have to mix a little of the oil that comes with it into your gas to make it work. My husband is you still on more so he figured that out quickly. Unfortunately you have to go to step to push this button in this many times in this that and the other and then pulling the cord just like a manual lawn mower, which takes a lot of strength.  Unfortunately for me with not much upper body strength, I could not do it, my husband had to do it for me.  When he had it running and handed it to me, I had to pull the trigger to hold the trigger you have to hold the handle the handle absorbs and operates with every bump and run off the engine. Ouch!This is only a good machine for somebody with you is very strong with lots of muscles.For those with arthritis ,I reccommend my favorite hedge trimmer the Black and Decker 20 Volt.Black & Decker LST220 12-Inch 20-Volt Lithium-Ion Cordless GrassHog Trimmer/Edger.  Check out my review of it on the last page.For a tall person OREGON Cordless ST275-A6 40-volt MAX Trimmer/Edger Kit with 4.0 Ah Battery Pac is ideal.Pros:gas powered no electric cord.  easy to assemble.  Revs up and is very powerful and cuts big weeds.  Oil is included.  Dual line (2 separate lines) for more cutting faster.  Bump end to make it feed down more line.Cons:have to mix oil and gas.  GAS IS FLAMABLE AND DANGEROUS, SO you can not store machine with the gas and oil in it.
