For storing you have to drain the tank.Complicated to start between pressing buttons and putting and levers in certain positions and then trying to pull the cord like a lawn mower cord several times to get it to go.Unfortunately the throttle button is located on the shaft of the trimmer and it vibrates every movement of the engine .  After only 5 minutes, I could not take it anymore and had to stop.  It made my hand literally hurt for an hour even with the use of aceptomyphen.
summary: extremely powerful gas hedge trimmer.  This does vibrate a lot, so not for those with arthritis.

reviewText: I've had a few trimmers, and am somewhat shocked by the utter inability for a company to make a good string trimmer that lasts longer than a single seasons.  The most recent ones:Poulan Pro (that looked a lot like this one):  utter trash.  It lasted a few months (maybe a half-dozen uses) until it died.  Took it for repairs, got fixed even though the repair guy said it's not worth it because its made so cheaply.  Worked again for about a month, and the engine died again and the shaft had a problem where it didn't spin the head anymore.Husqvarna 128DJx 17-Inch 28cc:  Very nice motor and options, but the shaft and the motor are connected with A SINGLE BOLT.  It rattles out, and is lost...often.  (And the authorized service centers are all incompetent liars.)Now this Remington...  The motor is a bit louder as has more of a rattle than a purr (compared to the Husqvarna), but there are 3 bolts keeping the engine and shaft together, which is an obvious plus.  I waited as long as I could to review this to see if multiple uses would cause any issues to arise:  if anything, I'm more fond of this unit than when it was new (and I was skeptical.)  Starting with a cold engine on this one took 3 pulls (rather than 2 pulls with the Husqvarna, and infinite pulls with the Poulan), so no big deal there.As far as vibration is concerned:  I can't speak for the Poulan anymore, since I barely got to use it before throwing it away...but to me it feels like comparing the Husqvarna to this Remington, the Husqvarna had a LOT more vibration at the spinning head (which amplified as it went up the shaft), whereas the Remington has slighly more vibration at the motor.  For me, when I'm done using it after 20 minutes, the Remington make my hand, wrist and arms feel better than the Husqvarna.  Granted, they're not the same power, which may have something to do with it...but it's not THAT much more powerful.Overall, about a month into ownership, I'm using this more often than the double-priced Husqvarna.  Husqvarna can do more (brush cutter attachment, which comes in handy), but do to the design/engineering failure of connecting to the head to the shaft, it can't be used.  Meanwhile, the Remington has had no such problems, starts easily, doesn't shake my arm off, and does a great job.I'd recommend this trimmer, and if problems arise later (or I try out the attachments), I'll update this review at that time.
summary: Great trimmer even without extra options

reviewText: I own rent properties. When properties are vacant, I take care of yard work myself. I have one 40V battery-based trimmer. I use the battery-based trimmer for properties with small yard. But two properties have a 1/4 acre yard with quite some think grass and some heavy vines also. My battery-based trimmer can barely handle the thick grass and it always struggles with the vines.I am glad to get the more powerful gas trimmer. This Remington RM2520 Wrangler is pretty lightweight...about the same weight of my 40V battery-based trimmer. The included manual gives very clear instructions about how to prime the engine and how to start it. I have no problem to start the engine. This is my 1st time to use gas-powered tool, and I am surprised how easy to start the engine. So far, based on my limited usages in one month, it usually starts within 3 pulls. The start-up instruction is also printed on the air filter hosing. So, no worry to keep the manual book around.Though it is more noisier than my battery-based trimmer, it's still in an acceptable range. This trimmer balances itself quite well. Even better yet, the curved shaft makes the trimmer head in parallel position against ground when I stand up-right. This really eases my back, especially when I use this trimmer for long period of time on the 1/4 acre yard.When it runs, the shaft does vibrate, which does not occur to my battery-based trimmer. After 40 minutes of usage, my arm does not feel sour. So, I think the vibration is not that bad.The trimming line is about twice as thick as my battery-based trimmer. I guess the line will last longer. When in high rpm, this trimmer sweeps through thick grass like chopping off cake with knife. And it rips though the vines easily.The package comes with a bottle of oil to be mixed with gas by user. However, the 40:1 pre-mixed gas can is widely available in Home Depot or Lowes already. The pre-mixed gas is in an easy-to-use metal can. Better yet, they add gas stabilizer additive to keep the gas last longer in the can. That's really convenient.So far, I am happy with this Remington RM2520 Wrangler trimmer.
summary: Lightweight. Easy to start and runs smoothly.

reviewText: It's been a while since I've used a gas trimmer. I have an electric B&D; that's held up for five years, and I like it fine. I've got two 100-foot cords for the far reaches of the lawn, and I really appreciate not messing with gas and oil and their smell and mess and health issues. But if your lawn is acres, then a cord may not do it, and some battery models lack power. Hence a gas trimmer.This one is pretty good. Price it against Troy-Bilt, Craftsman etc as they're all made by MTD, so be aware of what you're getting. The pull is spring-loaded, easy for ladies and geezers, and it has a good balance. It is definitely not quiet, another big plus of electric trimmers. I'm not nuts about the bumper load, and usually just feed it by hand every few minutes. I also don't like double lines, as they seem to just use up double the line with no more performance, imagine that. The motor also vibrates a fair bit, and after about 30 minutes it can get a bit wearing on the hands and shoulder. It's not meant for all-day use, no doubt there.But it's less than a benjamin, so if you're a pro you're not looking at this. If you're a home owner with a very big yard, or long long driveway you want to edge, this might be just right for you, and seems made to last at least a few years (remember when a hundred bucks meant ten years easy?).But what with the hassle and mess and smell of gas, and the quiet and lightness and solid power of my nice cheap long-lasting electric trimmer, I won't be trading it in for a gas model quite yet.
summary: A little loud, not meant for professional use, decent for the price...but consider an electric first

reviewText: My husband always says I am hard on electronics, lawn equipment and appliances (I even managed to break off the door handle on the inside of a car once, but that's another story).  Anyway, like many reviewers here, we have been through numerous trimmers through the years, some not even lasting one summer.  Since I just starting using this one, time will tell how long it holds up.  I am impressed with it so far.  Easy to start and easy to use, it's a powerful trimmer that has done a great job for me so far on some tough yard areas.  I do notice quite a bit of vibration during use, but that's minor.It does accept attachments, which is a plus for me.  It's lightweight and well balanced, and started on the second try.  The manual is easy to understand, and the trimmer went together quickly.
summary: Great Trimmer, Powerful, But Some Vibration

reviewText: This is a very nice looking unit and was easy to assemble out of the box. I had to remove and toss two plastic covers from the ends of the trimmer parts. Then snap the trimmer end onto the motor half and tighten the handle. Then use a screwdriver and attached the trimmer guard to the end of the trimmer. The manual said to attached the handle but mine was already attached.I did not have as easy a time getting my unit started for the first as the other reviewers. Maybe my gas was old. I'm not sure. But for an ez-start unit, the manual sure tells you to pull the starter a lot. I tried choke in all positions, and finally got it going with choke and holding throttle on. After warming up, it would then run with the choke off. Until it warmed up, I needed to keep it on partial choke (position 2).Once it was going it worked well. I like the curved trimming attachment. It's easier than the straight one I have. It has plenty of power and was easy to hold. Noise level seemed average to me. I wasn't bothered by vibrations even at high rpms. Line feed smoothly when I bumped the head on the ground. And best of all, the grass and weeds cut very very well.As for mixing the gas and oil for 2 cycle engines this is normal. They do now sell 40:1 premixed gas at most stores with garden centers. It comes in a nice metal can with a screw on top and is very easy to pour. It is a little more expensive but I really like it. I use it for my chain saw and trimmers.Notes:- They now sell 40:1 premixed gas at most stores with garden centers- Easy to assemble out of the box.- Curved trimmer head allows for a comfortable trimming position when trimming- The choke has 3 positions 1=Full Choke 2=Partial 3=Run- To feed line just bump the head. This worked smoothly- Noise level seems average- I wasn't bothered by vibrations

I have no issues with this trimmer, it hits all the high points I look for on trimmer.  The price is right, it is easy to start, it isn't too heavy and isn't too complicated to use.  I have used this a couple of different times and have no issues and is quite powerful considering it is so light.  I do with the gas take was a little bigger, but I guess that is part of it being lightweight.  Being a girl, starting gas powered equipment as always been an issue for me and this guy starts right up with no problems.
summary: Good price on a good trimmer

reviewText: The Remington RM2520 Wrangler 17" grass trimmer is one of the lighter trimmers that I have used. It is well balanced with an adjustable front handle grip. The directions for starting the unit is printed large and clearly on the air filter housing. I find I forget the procedure for best starting over the winter. The air filter is very easy to get at for cleaning, though it is small and will likely have to be replaced at some point. It is just a ring of flexible foam material. By following the simple directions it started quickly and stayed running. The level of noise is roughly the same as any unit I have used.I have an older Ryobi (17")which is still working and also started with no problem this first time of use after winter. I am a firm believer in using premium gas with NO ethanol. Ethanol is very hard on small engines so... even though the Remington indicates that it can use up to 10% ethanol, I recommend not using it. But don't forget to add the proper mixture of oil to the gas.The string for this unit is .095 which is larger than I have used previously and should hold up better than the .080 for the old Ryobi.The one thing I really like about the Remington is the curved front end of the tube leading to the string. Though the Remington is about 4" shorter than the my old trimmer, it is more comfortable to hold. The string ends up parallel to the ground and is balanced there. I found with the old trimmer, I was always raising up my right arm (back arm on the trimmer) to get the string in the right position for cutting. This gave me a sore arm after some time working.The bottom line is that this Remington seems to be a good trimmer. I have no idea of the longevity of this trimmer since only time will tell. I'm giving my old trimmer away and just keeping the Remington.

So, let me just start by saying that I LOVE the design of this hummingbird feeder. It's really beautiful and you can tell that it's very well made. The glass is nice and heavy. It looks a lot better than our old, cheap plastic feeder.That having been said, I feel like I do have to say that the one BIG problem we're having with this feeder is that none of our hummingbirds will use it! With our old feeder, we had tons of hummingbirds that would come constantly and use it. With this one, they come, look at it, then fly away. They aren't even attempting it. In fact, we had our old feeder sitting on our porch for a few days, and they all went to that one instead, even though it was empty. Not sure what it is about this feeder that is deterring the birds from using it, but if we can't get them to use it soon, we may be forced to to buy a different feeder. Which is a shame, because we really like the look of this one.
summary: Beautiful, but not popular with our hummingbirds

reviewerName: Beth DeRoos "Beth DeRoos from the California ...
reviewText: Have a couple of these and they look so wonderful in our yard. The red glass doesn't fade like cheaper red plastic hummingbird feeders. Easy to clean which is a major plus, having had hummingbird feeders that took me half an hour to clean.Lovely in a shabby chic cottage garden or in a simple zen garden.  24 Ounce nectar capacity also is a plus because I don't have to fill it every day.

Last year, I got to add the greenish/clear bottle hummingbird feeder to our porch, and we've enjoyed it since! My only issues with it was the small hole to fill it and the very small latch to hang it. The latch is exactly the same on the red and blue feeder. It's still small, so you might have to work a bit at getting it to work onto your hook. We hang all of our feeders on our front porch from a hook, and I have to stand on something to work the hook into the latch on the bottle. I have to admit it's a pain.The hole to fill it is actually a little bigger than the green bottle. My funnel actually fits inside the hole(it didn't on the green one), so it's easier to fill. It still takes a little work, though. The hole still isn't big enough to just set the funnel on it and pour with both hands. You have to hold the funnel in with one hand and pour with the other. Of course, your funnel might be smaller! Mine is average sized(the Tupperware "door prize" kind).As far as looks, these bottle feeders are a *beautiful* edition to our yard! The birds love them! They arrived within a couple of days of putting their food in there. The red bottle is their favorite. I've always heard that hummingbirds are most attracted to red, but I got to see that for myself. In addition to the red one, and the greenish one, we also got the blue one. When the red one was empty, we swapped it out for the green one, and placed the red one at the back of the porch to wait for a refill. The birds would fly past the green and blue one(although they do still eat from them, too) and go to the red one.All three of the bottles we have are different shapes and sizes. The red is the biggest, the green the smallest. The red one is roundish, the blue one is squarish, and the green one is like a glass coke bottle.Overall, we really enjoy the beauty of these feeders, and think they're worth the pain of filling and hanging them!

You can't get just one hummingbird feeder, because one dominant bird will claim it and make you feel sorry for all the other hungry hummingbirds he persecutes.  I like the looks of this so much better than the cheap red plastic feeders.  However, I wouldn't pick this particular one again, because though it is stunning in appearance, it has some functional problems.It is hard to refill and hard to hang, this particular model, because the hanger thing is fixed close & tight against the bottom of the bottle.  I had to attach some chain to it in order to get enough distance to hang it on a nail on my eaves -- it would have been nice for the maker to include some chain.  Also the bottle cannot stand upright for refilling or cleaning, because of this hanger attached to the bottom.  When I prop it up to fill or clean it, the center of gravity is off and it is unstable, so I fear it may slip and break.  Look for a feeder that has a bail that can swing out of the way instead.Also, they describe the base as metal, but only the decorative top half is.  The bottom of the flying-saucer shaped base, where the nectar collects after it flows out of the bottle, is plastic.  I wonder if that affects the flavor of the nectar at all?  Since it still contains lots of nectar in the reservoir when the bottle appears empty, it is hard to know if refilling is needed asap or not (as long as the underside is made of plastic, why not make it be clear instead for easier monitoring?).However, it seems to work fine.  I hung it near where the hummers hang out near my bougainvillea.  The nectar started disappearing within a few days, even though it took a while to actually see that one hummingbird had claimed the feeder and was chasing others away.UPDATE:  After a few weeks of use, nectar consumption dropped off, and on the next regular cleaning I found why:  Ants had discovered it, with a path up to my roof and down the metal hanger into the nectar resevoir.  There were at least 50 ants drowned in it, giving it that ant smell.  No wonder the poor things quit drinking from it.  Since ants won't cross a line of turmeric, I have added some at the top where  it hangs, hope that will work. But now I'm going to look for ant-proof feeders with a better hanger, as well as perches. [7/18/2013]
summary: Birds (& Ants) like it; bottle can't stand upright for filling, plastic base

reviewText: Oh this feeder is SO much prettier than the photos portray it to be! Such a lovelyred and in the sun...really pretty...I don't know how the hummer's will be able to resist this. When I received it I wanted to get it cleaned and hung up..it was easy enough to clean, what is good...as you need to keep hummingbird feeders clean cleanclean. Found that after a couple of days we had some little hummers eating away at this feeder...that makes me happy!  I think this would be a great gift for any bird lover, its that pretty.
summary: Red antique type bottle Hummingbird feeder

reviewText: Just like with thePerky-Pet 8108-2 Green Antique Bottle 10-Ounce Glass Hummingbird Feederand thePerky-Pet 8109-2 Red Antique Glass Bottle16-Ounce Hummingbird FeederI had birds the first day.  I think the red bottle helps to attract them and it looks so pretty hanging from the lattice over our deck.  What I really like, though, is how easy these are to clean.  The bottle is easy to rinse clean if you do it often, but if you do get a little buildup, theseCasabella 20530 Soft Tip Brushes, Set of 3work great.  The base comes apart in two pieces so it's super easy to clean it well too.
summary: Easy to Clean and My Birds Find Them Easily

reviewText: This is a gorgeous bottle, the bottom (where it shrinks and goes into the dispenser) has the raised leaves that really set the bottle off.  The bottle is pretty large (a little fatter and taller than a 20oz bottle of soda).  The opening is a little thin and you might find it a little easier to use a funnel to fill it, but it is possible to do without a funnel (it just takes a little more time).  The metal flowers on the dispenser are gorgeous.  I have three of these (a few different sizes and designs) and hummingbirds love them, I often see them flying around these and drinking from it (they do not land, they just hover near it).  I will admit that I do not love the hooks that these have (the metal pictured at the top of the glass), it is to small to hang on my garden hooks (to get around it, I wish they would include something to make it larger), so I always have to use Zip Ties to make a loop to go around it and hang it (I could buy a metal ring, but the plastic Zip tie works for me).I really like these glass and copper like feeders.  They are much better than the plastic ones (clean easily) and seem to last much longer.  These are easy to fill (either with a funnel or carefully by eye), and when you screw the base on and flip it (do it fast) it fills in the dispenser at the bottom and than is good.  You can just hang it and they will come (I use the pre-made [not concentrate] hummingbird feeder that you get at Walmart).  I think these are a gorgeous additional to the garden and put these near my flowers.  They are gorgeous and last much longer than the plastic ones!  Highly recommend (plus their weight helps avoid the wind knocking out the food)!!
summary: Beautiful Bottle and feeder at bottom

reviewText: This is a real jewel of a feeder, easy to fill and clean (use a bottle brush), truly sparkles in the sun. Placed next to another style feeder the little guys don't seem to have a preference and feed equally between the two. It has a nice feel to it, solidly made, everything fits together with zero leaks or issues.All the parts are chinese but it's assembled in the US. It came assembled and carefully packaged and after cleaning, filled it and had a hummingbird feeding from it within an hour of opening the box.Highly recommend.
summary: A really nice feeder, a red jewel in the garden.

reviewText: I recently got this to complement the green (pale) 10 ounce model that i have had for a couple of years.  I prefer the green bottle which I find much more attractive and natural-looking for the garden.  However I thought the red bottle might be more attractive to the hummingbirds but so far, not the case.  The feeders are hanging about 15 feet apart and the hummingbirds prefer the green one by 2:1.  I do like the larger 24 ounce capacity of this bottle.  If the feeding pattern changes, I will update this review.

I have 4 hummingbird feeders.  This one is definitely the nicest looking of the group.  The hummers seem to prefer the Hummzinger feeders (2) but that may just be because those were the first and they are use to them.Aspects 367 Hummzinger Ultra Hummingbird Feeder, 12-OunceThe forth feeder is a Perky Pet feederPerky-Pet 132TF 24-Ounce Glass Top Fill Hummingbird FeederThis one is also new and while it is easy to clean and fill, I don't like the way it looks as much.This feeder does have a narrow opening for refilling.  That makes it a bit more difficult, but not bad if you pour the solution in slowly.  I rinse all of my feeders with boiling hot water.  Never use soap!  Hummer HATE soap and no matter how much you rinse, they can tell :-(  All of my feeders contain homemade hummingbird food:  1 cup water + 1/4 cup white sugar.  I use boiling water to make the solution and put it into the feeders as soon as the sugar dissolves.  Close the feeders and then give them a chance to cool off before hanging them back outside.  Using boiling water helps keep the solution from going back so quickly.

This feeder is very nice looking and being bright red negates the need to color the "nectar" solution. I hung it up where we had the old one and we've got male and female humming birds feeding at it about every couple of minutes. The glass is gorgeous with sunlight shining through it and it puts a red glow onto the copper base. It's easy to take apart and clean the bottom parts, and easy to put back together. The bottle is tough to clean when mold gets into it.  Any bottle brushes I have bought don't fit. I may try the blue one out also, but I don't know if humming birds find blue as attractive as the red color.

I hung this new antique bottle style hummingbird feeder yesterday, and already have a few of the little guys hanging around.  I got the red bottle so it would be noticed right away, and it was! The bottle holds about 3 cups of nectar. I filled it with clear nectar, and it is difficult to see the level of the fluid in the dark red bottle, but I'll manage!  The Perky Pet brand makes a lot of nice feeders, but the best thing about this one is the ability to clean the two bottom sections. The bottle screws into the plastic bottom, with the metal top part with flowers in between. Other feeders have a one piece bottom that is impossible to clean properly. My other Perky Pet feeder has a ring around the bottom so the birds can perch while drinking, and I thought that with this new one they would have to hover, but there is a raised rolled rim around the edge that is perfect.  It is a very elegant looking and attractive hummingbird feeder.

this is so beautiful. it is a glass bottle that screws into the metal bottom. Just unscred and the top separates from the bottom metal part.  Fill the red bottle scred into place hten trun over and hang.  The red glass bottle is easy to break so be careful. The hummingbirds are attracted by the red, and seem to feed easily fromthe 4 flower ports in the metal. Highly reccommend.
summary: Lovely Red Antique looking Hummingbird feeder. Easy to fill and use.

reviewText: since hummingbirds are attracted to red, this is a great color and the brass bottom is a good accent.  this is glass and a little heavy, so be careful where and on what you hang it from.  heck, the 1st day we hung it the hummingbirds darn near drained it.  they seem to really like this feeder, even over the plastic ones wehave hanging.  wehave feeders out all year long so we will see if this product lasts through th winter
Very impressive looking nectar feeder. I like everything about it. It's attractive, unique looking, and easy to fill. It took awhile but it now does attract hummers.
summary: Very attractive feeder It took awhile, but now it attracts hummers.

reviewText: I have a number of hummingbirds in my garden, and while I love watching them flit around my plants and drink nectar, I was hoping to draw them a little closer to my home so that I can take the occasional photograph or just enjoy watching them a little closer.I hate those tacky little plastic hummingbird feeders, so I was delighted to see this antique bottle style feeder, which has copper detailing and a much more attractive look. I like that the bottle itself is red, so that it attracts the birds, and I found it easy to hang and easy to clean using a normal bottle brush.Overall, this is a great little hummingbird feeder and a nice alternative to those ubiquitous plastic ones. I would certainly recommend it as a gift for anyone who loves hummingbirds or bird feeding in general.
summary: Cute and effective little hummingbird feeder

reviewText: I have a  collection of these glass hummingbird feeders, they are so much nicer than the plastic ones. (I still have a few of those left too) I just received this pretty red one as a birthday gift and I love it! I have the copper one with leaves, the green, the deep blue, now this red one. They look so nice hanging outside on the patio. When the light hits them just right they look so pretty.  :)I like how the bottom part is plastic, that helps protect their little feet from getting burned on the metal piece so they can still perch while they drink or look around. I have some metal S hooks that I use with these to make hanging easier. I haven't had any problems keeping these clean, if I find any gunk inside or around the edges anywhere I use a tiny brush and it comes right off.The larger bottle size keeps me from having to refill them too  often, as it is we are buying sugar in the large Costco bags a few times a year. Hungry little birds. :)

reviewerName: In Memory of W. G. Simms
reviewText: We have relied on the Perky Pet model 203CP "pinch waist" type hummingbird feeders for years and those are durable and fairly user friendly.The fact that this feeder is red is the reason for giving it a try; we'll see whether or not the seemingly somewhat flimsy metal parts will stand the test of time.As far as attracting the little buzzers goes, jury is still out on whether it does a better , worse, or equal job to our old standby model 203CP.Will amend this review at summer's end!
summary: **** MIGHT HAVE DURABILITY PROBLEMS COMPARED TO OTHER PERKY PETS ****

reviewText: Beautiful feeder that holds plenty of nectar.  The insides of the copper flowers are enameled red, so the birds have no problem spotting where to drink. I have this red feeder and the similar blue glass one, and they both work equally well. The best part is that it is already red, so I don't ever have to color my sugar water or use pre-colored granules.  The humming bird's laid eggs suffer from the mother's exposure to most of the red colorants, so avoiding it is a priority.  I want lots of healthy baby humming birds in my garden in the years to come.
summary: Birds see the flowers just fine

reviewText: Very attractive Feeder---looks great in our back  yard and the Hummer's love it--Orioles do also!! I would definitely recommend--this is one of 4 Hummingbird feeders I own-it's very nice.
If you're looking for a gift-quality feeder, this one is very nice. Looks attractive and expensive, but won't break the bank. Also seems very durable and like it will last for many seasons.

This feeder is very nice looking and simple to set up. I have filled the feeder with sugar water and set it out for the birds and so far haven't seen any. I did find some ants visiting it, so it needed to be moved. Once it is settled into a better place I am hoping the hummingbirds will find it and begin to use it. The feeder is exactly as pictured and seems to be very good quality so I don't have any problem recommending this feeder to anyone with hummingbirds in the area and who can keep it away from the ants.

This Hummingbird feeder looks exactly like the picture with a design on the glass, a red color that is radiant, and it attracts the birds quickly.It has a sturdy thick wire hanger on the top and it is even attractive! The only thing that you may not notice is that the bottom part under the flowers is plastic, but does seem sturdy. The rest of the feeder is top quality, made with glass and metal. The little red flowers are even metal and attached to a brushed, copper metal top(wish it was brown like the blue feeder). It also sits flat and does not tip if you should need it to do that. It looks so great in the yard. I have the blue & red feeders but I have noticed that on both of them there is no place for the birds to rest and eat. Of course in nature the are always hovering to get their nectar so I guess they will be fine.Initially the birds are definitely attracted to red over the blue but they use both feeders. The Orioles have a harder time trying to eat out of this feeder than the plastic feeders.It is fairly easy to clean but**You will need a bottle brush to clean it and a chain or hook to hang it from.*** I used a zip tie to hang it at first because it was so gorgeous that I wanted it up quickly.Make Your Own Food: 1 c. filtered water/1/4 c. sugar, boil in microwave or on the stove-done! Double or triple as needed...cheap!

This feeder looks much better in person than on the website photos.  The color is a deep, rich red that positively glows in the sun.I disassembled it and cleaned it well prior to putting it out and found it to be easy to clean, and that is a big deal if you keep up with your feeders like you're supposed to.Most of my hummingbirds have already migrated on this year, but have a few stragglers that are still around.  I haven't seen them on this feeder yet, but that could be because they've habituated to the four feeders already on our property these past couple of months.  I am removing all of them except for this new one to see if they like it.Will change review if I find that they won't use this feeder.UPDATE:  After almost a year of use I thought I'd provide an update on this feeder.  The hummers still love it as do I.  IT IS IMPORTANT TO NOTE that you cannot wash this in the dishwasher!  After one washing all of the red coating was in the bottom of the dishwasher :>(.  I now have a pretty clear glass feeder and I'm happy with that.  I always run all seven of my hummer feeders through the dishwasher sanitizer cycle once per week.  It's the fastest/easiest way to clean them and I'm not going to fool with hand washing, scrubbing and sanitizing the inside of this particular feeder with it's narrow neck.  So, the price I paid for convenience was the beautiful red coating.  I still give the feeder 5-stars.

What I Like ~ This is a sturdy & quality made feeder, and the level of liquid can easily be seeneven through the rich red color of the glass.The hanger is made of  heavy metal wire, & four flowers on the top side of the base (the feeding ports)give a rich appearance against the copper finished metal cap.The bottom of the base is made of plastic. The total height is 11 1/4".This feeder has a rich appearance, and is the most attractive one we've owned.It seems we only have a few birds coming to our feeder, so this 24 oz is larger then we need.But I'll fill it approx 1/4 full and that's about right to last and stay fresh,for the approx 3 days before the time comes to empty, clean, & provide fresh food.What I Don't Like ~ As for ease of use, I was disappointed to find the inside opening of the topis only 5/8" diameter, and requires a funnel when filling.It's 10" deep to the inside bottom of the bottle, so this feeder isn't going to be very easy to clean.I purchased a bottle sponge specially for clean hummingbird feeders,but it's difficult to push through the top even when wet, and lacks 2" of reaching the bottom.My regular bottle brush with the little cotton ball on top, will go through the opening,but it also lacks 2" of reaching the bottom.I have a good variety of bottle sponge/brushes but none will clean this feeder.This product is likely, only going to get shaken for a cleaning, which is NOT what I prefer.The tag says to hand wash with soap & water twice a week, & for extra cleaning use vinegar & water.The hanger is of strong quality, but is somewhat close to the glass, - 1".If one isn't quick about the "tipping to the side & hooking motion", an 'S' hook may help.Four stars because of poor design for cleaning, which greatly subtracts from enjoyment.

I love having bird and hummingbird feeders out..Am in Va so according to PBS program on hummingbird migrations weget them on way back down to Mexico...or those who are flying to the tune of a different drummer! I never tire of watchingthese tiny birds and the varied colors and personalities they have.I use boiling water from the kettle in ratio of 1/4 cup sugar for each cup water...stir to dissolve..if in hurry use less boilingwater, stir well to dissolve, and top with cold water and stir again when in hurry. My Mother used to love watching the several feeders she had outside her windows in California...I was worried none would come since we are not in the MAIN DRAG so to speak, but they come.I like the antique look of this and just saw the cobalt blue so am ordering that today...they can go thru the dishwasher which I like,just a little tricky making sure all lined up so no leaks, but worth the effort! I like thinking I am helping the little ones get on their wayfor the migration...amazing creatures. If you see it on schedule on PBS make sure not to miss it...or Amazon has it !
summary: GREAT LOOK for a GREAT SERVICE!

reviewText: This feeder is even prettier in person.  The color is deeper red than it looked to me in the picture and it is beautiful when the sun hits it.The only thing keeping this from being a perfect feeder for me is there isn't a perch and I love to watchthe hummingbirds sit and look around.  But I keep a feeder out with a perch too so I have the best of both worlds in observing them.Very pretty design in the glass too.  Assembled in the USA of Chinese Parts.*Update* I decided to take it down and put up a different one.  This is such a pretty feeder, but it's not practical.  Also, after a month of use the red has started chipping off already. Cleaning the base is simple, but the inside glass gets slimy and the mouth of the bottle is so narrow that I can't get anything in there to clean it out.  I shake soap and water in it, but it still has some slime.

I love this feeder.  I'm an avid hummingbird feeder.  I have 4 feeders out at a time.  This one is very beautiful.  I love the copper bowl and the bright red antique look bottle.  A lot of times people think they need to add red dye to the sugar mix, but it's really bad for the birds.  This feeder will eliminate the temptation to do that.  It looks like it will be pretty easy to clean.  The bail hanger is a little tight, but it did fit on my wrought iron pole, barely.A very pretty addition to my yard.  And, the hummingbirds like it!!

This antique red bottle has been fashioned into one of the most attractive hummingbird feeders I've ever seen.  In addition, I appreciate having glass rather than the ubiquitous plastic feeders that abound in the hardware store.  I handle it carefully, it is glass after all, but I know that the bright sunlight will not cause it to crack, spilling sugar water all around.  In addition, the bright red color means I do not have to use the commercial feeds that contain red dyes.  The hummers can't miss this feeder.Just now, the hummers are focusing on pomegranate  blossoms rather than the feeders I've hung for them, but I feel sure that when blossom time is past, they will permanently migrate to this feeder.It's a delight, and I'm happy to recommend it to other hummer lovers!Five Stars!

Lovely Bird feeder.  It is definitely the prettiest of the bunch.  I have several plastic feeders and on glass feeder of the traditional hourglass shape.It took a while for the birds to find it but now it is one of their favorites.

Arrived quickly and in one piece.  The bottle is quite heavy but the jury is still out as to whether this is colored red or truly red glass - time will tell.  I did fill it and hang it in an "out of the way" area where I've never fed the hummers before.  Within hours - they were at this feeder in a continuous flow.As for the design - when you remove the bottom (feeding ports), it comes off in two pieces.  The feeding ports are metal on a metal housing.  That just slips onto the screw part of the bottle.  The bottom (round part shown in photo) is actually plastic.  Not only is that disappointing but it's harder than it should be to screw back onto the bottle and tighten.  The last drawback that I can think of - it's big.  If you don't have a lot of hummers eating, don't fill it completely.  And especially in the sun because you'll be throwing away more juice than the birds can drink.  It's not that expensive with sugar and water but it's a pain with that sticky water!In closing - it looks brilliant in the sun and the birds seem to have no trouble eating from it.  I'll have to keep you posted on the red coloring.

I love this hummingbird feeder.  The top is made of red glass that has a vintage style. It is quite beautiful!  (I get a lot of complements.)  I also have the company's older version which is smaller and made of clear glass.  I have to say that they have made some really nice improvements.First of all, they have increased the bottle size so you can fill it up with more sugar water.  Since the bottle is also heaver and larger it also makes the feeder more stable.  My smaller feeder has trouble tilting or falling over.  Also, while my clear feeder is very pretty, the hummingbirds just aren't as attracted to it so I had to add a couple red bows.  Since the new one is bright red.  It makes a fantastic beacon for hummingbirds!  The only real pain is cleaning and refilling the bottle since you can't keep the sugar in the feeder too long.
summary: Simply beautiful and the company has made improvements

reviewText: This hummingbird feeder couldn't be any better. It's beautiful, well-constructed and the birds love it. This is not one of those cheap plastic pieces of crud that moves in the wind and falls apart after one summer. This is a top-of-the-line feeder.PROS:Beautiful artistic red bottle.Bottle is real glass.The entire feeder is heavy so it's doesn't sway in the breeze scaring off the birds.The design makes it easy for birds to feed.Easy to clean and refill.Has a notched wire to keep the feeder centered on the you chain (of rope) when hanging.The feeder part looks so much like copper it may actually be copper.Excellent price on Amazon.CONS:None.

I received this hummingbird feeder today and I am very pleased with it. It's a beautiful jewel toned red and the antique brushed copper base is a nice compliment to the glass color. It a very sturdy feeder and the glass is nice and thick.  The base screws off and it's really easy to clean. The only caveat is that there's no hanging cord with it and the metal ring at the top isn't large enough to hook it over the metal hook I hang my feeders from so I had to fashion a hanger for it using some clip rings.  It does look just lovely hanging off the deck in the sun though and the hummingbirds seem to like it as well.

Our house is from the Victorian era, so the feeder fits right in with the look of the house/garden. The feeder has a nice, heavy metal hanger.  We have it hanging on a Shepard's hook in one of the flower beds which works out perfectly.  We've had the feeder out all summer without any rusting or wear; it looks as good as the day we got it.  We really like that the glass is red so we don't need to buy the red colored "food". Only one hummingbird has been feeding at it sporadically, but we are hopeful more will come.
summary: Looks great in a Victorian garden

reviewText: This is the perfect gift for the hummer lover or bird lover.  I have had butterflies stop by once in awhile and once I had a oriole drink from it.  I also have the cobolt blue one and the green one and love them all.  They are a very sturdy product but make sure to screw on the bottom properly or it will leak.  Everything needs to be lined up just right.I make my hummer juice from 1/4 cup sugar to 1 cup of water and bring to a boil in a pan.  Remove if from the heat once it starts boiling and let it cool before you put it in the bottle otherwise you might crack the glass.  Having a few of these keeps my babies from fighting so we are all happy campers as they get to feed and I get to watch.  One of the best things I could have gotten out of all the versions out there.

This hummingbird feeder looks like a beautiful piece of Yard Art.  In the morning light the heavy glass bottle glows and the brushed copper base shimmers.  The little copper flowers are also awesome, so intricate and detailed.The only thing that worries me is the absence of hummingbirds.  I do have a few hummingbirds in my yard, but I haven't seen one visit the feeder.  I'm worried that the little copper flowers are not bright enough, and there is not enough contrast between the color of the flower and the color of the base.I will watch it for a few weeks and see what happens.  If no hummingbirds visit I may try painting the flower a brighter color.But even if no hummingbirds visit the feeder, it still looks beautiful in the yard.
summary: No Hummingbirds yet, but the feeder is a beautiful piece of Yard Art

reviewText: Having purchased just about every type/design Hummingbird Feeder on the market, we finally discovered a quality  Glass Top Fill Feeder.  As the manufacturer's description indicates, this feeder has "exclusive top fill technology, 8 ounce hardened glass bottle [and] soft decorative flowers [most importantly] built in ant moat.  The top fill/no spill design and easy to clean feeder is a welcome addition to our feeding station.  The easy to follow step by step Filling, Disassemble/Reassemble and Cleaning Instruction and pictorial/text parts scheme come with the Feeder.  In addition to an 800 number and/or  website URL for questions and stuff.  No doubt will order more - highly recommended.

The Perky-Pet 130TF 8-Ounce Glass Top Fill Hummingbird Feeder is well designed and easy to use.  It is easy to fill and the ant trap on top keeps ants out of the sugar water.  Hummingbird nectar is made from 8 ounces of boiled water mixed with a 1/4 cup of sugar which is allowed to cool before being added to the hummingbird feeder.Just a note - do not add dye to the water.  It serves no purpose and could be harmful to the hummingbirds.  Some people used to believe that red dye helped attract the hummingbirds.  Use cane sugar only to make the nectar.  Do not use honey, brown sugar, unrefined sugar or sugar substitutes to make the nectar, as they can be harmful to hummingbirds.Be sure to clean the feeder frequently.Some notes from Domino Sugar on making Hummingbird Nectar:Hummingbirds feed on a combination of flower nectar and insects. Flower nectar is a plain chemical solution of sugar and water, known simply as Sugar Water. Many suppliers of birdfeeders sell commercially made hummingbird nectar however hummingbirds seem to prefer homemade sugar water best. Table sugar, or sucrose, is the most digestible form of food giving them the quick burst of energy they rely on. Domino Sugar has no preservatives or additives.Hummingbird Nectar:1 cup tap water cup Domino Granulated Pure Cane SugarTo make your own mixture, bring tap water to a boil and stir in Domino Granulated Pure Cane Sugar. Allow mixture to cool to room temperature before adding it to your feeder.To yield larger portions, mix at the ratio of 1 part sugar to 4 parts water. The solution will keep in the refrigerator for up to two weeks.Please don't use food coloring, honey, brown sugar, unrefined sugar or sugar substitutes, as they can be harmful to hummingbirds. Under no circumstances should insecticides or other poisons be used at hummingbird feeders.More Hummingbird Facts from Domino Sugar:Besides nectar, hummingbirds consume protein in the form of insects which they find inside flowers, on plants and in trees, in spider webs and in midair as they travel through your yard. Consider that when using pesticides in your yard and gardens. Hummingbirds also drink plain water.Hummingbirds feed 5-8 times an hour.Hummingbirds have the greatest energy output, gram for gram, of any known warm-blooded animal. If your sugar water freezes, replace it immediately (even at dawn). They rely on established food supplies.A hummingbird's wings can beat 200 times per second during courtship!A hummingbird's tongue is roughly twice the length of its beak. It licks the nectar. (Approximately 13 licks per second!) You might see its beak and think that it can't reach the nectar in the bottom of the feeder. Look closely with binoculars to see the tongue.The Bee Hummingbird is the smallest hummingbird in the world at 2" long, weighing 1/15 of an ounce!The best way of attracting Hummingbirds is to use a combination of their favorite flowers, plants, shrubs and vines; and, of course, homemade nectar of Domino Granulated Pure Cane Sugar and water.
summary: Great - Nice Size, Well-Designed.  Just Fill with Granulated Pure Cane Sugar Water Without Dye.

reviewText: This is my third Perky-Pet hummingbird feeder and they are all well-constructed and they all attract a lot of hummingbirds. This model has some nice enhancements over my earlier models. It's very easy to fill through the wide, top opening.  No more need to fill and invert!  And if you've ever had a feeder attacked by ants you'll love the built-in ant moat.  Finally, with the wide opening on the top and the removable feeding ports this model is very easy to keep clean.  All-in-all a great product!

Sturdy, easy to fill, and attractive. The flowers are nice and flexible. A bottle brush and some hot water will keep it clean between fillings. I do wish it had perches for the birds to rest on, but the overall construction and design is excellent. Looking forward to seeing more hummingbirds this year.

I love hummingbirds and this feeder is well designed.  It does not leak and I don't have to worry about bees bothering the hummingbirds while they feed.  The ant trap is very effective in blocking ants and bees who are attracted to sugar water.  If you want to treat your hummingbirds to a sweet repast, it's very simple.  Just follow these steps:Boil 1 C waterAdd 1/4 - 1/3 C sugarLet cool.Fill your feeder.Wait for the birds to come.The feeder itself is very easy to clean and frequent cleanings are required.  NEVER add dye of any color to your bird food - instead, place the feeder among brightly colored flowers.  I have read that any color will work equally well.  You are not limited to red.  You can set your bird feeder among blue, yellow or multicolored flowers.When you make food for your hummingbirds, always use cane sugar.  NEVER use any viscuous liquid sweetener of any kind.  NEVER put dye in your hummingbird food mixture.  The dye contains additives and serves no real purpose and could harm the birds.  Again, NEVER put dye in the mixture.  Refrigerate any mixture that you don't use.  It will keep for 1 1/2 - 2 weeks.
summary: It's Time to Feed the Hummingbirds!

reviewerName: Beth DeRoos "Beth DeRoos from the California ...
reviewText: There are so many reasons I love this hummingbird feeder.  Starting with the wide opening for pouring the sugar water in. Less mess.  Then there is the ant reservoir on top where you can place either water or in my case water with a drop or two of non GMO vegetable oil.And because I live in a wee cottage I love the size. This is perfect for someone in an apartment with a deck area, or a boat, or even a small trailer.  And the feeder itself is so easy to clean with such a wide mouth. Something my old hummingbird feeder lacked.Will post some photos which show the feeder with the top removed as well as the ant reservoir.
summary: TEN stars  LOVE this for so many reasons

reviewText: To be honest we were a bit skeptical when we selected this feeder given there are no perches for the Hummingbirds to rest on, like all the four different style Hummingbird feeders we own (on years when we have been on the migration path for Ruby-Throated and Black-Chin Hummingbirds we have had as many as 11 feeders on our property with "Hummers" in holding patterns awaiting (not always very patiently may we add--they are VERY cute but can be EXTREMELY possessive and/or aggressive!!!) their turn to fill-up. We placed this feeder next to one of our feeders with a circular perch that has been very popular and by the end of the day the nectar level of the Perky-Pet feeder was much lower that the other feeder--our fears had been disproved! The top opening feature make the feeder extremely easy to refill and it is also much easier to clean given you can open both ends. The built in ant moat on the top is also an excellent and effective feature as well. The layout of the bottom portion makes it easier to carry without spilling nectar and we have not seen siphoning like we have with at least two of our other styles. Well designed and constructed. bogie & tene'

I scored this item in the middle for two reasons. First, on a positive note the upper portion of the humming bird feeder is well constructed. The sugar water can be poured in the top and spare the normal mess of other feeders. Second, there is a negative note. The bottom part of the humming bird feeder is poorly and cheaply constructed. The plastic is too fragile. A part was broken off just in the shipping of the item to me.

Disclaimer: I am reviewing a unit I received for free through the Vine program.This is a nice hummingbird feeder. We have 3, sometimes 4 set up spread out across the back of our house, and we break them sometimes, so we have tried out a number of different brands and models, and this does seem to be the nicest one so far, for a couple of reasons in particular.1. Its small; the glass container is smaller than all the other feeders we've tried. The reason this is good is that you're supposed to change the liquid fairly often, but it's pretty much impossible for little hummingbirds to drink all the liquid contained in bigger ones, so you waste most of it & have to throw it away, with larger feeders.Also being small this would encourage you to put up smaller multiple feeders, which is good for most of the hummingbirds. They are very territorial, at least the males, and they fight viciously over each feeder! so generally one dominant alpha male chases away all the others, if you only have one feeder, or even if you have two that are too close to other. We spread ours out so a couple of them are around the corners, where the less dominant males still get a chance to feed without the mean alpha male chasing them away, meaning we have to fill up more feeders, so having them smaller like this works much better.2. You fill it from the top like a normal jar kind of container, with a nice normal fat wide screw-off lid on the top! and don't have to play the silly game you do with all other feeder designs, where you have to flip them over, fill them, and then carefully flip them again while full of liquid, trying not to spray/spill too much in the process. I wonder if all the other designers of other hummingbird feeders are kicking themselves and yelling "D'oh!" now that this one came out with such a logical design.(it has 2 lids, one nice one for refilling at the top, and then the usual one at the bottom like all other feeders, which has all the flower feeding hole thingies attached).
summary: very nice, better than other larger feeders

reviewText: Did you ever fill you old humming bird feeder and flip it to hang it and have the sticky goo all over you and the floor and the sink....well no more with the new hummingbird feeder from Amazon!  This is a wide mouth top you fill and screw it on then hang the feeder...no flipping it to get to the feed stations.  I love this convenience and you will too.  Order this from Amazon for you tiny feathered friends who come flittin by for that sweet nectar and give you such a breath-taking show in the process.Perky-Pet 130TF 8-Ounce Glass Top Fill Hummingbird Feeder

This a very nicely made hummingbird feeder. The wide mouth at the top makes it very easy to fill. It's heavy enough with the glass jar that it doesn't blow around in the wind like cheaper models, but not so heavy it's hard to handle. It comes completely apart, which makes it easy to clean. The ant moat at the top is a great concept and is easy to use.The instructions that came with it were not very helpful, however. They told me what to do, but now how to do it. I just had to figure out how to take the feeder apart and put it back together on my own. Illustrations and step-by-step instructions on how to disassemble and reassemble the base would have been nice.It took a while for the humming birds to find our feeder. They don't seem to linger as long to feed at this one as they do at feeders with perches.BTW--If you get this or any other hummingbird feeder, don't fill it with the red stuff they sell in most stores. It is laced with a dye that can actually make the hummers sick. I found a recipe for one part sugar or fructose to four parts water. You boil it for about two minutes, pour some of the cooled mixture in your feeder, and store the rest in the fridge. You have to clean the feeder once every 2-3 days with hot water and vinegar, so the mixture doesn't ferment and the feeder doesn't get gunked up.
summary: Very nice design; easy to fill

reviewText: A few short minutes after filling this little feeder and hanging it outside, the hummingbirds moved in for their first feast.  In the days since then, it has been a constant draw for the hummingbirds, as well as the occasional red headed woodpecker (its rather amusing to watch them acrobatically approach the thing!)  This feeder is brightly colored and sturdily built.  If you love hummingbirds, the Perky-Pet feeder will draw them in!  Great product.

This is a very high quality top-fill hummingbird feeder. Attractive, easy-to-fill, and it even has a water moat on the top to prevent ants from finding their way to the nectar (which may evaporate quickly). It has a small enough capacity to encourage frequent filling. And there's enough RED plastic, top & bottom, to attract the birds. It attracted hummers soon after being place on my front patio. My camera comes out next. Glass, so use some caution. Highly recommended.
summary: Very high quality feeder, attractive, easy to fill top opening, HIGHLY RECOMMENDED.

reviewText: This is one of the best feeders we've used. Most liquid feeders, like for hummingbirds, are notorious for getting slimy, sticky, slippery goo all over the place. Finally a feeder that opens from the top and allows you to pour without spilling. Where have you been the past 24 years?

It is within days before the first of this year's hummingbirds come looking for a quick sip and the new Perky-Pet 130TF will be there for them.  With the rains expected in the next few days it will be no sooner than Sunday before they arrive but they usually begin their new crop of tiny (real tiny) babies and that will add to the use of the feeders.  This time of the year is just more beautiful when several or more hummers are added to the yard.  This year with the addition of the 130TF we will have about 7 or 8 depending on hanging sites and each one will be refilled about 2 to 3 times a week with a 4 parts cooled sterilized water plus 1 part granulated sugar.This Perky-Pet is a new experience for us.  Top feeding makes so much more sense than bottom feeding.  It sounds good; however, the glass container and other components have to be cleaned.  I usually clean ours every time except when exceptionally lazy I will skip a cleaning if they were especially hungry.  Regardless, if it has to be turned upside down to add liquid or if the liquid if poured into the top it actually amounts to the same.  The birds could not care less so I won't either.There are no resting roosts for the hummers and too many of them it is no big thing.  If a roost is necessary for sitting and eating then there are other Perky-Pet locations in the yard for that.  I find it is more important to have parts that come apart easily and reattach similarly when cleaning is over.  The take down and put together is easy and quite effective when small pieces have to be cleaned and reused repeatedly.We are almost a 100% Perky-Pet household and the birds just enjoy their visits.  Not as much as we enjoy their presence I quickly add.
summary: They Are Coming; by the score, I hope

reviewText: This arrived on the day after I had my first hummingbird in the yard. I really like the top fill no more flipping over the feeder. I have wondered for years why they didn't make a top fill. I also like the glass as the plastic ones tend to get cloudy over years of use. The only con I can find is it didn't come with a hook or cord to hang it with. I had something here to use but usually you get a hanger. I still count it a 5 star product.
summary: Like the new top fill. Like that it is glass.

reviewText: This feeder holds just the right amount of nectar but after a few refills it began leaking.  Eight ounces is a good quantity for the birds to consume before the feeder should be washed out and refilled with fresh fluid.  When we first used it we were impressed with its superior functionality.  It's also attractive to have hanging outside a window.  Unfortunately, even though we gave it gentle handling and good care, it began to leak and ultimately became useless.
summary: Clever Design but This Hummingbird Feeder Eventually Leaked

reviewText: Great form, love the wider mouth for easy refill. Comes apart easily for cleaning. Includes a metal hook on top for hanging. Flowers have one large hole each, not the grid I've seen on past feeders. No cord or anything to hang it from.

This is a nice feeder. Sturdy core. Outside is flimsier plastic, but that's not really a problem. Smaller than it looks. Quite cute. Wide mouth top and easy to fill. A downside of the small size is that it doesn't last long, but that does keep you refreshing it.

I was quite pleased when I got this Hummingbird feeder that the clear container is not plastic, but glass!  I also loved that the flowers (the red part and the middle part where the bird would drink from) are not hard plastic but more pliable.  I believe that would be better for the hummingbirds.It still has that "classic" hummingbird feeder look, and the bright red color certainly does attract them (no need to put food coloring into your water - it can actually harm hummingbirds!)  I make my own food at home (sugar water) and refill as needed.This feeder also has a "moat" at the top that you can fill with water so that the ants can not get to your hummingbird food.  It hasn't been too hot here yet, but I imagine on a hot summer day it would not stay filled with water long, it isn't that deep.

This is a dream feeder...filling from top eliminates the mess that happens with most that have to be turned right side up, causing drips of sticky sugar water that often persists as you hang it...down the arm usually. I REALLY like the dishwasher capability too..no more toothbrushes and the mold issues. That can't be good for them either. I don't get too many because Va isn't a big area on their migration path but it is a thrill to see some turn up. So tiny and so many different colors. Try this feeder...you won't be disappointed!
summary: Top filler means NO sugary mess

reviewText: Not only is it well made but you fill it from the top. No longer do you have to fill it and turn it upside down to set it. I've had it outside for the past week and we've been visited by an early hummingbird twice so far. This area of Maryland has a lot of Ruby Throat-ed Hummingbirds. I am hoping to attract as many Hummingbirds as last year. I really like the design and workmanship of this feeder. Its recommended.

There are two features about this feeder that I particularly liked. (I maintain lots of hummingbird and other bird feeders):1. The small reservoir makes sense. Most people buy the larger feeders and after two or three days, the sugar water ferments and gets cloudy and they don't change it. This is not particularly good for the birds. So this feeder forces the owner to simply put in a new batch of sugar water. (It should be washed every time, which is easy to do.)2. The little flower pedals around the feeding holes are soft and pliable. I found them easier to clean than the hard plastic ones.On the top is an ant trap (which is just a small indentation around the top which you can put water in, OR, the rain keeps it pretty full. I had to laugh, though -- all my other birds are landing on the hummingbird feeder to use it as a drinking spot. This does not interfere with the hummingbird feeding.A very thoughtful design -- if you own only a single hummingbird feeder, this would be a great one to have. Highly recommended.
summary: For most folks, the perfect feeder

reviewText: While I like Perky-Pet feeders (especiallythis one), this small feeder misses the mark.  If you've got a serious hummer population, this 8-ounce feeder will empty in a day. But it falls a little short for other reasons.  It snaps together, supposedly for ease in cleaning (although their larger feeders aren't a problem in that regard).  The snap-together construction makes it feel a little cheap and it's a little hard to tell when it's properly assembled.  The top-filling opening, while a nice idea, is so large that it's still easy for fluid to slosh out as you carry the feeder.  The ant-trap (a little depression on top that holds water) will dry out in just a few summer hours.  You won't remember to fill it.But the biggest problem for me is lack of perches.  While it's fascinating to watch hummers feed on the wing, they'd prefer to take the load off and perch while they dine.  We have both rufous and blackchin populations, and they always choose feeders with perches.  Any energy that can be saved is an advantage to the bird.If hummers are infrequent visitors to your yard, then this little feeder is fine.  But when summer really gets going at our house, there are easily a dozen birds there.  They can drain 3-4 30 ounce feeders in a couple of days. Go bigger.
summary: OK for a couple of birds

reviewText: I am a first-time humming bird feeder owner, so I guess I never had to suffer through complicated humming bird feeders.  This one opens from the top, and you simply pour your nectar in.  I'm happy that the core of the container is made of glass.  The other parts are made of plastic, and let's hope they can hold up under the intense Arizona sun.  I am most concerned about the flowers as they are made of a soft rubber-like material that generally hasn't fared well under long term sun exposure.  Compared to my various neighbors' hummingbird feeders, I do see that they have larger feeders so it'll be curious to see how long 8 ounces lasts.  Included with the feeder are some disassembly instructions (for cleaning) in both English and Spanish.  Surprisingly, there is no 'nectar' recipe included.  Top of the feeder has an 'ant moat' which you can put water in to discourage and/or kill pesky ants.  I don't see that moat of water lasting more than a day during the summer in Arizona however so a bit high maintenance (but better than no moat).

I love having the hummingbirds around, and I use the Perky-Pet 30 ounce, bottom filling model (Perky-Pet 209 Our Best 30-Ounce Glass Hummingbird Feeder).  The hummers take about 3 weeks to empty the 2 feeders, then I cook up a new batch of nectar and fill them up again.This model holds only 8 ounces, and although the top-fill feature is convenient, it empties before the other feeders, then stays empty until I fill them all.So it works great as a feeder, but it is awkward having to make a new batch of nectar.  Yes, I could make more and store it in the fridge, but I'm already making over 60 ounces at a time in my pot.However, if you have only one or two hummers visiting, a smaller feeder may be just what the doctor ordered.  Perky-Pet knows their business.
summary: Why choose 8 ounces when you can have 30?

reviewText: I have two similar designed hummingbird feeders.  Immediately the hummingbirds prefer this one.  Could it be something to do with the design or materials?Works great

I've had many hummingbird feeders, but this is the first one that opens from the top. It is so much easier to fill, I didn't even need a funnel. And cleaning the glass jar is so much easier also. And if I'm going to be gone for a few days, I can top the nectar off. I like the ant moat on top also, as I do have that problem. I wish it was a little deeper though, as I think it will dry up very fast on hot days. I don't know if this feeder comes in a larger size, but if it does, I would like one. I feed a lot of hummers! By the way, you don't need artificially colored purchased nectar. Just boil 4 parts water and one part sugar for a couple of minutes, and let it cool.Well, sadly I'm only giving this 2 stars now instead of 5. Why? Because the hummers don't like it. It's not because it doesn't have a base. My other glass feeder doesn't either, and they love my old one. I have this one hanging in a small oak tree, so the have lots of places to sit after eating. So I think it must be the rubbery flowers. maybe I can switch the flowers from my other old perky pet feeder.

This hummingbird feeder is AWESOME!  It features TOP FILL and the jar is a heavy glass!  So easy to clean and fill!  Ant moat on the top to fill with water, soft plastic "feeding flowers" and a great design all make for one of the best hummingbird feeders on the market today!
summary: Perky Pet Hummingbird Feeder - Beautiful, Easy and GLASS!

reviewText: Like many hummingbird feeders from Perky-Pet, the bright red fixture really attracts the hummers, even with clear sugar-water solution (which is what I use - birds don't need red dye). The glass is a nice, solid construction. The top-loading feature makes it less likely you'll be spilling ant-attracting hummer food on the ground as you flip the bottom-fill versions over. The supplied hook was unusable on my shepherd crooks in my yard, so I got a large metal S hook at the store to hook this on there.I already had another hummingbird feeder, so I cleaned and filled both feeders - my old one and this one and put both out at the same time right next to each other (about a foot apart) for the first time this season. It only took about an hour before I started hearing the delightful chirping from our native ruby throated hummingbirds and they quickly were visiting the old feeder. The difference? This top loader does not have a perch for the hummers to rest. Why hover when you don't have to?I wanted to take photos/video of the hummingbirds feeding with my iPhone, but it was a tad chilly out, so I moved the old feeder to a crook closer to sunlight so I could watch and be warm at the same time. When having to choose between visiting a feeder with a human or without a human, the hummingbirds were then going to the top-loader (this model being reviewed)  even though there was no perch... but only when I had the old one near me. When I placed it back next to this one - they instantly chose to use the one with the perch.Hummingbirds are very territorial and seem to fight more than they tend to drink/eat. We're on 1 acre, and we sometimes get 5-6 hummingbirds (males & females) who all think that our land is THEIR property - so they dive bomb each other and rarely do we get more than 3 at the feeders at a time - usually just one, before another 1 or 2 come to drive the interloper away. Even with the second feeder, they prefer to congregate at the one with the perches. I think the reasons are multifold. They not only can take a more leisurely drink, but the buzzing of their wings is very audible and helps to attract other hummingbirds. They seem to prefer to stay low-key so they can get as much to drink per visit to the feeder as they choose.So - is it a decent feeder? Yes... but since it has no perch for them to rest, they drink from my other feeder exclusively unless I give them no choice. With the perched feeder hidden, they do visit this one, but their visits are extremely brief. They tend to stay longer periods with the perched feeder.Part of the joy of watching the hummingbirds is their amazing flight/hovering - which you definitely get to observe with this feeder - so it depends what your goal is with the feeder you get. I just love looking at these comical and beautiful birds, no matter whether they are fighting, flying or resting - so the variety is nice.

This feeder is even smaller than I expected, and I like it that way. We don't get a lot of hummingbirds where I live, so filling a larger feeder is a waste. Especially in the warmer weather, when you're supposed to change the sugar solution regularly to keep it from going bad.The feeder has a nice wide mouth on top, so it's easy to fill. Just pour in the sugar water and screw the cap on tight. Then you can put a little water in the moat on the cap to catch any ants that might be attracted to the feeder.So far I love this tiny feeder. It even comes with a little S-hook taped inside the lid, so it's ready to hang in your favorite spot. The plastic pieces at the bottom that come apart for cleaning seem a little flimsy, but only time will tell. For now, five stars, to be adjusted if necessary.

Starting off with the best feature: you can fill this feeder from the top. If you've ever refilled a hummingbird feeder, you know you usually have to flip them upside down to get to the opening, which means you have a good chance of getting the sticky leftover liquid all over your hands. With this top-fill one, you can just unscrew the top, refill, and done. Awesome idea.Also great: no leaks. I've had several feeders in the past, and they frequently started leaking after a while. I guess the plastic ones expand and contract in the sun, creating tiny gaps that allow the liquid to leak out. If you use hummingbird food rather than just sugar water, that'll create an ugly red stain underneath the feeder. Even if you don't, you can expect lots of ants or other critters to make a bee line for the sugary puddle of free nutrition. So, second plus of this model: no leaks, so far at least.Final plus: the ant moat! This isn't unique to this model, but it's something to look out for. The top has a little ridge, which will prevent lines of ants from wandering along the top of the feeder to get to the food.All in all, this is a very nice hummingbird feeder.
summary: The top fill feature is brilliant

reviewText: I love this perky, red hummingbird feeder!!  It is ~ 6  inches by 4 inches in size.  It has four soft, flexible flowers for the bird to feed from.  (Unlike the hard metal ones which I feel could harm the little guys.)  It is super to easy fill.  (Therefore, no mess.)  Just unscrew the plastic top and pour the sugar solution into the glass container.  The red color is cute and welcoming to the hummingbirds.  I have a bronze one and the birds bypass it. (Apparently they hummingbirds are very attracted to red.)  I also like that it has a built in ant moat -since we have a lot of ants in the garden I find this a very nice touch.  The only negative is that is comes with a flimsy S hook to hang.  Instead of using the hook I decided directly loop a sturdy rope through the open attachment on the feeder.This feeder is completely adorable, easy to clean/use and a hummingbird magnet.  This feeder is win, win, winner!
summary: This feeder is completely adorable, easy to clean/use and a hummingbird magnet.  This feeder is win, win, winner!

reviewText: a very nice feeder built of quality materials...here's what i like:- glass containerthis makes the feeder easier to clean; as you know, you have to clean out your feeder so the little ones don't get sick- opens from the top!what a great idea! most other cheaper feeders are invert-fed; this one is easy to fill and clean out...- clip included, or you can use your own lanyard...what is missing? well, a little perch by each 'flower' would be nice... and so would a simple recipe printed inside the feeder's label...other than that, this is a great little feeder! ours is outside right now, and we have a number of bottles of sugar-water ready to go!

When I first saw this as a product that Amazon offered for my review I grabbed it.I love hummingbirds and plant lots of flowers for their benefit all over my property.My first encounter with a hummingbird was in my girlfriends back yard we were eating lunch and although I never saw one in person I knew one was approaching.  I could hear the wings moving so fast it was like a smooth motor revving up. I was so excited, I knew I wanted to attract them to my home.  I had just bought my house and went out and bought every hummingbird feeder I could find. Small ones large ones, ones that had a tube hanging down so they could suck the juice out, the problem with those is when the wind blew all the water came out all by itself. I bought several with flowers like this one.The best design, as far as I am concerned is indeed this type. It is very functional, all you really need is a nice "bottle" that holds a minimum amount of "syrup" and a place for them to suck out the sweet liquid, that comes in the form a four little flowers. It has a good size hole in the middle. The bowl is 8 ounces. If you get one too large you may not clean it out often enough this one will keep you on your toes so to speak.Hummingbirds hardly ever set down so there is no need for  a perch on the feeder. They are not around long enough to get comfortable, they just flit from flower to flower, I really do not know how they get anything out when they go at it so quickly.Hummingbirds are very social birds when  they get to know you and feel safe they will greet you when the season starts and they will then come by sometime in October and say goodbye. I walked out on my deck the first time I experienced their departure, I heard the familiar hummmmm of their wings and knew he/she was there but it was so close I could not see it.  When I focused I could see it right in front of my eyes, it hovered for a few seconds. When he got close I actually felt the breeze as he passed.He swiftly flew away to greet me again the next spring.This bottle set up is vey easy to clean, first of all the cup portion is glass much better than plastic. Everything can be taken apart.  there is even a well on top that you fill with water so the ants cannot drink the nectar. The best part is it can be filled through the top, no more having to hold it upside down to fill from the bottom, a big plus.This is a very pretty, functional and inexpensive feeder I will be buying several more before the onslaught of hummingbirds arrive.  Hang them close to you and they will come and entertain you all summer long.

reviewerName: Y. R. Wu "The will to win is nothing without ...
reviewText: Update (October 2013) - we became "hummingbird Central"  for the month of September.  Might be part of the migration pattern.  In early fall we were treated to hummingbirds every few minutes for about a month.  We had to refill it almost every week!  Really a treat.Filled very easily, we hung it on a shepherds hook that is about 15 feet from our kitchen window.Taking it apart for cleaning, the way it works is that there is a internal float that prevents too much liquid from coming out when the reservoir is full.  This works well, hope it continues to work next season.Went up on Tuesday, we spotted a hummingbird on Thursday.  It filled very easily, our one complaint is that the S-Hook they supplied was too small and narrow to use on the shepherds hook.We're planning to move the feeder closer to our kitchen window for a better view.
summary: Saw our first Hummingbird after 2 days!

reviewText: Well, maybe you won't see that headline but we like hummingbirds and hummingbirds like our yard. We plant flowers and trees to attract them. We strategically position feeders in the shade all over the yard to encourage them to sit and sip for awhile.The Perky-Pet 132TF 24-Ounce Glass Top Fill Hummingbird Feeder holds a full 3 cups of sugar water. It is not elegant or pretty. It is practical. The sizable and nicely heavy glass body of the feeder screws open at the top and bottom allowing a small-medium woman's hand to fit inside the top for easy cleaning. Or put the glass portion through your dishwasher for more robust cleaning. The bottom base screws off and detaches in 2 pieces to allow for cleaning. Filling is easy from the top lid. Capacity and ease of cleaning are the chief selling points for this feeder.  You don't need a feeder brush.An "S" hook taped inside the lid makes initial set up easy. If this is your first time setting up a feeder, you might can pick up some inexpensive metal chain at your local hardware to hang from a Sheppard's hook, tree branch or whatever overhang you wish to use.Plastic does not hold up well in our brutal 100+ degree summer sun. I will have to be extra careful about keeping it hanging under the shade of awnings to make it last. The loop, part of the top of the molded plastic lid and the 2 piece base connectors seem like the critical failure points of the feeder. Should the top plastic loop break or crack, I think I can relatively easily fashion an alternate hanging weave to extend the life of the feeder. Should the plastic base connectors or screw cap become loose or fail, the leaking and the attracted ants are harder to correct and the feeder probably will need to be replaced. I do like the shallow indentation in the molded cap, which serves as an ant moat.
