However, because it is a very shallow moat it is best suited to more moderate climates where the water won't evaporate so quickly as in our heat. For our heat I would addRED ANT MOAT PARASOL by Parasolavailable in red or black.This morning I awoke to a pretty little lady hummer sitting on one of the sitting bars along the base and sipping her sweet nectar. Larger birds that try to steal water are surprised when their weight is not supported and they create a very wobbly feeder.This feeder does what it is intended and I recommend it as a basic feeder especially for older owners who want ease of cleaning over looks or durability.It is not the handsomest feeder availableSchrodt Designs Model HBL-C Crystal Hummingbird Feederbut I do expect it to last at least 2 summers in the hot desert sitting in the shade. If beauty in your garden is more important to you, you don't mind cleaning and filling your feeder more often, or (moving to the next price point) you want a feeder built more durably, you may want to continue your comparison of feeders. But don't be surprised when you find yourself keeping this Perky-Pet Hummingbird Feeder as one of your top contenders.
summary: Mayor Bloomberg Seen Giving his Hummers a Big Gulp

reviewText: This looks wonderful.  It has the red coloring you need to attract your hummingbirds.  It is nicely made and the white "flower" feeding sections are adorable.  Much nicer than I thought it would be!!  Great addition to any yard!

reviewerName: Beth DeRoos "Beth DeRoos from the California ...
reviewText: Have a Perky-Pet 8 oz hummingbird feeder and love it because its easy to clean. What I LOVE about this one that Perky-Pet also makes is because it holds 24 Ounces of sugar water which means I only need to fill it every 3 days instead of once every day or day and a half.Also easy to fill and clean.  Love glass hummingbird feeders because they don't get cloudy like plastic can do.Get two of these because I swear hummingbirds tell all their friends 'hey guys she has free food for us'.  I thought I had two hummingbirds,but saw over a weeks time I had dozens.May 31 2013Have been watching the hummingbirds at the three feeders I have and this one really is loved by the hummingbirds, because of the wire ledge they can sit on and feed. Unlike another feeder that they have to stay in flight when feeding.  It's nice to have a variety of feeders so the birds get the one they like best.  Am reading up on hummingbirds, because I was curious if older hummingbirds are the ones using this specific feeder with the resting ledge.
summary: Perky Pet is a great brand

reviewText: This isn't as pretty to my eyes as the antique red one I just reviewed, but, I will tell you this, it was shipped to me with a couple of air pillows as padding pitched into a cardboard box, I was SHOCKED it did not break! So this IS a hardened glass as they say it is! It's a top fill feeder that you can put water in the cap (on the top outside part) to keep the pesky ants away. I don't have that problem, but I know of others who do, so this might be a good answer for those of you battling to keep ants off your feeder. As they say it IS easy to fill, no inverting needed, has soft plastic flowers for the birds to feed from, it's more of the style that most people use.I would give it an A just because of the durability of the glass bottle!

reviewerName: Clark Isaacs "Clark's Eye on Books by Clark I...
reviewText: Are you looking to be a good neighbor to the birds?  If so, this is ideal for the hummingbirds! They do not hum, but they sure can entertain when gathering around this feeder.  Well constructed, the glass seems to be very strong, the wife dropped the feeder on the tile counter top by accident, but this did not crack or break it. Using what is recommended on line as a nectar is simple.  Take 1/4 cup of sugar to 1 cup of water, use two of these to fill to the neck of the glass about midway to the top bubble.  Works great and the birds simply love it!  Have some summer fun by watching these little birdies take a sip and hover in mid air while they eat.  Bet you can't do that!

This feeder is now number ten that we have in active use.  We have been feeding hummingbirds here for over 30 years now and we get a lot of return customers each year.  We also act as a way stop for these little fellows as many of them pass through in the spring on their way further north.Anyway, I have absolutely no complaints about this feeder so far.  All of our feeders are of glass which we prefer as we are able to keep them clean as they should be kept.  Also, unless of course you drop the thing glass lasts much longer.  I love the fact that this one is a top loader, our first by the way, and is extremely easy to fill and easy to clean.The color of course is what attracts the birds.  We have never used commercial nectar and make our own.  We use four cups of hot water to one cup of sugar.  We have found that we do not need to boil the water and it is quite hot enough to melt the sugar as the temperature the water comes from our tap.  So far we have not had any sign of leakage what-so-ever.  I might recommend that when you screw the bottle portion in, you do it firmly and not too tight.This thing is easy to hang by using the "S" hook you will find tapped to the lid in the package.  I personally use those large angle iron shelf hangers you can buy anywhere and mount them to either the house or to one of the many trees we have.  This seems to work fine although I might recommend using some nice heavy duty electrical coated copper wire if you place your feeder in an area subjected to high wind.I am not complaining, only observing, but of the literally hundreds of things we have ordered from Amazon over the years, this was the most wretched packing I have ever seen.  Even though the box was designated as "fragile," the primary box was pretty well crushed upon arrival.  The thing was packed in wadded up brown paper...that was it!  I do not know how it survived!  I think luck had a great deal to do with it.Now since we maintain so many feeders, we never fill the feeder to capacity.  I check the feeders daily and if there food available I tend to put off refilling them as I should....sheer laziness on my part.  If the feeder is getting quite low then it forces me to do what I should be doing anyway.  Old nectar can be deadly for the birds and must the changed often!  One other thing of note is that the ant mote on top is nice but does not hold much water.  With the heat we have here it is evaporated within less than an hour.  I keep ants off my feeders by liberally coating the wires I hang the feeders by with Vaseline.  It works wonders!All in all I am extremely happy with this feeder - actually we use a lot of Perky-Pet products and have never been unhappy with any of them.Don BlankenshipThe Ozarks
summary: OUR FIRST TOP LOADER - WE ARE DELIGHTED!

reviewText: This is a high quality feeder.  I like the glass bottle and the bottle shape is kind of fashionable.  It has a high capacity and fills from the top.  I'm not sure that the soft flowers make any difference to hummingbirds and they may even avoid them (see later comments).  The ant moat is a good idea, but the water evaporates fairly quickly and I do not take the time to fill it up frequently.I washed the feeder and rinsed thoroughly, made my standard ratio of sugar: water nectar (boil the water first), hung the feeder in the usual spot and within a couple of hours I saw a chickadee attempting to drink out of the feeder (not sure if the bird was successful or if it likes sugar water).  The hummingbirds took longer to come to this feeder, only after it had been up for several days and they do not frequent this Perky-Pet feeder much.  The liquid level has gone down slightly over the last three weeks, so hummingbirds were not visiting much, even when I wasn't looking (and yes, I do need to change out the nectar - with our previous feeder the hummingbirds drank up the nectar quite quickly which prompted refilling every few days).  We have lots of hummingbirds but they just do not seem to like this feeder compared to our previous feeder and that is why I am giving the Perky-Pet 3 stars.
summary: High quality but infrequent hummingbird visits

reviewText: I washed this new hummingbird feeder and poured the nectar in through the top, which was really nice.  Usually, I spill it on my shoes when I turn the other feeders over after filling them.  Top filling is a real plus!  Anyway, I sat and watched this feeder and it only took 17 minutes for the first hummingbird to stop by and try it out.  I tried to get a picture, but I am not fast enough.  The hummingbirds love it!

This feeder is definitely the easiest to clean and fill!  I have a total of 4 feeders including two Hummzinger feedersAspects 367 Hummzinger Ultra Hummingbird Feeder, 12-Ounceand onePerky-Pet 8109-2 Red Antique Glass Bottle16-Ounce Hummingbird FeederThe Hummzingers are the oldest so the hummers tend to go to them first (most familiar)I really like the convenience of this one!  The only thing that I don't really like is the white rubbery flowers.  I think that over time they will be likely to get old and drab looking and maybe brittle.  Time will tell :-)

I have a hummingbird feeder with the same exact look by Perky-Pet and it attracts the birds and is fairly easy to maintain.  However, it is a bottom filler and you need to disassemble it almost completely to refill the nectar.  All I have to do with our new additional feeder is remove the top and pour in the nectar.  So Much Simpler~  It isn't the season for hummingbirds in NW Indiana yet, so I cannot test it, but with the same appearance as our current feeder I have no doubt it will be successful.
summary: The top filler makes this a winner

reviewText: We love our hummingbirds and the feeder fits the bill.  It holds more sugar water than our others so we don't have to fill it as often.  Also another great feature is it can be filled upright without having to flip over.  You simply unscrew the cap pour in the liquid and your done.  No more sticky messy clean up!  Overall we are happy with it and will get another for a housewarming gift for our friends who just got a new home.

A bit smaller than I expected but definitely pegs the cute meter. This is the first top filling feeder we have and I am finding that the size does't matter as much since it can be refilled or topped off without a big mess and without wasting a lot of syrup.

I now have 6 hummingbird feeders and like this one the best. It's easy to fill, attractive, glass, and has flexible soft plastic white w/red flowers for the birds to sip through. Within 15 minutes of hanging this one out, I had hummers. It holds a decent amount of nectar, just about right to last a few days. I am also finding I get more backyard hummingbirds by having more than 1 or 2 feeders out for them. Also have a hanging water jug for birds, they drink from it often.
summary: Attractive, top fill, glass, attracted birds quickly. Recommended.

reviewText: I like the feeder, but with that said...there are some characteristics that the buyer needs to think about.It's made of glass and it's large.  It also holds 24 oz.  That means it has substantial weight, which is important to remember.  It can't just hang from a lightweight hook screwed a few turns into something, nor can it be hung from a lightweight wire hanger in a tree branch.  It needs a bit of support.  It's also not easy for anyone who has any impairment to lift on and off, which may be another important consideration.  Dropping it, or having it fall, could have not only messy but potentially hazardous results.  Make sure your hanger is firmly attached and strong enough to hold this.  Use care when removing it for refilling or rehanging it after it has been refilled as well.Because of its size, if you don't have an established batch of hummingbirds that feed in your yard, you may want to not fill it completely full either.  (At least at first) You don't want the sugar mixture to begin molding or fermenting before the hummingbirds eat it all.Because of its weight, I can't hang it where I intended originally.  We'll put up a hanger specifically for this feeder.  Because of that, I don't know how the hummingbirds will actually react to it, but I'm assuming that they'll find it as attractive as I do.  As for the work of maintaining it, it's not much different than any other, although it's much more durable in one sense than a plastic feeder, in another, a drop of the feeder would indicate it lacked durability.

It took only a couple of days for the hummers to find this feeder and accept the liquid. That's the bottom line on hummingbird feeders. Do they work? Does it attract hummingbirds? Yes this one does.I really like the large reservoir, a full 24 oz capacity, making the juice last a long time. No funnel needed to fill this top-loading, wide-mouth, hummingbird feeder. The lid screws on and off with ease and has a dip in the lid forming a rainwater catching ring to keep ants from climbing down the hanging wire and stopping up the feeder holes. Even comes with a metal s-hook for hanging.My one dislike is the fact that the reservoir is made of glass. It's strong glass, but if dropped it will break. Of course if a plastic one is dropped while loaded, it will likely break as well.The base also separates easily for cleaning when needed. As long as the ants do not get inside, the feeder can be refilled a few times without cleaning, I have found. Perches below the white and pink plastic blossoms containing the feeder holes are enjoyed by the hummers. I've found, the feeders with perches are used more often than a hummingbird feeder with no perches.My wife makes our nectar soup. 4 parts water to one part sugar, heat to boiling, cool completely, and then fill. With all the red on this feeder, it is not necessary to add red food coloring to the nectar. The red on the feeder attracts the hungry birds.Our large capacity hummingbird feeder hangs about 18 inches outside our kitchen window, under an overhang. It is a delight to get to watch the hummers up close through the window. With the window cracked open a bit, you can even hear the wings humming as they arrive and leave. And occasionally hear a squeaking chirp, yes hummers do chirp, not hum.Our ruby throated friends love this feeder.Who can argue with a hummingbird?

reviewerName: In Memory of W. G. Simms
reviewText: Like many others, we have relied on the Perky Pet model 203CP "pinch waist" type hummingbird feeders for years and those are durable and fairly user friendly. They also clean up pretty easily.When this top-filling model was made available via the Vine program we decided to give it a try to see if it could supplant our old standby.I will amend this review with a comprehensive side-by-side comparison at summer's end!
summary: ***** CAN IT SUPPLANT THE OLD PERKY PET STANDBY? ****

reviewText: Spotting hummingbirds in your garden can be a really exciting event and if you have lots of gardens and lots of nectar-producing plants (even just hanging plants) you will almost certainly attract them. Studies have shown that hummingbirds are attracted to reds and pinks, so I always have red and pink hanging plants near my porch. I live in Connecticut and there are hummers in the garden all summer long, well into the fall.If you really want a consistent stream of visitors though, you're better off putting out one or more feeders. Once the hummers know there is a well-cared-for feeder near by, they'll return to it many times a day. The number of times that they return is partly based on the sugar-to-water ratio that you use in making the food you put in the feeder--the higher the amount of sucrose (table sugar) the less they often they have to feed. There is an excellent article on this on the web but I don't think I'm allowed to post link here. (Just search on feeding hummingbirds.)This feeder offers a pretty big capacity of food (whether you make your own or buy commercially made nectar) and that is a good thing if you have a lot of hummers, but if you only have a few visitors, the food may go stale (or develop dangerous mold) if you don't clean the feeder regularly. It's important to keep any hummingbird feeder clean and to keep the nectar fresh. Fresh is very important to these birds, this is not a feeder you can fill once and forget about. Even if they only drink half, you must pour that out ever few days and give them a fresh supply. So, if you have a lot of hummers, this feeder will be great; if not, I'd probably go for a smaller feeder.The feeder is pretty well made and easy enough to clean. I think the perches might be a bit close to the flowers (feeding outlets) but I'm not sure. I have just put this out, so I'll know shortly. I'm in Connecticut and the hummers are here now, so I should have visitors soon. I'm not sure why they used white flowers, most feeders use either red or yellow, but we'll see, that might be fine. This book would probably be a big help:Hummingbirds of North America: Attracting, Feeding, and PhotographingOne small note: The feeder comes with a small s-hook (look under the lid when you open it, it's taped there) but it's pretty much useless for hanging the feeder. I would go to the garden store and buy a longer s-hook--the kind that are made for hanging plants (or just make one from an old metal hanger).I like that the feeder fills from the top (much simpler than the bottom-fillers that you have to flip over once you fill them) and the fill opening is big, so it's easy to pour into it. Overall a very nice feeder, I'll update this once I get some customers.
summary: A large capacity feeder that fills easily

reviewText: PLEASE NOTE ADDITION TO REVIEW BELOW.I *love* this hummingbird feeder!!! I have two others, both your standard cheap feeder that is so difficult to fill because of a small opening, and once filled, you have to flip it upside down and it notoriously drips across my deck, inviting ants to the sugar syrup. This Perky-Pet 24 ounce Glass feeder, however, fills from a VERY large top opening! It also has an "ant moat" on the top which you can fill with water so your feeder isn't crawling with sugar-seeking ants. What a great idea! Another plus is that this feeder holds a full 24 ounces of food, while the smaller cheaper units hold only 8 ounces. My birds will be so happy!Just an FYI. Do you know you can make your own hummingbird food for your feeder? You don't need to buy the expensive packets that include red food coloring, which the birds don't need. Simply boil 4 cups of water in a pan, add 1 cup of sugar, stir until sugar is dissolved, and boil gently for 2 more minutes. Let it cool and put in your feeder. My birds love this food and there is no reason to have to add any red coloring.I highly, highly recommend this Perky-Pet Hummingbird Feeder. Another FYI. When you take the feeder out of the box, you'll think it comes with no hook to hang it with, but look under the top lid and you'll find it.My hummingbirds are so happy!ADDED 08/10/13: I return to revise this review. After 2 weeks of using the hummingbird feeder, it started to leak around the base near the flower feeders. This base comes apart for cleaning, but there is no gasket of any kind to create a water tight seal. Once I took it apart to clean, it never sealed properly again. My husband even used an epoxy glue around the base in an effort to seal it, but that didn't work. I ended up having to throw the feeder away!!! So fair warning -- this feeder looks good, has great potential, but since it won't hold the liquid for more than 24 hours it's actually quite useless.
summary: Revising review. Not as good as I originally thought

reviewText: It is glass and that is a great start for me and for most hummers.  It fills from the top and that is great for me.  I prefer the top filling far better than the alternatives.  The size is suitable and best for most applications but right now the hummers are a bit stand offish and have avoided our top-filled feeders including this one.  The hummers have not chosen to use the footrests and it might have to do with the inability to support their 1 to 2 grams weight.  It appears that the internal mechanics do not permit food to fill the holes properly and that may be a reason for less activity.  I cannot tell yet.  I like the wide mouth of the top opening.  It makes filling less cumbersome.  I normally use a funnel to accomplish most fillings but do not need it for the Perky Pet 132TF.  There is a pleasant surprise when the sugary water is NOT spilled.  I recognize it might be too early in the season to get a full appreciation for those little critters but two of the other Perky-Pets are getting empty every two or three days but the new top-filled one are not as popular.  The weather has negative overtones also especially since the hummers' flight paths were disturbed this winter and spring.  When the gang arrives it is a sight to behold and makes even the most critical curmudgeon happy.
summary: I Like this One but the Hummers remain Silent, so far

reviewText: This is definitely an upgrade from my bargain store hummingbird feeder.  At first, I got a feeder to see if I could even attract any hummingbirds.  After a week I found that there were at least 5 hummingbirds fighting over my single-opening feeder.  This one has 4 "stations" so there is less fighting though I still have a "bully" dominant bird in the group.As for the feeder, this one has a huge capacity.  The glass container is easily washable and it is easy to re-assemble after cleaning.  As one reviewer pointed out, the plastic bottom is a bit flimsy and you shouldn't screw it on too tight.  This feeder is really easy to fill and doesn't leak when transporting it.  I have not had a problem with ants (yet) and I am somewhat skeptical of the ant moat.  I guess time will tell.  I might take the advice of coating the hanging wire with petroleum jelly.  Bees/wasps haven't been much of a problem with this feeder like they were with my cheaper feeder.I make my own nectar, and doing so is something you can easily web-search if you don't know how to do it.The feeder arrived in a large box with no packaging (bubble wrap, etc.) around it, just the feeder thrown into a box with a sheet of packing paper that wasn't even in contact with the feeder.Overall, I like this feeder and I hope that it survives the hot FL sun.  The hummers seem to enjoy it as much as I like watching them dart about.  This is an item I would order again.

reviewerName: Juanita A. Floyd "Life is too short to read b...
reviewText: We feed a lot of hummers here and I am always looking for good feeders. This one has a lot of capacity and the glass container is easy to clean in the dishwasher. Love that the top screws off. There is a built in ant moat which is a big plus although it isn't very deep and won't hold much water in a hot environment where things evaporate fast.On the down side, the glass screws into the plastic bottom and it is loose. if you screw it in tightly it forces the plastic apart and then the feeder leaks. It also was not packaged very well and I was lucky it arrived intact.
summary: Looks Good, Has a Few Flaws

reviewText: My hummers don't seem to be attracted to this feeder as much as they are to some others.  I don't know if it is because the flowers, which are soft, are white instead of that bright yellow they've become used to, or something else about the feeder.  So now they have finally found it and become a bit accustomed to it and do eat from it.This feeder has both pros and cons.  The easy-fill wide mouth is a definite advantage, and I like that the jar is glass and easy to clean.The major advantage for me is that this feeder doesn't seem to leak, at least so far.  The last one I had, another Perky Pet of a different design, was accepted by the hummers more quickly, but even though I hung it in the shadiest part of my yard, temperature variations caused it to leak onto the ground below, attracting armies of hungry, biting ants.  That one had to go.The "innards" still have too many little nooks and crannies, and is hard to clean.  Cleanliness when feeding hummers is of the utmost importance, and although manufacturers emphasis the importance of this, they don't make the job easy, at least in the feeders I've seen. The jar part -- yes, that's a snap, but the rest, not so much.The size is not an advantage for me.  In hot weather, I empty and at least rinse the feeder every day, and refill with only a tiny bit of food.  I'd think that in most situations, 24 ounces shouldn't be put out at one time because the food is going to go bad before the hummers eat it all.There is an ant moat at the top of the lid, really just an indentation in the lid that holds a tiny bit of water.  It is pretty much useless to me because the water evaporates much too quickly to be a deterrent.The feeder came with an s-hook, and one side of it is spread open quite a bit.  To me, it looks like it could come loose in a strong wind so I tightened it up.  However, I wish the manufacturer had included a bit of that plastic-coated bendy wire instead of just the s-hook.  Those, in my opinion, add so much versatility and would be much better for where I hang this feeder.  Just a couple of inches would allow me to remove and hang the feeder without dragging over a chair to climb on.The feeder came with no instructions for making nectar and no prepackaged nectar mix.  Not a problem for me, but frustrating for first time feeders who don't know how to make the mix.  (4 parts water to 1 part sugar, boiled until thoroughly dissolved and allowed to cool before filling the feeder.  NEVER use honey or artificial sweeteners, and dye is unnecessary and possibly harmful.)While there are things I don't like about this feeder, it is the one I'm going to use just because it is the one that, so far, doesn't leak, a huge plus in my book.  I'm still going to be in search of the perfect feeder though, and this one isn't it.

Perky-Pet 132TF 24-Ounce Glass Top Fill Hummingbird FeederI usually use a plastic hummingbird feeder (May - October), but have always wanted to try a glass one.*Perky-Pet 132TF 24-Ounce Glass Top Fill Hummingbird Feeder has a 24-ounce nectar capacity.  That's 3 whole (8 ounce) cups of nectar!  This will make the feeder a bit heavy, so one will need to select a sturdy hook, or tree branch, to hang it  from. One will find a convenient, small, "S hook" taped to the underside of the top lid.*Hardened glass container -- the glass seems thicker than a mason jar.  It's easier to clean than the plastic humming bird feeders I've been using.  The weight of the feeder, combined with the liquid nectar, helps keep the feeder from swaying back-and-forth, too much,  in the wind (like the plastic ones do). A Plus, if ya ask Me. :)*Convenient top-fill design with wide mouth top for easy filling no need to invert.  Just unscrew the top, pour the nectar in, screw the top back on, hang.  Quick and Easy!*4 soft, life-like flower feeding ports. I'm not sure how long the soft rubbery flowers will last in the outdoor environment (wind, sun, rain etc.) but, they sure are pretty (snow white with light pink around the feeding hole) and look real.*Ant moat on top of lid -- just put water in moat and ants drown, or back away, before reaching the nectar.*Very easy to clean:  everything is detachable, for a thorough cleaning...and, reattaches with ease.  I use a simple bottle brush to clean the glass container.*Aesthetically pleasing -- goes with most any outdoor decor, or natural setting.*Neighbor-envy... The hummers flock to my new Perky-Pet 132TF Hummingbird Feeder..  *smiles, sips espresso*tip:  this is the nectar recipe I've used for years:  add 1/4 cup of pure cane sugar to 1 cup boiling water -- stir till clear -- let cool -- add to Hummingbird feeder. Change out once a week...Does the Perky-Pet 132TF 24-Ounce Glass Top Fill Hummingbird Feeder, sound like what you may be looking for? :)  Highly Recommended!  --Katharena Eiermann, 2013

Perky-Pet 132TF 24-Ounce Glass Top Fill Hummingbird Feeder. The humming birders love this feeder, it did not take them long to find it and bring their friends. It is so easy to fill, I love the opening at the top it is so convienent and much eaisier to fill and keep clean than the other feeders. It is a sturdy feeder also, it should last a long time. We love sitting on our porch and watching the hummingbirds eating.
summary: Perky-Pet 132TF 24-Ounce Glass Top Fill Hummingbird Feeder

reviewText: What I Like ~ (Almost) ~ Everything about this feeder!This Humming bird feeder has a very rich appearance.The red serves to catch the Humming birds attention, the center is made of clear hardened glass.Starting from the top ~A solid tab, 1/2" above the lid, has an ample 3/8" circle opening for hanging,and a 'S' hook is included with the feeder, taped to the under side of the lid.The lid has a 1/2" deep ant moat, when filled with water after the feeder is hung, - ants won't cross.This awesome idea eliminates the need to buy the traditional ant guard for Hummingbird feeders.The top lid screws off the glass bottle, which has an inside opening of a full 3".This allows complete access inside the bottle for easy cleaning,I can put may entire hand in the bottle & reach the bottom which is 6 1/4" deep.The base un-screws off the bottom of the glass bottle. The top of the base snaps on-to the bottom of the base,which means to pull them apart, it easier to use the 'pull tabs' to pull with.The flowers (the feeding ports) are of soft plastic, which allows for easier washing/drying,and there's a perch in-front of each flower.The one part of the feeder I'm not as crazy about is the rest of the base,which is in 3 sections, and needs pulled apart for thorough cleaning.The center needs pulled out first, and is a bit stiff to pull, but the partition disc simply lifts out.All parts are plastic except the clear harden glass bottle.This 24 oz feeder is 8 1'2". tall.
summary: Clever ~ Ant Moat Design! ~ and ~ Easy To Clean!

reviewText: This feeder has several things going for it, that make it a cut above the others.  It holds three cups, so a fill will last a day at the prime hummingbird season.  The glass bottle is sturdy, but not excessively heavy.  The shape is attractive.  It comes, as it should, complete with hanging hook.  The ant-trap is easy to access.  A good feeder for oneself, and nice enough to be a gift.

This is a revision of a previously posted review. I had to bump my rating down to 1 star.We very occasionally get hummingbirds in our yard, and I do have a feeder, as well as "hummingbird-friendly" plants. Because people in the area have been seeing more of these winged jewels, and because the rufous hummingbird is said to be expanding its range into the Midwest, I am trying to do everything possible to lure these little beauties into our yard.Perky Pet makes bird feeders that are reliable (based on my previous Amazon Vine selections), so when this came up on the catalog, I requested it right away. (Also, our local bird authorities at Wild Bird store highly rate the brand on many levels.)It's an attractive item. The red should draw in the hummingbirds, and the feeding ports are soft rubber flowers that appear very accessible to the bird. There's an ant moat at the top of the feeder, a little trough that you fill with water to drown invading ants, and so keep the bird stations clear of insects. Assembly for filling, and cleaning, is simple.The feeder is fairly large. Because Chicago gets few hummingbirds compared to other parts of the country, a full feeder would last a year even if you have a steady stream of visitors. If you live in Texas and your garden is the center of hummingbird activity in your area, maybe that's practical. But a 24 oz feeder is a little too big. The temptation to fill it up and then wait until it's half empty means that stale nectar will just sit in the feeder, attracting nothing besides suicidal ants.Initially I thought there was no hanger included. Then another reviewer (see below) pointed out to me that the hanger is taped inside the lid...which I had not noticed, even though I had to remove the lid to fill the hanger. So I went out to check, and sure enough, there it was---but it's really inadequate. It's just a little S-hanger, like you get with your dog's rabies tag. So, we still had to make one. We used one of those fake caribiners.The other Perky Pet feeders we received did have hangers attached.We've had it up for a few months now, and have yet to see a hummingbird. That's okay, because I know they're in the area. I think they'll discover our yard next year when our various trumpet vines mature and we get a jump on the season.But they won't be coming for this particular feeder...we had to throw it out. The seam where the glass meets the base started leaking. We considered attempting a repair with epoxy, but I don't know if that would have introduced toxins into the materials. So we cut our losses and removed the feeder entirely. We still have another feeder out there, and we'll probably replace the Perky Pet with another feeder similar to the one that has remained intact.

This is one of my favorite hummingbird feeders. It's well-made, easy to fill, easy to clean, and the hummingbirds love it. The "flowers" are large so the birds can't miss it. I really appreciate the non-drip aspect. I can hang it over the patio and don't need to worry about a sticky mess below it.The ant trip is small and the water evaporates quickly, but I've learned to put a sticky goo on the hook that holds the feeder and the ants can't get past that anyway.The sugar solution lasts about two weeks at my house (I have another feeder, too), and that's about the time it needs a good cleaning.Keep an eye out for the "S" hanger that's taped to the inside of the top.All-in-all, a nice feeder that holds a large amount of feed.

This is a great bird feeder. The top is durable plastic and the body is solid, thick glass.  The flowers on it are a nice rubbery material that also seems like it will weather well.  It comes with a nice hook to hang it with.  One feature I really liked about this is they put a dip in the top that you're supposed to fill with water, when you do this, it traps/drowns ants who may be trying to climb down the feeder to get to the sugar water.  It's also SUPER easy to fill. You just take the top off, fill it up, and screw it back on, no fuss at all! Overall, this is a great feeder!

If you have had other hummingbird feeders you will LOVE this model...comes apart, goes thru dishwasher, and fills from top....no red sugar water dripping down your arm as you replace it on the hanger! My 2yr old grandson loves watching the birds but makes a funny SWISH noise when he sees the hummingbirds darting about...great entertainment and break from chasing him all over! Try this feeder you won't be disappointed! the hummingb irds seem to like it just fine...amazing to watch them so tiny!

reviewerName: N. Ferguson "Two, Daisy, Hannah, and Kitten"
reviewText: This glass feeder is an improvement in many ways upon our previous feeders.  One noticeable and surprising feature is the softness of the white flowers-- much more lifelike for attracting hummers.  The ant moat is also a great feature!  I agree with other reviewers that the screw-on plastic connection is a bit difficult (overtightening causes problems), but that is a manageable issue/a matter of feel, and I would say is even more troublesome on typical plastic feeders.  The only concern I have is squirrels/making sure I hang the feeder very securely so that glass does not break.  Overall a highly recommended feeder, worth the few extra dollars beyond the usual hummingbird feeder price.

Not much to say about this one.  It is an easy to setup hummingbird feeder, food not included.  I have not yet had to clean it, as the hummingbirds are just discovering it, but once its empty I will post an update.

We have multiple bird-feeders for various species in the back yard, including two hummingbird feeders. Since my neighbor also maintains hummingbird feeders we have LOTS of birds coming in. This particular feeder has worked out great due to its thoughtful design.First, the reservoir is large enough to last for two days. (You don't want to go too long without changing the sugar water because it will cloud and ferment.)Second, this is an incredibly easy feeder to clean. I can take this feeder down, scrub it out, rinse and refill it in less than five minutes.Third, the "ant trap" on the lid, (a small ring/water reservoir), gets added to by any rain we get. Additionally, I see other bird species actually drinking the water from the ant reservoir which is okay since we don't have a significant ant problem anyway.In summary, this feeder gets my highest recommendation. If you are a more casual feeder of the birds, you might wish to get the feeder from the same company which has the smaller reservoir.
summary: The perfect Hummingbird feeder for active bird-feeders

reviewText: This was perfect hummingbird.  They work so well. We even get butterfly on that.  They even come divebomers.  They a really hummingbirds.

We don't get a lot of Hummers to our yard.  We're surrounded by trees and forest, so I sure do appreciate it when they show up.I've tried a number of Perky Pet feeders.  This is my most successful feeder thus far:Glass 8-Ounce Hummingbird Feeder.  I like that I can purchase new bee-guards when the old ones get moldy, and I like that it's glass.I tried thePerky Pet Antique Bottle Glass Hummingbird Feederand it was a bust.  I hate the colored glass as you can't see if there are ants or other nasties floating in the sugar water; and the small opening makes it difficult to clean.  Worst, the Hummers don't seem to like it.So it's with great anticipation that I hung this new feeder to await warmer weather and for our regulars to return.  One thing I love about it is the wide mouth opening.  This is going to make it much easier to clean than it's 8-ounce glass cousin.  Though I must say that the greater size is not all that advantageous.  In Virginia, where I live, it gets far too hot to put out a full feeder.  The sugar-water just goes bad in a day or so.  (If you see cloudiness, it's time to pull the feeder and clean.)  What I do is make up two cups and pour only part of that into the feeder.  The rest goes into the fridge.  (note: no need to use red dye.)It's being larger though, is certainly not a negative.  As I said, it's really great to be able to have easy clean up.Another feature I'm looking forward to testing is the Ant Moat!  It's supposed to create a barrier to the sugar loving pests.  But so far no ants.  (I'm thinking of leaving crumbs to see if I can get them to the moat.  In any case, if you want a barrier, Vaseline works fine.  You just have to put a thickish barrier on the support rod the ants crawl on.)What I don't like are the white plastic flowers and the fact that it doesn't appear that the sipping access is going to be easy to clean.  I'm not willing to pass judgement though until after a season passes.This feeder is definitely worth testing.  It's sturdy and has many good features.  I do suggest though that you rig up a more substantial method of hanging it.  The little s-clip that was shipped with the feeder was too flimsy for my taste.Pam T~mom/friend of the feathered ones
summary: Nice -- I'm waiting on the birds...

reviewText: The Perky Pet company has been rolling out this new series of feeders this year.  I wasn't completely impressed with the smallerPerky-Pet 130TF 8-Ounce Glass Top Fill Hummingbird Feeder, in large part because of the absence of perches.  But this one fits the bill.  Fillup is a little easier with the large-mouthed top (you've still got to be careful walking with it), and cleanup is simplified by the snap-apart design.  The perches are there and the overall appearance (at least by human standards) is more attractive than the previous large model with its more cylindrical shape.But of course the real proof is the birds.  In my experience the birds tend to stay away from a new feeder for a day or two.  Perhaps they're watching to make sure it doesn't turn into a cat or something.  But not with this one.  As soon as the birds were out and about, they were on this one.  Perhaps it's the bright white 'flowers'.  It would be interesting to know just how these flowers are designed, but the hummers seem to like these.  It's nice to keep them coming back.

I've gone through many hummingbird feeders over the years, and have finally found what I consider the best feeder out there, the greatest bang for your buck.These are the Perky-Pet Glass Top Hummingbird Feeder's best features:* This feeder holds a lot of sugar-water, 24 oz! It's double the size of most others.* The glass jar is SO EASY TO CLEAN THOROUGHLY.* No special jar cleaning tools needed, just a regular sponge. Seriously.* The bottom area also cleans well & quickly.* Well attached, no parts that fall off.* Built in ant mote is a nice bonus.* The white flowers are soft and quite lovely.I've gotten other prettier hummingbird feeders that I resent. Comparing them side-by-side, this one is the clear winner.

I have been using this Hummingbird feeder for the last two weeks and I must say I love the looks and the quality. I have total of three feeders hanging in my backyard in the midst of flowering plants. So far they are doing a pretty good job in attracting the Hummingbirds.This pretty feeder is large and holds about 24 oz of nectar; bigger than the other two I have. It is equipped with an ant moat on top of lid to stop ants reaching the nectar. The glass top with convenient top fill design is a plus, but the plastic flowers at the feeder holes are of poor quality. I rated four stars based on design, quality and overall satisfaction.

Wow! We have this feeder set up on our property in the mountains near Shenandoah National Park and we have at least 8 hummers there. We are thoroughly impressed with this feeder. It is large enough to hold a hefty amount of liquid. It has perches for the birds to rest on while they drink. The birds love it. It has a wide mouth for refilling and it is solidly made. I am sold on this feeder and I want more!

We already have three hummingbird feeders, all difficult to clean.  This new product has perfect visibility so we know when to fill it and when to clean it (when murky). It is easy to do both. Another bonus is the small ledge around the feeder where the hummingbirds rest.

I didn't realize until this arrived that there were perches for the hummingbirds, so I was very pleased. The hummers in our area definitely prefer feeders with perches over those without and will empty the one with perches before subjecting themselves to the one without. Perky-Pet has done some feats of engineering to get a top-loading feeder to not spill out from the bottom. It lets you put more in and it's really nice and has a deceptively larger capacity than you'd initially think if you're accustomed to filling hummingbird feeders each week. To test this one out, I took down my other feeders (as is my weekly custom for cleaning) and replaced them with this lone feeder, filled to the brim with home-brew hummingbird nectar (no red dye) that I always prepare for my little flying jewels. At any given time, if you look in the right spots, you can see about 20 hummingbirds perched on branches of trees along our 1-acre yard, but they are so territorial, you usually only see one at the feeder at a time and only for a few seconds before another one or two chase the interloper away.I had this hummingbird feeder out for 10 days with zero traffic to it. I don't know if it's the white flowers, or what that is keeping them from visiting. I would sit vigil (they're used to me standing close for photos, but I was standing many yards away on our porch) for 2 hours without seeing one visitor coming to the feeder... not even hovering to inspect it. I wondered if they'd all migrated away or what happened. After 10 days, I put one of my regular feeders back to join it and the next day, there were hummingbirds at my old feeder, but no hummers would even look at this new feeder. None of my feeders look alike - I've got a square one and a few other designs from Perky-Pet - so it's not like the design would be starkly different from what they're used to being the issue. I don't know if the ruby-throated hummingbirds that are native to the North Texas area in which we live are only interested in red flowers or what is causing the aversion to this feeder - but I have as yet not had one visitor to this lovely feeder.
summary: beautiful, large capacity hummingbird feeder with perches

reviewText: I have tried MANY hummingbird feeders over the years and my main complaints have been: they are difficult to clean, ants get in, and they always drip when I flip them after filling. The Perky-Pet 132TF 24-Ounce Glass Top Fill Hummingbird Feeder has addressed all of these issues and created a hummingbird feeder that I LOVE!The whole feeder comes apart for extremely easy cleaning (see my uploaded photo). No more out of reach areas! Easy to disassemble and reassemble (instructions with illustrations are included), you will be sure there is no hidden mold anywhere, creating the healthiest dining atmosphere possible.With a large top opening, filling is soooo easy and no more spills or drips! That alone keeps the ant population down, but Perky-Pet went one more step by putting an ant moat on top of the feeder. Fill the moat with water and no more ant problems!The hummingbirds love this feeder and with a perch in front of each flower, they don't have to expend energy while feeding (Perches are recommended by many aviary enthusiasts/groups). This feeder has addressed every requirement I've been looking for in a feeder and comes highly recommended!
summary: Easy to clean and a breeze to fill!

reviewText: This hummingbird feeder is a pretty standard design with the benefit of having a top that screws on which can be used for filling the bottle with hummingbird nectar. This is a fairly heavy glass bottle - not cheap plastic - which feels substantial. I had just a little difficulty attaching the bottom parts which are the resevoir for the nectar. These pieces are plastic and feel as though they could break if you exert much pressure. Again, though the design looks like most every other hummingbird feeder out there, it is a substantial piece.  It is mounted outside my window where I hope to soon see hummingbirds coming to eat.

This is my favorite bird feeder. It is so easy to use, fill, and set up. Our hummingbirds love it and I love the fact you don't have to invert it to screw it together. No mess, no spills. The only thing I would have changed is the hook to hang it. It was a bit too small so I used one of my carabiners instead.

This thing is cool.  It has some sort of valve so you can take the top off even when it is full.  That means you can just add nectar through the wide open top and never have to turn it upside down.  Nice.  The bee guards are effective as well.  Keep in mind that orioles cannot feed from it, however.

This feeder has a heavy glass bottle, blue in color in this model, that has a threaded neck which screws into the metal base. Very sturdy. It has a metal deck which has four feeding ports shaped like flowers. These "flowers" are metal as well. The flowers are red and attract the hummers. The blue bottle doesn't have any effect on whether the hummers will use the feeder, (most hummingbird feeders are red). I have a red one next to this blue one, and the birds don't seem to prefer one over the other. A common problem with cheaper hummingbird feeders is that they leak, either at the feeding ports or one of the other joints. This one doesn't. Holds plenty of nectar but remember that the bottle needs to be washed regularly and often or bacteria can grow and make the birds sick. So depending on how many of these mighty mites that visit you at once, you may want to use less than the full 16-oz capacity. Hummingbirds are very aggressive, they don't care if you watch them and they "talk" a lot. Amazing animal. And a very good product.

I had a hard time picking out a new hummingbird feeder as I didn't want the traditional kind. I love antiques and the second I saw this one I knew it would be perfect for my smaller deck outside my art room. Absolutely one of my favorite feeders. Love it.

This company makes great feeders. They are thick glass. I dropped it out of the back of my vehicle onto the concrete accidently and the thing did not break or crack. I may have just been lucky on that one. Had it sitting in my house on my desk for about a week and everyone that saw it just wanted one. It is so nice you may have to keep an eye on it so it doesnt walk off. Propper placement is essential for humming birds as you know, they are very skiddish. I have this one and the larger green glass model. FYI humming birds dont care about the bright red color thing. I have always used clear feeders with clear food. Good materials and solid, shoud last a long time. HIghly reccomended.

...but I remain hopeful!It is safe to say that I am a bird lover, I have always enjoyed feeding my birdies and watching and listening to them enjoy what I serve.  Living in my home for about 11 years now, somehow I have neglected the hummingbirds.  I don't know why... I love them; I just somehow never have purchased a feeder for them.When I was offered this beautiful feeder, I snatched it up.  I love the classic and elegant design of the cobalt blue bottle.  I hung it up in my Flowering Crab Tree and the blue stands out wonderfully against the flowering pink petals.  I have received several compliments on my bird feeder since I have hung it. It is truly beautiful.It is also very easy to fill and clean.  Very sturdy and seems to be well made.  Unfortunately, I have yet to attract a hummingbird.  In all fairness I have only seen a handful of hummingbirds in my neighborhood since I have moved in, so it's not like the feeder is repelling them.  We just don't have an abundance of hummingbirds here.  I haven't given up yet.  My mother-in-law who is the hummingbird queen assures me eventually they will come.  But I am willing to take any advice from anyone reading this.  I really want to add a hummingbird to my bird menagerie.So I will continue to feed them and maintain the cleanliness of the feeder and I will update this review as things do or do not change.Cherise Everhard, June 2013

Yes, I'm one of those blue bottle lovers, so when I got the chance to get either this cobalt blue or a red hummingbird feeder, I went with the blue. It's a beautiful bottle, and the steel finish on the bottom plate (with the little steel-finished feeding rosettes) is very attractive.I made up a solution of 1/2 cup white sugar to 2 cups of boiled water (4:1) and it was just a little too much to pour into the feeder. Had the blue bottle been slightly larger, this easy-to-remember nectar recipe would have filled the bottle perfectly. One thing to note: You'll need a small funnel to get the solution into the bottle, as the bottle neck is pretty small.The steel plate is just a loose-sitting decorative top part of the bottom solution-holding part of the feeder; the rest is plastic—which is good, because it's easier to clean. The bottle itself will not be so easy to clean; a small bottle brush will be required. Directions recommend cleaning out the feeder and putting in fresh sugar solution every few weeks. This prevents bacteria building up in the feeder, which can hurt the hummers.I hung this feeder (using an S hook) from the outside shelf of one of those chrome shelving units (with the zig-zag detailing) like you get at Lowe's or Home Depot, and it works great. Our "front porch" is a concrete strip alongside an asphalt drive up on the side of a mountain, and so far I haven't seen any hummingbirds come to the feeder. I haven't exactly been outside watching for them, though. I do know that a wren is nesting in a small bird house in front of my nextdoor neighbor's apartment, so I guess the little birdies do come up here where we are.It's a pretty feeder, no matter what. I like the looks of it.

This is one of the best looking hummingbird feeders I have ever owned. It holds the right amount of feed. It is easy to put together, to take apart, and to clean. The only negative is that the hanger is not large enough to go over my porch hooks, I had to find a wire loop to use between the two.
summary: Perky-Pet Cobalt Blue Antiue Bottle Hummingbird Feeder

reviewText: I bought this blue feeder to have a pop of color outside my window, and the hummers figured it out immediately. They show a preference for the red one, but they don't utterly ignore the blue that is nearby. HOWEVER, it does not come with its own hook: a hook must be purchased/installed separately. And...even though hummingbirds are well-known for being capable of hovering while they feed...they'd much rather have a perch, like the plastic dishes have.(I also notice that the mouth of this bottle is slightly narrower than the red bottle, which means I need to carefully balance my funnel while filling it.)UPDATE: Although one reviewer said that there is no problem from mildew with these Perky Pet feeders, I was surprised this morning to discover lots of mildew on one feeder. My birds had not been using one of the feeders so I finally took it down to see why. The base was full of mildew. All around the join of the two pieces, but also on the interior around the inside edges and down around the baffles. Yes, I should have cleaned it earlier. But I just thought I'd let folks know that mildew can take over this kind too.

now fr the 4 instead ofa 5 is because of the color.  i have the red one and the birds empty that one first then go to the other red ones we have.  te humming birds will go to this one last if no other feeder has any liquid in it.  other than the color this is a great product

This faux antique hummingbird feeder is beautiful and at the right price.  Perky-Pet offers a nice selection of hummingbird feeders to match most any décor and surroundings.  If cobalt blue is not your first choice, see their other offerings for something that might better suit your décor.  I love the deep blue color.  It's easy to fill as well as clean.  It's not too easy to tell if it's empty, especially from a distance, but that's really a minor concern as I have it right off the patio and it's easy to check.  If cobalt blue is your color, then this hummingbird feeder is the one for you!
summary: Simply Beautiful Hummingbird Feeder.  Easy to fill & clean

reviewText: I liked the pretty green antique feeder so much I started looking at the other colored glass feeders and saw this beautiful blue one. I enjoy watching the hummingbirds on the back patio. My husband purchased this for me and it arrived today. It really is very pretty!I love these glass feeders, they are so easy to fill and keep clean. I love the way the light shines through these and our selfish little hummingbird seems to prefer this blue one over his red and green feeders. He now takes a drink out of each one before he flies away.  He is so serious when it comes to keeping the other hummingbirds away from his feeders that he is never gone for more than a few minutes. He will even hover over you to check you out while you remove the feeders for cleaning and filling.I started  hanging hummingbird feeders as a fun thing to do with my granddaughter when she was was just a toddler. She loved watching the birds and hearing them fly around. Years later she still loves hummingbirds, I like to think I played a part in that.  One of these would make a wonderful gift for a child. Hang one up outside of a window and they will be able to watch as they fly back and forth.

I bought this as it looks alot different than normal hummingbird feeders and offered a different style that I thought would be a great eyecatcher.  I read though that if your feeder doesnt have alot of red it wont atract hummingbirds.  This doesnt have really any red on it as the bottle is blue and the flowers are a reddish bronze color.  The feeder seems to be working ok with atracting hummingbirds though as we have already had a few come to it at first.  We also have now tied some red ribbon bows around the handle to try to atract more closer to the feeder so they will then see the flowers.  We have just put in a sugar water mixture and the seem to really enjoy it so far.  We will see hw the red ribbons work and if they seem to atract more.  I like the look of this but really think that a red bottle might atract hummingbirds more often.

The first thing I checked was how easy this would be to clean.  With the cheap plastic ones, sometimes not so easy to clean the base.  This one is WAY easy.  When the bottle is unscrewed the metal plate with the flowers comes up and separates easily and cleanly from the bottom metal base.The blue glass holder is really pretty and the metal hanger is not coming off unless the whole feeder gets broken.  It's a great design.This by far is the best feeder I have ever owned.
summary: Easier to clean than cheap plastic feeders

reviewText: I was worried that the hummingbirds in our area wouldn't find the flowers on this feeder, but they found it immediately.  This feeder does not hold as much liquid as the red version, but it is quite pretty and seems sturdy.  It's easy to clean, too.

reviewerName: Jill Clardy "So many books, so little time...."
reviewText: We hung the bird feeder on an ornamental bracket outside the kitchen window about 10 days ago, a few feet away from another red plastic Perky Pets feeder that has been very popular with the local hummingbirds for a long time. They completely ignored the new blue one, so we switched positions with the red one. They still ignored it and kept going to the red one. Finally, after ~10 days we took down the red one and put the blue one in its place in the original position and they found it right away! So it doesn't appear to be the color that is off-putting after all.July 1st update - the hummers visit regularly now but usually only when the feeder is in the shade. They don't appear to like it when it's hot and sunny. Some hover in front of the feeder, sipping daintily; others perch on the edge slurping voraciously. I intend to bring back the red one now and see if they still visit both feeders.The antique blue glass is so much prettier than the red plastic container that I may eventually retire the red one completely and replace it with another glass feeder. It is quite sturdy and has a large capacity. To fill it you must invert and screw off the perch at the bottom and thoroughly rinse all parts before refilling with fresh nectar. We make ours from sugar and water (no food coloring) and they seem to like it as well as the mixes we've used previously. Do not turn it right side up until you are back outdoors, to prevent dribbling sticky nectar on the floor (it's a mess to clean up ! )The feeder provides us with an opportunity to watch the fascinating parade of hummingbirds from inside the kitchen window or outside while sitting in the yard. I have posted 3 images of hummingbirds enjoying the buffet at our new feeder.
summary: Cobalt Blue Glass is a Beautiful Addition to the Garden and the Hummers Love It Too !

reviewText: This Perky-Pet Hummingbird feeder is beautiful and elegant looking!  The color is nice and the antique bottle is awesome.  I have several Perky-Pet bird feeders and love all of them, but this is the first Hummingbird feeder from Perky-Pet that I've had.  It really spruces up the yard!  And best of all the hummingbirds love it too!  Definitely a 5 star product.

Perky-Pet 8117-2 Cobalt Blue Antique Bottle Hummingbird Feeder is a beautiful, stylish addition to any garden.  The cobalt blue bottle stands out nicely in amongst the greenery of the garden, and the decorative feeding ports are cute and stylish.  The glass of the bottle is thick and seems as if it will be durable.The feeder is easy to take apart for filling or cleaning.  Just unscrew the bottom, and you have access to fill up the bottle or clean out the reservoir and ports.The hanger provided is a little small, but sturdy and is attached well to the bottle.All in all, I'm happy to have this cute hummingbird feeder as an addition to my garden.  It is beautiful, functional and well made.

I grew up with my parents feeding and caring for the many birds that visited our back yard in Virginia. Hummingbirds were always their favorite birds since they were unique, quick and charming! My parents were raised in the North and were not familiar with the tiny hummers until they moved South!The Perky-Pet Hummingbird Feeder is indeed a wonderful find. I love the old fashioned style of the feeder. The deep blue color of the bottle almost sparkles when the sun shines on it! The feeder holds 16 ounces of juice and the four red feeding ports add another colorful touch to the design! It's like having a shinning delight hanging from our tree.I'm now hoping to buy another Perky-Pet Feeder!
summary: --A Charming and Colorful Hummingbird Feeder with Lots of Style---

reviewText: Perky-Pet 8117-2 Cobalt Blue Antique Bottle Hummingbird Feeder, 16 OunceClassy, made of thick glass and in one of my favorite colors -- Cobalt Blue! *into my Shopping Cart it goes* :)*  A creative conversation starter, the Cobalt Blue hardened square glass antique bottle Feeder really sparkles in the sunlight -- aesthetically pleasing -- goes with most any outdoor decor, or natural setting. The glass is thick and easy to keep clean.  I use a simple bottle brush to clean the inside. It's easier to clean than the plastic hummingbird feeders I've been using.*  16-Ounce nectar capacity -- that's 2 whole (8 ounce) cups of nectar.  Just turn empty feeder upside down, unscrew bottom, fill with nectar, screw bottom back on, flip right side up, hang.  That's it! :)* Filled with nectar, the Perky-Pet 8117-2 Cobalt Blue Antique Bottle Hummingbird Feeder is not all that heavy to carry around, or hang. The weight of the feeder, combined with the liquid nectar, seems to help keep the feeder from swaying back-and-forth, too much, in the wind (like the plastic ones do). A Plus, if ya ask Me. :)* An antique (brushed) silver colored base -- that comes apart - 2 pieces - (for easy cleaning) with 4 realistic (slighty raised) dark red (metal) flower feeding ports add to the overall attractiveness of this particular Hummingbird feeder.  note:  there are no little foot rails (or, whatever they are called) for the Hummers to stand on (and rest) while eating -- but, that is not really all that neccessary, as there are no foot rails in Nature when they feed from Flowers.* There is no ant moat on this Feeder.*Neighbor-envy... The Hummers flock to my new Perky-Pet Cobalt Blue Antique Bottle Hummingbird Feeder..  *smiles, sips espresso*tip:  this is the nectar recipe I've used for years:  add 1/4 cup of pure cane sugar to 1 cup boiling water -- stir till clear -- let cool -- add to Hummingbird feeder. Change out once a week...Does the Perky-Pet 8117-2 Cobalt Blue Antique Bottle Hummingbird Feeder, 16 Ounce, sound like what you may be looking for? :)  Would make a Fantastic Gift!  Highly Recommended!  --Katharena Eiermann, 2013

Okay, basically anything would be an upgrade from our dollar-store plastic feeder, but this is so much prettier and I do believe that the hummingbirds like it too. It is well made, easy to assemble and disassemble, holds a generous amount of nectar, and is very attractive. Can you tell I love it? And I usually don't care for blue, but this is a beauty--it has character.

The Perky-Pet Hummingbird Feeder is really beautiful! The bottle holds much more sugar solution than any of my other feeders, and it is easy to screw on the feeding ports and saucer base.I haven't had a any hummers yet this summer, but I have really enjoyed having this sturdy and unusual feeder hanging on one of the arms of my backyard feeder. I'm sure we'll soon see the little fellows!
summary: Very pretty feeder, no birds yet

reviewText: We have a huge bird population in our backyard, mainly because we have a half dozen or so feeders. It's one of the nicest features of our property, and we enjoy watching the birds very much.We've seen hummingbirds hanging out near some of the plants, and I have wanted a hummingbird feeder for some time.I was thrilled to get this one through the Vine program. It's a beautiful product, and I love the cobalt blue color.The feeder was easy to fill (I got the recipe off the Internet), and it appears that it'll also be easy to clean and refill which was something that concerned me about these kinds of feeders.Right now it's parked a few feet from the kitchen window, near a birdbath, and nestled among other foliage. I'll update on whether it draws cool hummingbirds.

This Hummingbird feed is really gorgeous and is made well.It looks exactly like the picture.  The only thing that you may not notice is that the bottom part under the flowers is plastic.  The rest of the feeder is top quality, made with glass and metal.  The little red flowers are even metal and attached to a brushed, brown metal top.  It also sits flat and does not tip if you should need it to do that.I love the sturdy hanger on the top and it is even attractive!  **All in all, it's perfect.** Looks so great in the yard I am thinking of getting the red one as well. *I got the red one but I have noticed that on both of them there is no place for the birds to rest and eat.  Of course in nature the are always hovering to get their nectar so I guess they will be fine.  Also they are most definitely attracted to red over the blue but they use both feeders.Get a bottle brush to clean it and a chain or hook to hang it from.  Whip up some food: 1 c. filtered water/1/4 c. sugar, boil in microwave or on the stove-done!  Double or triple as needed...cheap!

This is a beautiful feeder, and the glass is high quality, but the feeding solution leaked out of it.  My husband says it's because we have a lot of high winds, so if you live in an area without a lot of windstorms, this might work out for you.  If you decide to try this hummingbird feeder, you'll appreciate that the base is in two separate parts that are easy to clean.

This feeder is beautiful and functional all in one. This feeder is constructed of three parts. The blue glass bottle has a vintage look to it and the feeder part is a combination of metal and plastic. The top of the feeder with the flowers is metal, and the bottom is plastic. These two feeder pieces separate for easy cleaning and seal tightly together when turned onto the bottle.To get the best seal with no leaking, the two feeder pieces need to align correctly. Since you fill the bottle and then must turn the feeder pieces upside down to turn them onto the bottle, it takes a little extra care to make sure the two align properly. However, it does make a nice leak-proof seal.This is a large bottle, so if you have only a few birds feeding each day, as I do, you'll want to mix up small amounts of nectar at a time and you won't nearly fill the bottle. Otherwise, it will ferment. So, I'd recommend this bottle for someone who is constantly filling their feeders because of heavy bird population. For the rest, enjoy its beauty, but don't fill it all the way.

I was really not sure a blue hummingbird feeder would work but I'm here to tell you - it works and it stays looking good and I have the only blue feeder in my neighborhood. Birds come sip, sip, sip and soar away! It's substantial (not flimsy) and hasn't changed one bit being in the weather.  It's a good purchase and your hummers will find it.

I have a red one that is made very similar to this one but I prefer this one because it can sit on a counter top. The other one, can't sit on a counter due to the bottom being too rounded.  Hummingbirds love these feeders!  I love the antique look and they are easy to use. The only thing that would make it better is to be able to sit the bottle on the counter for filling but the hanger gets in the way.

I have purchased the red and the blue of this feeder and like the  look and the ability to put thru the dishwasher.they are sturdy and the color in the sun is very pretty in the yard. Plastic is being phased out of my home..recycling is not being done and the oceans and landfills  are choking with the junk. We need to think too that plastic no matter what they say, is toxicand we need to think of not exposing the hummingbirds to it nor the foolish belief that recycling is being done properly. SO this is why I purchased them and am very happy with the purchase!

I have the red one and the blue one and they both look so pretty and make for great pictures.It's easy to clean; they recommend washing with warm water and soap twice a week.  It's also easy to fill and no leaks.It didn't take long for the hummingbirds to find it.  I liked mine so much that I sent my sister one and within an hour of herputting it up she sent me back a picture with a hummingbird at it.  My suggestion is to put it in a shaded area.
summary: Beautiful, looks even prettier in person

reviewText: I have dozens of feeders in my yard and this is a nice addition.  The bottle is a good, heavy weigh glass.  However, the metal base is a little sharp and doesn't seem all that long-lasting.  The neck of the bottle is very narrow and I need to use a funnel to fill it.  It is a nice garden accent and looks good for now, but I don't expect it to be around in 10 years.  The hummers are using it, but seem to prefer the saucer-shaped ones.  I prefer the looks of the Parasol glass feeders but am still happy to have this in my collection.
summary: Looks good, but doesn't feel like it will last

reviewText: I love this hummingbird feeder so much!  It is so pretty!  It's very heavy and well constructed, you can tell that right away.  It feels substantial like it will last a very long time.  The bottle is beautiful, a very bright vibrant cobalt blue and the bottom part is really pretty too!  It's extremely easy to fill and to clean.  I mixed up some sugar water and the hummingbirds love it!  It's so nice to sit outside and be able to watch the birds feed at such a pretty feeder.

I have a similar hummingbird feeder (green glass) that has been one of my favorites for years. This one is made the same but is a little larger (16 oz. capacity) and in a beautiful cobalt blue color. The feeder is easy to fill, just unscrew the bottom section and pour the feed solution into the bottle. The bottom section comes apart and is very easy to clean. There is not much space between the hanger and the top of the bottle but I find that it is best to attach a wire to the hanger anyway and add an ant moat to keep ants and other insects out.

This is a quality feeder at a reasonable price and it's good looking too.  If a feeder is hard to clean, human nature being what it is, it will be cleaned less often, and this results in an unhealthy as well as unsightly situation.  With this in mind, the best designed feeders are those like the Perky-Pet 8117-2:  a bottle that threads into a base containing the feeding ports.  The Perky-Pet base is in two halves that come apart when the bottle is unscrewed, making cleaning simple.  Unlike every other feeder I've had, the Perky-Pet base is made of metal, even the flower shaped feeding ports are metal; hopefully it will be long lasting.  The antique style blue glass bottle is as attractive in use as it is in the Amazon photos.  The 16 ounce capacity is, for me, the ideal size; the 8 ounce feeders need filling too often, the larger feeders produce a lot of wasted sugar water if filled to capacity.The metal hanger on the 8117-2 has a small loop that doesn't quite allow it to fit on my feeder poles and makes hanging it clumsy, so a separate S-shaped hanger would seem to be a necessary accessory.  For my purposes the 8117-2 is incomplete as is, so only 4 stars.Hummingbirds can perch on the edge of the base while feeding.  Any hummingbird feeder should be located out of direct sunlight to keep the sugar water from evaporating and turning bad; I'd think that the metal perch on this unit makes it all the more necessary to keep it from getting too much direct sun in the summer.  This is my only reservation about this feeder.

Received this lovely hummingbird feeder last week, filled it with nectar and hung it in the yard near the red flowering plants that draw hummingbirds. I hope to include a video piece with the review when the birds show up. The antique bottle design is beautiful when the sun shines through it, and is easily filled and with the nicely designed bottom where the birds should visit the little red flowers which are made of metal on a metal lid over a plastic container. It looks snug enough to keep bees and wasps from getting in. My only concern was if the metallic red paint on the flowers is bright enough to draw hummingbirds. And it is, after a mere 5 days in the garden, this morning we had our first customer at this beautiful feeder. I ran to get a camera to capture the promised video, but a dad-gone robin plunked down on the deck railing adjacent to the feeder and the hummingbird flitted off. Not giving up, though. Will be watching and maybe can catch these tiny little birds chowing down at the cobalt blue feeder that is so pretty in the sunlight.

I was hesitant to order this antique blue bottle, unsure if it would attract the hummingbirds.  No worries.  They love it.I am quite happy to have this outside my kitchen window too.  It is a beautiful cobalt blue and a nice match to my red antique feeder.  My other hummingbird feeders are the traditional red tulip design made of plastic.The hummingbirds seem to prefer the glass ones.Lovely addition to my garden.  Recommended.
summary: Yes, hummingbirds like blue bottles too.

reviewText: The square cobalt blue bottle of this hummingbird feeder is just gorgeous! The metal hanger and feeding base-top are equally gorgeous, and fit the overall look the feeder beautifully. However, the feeder is not perfect: The gray plastic bottom pan is a bit of a let down, it looks about as nice as curb feelers on a Lamborghini. Otherwise the feeder is quite eye-catching, and the hummingbirds seem to be as attracted to it as the standard classic red feeders.The glass bottle is quite substantial even when empty, so be sure you hang this from a sturdy support. There is no rubber seal between the metal top plate and plastic pan, so I was concerned about possible leaks. I have not noticed any leaks so far, so I reckon the design is pretty well thought out.

With this feeder, you more than get what you pay for - it looks antique and looks like its crafted with high quality materials.  The feeder's main component is a cobalt blue, square-shaped glass antique bottle, with brushed silver accents. It looks quite classy.The feeder is easy to fill and clean, though it's important to note that hummingbird feeders are, in general, high maintenance. They need to be cleaned at least once per week.  As hummingbird feeders go, this one is an easy one to clean.We found the perfect spot for it in our backyard garden and we love it.

We've had a couple of feeders over the years but none have been as sturdy as this. The only problem is that the color of the glass attracts heat and so you need it in a very shady place. We had it in the sun where the birds like to hang out but they were not touching it. I checked on it and discovered that the nectar was hot. It looks nice but you just need to be careful where you put it.

I received this hummingbird feeder today and I am very pleased with it.  It's a beautiful cobalt blue and the antique silver base is a nice compliment to the glass color.  It a very sturdy feeder and the glass is nice and thick. The only caveat is that there's no hanging cord with it and the metal ring at the top isn't large enough to hook it over the metal hook I hang my feeders from so I had to fashion a hanger for it using some clip rings. It looks just lovely hanging off the deck in the sun and the hummingbirds seem to like it as well!

I have the origional green hummingbird feeder that is just like this one and bought it last year and loved it.  The hummers were more than happy with it and so I thought I would get the cobolt blue one this year since it happens to be my favorite color.  My little hummers are in heaven with all the feeders around now.  There is less fighting and certain hummers like certain colors.This particular bottle seems a bit smaller than the red and green one but that's okay, I'm sure my babies won't care one way or the other.  The bottom unscrews from the bottle and it seperates in half for easy cleaning.  You do have to be a bit careful putting it back together that everything lines up or it will leak.  I learned the hard way.  Once you get the hang of it though there's not a problem.  Just remember, don't give the hummers that red gunk you buy in the stores.  Make your own by using 1/4 cup of sugar to 1 cup of water and bring to a boil then shut it off and let it cool before putting the mixture into the bottle.

Finally, there are some absolutely gorgeous, glass hummingbird feeders available for your garden instead of the cheap, plastic ones of the past.  I got the blue one and now I want one of each color.  These are quality, sturdy feeders, beautifully made, easy to clean.  Can't really ask for more!  The hanger is made of metal, there ae 4 red feeding ports on a shiny metal base, 16 oz capacity, and the antique glass bottle with unique square shape.  It's easy to use, easy to clean, easy to fill, and beautiful to look at.

I love this feeder it is so unique.  It is a beautiful cobalt blue with red flowers around the base with little holes on it for the Hummingbird to drink from. Along the body of the bottle are beautiful "etchings" making it look a bit old fashioned.It is very easy to clean but you may need a small bottle brush to get down into it.It is advisable to make the nectar at home it is much healthier that way and it is very easy.Take one cup sugar to 3 cups water and mix together (the formula is 1 part sugar to three parts water) It is also advisable to boil this solution for a minute to kill any bacteria that may be present, just in case.Hang it in the shade to encourage the little birds and it will stay fresh longer.  If treated right I believe this feeder will last for many years to come.

WeI like our hummingbirds. We plant flowers and trees to attract them. We strategically position feeders in the shade and all over the yard to encourage them to sit and sip for awhile.  Color matters nothing except to me; never the birds. The soft green of the glass bottle is pleasant.Holding 3 cups of sugar water, this is the "Big Gulp" of feeders. It took our Annas 3 days to find our new "Green Antique Bottle" Hummingbird feeder.  It is not as pretty as our favorite French glass/redwood feeders but it holds twice as much, costs a lot less and is attractive. The base is plastic and screws on to the bottle. We will see how plastic holds up to our brutal sun. I will have to be extra careful about keeping it hanging under the shade of awnings to make it last.
