Especially when trying to identify a spider, it's nice to have the white background and green goo.Highly recommended so long as you aren't trying to nab a rodent.
summary: I don't use this for rodents but I love it for crickets and spiders

reviewText: First, these sticky traps have a day-glo green color to them, not white as the photo shows.  Second, they work well at catching mice - I get them in my garage from time to time.  But they are not so good at catching bugs.  I keep some around my place to catch any gross creepy-crawly things.  The flat pieces of cardboard-like paper with the glue on them work well, but these are trays, and the bugs don't crawl up and into them.  But still, for catching mice - they do the job!!!
summary: Good for mice, not for bugs

reviewText: Ok, so maybe you want to be humane about catching mice. Or maybe you just don't want to see their dead lifeless body squished inside a spring trap.  So you buy one of these sticky traps because there's no risk of snapping your fingers and maybe it can be a more humane way to catch that mouse. Just keep in mind, this traps mice, it doesn't kill them. so if you catch a mouse with it, he will still be very much alive; just his feet will be glued down to this thing.  I've seen mice only get one or two feet stuck on one of these, and then go hobbling around on the other 2 feet, dragging this trap clumsily along; talk about gruesome and inhumane.  So just keep all that in mind when buying this one. It works ok, but a more humane trap has its trade offs.
summary: Think it through before you buy

reviewText: I use these in the closed garage, away from friendly dogs and cats, but perfect for the intruders that I want gone!Place the sticky trays out in areas that those pests will walk around and suddenly they ain't going nowhere (Sorry B.D.).Give them a few days and then throw out the whole trap along with any "visitors".This Tomcat stuff works!
summary: These Glue Traps Do The Job

reviewText: I would love to build one life-size and stick the inventor on one of these things.  Any animal, target species or not, will die a slow, cruel death, often breaking every bone in its body trying to free itself from this monstrous device.  When used outdoors owls have gotten trapped in those damn things when they tried to grab a perceived easy prey item.We are trying hard to get these horrible traps banned from markets, so please help spread the word.  You would not want your kids or pets to get stuck on these things, so why would any decent human being want to torture wildlife?  There are more humane methods to kill rats, this is absolutely, most definitely, the worst possible choice!
summary: PLEASE DO NOT BUY SUCH TORTURE PRODUCTS!!!!

reviewText: well it worked, too well I had five mice stuck to it. If you have that many , you have an "infestation" call the pros to get rid of them. I wish I had done it right away. Now I have to fix ducts, crawl space problems, and more issues, to the tune of 2000$ so do not  think this fixes the problems,  call the pros.

This is good for catching multiple rodents without having to reset, while at the same time not being a poison source that the rodents might take back to the nest and then die behind your walls, later stinking.  It is sort of gross, though, and you'll end up with all kinds of stuff on it.  I guess everyone wants to kill roaches and rodents, but if you want to let spiders or anything else live, then you probably want to rethink your pest control method.  It seems to work, though, and I would recommend the brand.

This is too cruel a device for me to want to use for mice and rats, but I've discovered it's great for spiders and insects.  Yeah, it's still cruel.  I guess it's easy not to care about being cruel to insects.
summary: Good to use for insects and spiders

reviewText: I know, I know. We all want to live in a Walt Disney World where bluebirds flutter around us and mice help us become princesses. ~sigh~ But sadly, the real world is NOT like that! When you find mice gnawing into your Starbuck's whole bean coffee bag or eating MATCH STICKS in your pantry, it comes down to YOU vs. THEM and how much damage you will put up with happening in your home!We live in an almost 100 year old house that used to be a grocery store in the 1920's. After 94 years of settling into the sand dune it was built upon, there are loads of mouse-sized cracks and crevices from the root cellar beneath us for the little buggers to make regular trips into our home. When you pull your Granny's perfectly seasoned frying pan from the oven, only to find it coated in mouse urine and turds, you'll do ANYTHING to stem the flow of rodents.I use the regular Tomcat Glue traps for catching mice but those boards are way too limited for the nastiest of nasties: VOLES!!! We had a massive family of voles that chewed through our wood siding to get to our bird seed in the breezeway, and then chewed from the breezeway into our coat closet, setting up shop! Even our 4 cats wouldn't tangle with the voles, they are such violent Tasmanian Devil-like creatures!I found that the Rat Traps were the ONLY glue boards that would hold the trashing and squealing force of the 1.5" voles, who could chew/tear right through a standard trap.If you want/need to be very humane, as soon as I hear one being caught, I wrap the critter and board in soft paper towels, then into a plastic shopping bag, and then right into our garage deep freeze for the kindest method of extermination. Half an hour at 20 degrees puts them into a gentle forever sleep; it's the best compromise I can come up with in having a rodent-free home and being able to sleep at night from guilt.

This is not a very humane way of killing the menacing rodent, but it works. Keep a small piece of cheese or peanut butter and let it sit in the path of the rodent. When the animal steps on the glue trap, it gets stuck, and slowly dies within a day or two. The design is fine and it works but in my experience, the rodent poison is more effective and quick. There are several types of bait station containing the poisonous material inside (Bromethalin) are available. If humane way of getting rid of rat/mice is your main consideration, then this baby is not yours.

If the thought of finding a live critter struggling to be free doesn't bother you then these glue traps will be good for you. I find that they work very well and not only catch critters, but also creepy crawlies. You will find spiders, centipedes, and other legged creatures in these traps. I've used them in areas where I have insects and no mice/rats just to catch the bugs. The only downside is that sometimes when you catch mice in these they live for quite a while, trying to escape. If you're using it in an area that you don't frequent (shed, garage) then that won't be a bother for you. We've had lots of luck with these glue traps over the years.

When properly (strategically) placed, this trap is very effective at catching rats and mice.  The problem is that you then have to deal with the killing part, which is the kind of work that nightmares are made of.That said, this is kind of the lesser of several evils.  Poison is dangerous and environmentally unfriendly, snap traps are difficult to catch anything with and can be dangerous to pets, and these things are messy and medieval.I'm not sure what the best solution is, but this is certainly among them.
summary: It works, but leaves the worst part to you.

reviewText: Used it the first time and saw mice prints till my brilliant wife told me to use the glue-trap by taping it against the wall rather than on the ground.Worked the 2nd time around when the mice got its body tapered to the glue, though it was still alive when we found it. Had to kill it manually but its not an issue with me..
summary: Place it against the wall (as opposed to on the floor) for results

reviewText: What you get . . . . A package of 2 glue traps.  Each trap is rectangular, approximately 4 1/2" x 9", a shallow 3/8" high plastic tray containing and ultra-sticky day-glo green glue.  It's pesticide free, and ready and easy to use immediately.Does it work?  Yes, it works great on mice, rats, insects, spiders, scorpions, etc.  It also works on pet hamsters, kittens, birds, etc -- so use caution and common sense.Personally, I use mine exclusively for insects/spiders . . . in the garage (hiding it on the floor under a shelf where it collects spiders), and adjacent to a sliding patio door that insects occasionally slip in through.  In the case of the patio door, although the trap is 3/8" high, I butt it inside against the raised lower frame rail of the door.  Insects do not have to climb to get into the trap, they simply crawl over the rail and down into the trap.  The curious and mobile spiders in the garage also have no problem getting into, and stuck in, the traps.An additional note about the plastic tray design.  I prefer it.  In my patio door application, I had previously used an Ortho Home Defense branded trap, in which the glue is simply deployed on a flat paperboard base.  Over time, the glue slowly melted and migrated onto my doorframe and carpet (where it continued to do its job, but also made a mess).So how about rodents?  Sorry, but I will not use this trap for mice, which will indeed become trapped - but also terrified and/or eventually starve to death (or even possibly escape, but with less than four feet).  With mice, I prefer to live trap and relocate.  For rats, which thankfully are not currently a problem here, I admit I will use ANYTHING (I had one invade once through a basement drain.  He laughed off the snap trap I used, but succumbed to the poison I put out).An additional note - This trap works only by trapping with the glue surface.  It contains no poison or bait.  However, I see no reason why putting a little food bait in the center of the trap would not enhance the success probability.
summary: Great for trapping invading insects (I won't use it for mice)

reviewText: This is very heavy so when it arrives at your door and you have to bring it inside you will know that you did something. Buy a bench get a free workout.Very solid construction. My box was not damaged so most parts went together pretty easy. A rubber mallet is always good to have to smack stubborn parts together. This will last for a long time and makes your garage or even a big closet look organized and stylish. Downside is it makes the rest of your storage solutions look like crap.

What would be an otherwise great product is marred by the company's inattention to a major problem that has been pointed out in other reviews:  the poor packaging.  Read the other reviews, and you'll see that many have had the same experience:  They open the package to assemble this item only to discover that parts of it are bent due to poor packaging.  Another reviewer pointed out that he just used a rubber hammer to fix the dent in his door. However, others are not so fortunate with regard to where the damage occurs. For instance, on my product, the tracks that the doors are supposed to slide on were significantly bent. My husband tried his best to straighten them, but couldn't get them 100%, so now my I have a hard time sliding the doors.  Yes, I could call the company and ask them for replacement tracks, but that's an extra step I should not have to take.  This problem is pervasive enough (based on the other reviews) that Gladiator should rectify it by packing their products more securely.  I won't be ordering any other products like this from Gladiator until I'm sure they've corrected this packaging issue.
summary: Poor packaging almost ensures a defective product

reviewText: This is a large and heavy storage bench that is built like a tank.  I was able to put 18 shoes/boots in this which freed up my shoe cabinet.  The added bonus of this is that it is a proper bench that looks fantastic.  Full grown men can sit and stand on this and it will not break.  I expect this to last a lifetime.It is very simple to assemble as well.  This is a definite must have.
summary: Built like a tank and very functional

reviewText: This is a quality, solid bench that looks so nice I put it in the family room instead of the garage. The wooden bamboo top matches my furniture and the storage below is handy to have. It comes with several adjustable wire shelves. It has adjustable feet and the bench stays put with no wobbling even if I stand on it. Several people can sit on it and it doesn't budge.Assembly was easy. It took my husband and I about an hour from start to finish. The instructions have photos and good directions. If followed step by step you will have no trouble putting it together.This is a gorgeous 5-star product that arrived with some shipping damage, and therefore the loss of a star in the rating. I have received high tech products in perfect condition so I know the shipping can be done almost flawlessly if packaged correctly.It is a testament to the quality of the product that the damage was not worse and we were able to pound most of it out with a rubber mallet. The remaining damage is not so horrible as to send it back but it is annoying to have several small dents in the wood top and a still slightly crushed spot in the door. Unfortunately the dent in the door is near the track so it does not slide smoothly. It works, but it sticks and needs an extra push. All this could have been avoided if the bench had better packaging. A layer of stiff foam surrounding the product would prevent dents and tears in the cardboard. If packaging changes aren't made, this type of damage will continue to occur as most shippers are not careful.Other than the shipping issue I am pleased with the bench and it's a fine addition to my home.

If you're familiar with the Gladiator products, it will be no surprise to you that this bench is heavy, durable, and very attractive.The top is thick bamboo (looks like kitchen butcher block), and the unit weighs about 90 pounds. I actually think it's overkill ...especially for storing your work boots! LOL (like the pictures show)The only challenge with the bench is getting it delivered in one piece (mine came in perfect form, but there really is very little padding).However, this is actually my least favorite Gladiator product - at almost $300 it's about the most expensive item in the Gladiator line, and the least practical & cost effective.If you're wanting to upgrade your garage/basement storage, I would actually start with the cabinets (they call them "wall boxes", which start at around $125) or the modular gearbox (i.e. base cabinet), which actually are great values. Those are actually less expensive & higher quality than typical kitchen cabinets (and they don't need to be finished LOL). As for the storage bench, it's super nice but I'm kindof at a loss on how to use it.
summary: Super heavy duty (almost 100 pounds) ... too nice for boots LOL

reviewText: This looks too good for most garages, but not quite nice enough to put in most houses.  Anyway, it is really quite strong, to my surprise.  The top - even though just bamboo - is super solid and the steel frame and leveling feet keep it firmly planted on the ground.I have mine behind one car in the garage below the power sub panel.  It's nice, but I end up just piling stuff on top of it, so I could imagine I might like a taller storage unit for that space instead.  It does seem like it might be ideal for a mudroom, and I think that's what they're going for, considering it's deep enough for shoes.  Even so, it's got plenty of uses, considering you couldn't want for a stronger item and it's not going to bring down the appearance of your average garage.If this proves too difficult to move by yourself due to its weight and strange size, simply open the box and move one piece at a time.
summary: When you need a step stool

reviewText: Summary: Damaged during shipping, but great customer service comeback.Details:This storage bench is a very sturdy and well engineered product. The parts are all sturdy and high quality, with nice finish and fit. Clear instructions, and a wonderful piece for my garage and all the boots and shoes that we don't want coming into the house. The one negative issue is that the unit came damaged, as apparently a good many of them do according to other reviewers. I have posted some of the damage photos on this product page. It's strange because the part that was damaged was the metal base. It is in the middle of the box the unit comes in (BTW, you have to assemble the bench, which is no big deal at all). The box was totally fine. The internal packing material seemed OK, but the base was dented. I'm no packaging engineer, but apparently someone that works there isn't either. I think they need to pad the base better and somehow keep the heavy laminated bamboo top from crushing it during shipping. Like I said above, the external box looked fine, so I didn't gig the shipper. I think that somehow the internal load shifted and dented the base, even though it is not obvious to me how this happened.One other damaged piece was the top, but since it was minor, and the damage was in a back corner, I didn't bother. If you are more picky, you will want to make sure you go over this carefully upon receipt.The good news is that I called the GGW help number and it was immediately answered by a nice lady in the midwest who was able to help me. She quickly figured out which part I needed and had it shipped out to be received within a week. Of course, I need to figure out how to get rid of a five foot piece of 18 gauge formed sheet steel while paying attention to the environment ...After discussing the scarred top, I decided to just let it go as above because it would have required getting Amazon to ship a whole extra unit. For some reason, they can ship all the parts as repair items other than the top. In any case, it occurred to me that the next set would just as likely be damaged if I ordered the whole thing, so I thought there was less risk in shipping just the one part. It turns out I was right and the individual base that shipped as a replacement was flawless.Conclusion:Nice bench. Works great once all the parts are there. Don't expect the first one to arrive perfectly so give some extra time to make fixes with the cooperation of the wonderful GGW service crew. This means you also need to inpect it immediately upon arrival. Don't let one of these sit around waiting for that spare time to do the assembly - just do it now so you don't blow your parts warranty period, or your Amazon return time. I took off one star for this imperfect shipping. If all had been well out of box, I would give it a five.
summary: Poor shipping quality, great customer service

reviewerName: Y. R. Wu "The will to win is nothing without ...
reviewText: Very nice, solid feel.  Mine arrived with a few dings in the door, top and back panel.  Nothing terrible, but I have to think that someone is going to end up with worse damage out there.This assembled quickly, one person, in about 35 minutes.  The wire shelves are sturdy enough for shoes (which is their recommended use), but if you're thinking of putting heavy tools in there, you may want to think again.  There are a few different options for how to install the shelves (for example, if you want to be able to put boots on one side).The bamboo top is really nice, though of course there is now a ~3/4" gouge on the top from shipping damage.  I'll post some pictures of the shipping damage.  Nice sturdy feet are adjustable to eliminate any rocking.5 stars for appearance, 4 stars for function and feel, 5 stars for assembly ease, but shipping damage ends up with 4 stars overall.
summary: Solid and easy to assemble, but watch out for shipping damage!

reviewText: After building a house which has two stories, we found that the 2nd story air ducts in the master bedroom were fairly weak with their output. I had been wanting a solution to help drive cold or warm air into that room. After receiving the iPower GLFANXBOOSTER6 Inline Ducting Booster Fan, I plugged it in to gauge the strength of the air movement and was impressed. I decided to put it in-line in the basement duct work that leads into the master bedroom on the 2nd floor.It's important to understand a few things about this fan. While it does come with a plug-in cord, for most installations it would be better to cut off the plug and simply wire it into the system so that it comes on ONLY when the HVAC is running. It's not rocket science to do this, but if you are not familiar with wiring or HVAC systems, you would be better served to get help from someone who is. As well, considering it's going to most likely be installed into existing systems, you will need to cut duct work which is not something most consumers are prepared to deal with. Get help if you need it, don't try this if you are not experienced at such things.One way that this product could be improved is to have crimping on BOTH ends because when you are putting a booster fan into a system, you are most likely going to be cutting the existing duct work to fit it in. While purists might argue that you don't want to cause drag on the air flow by an incorrectly placed overlap in ducting, I doubt that one instance of this would harm efficiencies to any great extent. Considering you are going to place this in-line into existing ductwork, it's much easier to do by cutting the duct a bit smaller than the overall length of the fan's duct work and (if both ends were crimped) simply install the fan in the gap.This fan did improve the flow into the bedroom and I'm looking forward to the cooling season to see if the results are the same with AC that I'm now seeing with heat.Four stars, one taken away for the fan having a plug (which will not be used in most instances, IMO) and also for not being crimped on both ends.

This is an impressively powerful fan. It came without instructions, but it simply plugs in and oola!It is very small and compact -- it would fit in a shopping bag.I didn't particularly need an air duct ventilation system, so I found myself turning it on and experimenting with what it was able to do. I found it is capable of cooling down a medium size room, a garage, or a wet basement, or an outdoor tent in about ten to twenty minutes.
They were easy to install in my tent, definitely a little louder than I prefer but not horriible. I dont like them not having power switches and having to unplug to shut off.

I installed this in a detached greenhouse. It is lightweight and keeps the air moving. It is a tad noisy but that is not an issue since it is not in a living space. Essentially a no frills version, this fan does not have adjustable speed, it is either on or off. The power cord is short, be prepared to use an extension cord or position near an available plug. For a low end fan, it is simple and effective. Recommended.

I won't go into the technical aspects of the fan as other reviewers have covered that information well.This fan was designed for duct work but have modified it for different uses.I have attached 4 door pulls, pop-riveted two to each end for support, for hanging and for guiding direction of air with the usage of tie down straps or bungee cords.I have used it in the attic to move air while I was working in the attic pulling fresh air from outside.I have also used this in the crawl space to move the air in the dead areas an hour before working in the crawl space, this removed the bad air and for some reason the high vibration and noise of the fan seems to move the  spiders away from the area where the fan is , we live in the south and there are often brown recluse spiders in the crawl spaces.I have also used this in our garage while welding to ventilate. I am eager to try using it in the winter to ventilate the garage while working on a running car.  So far this has been a great little fan for the money , but as others have said it is loud.This little fan is only limited to applications by your imagination, handy, powerful air mover.PS Do not try to use this as a leaf blower, it does not work.....(just kidding.)
summary: Great little fan for the money , lots of uses

reviewText: This iPower Inline Fan doesn't come with instructions but is easy enough to figure out. We installed this to help vent fumes out of our workshop and it performs that function well.My only issue is that it does rattle a good bit.Recommended!CFH
summary: Works Well For My Needs - Recommended

reviewText: This review is from: iPower GLFANXBOOSTER6 Inline Ducting Booster Fan with Cord, 6 inch (Lawn & Patio)Customer review from the Amazon Vine Program (What's this?)This booster fan has limitations that make it a great solution only under certain circumstances.1) This must be the primary fan because it otherwise slows air too much when not powered up and running.2) This fan moves air very well. The other side of that benefit is the noise. It will be a constant noise, although that can be mitigated through the use of inexpensive insulation.3) There are no speeds. It's on or it's off.4) The pricing is more than fair. That makes it tempting to use this in other than the precise circumstances it requires.
summary: Great solution in very precise circumstances

reviewText: The overall concept of this product is great - a fan housed in an 8-inch section of duct work that helps boost the airflow to a far room that doesn't get enough heat/cooling. However, in actual practice, it's not very convenient to use.The fan moves a lot of air - very powerful motor. The build quality of the unit appears quite good. It feels solid, and the attached power cord is stout.It is a bit on the noisy side, especially if there's a bit of duct work rattle. Not horrible, but don't expect whisper-quiet running. You will clearly hear this fan when it's operating.My biggest problem is the lack of an auto switch that turns the fan on/off only when there is air movement in the duct work. This is strictly a manul operation - plug it in and it turns on; unplug to turn off. While having a switch that senses air flow in the duct would obviously add to the cost, it would make this a far more practical product for duct work boosting.I found that it's better suited to on-demand venting. I added some inexpensive flexible duct to it and use it for venting the kitchen when I'm grilling indoors or roasting coffee beans (both of which can be smelly/smoky tasks). This works far, far better than just the range vent since I can position it exactly where it's needed, and direct the exhaust outside.A useful item, but not as useful as it could be for its intended purpose of duct work boosting. Three stars.
summary: Bit loud, not all that convenient to use as a duct line booster

reviewText: Listing description seems to be for a house air conditioner booster, I would not recommend for that use.However as a bathroom, laundry room, etc. exhaust or for airflow in a greenhouse this fan is perfect.The fan is not super efficient or create a lot of speed but it does seem to move the rated 240cfm and is not very loud.The sound is not annoying or high pitched. Imagine the sound you might make with a comfortable ooooooooo sound you can make with your own voice. Probably quieter than your current bathroom or kitchen exhaust.The fan has no switch or speed control, just a 3 prong 6 foot cord. Provide power and it runs.
summary: Great for a green house or exhaust fan

reviewText: I have a basement furnace that sends hot air to a single output vent, centrally located. There is one room that is away from the main area to which we sent a duct from the central location. Unfortunately, given the obvious issues (air will travel along the route that has no back pressure preferentially, and the single large output vent is preferable to the duct), the duct alone doesn't bring in very much heat and a booster fan should solve the problem.Fortunately, the output of the duct is nearby to a wall AC outlet and so this particular model, with its cord already attached, is perfect for my setup. A few sheet-metal screws later, the fan is mounted and we've got plenty of heat coming through. A couple of issues remain. First is that you probably won't want the fan running all the time, and second is the noise. This is not a quiet component.Running the fan to a switched outlet will solve the first problem, but having a rheostat in line with it might solve both. This is a powerful enough fan (drawing about half an amp) that turning down the power should result in still getting significant flow while cutting the noise considerably. Some of the noise is the fan motor itself - you can deal with that by wrapping an insulator around the outside of the motorized section of duct. Some of the noise is simply the air blowing through the duct and out the end. That will be cut by reducing the flow speed. There's nothing here that isn't straight-forward, and I'd rather start out with too much power than too little.
This inline ducting booster fan is made to be used as part of a system. Not a stand-alone fan. It does work as described to move air, but it just makes too much noise for us.
summary: Reasonably priced inline ducting fan that works to move the air, but makes a lot of noise.

reviewText: I didn't particularly have a ventilation issue that I was hoping to address with this fan, but I do have a one story home that sprawls a bit, so I had a notion that locating this fan in front of the master bedroom (the room farthest from the HVAC unit) would probably give the room a heating and cooling boost. When I opened the box, however, there were no instructions. That's fine, because I  guess you just open up a duct and insert this between the ends you open up and away you go. But that brings us to the next problem: this plugs in and doesn't have a switch. My ducts run through the crawl space, where there are no electrical outlets. On top of that, without cutting a hole in the floor, there would be no access to turn it off and on by plugging and unplugging it. So, in order to be able  to use this, I'd have to do some major electrical work and have to come up with some way to be able to reach it without having to go outside and crawl around under the flooring. Since, as I said, I don't really have a ventilation issue, I decided to cut my losses and leave it uninstalled. I'll tell you though, when I plugged it in this thing blows a very powerful stream of air and is pretty quiet, so for someone who is handy with electrical and HVAC work, this will be an easy and effective solution to boost airflow in a home. If you're an average guy like me, you'll have to call someone to install it for you.
summary: Better be handy if you order this product

reviewText: All iPower Inline Ducting Booster fans suffer from the same deficiency, as many larger fans do - noise.  Due to unsophisticated design, their simplistic propellers generate noise (air vibration) driven by the vibrating blades, which edges are straight and allow small blade vibrations to travel away from the axis and to gain strength and amplitude along their path up to the blade's outer end, which thus vibrates even more and pushes the air to vibrate along that can be heard as noise.  If the blades were narrow and shaped like arcs curved forward in the direction of the rotation, as in the submarine propellers, the waves of vibration would travel away from the end of blades toward the axis and cancel themselves mutually.  However, iPower fans are useful where noise is not a problem.  They are robust.
summary: Poor design of propeller causes noise

reviewText: This fan works very well and does everything it was aid to have done. The only thing is like most people said it is a little noisy. Still it gets the air moving nicely so over all I think it is a good product.

iPower Inline ducting 6 inch booster fan has enough power to boost the air to wherever it is needed.  There is no on/off switch just a plug in power cord.  Place this little guy wherever you need air in or out.  I'm trying to decide how well this will work in moving the air around the attic.  If your in need of an inline booster fan this guy will certainly do the job and is well worth the look.

I'm a unhandy Women.But I thought this might work for what I needed it for!I hired a man to installed this iPower Ducting booster fan through a duct in my 14 ft. ceiling in my living room, through to my TV room about 20 ft away , to hopefully bring the warm air into the tv room..There was a new switch installed into the tv room. When turned on the fan worked, but did not bring in any warm air.!That said, I do not think it was the fault of the IPower ducting booster, but I did expect at least some warm air coming through.I took a chance this might work, but as I said it did not bring warm air into the room. That is the reason for the 4 star.

I am editing this to remove a star. We have used this some more and it is louder.Original reviewWe have a wood burning furnace. It has a huge blower on it that distributes the air throughout our (large, drafty) house. The furnace will produce heat no matter what. But I have always been a little concerned about a power outage leaving us without a way to heat since the blower is powered by electricity.We had a relative help us install this. We wired it so it could be run off a battery system that he set up. I am not sure exactly what he did. He did mention that you could use a marine battery too. We have a solar panel and will wire it so that it is solar next summer when it is warm.A few days after we put this in, we had a power outage with sub zero temperatures. This little fan was very noisy but it kept moving the heat from the furnace into the kitchen and an adjoining room. Our pipes didn't freeze and we were comfortable. This is too noisy to use every day. But this a great emergency preparedness item.

I like it fine, and I'm enjoying looking at it and dreaming. Plug it in and it goes.  There is no on-off switch.  You could plug it into a timer or thermostat for intermittent use.  It is sturdy and moves a lot of air.  It is not terribly noisy.  I got it to boost the passive geothermal heating/cooling for an earth-sheltered greenhouse that we will be constructing.  As soon as we get a round tuit.  I hope they feature them on Vine soon.
summary: Good air movement, straightforward and little to go wrong.

reviewText: The simplicity of the unit can't be beat. It's a powerful fan in a 6" duct that you can plug into a timer or regular three prong outlet, with a 4'.5" cord. Moves a lot of air.Only con is its a bit noisy, similar to a hair dryer, ok for garage, garden shed, or chicken house.
summary: Works well but loud, easy install

reviewText: This strong ducting fan arrived with one of the screws anchoring the fan to the metal strip at the base having fallen off, so I had to screw it back in place so the fan wouldn't be loose and hitting the sides of the cylinder. After that I just plugged it in to an electrical outlet with its grounded plug and it was running smoothly. If you have this fan you will probably want an extension cord unless your outlet is very close to where the fan will be - and some type of switch for the power outlet since this fan has no power switch. This is a pretty simple, basic fan, ideal for air ducts or small areas where air needs to be blown and circulated. You may want to cover the end of it so that nothing accidentally goes into the spinning metal blade. Overall this fan is OK, seems like it will be durable, and is valuable for specific uses. It could have had more frills considering the price point, so I'm giving it just 3 stars.
summary: Strong ducting fan, needs external power control, extension cord.

reviewText: First, let me say that I don't use this fan for duct boosting although it was designed as such.I use this fan with a 20' length of plastic flexible duct to give myself some much needed fresh air when working in my shop. I place the fan unit just under the overhead door and run the duct to my workspace, usually in the corner. The airflow is exactly what I needed to keep cool and not blow everything around like a traditional shop fan or orbiting fan.Noise isn't issue because the motor is far way, but I can see where the noise might be an issue if you're up close and personal to the fan. Since the fan housing is thin galvanized metal I'm sure a bit of duct tape will quiet things down quite a bit.The 5' cord is more than adequate, but you can also add a proper extention cord if needed.For my needs this is a decent fan and works well. The plugged cord adds a mobile aspect as well.

Only the best designed HVAC systems provide a good flow of conditioned air to the rooms that need it the most.This device allows a retrofit when you have access to the ducts that have an exposed 6 inch diameter round duct.Mrs. Gearhead thinks it a little noisey, but I did not find it objectionable.There are a few changes I would make to the design. The 6 foot ac cord required that I install an electrical circuit to feed power to the elecric motor in this "booster". And then the there is the problem of activating the motor only when it was needed. To automate this, you need a relay to attach to the furnace blower motor so that this booster only runs when the blower is moving air. An experienced HVAC installer can do this, but then he could also trim the other ducts so theis auxilliary booster is not needed.So, it is no silver bullet to the average homeowner.
summary: This duct booster should be installed by a pro.

reviewText: This is a 6" inline duct booster fan.  It is intended to go along a 6" round duct to increase air flow.  It works well and moves a fair amount of air.  It is not noisy.  It comes with a cord with a three prong plug.  I had to cut that off and wire it into a junction box with a wall switch.  I don't think many people have ac plugs inside their walls.
summary: works very well - fairly quiet, but plug is fairly useless

reviewText: This fan has very good air flow and hardly makes any noise if properly positioned.  When I first plugged it in to test it I thought it didn't work.  Then I noticed the piipe around the fan was slightly out of round.  I pushed it in place and plugged it back in and it took of with no problems.

This inline fan boosts air circulation to a distant heating/cooling vent, but it is too noisy for constant use. It can be turned off by unplugging it (down two flights of stairs), but then it occludes almost all air coming through the vent, making the vent more ineffective than it was to begin with. It may suit someone else's situation, but not mine. 3 stars for moving air, minus two for noise and inconvenience.
summary: Noisy when used, blocks air when off

reviewText: I ordered the iPower GLFANXBOOSTER6 Inline Ducting Booster Fan for our basement because the air was too musty and stagnant down there. After an easy installation and running it for a week now, the air has markedly improved. A must have!

I have a wood stove down stairs and an ineffective grate in the floor between stove and upstairs.  This fan was inserted between the top and bottom of the great and fitted with a speed control.  Now the heat comes upstairs where it is needed.  Good product, well made and recommended.

We ordered this fan to use in tandem with our bathroom exhaust fan to increase air movement. As a casual DIYer it was a breeze for him to install. The fan is on the loud side but being up in our attic it really doesn't bother us. The fan works great and has helped to keep the moisture that used to condense on the walls during showers to a minimum. Great product at an affordable price.

This is a great little fan that moves some serious air volume.  In my opinion the fan is plenty quiet, but I am one who tends to like a little bit of white noise (especially when sleeping at night).  Do be aware of what you are getting; you should expect to need to be able to do some ductwork, possible some wiring, and generally be handy to install (depending on your application).  This isn't a Fisher-Price desk fan from WalMart!  So depending on how fancy you want to get, you may want to install the fan in conjunction with a thermostat so that when temps are high the fan will automatically start moving air.  Anyway, it does the job - highly recommended!
summary: Works great - pushes a large volume of air!

reviewText: I needed a quiet fan that was going to get the job done, this was perfect.  This is a small fan, it fits well in small spaces, and it is extremely quiet.  I was amazed at how quiet it was.  I also liked this because the cord that it came with was grounded and it was long, which worked well for me.
summary: iPower 4 6 8 inch Inline Ducting Booster Fan with Cord

reviewText: My plan for this fan is to provide air circulation for a home greenhouse. It arrived in perfect condition, and after plugging it in, found it operates smoothly. The level of noise is not as loud as a kitchen blender, and although noticeable is certainly nothing extraordinary. Out of curiosity I visited the manufacturer’s website (printed on the label pasted to the fan casing) hoping to obtain more information on the warranty, or instructions, etc. All I found were grow lights and accessories for them. At the time of this review there is nothing posted about this fan on the site.What is seen in the two pictures on the product page, besides the shipping box, is all that is included. So, preparation for installation of the fan will vary depending upon its intended use. Simple and straightforward, this bare bones device provides the perfect solution for my needs. Again, nothing but the fan wired to a five and a half foot three-prong cord is included. The intended use will dictate how much work will be necessary to incorporate the device including installation, wiring, etc. in individual applications, but because of its simplicity, it can perform in a variety of situations.
summary: iPower Inline six inch ducting Booster Fan

reviewText: You get what you pay for applies here. This is a mid-quality product. It is made pretty well and I expect it to last 5-10 years of intermittent use. It is a bit loud. This noise can be reduced with insulated duct wrapped around it and using it in the proper places. Installing it at the beginning of runs seems to be the quietest place to locate it. It seems to "push" air better than it "pulls" it.Solid for stars for performance, less one for build quality.

We received an "iPower GLFANXBOOSTER6 Inline Ducting Booster Fan with Cord, 6 inch" via the Vine Program to evaluate and found it to be a well-constructed unit, albeit a very basic one. Here's the breakdown on the pluses/minuses:Pluses (▲):▲ Solid construction: both the 6-inch can and the fan appear to be of good quality and assembled well▲ It moves air nicely▲ Easy to install between 2 sections of standard 6-inch ducting▲ AffordableMinuses (▼):▼ It has no on/off (neither switch nor air-flow sensor)...just a standard plug▼ It is quite noisy...about as loud as a hair dryer running at high speedWe feel that having a constantly running fan (and noisy, to boot) even when there is no flowing air to boost, is a considerable drawback. It might be possible to setup and use a relay circuit that will energize the fan's outlet when the heating/cooling thermostat activates...maybe that was their intention and/or expectation...but it would be nice if it were designed into the unit. Thus, we gave this a "good" 3-star rating, since it is well-made and affordable...but has room for improvement.

I have a large multi-story house and the air-conditioning/heating has a hard time getting to a couple of remote rooms.  This generally calls for a booster fan to assist in the distance that the conditioned air needs to travel so I ordered this unit.  Here is what I liked:1.  The unit is a very simple construction that consists of a 6 inch wide piece of metal ducting that is 7 inches long. The ducting is configured to join two pieces of metal ducting with one flared end and one ribbed end.  The fan is mounted in the middle of the unit and the cord exits the unit with a three prong plug at the end of about 5 feet of cord.2.  The unit does move a good volume of air.3.  The motor unit is supposed to be sealed so it should not need servicing during its life span.What I did not like:1.  The fan is just that, a constant running fan.  There is no air flow sensor so unless you want this running 24 hours a day, 7 days a week you need to wire an outlet that is controlled by your air handling system.2.  The fan unit in mine made a god awful racket when it was plugged in.  Turns out that the mounting screws were very loose and allowed the fan blade to contact the metal housing.  The nuts that they used have ribs to prevent it from coming loose, but they do NOT do a good job of that.  They came loose within a few minutes of running.  I added shake washers to it and then it worked just fine.3.  This unit also presumes that you have a 7 inch section of metal pipe missing from your ducting.  If you have flexible ducting or you have long lengths of metal ducting you will need to modify your ducting to accept this unit!!!As long as you are aware that you are going to need to modify your ducting and install a control unit to turn this on and off with your heating/air-conditioning system, and you install shake washers to hold the fan in place, then this is a decent unit.I would recommend this unit as long as you understand the above caveats.
summary: iPower GLFANXBOOSTER6 Inline Ducting Booster Fan with cord

reviewerName: Richard C. Drew "Anaal Nathra/Uthe vas Bethod...
reviewText: If you have a room at the end of a long duct run that's always too cold in winter and too warm in the summer, this is a great solution. It can also be used as an exhaust fan - I actually have a couple of these. Our basement has a bar and pool table - when we have a party, it's not unusual to have 10 people smoking down there.  So I installed a large 12x12 vent over the bar, reduced that to a 6" duct, then installed this about 4 feet away. This way there's almost zero noise. The other end connects to a spare heat vent against the chimney. Sucks out ALL the smoke.For the bedroom with the temperature problem, I installed this at the final reduction point - where the ducts hit 6 inches.  It makes a huge difference!With any use, you'll have to figure out how to control the fan. By the bar we did an extension cord run with a remote control (used one of those X10 things.)  Amazon also sells several 110v remotes.  Since the ductwork for the bed room runs through the garage, I concocted a similar arrangement.  This way I can use the remote control to turn the fan on or off. There are also variable speed versions of the remotes.As for the noise. There is ZERO mechanical noise. All the noise is the air moving. If this is only a few feet away, you will hear very little sound. It's also well balanced, so there's no vibration.  This unit weighs just over 2 poinds. If you install it in a long run, you may have a sagging problem . Simply use some galvanized pipe strapping to hold it up. To zero-out ANY noise from the motor that may occur over time (balance problems caused by debris, dust, etc.) place a thick piece of rubber between the strap and whatever you attach it to. Old rubber floor mat, chunk of tire, etc. Anything works.
summary: Wow - this thing moves the air!

reviewText: I put this fan in my laundry room, when I bought the house there was hole space in the floor from the previous occupier, I figured they had a different washer then realized when I got this that it was probably what they had also because it fitted straight into there.  A stroke of luck on my part and remarkably it now vents the laundry room perfectly.  This room also doubles as a kitty litter place so I now get less smell of both damp and kitty poop.  I don't run the fan all the time, I decided to wire it on a timer but it does the job and it is fresher in there.As far as noise it is quieter than a roof fan so it suits me and laundry rooms are noisy anyway when you have the washer running which is primarily when the fan runs.  I can't complain about the build quality of the fan, it is made from galvanized steel and runs smoothly and efficiently for me.  Certainly worth a try if you need more venting in a room.

This inline booster fan is an easy to install addition to help increase airflow in long runs of central heat and air duct-work. The fan comes with no instructions, but how to install it is pretty much self-explanatory. Of course, you'll have to run an electrical line in your attic to provide power for it, and it would be best to have it controlled by a relay switch controlled by the main air-handler so that it only receives power to run while the main air-handler fan is running. The fan itself is a bit on the noisy side, it would not be an issue in most industrial settings, but in a quiet home the drone it makes will quickly become annoying as it travels through the ductwork and makes itself known in every room of your house.

Being in an older double-wide, our A/C & heating units are one one side of the house, so the two bedrooms on the opposite side of the house don't get the same 'gusto' of refrigerated or heated air as the master bathroom or master bath. If we've got the A/C on, we tend to turn it down when it gets really cold on the master bedroom side of the house, but if we go into the other rooms, it's sometimes a 20 degree difference. The criticisms of the fan being loud are legitimate, but it would depend on where the fan is located. For us, we're using our extra bedrooms as offices - the fan is under the floor with the ducting and over the sound of the ceiling fans, computer, etc., it's not noticeable... or at least it doesn't bother me. What it does do, is help to bring some of that warmed or cooled air to the other side of the house, somewhat evening out the temperature throughout the house. I'd imagine if your duct work is between thin walls, the noise would be irksome if you put the fan there. It would all depend on placement - such as in the attic, or where appropriate for your home situation.
summary: Helps to push cold/warm air to the other side of the house

reviewText: We use this fan primarily for cooling off the grow light in our hydroponic garden. This has worked great for us. It is very quiet. We can barely hear the fan when it is running and it keeps the light cool and the room cool as well. It's also energy efficient, which is very important for us and works great for our needs in general.

We needed something to replace the obnoxiously loud fan over the stove that came with the microwave. Moving the fan up into the attic would be the ideal solution and this fan works perfect for that.The fan comes with an attached power cord right out of the box. So first thing I did was plug it in. And yes it was noisy but due to a major problem - it wasn't put together! The screws holding the blades and the motor in place were not tight! I don't think that is something  you should have to check especially since these are inside the unit. Once I tightened these the fan wasn't nearly as noisy and should be fairly quiet once placed up in the attic.Overall it seems like a decent unit but having shipped it out with loose pieces does leave room for concern.
summary: Great fan but with a warning

reviewText: When this arrived, we used it to replace the booster fan that we had pushing heat to our master bedroom.  Prior to the old fan, we used to have a problem where heating and air conditioner performance would be lacking in that one room.  We'd turn the heat up and the rest of the house would get hot, but the temperature in the bedroom would barely change.  The fan we had in there solved the problem partially, but it was lacking in the amount of air that it moved.This fan does a lot better in terms of the amount of air that it moves, but it is a little loud.  Since we have the fan in the basement and our bedroom is on the second floor, we didn't think that the noise would be an issue, but you can actually hear it coming out of the vent.  This might not be a huge problem if it only ran when the HVAC was on, but we have it plugged into an outlet that constantly provides power.The bottom line is that this fan does a good job, but you should wire it in a way that only has it come on when the HVAC is blowing.  This would be better both in terms of noise, but also because it would reduce your energy usage.

The room over the attached garage never gets warm. This room is where the washer/dryer live and also my sewing room.I thought I would try this fan to see if I could get heat to the room and start using the room again for sewing/crafts.It was easy to install but you will need an extension cord as the cord is only 5.5 feet long.It provides good air flow and delvered heat to the  room quickly. It is also quiet.While I realize it is meant more for permanent installation I have it set up so I can move it to a different area if I want to . I use it only when I am in the room, just turn it off when I leave the room. It has also helped to take the chill off  the Master bathroom ( which is right next to this  room and also over the garage) . The price is reasonable and you do not need to call a serviceman to install it. You can move it to other areas of your home with ease.

This is a booster fan designed to be installed in existing ac/heat duct work. Its best use is to boost air flow into rooms that get less air flow because they are located far from your air blower. These fans come in 4", 6" and 8" diameters so check to see what size your existing duct work is.This is powered via a 5 1/2' grounded electrical cord so you need to be sure there is an existing electrical outlet near where you want to place it. It's permanently lubricated so once installed, you don't need to do any regular maintenance on it.It is designed to move air so it makes noise. Think of your vent hood over your stove or a vent in your bathroom - it's that kind of noise. Noticeable but not annoyingly so to me. In fact, I had been using a standing fan in my bedroom directly beneath the vent to move more air and I enjoyed the white noise it created. This has replaced the standing fan and the noise doesn't bother me at all.Note: there are no instructions for installation included so if you have never installed ducting, you will need to do some Googling or have someone install it for you.

The fan is lightweight, and the cord comes with a plug attached.  However, we are still taking the route to have an HAVAC tech install it in the house.  Why?  Because I am not the handy type and anything done to the heat/air, I prefer a professional.Will have to wait for summer to rate the cooling assistance to our warmest room.

Plug it in and it a nice volume of air get pushed along.The “ipowergrowlight” tag implies this thing has a use I don’t quite understand.  So be it.  Now I know where to get high power digital ballasts and stuff.My particular use is an amateur wind tunnel.  It’s wonderful for that.The unit I received had a few screws loose and the fan could scrape the edge of the duct.  No big deal, but it does mean that someone installing the unit had better be clear headed enough to pay attention to details.This unit does not have a way to change the fan speed.  Different airspeed can only be obtained by restricting the air flow.

reviewerName: Wendi Barker "Wendi's Book Corner & What Wend...
reviewText: Our dryer is electric, and the air vent is about 15 feet long, which the Sears service tech said is LONG - but, he looked, and there is no good way to shorten it, so our dryer runs hot.  He did suggest adding an inline fan to help with the cooling and to move air more effectively.This is easy to install, and we currently have to use it with an extension cord.  I don't use it all the time because there is some noise, and it is against the wall to our family room.  I will certainly have it on during hot days, but the house is cold enough now that I think the air flow is ok.I read another review about adding it to a dimmer switch and tying it into a thermostat - love both ideas and may eventually try to do the same.  In the meantime, this is a great solution to a problem, and it should potentially add extra years to our dryer.
summary: Does a Great Job of Moving Airflow Through the Dryer Duct

reviewText: I didnt know much about carbon filters and have used mine for a few weeks now and it really seems to lend a huge hand as to control the smell.I do recommend this.also its supposed to get heavier over time too just so ya know,and it does it seems.esp. in humid climates.
This air scrubber does a great job for its size. wont get all the smell, but it gives it a good try.

This another ipower product that is a must in my garden.Helps keep the air clean and cuts out the smell when in the bloom phase.I recommended that ya buy something stronger than a booster fan with this filter.

I own a few of these and they all seem to work just fine. I can also reverse them for longer life, and replace the media when it becomes ineffective. The prefilter is washable and is easy to remove/replace.I'm not sure what else I could possibly want from this thing.
Now, this is quality. It got here in perfect condition and it is the second one I have ordered. Very well made! They are real nice people to work with.

This is a huge bag of the repellent. Sadly, this is also a product that's been discontinued for the reason that it most likely doesn't work. After following instructions and spreading the repellent over 4 days in different parts of the yard, I have not been able to spot any difference. I switched to Tomcat 34532 Mole and Gopher Liquid Repellent, 32-Ounce and was able to drive the mole(s) elsewhere.
summary: didn't work but another product from the same company did

reviewText: I had really hoped this product would get rid of the mole(s) or gopher(s) that have built tunnels in and under my vegetable garden.  This is the first year I've had to deal with these rodents possibly because of all the wet weather we have experienced this year creating very soft ground for the pests to play in.If I understand this product correctly it's not poison and will not harm moles or gophers.  The moles and gophers are supposedly repelled by the scent this leaves behind.  Whatever it's supposed to do, it's not doing it.  I'm seeing more and more tunnels every day.  Application is easy,  I'll give it an extra star for that, it just doesn't work.

This seems okay, but it was sort of fussy to use. Having them want you to spread it and then water it seemed like a pain, so I'll admit that I kinda put it out before a rain shower was supposed to hit and figured I'd let nature take care of the watering. I'm not really sure if that was a good idea or not, but this seems like it's temporarily done okay for discouraging the critters from hanging out.
summary: Having them want you to spread it and then water it seemed like a pain

reviewText: I've been having problems with my vegetable garden last year and this year.  There's a neighbourhood gopher that has built an intricate tunnel system under the road and across 6-8 back yards.  My kale was limping along last year after being munched on, and my cauliflower was completely gnawed to the ground.  This year it seems that the creature has developed a taste for squash leaves and has pulled the plants right our of the ground.Last year, I had the most success with liberal amounts of cayenne pepper as long as it didn't rain too much.  I also put a cayaenne and cat poop down its 2 tunnels that came by next to my vegetable patch.  But what really chased it off was my neighbour's 2 dogs.I have applied this repellent on 1 entrance and the liquid version offered by the same manufacturer on the 2nd entrance.  These seem to be more weatherproof than the cayenne and so far after 3 weeks I have not seen any additional damage to my growing vegetables.I will report back if anything changes for better or worse.

People have been experimenting with castor oil as a mole and gopher repellent for some time. Some folks say it works, some say it doesn't. I can't tell yet.The castor oil in this product is contained in pellets. The manufacturer, Motomco, says to "spread the granules on your lawn by hand or spreader. Water the granules into the soil for about 20 minutes to allow for the best penetration."  They also claim that since the ingredients are natural, the product is completely safe.But be cautious. Castor oil is fairly safe and is sometimes taken internally, but it can cause stomach discomfort, cramping, nausea, and faintness, according to WebMD, which also mentions that it is occasionally used to cause abortion. Probably you should not spread this by hand if you are pregnant.Another website (Washington State Fish and Wildlife) tells us that castor oil has been used in commercial preparations to repel moles with some success.  Supposedly the repellent "coats earthworms and other prey with castor oil. This renders the prey distasteful and, if eaten, gives the moles diarrhea."  The article says that "repellent may need to be reapplied before moles depart. Once moles move elsewhere, the solution usually remains effective for 30 to 60 days." It warns against using insecticides to get rid of moles, so the implied message is that the castor oil repellent is preferable.I should add a caution here. An old home remedy to repel moles involves castor beans. Do not attempt this unless you are familiar with the dangers of castor beans. Their shell (not the oil inside) contains ricin, a dangerous poison. So you are better off using this Tomcat product.
summary: Granules Contain Castor Oil to Repel Moles and Gophers

reviewText: I'm not sure that this is the most effective way to deal with moles in the yard. It is just a repellent so it's used to repel moles not to kill them or eliminate them. For me, the application process is quite lengthy and time-consuming for just a repellent. You have to apply daily to different areas of the lawn for 4 days in a process of trying to get the moles to move away from your lawn. Each day the process takes watering 20 minutes at a time. I think it an time-consuming process for something that is just an iffy solution from a product that has been discontinued by the manufacturer.

I cleared some drybrush and trees from the slope behind my backyard for fire prevention.  The gophers that were digging countless holes in the hard dirt of the slope decided to relocate to my backyard lawn.  It is "ON", varmints!  I've tried gopher repellents, gas bombs, traps, solar spike deterrents, and baits, with varying results.  Why not give this Tomcat Mole and Gopher Repellent a try?Dislikes:*Have to use a rotary type spreader to dispense these repellent granules THEN water for 20 minutes to let the ingredients soak in.*Main ingredient is Castor oil.  The gophers I'm trying to eliminate are smart as hell and were not deterred by these repellent granules.Results:*I followed the instructions precisely and spread my lawn in sequential areas from undamaged lawn towards the lawn boundaries.  Trying to "flush out" the gophers.  For the first two weeks, the gopher activity seemed to have ceased.*During the third week, gopher dug new smaller holes in other locations that branched out from the original gopher mound.Overall:Did deter the gophers for two weeks from digging holes near the original site but the damn critters simply branched out to other locations with less deterrent scent.  In order to end gopher destruction, these varmints need to be eradicated, not just deterred.
summary: Did annoy the gophers to dig more holes elsewhere.

reviewText: It’s really a year in which the critters are running rampant.  I can actually see them skittering into a hole in my foundation.  Of course I’m not particularly happy with this, but am determined to defeat them this year.  I’m not quite sure what’s happening, but another family member just mentioned she is having similar problems.I certainly have the holes to prove I’ve got them, but the problem isn’t quite as severe as it has been in the past.  I’ve made my own homemade concoction, which is somewhat similar to this one.  The natural granular method seems easier to deal with that my Mason jar recipe, but will they quit putting holes in my lawn?  Perhaps the only way I’ll know that is throughout the summer when I’m mowing it.The formula is very heavy on the castor oil (I like this), so don’t know how well it will work.  I’m doing a combination of treatments this year, all somewhat similar.  I don’t really wish these little varmints to head for my neighbor’s houses, but hopefully they’ll head into an area where they won’t inconvenience people.ACTIVE INGREDIENTS:Castor Oil:  9.9%Lecithin:  1%Fuller’s Earth:  100%
summary: Very convenient way to try to rid my lawn of those pesky moles ...

reviewText: After I received this I noticed that the manufacturer has discontinued producing it and it makes me wonder why. I am far from being an expert on these matters but in my personal experience a product is usually discontinued because it doesn't sell or it is flawed. So, I really did not expect much when I spread this on my yard to combat the one gopher and the more than one mole.I got exactly what I expected - not much. In fact, I got nothing except possibly ridicule from my unwelcome yard guests. I can see why it was discontinued. I gave it three stars because other reviews said it worked for them. I am trying to be fair because although it did not work for me does not necessarily mean it does not work for everyone, as the reviews indicated.

Tomcat Mole & Gopher Repellent is an all-natural organic formula that repels by taste and odor moles, gophers, voles, armadillos, and other burrowing nuisance animals unless they are starving or otherwise out of normal control, e.g. rabid.  This is not an industrial repellent working against anything that walks, but rather for the suburban home and garden use.  Its castor oil active ingredient is not offensive to all people and thus applicable not only in gardens, lawns, and landscaped areas, but also some basements, cellars, and storage.  However, it is ineffective against very determined animals.
summary: Ineffective only against starving or rabid animals

reviewText: The repellant does not smell, which I love, and consists of dry granules with castor oil. The package recommends to use spreader on setting 4, which I did. But then you need to water for 20 minutes, which is a great bother, if you ask me. You are supposed to treat the most infested area first, then the next time, bigger area, and do it 4 times. I didn't notice new holes in the ground since the application, I wonder if it will last long.
summary: needs 20 minutes of watering to apply

reviewText: I read that this product has been discontinued by the manufacturer. That is really unfortunate because it seems to be fairly effective. I used it on entrances around a garden and then set the sprinklers. I have noticed significantly less activity. I have also tried a killing product and this actually got me better results.

The problem with these products is that you can't ever really be sure it is working. We used it according to the directions and have not seen any new tracks on the ground. We assume that it is working but it is hard to tell for sure! As of today we haven't seen new activity since we laid the repellent down, 3 weeks ago. I will continue to use this as long as we don't have new tracks, because I assume it is doing what it is supposed to do!It does not work on pesky chipmunks, we still have those running around wild.

I got this to help get rid of the moles that have started to invade my yard.  It is very easy to use.  This is a repellant and it does seem to be working .  This just repels the moles and makes them move to another area.  So you will have to continually keep applying to keep the moles from coming back.  I would rather kill them and know they are not going to come back instead of herding them to another area for a time and then just waiting for them to eventually come back.

We've had occasional issues with gophers in the past, and use castor-based repellents annually as a result. Since we started doing so, we haven't had any gophers burrowing in our yard, though they're still in the area, as witnessed by the mounds in the yards of some of our neighbors. While getting them out of the yard in the first place takes a bit more work, castor-based products has proven effective in our experience when it comes to preventing repeat invasions.This particular repellent is similar to others on the market, but seems to be a finer grain and, as a result, dissolves more easily in water than others I've used. Thus, less water is necessary in its application.

I don't have gophers here in the backwoods, but have tons of moles.  We used this, using a spreader, around the perimeter of our garden this year.  So far, no mole tunnels, so I would have to assume it works.Of course, now that the heavy rains have started - the scent of the repellent may wash away and the product reapplied.  Only time will tell.  But for the first time in years, we don't have moles running beneath our asparagus bed - and that's a good thing.

I had never dealt with moles before but a building reconstruction a few doors down from me, got a pack of the pests to move to my yard and it was horrifying.After closely following the instructions, my life has improved greatly, no more burrows!I plan on keeping a bag of this wonderful stuff around in case more of these pests decide to visit me again.
Would not use and will not repurchase.  Inhumane product, promotes lengthy death.

I'm going to preface this review with a little disclaimer first.  What works for the particular moles in my yard, may be more or less effective with those found in your particular area.  Anytime you're trying to repel wildlife (at least with a modicum of responsibility and safety), you're going to have to resign yourself to imprecise results.With that out of the way, Tomcat 34784 appears to have done the job for me.  You have to apply it over a 3 or 4 day period, basically herding (if that word can be used) the moles off to somewhere else, i.e. not your yard.  I've tried both the liquid and the granular, with no visible difference in effectiveness.  Choose whichever method appeals to you.
I'd rather chase the varmints away than kill them, but this isn't the product that works, not for me anyway.  I guess that's why it's been discontinued.
summary: Sorry, this just doesn't do anything for me

reviewText: There has been relatively significant traffic of moles under the soil in my yard. I have tried a wide variety of repellants, traps, and poisons for moles, but not all of them have worked, but this one did not work well. I spread them over the mounds where moles were most active, but still this product was ineffective in decreasing the mole activity.

These granules work fine. They are like fertilizer and they spread easy. It says you can use a spreader or hand and I just usedmy hand.  We tried a spray version and I think I like the granules better as it's easier to see how much we are using.  The big test is, though, is if this makes the gophers go away.  So far, we haven't seen any more activity.  Fingers crossed!  These little creatures can destroy a yard.
summary: Tomcat Mole and Gopher Repellent, 4-Pound granules

reviewText: Applied as directed, it was easy to apply,  but unfortunately haven't seen much difference in gopher activity. They are persistent!I was hoping this would work. Also, this seems to have been discontinued by the manufacturer...
This repellent doesn't seem to work at all. We'd recommend using spikes instead because this product did nothing to keep them out of our yard.
summary: Didn't work. I'd recommend you use spikes instead

reviewText: I was sent another mole product and I hoped this one might work better.I used it as instructed and spread it around my first yard where there are two to four active moles tunnels running paying particular attention to the areas nearest my flowerbeds that I spent thousands of dollars to build over the years.  The moles have been venturing into the flowerbeds and causing damage so I was hoping to prevent them from coming into them in the first place.I applied this product once but it rained less than 24 hours after that.  So when the mole activity seemed more intense a few days later I reapplied it this time only around the flowerbeds in a more concentrated form.The activity seems to be less but I can't be sure this product is the reason.  If it is, it might be because of the increased concentration I used but that wasn't as directed and it should have have required as much to work if the product performed as promised.

reviewerName: Valerie J. Wood "Author and Sports Journalist"
reviewText: We've had a mole problem the past few years. My husband put this down, as the instructions said, and so far we've not seen any of the little varmints' paths. It's still early, but so far, so good.

This product does not treat a very big area, not even an average size lawn. If you use it as directed you would have to buy several bags of the repellent.Since it also stated it repeals voles I wanted to try it and spread it around the areas where I have beds of hostas which I am trying to keep the voles from dining on. I have to admit after spreading it for 3 or 4 applications I have seen the burrowing staying away from those areas. However with my yard size (70'x150') it would be extremely costly to keep this applied in the amount the directions call for.I have had just as effective results with other products that are applied directly to the tunnels.

reviewerName: Y. R. Wu "The will to win is nothing without ...
reviewText: We've tried other castor oil based repellents, and it's not clear how well they have worked.  The theory is that the taste / smell of the oil repels the mole.  After application, I still see about the same level of activity as before, but it's hard to say whether the level of activity wouldn't have gotten worse without the application.

I like that this product is a mole and gopher repellent as supposed to a trapping mechanism I reviewed a while back on here (Sweeney's 9015 Deadset Precision Mole Trap).The administration of this is easy --  the concentrate conveniently attaches to your garden hose and lasts up to 3 months.To prevent the bald spots created by the holes and mounds that moles and gophers dig, spray this repellent on up to 10,000 feet of your yard.The manufacturer claims that the ingredients in this formulation won't harm the animals; this repellent works by creating an undesirable environment for moles, voles, and gophers, and will force them to go elsewhere. It safely and effectively saturates their food sources and surrounding areas, making it taste and smell unpleasant, consequently forcing them to relocate from your yard.I have not seen any moles or mole mounds since using this product. I have seen no negative effects to the grass on the yard either.
summary: works great thus far and supposedly doesn't harm the creatures

reviewText: My problem is with squirrels and gophers. The strategy with this product is to soak the ground with an unpleasant taste in an effort to repel tunneling pests. In terms of gophers, so far, it seems to have worked. I had a problem with gophers tunneling under my sidewalk then pushing the dirt out in to my flowerbed. The sidewalk section is covered with pavers, so there were enough cracks for this spray to penetrate. I thoroughly soaked the entire sidewalk area and I have not seen any gopher holes since. I hope it works.Squirrels are another issue. Their tunnels tend to go deeper into the ground, so the castor oil in this product doesn't affect much of what they do. But, from my understanding, what you try to accomplish is you spray the whole area around where they search for food and you hope they go away because the food is unpleasant. In addition to spraying, I soaked nuts and sunflower seeds in some of the solution right out of the bottle and spread them over a wide area. I can't say this method has worked as well. The squirrels are still there, but there seems to be fewer and they have at least moved their ground entrances, so I know something is bugging them.At any rate, I think you need to use everything in your arsenal to get rid of pests and this product would certainly be worth a try.

I have both the liquid and solid versions of this repellent.  I am using both for different areas of my yard. The solid one is being use in the ground entrance which is a tunnel type opening for the gopher that has been treating my vegetable garden like its own all-you-can-eat salad buffet.  This liquid version is being used for its second entrance to my yard in the hole it dug for itself in my stone wall.  The wall is really old and is made of field stones over the past 100 years or more and so it's hard to put repellent in the nooks and crannies. The gopher has already destroyed part of this wall when it moved its original 2nd entrance a few feet.  By being able to spray a larger area, I am hoping to prevent it from moving the exit/entrance to its den along my stone wall and in the process destroying the wall itself.So far, for the past 3 weeks, I have not seen any sign of activity along that wall.I will report back if anything changes for better or for worse.  I had previously used cayenne pepper which worked well for the plants themselves but was however tricky to apply to the stone wall.

We have a big garden and keeping moles away can be a big problem. Unfortunately we've also had a very rainy spring here in New England and that cuts back on how effective this stuff is as the rain washes this away. But so far over the last week it seems to be helping keep our plants safe.I am concerned that it's been discontinued by the manufacturer I hope it doesn't kill my lawn. I am a little bit concerned as I'm not sure why it was discontinued. Time will tell if my lawn and garden dies I'm good to be a little bit upset.Thanks for reading!
summary: Seems to be working at the moment...

reviewText: I think the spike trap method works a lot better than this one. I don't like hurting moles though since they are good for the environment if not our lawns and gardens.  No positive effects noted.

Tomcat Mole & Gopher Repellent is a spray application that is to be used with your garden hose. The active ingredient is castor oil. Castor oil mixes with water to penetrate the soil. You can use it immediately after seeing the presence of moles or as a preventative treatment.The application is easy to use but I'm not sure that this is the most effective way to deal with moles in the yard. It is just a repellent so it's used to repel moles not to kill them or eliminate them. I think it depends on what type of solution you are looking for. For me, if you repel them, they are just going to move to a new spot in the yard.The bottle will cover an area of 100' x 100' area. It also is necessary to apply again if heavy rainfall falls right after application. It may be necessary to purchase quite a bit of product depending on the size of the area that you are having the mole trouble. I think it an expensive iffy solution from a product that has been discontinued by the manufacturer.

I cleared some drybrush and trees from the slope behind my backyard for fire prevention.
