The gophers that were digging countless holes in the hard dirt of the slope decided to relocate to my backyard lawn.  It is "ON", varmints!  I've tried gopher repellents, gas bombs, traps, solar spike deterrents, and baits, with varying results.  Why not give this Tomcat Mole and Gopher Repellent a try?Likes:*Easy to apply using a garden hose connected to the bottle/applicator.*Claimed by manufacturer to treat 10,000 sq. ft.Results:*I followed the instructions precisely and sprayed the entire 45x45ft.  backyard lawn with plenty of the deterrent liquid left over.  For the first two weeks, the gopher activity seemed to have ceased.*During the third week, gopher dug new smaller holes in other locations that branched out from the original gopher mound.Overall:Did deter the gophers for two weeks from digging holes near the original site but the damn critters simply branched out to other locations with less deterrent scent.  In order to end gopher destruction, these varmints need to be dead, not just deterred.  The battle continues.
summary: Only "repelled" the gophers to dig more holes elsewhere.

reviewText: It's really a year in which the critters are running rampant.  I can actually see them skittering into a hole in my foundation.  Of course I'm not too happy with this, but am determined to defeat them this year.  I'm not quite sure what's happening, but another family member just mentioned she is having similar problems.I certainly have the holes to prove I've got them, but the problem isn't quite as severe as it has been in the past.  I've made my own homemade concoction, which is somewhat similar to this one.  The bottle is actually easier to deal with that my Mason jar recipe, but will they quit putting holes in my lawn?  Perhaps the only way I'll know that is throughout the summer when I'm mowing it.The formula is very heavy on the castor oil, so don't know how well it will work.  I'm doing a combination of treatments this year, all somewhat similar.  I don't really wish these little varmints to head for my neighbor's houses, but hopefully they'll head into an area where they won't inconvenience people.ACTIVE INGREDIENTS:Castor Oil:  99%Lecithin:  1%
summary: Very convenient way to try to rid my lawn of those pesky moles ...

reviewText: One side of my house is a favorite gathering place for burrowing animals. I hooked up this smelly gunk to a hose and every day I sprayed the entire area of the house where the holes are located until the container was empty. The result? More holes. It is easy to understand why the manufacturer discontinued this product. The only thing it provides is a stinky odor. The forecast is for thunderstorms which will take care of the odor. Win some, lose some. This one is a loser.

Tomcat Mole & Gopher Repellent is an all-natural organic formula that repels by taste and odor moles, gophers, voles, armadillos, and other burrowing nuisance animals unless they are starving or otherwise out of normal control, e.g. rabid.  This is not an industrial repellent working against anything that walks, but rather for the suburban home and garden use.  Its garlic, putrescent egg, and capsaicin are not offensive to all people and thus applicable not only in gardens, lawns, and landscaped areas, but also some basements, cellars, and storage.  However, it is ineffective against very determined animals.
summary: Ineffective only against starving or rabid animals

reviewText: This is a spray that you hook up to your hose and then apply to your lawn.  It doesn't kill the moles just is a repellant.  It basically tries to get them to go to someone elses yard.  It did work a little but you would have to keep applying and I am not sure how long one application will last before they start coming back.  Would definetly get something that kills them and keeps them from coming back.

I had the chance to try this out and I can't rate the product itself much, all I can rate is the bottle sprayer part because that failed me. I hooked up my garden hose to the bottle as directed and tried using it and it didn't spray as you would have thought. Upon closer inspection it looks like the nozzle part actually has a crack in it which pretty much rendered this useless. I don't know if it came from the company damaged or was damaged in shipping but in my case this was not useful at all due to poor/cheap design of the sprayer which failed.
summary: Sprayer designed cheap, small crack = worthless.

reviewText: Did not work.  We have a groundhog that lives under our deck.  He is very active and comes in and out through a hole in a corner of the desk.  He has a back door hole another 100 feet away.  I followed the instructions and provided a heavy application, especially around (and in) the two holes.  12 hours later, the groundhog was happily going in and out of the same two holes.  I actually hooked this up to the hose while he was out sunning himself on the lawn.  I sprayed him directly.  He didn't seem to care and went back to chomping the grass in the same spot I sprayed.At the end of my application, there was still a bit of product left in the bottle.  So, I dumped it fully concentrated down the hole.  No effect whatsoever.The listing says it was discontinued.  I'm not sure sure why, specifically.  But this does not work on my groundhog.

I got this more for spraying around the wire compost bins to keep the armadillos out.  And so far it is working fine.  Also haven't seen any mole tunnels in the area, so I'm assuming (with the proliferation of those we've had this year) that it is working to repel them also.Very easy to use, simply hook the bottle up to your garden hose and spray the desired area until wet.Would probably buy this again, if available.
Would not repurchase.  Toxic.

I'm going to preface this review with a little disclaimer first.  What works for the particular moles in my yard, may be more or less effective with those found in your particular area.  Anytime you're trying to repel wildlife (at least with a modicum of responsibility and safety), you're going to have to resign yourself to imprecise results.With that out of the way, Tomcat 34532 appears to have done the job for me.  You have to apply it over a 3 or 4 day period, basically herding (if that word can be used) the moles off to somewhere else, i.e. not your yard.  I've tried both the liquid and the granular, with no visible difference in effectiveness.  Choose whichever method appeals to you.

We have always had trouble with moles in our backyard. This stuff is easy to use.  You simply attach it to your hose and spray away.  We sprayed the key places we had trouble with last year and so far the moles have not come back, so I guess that means it's working.  It does have a little bit of an odor as you're spraying it, but once it dries, the smell goes away completely. Overall, I'm please with the ease of use, and it's working.
I had hopes for it, being the type of guy that would rather chase the critters away than kill them.  But after several tries, I had no success.
summary: Sorry, it doesn't have any effect for me

reviewText: This was one of the only things that I've found that actually seems to really work as far as moles and voles.  I used it just as instructed and within 2 days I noticed less mole activity in my yard.  I'll continue to use and hopefully will eventually eliminate the problem altogether.

There has been relatively significant traffic of moles under the soil in my yard. I have tried a wide variety of repellants, traps, and poisons for moles, but not all of them have worked, but this one did not work well. I am not sure if the product was too diluted or it simply did not work. If this product is good, then why is it that the manufacturer discontinued this product?

I have little confidence when it comes to controlling the varmints (moles) that burrow under my lawn and gardens. I shoot them when I can, trap them when I get lucky and use chemicals when failing at the first two. I applied this to an area that was infested shortly after the snow disappeared. Its been four days and all evidence of activity are gone. This is good news, because TNT was being considered. It claims a couple retreatments will be required, as the little rats will likely return, but I'll gladly comply. I'd rather kill them all, but I don't want to risk harming my local bird population so I need to take special care. For now, I'm pleased with the results.

This spray version hooks up easy to the garden hose and it sprays out fine.  I think it is hard to figure out how much of the spray is coming out at a time so I think I would probably prefer the granules. We tested out the spray and the granules on different areas of the lawn and so far they both seem to work well.  No more mounds of dirt on our lawn.  And no more dangerous holes where my little nieces feet can fall into.
summary: Tomcat Mole and Gopher Liquid Repellent, 32-Ounce

reviewText: Using this has been a challenge given the time constraints of the Vine Program I received it through -- it has been a very rainy month but I did manage to use it once.  After I've used it again I'll come back and update this review IF the results are different but I'm not hopeful.I followed the directions on the product and sprayed this over the first two flowerbeds that have been wrecked by mole tunnels.  Three days later there are new even larger tunnels in the beds as though this spray attracted them!The only positive is that this did not damage the plants and flowers in any way, they look as good as ever, and the number of butterflies and bees seems steady.

reviewerName: Y. R. Wu "The will to win is nothing without ...
reviewText: This product is 99% Castor oil and 1% lecithin - I am guessing the lecithin is an emulsifier so the castor oil can be sprayed.  Very easy to apply - just hook up a hose and spray on grass and ground.  I've put up a perimeter of perhaps 10-15 feet at the boundaries of my yard to discourage any moles from migrating into our yard.
summary: Easier application than castor oil granules

reviewText: I have previously had such bad experiences with outdoor umbrellas I had pretty much given up on having one. I am very glad I was given the chance to try this one.It is very SMOOTH. The handle and opening and closing mechanism is very smooth. Nothing like my previous umbrellas. It is a pleasure to open and close it. It makes using it so easy and pleasurable. You have the choice to use it vertically or at an angle.It is a pleasing neutral color that will go with any existing patio furniture. Highly recommended.
summary: Great product that is a good value; incredibly smooth and well-made

reviewText: I have purchased a couple dozen large yard umbrellas.  We have them placed in the center of home-made picnic tables and bar tables, in stands around the kid's sand boxes and around the pool, and to cover the oyster table if it's raining.  It gets really hot in Georgia and we stay outside a lot.I buy my umbrellas from all over the place - whomever has them on sale.  None of them were full price when I bought them.The only ones that have broken so far were the most expensive ones that got damage when they blew over in the wind.  The cheaper ones seem to be the most resilient.  None of them have had to be replaced due to sun damage or just being in the elements.I tell you all that so you won't be deterred by the low price.  This umbrella is well designed and very attractive.  It looks similar to ones I have purchased that retailed for $200.  Only higher priced umbrellas have the hand crank and tilt feature.I'll buy a stand for it and put this one over the sandboxes at my daughter's house where the tilt will be particularly useful for adjusting for the movement of the sun.

you will not go wrong with this combination . the base was 4 " to tall to go under my table but after cutting it off if fit perfectly and they look great . we liked so much we are going to order another of the same combination next week. well we ordered another one and received it these are fantastic-look great-open smoothly-before summer gets here we will have four of them on our deck by house and the deck at the pool. don't hesitate this is a super fantastic great buy. thanks amazon for such great products!
summary: great buy! both strathwood rhodes market umbrella and we bought the strathwood rhodes cast iron umbrella base they look great!

reviewText: Like everyone else has found out I'm sure, outdoor umbrellas seemingly are not what they use to be. Finding one that can endure the harshness of the sun's rays or those unexpected high winds is half the journey. Getting a quality umbrella that can mechanically hold up to the task is even harder. Like many other outdoor enthusiasts, I jumped at the opportunity to test drive the Strathwood Umbrella. After six weeks use, these are my thoughts.Upon arrival, I completed a quick inventory and read over the instructions. With all parts accounted for, in fifteen minutes the umbrella was up and mounted. Weighing in at a little over 14 pounds its a little heavier then the one I picked up at the big box tool store. This model measures 100" height and 9 feet when fully expanded. The polyester fabric seems better then most and is mold and rain resistant. The manufacturer did an above average job on the stitching. The umbrella mounted easily into our iron stand without any adjustment.The light weight aluminum is coated with a black finish. The frame looks formidable and ready to withstand Mother Nature's test. For me personally, I like the heavier gauge aluminum on this umbrella. The jury is out on the ribbing support. The tilting feature is a nice add on but not something I see myself using all the time. The crank assembly is fluid and hasn't stalled or locked up. Being that is the usual problem with other brands, I'll see if this one holds up. By the end of summer I'm sure I'll have my answer and will gladly update this review if it doesn't.Overall I like this umbrella. Its come in quite handy down here on the coast.  Now at the six week mark,  this umbrella has held its own against the elements both fully masted and tethered.  For Amazon's current under $80 price listing, its quite a bargain. I'm sure others will agree.UPDATE: June 5, 2014Its still functional and with the exception of a little fabric fading, it has held up well against the elements.

A patio umbrella is a blessing in the summertime when sitting outside at a table, enjoying the day. It provides shelter from the direct sun and can add a style element as well which is an added bonus. Not all patio umbrellas are worth their price, though, and as far as they go I think this one is a little better than most others I have used.First things first - this umbrella does not come with a stand. Without a stand, keeping it steady (or even having it stay up at all) is going to be difficult. If you are purchasing this umbrella remember to buy a stand too if you do not already have one. Stands are not especially expensive, but I would have liked to have seen a stand in the package with the umbrella, even if it would not fit my table. As one other reviewed observed, having a table with a hole in the middle will work but keeping the umbrella steady will be difficult. You really should have a stand.Setting up the umbrella (once you have a stand in place) is easy and does not take long. In less than half an hour I was able to have it stood up and ready to use. It probably took me longer than it could have taken just because it was a little awkward to set up alone.Operation (opening/closing, etc.) is very easy. The hand crank for raising and lowering the umbrella operates smoothly and does not require a lot of strength to use. More important than operation, though, is durability. To me, this umbrella seems a little more durable than most. It feels sturdy and strong and the fabric is a little better polyester weave than I have seen in other umbrellas. The pole and ribs are coated and should resist rust and corrosion. There should be no issue with this umbrella lasting in all sorts of weather for a long, long time.This is a nice outdoor umbrella, well made and easy to use. Other than not having a base, it's a nice addition to the outdoor table and should serve well for many years. The asking price on Amazon as I write this is $80 - a bargain.

If you read the description ("cast iron") for this umbrella base, it should come as no surprise that this puppy is solid. It's not going anywhere and it ain't gonna let your umbrella go anywhere either. Super easy to set this stand up...I thought at first there was a mistake and I didn't get all the parts and pieces because there were so few. It went together easy, I dropped in our umbrella, used the two screws to tighten it up and was all set. I like that there are multiple screws to anchor the umbrella because we live in a windy place and the previous base we used struggled to keep the umbrella stable in our windy conditions.My one issue with the base is how tall it is. It's big and just _barely_ fit under the umbrella support under our table. We did get it to work, but just be aware that it's tall if you're using a table with some low level supports.

would not fit under table that we bought it for but that was no problem. cut 4 inches off and it fit perfectly and looks wonderful. liked the combination for this base and that umbrella and looked and worked so well we are going to order another one nest week! buy them you will love them! well a week later and we ordered another one-looks great-what a great purchase from amazon. put another feather in my cap, my wire thinks i am smart for ordering from amazon. we liked so much before summer gets here we will have 4 on deck by house and on the swimming pool deck.
summary: great umbrella base orded with umbrella (strathwood rhodes market umbrells with black post and beige covering. perfect!

reviewText: There are tons of various brands that try to sell their various outdoor products - it's difficult to figure out which ones are reasonably priced for high quality, just high priced, or low quality.  Last year, I took the dive with Strathwood (first I had heard of them) with a beautifulStrathwood Basics All-Weather Hardwood 3-Seater Bench.  It's an awesome little bench, especially for the price.So sticking with the same brand seemed like a smart thing to do...and it was.  This umbrella base is just as great as their other products.  Very easy assembly:  two bolts on the bottom, and then, depending on the girth of the pole you put in the base, 2 tightening screws that hold the umbrella in place firmly.  And then you have a piece of outdoor yard equipment that will never need replacing.  This this is a heavy base that I wouldn't hesitate to put larger umbrella in, and with the little feet on the bottom, putting in on gravel (rather than a pristine deck, for example) is no problem, either.  And the powder coat finish means it's not going to start rusting after the first drizzle.Recommended...likely complements Strathwoods own outdoor furniture (which I don't have), but it looks great with existing tables and chairs, too.
summary: Very sturdy - won't need to replace it...ever.

reviewText: This base is VERY sturdy, and heavy (about 30#).  Once you place it somewhere, you will not want to move it very often.  It's very durable and functional, but I can't really say that it's "pretty".  The pictures show this base being used with a table, but in my opinion, if you have a table then you probably would use a different base that's a lot less expensive than this one that doesn't have to be as sturdy as this one.  This base is more suited for a stand-alone base for an umbrella.  I like the fact that it's large. . . square and flat.  This makes it easy to place something on top of it.  The large size makes it less likely to tip-over due to wind.

Update May 27, 2013: After being used on my deck for 2 months, I noticed it's starting to rust where the pole-holder piece meets the base. I think water is possibly getting down the tube and there is no exit for the water. I can't remember if I saw exit holes for water when I assembled it. Downgraded to 3 stars.************************************************Update May 1, 2013: We've had some severe storms recently; in the past I'd always run outside to remove the umbrella to a safe place. The cast iron base is so substantial I don't bother now. I keep the umbrella closed and tied shut, and so far it's been OK to leave it this way, even during a bad storm with high wind.************************************************You have to assemble the pole-holder to the base with two bolts/washers/locknuts that are included. No tools are included; you supply your own 9/16" wrench. It was difficult doing this alone, so make it easier on yourself and find someone to hold the base for you while you attach the pole-holder.There are 1-1/4" high legs with anti-skid rubber bottoms on each corner, so this won't be sitting in a water puddle on your patio or deck. My umbrella pole is 1-1/4" in diameter, there's plenty of wiggle room, so the two knobs are great to screw in to keep the umbrella more stable. This is heavy enough it won't be going anywhere.Note: There's a rubber insert that fits inside the tube; not sure it serves any purpose other than possibly keeping the rain out; but if you were to remove it, you could probably fit a pole that's 1-3/4" in diameter, but I wouldn't push it any further.

One complaint, perhaps because I received them as a Vine Voice, but they do wobble.  Both.  So I had to put about 1/2 inch thick pad on one of the legs of each chair.  I assume they send the slightly 'defective' units to Vine folks, so I won't count off for that.  I read their warranty and they will replace damaged or defective chairs free of charge and pay the return shipping.  Nice.Each chair is the lighter wicker, woven very thickly.  It matches most of the Strathwood Griffen style furniture.  There might be slight color variation though.  Each chair has a padded cushion, but you might need a pillow or cushion for your back.  I wouldn't recommend trying to match the seat cushions since the company states that the fabric can be slightly different color depending on the ream.I like the chairs, but I do recommend them as outdoor chairs rather than indoor chairs.

My wife and I absolutely love these chairs. We bought 4 of the armless chairs and 2 of the armed chairs for a total of 6 to go along with the matching dinning table. We were looking for a new outdoor dinning set for a long time before finally settling on this set. These Chairs are lightweight, durable and comfortable. We loved the contemporary design. Most wicker is "old lady" looking and doesn't fit our contemporary style, and we found flaws in most other materials like wood's high maintenance, iron's cold look, etc. But I highly reccomend these chairs for their comfort and style. They look great and we have gotten many compliments thus far. Delivery was also quick and painless, arriving via Fedex. I also bought the matching sofa and coffee table to create an entire outdoor living area.

The chairs are a nice size, although I do not think they would hold much weight!Behind the woven vinyl covered legs are metal bars. The medal bars are hollow, and the front legs on both my chairs come in Bent.One front leg just broke off so I can see there hollow. One chair, the leg is still there although bent. It is too hard to move back , and if I did , I think it would break off! I'm thinking this got hit by a forklift!!!I took a chance, and sat on it very easy to just get the feel if the chairs would be comfortable. (I'm not heavy).Yes, the chair is deep, and comfortable. I didn't sit long, as I was afraid the chair would fall forward.The Cushions are 2 inches thick, and felt like they where bottoming out, so to speak. Although they fit nice on the seats ,and look good.I have the outdoor sofa to match these chairs.The sofa has held up good, although for the winter we put it in the garage. The cushions on the sofa are much thicker then the chairs are.The vinyl faux wicker has also held up well.

A gorgeous set! These chairs are currently inside the house and look great. I have gotten a lot of complements on how nice they look and feel. There are a few things to note about the construction of these chairs. There are no supports under the seat area that the cushion sits on, it is only the woven wicker material. While it supported me just fine, I took the cushion off and it seemed as though if you stepped on it your foot might go through the bottom. They feel really sturdy to sit in, but I am unsure what the weight limitations might be. I had a bit of a wobble on one of the chairs, but it didn't actually wobble when anyone sits in it, only when it is empty does it wobble. The arm rests are really nice and the back is quite comfortable. I sat in one reading for over an hour without any discomfort. When the snow melts these will be on the back deck as part of the dining set. The cushions are easy to clean, we already had some chocolate milk spilled on one and it wiped up easily without leaving a stain. They are thin enough that they will dry out quickly, but thick enough for long term comfort. Overall I highly recommend this set of chairs. I think they are great and they seem durable enough to last for many years. Feel free to ask questions about them and I will answer as quickly as possible!

reviewerName: Modern Blue Argonaut "No I do not have a shoe...
reviewText: I already have several Strathwood pieces so I was excited to add these for additional outdoor seating. The chairs come (2)to a very large but lightweight box. The box is easy to open and there was adequate yet minimal packaging, so they were easy to get out of the box, remove packaging, and set up within ten minutes. I have the matching sofa and even after almost a year the sofa cushions still look new despite sitting outside (covered area). I have placed a small table in between these chairs and find them to be more comfortable than the sofa. Previously I had (2) white rockers that I battled mildew with. This plastic wicker is mildew resistant and washes so easily when needed. I highly recommend these!

QUICK SUMMARY:  I like these chairs!  They are a beautiful, rich brown color and they're quite comfortable even for my 6' 2" frame.  Recommended!WHAT I LIKE:- The color is rich, dark brown.  I have a similarly-constructed table, but it's more of a weathered gray color, and I much prefer the vibrant color of these chairs- The seat cushions are complementary and comfortable, and easy to remove if you don't want them rained on- The seats are comfortable, with a slight recline so you sit upright, but not uncomfortably so- Although they're not intended to be used with our outdoor dining table, they can very comfortably be used for that- The wicker is very smooth and feels good to the touch.  I prefer it over the rougher style of wicker.- Nothing creaks when I plop my nearly 200lbs frame onto themSomething to take note:  I'm 6' 2" tall.  As such, the chairs are a little small for me; they don't offer much under-thigh leg support.  My mother-in-law, however, who is 5' 2", is almost too short for these chairs; her legs almost dangle and barely touch the ground while she sits in them.  All that said, these chairs are constructed for an average-height person.  If you're especially tall or especially short, the chair might not be ideal for you.CONCLUSION:  These are a great addition to our backyard patio!  Recommended!
summary: Beautiful chair looks great, feels good

reviewText: I must admit at the outset of this review that these chairs have not gone outside due to the weather and our lack of a nice outdoor location to place them. So, I do not know how well they truly withstand the weather or clean up for use.In an indoor setting, however, they are definitely comfortable and clean easily. Both the wicker and the cushion seem to repel stains, especially when quickly wiped.As for the construction of the chairs, they are deep, which makes them a little difficult for me, short as I am at 5'2", to sit comfortably in them at any sort of table. But, if I am not worried about being pulled up to a table, they are very comfortable. The chairs are lightweight and easily managed, yet they also seem very sturdy and of good quality. Because of their lightweight nature, however, I would not place them in an outdoor location that received regular winds. These chairs would easily be blown about or toppled.We are enjoying these chairs as an addition to our living/dining room arrangement, and I am sure that I would enjoy them just as much on a patio.
great around the dining table After shopping and considering many options I found this furniture to be very good value for the money, light but strong, happy with purchase

Since it's still cold here in Iowa, we've been using these chairs indoors. :) I've always bought chairs with arms, but I have to admit, I like these! They have ample seating area.Right out of the box, all we had to do was unwrap and slip the cushion strap over the back. I have doubts that this "strap" will hold up long-tern, but even without the strap, the cushion can be used on the chair. The cushion isn't anything substantial, but does provide some softness for your bottom. The cushions can be removed for cleaning, so that's nice.I liked how lightweight and easy to move these chairs were.Both my SO and I sat in these chairs. We're very different weight-wise and we both found the chairs to be comfortable.I do like that these are plastic (resin) wicker, or as I like to call it, "plicker". I have other chairs made with this material and it's easy to care for, clean and always looks nice. They are comfortable to sit on, too, as the plastic won't burn your thighs like metal chairs can. These new chairs will compliment my old ones easily. Being a brown color, they'll go with everything I already have on my patio. I don't need everything to match, but most people like matching stuff, so these will compliment any decor nicely.

My wife and I absolutely love these chairs. We bought 4 of these armless chairs and 2 of the armed chairs for a total of 6 to go along with the matching dinning table. We were looking for a new outdoor dinning set for a long time before finally settling on thise set. These Chairs are lightweight, durable and comfortable. We loved the contemporary design. Most wicker is "old lady" looking and doesn't fit our contemporary style, and we found flaws in most other materials like wood's high maintenance, iron's cold look, etc. But I highly reccomend these chairs for their comfort and style. They look great and we have gotten many complements thus far. Delivery was also quick and painless, arriving via Fedex. I also bought the matching sofa and coffee table to create an entire outdoor living area.
They are perfedt.

Strathwood - a product by Amazon.comApproximate measurements:Cushion: 20 1/2" x 20 1/2" x 2" thick.Chair without the cushion: floor to seat - 17"; floor to top of chair -  36" which raises to 37" at the highest point of its curved back.*****Thoughts:~The chairs are very roomy. My husband finds them very comfortable. I'm short, if I sit all the way back,  they're not as comfortable for me.~The back of the chair is not straight up & down, but is angled back with a gentle  curve that adds character as well as comfort.~The chairs are lightweight & easy to move.~I wish the cushion's matching elastic band, which secures it to the seat, was the same color as the chair. Because the chair is dark brown & the cushion is beige, the elastic band shows up quite a bit when the chair is viewed from the back. Check  Amazon's product images to see a photo of what I'm describing.~The elastic band is easy to slip over the back of the chair & securely fastens the cushion to the chair.~The cushions have zippers & piping. The covers can be removed for thorough cleaning.~I plan on protecting the cushions with a fabric spray such as3M Scotchgard Fabric Protector.~These chairs can be used alone, or with a dining table/Strathwood Griffen table or even with the Strathwood Griffen Ottoman.*****I called customer service to inquire about the weight limit for Amazon's Strathwood Griffen Outdoor Furniture Collection. I think it would be a good idea to have that information, so I submitted a suggestion.These chairs are lightweight & have a sturdy aluminum frame. The chair seat is supported by  resin wicker under seat webbing. Check customer images to see the photo I uploaded  of the underside of the chair.No assmebly was required.Amazon's product description covers cushion care & cleaning so I won't go into that. You may return this item sold by Amazon.com within 30 days of delivery for a full refund. Amazon.com will pay the return shipping cost if the return is a result of their error. Amazon is unable to exchange items.A note concerning all-weather, resin wicker: It is meant to look like natural wicker, but is made of a synthetic material that requires little maintenance. It is durable, strong, resistant to humidity, water & UV radiation, & somewhat elastic. It's easy to clean & can be hosed down (remove the cushion first). The color is part of the fiber & shouldn't fade.

I was surprised at just how big these chairs were! They are a tad deeper in the seat than our current set of deck chairs. But, these are surprisingly comfortable! They are very well suited for lounging back and chatting. They are tall, but not at all tippy thanks to a wide base. They appear to be very well made and exceptionally sturdy. They are lightweight enough to move around easily. And, they are stylish enough that we'll happily use them indoors when the need for additional seating arrises. Much better looking than folding chairs!! The seat cushions remove easily yet stay in place well, no slipping around. I was very happy to find that these chairs, unlike our other deck chairs, are quite comfortable even without the cushions on them!So, check the dimensions of these to make sure they fit what you're looking for, if they do, I'd buy with confidence!

I  like these chairs a lot.  I got them because they will be perfect for my unheated summer porch. Since it is the middle of winter I have been using them in my house as extra chairs at my dining room table. They look and feel great.While I am not much into interior decorating I am amazed that wicker chairs would actually look good inside my house.  The dark brown color come close to matching the color of my dining room table. The simple look of a wicker chair with a cushion works well.The chairs feel strong. I have had 250 pound friends sitting in the chairs and the chairs held steady.  When I sit in them I don't notice any difference from regular chairs and these are stronger than the old dining room table chairs that I am currently using.When I lean back the wicker gives a little so I my back feels comfortable rather than feeling like I am leaning back on a hard surface like you would get from a wood chair.  The wicker should work well in the heat because air can circulate better through woven wicker than cloth or wood.The seat cushions are comfortable.  I feel like I am sitting on a soft surface rather than a hard chair.The chairs are relatively light and easy to move.The bottom of the chairs seem to be made of a wood like material. It will not damage my wood floors at all.Since I am in New Jersey I have not used these chairs outside so I can't comment on how easy it is to clean them. I plan to use them in an enclosed screened in unheated porch which can get over 100 degrees in the summer. I also plan to use them when I have parties in my back yard. I will have more of a chance to test how they hold up to changes in temperature and the dirt than can accumulate from summer parties when that happens.I really like these chairs.

The chairs are attractive, sit well, and easy to move as they are very lightweight.  The seat area is very generous in size and the cushion is comfy.  One thing about the cushion that I really like is that it has an loop that can be slipped over the back of the chair to hold it in place.  No string ties that easily come loose here.  Tall guests will really appreciate the height; I'm 5'7" and in flats my feet do not touch the ground in these chairs.

Arriving in a huge corrugated (and wrapped with sheet plastic) cardboard box, with the words "Team Lift" (great idea) on the outside, the table was somewhat well-protected during transit. A deep dent on the bottom of the box caused me some concern, which was allayed when I saw the Masonite squares within the box, reinforcing each corner - nothing within was damaged.The table arrived dent-free. However, while unpacking the table from the box, sheet metal screws were raining down on me. I thought that the plastic bag holding the hardware must have had a hole in it, but NO -- these were screws that were holding the resin planks to the metal bars(under the table) running perpendicular to the table. And since the planks are made of resin and the sheet metal screws are screwed directly into the planks, some screws had come loose and fallen out, some to the point of almost losing their "grip" in these resin planks. THIS will impact the longevity of this table for sure. I believe a threaded insert in the resin and then a round headed bolt with a Phillips slot-head screwed through the metal bars, and then into that threaded insert would have been much much sturdier and better in the long-term. So, Three Stars for this -- had the slats been more securely fastened, I would have initially given this table Four Stars.That being said, the table is handsome - and I am glad I have a 14 foot long balcony -- as this table is large -- wicker woven on a steel structure, surrounding faux wood planks. It is heavy -- and large enough to hold some plants as decor while still leaving plenty of room for food, be it potluck or pizza. The hole in the middle of the table -- for the umbrella -- is a great touch. The FOUR wicker-on-steel table legs (which I have yet to assemble onto the table) seem heavy enough to hold the table up, but I think SIX legs might be better than four -- more needs to be said about this, and once I attach the legs, I will be better able to judge this. I DO wonder if, when I add the patio umbrella (also sold by Strathmore Furniture), should a gust of wind twist it to and fro (despite the weighted base) would that make this Four-legged table fall over? To be determined, at a later date (mid-late Spring)......One plank seems to be longer than the other -- It is not flush with the edge of the table -- I took it apart and repositioned it to make it sit flush with all the others.I also keep a big heavy tarp nearby, to cover the table against inclement weather, as per the initial instructions. The biggest test, other than the screws' ability to retain their grip on the planks long-term, will be in the summer with its significant heat and humidity, and how THAT affects the table (warping? Mildew?).UPDATE-- Summertime!! The heat and humidity have been pretty bad for about 2 weeks. Things are better now. I have two fans on my balcony -- one of which is trained on the underside of this table. It helps. So far nothing has warped or mildewed.

clear leg room, wish it had something to close the hole up I don't need it, After shopping and considering many options I found this furniture to be very good value for the money, light but strong, happy with purchase

The table is quite substantial in size and weight. The nearly 3 feet by six feet looks even larger than I had anticipated.Functionally, it works great. The resin table top panels are spaced for rain runoff and the hole in the center of the table is for the addition of an umbrella.The table is quite eye catching. Though there are other brands that look similar, this really looks nice.Assembly was quite simple, though the feet do not want to stay embedded into the bottom of the legs. Moving the table means having to put the feet back under the legs. That is annoying and the reason for the absence of the fifth star. UPDATE: enough pounding with a rubber mallet will get the feet in so they will stay.Time will tell about how it maintains it's color and overall appearance. The resin should hold up and we're looking forward to many years of use. UPDATE: after several months in Texas sun, the table is still looking new.

My wife and I absolutely love this table. We bought 4 of the armless chairs and 2 of the armed chairs for a total of 6 to go along with this matching dinning table. We were looking for a new outdoor dinning set for a long time before finally settling on this set. The Chairs are lightweight, durable and comfortable and the table is very stable and well built. We loved the contemporary design. Most wicker is "old lady" looking and doesn't fit our contemporary style, and we found flaws in most other materials like wood's high maintenance, iron's cold look, etc. But I highly reccomend this table for its style and durability (what else so we look for in a good a patio set). They look great and we have gotten many complements thus far. Delivery was also quick and painless, arriving via Fedex. I also bought the matching sofa and coffee table to create an entire outdoor living area. Love it!!!

The table looks really nice. The color tone of the table matches regular garden background very well. The table measured 3 feet by 5.5 feet. So, you need a quite big garden umbrella to get the table fully covered.Assembly is quite easy as tool is also included in the package. So, virtually, I don't need anything from my own tool box. The resin table top panels are spaced apart to leave room for water runoff. At the bottom of each leg, there are screws to adjust the length of each leg to ensure stable standing.Somehow, two nuts for assembling the legs to the table are missing from the package. Also, 8 screws for securing the table top resin panel to the metal frame are missing also. Fortunately, the missing nuts and screws can be easily found in Home depot.I am confident that the resin top panels should last for long time. But the I am not quite sure how long the woven risen wicker around the edge of the table can last. The legs are aluminum covered with resin wicker. So, no metal rust issue to be worried.All in all, this is a stylish garden table. I take one point out due to the missing nuts and screws.

On the plus side, this is a nice looking table that is easy to assemble and feels very sturdy once put together.  The sturdiness of the table is from an interesting steel rod and bolt assembly that spans the entire length of the leg (on the inside) and tightens down with a large wrench (included).  The resin planks that form the table top are textured but not so much that they will be difficult to keep clean.  The planks are also well supported by two metal cross bars spanning across the table.  The wicker is made of some type of vinyl or plastic - much like other patio sets I have used and that have lasted well.  The overall look of the table is pleasing and gives a quality impression but would never be mistaken for anything upper end.The biggest problem with the table was related to shipping.  The table arrived in a box without reinforcement or padding of any kind.  The UPS driver stated he was surprised it was packed more for a freight delivery than for a standard shipping delivery (which gets more man handling).  The result was that the box corner was torn open and one corner of the table wicker damaged (see photos at top).  But it doesn't stop there.  Some of the table planks and been jarred loose.  The screws were partially ripped out (another photo at top).  Since these are self-tapping screws they would not retighten as snuggly as intended.  And to top it all off, a nut was missing from one on the rods in the table legs.  I ended up having to make a trip to the hardware store for a nut and some thicker self-tapping screws.  But I guess that was easier than going through the whole "contacting the manufacturer" process.
summary: Cross your fingers and hope it arrives in good shape

reviewText: Excellent

We've been looking for a patio table big enough for our family of 8 for several years.  Everything we've found is either round (we really wanted rectangle) or too expensive for a cheaply made product.This arrived earlier this week and we immediately put it together, even though the weather here is cold & blustery.  We decided to go ahead and put it out on our patio and see how it stands up to the wind/rain and snow.  This is a VERY substantial piece of furniture!  It comes in a huge box and takes two people to move it, but is very simple to put together.  The frame is aluminum, but it's still pretty heavy.I love how it looks like real wood but without all of the maintenance that comes with real wood. It says to bring it in during inclement weather which would also not be practical for us and is sort of contradictory to the "All Weather" label it has, so we're leaving it outside.  It is heavy enough to not be blown away (though this area is prone to tornadoes, in which case I WOULD bring it inside).It's about 6 feet long, plenty big enough for 6 large chairs or 8 smaller, so it's perfect for our family.  It also has a hole for an umbrella which is a deal-maker for us.  It has a very classic look and blends in nicely with our older house.  I'm looking forward to using it this spring/summer for BBQ's and relaxing with my family.  It took our 14 year old about 15 minutes to assemble, very simple.
summary: Now THIS is a piece of furniture!

reviewText: Update: I do like this chair, but I downgraded it from 5 stars to 4 stars.  The reason is doe to the depth of the seating area, which I mention further on in the review.  I think that they ought to shave off a few inches of depth.  I'm roughly 6' tall with shoes on and I can barely allow my legs to hang down with my back resting against the rear cushion.  Certainly, a shorter person can sit on the chair, but they aren't going to likely have much/any back support due to the chair's depth.Quality seems very high.  It's a good weight, not too light and not too heavy.  The seat is a bit deep, so those with shorter legs might need to scoot forward a bit.I believe it's made with simulated wicker. I flipped the chair upside down and the metal frame seems well-built.  This chair arrives in one very large box, although again it's not super heavy.  No assembly is required.  Just throw the cushion onto the base.It would also look quite nice when configured into a sectional with other matching pieces.  If you a search here on Amazon, you can see how it would look as a part of a sectional.  Unfortunately, you are talking about a lot of money once you add in all of those other sectional pieces.Only time will tell how well it holds up.  I'll try to add some remarks that address this in the future.  Preliminarily, it seems like a very nice chair for one's patio or maybe even their living room, depending on one's taste and needs.
summary: This is a very nice-looking chair

reviewText: I really like this Strathwood Griffen faux resin wicker patio furniture. It is lightweight to carry but feels very heavy duty to sit on. I am 5'10" tall and weigh 265 pounds and the chair feels solid.  I also have theStrathwood Griffen All-Weather Wicker Chair, Dark Brown. It has arms while this sectional piece doesn't but I love both pieces.  I also ordered the matching ottoman, which hasn't been delivered yet.The chair was packed very well and was delivered right to my door by FedEx. The box was cumbersome but was light enough for me to carry into my house.The seat on the chair is deep. I sit way back using the back cushion and my feet touch the floor. I think if you are a shorter person, you will need a throw pillow or some bolster behind your back to push you forward to allow your feet to touch the ground.I sprayed the cushions with3M Scotchgard Outdoor Water Shield, 10.5-Ounce. The cushion covers are made of an easily cleanable polyester fabric but I wanted to be extra sure on stain protection.  I do wish the fabric covers were a darker color so they wouldn't show dirt so easily in the future. And I do wish the furniture as made in the USA rather than China.So now I'm getting ready for summer and I hope it hurries up and gets here.
summary: This is second piece in set for me

reviewText: I picked this item as a Vine product because I felt it was a good looking product and would look good on my patio with a flower pot next to it.The pros:It does have a modern, classy lookExtremely light weight and easy to maneuver.  Fits through a normal door way.Covers from the cushions can be removed and washed if needed.Cons:The cushions are plenty comfortable for a bit---but it's just an awkward way to sit for an extended amount of time.  I would not purchase a full set because of this.Does not look like it will with stand rainy weather.
summary: Not quite what I had in mind, but cute

reviewText: Just as advertised. Love it.

This chair looks in person exactly like it does in the product picture.  It is a nice neutral and natural looking color so it blends in with many decors.  I think the ottoman is a must with it if you are going to sit on it for long periods of time and want to be comfortable. The chair is pretty solid in construction and is sturdy, I'm 6'1" and pushing 240 and it holds me just fine.  I worry the cushions will get dirty over time where spot-cleaning isn't going to cut it, but time will tell on that. Looks really nice on the patio.

When I unpacked the box, I was stunned at the size of this chair.  It is the size of a chair you'd put in your den before the fireplace.  Initially, I thought to purchase the matching ottoman; however, after putting it out on the patio, I realized I did not have enough room to include the ottoman.  Since most patios are fairly small, I thought you ought to know.However, there are a number of good features about this chair:1.  The resin-based wicker will hold up to most weather conditions without damage.  Not tornadoes, of course, but it performed well in a high wind situation.2.  The chair is heavy.  It will stay where you put it; however, this applies only to the chair itself.  The cushions are loose and can be blown around.  You could reduce this problem by applying sticky velcro strips, available at your local hardware store, to the chair and its cushions.3.  The chair is large enough to accommodate very large people, so if your family is full of six-footers, this will be perfect.  I'm small, so when my feet are on the floor, there is fully seven inches of space between my back and the back cushion. On the other hand, there's enough room for me to sit cross-legged on the chair.4.  Cushion fabric is a tough duck material.  The manufacturer suggests bringing in the cushions during bad weather, but I think they would survive well, should you forget.  And the covers are zippered, so you can remove them for washing.Overall, this is a nice chair if you have the need and the room for a BIG patio chair.Four stars!
summary: Too Big for Comfort (Unless You're a Very Large Person)

reviewText: You can use this all-weather armless wicker chair in a playroom, living room, patio, porch, deck or anywhere you decide.  It would be great in a child's room, because it is sturdy and can stand up to abuse.  I was amazed as I unpacked the chair with its style and high quality.  The wicker is strong and easy to clean.  This is the most practical piece of furniture.  The ONLY problem, I have had is that my cat like it as much as I do.  You cannot go wrong with purchasing this chair.

I really like this Strathwood Griffen line of faux wicker resin patio furniture.It is attractive, made well and is very sturdy.I already have theStrathwood Griffen All-Weather Wicker Chair, Dark Brown, which has arms, and the Strathwood Griffen armless wicker chair.The ottoman is a nice size without being too huge. The cushion fits well though it would have been nice to have straps or Velcro or something on the cushion so it didn't slide around when used. I do like the color of the cushion (light beige) but wish it was a bit darker; it would have been more practical. I did spray it with3M Scotchgard Outdoor Water Shield, 10.5-Ounce. The cushion is made of a sturdy polyester fabric that is easy to wipe clean but I wanted all the protection I could get to keep it looking nice.It came packed very well, just like the chairs did. It was delivered right to my door by FedEx and it was light enough for me to carry into the house.Without the cushion, the ottoman can be used for a table, though Strathwood Griffen does make a side table and a coffee table that matches this set. Or it can be used for extra seating. Very versatile.One small thing - the cushion comes stored underneath the ottoman and it is a BEAR to get out. Talk about a tight fit.All in all, a great ottoman AND patio set.
summary: I like the Strathwood Griffen line

reviewText: This is a great accompanying piece to the other Strathwood Griffen pieces. It is larger than it looks and is a great looking ottoman. The one issue is that it is rather tall so you're legs are almost vertical when in the Griffen chairs. It's not that big of a deal though, but in case you are thinking it is smaller than it is just realize the picture of it alone is not a good estimate. You can see the height in the other photos.So it really works well as either a foot rest or as a place to deposit a tray. The cushion is actually pretty flat and sturdy. Only problem is that it doesn't attach to the base. So it does slip a bit.It's well built and solid though, and that is a nice comfort. The legs were all even. The weave is very natural looking. The cushion has a removable cover and is washable.It's a nice piece. But it is pretty spendy. And it arrived in a box with several Chinese freight stickers. So I'm assuming made in China.

Looks great, just as pictured, light weight, I received it in a timely manner. Noticed some rust on the plastic it was wrapped in. So I anticipate that if placed outside it will rust when it rains, so watch out for your floors. Worst of all, the cushion will not stay in place. Keeps sliding off, so I ended up using it without the cushion on it. I may return it.Update~ I returned it. No good without the cushion.

First off, it was nice not to have to assemble something, and that notwithstanding, there wasn't wasted space in the packaging (cushion came in the inside of the ottoman).Onto the product:It is incredibly light--a child could carry it! The cushion can be used, making this a seat or ottoman, or you can leave the cushion off and use it as a table. The cushion itself is very firm and feels great; quality fabric and materials. I wouldn't leave the cushion outdoors, but the rest should be safe there. Beautiful product!

We are always looking for ottomans.  Why is it that outdoor chairs and furniture sets don't come with them?  The fact that you can order this ottoman separately is a major plus.  Too bad though--after over a year of trying--the manufacturer still cannot attach the woven resin material evenly.  You know how it is when the stripes on a shirt/skirt/shorts are crooked?  Or when the lines don't match at the seam?  Well, my ottoman looks like it's tilted, but it isn't really.  It is the resin material that is applied on an angle and is heading off the bottom edge. Last year I ordered a cocktail table and an end table.  Both had the same problem:  The resin material was not lined up when attached to the frame.  It wouldn't be so bad if there was no color variation in the weave, but if you look closely at the picture you can see stripes--not severely contrasting stripes, but stripes all the same.  In my opinion, stripes need to line up:  On shirts or on furniture.NOTE:  I don't even need to post a picture of my own:  Just take a close look at the pictures posted on this product page.  Look at the front-on view and you can see the weave is angled.  It is more prominent when you stand a few feet away, and the tilt of the weave is even more prominent on my piece.  Highlight the close-up picture along the bottom edge and you can see where the weave runs off the edge.**UPDATE:  If you really want to buy this furniture, but are concerned about receiving a piece with the "crooked look", consider the darker color:  There is not so much difference in the weave color and you can't see stripes.**This ottoman is a nice height and is lightweight enough that anyone could move it around.  If you need a little extra storage space in the area when you use this furniture, the inside is hollow.The color of the resin weaving is identical to what was sold last season; so you can feel some confidence in a new piece matching one purchased last year.  The cushion is a neutral color and the material feels substantial.Regarding the cushion:  It is not attached at the base, so it slides around when you lift your feet up.  Also, there is no indication that the material is treated with Scotchguard.  We are going to spray the material with Scotchguard and apply some Velcro pieces.  It is a zippered cover, so I suppose it can be washed.The base is exactly like the tables, just a different size.  So, if you wanted to, you could remove the cushion and use it as a low table.  Like the tables, there is no support under the weave, but you can use it for very lightweight items (glasses, yes; not stemware).One last observation:  I got a table in this line last year that arrived with a broken leg and Amazon did not want it back.  We put it behind a storage shed in case Amazon changed its mind.  It has not gotten any use, but it has been out in the weather for a year now and the color and texture of the resin weave has not changed.

Strathwood - a product by Amazon.comApproximate measurements:Cushion: 24" x 24" x 6" thick.Ottoman without the cushion: 25 1/4" x 25 1/4" x 12 1/2"No assmebly was required. I did have  some trouble pulling the cushion out from under the ottoman; it was in there very tightly, but I finally got it.I find the ottoman to be  comfortable. Most of the time it will be used for extra seating; other times it might become a special spot for the kids to play a card game or board game...and without the cushion it could be used as a low side table. Oh, and what ottomans were designed for, to prop up my feet and relax. In my opinion, an ottoman is versatile piece of furniture.I called customer service to inquire about the weight limit  for Amazon's Strathwood Griffen furniture. They don't list a weight limit & the customer service representative didn't have any information on it either.  I think it would be a good idea to have that information, so I submitted a suggestion.Thoughts:The ottoman is comfortable enough to use for seating. It's lightweight & easy to move,The cushion slips around & isn't secured to the ottoman which is annoying.The cushion has a zipper & piping. Its cover can be removed for thorough cleaning.I plan on protecting the cushion with a fabric spray such as3M Scotchgard Fabric Protector.This ottoman pairs nicely with all the Griffen line of chairs including the dining chairs with or without arms.Amazon's product description covers cushion care & cleaning so I won't go into that. However, I will remind you that during inclement weather it's recommended to bring both the ottoman and the cushion indoors or securely cover them, and to store them in a dry place when not in use.A product guarantee isn't mentioned. However, you may return this item sold by Amazon.com within 30 days of delivery for a full refund. Amazon.com will pay the return shipping cost if the return is a result of their error. It is durable, strong, resistant to humidity, water & UV radiation, & somewhat elastic. It's easy to clean & can be hosed down (remove the cushion first). The color is part of the fiber & shouldn't fade.
summary: Cushion doesn't attach to the base...

reviewText: I wrote a review on the Strathwood Griffen All-Weather Wicker Chair last year. It was the chair I blame for me having to build a deck because we needed a place to put it, and while I love the deck and the chair, I will be making huge payments on the deck for another six months.  But I can hardly be angry at the chair, so I got the ottoman to keep it company.Like the chair, it came in an enormous box, in one piece.  And this one has a huge pillow matching the chair to put the feet up on. Aside from taking it out of the box and getting all of that cardboard to the recycling center, it was in perfect condition.The comforter has a nice home inext to the chair in the corner of the deck, and as I mentioned in my previous review, even with some supremely comfortable deck chairs ("let's get a table and deck chairs" came soon after the building of the deck began), people gravitate to this wicker combination. It is wide and a very comfy place to sit back and relax. It is very sturdy, and I'm sure with care it will last for some time, but some of the reviews I have read do make me a little concerned about the longetivity of the piece. For right now, it is beautiful and my family loves it.I should remark that the ottoman, like the chair, isn't "real wicker." It is a woven resin material which looks strikingly like wicker, treated to protect from ultra-violet light and keep its color and elasticity. It does seem that the material has some give to it, and I hope this doesn't promote fraying such as in the picture posted by Mr. Petersen at the top of this page.The ottoman, including the cushion, wieghs in at just about 16 pounds, which I think is amazing. It is very easy to move about. I wiegh in at about 275 pounds, and I feel comfortable parking myself on the ottoman.  When it rains, I have managed on almost all occasions to bring the cushion inside, but even when I was too late and it gets a little wet, like the pillows for the chair, it dries out quickly and cleanly. The cushion is zippered so that you can remove the foam insert to clean the cover.I am very happy with the ottoman, and my wife is as well. She loves how it looks, especially, of course, with the matching chair. Everyone who has sat in the chait loves the addition of the ottoman. You can see other people on the deck plotting to snatch the seat should the current occupant leave.  I do recommend this ottoman, and I will try to remember to come back and write an update in a year or so, or less if something happens to dispariage my feelings on it. Cheers!
summary: Another happy review on a Strathwood product

reviewText: This ottoman looks in person exactly like it does in the product picture and we are pretty satisfied with it's performance. It is sturdy, seems well-built and is a nice natural-looking color that blends in well on the patio. It is lightweight enough that we can easily move it around or bring it in to store if it's going to rain. The cushion is nice and thick and comfortable to use. Two things I think would improve this product is if the cushion could be attached and if I could just throw the cover in the wash.

I have an armchair that matches this lovely all-weather wicker Ottoman.I switched the cushions.  The chair had a thinner cushion, and the ottoman had a larger cushion, and when I switched the two, it just felt and fit better.This is light, easy to move around, durable, and works indoor as furniture, or out of doors.  The cushion is not attached, and so it swings off the wicker ottoman easily, but that is OK, as my feet hold it in place.  This is strong enough for my kid to sit on this as a chair, when a larger group of people are squeezing onto the porch.As a 240 pound man, I like that these wicker pieces stand up to my weight, don't feel like they are about to break, and are attractive in a clean way.  Good buy.
summary: Strong, light, and easy to use... with huge cushion.

reviewText: This is a good looking, fuctional ottoman with one flaw.  The cushion lays on the top without anything holding it in place. Even though it is heavy it has moven a number of times when I have pushed against the side of the cushion with my legs or feet. Aside from that this is a very nice product.I love the look of the wicker and the feel of the cushion. It feels great to rest my legs on such a soft cushion.I weigh over 200 pounds and I can comfortably sit on the ottoman as well. It feels very comfortable.The ottoman measures 25.2 inches long by 25.2 inches deep by 12.6 inches high so it is big. You could easily have two people sitting back to back on it. The bottoms look wood like and seem like they will not damage floors.Since this is the winter, and as I write this it is snowing, I have been using this in my basement.  The dark brown wicker looks great and I could see using this in a basement or another room in a house.While the cushion is heavy there is nothing holding onto the ottoman. As a result if I hit it with my knee or leg it moves. I could imagine the cushion being moved or coming off the ottoman if you have a party with a lot of children or clumsy adults. I wish there were velcro tabs or some other mechanism holding the cushion in place.Since I am in New Jersey I have not used this outside so I can't comment on how easy it is to clean them. I plan to use it in an enclosed screened-in unheated porch which can get over 100 degrees in the summer. I also plan to use it when I have parties in my back yard. I may even keep in down my basement where it looks good. will have more of a chance to test how they hold up to changes in temperature and the dirt than can accumulate from summer parties when that happens.
summary: If the Cushion Had Something Holding It In Place I Would Have Given This Five Stars

reviewText: It works well alongside the Wicker Chair. It matches the rest of the set nicely and holds drinks and snacks as intended.

This table looks great! It matches this sofaStrathwood Griffen All-Weather Wicker 3-Seater Sofa, Dark Brownperfectly. I use this table on my patio and it fits the build perfectly as I don't have enough space to fit a larger table.My table is leveled perfectly and does not wobble as others might have mentioned.

I bought 3 to put around the deck wherever needed very handy After shopping and considering many options I found this furniture to be very good value for the money, light but strong, happy with purchase

I just received this item. I plan to follow up in 6 months, after using it outside this coming spring and summer. Right now it looks good, Just as pictured, it's functional, great size, which is perfect for my small sun room. I think it's prized right for the quality.

This is a very nice end table and goes perfectly with my other Strathwood Griffen pieces.  It is a plastic wicker which holds up very well to the weather.  I leave my stuff on the deck outside year-round in the northeast.  The table has a metal frame that seems to be powdercoated to prevent rust.  It is light enough to easily move around, but not so light that a normal wind will blow it off of the deck.The top is not perfectly flat - it is bumpy - but it has no problem supporting a drinking glass.My only complaint is that the wicker "lines" are not straight to the edges of the table.  They are all at about a 10 degree angle.  They are straight to eachother, but the lines are not at 90 degree angles to the lines of the shape of the table.Table does not wobble, as someone else experienced - just visually askew.
summary: Nice table - weatherproof - wicker a bit askew

reviewText: We had a casual backyard barbecue the other night, and following dinner, the guests converged around our CobraCo Copper Mission Fire Pit, which we had set up just hours earlier.  Right out of the box you notice how sturdily-constructed this unit is, with an ample 100% copper bowl, and an attractive Mission style design.What we really loved was how quick it was to assemble--just attach the ringed handle to the screen cover and the legs to the base (with the included Allen wrench) and you're good to go.The kids loved toasting marshmallow for their s'mores over the domed spark guard, and the unit provided ample heat (but not too much!) as the night's chill crept in.We also appreciate the fact that it comes with a protective vinyl cover to help preserve the buffed shine on that copper bowl for as long as possible.
summary: A sleek, attractive, easy-to-assemble addition to backyard entertaining

reviewText: Since I received this via the Amazon VINE program, it has either been in the high 80's / low 90's or raining daily.  As such I have not been able to give it a functional test (and probably won't until the Fall).  However, since Amazon VINE issues a review deadline, I will comment strictly on the appearance and construction. From an appearance standpoint, the fire pit is fairly nice from a distance.  Up close , however, you can see the construction/packing/shipping flaws which give it the air of an older beat up pit.  In particular, the bowl has a major "bend" in the upper flat lip.  I've considered that this is by intent to give it a more rustic flair, but since it prevents the spark guard from sitting properly on the top, I doubt it.  Also about 1/3 around the top, also on the flat lip is a "ding" which looks like someone gave it a mighty whack with a ball peen hammer.  The material seems to be stronger than plain old copper so I have not been able to fix either imperfection by hand.  Finally, the cover supplied is rather flimsy and I don't think it will last long in our Chicago weather.  All in all, I would have to say that had I paid ~$300 for this I would have returned it as defective.  As it is, as the weather normalizes and evenings cool a bit, I'm sure we'll get some use out of the pit.

When this was offered for late/spring early/summer reviewing, I wondered about the timing. When testing this, I also wondered about what the neighbors were thinking. Then I remembered that they had frequently let me know such, so all was well.Assembly should have been a snap. Unfortunately one of the bolts for the legs was poorly threaded. I had neither the right sized black metric bolt nor the right threading in my tap and die set to rethread the bolt or the hole. So, to put on one of the legs I had to use a bolt I had that was almost right and force it in with some thin metal stock as a shim to make the hole a little smaller. Thus a ten minute assembly took over an hour.This has a very nice appearance and, once assembled, is quite sturdy. The lid fits well enough, though it's circular shape is not quite the same as the circular shape of the bowl. I'm hesitant to put too much force on the lid to change its shape. It does contain the ashes while burning. There is also a vinyl cover for it (when not in use).The grate is sturdy enough, though I would have preferred that the spacing between its bars to have been smaller. It is difficult to use tender to get the fire started without it falling to the bottom of the bowl. I have taken a smaller grate from another grill to go crosswise and it works much better.Overall, this looks nice on the patio, burns well and I'm sure we will use it more often once the appropriate season gets here. Maybe I'll be getting an outdoor fan to review then, too.
summary: Great in Texas - cooled off the patio.

reviewText: This outdoor fire pit is beautiful 100% copper (bowl) with a sturdy metal stand.  The screen cover (which our last fire pit did not have) seems like a good idea.  The vinyl cover that comes with the fire pit seems to work well, keeping it clean and dry.  That is definitely a nice addition.We're looking forward to many years of sitting by the fire, cooking hot dogs and toasting marshmallows!  A great addition to our outdoor pool area.

I love having a little bonfire on evenings when the weather isn’t too hot to tolerate it. There is something comforting about sitting by a crackling fire – especially if you have marshmallows or hotdogs on hand.The CobraCo Copper Mission Fire Pit FBCOPMISN-C is a beautiful fire pit. The copper finish is just stunning. I have had another fire pit from this manufacturer and it was difficult to put together. This model, however, was very easy to assemble, which I am very grateful for.This fire pit comes with the stand, the bowl, a little rack that sits inside the bowl, a spark screen, a spark guard removal tool, and a vinyl cover to keep it protected. My older CobraCo fire pit also came with a cover, which I soon discovered did not keep rain out of the fire pit, and turned into a nice place for mosquitos to breed. This model, however, works much better. It has rained half the month since I got this fire pit and every time I have checked underneath the cover, the bowl was dry.The pit works as well as any other for building fires. The round shape make it easy for several people to gather round – especially important if you are toasting marshmallows or wieners.CobraCo has really improved a lot with this model and I would highly recommend this fire pit to anyone looking to invest in a really beautiful model that will last a long time.
summary: CobraCo has really improved with this fire pit model

reviewText: This is a pretty bowl (until you fire it up--all metals discolor under fire eventually.) The screen top is a bit flimsy, in my opinion. Seems you can dent it easily, or else I'm a bit clumsy.It goes together fairly well--you do have to do some assembly to put the legs on the base. And it's a bit large. I have a smallish space, so this worked better out in the yard, and then of course, if you don't have a patio, you have to put something under it to protect the ground from the heat. (Fire mat, for example.)Summer is short no matter where you live, but our autumn actually lasts into November with good weather, so this can be a nice way to sit outside, especially when it gets dark earlier. It adds warmth and the ancient feeling of gathering around the campfire or hearth, which is one of those elemental human experiences.Best for a patio of a decent size. Not good for flammable decks or where you are not allowed to have open fires for safety reasons, even with the screen. Fire pits have a safety concern --what if there is a sudden gust of wind? Embers can blow onto your house, your neighbor's house or the dry grass, starting a fire. Not only can there be property damage, but injury, danger and liability.  A few of our less fortunate neighbors had devastating fires due to poor handling of hot ashes from their charcoal barbecuers.After using this, you have to completely douse the embers and not leave them smoldering--but you can't throw water into the bowl. One method is a metal bucket to scoop ashes into that you can then smother in cold ash. (Wet wood ash make lye--a corrosive. So if you wet the ash, you have to figure out how to dispose of it safely.)  Another is to put a solid lid, like a 55 gal lid onto the pit to smother the embers. Safety considerations are an issue with fire pits.
summary: Beautiful copper pit, safety issues are a concern

reviewText: Putting this together was a total snap, which I appreciated.The copper was quite shiny initially, but after a couple of fires, it took on a "patina", which was pretty nice. But, don't expect this to look new for very long.I'm mildly concerned about the grate, though. It's very similar to another fire pit I had, and it rusted after a year.Otherwise, it looks very nice for the price. If this is your style, I'd totally recommend it.
summary: Beautiful, but smaller than I expected.

reviewText: This is a beautiful but simple fire pit.  The copper bowl has a hand hammered look and the stand has very clean lines which could be described as modern or craftsman style so it goes well with pretty much any décor.  It's well made and hopefully will withstand the elements for many years.  It has a cover to use during the off season but I think I will still have my husband move it unto our covered patio during the winter because I don't want it to look all rusted out in a couple of years.  Yeah, we've all seen those poor neglected rusted out fire pits in our friends yards and I don't want mine to become one of them.

The instructions that come with the pit make it clear: you can expect the pit to discolor when you use it.  All the photos highlight that new-copper shine, but after one fire, the shine quickly fades, inside and out.  Not a big deal, but if you are spending extra because copper looks so pretty, you might be disappointed.Overall, I really like the pit, and don't mind the discoloration.  The included grate, and the holes in the bottom of the pit, assist with airflow...this will keep your fire burning longer without having to fuss too much with the wood.  I did notice that after just one use, the metal on the grate itself had warped a bit...not a huge surprise, I guess, but I wonder what it will look like at the end of summer.One other thing: I really appreciate the provided tool for removing the lid.  I've never had a fire pit before, and maybe all pits come with such a tool, but without it I would need to keep protective gloves nearby for removing the lid during a fire.In summary: If it's important for you to have copper, this is a fine fire pit, but you may need to do some work to keep it looking as nice as it did when you bought it.
summary: Don't expect the shine to last

reviewText: First, this looks great out of the box. You get a solid ring, four legs (nicely packed in rolled corrugated cardboard so that they don't rub together in transit), a brass bowl, a grate, a screen top, a ring holder for the top, and tongs. (You also get a hexagonal Allen wrench, so no tools are necessary.) To assemble the thing, you have to screw the ring holder onto the grate. That was easy and took less than a minute. (The screw to hold the holder onto the screen comes screwed into the ring so that it's obvious which screw to use.) The next thing to do is attach the four legs. Here is where I ran into difficulty.The legs have two screw holes, and the instructions seem to suggest that all the legs are identical. (The instructions do not say as much directly, but the legs are not distinguished either. The instructions state simply that you have four legs, nine screws, and so forth. I was able to attach the first two legs fairly easily but I couldn't get the next two on. The holes did not align properly. After spending about 15 minutes struggling with the legs, I gave up. But a bit later, I tried again and rotated the legs. I removed the first two and was able to get the four legs to fit. Well, three of them fit well, and one doesn't fit well, but at least I was able to attach it.The end result is a fire pit that wobbles since the legs don't seem to match up well. The pit works (and quickly loses its sheen), but it does wobble. The problems I had assembling the pit may have been my fault, but I did read the directions as best I could.
summary: Maybe the fault is mine, but . . .

reviewText: This fire pit requires only basic assembly out of the box to get it up and running. You only have to put together the ring (attach legs) that holds the bowl which, even for my non-handy self, took less than 30 minutes.
