Ordered from Amazon, competitive price, even to regional sellers, free shipping.  Came packaged really well and was easy to put together, if you follow the directions.  Started on the first try.  Love that!  Hopefully this grill will last as long as the last one.  Heats up fast, sufficient cooking space.  I use it almost every day, I love grilling- veggies, fish,chicken etc.
summary: Great Grill Starts on first try!

reviewText: This grill is wonderful. We will never need to replace it as all parts are replaceable. It moves easily; heats well; even cooked bacon and eggs in a skillet. It is sturdy and well-made.

I have had the grill for about one month and have used it frequently. Pros: Fairly clear assembly instructions; Quality construction; Heats up to max temperature (around 550 degrees F) in approximately 10 minutes in warm weather; Temperature gauge useful to monitor RELATIVE not absolute temperature; Even temperature throughout two burner area. Cons: Stainless steel surface on folding wings is easily scratched; Door to cabinet must be exactly at 90 degrees to allow removal of drip pan; Hanging full propane tank on the weight gauge requires some flexibility and upper body strength.My assembly of the grill took about 3 hours. The instructions use pictures more than words and I had to redo the placement of the igniter line because it was not clear that it must run outside of the bracket for the drip pan. I have cooked not only for my spouse but also other family members. The two burner size requires cooking some meals in "shifts." Your mileage may vary if you have teenage boys living with you.You may wish to consider getting the Weber 7589 Premium Cover and the Lodge Logic LDP3 Reversible Grill/Griddle that I use with this grill and have separately reviewed.
summary: Excellant grill for couple or small family

reviewText: THE QUESTI started my quest for a new grill fully expecting to quickly buy a $199 special and then pay for the lava rock option which over time had gone from standard grill equipment to an option the last time I bought consumer grade grill -- some 6+ years ago.  My how times change. I quickly discovered that despite the nameplates there are really only three manufactures of consumer level grills left and that NONE of them were offering up lava or ceramic bricks even as an option anymore!The high end units still have lava or ceramic bricks at least available if not standard fare, but the inexpensive consumer units were all relegated to the porcelain coated steel “flavor” bars which are supposed to take the place of lava rocks. From previous experience testing the effectiveness of the steel bars, let me tell you now that this just isn’t true! Proof? Well for one thing the commercial and high-end units still mostly have either lava or ceramic bricks and that’s all the hint you should need!Another good hint is the addition of the “catch pan” to consumer grills to collect juice runoff from your food. In a lava system most of these juices are vaporized back into your food. My previous grills didn’t NEED a catch pan because the yummy juices and drippings were being vaporized and reused! Put simply, the porcelain covered “flavor bars” now in use in all the consumer grills are simply not as efficient at the vaporizing process as evidenced by the mere existence of the “catch pan” in current models!My take on the lava issue in short is: If you don’t want to use charcoal, and you don’t have a lava gas grill, you might as well just cook inside!(WARNING –THE FOLLOWING INFO IS PROVIDED FOR EDUCATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY AND PROBABLY VIOLATES YOUR WARRANTY)CONVERTING TO LAVAThus, I set about trying to buy a grill that I could easily modify to a lava grate system which turned out to be quite the hunt! While my Home Depot still sells lava grates and lava, they didn’t carry a single grate for ANY of their current models and no one there knew what I was asking for. Lowes had nothing at all but at least their employee knew what I was talking about. I headed for Sears who had a rep who remembered the great taste of lava grills fondly but who informed me that Sears carried nothing I wanted.After a long hunt I decided to move up to a mid-range grill which eventually led me to the Weber 320. In the end, I decided on the Weber grill because in my involved quest I determined that not only was the Weber 300 series a quality grill, but that the Weber 300’s still have support stubs built into the grill mold that will support a lava grate! Since Weber doesn’t sell lava grates anymore I am assuming these are a remnant of the casting process from models past as the grate stubs are not used with the porcelain “flavor bars” that come with the 300 series today. Regardless, I knew it would work!After much measuring and hunting I found that the “Char-Broil 2989704 OE 7000 Porcelain Grid” can be easily modified to fit the Weber 300’s like a glove. The grid is already the correct depth but is too wide by three bars. So you just have to cut off three bars on one side of the grid to decrease the width and you are all set. I did this with bolt cutters so it literally took me 10 seconds, but even with a hacksaw you are looking at three simple bar cuts that shouldn’t take more than a few minutes.I also ordered a package of “Char-Broil Char-Diamonds” which are processed lava rocks, for lack of a better term, so that all the rocks are the same size and shape. Lava purists will insist on actual lava, but I have used the char-diamonds before with great success. The advantage of the diamonds over natural lava is that they have a more even heat distribution and (in my opinion) greater sanitation since real lava has large pores that collect grease. Lava purists will say that those same pores make a difference in the flavor of your cooking by vaporizing even more juices (that get caught in the pores) and that any bacteria left inside them gets killed off when the grill is pre-heated the next time you cook. They may be right, but I live in bug-filled Florida and want as little left behind after cooking as possible, so it’s Char-Diamonds or ceramic bricks for me!After cutting the lava grate to size, place the grate in the grill and place the diamonds on the lava grate (see photo’s.) Meanwhile, put the “flavor bars” on ice as you won’t be installing/using them. What is shown in the pictures is one full bag of “Char-Diamonds” so it is a pretty good fit. Be sure you have a row of diamonds over each of the burner tubes to reduce the amount of drippings that reach the tubes. The flavor bars cover the tubes better than the lava does so you want to maximize the covering to reduce any maintenance mess.ADVANTAGES/DISSADVANTAGES OF LAVAThe primary advantage to a lava system is that you get the flavor of charcoal grilling while maintaining the convenience of a gas grill. In fact, I would argue that the flavor is better with lava as you don’t taste the starter fuel used to light the charcoal but still get the flavor advantage of charcoal style grilling. But there are some other advantages and disadvantages as well:ADVANTAGES OF A LAVA SYSTEM-Food will taste better because most of the fats and juices are vaporized and sent back into the food.-Self-cleaning to some extent--When you are done cooking, simply turn off the gas and close the grill.--The lava will still be hot for some time and this “free” heat will burn up whatever mess remains!-More even heating surface (in theory at least – remember this grill was not DESIGNED for lava) I will update on this after more use.-Reduces your propane use (my personal experience) since the lava holds heat and also lets you clean up after grilling with the propane turned off.-Allows you to drop hickory, mesquite and other wood chips directly onto the lava rocks which will GREATLY enhance the flavor of what you cook.--Put a handful of hickory chips “Weber 17053 Hickory Wood Chips, 3-Pound” in a bowl of water for 15 mins.--Drop directly on lava rocks before you start cooking if it is something fast or for the last 15 mins or so of cooking if cooking something slowly.--You need to watch your meal when you use wood directly under what you are cooking as the chips will dry out and flame up after they dry out.--This wood chip flame out can also be a good thing sometimes, it depends on what  you are cooking!--If you are cooking with the lid closed you can put the chips on a part of the grill without food over it as the smoke will fill the inside of the grill.--Optionally you can purchase steel boxes to place on the lava and put chips in. I have never tried this method.DISSADVANTAGES OF A LAVA SYSTEM-Lava modifications likely void your warranty and is not what the grill was designed for – do it at your own risk! Watch your grill!-The Char-Diamonds are only good for 1-3 seasons before needing to be replaced depending on your usage and environment.-You have to spend another $40 or so on lava and a lava grid + modify the grid.-If you try the wood chips (and you should!) you may need to clean your grill more often.--The jury is still out on this one as I am finding the Weber juice collection system is now collecting my wood chip debris instead!-Lava maintains heat! (This is both an advantage and a disadvantage)--With the flavor bars, when you reduce the heat setting, the temperature in the grill will drop fairly quickly -- especially with the top up.--Lava on the other hand maintains heat, so if your recipes call for a heat reduction mid-cooking be aware that the grill will take a while to respond and you will need to lower the heat sooner!THE WEBER 320 GRILL ITSELFThere are lots of reviews about how great this grill is so I will summarize my thoughts rather than repeat.-This is a quality grill! Much more so than the $199 specials but then again it should be as it is more than twice as much!-Materials and packing are top notch.-The propane scale is a nice feature as is the temp gauge but the scale seems to be 100% steel so only time will tell if it holds up. It is well coated.-The igniter is only on the left burner, you then light the others in sequence. I have never seen this design before so no idea if this is an issue.-My unit shipped with no nuts for the side burner controls. The manual looks like there should be pre-tapped nuts on the shelf but there were none.--This could be fixed with a quick trip to a hardware store for two stainless steel nuts but as my grill was shipped damaged I am going to Weber customer service for help. (See Below)SHIPMENT-My grill arrived kind of beat up looking in what was by far the largest/heaviest box I EVER got from UPS.-The box is huge and weighs 136 pounds so be prepared.--If you don’t have a friend or a hand truck you will have to roll it in the house or unbox the grill and move it in pieces.-If you have stairs you will be hurting!-The box even has a “MECH” sticker on it -- telling the warehouse people they should move it via mechanical means such as a forklift.-UPS dropped it and ran without ringing the bell like they usually do. I suspect they get requests for help moving it into the home too often.CUSTOMER SERVICE-I called Weber customer service upon learning I had two damaged parts (I later found a third) their instructions were not to return the grill to Amazon.--They told me to build the grill and call them for replacement parts when I was done.--The back panel, base, and door were all bent. I fixed the back panel and base to satisfaction but I am unable to fix the door as it is riveted.--I doubt most people would have been able to repair these parts as they would not have the tools/skills to do so.--I will report back on how Weber handles my customer service/damaged parts issues.-When I called customer service they answered quickly and promised to mail the damaged/missing pieces to me next week.--I will report back on how that process ends but so far they get 5 stars!Good Luck!
summary: How to turn  this grill from great to awesome for $40 in 10 mins!

reviewText: This grill is new for 2013 and it was very easy to assemble. All the parts were in the box and there wasn't any damage. I cooked chicken and steak on it the first night and it worked Okay. I bought a aftermarket grill 2 years ago and it leaked grease all over my deck plus it didn't cook evenly and had hot and cold spots so I went back to a Weber because we could afford it this year. My last Weber lasted 10 years and I can't imagine why this one wouldn't do the same. The Stainless is heavy duty and I like that the propane tank is hidden behind the door and out of site. The small foot print is a plus but not the reason I bought the grill it's simply because there are only two of use now and serves our purpose. Update 5/18/13 I have cooked several times and the grill is not heating very well. The cross over tube flame is red not blue and cooking times have decreased. I called Weber and there going to send a new burner and we will see if it solved the problem. I will update when I replace the parts. Update 5/26/2013 I have installed the new burner tubes and had a party this weekend and it took over one hour to cook thin burgers. This is the worst grill I have ever owned. Weber is sending a rep to see if it can be fixed but at this point I just want them to do the right thing and take it back before the summer is over. Update 5/28/2013 Lowe's has a 90 day return policy so I took it back and ordered a Genesis S-310 three burner with 38,000 BTU. I have to wait two weeks for the order so I hope it's worth it.
summary: Weber S-210 Worst Grill I Ever Owned

reviewText: This is my second Weber purchase (Genesis was the first).  Based on the Consumer Reports review I purchased this blindly.  It is a low end version of the Genesis.  The major bummer was that it came with dents in just about every part of the grill.  It was especially bad in the hood where it was very visible.  I wished I had purchased it locally so that I could return it.  After the grill was out of the box and spread out on my deck the "genie was out of the bottle" and I put it together.Lastly, it is smaller than most three burner grills.  With a family of 5 and the need to grill pizza, it has a small surface size that we could have worked with but not the size I expected.It was very easy to put together if you are worried about that.  It took about 2 hours.My last review, I gave my Genesis 5 stars... Would definitely not buy Spirit again.
summary: It had many dents and is flimsy...

reviewText: It was not easy to consent to my husband spending so much on a grill...but his main point was true we have to changed them out evey 2/4 years so this will pay for it self. Great quality craftsmanship - took just under 2 hours to put it together. This thing is amazing...I was setting the table and making a salad and just like that he was coming back inside with 3 steaks and a lobster cooked, done, finish lighting fast. LOVE IT GREAT INVESTMENT. We also bought a companion Webers gilling cook book.Happy Grillin

I have bought many inexpensive grills in the past that rust out and fade away after a few years. This grill is really well made. It was very easy to put together. I could tell as I put it together that the parts were well made and the grill well designed. I have used the grill and it is a pleasure to cook with, I highly recommend this grill and I suggest you order it before there is sales tax slapped on.

This Weber grill is the perfect size, and has lots of grilling space. The construction is solid, and the time to assemble is around three hours. The directions are easy to follow with many pictures, and the finished product looks nice. The grill cook foods quickly and evenly.

We moved into a new apartment where charcoal was not allowed, and we have a very small balcony, so I needed a compact gas grill. Despite the great reviews the Q-series grills have, I wanted a "full-size" design. Given very positive experiences with my Weber charcoal grills, I was hopeful I could make the transition to Weber Gas. I also looked at the similarly compact Napoleon grill (what Weber is to the US, Napoleon is to Canada) which gets great reviews, but it is more expensive. The Napoleon is also the top rated small grill in Consumer Reports, but CR has not reviewed this latest Weber offering yet.For those of you looking to squeeze this into a tight space, as we were, the grill itself is 22" wide (straight across the top of the hood). The side tables (and base) each add 4" folded down, for a minimum width (with tables attached) of 30". You might be able to get down to 28" or so without the tables attached. The tables are 14.5" extended, for a maximum width of 51".I have been very pleased with the performance of this grill so far. As others have noted the grill easily reaches about 550 degrees in about 10min (a little faster or slower depending on weather conditions), and the cast iron grates give a great sear. Flare-ups are a non-issue and the proven flavorizor system does a fine job of protecting the burners and turning drippings into flavorful smoke, seasoning your grill over time. I haven't tested the evenness of the heat yet, but it does appear to be fairly even on high and low settings. The features this grill has are minimal, but useful, especially coming from a much simpler charcoal grill - the warming rack and side tables are secure and a luxury to have, along with the propane tank scale (fits a standard 20lb tank). The wheels on the bottom are very sturdy and the construction is all metal and also plenty sturdy.Notes on assembly: First, you gotta love getting free 2-day prime shipping for an item like this! Second, mine came with the updated hardware to attach the shelves. It was packed very well (this has been my experience with the Weber charcoal grills I purchased as well), and assembled easily in under an hour. Note that you will want to have two pairs of hands for assembly, the entire upper grill must be lifted up onto the frame and various wires/gas lines routed for one step. That would be tough without a little help, but it's a breeze if you have a partner to lend a hand.

As soon as you start unpacking this one you know it is good quality.  Heavy construction, well thought out.  (the assembly instructions are not great but acceptable)  Assembly is a one hour, two man job and not difficult.  The grill grates are first rate.  Easy to light up and the controls allow you to control.  I know how that sounds but if you have used cheap grills you know exactly what I mean.  My first use was in 25 degree weather with spitting precipitation.  4 large chicken breasts and 10 thighs.  All done in 20 minutes.  I love this grill.

I just bought this Weber Grill. I have been using gas rills for the past few years. I am very excited to go back to Charcoal. I really like the Weber family of grills and look forward to using this one.
summary: Very easy to put together and I look forward to goingback to Charcoal once more.

reviewText: I've had my Performer about a month now and am really enjoying it. Only a couple of gripes.First, the green is a different shade than the pictures depict online or in pictures I've viewed. However, the color is growing on me so I'm not too disappointed.Second complaint was the instructions. The instruction manual in the box was for a Performer that was at least 2 generations back. Pulled up the Weber website and found the correct instructions. Took my laptop computer outside to assemble the grill. The grill went together easily after that. Wear leather gloves when putting on the ash catcher!I really enjoy the grill and look forward to using it for indirect cooking and smoking. Glad I got this model because the extras enhance the experience. The cart is much more stable than the tripod models and the worktop is very nice. My old "Silver" didn't have the ash catcher or temp gage and I love both of these features.No regrets at this time and I recommend this model.

This grill was my Christmas present. Upon assembly I had my first usage for it ( baby back ribs). I really like the charcoal holders, which allow for indirect cooking and is excellent for foods like chicken and ribs.. I also thought the sideways lid holder would be awkward since I am a lefty but it feels natural. The char bin holds about 30 pounds of coals, up from the stated 20 pounds. Do yourself a favor. Buy a scoop for the charcoal, a nd lack of gas ignition like the platinum model has you will need a chimney starter. There are lots outthere but the Weber starter is designed well. I also plan to buy a rib rack and have already ordered the sear grate, which will make excellent steak. My old faithful genesis platinum II will get jealous but I love both my Weber grills!!!!!!
The counter top feature is awesome, as is the charcoal bin underneath.  It's also nice to have storage under the counter.  Very happy with the results.
summary: Just used it for the first time after unboxing it, worked perfectly.

reviewText: No gas ignition and that's all right by me.How many realize this without reviewing in detail the difference between this Performer and the one selling for $50 more? So, if it wasn't obvious to you before when you happened to look at this model please allow me to point that out. And, that's the only difference - all other parts and functions are the same.I bought this latest model as a gift for a friend.  I own this model's immediate predecessor that does not have the LCD timer.  And, this is my second Weber Performer; the first was the original, all metal model, which I finally decided to replace after many years of service and countless grillings.Why not opt for the gas ignition? I've been using a chimney charcoal starter for many years since the gas ignition feature on my original Performer wore out and decided to just save $50 with this one.The 22.5" Weber Kettle is the best charcoal grill for the money available today. It's simple to use and very versatile. It's big enough to have different cooking zones. Charcoal uses radiant heat to cook and direct grilling allows for extremely high heat to sear steaks and burgers. The grill's style also allows you to cook with indirect heat for chicken, ribs and other foods needing lower heat and longer time to cook just right. Of course, charcoal gives all your food a superior taste over a gas grill.The Performer just makes the Kettle so much better with a work table surface area, integrated tilt out charcoal storage bin, large storage rack beneath and it rolls / moves easier than a standard Kettle.Some useful tips if you buy the Performer:* Buy a Weber rotisserie insert for this grill. Absolutely fantastic accessory for making incredibly delicious, moist chicken, turkey, etc.* For grilling, I switched to the cast iron insert by Craycourt a couple years ago. Wonderful! They are relatively expensive, but once you've tried them you'll wonder why you didn't switch earlier.* There are so many great places to learn using your Weber.  One of the best is The Virtual Weber Bulletin Board and its forum (w w w . tvwbb . c o m)  People there cook just about everything over these kettles and it's amazing!  Lots of fun.
summary: No gas ignition on this model... everything else is the same.

reviewText: Got rid of my gas grill for this thing.. little more effort involved, but the flavor is ten times better.
summary: but the flavor is ten times better.

reviewText: When I assembled the grill the legs were loose and they wobbled.  I contacted Weber for a replacement.  They pushed back a little stating that this problem never happens but they sent me a new bottom for the grill.  That solve the problem and it is now as solid as a rock.  The grill cooks well for direct and indirect grilling.

I thought this was going to be too big once I opened it, but the surface is perfect. I've grilled tons of variety and also cooked for 2 people up to 20 people, and it was sufficient. You do have to use a decent amount of coal to get the heat up, like a full chimney starter, no matter what, but I just reuse the coals that haven't burned all the way through.

This grill is great It cooks evenly and the lid can hang on the side of the grill while tending to the food. The hinged grate is great for adding wood chips for flavor. The ash catcher makes for easy cleaning of the ashes and is worth the few extra bucks. Our grill arrived in perfect shape and was very easy to assemble. This grill is sturdy and heats evenly and has the Weber name behind it. We expect to be using it for many years. I now plan on buying the Weber 2290 22-1/2-Inch Charcoal Kettle Rotisserie, and the Rib-O-Lator Barbecue Rotisserie for it. this weber grill is worth every penny i paid for it.

We have a Weber One-Touch Premium (european model comparable to this) and use it since four years all year round. This grill always works withour any trouble and keeps temperature very stable. The ash catcher prevents ashes flying around on the patio and I would ever go for this model as the original. The catcher gives advantages and is worth the money.The grill comes ready to use but I suggest to buy charcoal baskets since they work better as the included holders.Assembly works easy the tricky thing is to mount the catcher. Its not very difficult but requires some trials. When you once know it, its very simple.I never regretted buying a Weber grill.
summary: This thing lasts for very long time

reviewText: This a extremely well-made grill. Sturdy, very easy to assemble, with excellent materials and finish.It's just the right size. I've entertained parties of 6 to 15 people, easily, grilling red meat, sausages, chicken and even pizza (with a few tricks, it's actually a great way to get a crunch tasty one).I'm from Brazil, and for most of my fellow countryman (including myself) there's no way to grill other than charcoal. I've recently moved to the US and I had no previous experience with Weber products, but I have to say I'm extremely impressed with this grill.I don't have the custom of grilling hamburgers because in my country we barbecue big pieces of red meat, especially alcatra and picanha (special cuts of top sirloin and tenderloin). They are slowly grilled and the results with charcoal are far more superior than gas-grilled ones.Besides, with a good quality charcoal, pieces of newspaper and a lighter, anyone can get a good fire with this grill. I don't even have to use the starter chimney (sold separately). From the nice handles to the thermometer and the ash dispenser (great feature by the way), everything in this grill is good quality.And the price is more than reasonable. I truly recommend this product.

Weber is the best got it here yesturday put it together in 10 min and was smokin ribs 25 min later. This is a very efficient grill so I ended up slightly over cooking them but they still came out good. Anyway the grill is sturdy easy to use and easy to keep clean. After I ordered it I continued reading reviews and I was worried because I read in someone's review that it was not made here but to my relief its made in the good old USA if it wasn't it was going back. I got the chimney starter and the cover and they are made in china or taiwan but the grill is made here.

For decades I made the tasty mistake of using my two Weber Kettles (18.5" and 22.5") as only outdoor grills.  I'd load a charcoal chimney, get them hot, dump them in the Weber, grill, then serve.  I found myself using them less and less though so my wife bought me a propane grill.  For grillin' the propane worked great and was so convenient.  My Webers were put in deep sleep while I propane grilled on average 50 to 100 times a year.After many years I went looking online to see if there was another use for the hibernating Weber Kettles.  I quickly learned how to turn it into a smoker and an outdoor oven using just a few aftermarket accessories.  Using two fire bricks as a heat fence, charcoal, smoking wood, a good digital oven thermometer, and a proper charcoal/wood "snake" you have a near competition class smoker!  I dusted off the Webers and have been using them to smoke everything from ribs to turkeys.  I've cooked low 'n slow and hot n' fast with fantastic results, leaning more and more toward the hot n' fast style for saving time.  The Weber Kettles are not just grills!  In fact I don't use mine for grillin' at all since I have the gas grill for steaks, burgers, and hot dogs.  Now the gas grill gets very little use and the Webers are king once again in our backyard. You can smoke two pork butts or chickens on Saturday and have enough leftovers for the whole week!  And turkeys?  Brine a turkey and smoke it on the Weber for the best turkey you'll ever eat!If you are just using the Weber Kettle for grillin' you are cheating yourself out of incredible smoked meat dinners.  If you are looking for an all-in-one backyard appliance you will not find a more versatile outdoor appliance on the market than the Weber Kettle.
summary: Most versatile grill, smoker, and outdoor oven on the market!

reviewText: I like the way new Weber kettle grills cook. Unfortunately, the long term durability is poor. The grates are cheap, the porcelin finish on both my grills was flawed and cracked, and corrosion and rust take this grill to the curbside prematurely.. For the money, you are better off to buy a $50 Charbroil grill. I live on the coast and my Webers rusted straight away. I bought a Stok grill for less than the cost of the TOL Weber and so far, no rust or corrosion.....plus I have cast Iron grates instead of the caot hanger style grates that come with the Weber. The Stok also comes with other handy accessories like a charcoal starter that lets you avoid charcoal lighter fluid entirely.Follow up: My Weber grills took a beating due to inadequate packaging systems. This likely contributed to damage of the handle attachment points and the corrosion that was able to exploit the damaged areas. The marine environment I live in can be harsh on any metal that is not protected.

You can not find a better grill for the money. We have lived in many countries and the Weber Kettle Grill is a very expensive, highly prized grill. Americans are lucky that Weber is a domestic company.
summary: The best grill out there for the money!

reviewText: I have 2 sets, one holds a Hydrofarm 250 watt hooded light with no issue.The second set are working great holding up a 600 watt Apollo gull wing mh/mps set up, I'd reccomend then highly.

I used to use a rigged up system of cinch straps (commonly used for securing dirt bikes and motorcycles) to hang my lights. I found these when ordering another light system and I'll tell you what, I don't know how I EVER used to deal with hanging lights before. Sure chains are cool as you can move a link at a time, but these ratcheting style lights are awesome.Depending on the light I have hanging I am able to pull the slack and raise my lights and can reach up and release the locks to lower as I need. They metal gears are pretty strong and the whole system seems very well built. I have since bought two more sets.

I bought 3 sets and am using all 3 with success. No lights on the floor, the mechanisms work well, and that's that.I like them, I'm happy with my purchase, and I will update this review if anything changes.
It took me a few to get the hang of it, but, they work great.  So, I ordered some more.

you'll need these if you're growing plants indoors. My lights are often moved from one place to another, and with these I can easily switch them out and adjust without a lot of trouble. Could move a bit smoother, but for the price, I don't expect any better.

These are some real solid hangers. I've owned a few different ones but after getting theses ones for cheaper than the other brands I got I've ordered a lot more of these.Pros:Rope is thicker than other brands.Has more metal parts on the inside. The release clip is metal and not plastic.Overall the quality and feel is a lot better.Cons: None that I can find.
summary: Stonger and heavier duty than similar hangers

reviewText: I asked the question before purchasing so figured I'd share it in my review.  The item is superb quality.  To lower the grow light (or whatever you are hanging from it), you need to be able to reach the ratchet end to press the release button.  Since my grow light hangs from a ceiling, I hooked the ratchet end to the grow light and the hook-only end to the ceiling hooks.  I also shortened the ropes so they aren't in the way as much since they would hang below the light.
summary: You need to reach the ratchet to lower....

reviewText: These rope rachets work really well. Very easy to use with my lights. They also are very strong, i don't have any doubt they will hold up my lights easily.
These are great hangers, better than others I have for the same price. I would recommend for any grow lights.
Excellent Hangers !!!Found them to be easy to use and very easily lifts heavier items (Grow Lights, and other items)
summary: One Of the easyest hangers i ever used!!!

reviewText: Bought this brand for the first time (two ) a few months ago and have not had any problems or complaints.  Very easy to raise and lower but I am worried about the fitting holding the end of the rope together; which is the piece keeping my lights from crashing down onto my garden.  However I am very pleased with the security of the metal gears.

Okay, I have to remember that BBQing is NOT the same as cooking indoors.  And I have to remember that you (Amazon shopper) probably have a bigger grill than me.  This infusion cooker is very good for small tasty portions of food you want cooked simultaneously on the grill with your regular food.  It works best with a large gas / propane grill with dual controls.
summary: Helpful, but smaller than I'd like

reviewText: This product sounded like a great idea to me.  Be prepared that it is cheaply made enamel finished metal with sharp edges.  It is so small that you won't be able to smoke a decent sized piece of meat. You may be able to do a couple of chicken breasts or pork chops, but that's about it.  There is a grate that fits over the basket, which would allow you to cook a somewhat larger piece of meat, but it doesn't fit unless you keep the basket inside, which cramps the wood chips.  This is contrary to the instruction manual, which really doesn't give many instructions.  It just shows diagrams of the cooker.  It would be nice to have a few recipes of cooking suggestions.  This item is definitely not up to Charbroil's normal standards.

Nice pan but its so small that its useless for anything but to throw some veggies in. For a family of four like ours, that's really even pushing it.I was so disappointed with this because I was really looking forward to using it. It would be great if it was just bigger.

This device is nothing more than a pan and is not something I would use often.  I had Charbroil's Inferred grill and that was a big mistake.  This continues the mistake on a Weber.  Inferred to Charbroil is nothing but a pan between the flames to eliminate the flame.  Wow, now there is a concept.  It is all hype as far as I am concerned and not too useful.  Use a low priced pyrex roaster or a low metal pan and you will get the same thing for much less and probably much easier to clean and store.  This probably won't burn through as fast as the Charbroil grill.  I was skeptical and my fears were confirmed.  Sorry, I find it a dumb product which is not needed.  It is in the garage already.  Like the Beatles sang "I should have known better".

I looked forward to receiving this item but my hopes were pretty much dashed when I opened the box.First of all, it is very cheaply made with rough metal edges.  I didn't find any that were sharp enough to cut me but the potential is there.  What is with the lid not having a handle of any kind?  Be prepared to use a spatula or fork to clumisly remove the lid when you want to check your food.  As far as I'm concerned that is a big omission.Inside the unit, don't expect to cook large volumes.  The inside is big enough for one steak or two petite cuts.  Two or three chicken breasts will fill this one to capacity.  If you're thinking of smoking a small roast, it better be pretty small.  A boneless pork loin might fit but most likely you will need to cut off one end or cut it in half.Charbroil does include some wood chips with the infusion cooker so you won't need to run out to buy some to try this out.  Following directions and putting them in the proper place it seemed I needed to heat my grill to a temperature higher than I normally use.  Plus getting 4 big burners going to cook with this unit is quite a drain on the propane vs. the achieved results.My test food was a thick, stuffed pork chop which barely fit in the cooking chamber.  Keeping all four burners going at about 3/4 capacity I was able to achieve a good tastiing meal.  There was some smoke flavor but not near as much as if I were to use either my electric smoker or scatter wood chips above the burners.  it did however seem to keep the pork chop moister than if cooked directly on the grill for a longer period of time (infusion?).In conclusion, I'll keep this around and perhaps use it every now and then when grilling just for myself but it is far from being my favorite tool to use on the grill.  It is hampered by being cheaply made, inconvenient to use (no handle on lid for example), a marginal design and small interior space.
summary: Not what I hoped it would be

reviewText: Okay, first of all, this is not a specialized smoker, something that seems to have surprised some other people.  It can add smoke flavor, but if you want truly smoked foods, this isn't going to deliver what you are looking for.It's best purpose in my opinion is to add functionality to your propane grill.  It's basically a pan that serves to help control the heat better.  Is it something that you will use every single time you get out your grill?  Probably not, unless fish and vegetables are the primary items hitting your grill.All in all, I'd say if you frequently do more than the typical brisket/burger/sausage kind of grilling, you may find this of use.  It's not huge, so it's not something you'd choose to use when feeding a crowd.  That also means it will fit on smaller propane grills or into your dishwasher.  The grate-like inner pan will allow you to easily manage those veggies, seafood, etc.This isn't something every outdoor cook is going to love or need.  It's not made out of stainless steel to last a lifetime either.  It is an additional tool to make your cook outs a bit more interesting than just scorching some hot dogs though.
summary: Great addition for the grilling family

reviewText: If you have a wood fire or charcoal, you'll already have a nice flavor from your heat source, especially if you're using wood. You can just as easily grill on that, or on skewers, without adding fats. If you want to smoke it with a wood fire, you will treat some of the wood with water, soaking over time, so it burns slowly and smokes, creating less heat and more smoke to get that flavor. This little thing basically does what the wood fire already can, or in some cases, that the coal fire can. So basically, if you have wood or coal, this product is unnecessary.IF you have a propane grill, then this is useful, though very small.
summary: only makes sense if you use propane

reviewText: This is over all, a good product. The Char-Broil Cooker is and does what it claims. It smokes and roast anything you can fit in it. The only negative to this product for me is its size, as you can not fit alot of meat in this cooker. If you are looking to smoke more than a whole chicken you may need more than one of these smokers. It is perfect for smoking a chicken, it fits one whole chicken perfect and it cooks great. If you are cooking for two it is perfect. It fits on most any grill and works great.

I love grilling.  And since I live near a place that makes the most awesome brats I've ever had (cajun, garlic, onion, etc), I spend a lot of time on my grill.  That being said, I'm a simple eater.  I like meats and potatoes and veggies, especially when I'm grilling.  Simple things that are quick and easy to do.And while I love throwing onions, mushrooms, peppers, and such on shishkabobs, tending them (especially in winter) gets to be a bit of a pain to keep them from getting too dried out or blackened around the edges.  So I thought this would be a handy thing to try.For those looking into this, there's a video on youtube showing it in use, both with liquid and with the wood chips.  And their website has an online recipe page for things like pork, shrimp, salmon, and chicken.First thing I liked - no more flareups.  No more rushing out there when I hear the juice from something sizzling on the burners in case it was greasy enough to be flammable (lost count of how many "fireballs" I've had opening the top of my grill when doing some brats).  The second, it really did help things cook evenly.  I played with some beer in the bottom, I tried a marinade, even did the wood chips as well, though I only put in a few since I didn't want to overdo it by putting in too many...  I'll have to experiment a bit to see what ends up tasting the best.  But everything I've done so far has turned out better than I had hoped.So it does work, but the size is limiting for many people.  I live alone with my 9 year old son, so the size works for us, but for larger numbers, it can be limiting.  Not very expensive though, and easy enough to buy two if you really need to give yourself some more room.
summary: It works, but as others have said, it's small

reviewText: Many Americans have a grill, though far fewer have a smoker.  It makes sense most of the time, but there are times where a smoker is the way to go.  What's one to do if they don't want the expense, hassle, and space commitment of a smoker?  Well leverage their grill.I've tried various smoker boxes (spoiler alert: they work better than this btw) as well as a few improvisations, and I had high hopes for this.  It had its own sealed (kinda) box, a place for wood chips, and the promise of simplicity.  Well simplicity is a double edged sword, as it lacks any kind of thermometer (no biggie, as many are lacking anyway), limited space (a bit more of a challenge), a lousy grill (well that's a bigger problem), and lastly no real handle for the lid (how did that happen?).  All in all it's not too practical or safe.  It's sad, as it has promise.  Build a bigger box, give it a handle, and a better grill, and well it may work.Please look elsewhere, you'll be better served.

Reading the description, which reads "Enjoy healthy, Infrared cooking on any grill or campfire.".  I mistakenly thought this had an infrared heater built into it as most items listed as 'infrared' do.  It does not.  This is basically a steam box or smoker box that sits on your grill.  I'm still not sure how the infrared aspect comes into it as it is a light spectrum radiation.Anyway, that said, I did find the quality of it to be very good.  We've used it several times on our gas grill and it has cooked perfectly.  Char-broil has apparently done some research and provides perfect ventilation for the food.  I'll continue to use it for a smoke box, but an occasional beer in the bottom provides a good steam for chicken.As long as you realize there is no infrared emitter inside of it, you should be fairly happy with it.
summary: Not 'infrared' in the traditional sense. This is basically a steamer/smoke box

reviewText: This cooker seems to be constructed pretty well--hard to tell until I use it longer and see how long it lasts.  It works just like it should--which is easy because it doesn't really do anything but hold food!It is pretty small, however.  That isn't a bad thing, just read the description for the size and make sure it is big enough to hold what you plan to put in it.Also, it is packaged in a cheap, plain cardboard box, which isn't bad at all unless you plan to give it as a gift.  Then, the box makes it look kind of cheap.Anyway, for what this costs, it is okay, just small.
summary: Is what it says it is

reviewText: We used this Gronomics GBO1Q Cedar Garden Bed Oil on the fencing around our garbage can enclosure and are quite happy with the results. Here are my observations:- Cap is very hard to remove+ Very thick+ Applies easily but is messy+ Strong, not unpleasant odor that fades fairly quickly+ Looks great when applied correctly- Somewhat priceyThis is a good solution for treating outside cedar wood.Recommended!CFH
summary: Works Well For My Needs - Recommended

reviewText: I used this oil on a small part of my fence and the results are very good.  But the small part I did absorbed quite a bit as it was very dry.  Immediately I'm concerned that I don't have enough and the product is quite expensive.

Although you may find its price and application process a bit frustrating, this Gronomics product is a prudent choice for at least two important reasons.* It is a blend of vegetable and citrus oils, all of which are safe if they come in contact with your food. Until I found out about this product, I'd resigned myself to the "gently weathered" look for all of our wooden planting barrels and raised beds. This healthy choice led to periodic and perennial frustration, because between sun and rain and year-round use, our tubs and beds took a beating that required repair and replacement.* This product is developed and distributed by the manufacturer of a line of upscale cedar garden planters. Thus, it stands to reason that this formula has been created to add to the appearance and performance of cedar planters and tested to ensure that it does provide protection and does not have long-term negative effects on the wood.Application is pretty straightforward, as long as you budget for sufficient time and patience and have a couple of basic tools on hand. The tools I used were a sturdy nylon brush, a large rectangular plastic food container (similar to the semi-disposable Ziploc containers), and a 3-inch paint roller. Because the container and the roller sleeve came in contact with the Gronomics oil, I wanted to use items I could dry and discard safely and following combustibility guidelines. Here's how I prepped and treated a new raised Gronomics bed and a relatively new barrel planter.On the first day, I made a weak solution of Dawn dishwashing liquid and water, and used a sturdy nylon brush with grip handle to scrub my newly assembled Gronomics planting bed. I also emptied and hosed out my barrel planter, and took the extra step of rinsing the interior with boiling water before scrubbing the exterior with the soapy solution. I then rinsed both planters with a pressure washer to ensure all soap residue was removed.On the second day, working in a shaded area, I poured about an inch of oil into the food container and dipped my paint roller into it. I applied two light coats rather than a single heavy coat to reduce drips and spills. I also portioned out relatively small amounts of oil to avoid wastage; same for using a roller with relatively low nap.I applied a coat to the inside of the Gronomics bed, just below the level to which I planned to fill it with dirt. However, I left the interior of my barrel untreated so I would be able to compare its rate of weathering to that of the treated exterior of the barrel.

This really livened up the look of my weathered cedar planters. Although they are only a year old, spending all that time in the sun didn’t do wonders for my poor cedar’s complexion. Since they are used for herbs, I didn’t want to use traditional stain or waterproofing. This product fit the bill very well.Application is the same as with any stain. Just clean the surface first, then apply with a brush or rag. I went for the rag approach since the consistency is rather runny and a rag seemed to offer the best chance of limiting a mess in the garage.It really livens up the look of weathered cedar. It’s not as good looking as it was when new, but the difference is very nice. Wish I had applied this earlier to stave off the weathering.There are two big downsides: cost and smell. The cost is prohibitive for laying in a supply that’s enough to treat a large raised bed. As it is, I went through about 1/4 of the bottle for just one planter. There’s no way I would be willing to spend the money to get a gallon of this stuff. The other issue is the smell. I applied it in a garage since the weather was not all that great, but next time this is definitely going to be an outdoor project. Not nose friendly!Works well and is certainly worth a look for small-scale applications.
summary: Makes cedar look great, but costly and very smelly to apply

reviewText: I value any natural wood products I have and like to oil them a couple of times a year.  For example, even my oak kitchen cabinets get the once over spring and fall and they look as good as new fifteen years after installation.  A simple upgrade of the hardware kept them from looking like something I purchased in the dark ages.  The same holds true for garden beds or any wooden furniture you might have.One of my neighbors sunk some wooden railroad-like beams into the ground many years ago without oiling them.  They have warped, splintered and look terrible.  I’m not about to tell him that they look rather offensive because I’m sure he knows that.  Hindsight is the best kind of sight, but being proactive is what I prefer to be.FEATURES:►  Food contact safe►  Easy to use on all cedar garden products►  Preserves and minimizes drying and cracking►  Specially formulated with enhanced UV protectionAny kind of oil is pricey, but I do like the Gronomics blend of oils.  I’ve tried it on a few different types of wood and have been pleased with the results.  FYI, the oil that I use on my kitchen cabinets is a citrus oil blend.  This type refreshes the wood and keeps it from drying out and that’s why no one ever guesses that my cabinets are so old.  They are, but they aren’t if you know what I mean.I like the way this oil is absorbed into wood, cedar or not.  It is specifically, however, made for cedar gardens.  It would work quite well for any raised garden beds that you wish to put into the ground this upcoming spring.  Are you asking yourself why you should spend the extra money to protect your expensive garden beds, but my question to you would be why not?  If you wish to check out the Gronomics cedar beds I’ve made a list of them below.GRONOMICS:Gronomics REGB 24-48 24-Inch by 48-Inch by 30-Inch Rustic Elevated Garden Bed, UnfinishedGronomics EGB 32-48 34-Inch by 48-Inch by 32-Inch Elevated Garden Bed, finishedGronomics VG3245 Vertical Garden Planter, 32-Inch by 45-Inch by 9-InchGronomics RPB 18 - 48 18-Inch by 48-Inch by 19-Inch Rustic Planter Box, UnfinishedGronomics GBDIK Garden Bed Drip with Irrigation KitGronomics MRGB-2L 48-48 48-Inch by 48-Inch by 13-Inch Modular Raised Garden Bed, UnfinishedGronomics Pergola PlanterGronomics Raised Garden Bed, unfinishedGronomics Bench Planter
summary: Why not spend the extra money to protect your garden bed?

reviewText: I purchased this to paint my cedar raised gardens.  It seemed to have worked well and it goes a long way.

We use oil for our deck. I worry about using paints and stains because it is so near to where the cattle get water. But we do have to protect the wood since we have miserable winters. I had bought an "environmentally friendly non-toxic" stain but it did not last 4 months.This oil is perfect. It smells like oil but not as bad as many others.It just rubs on easily. I wear nitrile gloves  so my hands don't smell or get irritated. But it looks nice.

The lid is impossible.  I think the problem was the black seal on ours wasn't stable, so the whole lid turned.  It's very childproof.  It was adult proof too.  After I gave up trying, I gave it to my quite capable DYI hubby to open.  He was working on a toilet tank at the time, but gave it 5 minutes then started cussing.  I was afraid I'd get popped with an elbow if the thing flew off.  After 10 minutes he said "We're just going to have to cut this thing off, get me a knife. I'd give it a 1 star just because of that lid if I were you"I didn't want to keep frustrating him, so I took it in the kitchen and got a knife.  I cut down into the 2 child safe rings, but it still wouldn't unscrew, because the black seal turned around too, and there wasn't anything to use vise grips on to hold it.  I was ready to just stab the can to get the oil out, but stabbed the black seal instead, and that let me unscrew it.  What a pain!The oil itself says it is a vegetable based oil with citrus.  It smells like oranges and lemons, but maybe those oils were not cold pressed- I smell a hint of a solvent in it, or perhaps the oil is a bit rancid, but it is supposed to be all natural.  It smells fairly nice when on the wood.It's fairly thick- it reminds me of olive oil, it seems to get thicker and cloudier when cold and absorbs into a paper towel like that.  I don't see the ingredients listed so I'm not sure.  It slightly darkens the wood, and then water repels off.  The wood smells nice and looks new.  I used it on my garden bench, and it looks new again, and hopefully it will help it last longer.  The wood absorbed the oil well, and I rubbed my elbow across it- it did not stain my cotton shirt.  I probably would not sit on it with white pants or shirt on for a while, but with it being winter, that's not going to happen anyway.I only have one bed- a salad table, and it made it look nice, again, darkening the wood a bit and giving it a soft 'new' gleam.They need to do something about that horrid lid design if they can though.
summary: We couldn't get the lid off!

reviewText: I have a small cedar planting bed that I built myself. Granted it was not a very complicated project but I did have the foresight to use bolts, rather than nails, to fasten it together. Wanting to prolong the life of the wood and worry about adding toxic chemicals to my small harvest caused me to select this product.After taking out the bolts it was easy to apply the oil to every square inch of the wood. I used a rag which gave me more control than a brush, but I also wore gloves to protect my skin. And, I don't like leaving flammable products around, so I was determined to use the entire contents of the can, and did. I ended up putting about two coats on my six by three foot rails. I used the product outdoors and followed the cautions noted on the can about proper handling and disposal of rags used with the oil.Again, following the instructions on the can, I first washed the boards with a mild soapy solution of one teaspoon soap to a gallon of water (I used Simple Green soap) and allowed a day for drying. Next I applied the first coat of oil, let it soak in for fifteen minutes and then wiped-off the excess. I allowed another day for the oil to dry and then applied the final coat repeating the instructions used for the first coat.After visiting the website I did not find any additional information on the product. Specifically,, I was seeking guidance regarding how much coverage could be expected for each quart can, but I suspect no information was provided because the condition of each board will dictate how much oil will be necessary, so this will vary from project to project.I like the idea of a food-grade oil but am not crazy about the flammable nature of this product, so I will probably seek out something less volatile next time, likeVahalla Wood Preservatives 470-112 1-Gallon Eco Friendly Non Toxic Lifetime Wood Treatment Pouch.

I really do like this product. It to me is a better alternative to Thompson's Water Seal or Other Petroleum Based Products. It is very potent, goes well and really soaks into the wood. It seems to be standing up to the elements well. Like most natural products I do suspect that it will need more periodic applications than some synthetic formula. However I wish is was more economical. It costs so much for a single can that will only do one or two garden beds depending on the condition and species of wood. Price is quite high.4 Stars for Quality, 1 removed for cost.
summary: Does a Great Job, Is Natural, But Pricey

reviewText: This was easy to apply on the garden bed, right after we assembled it.  It was easy to apply and seems to be protecting it well.  We did two coats, but still had a lot of oil left over, so we also used it on a section of our cedar privacy fence as well.It goes on easily, soaks in, and seems to protect well.  Once dry it looks good.
summary: Works great on the garden, and used the extra on our fence.

reviewText: We have several cedar planting beds near our back yard deck.  We live in a harsh climate so we're already accustomed to treating all of our outdoor wood as well as taking care when purchasing so that what we get will survive our long cold winters and hot muggy summers.This product is a more natural choice, and although it has a VERY strong odor like many other products of this type, it is intended for outdoor use and the odor decreases.  We preferred this to petroleum-based products, and kept it in a safe location as it is flammable.We plan tomatoes in our beds so we wanted something that is safe to apply to the wood.  It has UV protection and over time will keep the wood from drying and cracking.If you've ever bought something from Wilson's Leather, you know that they will always try to sell you Wilson's leather conditioner that costs about $15.  However, you can get the same type of product for 1/3 that price.  This oil is made for the Gronomincs cedar beds, but it's not quite the same deal as Wilson's.  Although you do have a high price point to this cedar garden bed oil, it is the only 'natural' oil we found.  So you have to decide if, like everything else out there that is 'natural' or 'healthy', you want to pay more.\

My favorite feature is the 30 minute watering.  You just press the button and it waters for 30 minutes.  My neighbors think its pretty amazing.  I bought it because I knew I would go insane after a bunny or squirrel takes my hard work.  This thing sees motion and sprays.  Excellent build quality, and and all around awesome garden necessity.  I did end up replacing the head on top, it was designed for a much larger garden.  I bought a 6 dollar sprinkler head that was not going to shoot as far.  Excellent purchase, highly recommend.

If you can't have an 8-foot deer fence, this is the best way to protect your plants from deer, rabbits, squirrels, and other plant-grazers.  Stinky chemicals have to be purchased, reapplied, and ruin the fragrance of your garden. This method simply uses water and runs on 4 AA batteries all season. This is the way to go.For the past two years, we have used theContech CRO101 Scarecrow Motion Activated Sprinklerto keep deer out of our flower beds. It did keep the deer away, but with a few drawbacks. The biggest disadvantage was that it was on all the time.  After my husband received a faceful of water while dressed in a suit and on his way to work, he became so concerned about inadvertent drenchings that he turned it off.  After all, showering your neighbors or their children who come into the yard to look at your tulips is not good for your reputation.  Also, the sensor didn't seem to work reliably.The Yard Enforcer solves the inadvertent drenching problem with a dial that gives you the option to operate it in daytime, nighttime or always.  Perfect!  The infrared motion sensor recognizes movement (people or animals) at about 30 feet, day or night.  The sprinkler is forceful and has very good range.  Unlike that of the Scarecrow, the ground spike is sturdy metal. Orbit has taken an effective concept and improved it.Tulip Munchers, beware!  The Yard Enforcer is on the job!UPDATE: We have a beautiful bed of 400 tulips in front of our house. People stop to photograph the flowers. Without Yard Enforcer, we would have NO tulips. It works!

I have various motion-sensing watering devices and they all work well.  This one works well and is built well.  And it seems to be able to hit up to 40' away, farther than my other two devices made by two other companies, and as advertised.I placed this device near my strawberry patch, the last place in my garden that the dogs haven't yet dug up.  While my younger shepherd is persistent at digging, this device does shoo her away.  She loves water, but she doesn't like it sprayed at her in a loud fashion.I can't speak for deer or elk since we don't have those in our 'hood, but it definitely keeps dogs and cats out of the area.

I generally like this self-contained yard defense sprinklers (have their own water supply and don't need to be hooked up to a hose) because the kind of hook up to the hose seem to have a lot of problems with leakage etc. But I have to say that I like the Orbit yard and force are a lot. First off I think it feels a little bit more sturdy than a lot of other units in its price range. For instance a lot of units have a plastic spike you jam in to the ground where is this sprinkler has a metal one and it really secures it and keeps it from coming loose. And just in general this thing feels like it has some longevity built-in.I think is this price point this might be one of the best ones you can buy. Now would like to point out that I generally would encourage people to get the self-contained units that have solar power and their own water basin. Just generally because I think it's easier to move around and put them where you need them and then not having to worry about running the hose which will affect your grass. So something to keep in mind but those units generally are about $100 more than this one.Thanks for reading!
summary: I like the one more that the Havaheart I used.

reviewText: This unit performs relatively well. Construction is solid, with a well-painted metal stake, brass connections, and the ability to daisy chain these sprinklers . The battery pack uses four AA batteries, I have had good luck with rechargeable NiMh cells.The night/day/anytime spray settings are a nice touch, i.e. you can set this unit up to only go after skunks and bunnies and ignore the postman by virtue of the postman not showing up when it's dark. I currently have a skunk upending my yard even in the early morning so the unit has to be set to 'always' for now.The rotating head can be set to stay inside a sector (i.e. swing back and forth) or just spin around in one direction. I've elected to use the latter setting since the sprayer can get 'stuck', i.e. not reverse direction, as intended.I'm not delighted by the limited range of the sensor for smaller, slow-moving pests like skunks that don't move quickly. The sensor (even on the most sensitive setting) has a very hard time detecting them. Other pests like squirrels that are more jumpy set it off more reliably. Large animals like deer, etc. should set it off as reliably as humans do (to the great delight of our kids playing with it).Despite the 'solid' construction, ours failed after just one year of use - the valve no longer closes, even with fresh batteries. The thing was never outside in cold conditions, the batteries are fresh, so I'm at a loss what would cause the vale to fail open.
summary: Don't expect miracles, especially with skunks

reviewText: Deer have eaten my wife's favorite plants. Squirrels are one of the slyest creatures on earth and keeping them away from the bird food is quite a challenge. A beautiful red fox visits on occassion but I am not sure for what purpose. Anyway, when presented with the opportunity to get this alleged pest deterrent it was an offer I coud not refuse. My wife would be happy, my dog would bark less and life would be better.Read the manual and went out to the front yard to give this a go. Could not get it to work. Water leaked out of various parts of the unit but none out of the sprinkler part where it is intended to spray. There are more knobs, dials and wheels to turn then would be in the cockpit of a 747 airplane. I tried turnng them all but to no avail as far as water out of the sprinkler part. The base part that is inserted into the ground is made of metal and is easily set in the ground. That is the only part that worked for me. This takes 4 AA batteries and there appears to be a light in the portion that holds the battery pack. I could not make it light up. This has been a total failure in every respect including yours truly.There is a sheet that is 11" x 17" that contains usage instructions. I read it from end to end at least 4 or 5 more times but could get nothing to work. I noticed that there are three other reviews and they are all satisfied with this product and it apparently works for them. That leads me to conclude that either I have a defective unit or I am missing the big picture. In either case, I am through with this gadget and into recycle it goes. I have changed my attitude as a result of this hassle. Pests, especially squirrels, deer and fox are now welcomed to my yard and can stay as long as they wish to do so.

What is in the box?Sprinkler systemWhat is not in the box?4 AA BatteriesConstructionSolid and sturday black construction with a metal stake.  There is a motion detector that is integrated into the system serving as the sensory mechanism.  Powered by AA batteries, this works for about 6 months.  I have it in the perimeter of the other side of my property to keep the skunks, raccoon and deer away.  The sensor has great sensitivity which is as long as the spray distance.SetupAside from deciding upon where to place this, the setup only requires placing in the batteries and attaching a hose.  That's it.You have the option of running this during the day, night or 24 hours continuous.The main problem is having a hose near where it needs to be set up.EffectivenessIt keeps critters away without the use of harmful chemicals or cumbersome spraying units.Two thumbs up.

I had this set up in a snap. It works well on the squirrels but because of the way my garden is they can still bypass it and a few of them have figured it out. The unit is well built and sturdy. I have started to get leaking problems in this intense heat but I think it's more of a hose issue.
summary: Worked OK. The squirrles will always find a way around it

reviewText: 1.  Metal push in stake - similar item from another manufacturer has plasic, making it hard to use in hard clay or rocky soil.2.  Ability to connect 2 other regular sprinklers and have all 3 turned on by the sensor for better coverage.3.  Can be used as a regular overhead sprinkler.4.  Can be set for day, night, or any time to prevent getting your head soaked on accident as you enter the area.The box says the batery will last up to 7500 cycles.  This spring will be the test.  I intend to use this in an attempt to keep the armadillos out of my garden.I will update my review after I have used the product for awhile.
summary: Better Design Than Ones I've Used Previously

reviewText: I bought a cheap hose to use this with since I was going to put it in one spot not far from the spicket and not move it - wrong answer - it busted within a week.  There's no release valve and the pressure builds up.It's a nice unit- very sturdy and much better than a competitors that I've tested and used, and well worth the 30 dollar difference as the motion controller works much better.There's a little device called a tethercell that I'm looking forward to getting for this - it will let you turn battery operated devices on with your smartphone.  That would make this 100x even better, because as it is, I'm getting blasted myself when I go into the area it is protecting.It's working ok.  It comes on so fast that it scares me!  The chickens aren't going near it now after one week.  I've still got the feral cats going in this area though, because the catnip is getting eaten and rolled in.
summary: Great unit, but some sort of pressure release would be nice

reviewText: I have constant problems with deer, elk, and various critters that eat my bushes and plants.  I have found these units to be one of easiest and most effective ways to deal with the problem, and accordingly I have surrounded critical parts of my house with them.  This is a nice heavy unit that works well.  Recommended!

Between the fruit on my fruit trees and the fish in my pond, I've taken major hits over the years from the neighborhood critters. This unit not only gives me a fighting chance, but is humane in that it scares the critters and maybe gets them wet, but doesn't injure or kill them. And it works! I have it set for night around my pond. I bought another one which I'll set for daytime to frighten off the squirrels around my fruit trees. So far, it's proven infinitely adjustable and reliable.
summary: NOW I HAVE A FIGHTING CHANCE

reviewText: After fighting with the deer and the rabbits for several years and trying to keep them away from our flowers and shrubberies, we tried a cheaper "scarecrow" type of sprinkler.  Sometimes it worked, sometimes it didn't.  It helped some but was very inconsistent.  We decided to step up our defense with the Orbit 62100 Yard Enforcer Motion Activated Sprinkler.  I am happy to report, so far so good!!!  All flowers and shrubberies (in range) are in tact.  I also love that multiple sprinklers can be connected.  We haven't used it as a pure "sprinkler" setup and am not sure if we ever will.  It just works too well as a critter deterent to mess with the success.  We currently have it in a location so that it isn't set off unknowingly by ayone such as mailman, ups delivery, etc., so we haven't used the timer function either.  It's nice to know it's available if we decide to move it or purchase additional units in the future to cover other more "traveled" parts of the yard in the future.  OH -- one more bonus is that my neighbor's cat no longer uses the flower bed as his litter box!!! Yahoo!!!!  He hasn't moved to an area in the yard yet that isn't covered by this sprinkler, so we're set until he figures that out.  Once he does, we will probably purchase another unit.  The one time I saw his reaction when he got drenched was totally priceless!!!  I just wish I had also set up a motion activated video camera for that!!!

These are great! We have kept cats from going to the bathroom under our in ground tramp.  We have kept deer from eating all of our bushes, and we have used it to keep deer off of our swimming pool cover.We have 3 of these and keep them around our yard.  There is a delayed spray time, but if you have it aimed in the place that you do not want the animals, they quickly learn.  These used to go off all the time, but now the animals are trained to go somewhere else.Additionally, our kids love to play in these.  Because of the delayed spray, they never know when they are to go off.  We used this for 3 months, and it is still going strong.  I would highly recommend it.
summary: This is a must have for keeping wild life from your yard!

reviewText: I have used several of these type of products.  So far, this seems like the best constructed. I particularly appreciate the metal spike. It has worked well against deer in my yard.The real test this year will be the birds however.  I really need to keep them from eating my blueberries.  No product so far has been successful.  I cannot comment yet on this so I will add an addendum but I am not optimistic.This goes together easily and I had no trouble understanding how it works.There is one issue however that I would warn people about.  It isn't the devices fault but is an issue with this type device that you must be aware of.  The hose is under pressure at all times.  It sits in the hot sun.  Every hose I have used so far has eventually burst.  They all have a warning about this.  It is a disaster every time because the water runs and runs.  In my case, with a well, I eventually lose water entirely.  You need to have a high enough quality hose that won't burst.  So far, I haven't seen one without a warning.. The warning says not to keep constant pressure.  Since  you need to do this with this device, I am wondering if anyone out there (or the manufacturer) has any suggestions.The alternative is the sprayer that has its own reservoir.
summary: Very good product but some concerns

reviewText: I've gotten a bit testy when it comes to my garden issue. We have a terrible cat problem in the neighborhood, but the positive is... no mice.The cats tend to use my raised garden beds and my children's sandbox as their liter box. Which just irratates me. I got a few Havahartt traps last year and caught a group of them, but they seemed to have wised up to the traps. FYI: I am by no means cruel to the cats. I have a live and let live philosophy. Therefore I catch and release, just not back within city limits. If they want to breed, let them feed and breed elsewhere, just not in my neighborhood.The Enforcer Motion Activated Sprinkler works very nicely and gets them before they get to my raised beds.The sprinkler has a dual purpose... first, it is security for protecting your garden. Second, it is an active sprinkler with a timed setting as well. So, it's a pretty smart design.Very satisfied with this one and plan on picking up a few more for other areas we plan on installing more raised garden beds.
The way this is designed, the brushes get in between the bars and into nooks and crannys. It makes cleaning your grill much easier. Be careful as the brushes are sharp and will stick you!!

I've had a lot of grill brushes as most of you grillers have had. This just works better than the square ones with the wires. The curved edges really get in there and get all the baked on stuff off those grates. Very glad I got this!

reviewerName: C. Beard "I have not gone where I intended to...
reviewText: I have tried them all and this design just doesn't cut the mustard. I have recently moved to grill stones that work a lots better.  This brush is built better than others I've tried but they just don't do a great job.

This is an OK way to clean the grill and Im satisfied with it but I would have used my old one if I had seen this in person before ordering. Theres nothing wrong with it but there are a few things I would have done differently.
summary: ... an OK way to clean the grill and Im satisfied with it but I would have used my old ...

reviewText: One of the best grill brushes i've ever used. It's very well made and durable. I wish the design had a scraper though. That would be my only complaint.

This is a nice, study brush that does a good job cleaning our Weber grill. The brush bristles seem to fit the grill grid perfectly and thus clean quickly and easily. I am glad I purchased it. It works much better than other grill brushes I have used.
Price is right and this little brush really cleans the grill surface fast and easy.  This doesn't look like it's going to wear out anytime soon.
summary: Sturdy and quickly cleans the grill

reviewText: Like every Weber item I have ever owned, this one is quality and does what it should. One thing to keep in mind, talking to Weber, is that it's best to clean the grates prior to cooking instead of after cooking.  Also, remember to drizzle your food (not the grates) with olive oil prior to cooking. Happy grilling!
I like using but not anymore than my other ones.  I do like the shorter handle.  I'll keep using it though because it does work.Fast delivery.  I was very pleased.  Thank you.
Used this to clean out the ashes from my WSM 22.5 and works perfectly!!  It is a must have for all people who are smoking.
This came in handy when removing the ash from the bottom of my Weber smoker.  Instead of leaning the bottom to plastic bag its less of a mess with this ash shovel.

Got this little shovel at a Nat'l Hardware Store! A nice item to have, cleans the ash out nice, but also serves as a pretty good tool to scoop up a meat loaf off the grill or other hard to handle food items. Slides right onto the serving plate.
A really great idea, it makes scooping out the the ash & residue from a WSM a snap.  Should be equally good on a Weber Kettle
summary: Makes cleaning a WSM a snap

reviewText: I use this all the time to get coals out of my Weber Smokey Mountain or my older Weber Kettle.  It works well and is well made.  If you want to save money, just wait for the coals to go out overnight and then use a plastic 1/2 gallon milk jug with the bottom cut out.  That's what I used for years until I received this as a gift.  Much better way to go.

I am overly safety conscious with my backyard BBQ grills and smokers, all Webers.  We had a neighbor once who put used charcoal ash they thought was cold in their trash can.  Unfortunately a few of the coals were still hot and the resulting fire caused their garage to go up in flames.  I use my grills and smokers constantly, year round, so to avoid any such issues I tend to let my charcoal ashes build up in my equipment until I know the ashes are cold and not a fire hazard.To avoid the ash buildup I purchased a Behrens 6 gallon galvanized trash bucket with lid to keep with my grilling/smoking equipment.  It was a bit of a pain getting the ash out of the grills and smoker into the galvanized bucket.  I needed an easy way to remove the ash.  I purchased the Weber Ash Shovel and it works beautifully.  I can easily scoop out the ash, put it in the galvanized bucket.  The lid helps smother any sneaky hot coals, then I dump the cool ash in the trash can on garbage day.  I just keep the ash shovel in the bucket and it use it when needed.The Weber shovel is not absolutely necessary but it is an effective and convenient addition to my outdoor kitchen setup.

I had the full size chimney starter and ran into issues of not needing to fill it up all the way when using the bbq grill.  This is a great fix for that so the charcoal sits overtop of one another to burn more in a stack than the bigger version.
The full size chimney was too big when lighting the 10 coals needed when using the Minion method.  This works perfectly.
summary: Great When Using the Minion Method

reviewText: I use a Big Green Egg for smoking and was looking for a quick way to ignite a small amount of charcoal to add to the remaining charcoal in the pit. I owned a generically-branded chimney starter for over 20 years that finally rusted out. I wanted to replace it with a smaller one, and this Weber was the perfect size. Surprisingly, this size was not available in Home Depot or Lowes.Simply fill it 3/4 full with your choice of charcoal (lump or briquette), stuff some old advertising circulars in the bottom, and you'll have lit coals in just a few minutes, ready to pour on top of the existing ones. I put the chimney on top of the grate, but you can also put it directly on top of the coals and then ignite the paper. Just make sure that there is a way for air to circulate underneath the chimney in order to create the necessary flow of air (draft) to ignite the coals.If you buy a chimney starter, regardless of size, here's a tip on how to make sure you get hot coals in the shortest time. Roll the paper into a donut shape and then put it in the bottom. That will insure that there is sufficient air and draft at the very beginning of the process to light the coals.Let's eat!

There is no better way to start charcoal briquettes or lump charcoal than this. Forget the crumpled up newspaper. Try the Weber starter cubes.Weber 7417 FireStarters Lighter Cubes, 24 CountOne is all that is necessary, and you will have charcoal ready to go in 15-20 minutes!
