There is a built-in dial thermometer in my BGE, but I have no way of knowing whether it's accurate or not since they have a reputation for being inaccurate, sometimes by as much as 50 to 100 degrees. By using one of the dual probes to monitor the BGE internal oven temperature and the other to keep track of the meat, chicken or pork, I know exactly what needs to be done to maintain the temperature as well as when the meal is cooked.Many of you who are experienced BBQers know that there is often the famous "stall" that happens when cooking low and slow. It will look like the meat has reached a certain temperature and won't go any higher, even though it will if you're just patient and leave it be. That means that it is difficult to cook by time alone on any smoker, including a BGE. With the second probe monitoring the meat, you can watch it hit the stall point and then confidently wait while the meal continues to cook and it reaches the correct internal temperature.The probes are easy to use and set-up. The oven temperature gauge attaches to the wire grill with a special clip. The other control inserts into the meat exactly the way any internal cooking gauge does. You'll need to read the instructions to understand how to pair them and that each button means, but it took me all of 5 minutes to unravel the whole thing. I admit that I'm good with technical things, but this really isn't a difficult item to master.Now that I have this product, I can't imagine cooking without it. I think it gives me much more control over both the oven temperature and making sure the meat is to the temperature I want for maximum tenderness. Highly recommended.
summary: Top notch item for BBQs and smokers

reviewText: I'm a big fan of wireless thermometers for the BBQ and smoker, and have been using the Oregon Scientific talking thermometer for years. However, this thermometer has an important and very useful feature: two temperature probes, so I can track the temp of both the meat and the smoker.That's a huge plus, especially when I'm using the smoker when it's cold out (such as now). Even though I use the smoker in an outdoor enclosed area to eliminate (as best as possible) the impact of the wind and wrap the smoker with an insulating jacket, temperature fluctuations are inevitable. I can now see the temp of the smoker itself so I don't have to guess as to whether it is keeping up with the heat loss due to the cold weather.As with any remote thermometer setup can be a bit fiddly. Getting the remote to pair with the receiver is always the sticking point, and this was no exception. If the process does not seem to work, I find that taking out the batteries and resetting it tends to do the trick. The probe jack also needs to be seated firmly - give it a good push and twist to make sure it's making good contact.Again as with any remote temp, the probes are the weak link. These appear to be decently made, but they are always the first point of failure (I'm on my third probe for the Oregon Scientific). To extend their life wash them carefully and don't immerse in water. So far these have worked fine - finger's crossed that will continue.It uses AA batteries for the receiver and transmitter which are included. No problems with range - I was able to maintain a connection when I was inside the house with the smoker outside without any drops.The numbers on the handheld units are clear and easy to read. It does not speak like the Oregon Scientific, but I've always found that to be a gimmick that gets annoying real fast. A simple display and beep is all that is needed.Very pleased with this. I'll update the review should there be any problems with the probe down the road.[Manufacturer provided product for review]
summary: Unique setup for smokers; more capable than the Oregon Scientific model

reviewText: I've had HORRIBLE luck with remote thermometers in the past.  Getting them to pair at all has always been a nightmare and keeping them paired is even harder.  And even when the base and the remote are paired, they have such a short range that there really isn't that much of a benefit.  Plus most of the remote BBQ thermometers that I've owned in the past don't have any functionality at the base unit itself:  The base unit just has a plug for the probe, but no readout.This Maverick Wireless remote is so much better though.Here are the things that I love so much about this device:* The range is incredible.  I carried this around the house with me to see if I could break the signal.  It worked in every room downstairs. It worked in every room upstairs.  It worked in my garage and it even worked in my front yard.  (I decided not to go any further, because I didn't want to interrupt the meal I was cooking.)* Two probes = two temps.  I never knew I needed this until now, but this is EXACTLY what a remote thermometer should tell you:  What's the internal temp of your meat and what's the  temp of the BBQ.  I've always babysat every piece of meat on my grill, because I'm afraid that if I walk away to use the bathroom or something the grill will flare up and I'll come back to an inferno.  Clipping that second probe onto the grill is a godsend.  The only other thing I could ask for is a camera.  :)* The remote and the base both have temperature displays.  That means I don't need to bring the remote unit back with me to the grill when I check on it.  I can leave it wherever I'm hanging out during the cook.Don't get me wrong, I still think it's best to just kick back and babysit whatever you're grilling.  But when I'm cooking something that takes a long time (like beer can chicken @ 20 min/lb), it's nice to be able to walk out to the garage or go back into the kitchen to prepare another course.I also love the meat temp chart that was included.  It's magnetic, so I put it on my fridge.This is definitely my new favorite remote BBQ thermometer.  I have three old ones that I can throw away now.I was provided this item for review.

One of the nicest things about having a wireless barbeque thermometer set is that it not only takes the guesswork out of barbecuing, but also insures that your guests will get something edible.  Frankly, I've been to more than one barbeque where the chicken, although charred on the outside, was practically raw on the inside.  The Maverick is particularly nice if you are into smoking.  Temperature control is essential if you smoke meats and if you don't have it, your meat may not turn out as wonderful as you expected.WHAT'S IN THE BOX:1.  Receiver unit2.  Transmitter unit3.  Detachable stainless steel food probe4.  Detachable stainless steel barbeque probe with clip5.  4 AAA batteries5.  Quick user guideSyncing or "registering" between the receiver and the transmitter is a four-step process that is relatively simple.  If you do for some reason lose contact between the receiver and transmitter, there is a "lost link alert" that will enable you to re-sync the units.  There is a magnetic meat temperature guide that came with my unit, but may not arrive with everyone's.  Simple USDA recommendations are listed below.Internal temperature of 145 ~  Beef~  Veal~  Lamb Steaks & Roasts~  FishInternal temperature of 160 ~  Egg Dishes~  Pork and Ground Beef~  Veal & LambInternal temperature of 165 ~  Turkey~  Chicken and Duck, Whole~  Chicken and Duck, Pieces & GroundThe user guide is quite clear and will assist you with a step-by-step setup, including visuals of both the receiver and transmitter features, something I've always found particularly helpful.  One of the most problematic features that people have with wireless barbecue thermometer sets are with the supposedly "defective" probes.  In reality, it usually is not the probe, but rather the way they are used.  The braided wire cannot be immersed in water, be exposed to flames, bent, or closed between grill lids.  As with anything, if you take proper care of it, the Maverick Wireless barbecue Thermometer Set should last more than a few barbecue seasons.Sample provided by the distributor.
summary: This is an excellent wireless BBQ thermometer set, especially if you are into smoking ...

reviewText: This thermometer has helped me pull of some excellent meals.  No more having to lift the lid to check if meat is done, no more cutting meat to check for doneness and no more guess work.After a few uses I tested the probes accuracy in an ice bath.  They read accurate.Set up was easy after reading instructions.  Reciever locks in fast.  Signal's range has been sufficient for my uses thus far.Battery life is great.  I am still on the original batteries and have used the units several times.  One smoke lasted 10 hours and batteries are still running.Extra Tip:I drilled two holes in my Weber kettle; one right above the top grate and one right above the coal grate (for smoking on the bottom grate). I then painted over the exposed  metal with high temp enamel paint.  I then put silicone grommets in them.  I run the wires through these holes so I don't have to worry about the lid damaging them.  Works like a charm.I highly recomend this set.

My wife purchased me a smoker/grill for Christmas but for anyone getting a new hobby, you have to buy all sorts of accessories to go with it.  I've never owned a grill/smoker, so you can imagine her face when I dumped about $200 on accessories (charcoal, wood chunks, grill tools, this thermometer, bbq gloves, etc).  But because I want to do everything right, I had to get the aforementioned accessories.  You may ask "most grills have temperature gauges built in don't they?" But the rule of thumb of most people who BBQ will tell you those things are garbage and never have an accurate temperature.According to various BBQ forums, there are better dual-probe thermometers out there but this one is the best one under $65 by various websites. What I particularly like about this is the ability to check the temperature of the grill AND the temp of the meat you're cooking.  For checking cooking temps, a nice metal clip attaches to your grill and you insert the probe into it. The temperatures are accurate after testing and functionality is great. Not only can you check temp, but you can set an alarm as well check temps in the dark with a built-in light on the receiver. Wireless works pretty good. Haven't tested it's limits but typically where I stay while things are on the grill, it works excellent for me.The grill probe is shorter than the meat probe, so keep that in mind when you're trying to find a place to put the thermometer. The only complaint I have about this item is that the wire stand that the thermometer sits on always seems to tip over (especially on a windy day). I kinda wish this item was heavier, but it's not that big of a deal.Also, the Amazon reviews for this item seem hit or miss (mainly at the failure of the device). After reading the BBQ forums, all I can say is READ THE INSTRUCTIONS. According to other reviews, this item is highly susceptible to damage when wet, so don't immerse it in water (ESPECIALLY THE PROBES). Not sure how it performs in rain, but make sure the probes and the jacks stay dry. Also, make sure your probes don't have any kinks, as this can damage it as well.Highly recommended.
summary: Excellent Dual-Probe Thermometer - Never Mess Up Again

reviewText: Great little tool... if you smoke, you want this. I had made good food using my smoker's door thermometer and an old hanging oven thermometer and a digital probe that I had to go out to check. But with this, I realized I was running anywhere from 20-30 degrees too hot and I can monitor it from my lazyboy! Now I make great food... and it really makes it nice for longer smokes to have the alarms set in case you doze off. My smoker door blew open in a wintry gust the other day and had it not been for the alarm, it may have wasted an extra hour or more of smoking time. I have already recommended it to several friends
summary: Awesome little tool for smoking & the grill

reviewText: I just started smoking and not sure how you would do it without this. Sat in the house and waited for the alarm to ring to know I should attended the to the smoker.  Wires should come a little longer to accommodate further distance from the grill.

I only used it once so far so I cannot talk about durability. This baby made smoking a boston butt a piece of cake on my Weber Smokey Mountain.  I just read the directions and it worked! I ran the wires of the probes just under the lid of the smoker. Put one probe in the meat and the other on the top grate. Extremely accurate. Smoked the butt for 13 hours and had this thing  by my side.  Get one!

No instructions came with this bird feeder (I don’t know if that’s the norm), so I attempted to figure it out on my own. The top didn’t screw off like my other feeders, so I eventually removed the spring/wire thing that was holding the bottom in place, since that appeared to be the only other logical way to get seed into the feeder. I was able to pull the perch and hoods out of the way to pour the seed in, but I didn’t get very far. Once the level of the seed reached the feeder openings, bird seed was spilling out the sides. Then when I tried to put the bottom back, the spring/wire bent inward and lost its “spring” so it would not expand again to fill the slots that would cause it to hold the bottom in place. I gave up and transferred the seed to my other bird feeders. After this ordeal, I came to the product page to leave a review and saw that there was something that looked like instructions there. It's a diagram with a lot of numbers but no explanation as to what the numbers correspond to. So even if I hadn't just broken my feeder, I still wouldn't understand how to fill it.This may be squirrel-proof, because the perch hoods should keep the squirrels from being able to hang down and get into the feeder openings, and the perches are not wide enough for a squirrel to hang onto. Squirrels are pretty clever, though, so I can’t say for sure. And of course, I can’t test it, because my feeder is broken.
summary: Not impressed – couldn’t set it up

reviewText: This is a decent tube feeder , that hangs well from a feeder hook.  Being a tube feeder it is a little unwieldy when refilling it, but it is as easy as any other tube I've ever had.  It has gotten a good reception from birds, chickadees, cardinals and nuthatches as I use this for a sunflower feeder since the holes are a little big for Niger seed.But as much as I like the design, I'm a little disappointed by the materials used in its construction. The windows are a thin plastic, not glass. The metal is decent, but I would have rather had a finished texture like some of their other products.  The landing posts are decent although I have an issue with the bottom post slittping out of position when filling.Pros+ Good Design+ Bird approvedCons- Cheaper Quality plastic windows.- Bottom post tends to slide out.
summary: Decent Design, Holes a re little big for Niger, Windows are Plastic

reviewText: We are comparing this unit to 3 other feeders that we currently own in the backyard of Minnesota winter. If you kept up with the news it's been a cold one! We placed this side-by-side with two other similar style feeders and it is the most popular of the two right now (All three have the same feed). I believe the birds like it for the larger holes/access ports. The squirrels have left it alone (or gave up on it) as we haven't seen any on or attempting to gain access to the feeder. That being said they do sit underneath it and wait for the picky bird eaters to throw down the seeds they don't like. Smart little rodents. The colors and materials which are metal are quite nicely painted and coppered. The only part that concerns me tis the plastic sheeting windows. They seem a bit on the thin side, I am presuming so they can be bent to fit the curve of the feeder, but I question how long they will survive summer heat and winter cold. I will update the review should they ever wear out. For now they are holding strong and allow us to see when the feeder is getting low. Glass would be a nicer alternative but would likely drive up the price of the unit.The other part I don't care for, but I suspect is part of the squirrel retardant features is that the wire loop it hangs from creates a lot of movement when a feathered friend comes to land on one of the stems. The feeder rotates around the wire and spins at a moderate rate until resting again naturally. This doesn't seem to bother the smaller birds, but the jays and cardinals don't care for it and pick the older feeder that has a sold bracket and does not spin.Overall I am happy with this unit so far and would give it 4 stars.
summary: Nice option, Good to look at, a bit moving

reviewText: This metal outer bird feeder holds a decent amount and the "hoods" over the perches do keep squirrels from easily getting seed. Smaller birds took to it right away.  However, larger birds were able to perch and actually pulled out one of the rods.  I used a piece of tape to keep it from falling out for now. The inner tube is a rather flimsy plastic that doesn't seem like it will last that long especially since several birds were pecking in that area trying to get to the seed.  Would spend my money on a different feeder.

I don't know what they were thinking when they put this together. The top is either too tight to remove or else it falls off!When I got this feeder, I decided to fill it for the first time in my kitchen. I've found that when temperatures are low outside, assembling things are best done indoors to avoid frostbite. Well, the top did not come off so I looked for instructions. There was a tag on the feeder but the only instruction was to clean the feeder every couple of weeks.Unable to remove the top but finding that the bottom came off easily, I decided to fill it from the bottom. Big mistake! Seed fell out of the little holes in the side. I put the bottom back on after a brief struggle with the wire bracket that holds in place the round metal disk that functions as a bottom cover. I tried the top cover again but it was firmly jammed on.Knowing that Amazon reviews often contain tips from other customers, I went online and learned that the top DOES come off but sometimes you have to use a hammer or other tools! Knowing this, I was able to force it off. Reviewers also reported that squirrels were able to raid the feeder, so I decided to only fill it half way. Even this turned out to be too much, because a great deal of seed again spilled out the portholes before I got out the back door! This gave me a big mess to sweep up.Once outside, the feeder was easy to hang. I like that the hanging wire is strong and probably chew-resistant. (I've had feeders with plastic wire that squirrels chewed through, dropping the feeder to the ground where they could raid the contents.)The next day the top was askew. I had not forced it back on tightly enough. It is as difficult to put on as it is to take off. I don't know why it doesn't screw on; that would work better. I put more seed in it and jammed it on as well as I could.On the following day, I looked out and a squirrel was hanging on the feeder. He only stayed there for a short time but he managed to spill enough seed on the ground to provide a nice meal for himself and his brother.I don't recommend this feeder; I'll put my old one back up.Note for photographers only: I was unable to focus on this feeder using autofocus. I suppose this is due to the round shape and perhaps even the non-contrasty finish. Also I don't think feeder is particularly photogenic.
summary: Design Flaws ~ Awkward Top and Easy to Spill Seed

reviewText: I own and use a LOT of bird feeders at our place.  We are year-around feeders and living on five acres of wooded property, orchard, garden and specifically planted area for just birds we have a very, very large following.  We also have approximately 35 to 40 squirrels who take advantage; squirrels being squirrels you know.  Anyway, we are using and have used in the past, quite a large number of various models of Perky-Pet feeders.  I must tell you truthfully that for the most part we have been delighted with each of these feeders.  They are cost effective, easy to clean, and most importantly, the birds are attracted to them and use them.Alas, I suppose you cannot bat a 1000 and Perky-pet most certainly struck you with this particular offering.  I like the concept and the feeder is attractive and the birds sort of like it but the flaws far out weigh the goodness of this feeder.To begin with, this thing is far, far, far from being squirrel proof and is indeed not even designed to discourage squirrels.  As a matter of fact they hit this thing within one hour after we installed it and within two hours had completely emptied it.  In addition to that the greedy little guys had made wonderful progress in removing the plastic ‘windows.”  We removed the feeder.This feeder does hold a lot of food but loading it is a true pain.  The top must be pressed down tightly and if you are just a fraction off in your alignment, a screwdriver or some other implement must be used to get the thing off again.  Overall the design of this thing is absolutely wretched.  What on earth were these folks thinking?  I am amazed that a company that offers so many fine products would come up with something like this.On the other hand, with the exception of the plastic ‘windows” this thing should last quite a few years...it is metal and has some sort of rust protector.  The problem is I simply do not have the time (with all of our other feeders to maintain,) to wrestle with the top of this thing each time I fill it or take it down for its frequent cleaning.I am sorry this product is below standard as the idea is great and it is attractive and I am sure the birds would eventually like it if the squirrels left anything for them...fat chance of that happening.Don BlankenshipThe Ozarks
summary: Great Company but they missed on this one.

reviewText: This Perky Pet seed bunker is a heavy-duty metal tube with metal perches, hoods, and a top. Too bad the company decided to cheap out with super-thin plastic in the windows. It's easy to fill and hang -- I have no problem securing the lid.The feeder arrived with the lower hoods removed and clanking around the box. At first, I couldn't insert it into the right place, but after using some force and persistence, I got the assembly in place. The smaller songbirds love this tube, but even some larger ones, like a red-bellied woodpecker, have figured out how to get seeds out of it. The capacity isn't huge, but it's just the right size to hang on the shepherd's hook I have attached to my deck.  The squirrels don't get to mine -- at least, not yet -- primarily because the shepherd's hook, high off the ground, makes it difficult.-- Debbie Lee Wesselmann
summary: Heavy-Duty Metal Construction Marred by Thin Plastic Windows

reviewText: This winter has been tough on our feathered friends. Lots of snow and very cold weather has created a tough environment for the birds around my home. We like to feed birds but during the warmer weather, the local bears rip the feeders apart so the the only time we can safely put feeders out is when the yard is snow covered. This feeder has replaced another Vine-supplied feeder and, so far, it's a much better product. First, it arrived in perfect condition. Next, the feeder hold a lot of seed so refilling isn't a chore that you have to do  couple of times a day. The little shields over the port help keep the really big birds from hogging the feeder and emptying it before the little birds get a chance.It doesn't have a way to keep the pesky squirrels away (bit, really can anything do that?) The heavy metal design means they won't eat their way through the tube.One minor gripe - the lid has to be force fitted on top and so far. it's TIGHT. That makes it a little tough to pop off to refill. Like I said, minor.So far, the birds seem to like it and that's really the point, right?

Nothing special about this feeder. As the illustration shows, it is a metal tube with two plastic windows. The feeder arrived without any instructions although none were really needed. The cap was loose on arrival so it was easy to fill the tube with seed. The cap is somewhat awkward to put into place because unless you have it exactly even with the top of the tube it will resist efforts to push it down into place. Once you get the top pushed down completely you will have quite a challenge to remove it for restocking the seed.There is nothing squirrel proof about this feeder. You will need to hang it from a squirrel proof pole to keep the squirrels away. If you hang it from a tree branch, for example, the squirrels will thank you as they gobble up the seed.China dropped the ball when they came up with this feeder. There are far better feeders available including some that are made in China. This one is not recommended.

This is a tube-shaped bird feeder for hanging in your backyard. It consists of a metal tube that measures approximately 14" tall and 3" in diameter. It has a total of 4 feeding holes, 2 opposite each other 4.5" from the bottom, and 2 more 3" below that, set off at 90 degrees from the first. There are metal perches beneath each feeding hole that extend approximately 1.75" from the tube. The holes themselves are about 1.25" wide by about 1.5" inches high. The holes are shielded from above with metal inserts that run through the tube so that a bird can stick its head inside the tube to feed and not cause a shower of seeds to fall out on the ground. The lid to the tube is a metal cone that snaps on. There is a metal wire loop through the top for hanging the feeder onto a hook or tying it to a piece of rope; this wire extends through the tube to the top of the first feeder shield. On 2 sides of the top (parallel to the lower feeder holes) there are slots measuring approximately 5"x1.5" so that you can visually monitor the seed level in the feeder. Behind these slots are a tube of clear plastic so that seeds won't fall out the sides. Empty, the feeder weighs approximately 1.75 lbs. The bottom is sealed with a loose metal disk that is (sort of) clamped on with a wire clip. Perhaps it is intended that this would allow the tube to filled from the bottom, or opened for cleaning. The tube is painted forest green, and the lid, perches, and head shields are a coppery brown, making the feeder an attractive addition to a yard.While it's certainly pretty, I faced a number of challenges when using this feeder. First, it took a bit of wrangling to get the shields, perches, and bottom seal installed correctly since the feeder ships somewhat partially assembled with no instructions (either that, or it rattled apart during shipping). On my feeder, the bottom perch was loose, and I had to re-engineer it by attaching it securely with an additional piece of wire wrapped around the bottom of the feeder. Once installed in the yard, the birds took to the feeder immediately. However, I was a little nervous for them because they have to stick their heads inside the shields to get at the seed, which restricts their ability to keep an eye out for predators while they feed. Also, the perches seem to be a bit close together vertically, and some birds didn't seem comfortable having neighbors feeding so near, so there seemed to be a bit more fighting over perches than with my other tube-shaped feeder. The lid isn't that easy to manipulate one-handed, which requires you to put down your container of seeds to get the lid open, and then again to shut the lid. If you don't take the time to push the lid down securely after filling the tube, it often comes loose, causing the entire feeder to hang at an odd angle, and allowing rain or snow to get inside the tube. The plastic sleeve inside the tube that lines the wide slots is made of extremely thin plastic, and I'm not sure how that will stand up to the elements for long term use. After just one week of use in my yard, it is already showing scratches on the inside from abrasion by seed shells. The worst problem, however, is the bottom seal, which doesn't seal at all. This morning, I woke up to an empty feeder--the bottom seal had worked its way loose, falling off in the snow, and all the seed fell out on the ground. Before I re-install the feeder, I'm going to have to re-engineer it again to try to find a way to make sure the bottom seal stays put.This feeder bills itself as a "bunker", designed to "provide maximum durability against squirrels". Good luck with that. Yes, it's a metal feeder, and that's a durable material. A squirrel could probably use the tiny gap between the metal and plastic sleeve for grip, however, to crawl down the tube and stick its greedy little paws in the feeding holes. A bear would simply grab the entire tube, pull open the top and help itself to a nutritious snack. If it's squirrels that you are worried about, the most effective way to protect your feeder is location, location, location--put the feeder out of reach by hanging it higher and away from buildings, trees, or other structures. In general, this feeder is attractive, but probably not entirely squirrel-proof, and it will require some fiddling, adding additional wires and/or glue to make it doesn't lose essential parts.

With a list price of $27.95 I would say do not waste your money on this Seed Bunker wild bird feeder by Perky-Pet.I came to acquire one through the Amazon Vine program in exchange for my honest review of it and my best advice to those of you who, like me, enjoy feeding the wild birds, get yourself a Brome Bird Care feeder instead.  Bromes are expensive and usually priced twice as much as a Perky-Pet but they are truly squirrel-proof bird feeders which are built to last and carry a two-year warranty.  Plus they will pay for themselves in what you save in seed that those hungry squirrels cannot access. I highly recommend theBrome 1015 Squirrel Buster Classicover this Perky-Pet 740.So, just what is so wrong with the Perky-Pet 740?1. It took the squirrels in my back yard exactly 5 minutes to figure out that the cover lid does not lock.  The lid does not snap or screw closed and easily enables the squirrels their better purchase on the feeder, allowing them to tilt the feeder and make the seed spill out through the feeding ports and onto the ground for easy feasting.2. While very attractive to the squirrels, birds have absolutely no interest in this feeder. I wonder if the perches might not be inviting to most birds.3. The transparent seed tube is made of the flimsiest of plastic. It screams "cheap-cheap".4. The plastic seed tube traps heat and moisture causing the seed to dampen and decay. This is a real problem in my Florida climate. The spoiled seed decreases bird traffic at the feeder and also spreads disease.  This is why Perky-Pet advises that you to thoroughly clean your bird feeder in soapy water every two weeks.What the Perky-Pet 740 Seed Bunker does have going for it and why I give it 2-stars rather than 1 is that it is not really a bad-looking feeder. It holds about 2 quarts of seed and the outer tube, perches, perch hood and lid are made of metal with what the manufacturer says is a "special powder" coating to protect the feeder in most weather. I do wonder if that "special powder" coating might be toxic especially because the feeder is made in China.Perky-Pet also claims that the outer metal tube provides maximum durability against squirrels.  It doesn't claim to be squirrel-proof and it definitely is not.If you really are interested in a beautiful, squirrel-proof bird feeder that attracts a great variety of wild birds, I once again recommend the Brome Squirrel Buster feeder that I mentioned above.  The Bromes truly do provide maximum durability against squirrels and are of superior quality.ADDENDUM of February 28, 2014I have down rated my evaluation of this bird feeder to 1 star.Today I had to remove this Perky-Pet bird feeder to the trash when the squirrels broke through the flimsy plastic seed tube. The squirrels had quickly learned to access the seed by easily clawing and biting through the plastic tube by way of the viewing windows.  Even though the birds never used the perches, the squirrels found the perches and the perch hoods a convenient way to hang onto the feeder while they worked their way through the plastic tube.
summary: Don't waste your money on this wild bird feeder

reviewText: What can I say about the perky pet 740 Seed Bunker? It is poor on so many levels. Squirrels can get into it in a hurry because they are smart and because it is so poorly designed. The plastic used is very thin  so they can get thru it. It is hard to fill , holds very little and the birds don't even like it! It is totally worthless!! I hung it by my other feeder and I had one bird land on it.I don't know what it is, but I have several feeders and this one they bypass. I use the same birdseed in all of them. This will be heading to the trash,

This is a very "strong" bird feeder.  It's heavy metal construction will last a good long time. . . BUT. . . It is NOT "squirrel proof".  If you do not have problems with squirrels, then this is fine. . . but if you do have problem with squirrels, this is not the feeder you want.I've seen a LOT of bird feeders which claim to be "squirrel proof".  99% of them are not.  The only "squirrel proof" feeders are the ones which "close" the feeding holes when a squirrel is on them."Perky Pet" makes an inexpensive model.  (see link below)  I have one of these.  A couple of things to note.  First, sometimes when a squirrel jumps off of the feeder (frustrated that it can't get to the seed) it will cause the feeder to "bang".  The outside "wire" part of the feeder is on a spring.  Sometimes when this happens it will cause the spring to come "unhooked".  You simply have to hook it back into the hole.  It's not broken.  Second, this feeder is good for small birds only.  Larger birds, such as cardinals, are too large for the small perch.  Finally, it's not that "weatherproof" so sometimes the feed at the bottom can mold.  But it's not that much of an issue for me.Perky-Pet 336 Squirrel-Be-Gone Wild Bird FeederBy fare the BEST squirrel proof feeders are from "Brome" and are called "Squirrel Buster".  There's no better squirrel proof feeders.  They are not cheap. . but. . . I have two different ones, and they last.  They make a few different sizes and types.  If you want to feed the most birds, the "Squirrel Buster Plus" is the one you want. FYI, they have just come out with a "weather guard" for this model.  It's a clear plastic ring that keeps the seed dry. I've had mine for a few years, and indeed the seed can get a little wet on the bottom and mold if you have bad weather.  So the "weather guard" is recommended.Brome 1024 Squirrel Buster Plus Wild Bird Feeder with Cardinal Perch RingWeatherguard for Squirrel Buster FeederIf you like to also feed birds with "suet nuggets" (little suet balls, often mixed with peanuts) Brome also makes a "Squirrel Buster Peanut Plus" feeder which works great.  Woodpeckers really like this.  Again, it's 100% squirrel proof.Squirrel Buster Peanut Plus Wild Bird Feeder
summary: This is NOT a "Squirrel Proof" feeder.  See review for better options.

reviewText: Once you muscle the lid off, the feeder is easy to fill. It will sit up and you can pour the seed in. It is sturdy and stays clean. The birds empty it frequently. Also it looks nice. It's a pretty feeder. I use black oil sunflower seeds in it.
summary: easy to fill. birds liked it. stays clean.

reviewText: We got this for our backyard so our boys could watch for birds. They really like this feeder. The bird feeder is simple to use and just hangs from the tree by a nail. We have had quite a few birds come to the feeder including a wood pecker. It is very easy to fill the feeder with bird seed. Overall a great feeder.

I had to read a few reviews on here to figure out that the top did indeed slide up to fill the feeder once knocked free, since it came jammed on so hard it felt welded. Now it slides up and down, but doesn't sit securely on the top of the tube... a little askew, unless I push it down and jam it on again.Assuming you can get the top of yours off, it's not hard to fill (don't try filling it from the bottom like I did the first time... you'll give up in frustration!).It's all metal. It will last. Okay, it's all metal except for the cheap-feeling plastic window you can see the seed through. They could have used something more durable here. It works, but that part may not last forever.Others have mentioned it's not squirrel proof. They won't chew through it, but knocking seeds out isn't difficult.Anyway, it's well built, but the manufacturer could have thought through the design a bit better. If you're willing to put up with its quirks, it should last a long time.

I love, love, love feeding and watching birds!  My backyard has 9 bird feeders and all but 2 are Perky Pet.  The birds love the feeders and this one is no exception.  The yellow finches especially like this feeder.  Now, for the 4 stars.....it is giving the birds a problem from time to time.  This feeder has 2 perches that fit, but one of the perches keeps falling out.  It doesn't stay locked in.  When the birds land on the perch it turns and falls.  I hope I am describing this correctly.  I fix it as soon as it happens but it happens often.  The other perch has not had this problem.....it stays locked in place.  Even though this happens the birds still love the feeder and keep coming back to it.

This feeder is a mix of a manufacturers good intention to some detail, while completely ignoring others.  The construction of it being metal that is powder coated should see it lasting through quite a few winters before it rusts or falls apart, and I like the little hoods over the ports that protect the seed from the elements.  Also, it's a good size unit that will hold and keep dry about 1 1/2 pounds of seed at a time...That all being said, the company completely missed the boat on of all the things, the top of it.  It neither snaps nor screws on, but is just is pressed on to make it tight.  Not only is it very difficult to keep from going on crooked when pressing it on, but Lord help you if you manage to keep it straight and press it all the way down.  I finally did and needed a screwdriver and hammer to get it off again.  It's in a word, flat out terrible.  I have a feeling most people will eventually stop using this for they will either get tired of pressing it on lightly and unevenly, (which still requires quite a bit of effort to get off), or, having to get out tools and naughty words in pulling it off when its all the way on. Also, although this feeder has a smooth metal finish that should aid in deterring squirrels, it really doesn't.  I have seen squirrels all over it hanging down and clinging to the what not, and its only been in use for a couple of days.  The hooded ports helps some, but trust me, most squirrels will easily find a way to get to the seed.  One innovative fellow just wrapped himself around the bottom of it like a donut and feasted till I chased him off.  Lastly, although this is touted as having a great finish on it that will last for years, the plastic insert that covers the windows on it is cheap crap.  You can easily bubble it with your finger.  Even if the squirrels decide to spare you that easy route, it will turn yellow and clouded in no time and crack in the temperature fluctuations, or with just the sun hitting it too long.In conclusion, with the top of this thing being simply awful, and, with the fact that its not at all squirrel proof, I can't recommend this feeder. (I'm still trying to figure out exactly what "maximum security from squirrels" means.  Does that mean the feeder won't wear out or break for years while squirrels crawl all over it and devour your bird seed?) It's not really all that bad a price they are asking for the quality steel and size of it, but the liabilities unfortunately make this a poor investment in my opinion.. : )
summary: Quality Construction, But Very Frustrating Top, And Far From "Maximum Security From Squirrels"

reviewText: This is a sturdy, well made bird feeder. The tube is rigid metal. The perches and feeder guards are metal. They are removable fr cleaning and storage. The cap is metal. The only plastic is the inner sleeve that covers the windows. This is made out of flexible plastic and has a seam. You need to rotate it so that the seam is not in one of the windows. It hangs by a metal cable that runs the length of the feeder until the upper perch. It is well balanced. The feeder holds 1.5 pounds of mixed seeds. The bottom can be removed for cleaning. The bottom is held on with a spring and is easy to remove and replace.I am worried that it might get hot if placed in the sun (in light of all of the metal parts). It's too early in the season to tell.The birds seem to like it. I do too.
summary: The birds and I like this feeder

reviewerName: Juanita A. Floyd "Life is too short to read b...
reviewText: Finally a fairly well built bird feeder. This holds a nice amount of seed. Seems to be well constructed and I think it will do well against the squirrel onslaughts. I gave this 5 stars because of a really neat feature this feeder has. The bottom panel of it comes out for cleaning. So much easier than trying to stick a coat hanger down the tube and stabbing around to loosen the seed that is stuck and wet. This feeder has an easily removable metal clip ring that comes out and frees the bottom plate in the feeder. Great design!

We've been using this bird feeder for a few weeks.It works well enough.  The birds spill some seed but no more than is usual.  The gravity feed system seems to work well and has not clogged.  However, we are using a small seed mix.  If you were using "all sunflower seeds" then I don't think it would clog and not drop.  We've had no problem with squirrels even though we have a lot of them.The window is a piece of plastic but seems good enough for the job.  The metal construction is sturdy.  The color scheme is unobtrusive.A couple points to mention:1) Any bird feeder you put up is going to have a mess under it, where the birds drop seeds and shells. So before you buy one make sure you are putting it over grass or some other area. Birds can be messy eaters.2) If you are really a bird lover, plant some shrubs that birds like and let the birds eat it as it grows.  This is supposed to be  a lot healthier for them.  However, a lot of the birds who come to our feeder are house sparrows and I'm not too worried about them eating freshly grown millet.
summary: Ok I don't love it but it works really well

reviewText: Although light weight, this bird feeder is solidly constructed and very easy to use. On other bird feeders of this type I've always seemed to have difficulty getting the lid back on tightly and had to struggle with the slack in the wire. The Perky-Pet has no such problems and the lid fits on tightly with no effort. I hung it outside and the birds found it immediately, which was great for them with all the snow we've been getting. Normally it takes a while for birds to find a new feeder but they arrived minutes after I hung it. The overhangs on the openings prevent squirrels from getting access while allowing small birds to feed easily. And the plastic windows allow you to see when the feeder is empty - which I can see from inside my house. Can't say enough good things about this feeder. Love it!
summary: Perky-Pet 740 Wild Bird Feeder is Fantastic!

reviewText: This is a very attractive feeder . As far as holding food and being easy for birds to use, we found that it functioned  well. Nice solid perches.  A deep green color which blends well with foliage, allowing birds to stand out. But the bottom of the feeder was no match for the two types of squirrels we have in our yard and it also was a cinch for raccoons to open.If you don't have a problem with  squirrels, raccoons, or other creatures going after your birdseed you may find this feeder suits your purposes.  Perhaps you found have a way to keep squirrels away ( and if you have, I'd love to know your secret). Otherwise, it could be a pain to keep replacing the bottom daily.Update: I did want to note that we are still using this feeder because my spouse tinkered with the bottom of the feeder and made it more difficult to open. It is not a perfect solution but at least we can still use the feeder for now. Will update if that changes.
summary: Bottom part too easy for squirrels to open and an update

reviewText: This feeder is designed to attract birds while keeping the squirrels away and so far, it succeeds. It's not the sturdiest feeder, with a rather cheap plastic window to monitor the seed level, but under a shaded tree, it should likely last for some time. Multiple finches come to feed daily, using the small perch and even the hood above to stand on the feeder. Recommended.

Yes, I know, it's not politically correct to point out that some squirrels are not quite as bright as others. But facts be facts. And to irate members of the SDL (Squirrel Defense League), I can only say, let nature take its course. The behavior of squirrels is what gives them a bad name, not inherent bias against them. We wouldn't try to keep them out if they weren't so greedy! But they insist on stealing all the other critters' food, even though the squirrels have more than enough for their fat little selves already.One has to wonder if they didn't have an insider on the design team for this very poorly designed bird feeder, because it's really a squirrel feeder. The top has no threads or snap-on feature to lock it down, so the squirrels just climb on top of the feeder and have their way with it. Plus the cheap plastic window is out of keeping with the otherwise solid steel construction. And most birds don't seem to want to use it, as almost all of them prefer the old school wood feeder we have a dozen feet away. The perches on this are small and round, hardly comfy for most of our flighty friends.Still, all they have to do is put some threads or a snap on top. And use some decent plastic for the windows! This stuff is like the plastic on top of folder files. This would only be worth its 28 buck price tag if those two things were rectified.Until then, this feeder is for the squirrels, not the birds.
summary: Very nice squirrel feeder! Keeps out only very low-IQ squirrels...

reviewText: I actually already own thePerky-Pet 2-in-1 Wild Bird Feederwhich didn't fare the elements too well last year as the copper finish not only began to tarnish quickly, but one of the ports actually corroded completely away during storage in our shed over the winter.So, when this Perky-Pet Seed Bunker feeder showed up, I was very pleased to see that for only a slightly elevated cost, the material on this feeder is of much sturdier quality.  This means that the feeder is pretty heavy and the metal is extraordinarily durable.  In fact, a number of the hoods and perches came knocked out of place during shipping.  (Amazon's usually amazing service for some reason did a lousy job with packing this item for shipment.)  But the perches and hoods were not damaged or bent despite what was probably a turbulent journey and they were easily snapped back into place.  I've only had it for a month, but my guess is that the quality material will probably fare a lot better and longer than my other bird feeder which is mostly made of thin plastic.For what it is primarily designed to do, it does it just fine.  It's easy to fill with bird seed and it attracted a variety of beautiful birds the very first day.However, it is not squirrel proof.I actually filled both feeders and suspended this one from a tree using ametal hookand the other from ashepherd's hook.  I noticed the very first day that half the seed was gone, very quickly.  Suspicious that a squirrel was getting into them, I swapped the two feeders, thinking that perhaps the lack of a plate on the bottom of this Seed Bunker feeder would make it harder for the squirrel to get a grip onto the feeder from the shepherd's hook.  A few hours later, I saw that much of the seed was gone already.  And then an hour after that, I caught the culprit in the act.  The squirrel was able to climb right up the shepherd's crook and then held himself upside down while raiding the Seed Bunker.  It did the exact same thing with the other bird feeder by climbing the tree and scooting himself upside down the metal hook.  At this point, I'm pretty convinced that very little will deter squirrels from the bird feeders, not even those fancy ones which have thecollapsible perches(designed to collapse at the heavy weight of a squirrel, but not a bird) since the squirrel made no use of the perches at all when he was lowering himself onto the feeders from above.It should be noted that Perky Pet does market a number of wild bird feeders that are specifically targeted for problem squirrelshere,here, andhereamong several others, but even those are of limited effectiveness against a determined squirrel.  (Which is what we've got.  Those little buggers have completely chewed through several thick plastic trash can lids of ours.)  Squirrels can chew through plastic parts of so-called squirrel-proof bird feeders.  And even if the feeder is completely made of metal (which this Seed Bunker feeder is not, as the viewing windows are very thin plastic), the squirrels can learn to shake the feeder and spill the seed onto the ground.  There are a fewfeedersthat seem to fare better at warding off squirrels than the ones from Perky-Pet, but they tend to be inthe next price range upand still not 100% effective for everyone.Our current hope, since we don't contemplate spending more money on bird feeders, is that greasing the pole and hook with ample amounts of vaseline will keep the squirrels away and perhaps make for some funny videos if we see them slipping off.  We will see if that does the trick and I'll come back here and update.  I guess, meanwhile, the silver lining in all this is that now that the squirrels have all this bird seed, they're sorta leaving my trash cans alone.  The other silver lining is that my kids have a good reason to scream "Those Darn Squirrels!" whenever they see the thieves raiding the feeders.If you found this review helpful or if you have any questions, please let me know.  If you have any solution suggestions for my pesky "friends", please comment!
summary: Quality bird feeder; but not squirrel proof at all

reviewText: Birds have been using this feeder everyday since it was hung. They seem to like it just fine.My only complaint is that the bottom perch slips to one side after several birds have landed on it.Thank goodness that bar is only for perching and doesn't have anything to do with holding the food.I move the perch back in place every time I fill the feeder, but after a few birds have landed on it,it's moved to the side once again.Although this model is suppose to discourage squirrels by it's overall design and hooded perches,the lid doesn't lock and if squirrels can reach it - they'll empty it.I used extension hooks to hang the feeder several feet from anything ~ and out of reach of squirrels lungingon the feeder ~ and so far squirrels haven't gotten to it.This all metal feeder holds 4 1/2 cups food.The clear window for viewing level of feed isn't as useful as it might have beenbecause the bottom of the window is 7" up from the bottom of the feeder.The window pulls out, bottom easily comes off and the perches pull out for cleaning.Feeder size - 17" tall, plus 5" hanger - x 3" dia.
summary: Birds like it fine ~ but bottom perch doesn't stay in place.

reviewText: I got this feeder at the same time as another feeder and this one I put up right away. When I got it, it was not packaged up nice; I had to adjust the plastic film that lets you seed the see and one of the little hoods was not aligned properly so right out of the box I had to make adjustments so it would be workable.When I hung it up it didn't attract birds. It was weeks before I saw any action at the feeder when the other feeder I got (a fly through filled with sunflower seeds) had birds on it the next day. This was kind of a disappointment in comparison.

We have several bird feeders set up in the yard and my family takes great pleasure in watching the birds come and go all day long. I always have an eye open for feeders that might work well for us and I was interested in trying the Seed Bunker tube feeder. It's not a perfect feeder, though so far it isn't too bad. It can be made better with a very simple and inexpensive modification.Right up front - this is not a squirrel-proof feeder and it is not advertised as such. If you are looking for a feeder that will keep the squirrels away, this is the wrong feeder and there are other options.Except for the clear plastic sheath inside the tube, this is actually a nicely made feeder. It feels solid and has a nice enamel finish that should keep it from rusting for a while and should help keep the squirrels from gnawing on it and damaging it. The clear plastic liner inside the tube (which allows one to see how much seed remains in the feeder) is made of a cheaper grade of plastic and I am concerned that it will eventually deteriorate when exposed to the sun for long periods of time.The feeder holds a good amount of seed and the ports are spaced nicely to allow up to four birds to feed at the same time. I would have preferred to see more ports, maybe some half-way up the tube so that more birds could feed, but this might invite more squirrels to come pillage the feeder and because the feeder is not all that large the level would quickly drop below the upper ports.The lid is a small issue in that getting it to clamp down and stay put is a slight challenge. As one other reviewer noted, it can be done but to clamp it down makes it very difficult to pop back off again. There is an easy and simple solution to this that is very inexpensive. A larger split-shot fishing sinker clamped to the cable does a reasonable job of holding the lid down without damaging the feeder and without making the lid difficult to remove again.This isn't that bad of a feeder. When considering that it is not touted as a squirrel-proof feeder it's actually a decent tube feeder. It isn't perfect but can be made better with a slight adjustment. Overall we are satisfied with this feeder - I would give this feeder 3.5 stars.
summary: Ok with a Slight Adjustment - 3.5 stars

reviewText: First things first, let's highlight the words "maximum durability against squirrels" in the product description.  By maximum durability, I can only assume that they mean that the squirrels won't damage the feeder, because they certainly like to get at the seed within.  That's okay, I figure that the squirrels probably need food too, and hanging around the feeder certainly makes them a little more vulnerable to the passing hawk (it's a circle of life thing, you know?).Anyway, the feeder fills easily enough and the perches are bird friendly.  And I suspect that this will also withstand the marauding deer that visit my feeders in the summer as well.
summary: Okay... not out of the ordinary however

reviewText: I am curse with multiple black walnut trees in and around my yard.  Although beautiful trees that provide a pleasant sun filtering, they drop stuff all year long and bring with them lots of squirrels, and provide said squirrels with filthy black nuts to hide under what used to be my plants.  Anyway, the squirrels get more out of this thing than the birds do.  There should be a circular layer of minimum 1/8" thick polycarbonate underneath the metal to match the durability of the metal.  It's unfortunate because it appears to be very well made in every other regard.

We feed the birds year around from multiple feeders and this one is the bomb.I don't think you will find a heavier-made feeder than this one. We no longer use cheap-made feeders because the squirrels and raccoons just demolish them in a short time -- there is no way to eliminate that problem so we just buy quality feeders and live with the issue.Not a lot of birds can feed on this unit at one time but I still like it a lot as I have multiple feeders and no one starves at my house.Highly recommended.

As most other reviewers have already pointed out this Wild Bird feeder is not designed properly. Perky-Pet did plan on making a super strong squirrel proof bird feeder based on the tubular design but failed to execute it properly due to:1. The plastic see-through portion of the seed tube is very flimsy. Squirrels can easily push or chew thru' this portion of the bird feeder and once that happens you will have to throw this bird feeder away.2. Filling bird seed is impossible without spilling seeds everywhere. I did not see any manual or instruction how to fill the tube other than removing the spring loaded clamp and removing the bottom circular plate. The top housing does not come apart for easy filling. Big messy problem can happen if someone were to remove the bottom circular plate.3. It does not breathe easily and thereby moisture builds up inside and the seeds start to germinate inside loosing the smell and flavor thereby birds do not come that often.I am glad I did not have to pay for this poorly designed contraption. Having said, Perky Pet does make other good bird feeders that I liked and one of them beingPerky-Pet 325S Panorama Bird FeederThis one is a big hit with birds of all kinds in our backyard and is way cheaper to own compared to this model.Happy Bird watching!

The Perky-Pet bird feeder is solid metal, attractive and simple to use.  It is not huge, but is perfect for the corner of a small garden. It does hold about a pound and a half of bird seed.  It is easy to fill and the birds love it.  There are two long windows in the feeder so one can see how many seeds remain in it from a distance.The feeder is supposed to 'discourage' squirrels and leave the goodies to the birds.  I have the feeder hanging from a long wrought iron hook attached to an eight foot 4"x4" post.  The post is about eight or ten feet from any trees.  I have not seen a squirrel attacking my new feeder yet and hope I never do.The issues with the cap on the top of the seed tube that others have complained about have not materialized for me.  It comes off easily for filling and goes back on just as easily with a bit of alignment and a slight push.The only surprise I had was how it was necessary to tap the seed port hoods and perches into alignment when the feeder arrived.  That was no big deal, but I would have thought the feeder might be properly assembled in the first place.  Perhaps the thing was bumped in shipping.  Anyhow, I took off a star for that small problem.  Otherwise the Perky-Pet 740 is working out well.
summary: Just Great for a Small Area

reviewText: I own several Perky Pet brand feeders and have enjoyed every one I have purchased.  This one is made of metal  that the birds can ACTUALLY perch on as the perches are nice and long.  However, make sure that they are in place and tight before installing as I lost one (then found). I use mostly chicken scratch grains and cracked corn.This is a sturdy and very well-built bird feeder as is all of the Perky Pet brands.Happy Feeding!
summary: Nice Feeder, Make Sure The Perches Are Tightened, However...

reviewText: I love squirrels - they are adorable creatures - but I cannot afford to feed them birdseed. I will say that my perspective has changed since moving from suburbia to the country. Country squirrels are smarter and more determined, as there aren't a lot of free meal choices around. Our country squirrels had no problem removing the plastic windows and emptying the feeder in short order. I will be transferring this feeder to my mother's house in the city, where she may have less loitering by squirrels that can go from house to house in her neighborhood and the cat will have fun looking at it out the window. For my personal feeders, however, I like to watch the beautiful birds - but they didn't have much of a chance with the squirrels all over this thing.
summary: Well constructed, but too squirrel friendly

reviewText: Really, why?I know the Squirrel Buster is more expensive, but it is sturdy and well made, a good investment all around.This product?It's so flimsy and poorly made, I'd be shocked if it outlasts the season.Pass.
summary: Cheap imitation of the Squirrel Buster

reviewText: This feeder came poorly packed, hence instead of arriving full assembled, it was in several pieces.  No directions were included, so I did the best I could in getting it together.  The bottom plate easily tipped, so that seeds do not stay in the feeder.  And I was unable to secure that plate.  The top does not snap or lock closed, so easily comes off.The metal is heavy duty, and so is the hanger, but I can't recommend this item.

The Perky-Pet Seed Bunker Wild Bird Feeder is very much a quality feeder. It is constructed of metal, even with a metal hanging loop. The top is also metal and snaps onto the base to keep it in place. The top comes off for filling and must be held to one side with one hand while filling with the other.  From trial and error, I feel the best way to fill this feeder is with a large plastic drink cup from a fast food place. This can be bent slightly to make sure that the seeds flow into the feeder. A very large cup is about what would fill the feeder.Some seeds fall out of the feeder openings while filling so it is best to fill it where it will be located. I estimate that about 20 black oil seeds fell out while I first filled it. I suspect that this might be more of  a problem with the smaller seeds in the mixed seed bags.The bottom of the feeder snaps out for cleaning.As far as being a deterrent to squirrels, the small openings from which the seeds are taken will certainly prevent the squirrels from getting too many seeds. My problem is not with squirrels, but rather with chipmunks. I'm sure they will be able to stick their little heads into the opening and help themselves. Overall, I highly recommend this feeder for its quality.

I have a lot of bird feeders, a few of them are from Perky-Pet, and the rest of them are from Droll-Yankee.  My other Perky-Pet feeder were well thought out and well constructed.  This one, not so much.When assembling the feeder I was really surprised to see that the bottom disc at the floor of the feeder was not attached and had I have to be careful that it doesn't shift when filling the tube.I also surprised at how flimsy the plastic was that allows you to see into the tube.  The little hood that covers the ports also makes it difficult for some birds to reach the seed.However, it is the lid of the feeder that really baffles me.  It has to fit tightly on the tube in order for the feeder to hang straight, but that is easier said than done as it tends to pop off without warning.I filled the tube with a scoop-funnel, hung it and watched it for a few hours.  The birds did not get much of a chance to try it out since the local squirrels must have emailed each other that a free lunch was just installed.  They emptied it out in short order so I took the feeder down and won't be using it again.  Even though I received this product for free through the Vine program, it is still a disappointing experience.
summary: A poorly designed feeder that should be recalled

reviewText: This was set to be my favorite feeder. It is easy to fill, attractive, and keeps the larger birds from scarfing down all the seed. Unfortunately either a strong wind or a persistent squirrel pulled it down and the plastic snapped just above the guard- so I would not consider it sturdy.

This bird feeder is based on the great idea - if a weight-based platform prevents squirrels from feasting at a bird feeder and a clear cover prevents squirrels from getting at a bird feeder, why not combine the two to make sure that no squirrels can get at the bird seed?I have another bird feeder that is based on the weight-based platform. It works well - the squirrels can't get at the bird seed. Unfortunately, this feeder just doesn't work well. The plastic dome prevents birds from getting at the bird seed. Only small light birds (smaller than a cardinal) could get at the seed.Overall, it was a good idea, but I like to see larger birds (like cardinals) at my feeders.
summary: Works OK for small light birds

reviewText: My neighbor' bird feeder attracts a variety of birds as well as squirrels. This seemed promising. Since my husband hung it up several weeks ago I've seen NO birds. I believe that the clear plastic dome keeps birds from getting to the seed. This may require some alteration, but out of the box this is a serious design flaw.

I must clarify that this bird feeder has only been out in the yard for a few weeks, but it seems to be doing a decent job at keeping the larger birds ans sqirrels out of the seed. I think the term slammer is a bit harsh, implying it is loud, when in reality it is fairly quiet when closing. The squirrels haven't given up and one wouldn't expect them too. I have had other squirrel proof feeders that were eventually cracked by the rodents so I will have to post an update to this one in the future if that happens. Maybe I have super diabolical squirrels? The feed stays dry and the smaller birds enjoy a quick treet. It is well made, solid, and looks like it should last. When we get through the Minnesota winter I will update to follow up on durability of the clear plastic and painted metal. If you like a pretty feeder, this might be the one for you.
summary: Good after two weeks out in the yard

reviewText: I love feeding the backyard birds and have 7 feeders and lots of feathered visitors so I was happy to get to try this feeder out - especially since the squirrels had battered one of my Squirrel Buster mini feeders (they still couldn't get at the seed though...). Like the Squirrel Busters, the weight of a squirrel or large bird will cause the tubing to move down over the feeding holes. Unlike the SBs, this has a non-adjustable hood and non-removable perch (the Squirrel Buster's are wire and a little to easy to knock off).  Though not as sturdy looking/feeling, it holds a lot of seed and seems easy to clean.I put it in the same spot as the old feeder and watched the seed level to see how the birds liked it.  After two days with no change in the seed level, I started watching more closely and noticed that small birds who tried it can't get at the food holes.  They have to perch on the upper ring to reach and the non-adjustable hood makes that difficult if not impossible for them to get to that ring.  So they stayed on the lower ring trying to get at the seed holes and couldn't.  Larger birds didn't even try.  I took it down after 4 days.

Our back yard is overrun with squirrels. One way or another, the furry little beasts manage to steal bird feed from every feeder we have. I was skeptical about the functionality of this feeder but decided to give it a shot. Well, this thing didn't even make it out of the starting gate, it arrived badly broken, bent and shattered. The packaging was market "Fragile" and the box showed no signs of damage so this thing is either incredibly delicate or they just pitched it in the box and broke it before it left the factory. Ridiculous in any event!I am interested in seeing what those who were sent a functioning feeder have to say about it. My squirrels would likely tear the filmsy thing apart.Not Recommended.
summary: All together now: "What a Piece of Junk!"

reviewText: I see a lot of negative reviews for this bird feeder on Amazon. Maybe it's because this is my first-ever bird feeder, but it seems to work just fine for me. Other reviewers have said that birds can't access the seed, but I work from home and see birds feeding from this feeder all day long. The only problem I had was with squirrels when I hung the feeder on a branch that was too close to the trunk of the tree. In that location, squirrels could climb the trunk of the tree and then lean over and sneak seed out of the feeder without putting all their weight on it. I solved that problem by moving the feeder to another branch, further away from the trunk. Now any squirrel that tries to get seed by climbing on the feeder gets shut out when the feeder slams shut from the squirrel's weight. Like I said, maybe it's because I'm a bird feeder neophyte; but this feeder seems like a decent product to me.
summary: Seems to work just fine for me

reviewText: I am a Droll Yankee bird feeder fan. I have had their feeders mauled by bears and with a little TLC, have come back for more. The Perky-Pet 5141-2 arrived today in a box that wasn't dented or damaged in any way. When I opened it, the feeder inside was in three pieces. The feeder was "packed" with three small air-filled cushions in a huge box so it rolled around freely and experienced every shock that is the normal part of shipping. I thought about just sending it back and not doing a review until it was replaced, but I decided that the best way to support fellow Amazon customers is to give a realistic impression of both the product and how likely it is to arrive in a hassle-free, undamaged manner.So, here are the facts: The feeder was packed without consideration for how it might be handled in transit. The cover over the feeder's ports was cracked - most probably from poor packing and / or poor quality construction. The barrel that holds the seed was glued poorly to the heavy metal, spring-loaded base - I counted only 2 spots where there seemed to be evidence of plastic cement, barely covering 30 to 40% of the contact surface. When I thought I could re-glue the pieces together, I discovered that the parts didn't seat together well enough to do that. (Actually the parts didn't seat together at all.)My wife, ever the optimist, said, "it makes me wonder how long this thing would have held up if it was getting banged around by a determined squirrel (are there any other kinds?). The kind of question I suppose you are asking yourself now...Bottom line - poor packaging, shoddy construction, broken on arrival.Not recommended.
summary: Poorly constructed and poorly packed and shipped - arrived broken

reviewText: This feeder just hung in the garden with no birds using it. I checked other ratings and realized I was not the only one with this problem. After taking the advice of other feeder owners,I broke the "dome" off and now it works fine.
summary: Perky Pet Squirrel Slammer Bird Feeder

reviewerName: Gina Pera "Is It You, Me, or Adult A.D.D.?, a...
reviewText: Update: The birds have gradually started using this feeder, and they seem to like it well enough.  Although I initially thought they weren't throwing out more seed than with the Brome (below), evidence on the ground says otherwise. We have some ground feeders that do clean-up duty but not enough to prevent luring rodents at night. They're a problem around here, so if that's an issue for you, you might want to find a feeder that doesn't have this problem (very few of them, it seems).------We've had theBrome 1024 Squirrel Buster Plus Wild Bird Feeder with Cardinal Perch Ringfor at least 6 years, hanging in the same spot year-round. By now, the birds (mostly finches, titmice, and wrens) are down with the routine: They hide out in the peach tree and make a break for the feeder 10 feet away, get their fill, and dart back.It's a great, sturdy feeder, with a nice lifetime warranty; when a few parts finally wore out, Brome replaced them quickly and without cost.Still, given our bird population, another feeder seemed in order so I selected this one. (Though it seems birds are just like humans: fighting over "territory" even when there's plenty to go around. Several holes will be open at the Brome, and still some bird has to knock another one out of the way.)We have a wrought-iron pole with two pieces arching out either side to hold a feeder (or something) at the end. So, we hung this Perky-Pet 5141-2 on the other hook. The first thing that happened was a squirrel gorging itself, which I don't blame on the feeder but the way the wrong-iron pole tilted a bit and allows a squirrel to wrap its legs around the pole and stick its head into the feeder, without activating the weight-closing mechanism. The Brome will do the same thing.  I straightened out the pole and tried again; no squirrel.Also, no birds.Finally, a finch did appear and I watched it for a while. It doesn't seem to throw out more seed with this feeder than with the Brome. (But with either I wish a dish was attached, to catch the overflow; it attracts rodents.)  But the bird perched on the lower rung and had to reach rather far to get the seed. It didn't climb to the higher perch, for some reason. Maybe because, as others have found, the plastic umbrella prevents quick entry or exit.I had thought the umbrella a nice feature in that it might minimize rainfall getting into the feed and creating mold.  But it does seem to inhibit bird activity altogether.It's probably designed as a deterrent to squirrels climbing down from the top of the feeder. The Brome feeder doesn't need this because its entire outer shell is weight-activated from the top to the bottom.Overall, I can't see any benefits to this feeder yet, and perhaps there are detriments. I'm giving the feeder the average of 3 stars for now and will update if, in the next couple of weeks, the birds adapt to it.
summary: The birds love it; the seed-waste is a problem, though

reviewText: I put this near my other feeder, also a Perky Pet product, that has been attracting birds (and squirrels) forever.  Larger birds like Cardinals couldn't get decent footing on the smaller feeder so I looked forward to getting more birds and having to refill seed less often with this bigger one.  Instead, the birds mostly vanished.  Even the squirrels, which I had taken to bribing with critter feed to try to keep them off the original feeder, vanished.  My lone bunny rabbit, who also liked the critter food, vanished as well.  That's a real shame because my dogs could see him out the window and were absolutely fascinated by him.  (No, they live inside a fence and did not get out and eat the bunny.)  This wasn't a tapering off; the new feeder went up and the critters went away just like that.After a few days of scratching my head I read some of these other reviews about removing the plastic dome and did so.  I also tightened the tension on the perch in case birds found the springiness disconcerting.  A few birds returned and a very small number briefly tried this new feeder. but what used to be a daily show was gone.So I completely removed the new feeder a couple of days ago.  Birds and squirrels are ever so slowly starting to return to the old feeder and the squirrel bribes I spread on the ground around the area.  It doesn't make sense to blame the feeder, but that's the only variable in the equation.  I will try it out again once the wildlife comes back and update this.
summary: Very weird - it seems to chase birds and critters away

reviewerName: Juanita A. Floyd "Life is too short to read b...
reviewText: As I sit here to type this review I am looking out my window at the new bird feeder I am reviewing. Happy birds flying to and fro. Didn't take them more than a few minutes to figure this out.Pros: This holds a fair amount of seed which is nice I suppose. That leads me to one of the...Cons: Only 4 feeding stations around the bottom of all that nice seed. The birds are lined up for a mile awaiting air traffic control permission to land.The biggest flaw in this that I can see is the plastic cover thing at the bottom. That will be the first place that gets assaulted in the squirrel invasion. They will chew that until it is gone and then attack the tube itself as they have done on every other plastic feeder I've had in 30 years.  The little metal "slammer" thing is just going to be the launching pad for the invasion. I give it 3 or 4 months before it will be toast and in the landfill with all it's fallen comrades.

When we first received the Perky-Pet Feeder we immediately filled it with seeds and hung it up. We watched and did notice a few birds visiting, however they appeared to land on the feeder, look around for a minute or two and then leave.  This went on for about 2 weeks.  It seemed that the birds were confused about the plastic disc which is the squirrel slammer located near the bottom.  We moved our new feeder to another site on our property where we've had feeders for several years. That did the trick!  Goldfinch and other small birds started to arrive and those that didn't know where the seeds came from, caught on rather quickly as they watched Cardinals, Wrens, Downy Woodpeckers and other small birds feeding. In fact, we've had more birds coming at the same time than we've ever had before. We watch from our glass enclosed garden room and are entertaing ourselves as well as visiting friends.Our yard is starting to look like a bird sanctuary!!!

What good is a feeder if birds don't use it?  This is the second Perky-Pet feeder we've gotten that just doesn't seem to attract anything, even though birds (and squirrels) are aplenty.  The feeder's weight-activated slammer is an appealing feature, but the flimsy tension knob which controls weight settings has a mind of its own.  The knob turns but produces insignificant (almost non-existent) tension changes.We have feeders of all types set up on several acres of land, and birds frequent every single one.  Not so with the Squirrel Slammer--even pesky squirrels haven't gone near it.  Wondering if the little dome was a deterrent, I took the advice of another Amazon reviewer and broke it off with a rock.  The plastic dome easily snapped in half.  Now a few clinging birds (chickadees, nuthatches) occasionally use the Squirrel Slammer, but it is readily apparent this is not any birds' favorite feeder.  I think the ill-designed perches and distance from seed has a lot to do with it.Perhaps colder weather will change usage, and we'll actually get to see if the product lives up to its name of slamming out squirrels.  Regardless, I look for bird products that offer immediate appeal.  For whatever reason, such little activity indicates birds just don't like this feeder.  If they aren't happy, neither am I.
summary: No Birds At This Feeder Speaks Volumes

reviewText: We're always trying to outwit our huge population of bold, birdseed-hogging squirrels. This year, we invested in one of those free-standing modular bird-feeder racks that includes a squirrel baffle, and we've been able to keep the feeders full most of the time. As a result, we're seeing more avian variety than ever.But we had to shelve our feeders that hung from shepherd's hooks that bolted to the deck. Reaching them was too easy for Mr. (or Mrs.) Shadow-Tail!Fortunately, Perky-Pet has come out with several models of bird feeders that WILL confound squirrels. The feeder incorporates and sleeve that, when pulled by a greedy squirrel's weight, slides down and closes the openings to the seed.You can adjust the pull on this, also, and it's easy to clean and fill.We've had this feeder up for a few weeks, and the squirrels have learned to leave it alone.
