I haven't actually witnessed their little rodentesque disappointment, but they steer clear of this feeder.The only caution I have is that the metal rim at the bottom of the feeder is really flimsy. When it arrived, it was bent completely out of shape. I was able to bend it back to the original circular shape with a pliers. But it's very thin metal, and I was lucky not to break a piece. If I'd done so, I would have had to discard the entire feeder, rather than risk getting cut on it, or injuring some little creature.I don't know how this feeder will hold up during our typically harsh Chicago winter, but it doesn't look as sturdy as some of our other feeders.This is a nice addition to what we have in our yard, with the exception of the flimsy base. I hope Amazon, or Perky Pet, is able to correct the shipping (or design) flaw. If you decide to order this, make sure you let Amazon know if it arrives in less than perfect condition. I otherwise like Perky Pet products, and they seem to be a company that is concerned with their customers and our little feathered friends. I will order another one of these IF customer reviews reflect that they arrive in better shape.

My wife has always loved feeding the birds and she has struggled like most people with greedy squirrels that hog the feeders and steal all of the seed. I was interested in the Perky Pet Squirrel Slammer feeder as a possible solution to the squirrels but there is a flaw in the build that makes it less than ideal.The concept is very simple and straightforward - the feeding ports at the bottom of the feeder are accessible through a sliding metal sheath that slides down when weight is applied to it. Perches on the sheath allow small birds to access the feeding ports and they are light enough to not cause the sheath to slide, but a squirrels's weight is enough to cause the sheath to slide down, closing the feeding ports and preventing the squirrel from eating the seed. Squirrels do not get hurt, but they get no seed either and they give up in frustration.Weight sensitivity is easily adjustable through a knob on the bottom of the feeder. The tension of the internal springs can be tightened to allow heavier/larger birds to feed while still preventing squirrels from feedings, or the sensitivity can be made very high such that only the smaller birds can eat. This particular feeder definitely has the easiest adjustment of any feeder I have seen and used.Conceptually, this is a great design. However...There is a flaw in the sliding mechanism. When weight is applied unevenly, such as on one side of the sliding sheath, the sheath tends to get caught and will not slide without several pounds of weight added. So, if a heavy squirrel grabs one feeding perch and hangs on, there's a fair chance that the feeding port could remain open.It's a shame. This is a nicely designed feeder and the idea behind it is spot on. Unfortunately, the catching sheath is a major flaw that prevents this feeder from reliably doing what it's designed to do. I think Perky Pet can fix this without too much effort, but until they do I have difficulty recommending this feeder as a true squirrel-deterrent feeder.

I see lots of negative reviews about people not getting any birds showing up to their feeder with this. I didn't have my feeders out in the summer and just put them out for the fall. Within the typical few days, birds starting showing up. I haven't seen any issues with birds getting food out of the feeder. The feeder is nearly empty after a week, whereas it normally took 2-3 days when the squirrels could get to the food. So I have to assume that the feeder is working, by repelling the yard rats. I can't completely vouch though as I haven't seen one get denied personally.

All bird feeders have at least one drawback. Most have more than one.The only issue this one has is that it is a hanging feeder. That just means it can blow back and forth. So you want to thing about that when selecting a place to mount it. Putting this solid pendulum directly outside of a window would be an issue during your next storm for example.Other than that minor consideration, this is the perfect starter feeder.* Large capacity silo ensures that you are only going to need to service it once a week* Solid construction will last a long time even in neighborhoods with a herd of squirrels* Adjustable baffle allows you to calibrate the feeder to a specific weight to discourage birds larger than your target* Clear silo allows you to monitor seed level* Much easier to use than other adjustable feedersThere is no "perfect" feeder out there, but this is one of the best I have tried for seed feeding small to medium birds. It's also the one that Rudy and Phyllis (our local cardinal couple) prefer to use. I am sure you will enjoy watching your avian neighbors shoulder bumping for a spot around this low profile feeder.
summary: As perfect as a single feeder can be.

reviewText: I have this hanging with some other feeder on my deck.  So far the squirrels have not been using it (I'm still waiting).  The mechanism seems sound to keep squirrels away as long as it is not near a place where squirrels can reach out and grab it or perch off the the feeder and eat from it.It took a little bit for the birds to find it (not that untypical) but the small birds to seem to like it. (note do to the location of the baffle only the smallest of bird can access this)  I'm using black sun flower seeds in the feeder and they have no problems moving through the feeder.Nice looking over all (though nothing all that special)I live in Oregon so keeping the seeds dry is very important.  This feeder does that quite effectively and in fact I think the squirrel baffle helps with that.

I've tried out this feeder for a couple of months now, and here are my observations:The birds are very reluctant to use this feeder; they seem to dislike the perches:  I see a lot of "squirming" (do birds squirm???) as they try hard to find a comfortable place to perch; eventually, they just give up.  I haven't even seen any squirrels attempt to get seed from this feeder, so I can't vouch for the squirrel-repellent properties of it.In any case, this feeder is always left mostly full, while my other feeders have been completely emptied.  Any of the Brome bird feeders such asBrome 1024 Squirrel Buster Plus Wild Bird Feeder with Cardinal Perch RingorBrome 1015 Squirrel Buster Classicthat Amazon sells are a huge hit at my house, as well as being squirrel-proof.The Perky-Pet Squirrel Slammer, however, is NOT recommended by me or the local birds.

This doesn't come in it's own box and it wasn't packed well.  The clear guard was split in half and the perch base mangled.  The base is very thin metal, so I wasn't surprised, luckily I was able to bend it back into shape with my hands.  The means of squirrel deterrence is the base being spring-loaded so the weight of the squirrel pulls the neck over the feeding holes.  This is hindered by the thin base getting bent out of shape and by smarter squirrels simply holding on to the midsection and feeding upside-down (they could reach around the clear guard after I glued it back together).For this method of squirrel proofing, I prefer the feeders that have the entire exterior spring-loaded, so that no matter where the squirrel grabs on, the hatches close.  The same company even makes that style and sells it for cheaper.

It's High Feeding Time in my acre garden, as the Goldfinch babies are all fledged and Mama & Papa are busy feeding their youngin's. Up to 30 pairs of goldfinches are feeding their broods and space at my 3 dedicated goldfinch feeders is crowded to the max. I was therefore quite happy and excited to receive this feeder through amazon Vine and give it a try.Two Words: EPIC.FAIL.Like the abysmal failure of a waterer that I tried and reviewed, The Perkey-Pet Waterer Cooler, you have to scratch your head and wonder if the manufacturer's of these products actually TRY THESE OUT ON WILD BIRDS!!!! I had my feeder up and filled with premium hulled sunflower seeds for three days and exactly TWO goldfinches visited the feeder as opposed to the 100+ that visit the other three feeders with the same seed product.Here are the multiple design flaws:1) As the other reviewer mentioned, for small birds such as finches and sparrow, they can't reach the ONE row of seed ports from the lower perch and because of the almost 45 degree angle slope downward of the perch circle, once they hop up to the upper portion of the perch, they have to twist their body sideways to reach the seed port. HOW utterly AWKWARD for the poor birdies!2) Since large birds have 0% chance of using this feeder and the weight mechanism is SO sensitive, I had to actually screw the weight to it's tighest setting so the birds that DID try, could actually hop up to the upper feeding ring; when they were on the lower ring, once they tried to get UP, the port closed. Tightening the locking mechanism so it doesn't move completely defeats the purpose of this feeder.3) Almost every bird that I encounter approaches feeders from UP ABOVE the feeder, as they fly into the surrounding trees and shubs, make sure the area is clear and free of predators, and then they hop from branch to branch to get to the feeder perches. As far as birds can tell, from the EXCESSIVELY LOW POSITIONED CLEAR DOME of this feeder, they have NO ANGLE OF APPROACH from above...the dome masks the one ring of feeder ports. The two Goldfinches that I mentioned that actually used this feeder got pushed off of the nearest Droll Yankee feeder that is 3' from this one, and landed accidently onto the now locked feeder circle. They did stay there and eat, but did NOT return when given a chance.4) WASTE! WASTE! WASTE!!! My birdseed for goldfinches costs me $32.00/bag for 25#'s of premium hulled sunflower seeds! There is absolutely NO LIP whatsoever or seed catching tray on this device so when a bird pulls a seed out to eat, more seeds naturally follow suite. Now, this is normally NOT a problem with any other feeder as there is usually a slight edge to prevent seeds from falling/being pulled or there is a catch seed basin for pulled seeds to collect into, and the birds actually eat from that. Not with THIS device! No seed tray, no lip, so at the end of three days, I had over 3 cups of premium seed laying on the woodland floor, which made the raccoons and possums quite happy!!!Honestly, there are SO many design flaws with this feeder, that I'd go back to R & D and fire the whole lot of them! They need to have an adjustable dome or one that is higher so it doesn't obstruct flight to the perches; you need to have a lip to prevent seeds from tumbling out; and you need to have the perches at a less acute angle to the feeder so birds can actually maneuver their body to get the seeds.For the cost of this feeder, you'd be better off going to Walmart and buying a $10 buck tube feeder with normal 2" perches so you can feed the birds you love.
summary: Back To The Drawing Board on THIS one!

reviewText: I've seen a great number of "squirrel proof" feeders fail.  Squirrels are pretty darn ingenious when it comes to gathering food.  This one seems to be a pretty good deterrent, but I'll be honest about the one major failure of our "scientific" experiment:  We left our other (non-squirrel proof) feeder up.  The squirrels completely ignore this one and feast at the other one.The action idea behind this is pretty simple:  The bottom rung is spring-loaded so anything heavier than a few ounces will cause it to drop, closing some trap doors around the seed dispensers.  The plastic dome near the bottom is designed to keep squirrels from performing reach-around theft.  Again, with a neighborhood full of squirrels, we've remarked at how they leave this feeder absolutely alone.  We've seen a number of smaller birds (chickadees, sparrows, cardinals, etc..) have no trouble grabbing a snack on this feeder.  It's too small to feed our horde of common grackles, which suits me just fine as well.Overall, we're very pleased with this feeder.  The lid slides up on the hanging wires making it a very easy feeder to fill.  Its construction is sturdy enough that I anticipate it will last for several seasons.UPDATE:  December 10, 2013I'm not sure if it's the cold weather or just overwork, but the spring-loaded mechanism is no longer working, leaving the seed doors stuck permanently open.  Even stuck open, seed doesn't spill all over, which is nice in that the feeder is still functional.  It's just no longer squirrel-proof.  (It broke after only a few months.)
summary: Our squirrels now eat out of our other feeder...

reviewText: There is no way to attach the body to the base.  No screwing threads, no clamps, nothing.  It is completely useless, as it cannot be put together.  Save your money!

Like others, I experienced this feeder as one that keeps squirrels away. But unfortunately also the birds.I've had it up for about a week and the seed level maybe has dropped by 1/2 inch while my other feeders have gone empty.So the good news is that I've not seen a squirrel on this at all - but if it doesn't feed the birds then, what's the point?Other reviews here note that you can break off the plastic dome and the birds can more easily get to the food.However - the product description says "convenient cover protects birds and feed". So if I break it off, will the birds be susceptible to attack from above, and will the seeds get all wet and jammed up at the bottom? Maybe moving the dome up (or fabricating a new one) would be a better solution. I'll have to investigate if this is possible.In any case, I'm going to hold off until the winter when natural food is more scarce and see if the birds like this any better. The dome will also protect birds and seed from the snow. We'll see.

UPDATE:  After having the feeder up and available for several days, I just wanted to add that none of the birds seem to have any problems with the rain shield.  Birds as large as White crown sparrows use it with ease.  We have even had an evening grosbeak use the feeder!The only major problem, and presumably the reason for buying this unit, is the way the unit was designed to keep squirrels out.  The bottom of the unit is supposed to slide up and down (adjustable via a nut on the bottom of the unit which tightens or loosens a spring) to open or close the access to the seed.  while the concept is good, the execution is not.  Instead of moving up and down smoothly, the unit binds unless the force of weight is evenly distributed around the feeder.  Sorry, but I doubt that I can convince a squirrel to wrap itself around the feeder to balance the weight to remove access to seed!  If the weight of the squirrel is off center, the unit binds and does not close.========================Original Review:We have a lot of bird feeders and we have had a lot of issues with squirrels getting into the feeders even with cages around them.  We saw this feeder and decided to give it a try.  Here is what I liked about it:1.  The feeder is easy to fill.2.  The rain shield works very well.3.  The hanger is very well designed.Here is what I did not like:1.  The squirrel feature that shuts the feeder does not work smoothly.  Depending on where the squirrel jumps onto the feeder, it will hang up and allow the squirrel to access the food.2.  The tension adjustment does not work well.  I think it has more to do with the poor fit on the adjustment for the closure.Over all I would not recommend this unless they fix the fitting.
summary: Perky-Pet Squirrel Slammer Wild Bird Feeder

reviewText: This is a clever, clever bird feeder.  Although it is a little early in the season to do so, I filled this birdfeeder Monday with the very enticing delicacy in the squirrel world - hulled sunflower seeds. The cardinals and songbirds I feed each winter love them and they don't leave a mess on the ground in my flowerbed.  This morning, I saw that the birds had gotten accustomed to this new addition to the garden, and figured it wouldn't be long until Mr. Squirrel dropped by.Word spreads quickly in my garden, and sure enough it wasn't long before a fat squirrel jumped up on the birdbath, reached across to the shepherd's crook holder for the bird feeder, shinnied right on up to the top, crossed over to the feeder and slid right on down, came to the domed squirrel baffle above bird perches and slid right off onto the ground.  Undaunted, he climbed right back up and tried again with the same result. Next, he vaulted from the birdbath directly over to the feeder, grabbed a hold of the bird perch only to find the doorways to the seed slammed shut as his weight pulled the perch down, slamming the feeder shut before he could scarf down all of the seed.Needless to say, this feeder worked just like it is supposed to. I look forward to a winter of bird feeding without fussing about the squirrels. After all, there are always some peanuts on the front porch of our house for the squirrels to have instead of the expensive hulled sunflower seeds that I buy for the birds.

So far the item looks great - but I can't be sure of the squirrel proof capability until Winter and we're feeding the birds.  I can't put sunflower seeds out now because we have a bear that LOVES to tear every feeder down...so I'll check back on function in a month or two - eh!??12-29-13  Having trouble with the item - the tube keeps getting stuck and the birds can't get to the feed.  They go to the other feeders but sorry to say, this one is a bust.

It only took one glance at this feeder to realize it has a major design flaw.  The clear plastic "dome" that is supposed to protect the birds/seeds actually stops the birds from reaching the food.The dome is positioned only a few inches from the perch.  This is way, way too close.  Birds flying above the feeder can't land on the perch because the dome is in the way, and if a bird tries to fly in from below they hit their heads on the underside of the dome.  The feeder actually looks like something designed for hummingbirds which can hoover over their food.When this feeder first arrived I filled it with seeds, hung it in my yard, and watched it for three days.  In that time I saw not a single bird on the perch.  My other feeders were being mobbed by the birds so I took those feeders down hoping to lure some birds to the new feeder.  No such luck.  I went out to inspect the feeder and found a large crack in the plastic dome.  The crack wasn't there when I put the feeder out so I can only guess that a large bird must have flown into it.Afraid that the feeder might actually harm a bird I took down the feeder and tried to figure out how to remove the dome.  Using large pliers I put pressure on the cracked that was already there until the dome splintered and broke in half.  Good thing I had glasses on because plastic shards flew everywhere.  The feeder, now dome free, was hung back in the yard.I stepped out of sight and within seconds, SECONDS I tell you, the feeder was mobbed by birds.  The little birds landed on the perch and began to eat.  Several large doves flew around the feeder but were unable to land on the perch because of its sloping angle.  It was really funny watching the doves circle around and around trying to figure out how to land.  In the end they just sat on the grass waiting for seeds to fall from above.I haven't seen any squirrels on the feeder which is a positive sign.  I usually have to chase them  from the other feeders so I guess the squirrel proof mechanism is working.So if you already have this feeder and it is not attracting any birds you can fix the problem by carefully removing the clear plastic dome.  Once the dome is gone it is the perfect squirrel & dove proof feeder.
summary: Squirrels can't get to the food, but neither can the birds.  But works great AFTER a major alteration

reviewText: Perky Pets is a consumer responsive company and that's a good place to start this review.I have tried several of their products including 2 other Hummingbird Feeders. One feeder broke within the first month when the plastic screw base broke in the desert heat. I've got to admit, I break under the heat too, My wife called the company and the gentleman on the consumer line recommended this design of all metal base with glass container.The GOOD1. No plastic to break.2. Large mason blue glass container that holds plenty.3. It can sit in your sink on its flat glass bottom (which is directed up when in use) and is easy to clean with no extra brushes to buy.4. It's attractive to humans.The BAD1. Hummingbirds will sit on the metal surround perch occasionally but they don't particularly like it and they don't hang out like they do with other feeders. This is even though we have moved it to the birds' favorite prime location. My take is that the metal surrounding perch is not like a branch twig and doesn't feel so good as it gets heated.2. Because the hummers don't "Hang Out" we don't see them feed like we are use to seeing.3. They don't buzz us when the feeder gets low.The  (potentially) UGLY1. The metal base does not have threads into which to screw the Mason jar. Rather it has four,  inch vertical protruding (let's call them) anchors, which hold the Mason jar in place on the base.  You screw the jar into the base anchors and if you haven't applied level pressure the jar may be off kilter and leak when placed upright.2. I have not had this problem. But -- I can foresee a heavier bird trying to steal water and causing the base to drop off because of their weight.  The jar screws pretty tightly to the base and this major ant attracting incident may never happen. And if it does, I don't imagine the base will break. It's just curious to me that there are no screw threads. I'll report if it ever happens but I am holding my breath.This is a good, attractive feeder. I just hope the hummers will think so come the cooler 8 months of the year. I need also mention that the water level keeps dropping so birds are feeding. It's just not dropping so quickly as I would expect in the hot summer.

Long gone is my red plastic hummmingbird feeder! I'm so happy to have this stylish mason jar one on my patio. It looks much cleaner and is a hefty product, unlike my old one. I love how easy this is to clean. I'm thinking this feeder is going to last a long, long time.

Well made, large capacity, nice looking.  The only real complaint (minor) is it didn't come with any instructions on mixing the nectar.  Of course this is online and available all over the place but I was a little surprised it didn't have something.  Overall, I'm pretty impressed with this feeder.

We really like the looks of this mason-style jar feeder, and I also really liked that this one has a perch so the birds don't have to expend energy hovering while feeding.  My husband thinks our red glass one, thePerky-Pet 8119-2 Red Antique Bottle Hummingbird Feeder, looks too garish (and that one looks so nice compared to the red plastic ones).However, when I hung this one and the red near each other, the hummingbirds seem to prefer the red one, based on nectar consumption. In a few days, the red one was drained, but at least half the nectar remained in this one (I measured the same quantity into each one).  I even decorated this one with magenta paper, hoping to attract their attention.Another problem with this one, there is not a gasket between where the bottom and the flower-decorated top of the reservoir join together.  So when carrying it after filling to put it up, unless you keep it perfectly straight, some nectar can slosh out of the sides of the reservoir and drip.Several other reviewers have noted that their hummingbirds don't like this feeder, and speculate that it is the metal base.  However, the base on our red one is metal also (copper apparently), with a plastic bottom.  So the texture of metal "flowers" doesn't seem to bother them, but perhaps the cheap galvanized metal does make the nectar taste bad.I still think this one looks great, and did see hummingbirds using the perch.  My next test will be to put the red one farther away from where the hummingbirds like to congregate, while leaving this one near their hangout.  If the red one is not so close, perhaps they will use this one more?  If they still avoid it, I wonder if I can get a different base that they may like better?
summary: Attractive, but they like my red glass, perch-less, feeder better

reviewText: I was so excited to receive this hummingbird feeder. It holds a generous amount of water, the bottle is so attractive, and it easily comes apart for cleaning. However, the birds do not drink from it, at all. After a week of no interest from the birds, we put the nectar from this bottle into another one of our feeders that the hummers drink from all the time, and they wouldn't drink it from that bottle either. I have to agree with other reviewers that there is something about the galvanized bottom of this feeder that repels the hummingbirds. Very sadly, we threw out this feeder. It's no good at all.

This is my third perky feeder. I love the old tyme look that they have. They are build better than the walmart type by a long shot. Solid metal bases and thick colored glass. Any hummgbird would be proud to eat from this jar.This one is shorter / less tall than the others FYI
summary: These Perky Pet Feeders Are Cool

reviewText: This is a pretty hummingbird feeder as shown here.  It's made from glass and tin and looks nice.  It's easy to clean, easy to fill.  But what it lacks is a sturdy base.  Since no chain is enclosed to attach from the top to whatever surface it is to hang from, it must either be placed on a high surface (away from predators) or attached to a non-swaying surface.  While I like the design, I do not like how this blows around in heavy winds.  Few birds come to the feeder this way.UPDATE 6-20-14:  The aluminum base discolors after rains, making it look old.  I'm also having a hard time keeping ants out of this thing.
summary: Easy to clean, but hard to keep from swaying

reviewText: This is a nice hummingbird feeder. It is decorative without being gaudy. The only complaint I have is that the hanger at the top is too short when trying to hang to a mounted hook. The feeder has to be tilted to hang and the hummingbird mixture spills onto the deck every time. It does not matter how full the jar is. I had to rig a wired hanging loop from 3 gauge wire.
summary: Good feeder, hanger too close to lid

reviewText: This is a very nice item that adds character to a bird watcher's collection of feeders.  Not your run of the mill-plastic hummingbird feeder!  This quality piece is built to endure many seasons of use.  The simple and practical design with sturdy steal construction is visually appealing to both bird and enthusiast.  Easy to clean and fill, with reliable seal.  Feeder is heavier than normal which may make placement tricky depending on your location.  Highly recommended item.

I have 7 feeders hanging on my back patio right now. The three most popular - and it DOES appear that hummers have preferences - are red plastic Humzingers. Two less popular are Perky-Pet green glass, but they do get some hummers. When my kids gave me this one, at least I thought that it's going to be easy to clean, but also had high hopes that it would do a brisk business.I'm no expert regarding hummingbirds, but I've been feeding them for 13 years, and I know their peak periods when not nesting and during the fall and spring when real flowers aren't in bloom, and I swear that hummers are avoiding this feeder. I don't know if it's because the flowers are yellow, but I doubt it since that would mean they'd also avoid the green glass (I NEVER use nectar with food coloring). My only educated guess would be that the feeding holes or the metal around them has a taste that they don't like.I just can't recommend THIS particular Perky-Pet.

This is the second hummingbird feeder I've used. The first was bigger and I never filled it up completely because I though the food might spoil. This one is slightly smaller and I feel better about filling it all the way up. The hummingbirds food seems to go quicker in this feeder.It shipped intact and was very easy to assemble and take apart. There are just the two pieces, the top and bottom that easily screw together. I'd recommend this feeder. I like the vintage charm and will probably buy another one for the front yard.

Our hummingbird feeder gave up the ghost last Fall, so we were in the looking stage for finding another fun design. Bingo! There it was. And, so we bought it to use in the mountains. It will surely do the job well with plenty of nectar for the hummers.Very sturdily made and big enough jar to last at least a week for us. We are very happy with the look and the resting rack for those hummers that are willing to share their fortunes.  :o)

reviewerName: Jill Clardy "So many books, so little time...."
reviewText: I had some experience earlier this year with attracting hummingbirds to a new feeder in the yard. I had installed the cobalt blue Perky Pet feeder near an existing red plastic feeder that we've had for years, and the birds wouldn't have anything to do with the new feeder. Finally, I removed the old feeder and they adopted the new feeder right away.When I got this new Mason Jar feeder, I temporarily put away the cobalt blue feeder and put this one in its place. Though the hummers have been visiting, they don't stop by nearly as often as they did for the cobalt blue feeder. Several other reviewers expressed a concern that the oxidation process that is affecting the metal base that screws on to the glass jar might be giving an off-taste that the birds don't enjoy. The texture and color of the inside of the metal base has definitely changed, though I don't know whether it is affecting the taste or scent of the nectar.I do like the form factor of the jar since the wide mouth is much easier to fill (you don't need to use a funnel as you do with other feeders), and the jar is easy to clean. I do not fill it completely since the nectar doesn't get consumed fast enough and I've read that the birds prefer fresh nectar.I intend to bring back the cobalt blue feeder and install the Mason Jar feeder next to it as a further test of the birds' preferences. If I do note any differences, I will post an amendment to this review.Edit approximately one month later: The hummers just don't visit this feeder often. The glass jar wasn't emptied in a week, so I dumped it out and put fresh nectar in each week. I brought the previous cobalt blue feeder back, and the hummers abandoned this new feeder altogether. I can't say for certain that it is the metal cover that affects the taste of the nectar, but there is something about this feeder that doesn't appeal to them. I like the form factor and appearance, and it's certainly easier to fill than others, but I think the manufacturer should re-design the metal base to use stainless steel or plastic.
summary: Very Attractive High Capacity Feeder, But Not as Popular with the Hummers...

reviewText: This large feeder is cute in a down-home, Mason jar kind of way.  I like that is is very easy to clean and fill.  (I hate those hard-to-clean feeders that get moldy in places that can't be reached, detrimental for the birds.)  I change the food often so it doesn't spoil in hot weather, so I fill the feeder only part way, but it hasn't leaked so far.Now for the negatives.  The birds don't seem to like it.  I've had it out long enough for the hummers to get used to it, but I see them fly to it and instead of eating out of it, fly to the other feeder I have, a glass one with a plastic base.  The food is changed at the same time, so it isn't a matter of one being fresher than the other.I had expected a high-quality metal, but I can't find any information about what kind of metal this one uses.  It feels a little cheap.  It has become a little splotchy inside where the feed is in constant contact with the metal.  Perhaps this isn't good for the birds or perhaps it gives the food an off taste - I just don't know.  At any rate, whether it is the taste of the food or the feel of the metal, the birds aren't using this one.  A hummer feeder that the hummers don't like, cute or not, is pretty useless to me.  Given the birds' reactions, I wouldn't get this one again.

Perky-Pet Mason Jar Hummingbird FeederI've got lots of Hummingbird Feeders, but not one like this! *into My Shopping Cart it goes* :)* An aesthetically pleasing focal point, the blue/green colored antique Mason Jar style glass nectar container -- with embossed bird detail -- really sparkles in the sunlight -- goes with most any outdoor decor, or natural setting. The glass is thick and easy to keep clean.  I use a simple bottle brush to clean the inside. It's easier to clean than the plastic humming bird feeders I've been using.*  32-Ounce nectar capacity -- that's 4 whole (8 ounce) cups of nectar.  Just turn empty feeder upside down, unscrew bottom, fill with nectar, screw bottom back on, flip right side up, hang.  That's it! :)* Filled with nectar, the Perky-Pet Mason Jar Hummingbird Feeder is not all that heavy to carry around, or hang. The weight of the feeder, combined with the liquid nectar, seems to help keep the feeder from swaying back-and-forth, too much, in the wind (like the plastic ones do). A Plus, if ya ask Me. :)* An antique (brushed) silver colored base -- that comes apart - 2 pieces - (for easy cleaning) with 5 realistic (slighty raised) buttery yellow (metal) flower feeding ports add to the overall attractiveness of this particular Hummingbird feeder.  There is an ample little metal foot rail (or, whatever they are called) that circles the entire feeder for the Hummers to stand on (and rest) while eating.* There is no ant moat on this Feeder.*Neighbor-envy... The Hummers flock to my new Perky-Pet Mason Jar Hummingbird Feeder.  *smiles, sips espresso*tip:  this is the nectar recipe I've used for years:  add 1/4 cup of pure cane sugar to 1 cup boiling water -- stir till clear -- let cool -- add to Hummingbird feeder. Change out once a week...Does the Perky-Pet Mason Jar Hummingbird Feeder sound like what you may be looking for? :)  Would make a Fantastic Gift!  Highly Recommended!  --Katharena Eiermann, 2013

I've had this hummingbird feeder in my backyard for a few weeks now and have not seen any hummingbirds - though I have seen them at another feeder 2 miles away. I notice that there is no red coloring to the feeder whatsoever and have to wonder if that may be partly to blame for the lack of interest. I intend to continue to keep it clean, replace the food regularly, and keep an overall eye on it for weeks to come. If there is no interest after that I may abandon it in favor of another feeder with red on it. I'll update this review if there is any change. More time is needed to see how this will perform long term.I also am unsure about the size of the feeder. I don't fill it all the way up with food because it would be a waste. Previous feeders I've had are much smaller and lighter weight. I've had to put this feeder on a heavy iron post in order to hold it. A small branch will not do.

This is a beautiful hummingbird feeder.  We do not have any hummingbirds that come to our house as of yet.  Hopefully this will attract them.  You can easily unscrew the base to fill the jar with sweet water (many recipes are on the net).  Also, this makes it easy to wash as well.It is a wonderful piece of garden decor...so lovely!  I think we will enjoy this very much!

I wish I had read other users' reviews before hanging this.  On pure looks, this feeder is a winner.  It holds a lot and is easy to fill.  But after never seeing a hummingbird on it, I went to post my review and I now see other reviewers with multiple feeders say their birds avoid this one.  It would be bad enough if the birds just didn't like it, but if there's any chance the metal is harmful to the birds, I have to take it down right now.
summary: Cute, but I won't be using it

reviewText: It's the height of hummingbird season here in Michigan, and I have at least ten feeders out to accommodate a feeding frenzy.  The hummers use every single feeder....except this one.  What do they know that I don't?  It's obvious these birds have feeder and location preferences, but no matter where I position the Perky-Pet mason jar feeder, it gets no action.  If you want to attract hummingbirds, look elsewhere.The brands the hummers like and use the most here areBest-1  8oz. Hummingbird Feeder,Aspects 153 Mini Hummzinger Hummingbird Feeder, 8-Ounceand First Nature 3051 16-ounce Hummingbird Feeder.

This is a very attractive, nicely constructed hummingbird feeder. It's made with a glass jar and metal base. The feeder arrived at my door in a large box, well protected with lots of bubble wrap.The wide mouth on the jar makes it easy to fill and clean. I change the nectar several times a week and rinse it out with the garden hose. The jar is fairly large and holds about a quart of nectar. Nice if you have a lot of thirsty birds but I've only been filling it half-way bacause the nectar spoils in the summer heat.I've had the feeder up for 3 weeks now and only a few hummingbirds have used it. I see them in the flowers but not at the feeder. So far all I'm attracting are ants and wasps. I'm not sure why they don't use it. Perhaps after the flowers die off they will use the feeder. It will stay up until winter and I'll update my results in a few months. Until then it looks great hanging in my garden.

I love hummingbirds and delight whenever they come to my garden. We live in a very hot and arid climate so the hummers are here for a short amount of time. Well I am prepared for them. With heat that reaches 118-120 this summer I had this feeder hanging from one of the patios and we have had drips or problems. The humming birds love to feed from this feeder. Love it!

32 oz is quite large for a hummingbird feeder.Here is a recipe-One part sugar-Four parts water-Boil for 2 minutes-Cool and fill feederYou may want to get an "ant mote"Perky-Pet 242 Ant Guard for Hummingbird Feedersif ants are able to make the trek to your supply of ready energy.
summary: Sturdy and larger than I thought

reviewText: I was super excited to give this a try.  The humming bird fight over the nectar in the feeder that we have so I wanted to add another one to our porch.  This feeder is BEAUTIFUL!  Much nicer than the red plastic one that I have now.  The only problem is that the hummers will not feed from it.  I am not sure why that is.  I had such high hopes for this product but I guess the birds just don't like it.  It's so easy to clean and I had high hopes of phasing out my old one and getting more like this one.  If it doesn't attract the birds there in no point in getting another one.

Love the design of this feeder, the blue glass jar and especially the metal base. Oklahoma weather is not kind to plastic feeders. I am lucky if they last two years. Now getting hummingbird to feed can be a task in itself. You need to have the feeder out before they start nesting to encourage them to nest near. They can be picky when there are multiple food sources around and sometimes a single male may decide a feeder is "his" and will try to chase off other humming birds.As to this feeder, the 32oz jar means you don't have to refill as often, and the blue glass canning jar adds a nice artistic touch. The metal base reminds me of the old chicken feeders my dad used. It is very easy to clean and since even the flower feeding ports are metal, they won't break off and get lost like the plastic one always do.Overall a very nice product and a great addition to my bird feeders.

I am lucky, because I have a lot of hummingbirds in my yard. There are other feeders up, so they don't have any problem zooming around and trying out all of the feeders. They took to this new feeder instantly, and what I liked about it is the great vintage look of the mason jar feeder.This feeder goes well with my red antique bottle Perky-Pet feeder. The metal and yellow flowers also look great. This is a nice feeder, and it looks good too.

This is really beautiful but . . . the hummingbirds are still going for my hour-glass-shaped, red plastic feeder with the bright yellow feeding stations. Exclusively. It's been about 2 weeks now, and they don't seem to recognize this as a feeder at all.I also wonder if the metal base could potentially burn them if left in the sun---but that is just guessing. Ideally, you don't want the feeder in the sun anyway.If things change and they suddenly flock to it, I'll update the post, but sadly I can't recommended it right now. If you do buy one, make sure you have a very sturdy cord to hang it (it does not come with one), because it's heavy and the last thing you'll need during barefoot summertime is broken glass on your deck.  Happy humming!
summary: Gorgeous work of art but hummers aren't going for it

reviewText: The jar is adorable. Absolutely adorable! I love the vintage look and I love the blue. Just a gorgeous bird feeder all around.The jar is easy to clean. At first I couldn't figure out how toopen it but it screws on from the bottom. Easy enough to work.The birds don't drink from it. They don't even attempt to. I see other reviews which state that the hummngbirds will hang out on the feeder, but won't drink from the feeder. I haven't seen a single bird even come near the feeder. I have no idea why, but they seem not to be attracted to the same things I'm attracted to.
summary: I don't think they like it

reviewerName: Mr. Deeds "Opportunity is limited only by ima...
reviewText: The Perky-Pet Glass Mason Jar Hummingbird Feeder is well-designed and I like that the jar is real glass vs. plastic. It reminds me of the canning jars my grandmother had many years ago.I've used a couple different brands of  nectar and the hummingbirds do come and use the feeder. It's very calming to watch them even though their wings beat at a furious rate.Filling it is easy: Just unscrew the jar and fill it up, then screw it back in. The only issue I have personally when setting it back on the post is that some of the nectar spills out because I have to flip it around to hang it. But that's no big deal.To clean it, I just hose it off. It's very sturdy and I look forward to using this for many years ahead. And it looks nice too in our flower garden. Two thumbs up.
summary: Looks great, well made and the hummingbirds like it, too

reviewText: As a veterinarian, I would advise against purchasing this product.  The metal pan base appears to be galvanized, which means it is coated with a layer of zinc to prevent rusting.  If so, that zinc will leach into the water and is toxic to birds.  I returned mine for this reason. Feeders containing copper should also be avoided, since copper toxicity is also problem for birds.  Also avoid hummingbird food containing red dye, which is associated with birth defects.  (Instead just use a 1:4 mixture of sugar to unsoftened water; which is the same thing, without the harmful dye).  Since you probably don't intend to harm the birds you are trying to help, I would advise choosing different products.  If you have already purchased these products, I would advise returning them or just throwing them away.  You won't see the dead hummingbirds, new ones will keep coming to the feeder, but you may be killing them off without realizing it. Even if they put a clear coating over the metal, it wouldn't last long enough to prevent the hazard.  It's just a bad material for what would appear to otherwise be a nice feeder.

I have been using this Hummingbird feeder for the last few weeks and I love the design and the quality. I have total of four feeders in my backyard in the midst of flowering plants, and they are doing a pretty good job in attracting the Hummingbirds.This pretty feeder is large and holds about 32 oz of nectar; bigger than the other three I have. The metal base and five flower feeding ports give plenty of access to the nectar. This glass container has a wide mouth and working with this is simple and easy. Simply unscrew the bottle from the base and pour the nectar, and it is also very easy to clean. I have rated four stars for its design, quality and overall satisfaction.

Well made, no leakage of nectar like you get in a strong breeze with most hummingbird feeders. I'd buy another one in a minute. In fact, I might. The back yard is looking a little bare without one.UPDATE:  While they are adorable and make a great decorative accent the hummingbirds don't seem to like the metal base. They have actually avoided it. Cleaning can also be a challenge; the base is difficult to get off.

Love this hummingbird feeder.  It has large capacity and looks nice outside my bedroom window next to the windchimes.  The hummingbirds were right on this feeder the first morning I put it out.  A classic and worth the money.

I love the antique Mason Jar design of this hummingbird feeder, but the base is made of dinky-feeling, cheap metal, which feels completely out of sync with the sturdy glass feel of the container. I'm also not crazy about the hanger, which doesn't have a lot of room - it doesn't fit over the hook I use for other feeders in my backyard. I'm going to leave this feeder up for a bit to see if the birds like it better than I do, but as far as this human  concerned, this is probably my least favorite feeder out of the handful I now have in my backyard.
summary: Beautiful design, cheap construction, hanger too short!

reviewText: I love hummingbirds and use plants and feeders to attract them to our yard and near windows so we can watch them. I really like this cute Mason jar feeder. The jar is made of the blue/green glass to make it look old fashioned, and I like that. The jar also has the Perky-Pet hummingbird logo stamped on it for an added cute look. The handle/hanging component on top is very sturdy and fits easily to an established hook (no hooks or wall mounts are included with this product).The base is silver with yellow and white flower designs to attract the hummers, providing five feeding stations. There is also a bar circling the base for the little birds to sit or rest on, and they often sit here and go into their cleaning routines after a long drink.The base is easy to install. After filling the jar with a home made or purchased sugar water feed, the base screws on top, then you turn the whole thing upside down for the birds to feed. The jar holds 32 ounces which will last several days unless you have a huge amount of hummers. Then the whole thing is easy to take apart and clean. Easy, easy, easy!
summary: Cute, easy to use, easy to install

reviewText: I'm a landscape designer, and since nothing clutters up a beautiful landscape like a bunch of pots, tools, and hoses lying around, I've been looking for an organizational product to recommend to my clients to hide some of this normal gardening errata. Since most of my clients are moving towards using composite decking rather than wood because it is longer-lasting and easier to maintain, I didn't want to recommend a custom or premade product made of wood, because I think wood and composite don't look good next to one another. So I was glad to find this line of deck boxes and coordinating furniture, since they come in a few different colors and have a clean, streamlined look that I like.Pros:Very easy to put together. I put this together six months pregnant and only needed a little bit of help in carrying the box outside to where I was going to construct it. It went together intuitively, all the parts were there, and it only took me about 40 minutes to construct, even though I don't think of myself as very handy.Love the generous size. A few small children could fit inside the king-size version, so a couple of hoses, tools, and pottery are no problem.Color is lovely, no need to paint, stain, or maintain it for it to continue looking good.Easy to repair small dings or scratches. HighwoodUSA has a video up on YouTube which shows the process, which involves steel wool and pledge.12 year warranty for residential use.The bottom interior of the box has tiny openings in the slats so it breathes and drains well. While I was initially concerned about spiders getting in, when I thought about it I realized that spiders get into everything even if it is fairly well sealed, and are more likely to hang out in areas that don't have good airflow. I've been storing gardening tools in my box for about six weeks now and haven't seen so much as a web. So I think the anti-mildew factor of having a breathable box is a good thing and might even act as a spider deterrent.Hardware is stainless steel, so it should last as long as the box itself.The hinges on the lid allow you to leave the lid propped open, which is a very nice feature when you're rummaging around for a pot or tool.Cons:The lid is not perfectly watertight, so if it is left out on an uncovered patio or deck, water will seep in through the seams in the lid. If you want it perfectly watertight, I'd advise sealing it with some caulk.Can't sit on it. The way the lid is built makes it unsuited for sitting on, and I think if anyone over 170 pounds were to plunk down on it, they would probably break the lid and fall in. I would love it if the company would make a small tweak to their design so that this could double as casual seating.Two other things that should be noted. One of the major selling points making me want to check out this brand over other brands is that Highwood also offers decking material, fences, and trim, so you could in theory coordinate your landscape and your accessories seamlessly. On their website they have a beautiful photo of a townhouse or rooftop patio area with yellow walls that has some of their fencing material incorporated into the walls for an open feeling. I was imagining how beautiful that would look to have a couple of their chairs, a table, and the deck box with some of the coordinating fencing nearby in the landscape so it all feels pulled together and like it was designed at the same time.I also appreciated their great customer service. I had an issue where one of the products I ordered arrived with a broken part, and when I contacted them with a photo of the broken part, they were great about sending me a new one. I didn't need to send the whole shebang back to get my replacement part, and the customer service people got back to me quickly, shipped out the replacement quickly, and explained that they have just changed their packaging to avoid that kind of problem in future. So they seem like a really responsive company that I would trust to make it right if you have any problems either with shipping or where you need to redeem the warranty.Overall, this is a beautifully designed deck box that looks attractive on a variety of styles of composite decking. Though it costs more than similar products found at big-box stores, to me the improved aesthetics as well as the ability to coordinate it with other elements in the landscape make it a worthwhile purchase.
summary: Thumbs up from a landscape designer

reviewText: I received this deck storage box a couple of days ago, and WOW. First of all, it looks incredibly nice - it's not made of wood (could have fooled me!), but a high quality recycled plastic, designed to look like wood. It's very pretty once assembled! Ours is the Weathered Acorn color - just beautiful!It is heavy, about 70lbs, and it's BIG (There was a "team lift" sticker on the side of the box that it came in - that's how big it is).The assembly wasn't difficult, but it did take my husband and I working together to put it together, just because it's big and heavy. He probably could have managed to put it together himself had he so desired.I don't yet have it on my patio since there's currently over a foot of snow on it, but I know it will be just fantastic once out there! It's huge, so I'm sure it will hold everything I need it to - patio furniture cushions, gardening tools, BBQ tools, etc.This is really a stunning, quality deck storage box, and I would recommend it if you're looking for one that is sure to last.

I'm not sure where to start.  This is big. Really big. Like a person or several kids could fit inside of it.  I like that aspect of it.  It arrived broken, and it really was not packaged well.  Most of the broken bits were corners and I thought it was mostly cosmetic and it was so huge that I didn't want to repackage it and send it back.  It will take at least 2 people to put this together.  When you start putting it together you are quickly met with frustration as the predrilled plastic parts don't match up and are really sort of ridiculous.  It took a lot of time and a lot of frustration and the bottom line is that it still didn't go together correctly.  I have boughth some liquid nails and and I am going to try and salvage it.  But I'm seriously not impressed for something that costs so much.  IF it went together nicely and IF it didn't break in shipping and IF it was everything it claimed to be, in my opinion it should cost about $100, certainly not 5 times that.  I was really disappointed.

Mine was delivered broken, so I can only comment yesterday quality of the wood substitute and the overall appearance. It's definitely nicer than your average deck box at a warehouse store, but not 10 times as nice for 10 times the price.  The product is relatively light.  It looks nice, but not much like wood.  Overall, there are other products with a better value for the dollar.

I'm really happy with the assembled product but we had to work through some issues to get here.Packaging & Shipment- The box for this was huge so I wasn't completely surprised that it took some beating in shipment.  I was disappointed to see that there wasn't hardly anything to keep the product protected.  I wish there had been Styrofoam around the edges to prevent damage.  My box had some holes punched into it and it had evidently been banged around so much that it caused some chunks to be broken off of the unit.  One of these chunks caused a bigger problem as described in the assembly section below.Assembly- The instructions were pretty easy for the most part but it was just copied onto a normal 8x10 piece of paper with the ink being way too dark that you couldn't even see the pictures to refer to as the directions instructed you too.  Luckily there wasn't much too it and the wording was enough for me.  It was pretty easy to put together with the exception of the damaged section that was caused during shipping.  There was some pre-assembly done prior to packaging up the product and where a chunk was knocked out during shipment it caused 2 screws to pop out of places causing the front panel to not stay in place where it was supposed to.  We had to remove these screws and attempt to find a place to insert them.  We couldn't put it back in the same spot as it was now stripped out so we had to be a little creative and put some screws in where they weren't necessarily supposed to go.  One other issue we had was the cheap screws that they included and the lack of a spare screw.  The 2 screws that we had to remove came out bent and one of the screws that we were screwing into the top for the lid broke in half so there's not top to that screw.Look & Quality- I'm very happy to say that I'm pleased with the final product.  It looks very nice now.  Luckily most of the damaged section is not seen from the outside so it look really good.  There are some scratches on the back but luckily those won't be seen.  I love the size of this box.  60 X 28 X 24.  I can store a ton of stuff in it.  The quality of the "plastic" pieces seems pretty good.  We have the Weathered Acorn and I really like the color of it.  I'm new to the Highwood brand and was confused and thought I was getting actual wood.  That wasn't the case.  I thought it would've been nice to have a nice sturdy lid that could be used to sit on as well but that's not the case.  There will be no sitting on this box or it'll break for sure.Overall this Storage Box turned out great in the end and I would recommend it.  It looks very sharp.
summary: Looks Great but had some issues...

reviewText: This is a beautiful planter and a wonderful idea.  It fits perfectly in my windows and looks great.  Although, I've bought a shelf to put it on in the kitchen.  The biggest problem that I can see is that it only holds a 4" pot and once your herbs get root-bound your out of luck and will have to start over again.  Maybe next time they'll make the planter a little bigger.

Because of the photo of this showing pots of plants, I had anticipated that this would be larger than it actually is.As it says in the description, it extends to 2 ft long, and is 5 inches wide (on the outside). This means that the inside can only hold 4 inch pots. This is great for sitting in a windowsill, but it does not convert to sitting on the kitchen sink over the faucet.It is cute, and I will be using it - just not in my kitchen as I had hoped. The rustic wooden look makes it just right for a place in my sunroom along with my other plants there.What I liked - your pots won't drain and ruin the planter since it contains nice plastic liners to hold the water. It folds and is portable. It can be stored in a small area.

Cute and goes with any decor, really.  It is easy to pop out the plastic holders and place dirt, seeds, or other plants in there.  The expanding racks make sure that all plants get equal sunlight.  With this, a variety of herbs could be easily grown on the kitchen windowsill!

This product can fit in most windows, especially as it can expand and contract.  We have a house, but it would be especially good for those living in an apartment that wanted a little greenery.  It is best for small pants and herbs.  We are using it for herbs.  It doesn't seem to be made for out doors.  You would want to keep it on the inside ledge of your windows.  It is not built to hang.  The color goes with anything.

I received this planter from the Amazon Vine review team. My first impression: 'It's so cute!'Made in Chine out of wood with small silver-toned wood screws, you could easily drill drainage holes in the bottoms of the containers, even with the plastic inserts in them.Cute and well made, it's "Ideal for herbs and starting seeds" is what it says on the packaging, and that's exactly right!  It's not meant to house large plants.The 'vintage' washed finished would look wonderful in a cottage-style house or apartment. It would also be easy to paint this expandable window planter to fit your decor.FYI...I could also see this item being a great asset in a small space as added storage.  Acting as a bathroom accessory - behind a sink with limited space, to house things like lotions, washcloths, lip balm, and other toiletries.  Maybe as a spice shelf in a cramped kitchen.A window sill or table top which would accomodate a 24" long planter, about 4" deep would suffice for a suitable location.  I could see a couple of these on an apartment balcony doing very well in the spring, offering fresh herbs in the early summer.Two 3" x 3" boxes on each side flank the top planter which has a planting area of approximately 8.5" wide by 3" deep and 3" high.I will be using it for seedlings, and drilling holes in the bottom of mine for drainage. You could remove the plastic inserts and let the drainage seep through the wood, but the planter will last longer if you leave the inserts in place.I like this product and think if you purchase it knowing these things, you'll enjoy it.
summary: Cute, compact, great for herb garden starts and extra small item storage

reviewText: This is a nice product and is well made.  It includes clear plastic liners.  It is smaller than I expected.  The liners don't have the depth you would want for long-term plantings.  I am going to use it for seedlings so it will be fine for that purpose.  If you want something for permanent plantings this is probably not for you as there is not enough room for root growth and drainage would pose a problem.

This planter is just the right size for a kitchen herb garden! We have ours in our kitchen window, with 6 different herb plants inside of it, and it looks great! The product is billed as "expandable," and it is, but you lose a lot of space in the individual planter box areas if it's not fully extended. I got 6 small 3" pots for my herbs, and there would be no way to fit them all in unless the planter is fully extended. But, it's pretty compact, so for most people that shouldn't be a problem. Seems like it's well made and sturdy. Thinking about buying another one of these, because I love this one so much.
summary: Just the Right Size for a Kitchen Herb Garden!

reviewText: I like this planter but I really messed up when I opened it up because I threw out the plastic inserts that hold the plants! Make sure you don't do this! I thought they were just part of the packaging.I'm still using it but the water does soak through without them. I suppose I could put some other containers in there or line it with something to fix this.It looks nice on my bay window in the kitchen, I'm growing some different grasses. It might not fit into every decor but I think it looks good with plants in it.
summary: Accidentally threw out the plastic containers

reviewText: The CobraCo Expandable Window Planter is a convenient, small flower box.  It slides open to reveal 5 boxes on 3 levels.  Each side has a pair of 4" x 4" boxes, to give you 4 total, and the top is 4" by 9.25" long.  All of the boxes are 2 inches deep.  These are not for large plants, but can be used to grow herbs, microgreens, or flowers.  The boxes and the sliding connectors are made of wood, and each compartment is lined with a plastic box.This sturdy planter will brighten up your window sill with 3 levels of houseplants.

I was actually pleasantly surprised by this little unique planter.If you aren't expecting it to hold a tomato plant, and you use it as directed (for small clumps of herbs, or better still IMO, as a seed starter), you won't be disappointed.I found the perfect place for it in my sun room that gets LOTS of morning sun, on the window sill.  It fit perfectly on the sill, but I had to kind of squish the herbs I had bought at the store into the smallish plastic chambers (they were planted in those "in ground" pots you are supposed to plant directly into the ground, that decompose quickly).I then used the remaining chambers for starting some broccoli and tomato seeds, which again, given the size of the individual chambers, it's more suited for.PROS:Looks fine aesthetics-wiseNarrow enough to fit on most window sillsUnique, expandable design allows for planting many different kinds of herbs or seedsCONS:Should come with at least ONE extra plastic liner...I am sure these are non-standard, so if you put a hole in one...oops!Even considering the stated use of this, I think the individual chambers are just too shallow, and quite small from an area perspective as well.  Just slightly bigger would have been perfect IMO.Overall, I would recommend this if you know that you don't want a lot of volume of herbs (unless you want to buy several of these), or use for starting seeds indoors.  I like the fact that you have several separate containers, but the sizes of those containers is REALLY limiting as to what you can put in there.
summary: Great as a seed starter, needs more depth for much else

reviewText: From a distance (and in the misleading label photograph) the CobraCo WINPLNTR13 looks promising, but upon closer inspection, it proves to be more decorative than functional.A tiered planter that fits on your window sill and expands up to 24 inches in length, the vintage stained wood packs a rustic appeal, but the five shelves (with removable plastic inserts) are simply too shallow to hold much in the way of an indoor garden.  There are also no drainage holes in the bottom of the shelves, and although you could probably drill a few small ones if you wanted to, it still doesn't address the soil volume issues.I'll end up using it for starter plants (mainly herbs), which I'll keep in mini pots and let them sit on the planter shelves until they're ready to transplant.
summary: It has a nice, rustic appeal, but it's not very practical.

reviewText: I like the "country/cottage" look, so this planter looked perfect to go in my kitchen. And it is, other than it's very small. It will only hold VERY small plants. There's one picture at the top of the page that is holding those tiny little cactus that will fit in the palm of your hand. I think that gives you the best idea of just what will fit in here. There are little plastic containers inside each of the compartments, so your plant doesn't leak when watering.I liked that one of the other reviewers mentioned this would be great for organizing, too(which is the reason I picked this thing). Again, though, it will only hold very small items. I like it for holding hair supplies(bobby pins, elastic bands, etc). It would also be great for small, random "everyday" types of hardware items that stay in the house, like nails and screws. (You never know when the urge to hang a picture might come about).Overall, this is a cute planter, but make sure you realize how small it is before ordering!

We currently have this set up to grow herbs in our window.  So far, all but one has begun to sprout.  I will say this however, the "pots" are very, very small and when you go to water it only takes a very small amount before the soil is soaked and the water is pooling on top.  Other than that, looking forward to our fresh herbs!

This expandable weathered wood finish window planter is perfect for anyone who wants to get a head start on herbs on a window sill. Its hinges open to give 5 compartments for planting. Each is lined with a thin plastic so that soil stays put and water damage to the wood, or any underlying surfaces, is minimized. There is no outlet for drainage so keep that in mind when deciding what to try to grow. The largest compartment on the top measures about 8 1/2 by 3 1/4 inches with the other 4 smaller ones at 4 by 3 1/4 inches. When fully opened, the planter is about 23 inches long and stands 7 1/2 inches high. It could also be used for small flowering plants, catnip, or small succulents.I planted some seed of herbs for transplanting outside when the snow melts and placed it on a sunny windowsill. This is a great alternative to my usual sundry assortment of plastic seedling pots!

This is going to be a great big, bunch of fun to have, and I plan on ordering others as gifts.  Many of us use herbs constantly and to have this window starter garden is wonderful.  It looks nice, it is well constructed, and when not being used, it folds to compact size for putting it on a shelf out of sight.  As soon as possible I am going to the local market and buy seeds for my new found toy and food source.

When I got this, I giggled. For some reason, I had pictured this item much, much larger. It's a small little thing, with each box only measuring about 4" high. There are plastic inserts in each of the wood boxes, which means when you water, the box won't get damaged. This also means there's no drainage. The plastic liners are pretty thin, so I have no idea how you'd replace them if they become cracked or ruined. They look to be a custom size specifically made for this planter.The concept is pretty cute and I know it will look nice all planted up, once I find plants small enough to fit in it. Anything that doesn't stay small-ish long-term will need to be moved out of this and replanted.This item is made in China (like everything else), but quality is decent. It's all wood, but a pretty simple design. I actually took mine apart and painted the wood connecting pieces so it wasn't so plain and boring (check out the pics).It's very cute, but has a limited use since there are only so many plants of small size you can plant in here. Most houseplants will outgrow this quickly. On the plus side, plants for "fairy garden" are all the rage right now and they would make an excellent choice for this planter.
summary: Cute little box, but limited use

reviewText: I expected it to be narrower, which would've been a nice addition to my kitchen windowsill, but my sills are too narrow to accommodate this planter.  It would've been perfect to hold my small cacti & succulents, even herb seedlings.  I have crystals and stained glass ornaments hanging on my kitchen window via suction cup, whichy fall constantly.  If one falls on this, it'll topple over in a blink of an eye.I have a gazebo on my deck, one section gets plenty of direct sunlight, so this will be a cute addition to the sill.  Just don't expect to grow full size plants in this, unless they have a very small root system.  It'll be great for seedlings, something I'm constantly growing and/or moving around throughout the season.

The CobraCo WINPLNTR13 expandable window planter is very small. The plastic lined wooden trays expand, stair-step fashion. It is made in China.  I do not know what product the wood is finished with (China's reputation of using lead based paint or toxic chemicals gives me concern) I am not comfortable recommending any food seeds or herbs in it.  I would not even really want it in my house. It would be very small for any amount of window herbs. A ceramic or clay pot on the windowsill to snip chives would be better.

This is a nice little planter.  Not all the little when you get it fully expanded.  It fits herbs perfectly.  I have it on a stand and not in my window though because my cats like to get in the windows.Each section has a plastic liner so that the water doesn't leak through.

The item itself is well made and finished for the price, and extends easily to its full length. The main caveat is that if you have a window sill narrower that its maximum width, some of the lower plant pots are not really usable, and it doesn't really function well unless fully extended. Liking this planter much depends on your home's decor since it fits more with a classic rustic style look. It's one of those products that either gets re-gifted or is exactly what you need.
summary: A nice gift and suits rustic style houses

reviewText: This is an attractive little planter that I currently have on a windowsill in my office planted with some miniature ivy. I've also started some seeds in it as well. It's well constructed, a little sturdier than I thought, and has plastic inserts to prevent water spillage from the wood. One word of caution: this is ideal size for a window sill, but that also means it is TINY--- the trays are too small for many types of plants, and don't hold much soil.  If you choose your plants carefully and understand size restrictions I think you will be well pleased with this planter.

This is a nice little planter that would look nice on a window sill or perhaps out on a porch. I have a screened porch and I plan on putting herbs in it and just placing the planter on a table in the sun. Should be fun. It's about two-feet across when fully open and that would probably fit in most windows, too (though you might need a slightly wide sill). Each section of the planter has its own little plastic liner, but you really couldn't plant directly into the liners because there would be no drainage. But you could place smaller pots into each division--though you'd have to use plants that are 3" across or less. I think it would be particularly good for starting seedlings in small pots or for growing a small window sill herb garden. It would also be nice for starting African violet plants from leaf clippings.One criticism some reviewers have made is that it's rustic looking--no question, it is, but I like that. It's not cheap looking and if you look at the photos it is obviously rustic, so they're not hiding anything. It is small, but small is nice sometimes. No, you can't grow a giant basil plant in it, but yes, you could start several herb plants in it (or seeds in pellets). As for price, I don't know, I think if you can buy someone a nice little gift for $20, it's worth it.It's pretty nicely made, opens and closes smoothly and it has a nice rustic look. I think that, for the price, this would make a nice summer gift for a gardening friend--particularly if gave it to them pre-filled with some nice baby herb plants. It would also make a nice apartment window planter. I'll take a picture of mine once it's loaded up in a few weeks and post the photo here.By the way, this is not what it's intended for, but I was thinking it might be an interesting desk caddy for paperclips, etc.
summary: Nice little planter for starting seedlings or an herb garden

reviewText: The CobraCo Expandable Window Planter is a very cute, very small window planter.  It fits easily on the windowsill, and is a delightful way to display small plants. The planter comes with plastic trays that fit inside the planter to protect it from moisture.  The expandable design allows you to display the planter in several different configurations, and the classic design will allow it to fit in with almost any decor.

CobraCo Expandable Window Planter is a must have purchase for those who love to grow small indoor plants, herbs and seedlings with limited space.  This small, compact and tough window planter has six mini beds that are built sturdy and strong enough for years of usage.  So, if you live in a small house with no yard, an apartment or condo and love plants then you will want to purchase one of these window planters.  They're the perfect size for city dwellers who are looking to add some plant life to their living space or wanting to grow some fresh herbs.  The possibilities are endless and you will have a lot of fun finding out.
summary: Just the thing for plant lovers with small spaces

reviewText: The design of this window box is pretty good for temporary use.You can see the staggered look it has when its unfolded.  I wouldn't call it "expandable" because its really more of a "collapsing" window box.  Its either completely open or completely closed.  You can't open it half way.  You can't expand it.We are using it to start sunflower seeds right now.They have some relatively cheap plastic inserts that keep them waterproof.  These end up being the part that your plant actually grows in.  It helps to make it waterproof, but, the entire wooden structure is really "just for looks" as you are really growing the seeds in these removable plastic trays.  We removed the plastic trays from the wooden structure so we could show our children the root structures.We are going to use these for herbs next, after we've started all of our seeds.Its a nice window box, and has more appeal than a plastic one.  We're thinking of taking out the screws and just using it as three separate little window boxes that sit next to each other in a straight row.

I have to admit to being rather disappointed when the box with my window planter first arrived. The size of the planter is 24" long, as indicated on the packaging, but I wasn't prepared for how shallow the plant boxes would be. I seriously thought about how I might re-purpose this item before I went back to Amazon and looked at what other reviewers had written and also reviewed the product details. It was in the review of the latter that I made my decision about how to use this planter most effectively.As I have something of a black thumb, I didn't think I would be able to use this to start seedlings, and other reviewers had commented that the boxes were too shallow to allow root development. But looking closely at the packaging, I see that the manufacturer, at least for the purposes of their product picture, used the starter plants you get from the nursery and placed those directly in the boxes. Since those already have drainage holes in them, the plastic liners in these boxes can catch overflow without the necessity of drilling any extra holes. Thus, this becomes the perfect indoor herb garden--I don't have to start anything, just maintain what the nursery has already started going.And the width of the planter, when fully expanded, is very close to the width of the sink on my kitchen island. As my house is designed such that I have no kitchen windows, I've decided to leave this on the island, where the ready access to fresh herbs is most useful to me. The planter looks great now, though I have no idea whether I'll be able to keep anything growing for more than a few weeks. Any herbicidal tendencies, however, will be entirely my fault, not that of the planter, and the great thing is I can easily replace the plants at the change of the season (or upon their demise). In the end, I'm rather pleased with how cute this planter is and the fact that it's bringing some freshness indoors.
summary: Use With the Starter Containers From Your Local Nursery

reviewText: First of, the design is really sweet and appealing.  But, looking at the size and depth of each compartment, and knowing how tall and large herbs grow, I wonder how useful this planter will be as an herb garden.  The other potential problem are the plastic inserts:  too much water will make the roots rot since there is no drainage.That being said, I will still try to get a tiny herb garden going simply because the design is so pretty.  It also fits nicely on my kitchen window sill.  If you pick from your herbs regularly they might not grow top heavy, so please don't let my review deter you from trying this out.  Even if herbs shouldn't work, I can see this as an awesome cactus or other small houseplant planter!

It's a cute item, and will work well on the window sill.  Probably great for microgreens, starting herbs to move outdoors, or maybe cat grasses.  It's just too shallow for most planting.  Additionally, with no drain holes you have to be very careful not to overwater.Not for serious gardening, but a good idea none the less, if you want very small plantings without deep root systems.
summary: Don't Think About It For More Than Microgreens Or Starter Herbs

reviewText: CobraCo WINPLNTR13 Expandable Window Planter. This planter is very easy to set up and it fits nicely on a 6 inch wide windowsill or a shelf. It is a wooden planter that fits five small plants and is easy to water, it is plastic lined so it does not leak water on your windowsill or table. It is very nice looking and even makes a great center piece for a table.

This is not worth $19.85 which is the current price of this product at this writing.  It would be worth the price if several small plastic pots were included to hold the individual plants. It's 4 side compartments are very small and a part of them are covered by the box that's above it.  There are no drain holes and only the cheapest plastic insert to hold the dirt/pot in each box is included.It's too wide for any of our windowsills so if we use it, it will have to go outside somewhere.  It won't last long in the elements and is really too small to grow much of anything.  The top box is the longest and I can see growing a few herbs but nothing that grows a lot and takes up much space.  And I doubt it will hold together for very long since the metal screws are cheap and doomed to rust and break.Instead of actually filling it with dirt and growing real plants, a better use for it would be to put glass beads (colored) and placing artificial plants in it.  It would look pretty cute and wouldn't get ruined by actually using it for real.
