At first glance, it doesn't look very sharp, but everything I've tackled with the grass shears, hedge trimmer, and pruner have had clean cuts, not torn or shredded edges.A few minor issues- The hedge trimmer can't handle woody stems so it's only capable of trimming new (still green stems) growth.- You have to hold down two buttons - one of which is generally placed on the top - to operate all these tools so trying to hold them at odd angles to cut irregular places makes it difficult to hold the tool in the "on" position since my fingers tend to slip off the top button while twisting my wrist around.- The pruner can't stop midway - it's either push the button to move the blade full down or let go to let it come back full open. I'm used to using my manual pruners halfway sometimes to just grip onto stem ends that I just cut off to pull it out of the shrubbery, etc, which I can't do with this power tool.Overall, I'm happy with the sharpness and effectiveness of these tools. They're very quiet and I was even able to be out at 7 in the morning itching a gardening bug without bothering the neighbors or others in my house.

Update, the charger was flashing the green light, I cleaned the contacts but that didn't help, the battery was only slightly warm but I just let it sit for a while and when I put it on the charger it started charging so I guess it has to be almost cold to charge.Update-- 4/25/13 I was finally able to give it a good workout and it does very well on tall grasses, it won't cut down the heavier weeds but works well on taller grasses and the battery lasted for the entire lawn and we mow over an acre so there is a lot of edging to do and I even went over to the shed area and did some work where the ground is too rough for the mower (long story but it was never leveled properly), it still had some juice left after I was finished and the recharge is very quick, I didn't time it but I think it was about an hour or so to fully charge it again.This is the end of winter and beginning of spring so we really don't have much to trim right now so I couldn't give it a normal workout. We have a gas powered trimmer but it is just too heavy for me to use. This is much lighter and I want it to be able to trim some around the house so my guys can do the heavier stuff away from the house. The handle is adjustable, I do wish the rod was shaped more ergonomically but this will do OK since I don't plan on using it for hours. The charger works pretty quick but we did have it show it was charged but the tester showed it was only partial, put it back on and it charged the rest of the way. I like the tester to see how much charge is on the battery. It has 3 speeds, the lowest gives you more battery life but it may be too slow for some applications. I will have to play with that feature this summer to see what works best. I don't know how durable this will be but so far it seems good to me.

This is a "decent" weed whacker. . but. . . it's really going to have a very limited audience, mainly for someone with a very small yard.  The battery will only last 27-minutes on the low speed. .  .and significantly less on medium or high speed.  This is a single-string machine.  So at low speed, it's not going to do the job on most weeds.  Hence you're going to have to have a very small yard to be able to make it through with a single charge.  Having said that, it's very lightweight, and it's nice that it doesn't smell, like a gas model does.  But in the end, for the price, you might be better-off with a gas model for a large yard, or even a corded model, for unlimited time.  Hitachi offers a nice gas model currently in the same price range.Hitachi CG22EASSLP 21.1cc 2 Stroke Gas Powered Straight Shaft Grass Trimmer (CARB Compliant)

I do my yard maintenance myself. I used to use a corded trimmer, but it's still quite some hassle to drag the cord around, and the cord makes you feel the trimmer is more heavier. Later, I bought the Black & Decker 36 V trimmer later. So far, I am still very happy with this B&D; cordless trimmer.This WORX WG168 40-V cordless trimmer is one step upgrade from my existing B&D; 36-V cordless trimmer.WORK uses 0.08 diameter line, which is heavier and stronger than the 0.063 diameter line used in B&D.;It has 3 speed settings, while B&D; has 6 speed settings. I always think the 6 speed settings in B&D; is overkilled. The 3 speed setting in WORK is more practical. I use the lowest setting for normal trimming, and use the highest setting for tough grass. Be sure to wear long pants and safety glasses when running the WORK at the high speed setting. As it is really powerful and can spit out rocks, gravels with dangerous speed.There is a gauge on the battery, with one push of a button, you can tell how much juice left in it. For pure testing purpose, with low speed setting, I am able to get almost one hour run time. That's far more than enough for trimming my yard. It takes about one hour to get a full charge.The handle is adjustable along the shaft for you to find a good balance for operating the trimmer. It's very quite during operation.Three things I don't like this WORK trimmer:One, the shaft (or handle pole) is too long and the length is not adjustable.Second, I don't like the metal guide extended as it limit how close I can get to things. However, the metal guide in WORK is very difficult to flip back up.Third, something is not quite right with the line feeding feature. Not quite sure this is an intentional function, or it's a defect in my unit. Whenever I push the button to start the trimmer, it always does line feeding first and cut some line (about 1 to 2 inches long) off. If I keep the trimmer on without stopping, it won't do line feeding. To save the trimming line, I just keep the trimmer running, instead of switching it on and off.After using the WORK several times, I switch back to my B&D; 36-V cordless trimmer.
summary: Powerful, but some minor improvement needed.

reviewText: I bought the Black & Decker 36volt trimmer when it first came out and I used it so much I wore out two batteries. The WORX 40volt trimmer is a great successor.It has all the features that I wished were on my old Black & Decker;A faster recharge: My old one would take all night to recharge, this one only needs a little over an hour.A gauge on the battery: With a push of a button, you can see how much juice you have left. This should be standard on all rechargeable batteries.A throttle: You have three speed settings so you are not running at max all the time. You can "throttle down" for just basic grass trimming, but "throttle up" when you come across a big weed or a tough patch.Longer run time: This is an aspect of the throttle control, and I have got almost an hour out of this trimmer which is more than enough to trim my yard.Now there are a couple of things that could be improved;All rechargeable trimmer should come with two batteries! One to trim while one recharges. In fact I haven't even found where to buy an additional battery.Needs twin cord head: All the commercial trimmers I use at work have twin cord on their heads but this one has just a single line. The head is easy to open and refill, but I just think the twin cord cuts better.It is very light almost too light: As I am used to using commercial trimmers at work, this one is just too light. I am considering adding some weights to the head just to make it easier to handle. And speaking of the handle, it needs a O ring to attach a shoulder harness so we can have that option.Overall this is a great trimmer and a definite improvement over previous models and is great for basic house and garden work.

reviewerName: Modern Blue Argonaut "No I do not have a shoe...
reviewText: I haven't edged in about six months.. shame on me because I ran out of string. This is so much better than the budget edger/trimmer I was using before, and it costs more than twice as much. For that I'm impressed with the power this has, the design, and that this can be recharged rather than using my corded electric trimmer. It's easy to use, the battery is more than sufficient for my large yard. I'm new to Worx products but after browsing their other outdoor/lawn products I think I'll be purchasing more in the future and considering this brand rather than my old standby, Black and Decker.

EDIT::: After more extensive use, I'd like to add the following1.  I had the dang metal guide on upside down.  Once I'd switched it, it flips up and down no problemo.  2.  If you use the trimmer on HIGH to get through particularly tough weeds, the battery life is SIGNIFICANTLY diminished.  If you consistently have large areas to edge,  you might want to go with a gas model.  For the average homeowner who keeps up on their yard, it will not be an issue.My trimmer experience ranges from an old school corded weed eater, a first generation Worx NiCad battery trimmer, a Toro Lithium battery trimmer and this Worx Lithium trimmer.  Each had been an improvement from the last.  Firstly, battery edgers are greatly preferable to hauling around an extension cord for an electric trimmer or the noise and fume pollution of a gas trimmer.  The trick is to find a battery trimmer with sufficient power and runtime to suit your needs.I didn't think I'd ever want a Worx edger after my my first experience with the original Worx GT.  It was gutless and the NiCad battery would give out before I finished half my yard.  I upgraded to a Toro 51486 with a 24 volt Lithium battery, 12 inch cutting width, weighing in at 8 pounds and it has always had enough oomph to edge my entire lawn before running out of juice.  As a 5'6" female I appreciate it's height adjustable shaft and wheel guided edger.Then I was offered a chance to test the new Worx WG168.  Pretty excited to see if they've improved from their earlier model.It took some time to assemble. The directions don't do a good job of showing how the handle goes on and I was convinced I'd been given the wrong part until I realized I had it upside down.  The dang sticker that covers the line cutter took me a good 20 minutes to peel off.  Once I had it put together, it took only about an hour to charge the battery.  Love that the battery has a built-in tester that indicates how much charge remains.When you first turn it on, there is a high pitched whine before the cord starts spinning.  This might be the line feed function.  Personally, I didn't notice the line feeding out automatically, but it is easy to push a little button down by the spool and manually feed line when you need it.  The trimmer takes a heavier line that doesn't break as easily, but it does not seem to part of the Worx "spools for life program" like their GT line.  The trimmer has three speed settings.  Lower speed will give you a longer run time and provides sufficient power for edging grass.  The high speed will use up the battery faster but gives trimmer power comparable to that of a professional grade gas trimmer.  The medium setting gives the best balance of run time and power.  Frankly I found it a little scary to use on high!  This is the first trimmer I've felt I really needed long pants and safety glasses to use.  I recommend you think twice about using high speed if there are any rocks or gravel present.It's very easy to twist the trimmer head into edger mode.  There are no wheels, but you can flip out the metal guide and kind of rest the head on that and slide it along the sidewalk or driveway.  I don't like having the metal guide extended when I'm in trimmer mode because it limits how close I can get to things.  The metal guide is inexplicably difficult to flip back up once it's been flipped down.For me, this unit was not as ergonomic as my Toro.  Though you can move the handle to adjust the balance, the shaft length is fixed and it is just too long to be really comfortable for me.  My husband, at 6' will think it's perfect, though.If you're looking for a heavy duty, powerful trimmer without messing with a gas motor this is a great option.  If you don't need that much power, the Toro 51486 Cordless 12-Inch 24-Volt Lithium-Ion Electric Trimmer/Edger is another great choice.

I have about 3500 SF of new sod and have been using this weekly (four times since purchase). I can mow the entire yard in one hour and the charge lasts through the entire yard. Much easier than pouring gasoline and pulling a cord 20 times. No shaking from the motor. Pretty quiet also. Easy to maneuver around rocks and over hills because it is light. Mulches well as long as lawn isn't wet. Will clump in wet areas. I'll post an update in about one year to make sure the batteries and mower last a good long time. It is a big investment so if it last a few seasons then it will be a five star for sure.
summary: Cuts mowing time by 1/2. doesn't shake you to death

reviewText: I have some tennis elbow issues and replaced my Toro gas high wheel mower with this and could NOT be happier.  Easy, easy, easy to start!  I have a wooded yard, so the grass is fairly sparse and I don't use the catcher, but have it set to mulch.  The yard looks great.This mower is quiet and I do not worry about mowing early in the morning or on a Sunday.  The Toro was self propelled and I really cannot tell the difference "pushing" this light mower.Was so happy, I bought the trimmer and blower which use the same battery setup and I am done with gas cans and the gas/oil 2 cycle mix.
summary: Light, easy start, great for me!

reviewText: Purchasing this Greenworks mower was a leap of faith for me.  I have a very large (~10,000 sf)  and somewhat hilly lawn, and for the past 15 years I've used a big, twin-bladed, 33" cutting path, 10.5 hp, self-propelled, four-speed, semi-pro Craftsman lawnmower.  It was fast (I could do the whole yard in 40 minutes), but it was loud and required all the usual small-engine maintenance.I just mowed the lawn for the first time using the Greenworks battery-powered mower and I couldn't be happier.  I expected it to take much longer, because of the narrower cutting path, but it went faster than I expected because the mower is so light and maneuverable that I wasted less time doing turns.  I was worried about it not being self-propelled, but again the light weight of the mower really made a difference.  It was more of a workout that walking behind the Craftsman self-propelled mower, but not bad at all.  I'd liken it to pushing a high-wheeled stroller with an infant on board.On this first pass, I took off the bag and used the mower in mulching mode.  It worked very effectively, including on the occasional pine cone.  My grass is mostly fescue, which is fairly thin, and the mower cut it easily and evenly.  In a couple of thicker patches the electric engine rev'd up automatically and handled the denser turf just fine.Starting the mower is very simple -- push one button and pull back the lever.  Much more convenient than starting my old lawnmower with its pull cord.  One delightful (and unexpected) advantage is that the mower is much quieter than my old gas mower.  I always used to wear ear protection when mowing, but didn't need to with this electric mower.  My family reported that it was also much, much quieter inside the house.One thing I'm looking forward to is the lack of maintenance and not having to prep the mower for winter storage, or change the oil, or store gas.I can charge the batteries from our solar panels, which makes this a very green solution.  I was surprised to learn recently that small gas-powered engines in lawn equipment are very dirty compared to modern cars, so this small change of mower makes a big difference in terms of my environmental footprint.The mower comes with two batteries, a 4ah and 2 ah.  Both can be installed at the same time, and the mower automatically switches to the second battery when the first runs out.  Unfortunately, the combination was not quite enough to finish my lawn.  Two 4ah batteries would be sufficient, and I wish this option were available when purchasing the mower.  A second 4ah battery is pretty expensive, but because Greenworks prices its bundles (i.e., piece of equipment together with a battery and charger) pretty aggressively relative to the cost of batteries alone, you can get a spare battery at fairly low marginal cost if you buy multiple Greenworks products.  As it turned out, I also wanted a cordless electric leafblower, so I ordered a Greenworks leafblower plus battery and I now have three interchangeable batteries, which is more than enough for my lawn.Bottom line:  This mower cuts smoothly and evenly, mulches well, does an average to large lawn on one charge, is light enough to push without needing to be self propelled, is much quieter than a gas mower, needs less maintenance than gas-powered small engines, and is seriously green (especially if you have solar panels like we do).  For me, it makes mowing a lot more fun (or at least a lot less of a chore).  Two thumbs up.Update May 5:  I ordered this mower through Amazon.  I ordered some additional items directly from Greenworks website.  One of the packages arrived, but another got lost in transit.  I emailed Greenworks over the weekend and received a reply first thing this morning that they would ship a replacement today.  Couldn't ask for a faster or more complete resolution.  So, in addition to really liking the product, I'm also impressed by the responsiveness of their customer service.  I hope this company does well.
summary: Great Battery Mower At Last:  Quiet, convenient, green

reviewText: Word of warning from the start: read and re-read the description. The description mentions "Get up to 70 minutes of run time with the G-MAX 40-volt high-capacity 4 Ah and low capacity 2 Ah Li-Ion Batteries (included with purchase)" which I didn't take as it includes one of each capacity battery. You get one of each which I was not exactly happy about. Additionally, extra 4 AHr batteries cost $149.99 list.On to the real stuff.I started looking at this when considering the various cordless electric mowers that are available. I like it better than the lead-acid battery based cordless mowers due to the size and weight of the batteries and the maintenance required for them. Our gas powered mower was getting annoying with starter cord breaks, oil and gas maintenance, and the self-propelled portion was starting to wear out. It was important to me to go green and make things simpler than gas powered.ProsOut of the box, this was so easy to set up. There was even a slight charge on the batteries to try it out (still, fully charge before use). It said "team lift" on the box but it wasn't that heavy. No tools were need to get this prepped for action.The first thing I noticed was the "push the button, pull a lever and mow" simplicity. There was no priming, no pulling the a starter, possibly multiple times, and no flooding. It just turned on and I was ready to go.Next thing I noticed was how light it really is. Coming off the weight of a heavy, self-propelled (weakly), all metal mower going to this largely plastic one was a gift. I didn't even notice it wasn't self-propelled. My initial thought was that it could easily have been built by Fisher-Price since it reminded me of my son's toy from so many years ago. Pushing it around is very easy.This thing is super quiet. Even more fun, it sounds like a bumblebee compared to the gas powered monstrosity I had previously. I even had a neighbor approach me after a mowing once with concerns that I was "losing it" thinking that, with my headphones on, I was pushing around a mower that wasn't running. I confirmed my sanity and explained the battery powered mower really does save your hearing.ConsI saw several references to uneven cuts and I would have to agree. Although some speculate that it is because the blades don't overlap, I think it is because of the mostly solid bottom of the deck. Most unevenness I found has been when dealing with dandelions that are so much longer than the rest of the grass. They tend to be missed if off to the side or dead center. There will also be some missed blades of grass on each pass, but I'm not meticulous about my lawn so it isn't an issue.There are quirks, too. I had the mower quit twice when it transitioned between batteries (the control circuitry uses one battery then switches when it runs out). Granted, it was early on and since then, I have only had it slow some, then kick in with the second battery.I also noticed that it adjusts the blade speed when the grass gets thicker. This is a great idea to maintain an even cut, except there is a time lag when you hit a change in the lawn. I have started working the system so that when I hit thicker lawn, I slow a little while the motor controller spools up the rpm's to handle the load. Minor issue, but the alternative is to have a machine that is psychic.The amount of time off full charge is a little less than advertised. It could be a smooth, even lawn that it was tested on so my irregular lawn might be what cuts the time down. I don't have a huge lawn, but it takes multiple sessions to mow it. Inconvenient, but I also don't get tired. If the weather cooperates, I get it done all in one day. Other times, it takes a couple.Overall, I am quite happy with this mower. I wish it had (2) 4 AHr  batteries instead of (1) 4 AHr and (1) 2 AHr. I also wish the motor controller was more responsive to changes in lawn resistance and better at the transition between batteries.None of this would prevent me from buying it again.
summary: Great, lightweight mower for city lawns. Without gas.

reviewText: We bought this after a (very expensive ~$400) Troy Built mower decided it didn't want to work hardly at all anymore. We bought this hoping for the best and it works amazingly well. We put both batteries into the device - just in case - and it thus far has only used one battery for the entire yard. If you're on the fence (or lawn!), just get it. It's light, powerful, and does a great job of mulching!

I have a relatively small lot, and this mower works fine for it. It's quiet, and is a pleasure to start compared to a gas mower. I'm replacing a mower with a Honda engine that was guaranteed to start in a single pull, and usually did. But this one is far easier. It's nice not having to deal with a choke or the smell of the engine. I don't need hearing protection either, it's easy to fold and store, and weighs very little.Setup was relatively easy and the only "problem" I had was that the instructions said I would need some force to remove the insert for mulching mode. Mine sat there loosely. I called customer service to find out why nothing was letting the part snap in place, and they said (after looking at a bunch of them locally) that mine was fine and they were all like that.Unfolding it and setting it up was no problem. Starting was no problem either. Even though it's the reverse of the way gas mowers start, it was clear from the instructions how to use the button and pull back the bar. Things worked fine the first time. Subsequently, letting go of the mower didn't stop it. There is a red key that can be pulled out, but this seems like a potential safety issue. I could walk away from my mower and it will stay on until the battery dies.The other question I had was with respect to the battery charge level. There is a button, and some reviewers implied that it was easy to use. Mine took a lot of effort to push. I posted a question about it and got mixed answers. Some owners said it was quite difficult. It turned out that if you press the button when the battery is installed, it's easy to see the charge level. But if you are holding the battery in your hand, it's very difficult to get the leverage needed to push the button.Overall I'm satisfied with the mower, but I had a three star experience with it.

Most people who try infrared grills think it's the best thing since sliced bread.Pros:- This grill runs hot! and produces an excellent sear on meat.- No flare ups- Even grilling as a result of even surface temperature- Easy grill cleanup* because there are no flareupsHowever, after a while (1-3 years depending on how often and how much you grill) on going maintenance costs and other issues resulting from the nature of infrared grilling (gas heating up a perforated panel that heats up the grill).  These expensive and fiddly bits of maintenance to keep the grill running smoothly and performing as well as it should are:Cons:- Preferably after each use, the grill is cooled down and the perforated panel disassembled (screw driver needed here) for cleaning.  This is the panel that the gas below heats up which in turn evenly distributes heat up to the grill grate above.  It also catches all juices from the foods cooking above and is responsible for preventing flareups.  As such, the little holes tend to get clogged and gummed up and need to be cleaned frequently for optimal performance.- After a year or so, this perforated metal sheet needs to be replaced with a new one because one can only clean gummed up food-juices out of holes a certain number of times.  This is a major part and is also quite expensive.- It is this maintenance that eventually wears down all but the most devout of infrared grill users.  This is why there are so many infrared grills that are approximately 2 years old in the classifieds section online and in print.  Many people just give up because of the effort and cost of maintenance, some others just use it until the perforated part dies, sell the old one and buy a new one and start all over again.  Others sadly, think their grill died without realizing that a consumable part needed to be replaced by design to restore the grill to its original performance.Additional notes:As with all portable grills, this one has a single burner. As this grill is also infrared, the entire cooking surface is one constant even temperature. There are no hotspots.Once maintenance issues and costs of running an infrared grill are understood, this little unit is recommended as a high performance portable grill and also as an inexpensive introduction to infrared grilling.

Love the new Char-Broil 12401734 TRU Infrared Grill2Go X200 Grill. It's a portable table-top grill so it's perfect for camping and traveling but would also be great for anyone that just needs a smaller table top grill for a deck or balcony. Ours fits perfectly in our RV storage area but we've been using it at the house too just on top of our picnic table. It's very sturdy and great quality but still compact and light enough to move around.It runs off of the small disposable gas bottles but we have a hose similar to theColeman High-Pressure Propane Hose and Adapterand just hook ours up to our 20lb propane cylinder which is more convenient for us and more economical too.The Char-Broil has Infrared technology which is designed to sear your meat and keep the juices in. It works great. This is the first time that I've used a grill with the Infrared technology and was quite pleased with it. We've cooked chicken breasts and steak on it and the outside was seared with grill marks and the inside was juicy and delicious. The chicken was absolutely wonderful and cooked to restaurant quality. It also held more food that I expected. I got 2 whole packets of boneless chicken breasts on it at a time and we cooked 6 steaks on it, on another occasion.We are really loving this grill!

Wow. I love this grill! I've never had a gas grill, much less an infrared one, before this one. We've always done the charcoal number, either using those cheapie disposable grills from the grocery store or theLodge Logic L410 Pre-Seasoned Sportsman's Charcoal Grillthat I finally sold because it was too heavy for me to deal with and too small, too. Some say charcoal grilling makes for better flavor, but I like the results from the Grill2Go much better. Meats definitely turn out juicier and cook more evenly on this grill.First, the grill grate has at least twice the surface area of my Sportsman's grill. We can cook an entire meal for two and then some on the Grill2Go. I love the temperature gauge on the lid and how much room there is "under the hood." The latches are solid and sturdy, as is the rest of the grill's construction. It's physically larger than I first thought when I saw the picture; I was imagining something more like the other portable grills I've used. But it fits on the second shelf of one of the grey metal Costco utility shelves in my kitchen so I can keep it stored and out of my way when not in use yet always ready to whip out when it's time to start dinner. We live in the South, so this grill will definitely see some use this summer. I really like it!
summary: Big, sturdy, well made, but lightweight grill

reviewText: Let it be said--this thing is amazing!I needed a little outdoor grill, and had purchased a really nice one for my boyfriend about a year or so ago (the Cuisinart CGG-200 All-Foods 12,000-BTU Portable Outdoor Tabletop Propane Gas Grill) and I liked the size and specs of that one...but this one came up to review, so I was happy to compare the two.  This one is cheaper (cost) and let's face it--Cuisinart has a really good name when it comes to cookware, so the competition was going to be stiff.Well, my boyfriend offered to do the comparison.  Since he is the BBQ officianado, I obliged...and became a bystander in the cooking process, but an active participant in the eating process :)He grilled up some steak the first night.  Really nice steaks from Costco (USDA Prime).  YUM.  The Char-Broil kicked the Cuisinart's butt.  The steaks were MUCH juicier, and the flavor was richer...Second night, chicken.  The chicken cooked up relatively the same on both grills.Third night, sausages.  The sausages were definitely juicier.  They seemed to get to temperature more quickly, too.Fourth night, mahi mahi and salmon.  The fish was outstanding.  This grill cooked it up faster and it had a really nice crisp edge (not too much) and the inside was perfection.  The Cuisinart did a good job, but the edges were blackened before the inside got to temperature.So, now that our test is over, you'd think I'd get my grill back.  Nope.  So far, he has all sorts of reasons to keep it at his house.  haha...!The Char Broil beat the CuisinartCuisinart CGG-200 All-Foods 12,000-BTU Portable Outdoor Tabletop Propane Gas Grillwithout a problem.
summary: Lent it to the boyfriend and can't get it back!

reviewText: Right out of the box, set up was easy. Instructions were adequate but left out some information, like where the vaporizer bar goes (inside, over the burners). There is much attention paid to properly attaching the propane tank and several warnings, so I performed the soapy water test to be safe.The igniter works well and efficiently. No need for matches with this product. If it does fail, however, there's a hole through which it can be lit manually.The thermometer on the top of the grill is efficient but, obviously, each time one opens the grill to check the food, the thermometer becomes ineffective and one needs to give it a little time to readjust once the lid is closed.It's very well-built, sturdy, and stable. I won't be traveling with it, but can see that the size and portability are perfect. It's a good size for four to six people, or just one, if that's how big the party is.There were no flare-ups at all. I've had several burnt areas on food prepared on my "other" barbecue and now it seems like I'm a better cook, when it's really just the grill.I love the grill surface itself. The size is perfect and fits in my sink for a good scrubbing. That's a huge plus for me.There's no fuel gauge for the propane tank. I understand that one can be purchased separately. That would be important since it's no fun running out of propane in the middle of grilling. It's also possible to purchase a converter so a larger tank can be attached.
It does a great jobs on steaks which is all we cooked so far heats up fast sears them just great . Its light and easy to move and the price is good .
summary: Wow works great and is light weight and sturdy

reviewText: I love this little grill.  I acquired one a couple years ago that was advertised as portable, and it was anything but.  Then I broke down and got one of the charcoal hibachi grills and it just seemed so flimsy.  I checked the weight of this product before I ordered it (26 pounds)which seemed heavy when I read it, but is actually not that bad.  The thing is, this grill is so durable that this is probably the last one you'll buy.  The other "portable" grill I have is also infrared, and they both cook very well.  If you're looking for a long-lasting grill that cooks well then this is the one.
summary: Durable and portable, will last a good long time!

reviewText: The Char-Broil 12401734 TRU Infrared Grill2Go X200 Grill is a no-frills portable tabletop grill that comes almost fully assembled. I always dread trying a new grill because the assembly takes forever. Not in this case!Despite its small size, it can handle enough food for 4-6 people. If you plan to use it with a large tank you need to get the propane hose adapter otherwise you'll need to use the small (and expensive) propane cylinders. The "infrared" part revers to the fact that food that you cook will never come into contact with flames since the grill grate surface is closed. That's where the flareup reduction comes in.Other little nice touches.. the started doesn't need any power to spark and it's solid and compact. You;ll need a high surface to plate it on to cook comfortably.Cleanup is a bit of pain since you need to remove the grate and clean it in the sink since unlike traditional grates you can't just scrape left over crud into the fire.There are no side-trays or other little conveniences and this is definitely a travel grill rather than something I would use everyday.
summary: Portable, easy to assemble, tabletop grill, not for everyday use

reviewText: Although I own over 10 grills, this is my first infrared grill.  For my current tests, I grilled hamburgers, brats, steak, jalapeno poppers (wrapped in bacon), and finally some chicken thighs.  Although flare ups were reduced due to the design of the grates, flare ups certainly are not eliminated with meats that have high fat (i.e., brats, bacon, and 80/20 hamburger).  Part of the flare ups that I experience, though, might have been due to me having the heat set too high as I was still learning the traits of this grill.For this review, I will be comparing the Char-Broil infrared to Weber's Q120 gas grills.  Let's dive right in to my PROs/CONs...PROS====+ 98% pre-assembled (no tools required for remaining parts)+ External temperature gauge+ No battery needed for ignition button (but I have had these types of buttons degrade over time)+ Convenient side handles+ Quality, solid constructionCONS====- Front handle not deep enough (fingers can touch hot metal if fully gripping handle)- No side trays (Weber's side trays nicely folds into the grill when not in use)- Using too much gas OR leaking gas?- Requires cleaning after each use and is harder to clean than competition- No stand or cart option to available to buy- No place to hang grilling tools- During daytime, difficult to see through infrared grate in order to check flame is still lit- Harder to grill precisely or with sensitive items (e.g., fish) due to hotter temps, even on low setting- Struggles to work with LP tanks bigger than 1 pound (although not officially supported in manual)After opening the box, I was happy to see the grill mostly pre-assembled.  The only real gripe during assembly is that the manual does not show how to install the vaporizer bar which other reviewers have also complained about.  I'll also add that the manual doesn't talk much about the grease pan, and I found it a tad tricky to remove.  Thankfully I am used to grills so I had a good idea how to install and use these two items.The company claims that food grilled on an infrared will be juicier -- and this is probably the number one selling point I'm interested in.  A good test for this claim would be to grill two pieces of meat from the same package -- one on the infrared and the other no a non-infrared.  Using an insta-read meat thermometer, I now have tried this test multiple times -- to my surprise the infrared version either comes out dryer or is about the same as the gas version.  I'd be interested if others have different results.  The company also claims the grill has even heat, but this is not a huge selling point for me as most modern, small grills at this price range do a good enough job.The number one knock on this grill is that it is high maintenance.  Due to the design of these grill grates, stuck-on-food (which often becomes charcoal-like substance) is unable to fall through.  This means that you'll have to use their special cleaning tool after each grill and then remove the grill grate to empty the debris.  With traditional grates, you can pre-heat your grill and nearly incinerate the gunk followed by some nice wire brushing.  Those ashes and 'coal' flakes fall down into the grill out of the way so that you only have to do a deep cleaning 1-2 times per year.  The manual does recommends running your grill 10-15 minutes after you cook to burn the gunk, but due to how fast infra-reds heat up, the clean burn time is usually shorter thankfully.  You then wait for grill to cool down a little, scrub it with their tool (and optionally a wire brush), empty the grate, and then apply cooking oil to help protect the metal.Opposite of the product's claims, I suspect that the grill uses more gas than its competition.  However this could have been due to a leaky valve or even a leaky gas can.  I am now unscrewing the gas cans in-between usages to test if my shutoff valve is indeed the culprit.  Unscrewing the can when not in use is per the advice of the manual, which I don't like to do but most grill companies advise this.  I'll likely do the soap/water leak test in the coming days.  Another gripe is that often there is a strange whistling sound made when the gas flows.  The product manual says this noise does not affect safety, but it doesn't give a vote of confidence either.  I've also had my fire go out 2-3 times now during grilling, especially during windy days.  This may be due to the exposed holes in the pipe from the regulator to the grill -- a style of design a don't recall ever seeing elsewhere.  If you add all this up, you can see why I don't have much faith in this regulator.Three other deficiencies of this grill is that there are no side trays, no hooks/pegs to hang your BBQ tools, and there are no options to buy a stand/cart.  Without these options, you'll quickly get annoyed.  You'll discover that without a side tray that you won't have a conveniently close spot to place a plate, for example.  And where are you going to stand this grill?  You can put it on concrete but who wants to squat down that far.  So you'll likely have to build a stand for this maybe out of bricks or figure something else out.  By the way, do not put this grill on wood unless you get a heat resistant grill mat/pad.Don't get me wrong -- this grill has many things going for it.  But I've been spoiled by Weber's Q series and all the features the Weber has to offer.  Further, I am not yet convinced that infrared is living up to the hype.  We were told that since restaurants use infrared, we can now have food as 'good' as restaurants at home.  I'm not sure that is always a desirable goal.  With a few exceptions, my steaks and burgers often taste better than most restaurants.  I suspect infrared is used in restaurants primarily for speed and not for taste with maybe the exception of seared, crusted steaks (which I don't care for).  In other words, it seems as if infrared is trying to solve problems that I do not have with my traditional gas grill and may come at the cost of being less diverse as it is not good at handling more sensitive meats.[07/20/2013] Update: Char Broil has lowered the price of their grill from when I originally reviewed it making it now about $50 less than Weber's Q120 (although both list prices are about the same).  This price change now puts the Char Broil in the league of the Q100 which does not have fold-out trays.

Please see the pictures I have posted on Amazon.This is a well designed product; adequate cooking surface in a compact grill that is easily portable. It is well built and definitely not delicate. The lid has latches to lock it down for transportation.It comes with an instruction manual, but doesn't quite tell exactly where every component goes. However, it is not hard to put together using whatever instructions available and other pictures.- It has a temperature gauge on the lid. I think it will be very useful for certain recipes.- A somewhat snugly closing lid keeps the heat leakage to a minimum. Quicker cooking and fuel savings.- It will accept 1 lb propane tank; I paid 3.25 for one at Home Depot.- It has a push button ignition that is very effective. There is also a small hole for lighting with a matchstick. I found the hole to be also useful for examining the flame.- The regulator knob allows for a wide range of control for the flame.The manufacturer claims 100% even heat, but I found that to be not exactly true. But, it is surprisingly even, though not 100%.Another claim is that there will be no flare-ups; I didn't see any flares and I think the design prevents them successfully.I like this grill and I am looking forward to using it often. I recommend it.

I love small grills.  I have, over the years, owned quite a few of them.  First I had aWeber Smokey Joe,then aWeber Q 100,which I replaced with aWeber Q 200when somebody decided that they were more worthy of my Q100 than I was. Recently I purchased a Napoleon infrared portable grill and I am pretty happy with it even though it cooks REALLY hot.  When I got a chance to try out the Char-Broil TRU Infrared I thought that I would give it a shot since I can never have too many little grills.  In the end I am glad that I did.Comparing the Char-Broil to my other grills is a little complicated as each has their own niche.  The Grill2Go cooks a lot more like the charcoal powered Smokey Joe.  The heat radiates from the central diffuser rather than from a ring of burners like the Weber Q grills.  The Char-Broil is, by far, the most rugged and portable of all the grills that I have owned.  There are two latches that keep the grill safely locked when transporting it. The finish is also very tough and less likely to be marred than the stainless steel Napoleon.I am a little confused with this grills description as "Tru Infrared."  While I understand that the heat radiates from the diffuser plate rather than from heated air, as with the Weber Baby Q series, it is nothing like the Napoleon which uses a ceramic block to cook the food.  The Napoleon is much more like what I think of as an infrared grill.  It sears a steak in seconds and heats up much hotter than the Char-Broil.  However, the Char-Broil cooks much more like a conventional grill, making it easier for me to use.  I like that it has a thermometer on the lid and although I question it's accuracy it's still helpful.  This is a great little grill for tailgating and picnics.  For the price I think that it can't be beat.UPDATE 06/11/2013  I wanted a cover for my grill and could not find one made for it by Char-Broil so I purchased aWeber Vinyl Cover for Q-100and it fits perfectly.  I also attached the grill to a 20 lb. tank using the sameAdapter Hosethat I used with my Weber Q-200 and it fits like it was made for it.
summary: A tough, effecient little portable grill

reviewText: Works very well and charges my Kindle PW quickly. Would have been nice if they had included this with the Kindle though instead of having to add it to the cart as an accessory. I guess I'm just used to other companies including wall chargers/power adapters with their products.I charge my Kindle using this and not by charging it straight to my pc so it was a necessity, unfortunately I didn't pay much attention to it after I bought it and paid way more than I should have. My fault for not checking.I found another Kindle adapter for only $5 (in white) for my husbands new Kindle on Amazons lightening deal and his works just as well, just doesn't fold up like mine but I don't fold it up anyways.

I just purchased a new Kindle Paperwhite second generation and I did not purchase this charger. Why? Because I own multiple USB chargers and there is nothing special about this unit except it is expensive. You get a discount when you buy the charger at the same time as the Paperwhite but you probably don't need it. You can charge your Paperwhite with your computer, your external battery pack, if you have one, and with any USB AC wall charger you own that outputs 5VDC and roughly 1 amp.I have multiple chargers for iPhones, older Kindles and other USB products and I decided to save the money. If you need one it is a good charger but I own a basket full of chargers now and decided that it is fine to reuse one of them.I gave it 4 stars for the high price and the fact that it should have been in the box with the new Kindle Paperwhite.

Right now, it just seems like you buy a product (lets say the basic kindle for $70) and if you want to charge it through an outlet you need to spend  $20 more, making it a $90 device.Way overpriced, and disappointed in what Amazon is doing with the accessories. Especially one as cheap as this.Save your money and use an existing one, or go buy a generic usb/wall charger.

I own a Black and Decker electric mower and a Greenworks electric mower (also requires a cord) so will compare to both of those as well as a standard gas push model.First, notice that this is only a 17 inch cut which is substantially smaller than other models which were both 20 inches each. A standard gas mower is usually 22 inches and up so plan on taking a few more passes to get the job done.Assembly was very easy - this is SUPER light weight...so light that there is actually a handle on the top of the machine to pick it up. The bag is easy to put on and take off, build is plastic but seems solid enough. You will need to purchase a standard long electric cord for use but otherwise, no mess, no fumes and very small storage required.Safety - there is one inferior feature associated with this machine...it lacks a "brake" or "instant off". Once released, the blade continues to spin for a second or two rather than immediately shutting down like other versions. In most instance this isn't a big problem but the user should be aware of the inferior safety function.Performance - I just finished mowing the front yard which I specifically allowed to grow while waiting for this to arrive. We live in Florida, summer with rain each afternoon means the grass got high very fast...it was literally to the knees! So, plugged this in and gave it a good first workout. Although the grass is severely overgrown, the front yard has few/no limbs, weeds etc so it's really just long grass. A standard gas powered push mower as well as the other two electric mowers handle this without any notable difference. Unfortunately, this mower did get bogged down...it never actually choked or stopped running but became notably slower and required "lifting" the front to keep it from stopping. Basically it doesn't have quite the power one would hope for heavier jobs.Now, having said that, there are some very real advantages to this machine...the wife loves it due to the extra light weight and easy ability to maneuver and push. Perfect for finishing or in between trees, other areas where larger mowers won't fit. Great option for the elderly and those who need to keep a well groomed lawn maintained without worry about long overgrown grass, weeds and/or other obstacles.I didn't baby this thing whatsoever and it performed well. Had zero issues with materials/other. Will update if it doesn't last or performs poorly after repeated usage.
summary: Should be a 4.5 Star - Compare this model to 2 other electric models

reviewText: I bought my first electric lawn mower when I bought my first house in 2004. It was a Black and Decker MM675 with a flip-over handle. That lawn mower served me well for about 5 years and never let me down. Then, one day I used it when my lawn was too wet and the motor started to smoke as it bogged down on wet grass! I could no longer get the MM675 model, so I went to Home Depot and "upgraded" to the MM1800, the 18" corded mulching/bagging mower from Black and Decker. Immediately I was dissatisfied. It didn't feel as strong as my old mower, was more unwieldy, and had this awful plastic shroud that made it hard to maneuver. Everything on it felt cheap, and two years later, it died on me while mowing grass that was not that thick.I decided to try to leave the Black and Decker world and see what else I could find.Bear in mind, I did not consider gas because I don't have the room to keep fuel around and I have a modest size yard. I did not want cordless battery power because I didn't want to have to keep batteries alive (some require charge/discharge cycles all winter) or buy new batteries.Corded lawn mowers are a fine solution. Many complain about "cord management", but here's the trick. Your lawn never changes. Unless you are a professional landscaper (and if you are, buy a gas mower), then you always mow the same lawn. So the trick is to come up with a mowing pattern where you mow away from the outlet and never trip over the cord. Once you have a pattern, stick with it and you can mow quickly.I finally discovered the Greenworks 25022 20" electric bag/mulch/side discharge mower. You can read my review there of that amazing lawn mower.  Since I have used the Greenworks for the past 3 years, I can only review Sun Joe by comparing it.The first thing I noticed about the SunJoe mower is that it was  far lighter than the Greenworks.  At 33lbs, it is exactly 23 lbs lighter and you can easily notice that as you move it around.  The SunJoe is really easy to transport around the yard and push on a steep hill.  It also has very large tires which makes it easy to push.  Unfortunately the tire tread is not rubber but rather hard plastic, so they aren’t the best tires in the world, but at least the size makes the mower relatively easy to maneuver.The mower was easy to assemble – just attached 4 hand-tightened bolts to assemble the handle and you are done.  The handle is a standard "push the button and pull the safety bar" handle.  The mower plugs in with a pig-tail cable, a very secure way of handling the power.  The mower is set by default to mulch, but there is a bag you can use.  The bag was a bit of a let down – there is a snap-in handle which just loved to unsnap as I used it.  There is also no side-discharge option like the Greenworks has - you can only mulch or bag.The mower also has an easy one-handle height adjust which made changing cutting heights very simple.In terms of performance, I found the mower did a decent job, but was significantly louder than any other electric mower I have tried.  This may be due to the all-plastic body construction.  I mowed my lawn while dry but a bit long and found that the mower did bog down on some of the heavier grass.  Trying an uncut patch nearby, I found my old Greenworks cut right through it.Overall, this mower gets a strong 4 stars.  It is lightweight, easy to use, and does a nice job on grass that isn’t too long.  My Greenworks mower still gets my vote due to the all-metal deck, the rubberized tires, the quieter operation, and more powerful motor.  But the light weight of the SunJoe will be less intimidating to many buyers, so I can definitely recommend it if weight is a concern..
summary: There are better electric mowers, but this one shines in its light weight design

reviewText: I think $174.00 might be a bit more than I'm willing to pay for this mower, but it's not outrageously priced.  Maybe the price will go down later as it often does.  However, I like this little guy quite a bit.It was very easy to assemble and I had it put together in about 10 minutes.  Just have to pull it out of the box, attach the handle bars, assemble the grass catcher and you're basically ready to mow.  It's very light weight for a mower and I (woman) was able to carry it down our patio steps to the back yard.  The hardest thing about it all was our cheap orange extension cord because it was twisted with a vengence!Super easy to start and adjusting the blade height is beyond easy.  It's all done with one easy to use lever and no more going to each wheel to adjust.  The motor is louder than I expected - I guess I was expecting a hum or something, but it's kind of loud.  It cut great and we have a small front yard and several raised beds in the back yard so getting between them was easy.  Pushing it uphill is much, much easier than our gas mower.You have to use a long, heavy-duty electrical chord because it does not have a battery to hold a charge.  The grass catcher doesn't hold a whole lot, but it's very easy to remove, empty and re-attach  The reason I'm giving it 4 stars instead of 5 is because when mowing the front yard the right front wheel popped off.  It took my husband about 20 minutes to figure out what was wrong with it (parts missing) and put it back on correctly.  It obviously was not assembled correctly at the factory, but it was a fairly simple fix with minimal swearing.Overall, great for a small yard and doesn't require filling with gas!!!!!UPDATE: 7.8.14 - We found out that this mower is for a very small yard.  Ours is sort of small, but not small enough.  We have fescue grass and the mower engine really struggled with it and began to smell burnish-like.  My husband turned off the mower and pre-mowed the grass with a rotary mower then went over it with the Mow Joe.  I would not advise buying this mower unless you plan to mow your grass every week.  If you let it grow just a little too much the motor can't handle it.
summary: Sun Joe MJ403E Moe Joe Electric Lawn Mower

reviewText: I didn't time it, but it probably took about 15 minutes between when I opened the box and when I had the mower ready to go. Assembly was easy and required no tools. (I have to say that the instructions could have been better, but there really isn't much to do: attach one handle to the base, attach a second handle to the first one, and clip the cord in place.So it did not take long before I was ready to try this out. There were two small problems initially. The first is that the mower came set with the blades very low to the ground. Even pushing the mower across slightly uneven ground was tough, and the mower did tear up the dirt a little. (I also used the mower with that setting, and it cut down to the dirt before I adjusted the setting and was much happier.) The second was that I neglected to remove the plug so that the bag could collect grass, and the result was a lot of grass and dust flying everywhere. Once I had the setting right and the plug removed, though, the mower worked well.I don't have a very thick or a very large lawn. Under either case, I think I'd want more power. But for a small suburban lawn in a near-desert climate, the mower worked fine, chopping up both grass and rather thick weeds.Two points worth noting: (1) You will have to supply your own extension cord. That fact shouldn't be surprising, but it's worth pointing out, I think. (2) The bag for clippings is rather small and fills up quickly. (The mower itself is small, so the smaller bag isn't a great shock.)For my lawn and my needs, I'm pleased with the mower though.

The Sun Joe Mow Joe 13-Amp Corded Electric Lawn Mower is easy to maneuver. It is also fairly quiet. I was able to mow thick grass without the mower bogging down, despite the fact that it was also set to mulch, which puts a bit more of a load on the motor. As mentioned elsewhere, the bag is rather small, and the bag's snap-on handle promptly fell off the first time I tried to lift the still-empty bag (doesn't anyone test these things?). The mower is surprisingly lightweight, and would be a good choice for someone with limited strength. That said, I would hope that a 50 ft. or shorter electric cable could be used, as the shorter length permits a lighter gauge to be employed. The heavy 12-gauge 100 ft cables are relatively cumbersome to drag around. It should be noted that even when the mower is set to leave the longest length of grass (highest setting), the grass still is not left very tall. If the mower is used at one of the lower settings, it might cause considerable stress to the lawn during a dryer or hotter period.

This is the first electric lawn mower I have ever tried.  One of my neighbors uses an electric lawn mower to mow her lawn, but this is not one for everybody.  This is ideal for someone with a very small lawn.  The advantage of this mower over a gas powered one is that it is very light and you never need to worry about keeping gas on hand to mow the lawn.  The mower seems just a bit louder than a vacuum cleaner when it is cutting the grass (in other words it is very quiet).The set up of the mower was common sense and didn’t take long at all.  Do not let the plastic construction fool you – this mower has some power!  I accidentally ran over the kid’s plastic pail and it destroyed instantly.  I didn’t think I would run over it and thought it would get pushed to the side when I got near it – but it got sucked right up and was ruined.The disadvantage is that if you have a large lawn, it will get tiring walking around with the extension cord.  I really don’t trust myself in using this mower, as I am afraid I will run over the cord.  So this is really only ideal for mowing a small patch of grass if one is diligent enough to keep the cord away and not run over it.

As gas prices keep inching higher and higher, there is probably not a smarter time to buy an electric mower.  Aside from not having to buy gas for it, there is less maintenance because you do not have to worry about an engine.  No tune ups, no checking the oil, no spark plugs, no pulling a cord to start.  And without an engine, they are lighter and easier to maneuver as well as being quieter.  Another nice bonus is after you are done mowing the lawn you do not smell like an exhaust pipe.The question is whether to get a battery or corded one.  If you have a long enough extension cord, than corded is your best option unless you are careless and think you will be prone to drive the mower over the cord.  Plus to keep it from dying, you will need to charge the battery in the winter every month or two which can easily to forget about lawnmower maintenance while snow is on the ground (but considering how much replacement batteries cost, you cannot afford to not remember to charge it in the off season).If you have decided on a corded This Sun Joe Mow Joe is a decent one to go with.  It was fairly easy to get it from box to mowing the lawn with a couple minor hiccups, still one of the easier mowers I have ever assembled.  The corded mower does as good of a job as a gas powered mower and is significantly better than the battery powered one that it replaces.  For those that are considered with height, this mower has seven settings to choose from ranging from .98 inches to 2.87 inches.  My main complaint is the cord unplugs easily.  There is an attachment that may have come in the box that I think may elevate this but the intrusions does not explain how to put it on the mower.  I did figure out about halfway through that the cord would stay plugged in if I hold the cord against the handlebar as I mow.My only other complaint is that I could not figure out how to put the handle on the grass catcher, but since I mow with the mulcher plug in, I do not really need to handle the grass catcher except from when I moved it from the box to the back of the garage, probably never to be seen again.  For those that do prefer grass catchers to the mulching feature, the bag does have some sort of indicator to tell you when the bag is full, but I did not test this out to see how well it works.
summary: Much Better Than Gas Powered Lawnmowers

reviewText: I like the TERRO killer because it's quite safe for indoor use. I usually bother about what i spray or use indoors. there is already so much Toxicity in the air  and environment that adding some indoors is not my idea of a good idea. However, Terro has proven quite safe. It is odourless and still works efficiently . It does not last long against mosquitoes though, which is a major use for me. But the good part is it does get rid of mosquitoes outdoors for a day. This means it's great to use before any outdoor event. Nice product and does work well if properly used.

I like the spray system, like the hose mobility, and so far it seems to be working.  I sprayed outside the doors & windows to prevent the annual Monterey, CA ant infestation, and so far it seems to hvae helped quite a bit.  Noticing very few six-legged intruders with this safe & low-toxicity (safe for indoor use) spray.
so far so good, after using this product I don'tsee any signs of bugs!!! also likethe fact there's no loud smellproduct works great kinda of costlybut it works

Like a previous reviewer, I normally just buy whatever is sold at Wal-Mart, Home Depot or Lowe's, usually Ortho or another equivalent brand.  I'm no expert on the chemistry involved and I really have no preference for ingredients or brand.  I just want an insecticide to kill bugs, in my case that's usually ants, spiders and roaches.  We have an abundance of bugs in my location.  The Terro appears to work in this regard so I have no complaints about its effectiveness.  I must note one negative factor:  the container I have has a slight leak around the seam at the grip handle.  More attention to the material or QC in the manufacture of the container would be a good idea.  On the positive side concerning the delivery system, I would like to commend the company for providing a simple trigger pump device for deploying the product.  My previous experience with the new battery-powered spray devices has been abysmal.I like this product.  It kills bugs.  That's what it's supposed to do.  Would I make an effort to buy it in the future over other similar products?  No.  I don't have an emotional attachment to any insecticidal product and I buy the brand that's available at the best price as long as it is effective.

We've had ant problems since we moved into our new house about a year ago. Most products that I used on the ants did an ok job, but not great. The ants always seemed to come back. Recently, I found a line of ants crawling along the outside of my house and into a crack in the siding. I got out the Terro T3400 spray for the first time and sprayed the line of ants. It's been over a month, and I have not seen another ant in that area of the house. More importantly for me, though, was that several weeks ago, we saw a cockroach in the kitchen. After freaking out a bit, I grabbed the Terro T3400, and sprayed all around my kitchen and outside my house wherever I felt the little critters could get in. The next day I came home and saw one more cockroach, but it was dead. (a good sign). A day later, another of the nasty things showed up in my bathroom. Again, I got the Terro T3400 out and sprayed all along the baseboards of my bathroom and under the sink area. We have not seen another cockroach for at least a month now. So, I'm convinced. This is the product for me from now on.

I have been using Terro products for years and have always found them highly successful in the control of all manner of creepy crawlies here in the Midwest.  This is no exception.  I sprayed down the exposed foundation and all entry ways first.  Then I made an expedition to the deepest, darkest basement and sprayed around the windows and sump hole area.  I can't say I had a major bug problem before, but since using this I seem to see far fewer bugs.  Recommended.

I consider myself to be a macho guy, or at least having a sensible amount of bravery, but I think we get exposed too much already, to a bunch of stuff that isn't good for us. The way I look at it, whatever kills, kills. Therefore I am always looking for a benign method of getting rid of pests. I noticed that some of the ant products have boric acid in them, and then I came across a homemade cure on Facebook.Boric Acid Powder 4 OZ.mixed with peanut butter, or jelly is ideal because the ants ingest it, and bring it back to the nest, and feed the queen. That way it takes out the whole nest instead of just getting a few. There are different types of ants; some like sweets, and others like proteins, so peanut butter, or jelly covers them both. You can Google this homemade recipe by typing in, "Boric acid and sugar to kill ants". I have seen Boric acid used, or claim to be used for an eye wash or personal hygiene for women. READ the label on the container whereas I am not an expert on boric acid. I like what one article said, "Even too much water can be toxic." :-)So anyhow I use the boric acid and sugar mix when I want to get rid of those kinds of ants in the house. Fortunately I don't have cock roaches etc. at least so far I haven't had a problem with them. On the outside of the house I like to use a spray as long as I am not spraying down areas that have run off into a gardening area where I grow vegetables. So a good home insect killer in a handy spray such as the Terro T3400 is great for outdoors, and the boric acid combo is great for indoors.I would like to say that I used the TERRO and say ants and other insects high tailing it out of there, but I can't really say that. This is later in the season, and not when ants go nuts and seem to be everywhere. So now is not the best time for me to give you immediate results. The thing I like about TERRO is how long lasting it is.I saw rows of the very tiny ants making their way from a window sill down an outside wall and into the ground. They were on the march. That too was early in the season. I am saying that because they need some contact with the ground. So spraying along your homes base edge is going to be effective in holding them from entering the house in the first place.There are a lot of reviews here about direct results. I just wanted to share with you what I have found to be a good solution, and a way of not having to ingest toxic substances into your system. Hope this helps.
summary: I'm squeamish when it comes to spraying toxic substances in the kitchen and inside the house. But...

reviewText: The Terro T3400 Home Insect Killer does just what it says. It kills insects. The main ingredient is Deltamethrin which is considered a safe pesticide. The one gallon container is ready-to-use  with an attached spray hose. Just attach the hose into the cap and you are ready to spray. The spray nozzle has a narrow setting or a broader setting for easy application. This insect killer can be used indoors or outside to kill all kinds of insects such as ants, silverfish, ticks, flies, cockroaches and up to 65 different types of insects. It will last for months. I would recommend this insect killer to anyone who has an insect problem.

Review of Terro T3400 Home Insect Killer: Here in Arizona we seem to have a zillion little critters, some very small to as big as your fist.  Here in their desert you would expect to find a little one under every rock.  True, so it is a must to prevent massive outbreaks.  My greatest fight is with ANTS!.  Ants this year have decided to hold their conferences in my garden, patio and in the greenhouse.This year it seemed that the Home defense spray used in the past had no effect to their invasion.I tryed all of the home folk lore recipes!! Nothing could slow down the invasion!So, I decided to try another home brand, to vary their little diets.  I sprayed my entire garden, greenhouses, patio ,in the evening, the following day, I did not notice the invasion, but found that I had missed the storage center and sprayed again, It has been 2 weeks since I sprayed and not seen a caravan of ants.So, this reviewer has the most favorable review of this product.I still have about half of this product left to spray again as the winter sets in, I also noticed that other critters unseen turned up legs in the air!As this was the beginning of our rainy season, we normally get around 2 inches of rain, this season we have already seen in three days around 10 inches.  I was afraid that the home defense would wash away, seems like it is still holding.Very pleased.

This stuff seems to keep the bugs out I put a barricade around my house and under the house.  I am also putting some around the walls (I have these little black ant looking things that show up every summer, I do not know what they are, but they are annoying and hang around the kitchen).  I am going to put this around the walls where I see them some times (they are usually on the cabinets, and no I do not have food anywhere, they just show up every year), I am not going to put this on the cabinets or anywhere where I have food, but maybe if I can find their path I can stop them.  I will also put some in the corners of the bathrooms (preventative) and in the future if I ever do have a bug problem I will be ready with this.  This bottle is pretty large and should last you a long time.  It claims 12 months of killing so I will see how it does around the house.So far it is pretty good the stuff is easy to dispense (included sprayer) and if its claims are true I should be good for a year!  So far all is good I have not seen any bugs inside and hopefully this stuff will keep it that way and maybe also keep them away from the edge of the house!
summary: Seems to work and easy to dispense

reviewText: I don't have a problem with indoor insects as long as I spray around the perimeter of my house.I like the Terro Insect killer. After using it I've noticed few insects and spiders around my home.There were certain spots that they would always return to. Shady areas and around my garage door was always one of their favorite spots.The Terro sprayer was easy to use. The spray nozzle is adjustable for wide or narrow spraying.I would use this product again.

I have little red ants in my house,not grease ants as they don't go near anything greasy that I put out to try to get them and not sugar ants as they don't go to any sugar in the sugar bowl I have out but small red ants, like the ones you need to eat on your peonie flowers on the bushes in order for the blooms to open and I do have those bushes on the south side of my house near the foundation and I did spray there too. They seem to be coming in all over. I sprayed this by all the outside doorways and all around the windows and around the foundation, so basically every where they would be coming in from outside. I also sprayed under my sink in the kitchen and bathroom and down the basement around the entire perimeter. I still have ants....Nothing seems to be getting rid of them. Terro is a brand I have used since I was 19 in my own home, I'm 61 now, and it's always worked but not this time. Very disappointing. I did see almost no spiders after I sprayed but I had very, very few of those to begin with. I did also try the liquid Terro that you put on little pieces of cardboard and that didn't get rid of them either. I guess I'm stuck with them for the season....

Terro has been a long trusted brand for me to get rid of ants, so I was ready to buy any of their products. I was having a problem with spiders especially, so I thought I thought I would try this stuff out. It came in an orange container that was easily distinguishable from anything else in my garage. It has a nice trigger sprayer that just hooked on underneath the handle when not in use. It is easy to use by pointing and spraying. There are a couple of options on the nozzle to spray a long ways or just a fan. I really like that it does not have a scent like so many other insect sprays I have used. In no time I had my house sprayed and did not have to smell it for weeks. I sprayed inside and outside. I was not sure if it washed off in the rain or not. It has seemed to to the job, because I have not seen any insects around the house since. The only thing I do not like about it is that the hose coming from the spray gun snaps into the cap on the jug and will not come back out so I can store it without the hose attached.

This insect killer arrived just in time for my quarterly treatment of the indoors and the garage. It is a gallon jug of insecticide that has no odor and does not stain. The directions for use are located on the back of the container. They are easy to follow and are clearly illustrated. There is a sprayer provided which has tubing attached. At the end of the tubing is a plug. A part of the cap is removed revealing an opening into which the plug is inserted. The sprayer has three setting for "off", "wide spray" and "narrow stream".After I read the instructions it was time to get to work. I pointed the sprayer downward and pumped the trigger. I sprayed along the bottom of all the walls in the house and garage. This is a 2800 square foot house plus a double garage to spray so, not being in the prime of my youth, my  hand was getting a bit tired of pumping the trigger. I could have taken a break and done this in parts but I wanted to finish the job so I kept pumping. When I finished I just turned it off and slid the sprayer into the spot reserved for it under the handle. This is a very handy product which does not require a separate sprayer or batteries. There is no formula to mix and no measuring cup to use. Everything you need to spray is included. This can be used outdoors as well but in my case I have other products which I use outdoors.As I mentioned, I do this every quarter and I do not have an insect problem as a result. Therefore I cannot tell if this actually kills insects unless I see some evidence by way of a dead insect. If I do see a dead or a live insect I will update this review. In the meantime I consider this to be a great and convenient product.

UI ahve a senstive nose an asthma, and most insect killers throw me into coughing fits or wheezing spasms. This does not. It says odorless and it really does not have hardly any smell a all, and so far it is working great.RoachI sprayed under the table of our pet parakeet to keep down any roaches, and I found 1 dead under the table. The next morning. So far no more.AntWhen We have hard or continual rain, we get ant infestations. Since we sprayed around the house, 1 week of constant downpour and the 1 week of rain at least once everyday, and low and behold no ants have come inside.
summary: Odorless Roach Ant Insect killer spray doesn't bother my Asthma.

reviewText: I sprayed this along the baseboard of my bathroom and I was surprised to see three dead roaches the next morning.  The spray nozzle has a setting that comes out more as a mist than stream.  That is what I used.  I am very satisfied with the speed at which it worked.

Since I don't keep pet spiders and give them names like Frankenspider and Fang, I'd just as soon all of them wishing to reside in the house with me be terminally denied.  When was the last time you saw someone bitten by a Black Widow or Brown Recluse Spider?  It's a scary sight and it could be fatal.An outside perimeter is the best defense against creepy and crawly things but many of the little boogers have developed a knack for finding their way into porches, garages, utility sheds and especially decks.The average consumer is not a chemist or a scientist.  They just want something that keeps their dwelling from turning into a giant ant hill or roach coach with minimum risk.Most all of the home insecticides, regardless of the active ingredient, come with the same precautions and warnings which are governed by common sense.  Don't put them in your fish tank or in Fluffy's water bowl and don't keep them in your liquor cabinet.I've been doing my own exterminating for 30 years and live in the woods in the middle of 10 acres and keep lots of pets.  I know what works and have never poisoned a pet, my wife or myself, at least not yet anyway.FOLLOW THE INSTRUCTIONS.This product works as well as the competition which is Ortho Home Defense Max.  They both boast 12-month control but keep in mind that this is based on ideal and perfect conditions.  I've found that 6 months is more accurate for a variety of indoor applications.Outdoors in the deep South you might need to apply every day during the Monsoon season. Maybe twice a day.I don't use this product outdoors.  There are many more effective alternatives that last for months and every home, landscape and situation is different and should be approached as such.Anybody attempting to do their own exterminating with only one product is like a plumber trying to do his job with only one tool: a screwdriver.
summary: IF IN DOUBT, SPRAY AND PRAY

reviewText: so far this seems ok... only have a limited about of time to review this (vine product) but seems ok. See a few bugs here and there but may not be the product but the application of product. I used it in a hurry but seems as good as any other brand. easy to use handle etc which was nice.

I have been using TERRO's insect killer in the granule format for most of this summer. The granule based product is excellent and gets the job done. However, I have not been a big fan of using it inside my house. Sprinkled around the perimeter of my front porch or my basement bathroom, it's rather unsightly.This liquid based equivalent solves the unsightly issue. Perfect! And thus far, it seems to be working just as well.

Apparently reviews don't necessarily 'go through'or perhaps I didn't say enough words.  So I'll try again.  This gives me a chance to update the review I wrote some time back, since I've used this productg for a few months now.  I live in the south.  We have ants.  In fact we have ants and spiders and slugs and all kinds of critters, and lately, 'giant mosquitoes' (caused by the rains, perhaps. These nickel-sized bugs are making a dent in the Red Cross's blood donor supplies :>).Would that this Terro stuff could make a dent in these critters all round, which they don't, nor do they pretend to do.  They do seem to deter ant invasions, however.  This is enough ant repellent to treat the foundation of a fair sized home all year.  I don't recommend it in or around homes where there are very small children or pets, as the granules might prove interesting for them to experiment with.I was most hopeful they would help with the slug population, as well as the ants.  While Terro didn't keep slugs out altogether, or ants either, I do notice a significant decrease in aunts and slugs this year over the previous years.  And I have not had the infestation of those tiny 'sugar' aunts this year at all. I give this a 4 star rating for reducing my indoor slug population to 1.  If it'd deal with stink bugs and spiders, Terro could have a serious fortune maker on its hands!
summary: I reviewed this item once, but I can review it again.

reviewText: This will be short and sweet. I live in a wooded area of North Carolina, and we have bugs I've never seen before. After spraying this, I've realized that it does nothing for fleas (don't ask me how I have fleas, when I don't even own a pet), and silver fish, nor does it work on these little long pincher bugs. (I don't know what you call them.) It did work on the ants, which we have a lot of. I just sprayed it a week ago, and perhaps it takes a while to kick in.
