But I think, if after I use the entire bottle, I don't see results, I'll stick to the local pesticide that I get at my local Home Depot or recontract Terminix.

I have used Terro bait traps for relentless ants for years.  Only one year did they seem resistant.  Just putting out a trap attracts hundreds within hours and they consume all the poison and disappear.  However, I have two cats and they don't seem to like to bite the traps.  I thought this one-gallon of spray container would work well by spraying into cracks.The container is strange.  You unattach the nozzle from under the container handle (which has a wide or specific spray nozzle) and within several pumps, it lets out the stream that goes into cracks or anywhere you spray it.  Even the thinnest spray was wide and I had to go back and wipe up the tile floor near the cracks to prevent my cats from stepping in it.The nozzle is unnecessarily over-designed, meaning instead of just simply having the sprayer on top permanently, it is held beneath the handle with an 18-inch thin clear hose that slides out of the sprayer.  This allows you to get some distance, but you have to slip the hose back into the handle when done.  I just felt that this was just too much.  The poison (Deltamethrin) is a much thinner solution than it is in the bait traps.  It does kill the ants but they returned again in a week.  I plan on using this outdoors only and will continue with the traps indoors.  By the way, I only have issues with ants and (occasionally) silverfish.
summary: The Bait Traps Seem To Work Better

reviewText: This insecticide comes in a one-gallon jug with a hand-powered pump included. My real concern is the active ingredient, which turns out to be Deltamethrin, one of the safer insecticides, generally considered safe enough for indoor usage. It is, however, highly toxic to fish. As I live near water, I won't be able to use it on the lawns.The concentration is 0.03%, which is on the more diluted end. Concentrates as high as 4.75% can be bought easily at economic prices if the user has massive needs, but this product should suffice for the majority of home owners as Deltamethrin is quite effective even at this concentration.Ants and roaches are generally susceptible to Deltamethrin. Some mosquitoes in the south may be resistant. Bedbugs, which have become endemic in NY area lately, are known to have acquired resistance, so you may have to look for something else if bedbugs are the reason for shopping for insecticide.Deltamethrin is very toxic to spiders as well. This is unfortunate, as I prefer leaving some spiders in the house to serve as natural pest control.

I really only use pesticides outside and in my garage.  The Terro Home Insect Killer seems to be targeted for hosing down the crevices around your foundation where the little buggers live though it does say it can be used to spray directly on plants too.  As with any insecticide, make sure to fully read the directions.  From the back label I got the impression it only worked on crawly bugs.  Once I read through the inside pages, I found fruit flies and white flies were also listed.This stuff is toxic to fish so should never be used where it can run off into a storm drain or lake.  It's supposed to leave a residue that kills flies on a treated surface for 150 days yet you are safe to spray it on your pet's bedding or even your own mattress provided you let it dry before coming into contact with it?  I don't know about you, but that creeps me out. I'd have to have a pretty desperate pest problem before I'd make any extensive inside use of this product.My biggest gripe is with the container.  If you tip the bottle to read the label AFTER you've inserted the spray hose, the insecticide runs out the cap and in my case-down my leg!  As I'm wondering why my leg is all wet, I'm reading about how contact with the skin can cause redness and tingling and should be avoided. While the spray trigger is easy and may be more convenient for the average user, next time I will just buy a concentrate I can put in my pump sprayer and not have to wear it.

The odor is minimal, and it works. Not just good, but great ... weeks after spraying an ant trail that started at my neighbor's house, went through my driveway and on to the next neighbor ... it still has not returned. This is the first product I have used that was able to keep the ants away! And while it isn't complete;y odorless, it is very mild compared with other products. I highly recommend this, and I plan to buy more.

This is not my first experience with Terro, but it is certainly my least favorable. I was looking forward to blasting some Argentine ants outside that like to crawl along the side wall, where they eventually are able to climb right into our orange tree from leaves that brush against the wall. This was not so successful.Setup is easy. The blue spray nozzle conveniently packs into the container's handle for storage, and to set it up all you have to do is remove the lid of the cap and insert the hose of the spray nozzle into it. The hose is actually coiled inside the sprayer and it can be extended a good 1.5-2 feet, which is pretty convenient so that you can hold it away from you as you're spraying. The nozzle turns so that you can spray in a narrow stream or a wider fan-like spray.So anyway, I went out to the ant line and began spraying, a mixture of the narrow stream and wide spray along the whole wall. Now most liquid ant sprays will essentially kill on contact, and that's what this promises to do. You spray it and you see the ants start shaking violently and then within seconds they're dead. And any ants that come after them avoid the area completely or die within 15-30 seconds of walking onto it. When I sprayed the ants with this, that didn't happen. They just kept moving and walked out of it. And not only did they not die, but the fact that I had just sprayed the area seemingly didn't mean anything to the rest of the ants behind them, as the ants just kept walking right through the wet areas. Now, I found that if I sprayed enough to essentially DROWN the ants, then they would (eventually) die (I had one that I thought was dead and then several minutes later I found it trying to walk away still), but according to the instructions I should only be spraying enough to lightly moisten the area. And even still, even with me spraying a liberal amount of the insecticide, ants just walked right through it afterward with seemingly no effect. They weren't discouraged, and they didn't bother trying to walk around it or turn the other way. This, in my mind, failed the first test of a store-bought insect killer, the ability to easily kill and deter ants.I will keep trying, but for now this failed miserably at handling a single ant line.
summary: Failed the first test of an insect killer

reviewText: We had a lot of rain early this summer and because the ants (red ones) and centipedes got flooded out of their homes they thought they would move into mine.I have used the random ant bait traps in the past but this time they were just coming in from too many areas - I needed more help.The Terro sprayer was so easy to use I love the fact that I didn't have to pour it into a smaller spray bottle and that the sprayer that attaches would fire a nice thin stream into every little crack I wanted to dose.I used it indoors, kept my dogs and cats away from the sprayed areas until they had dried (most were out of their reach anyway) and then moved outdoors where I sprayed any and hills close to the foundation and then in as a spray all around the house at the base of the foundation.By the second day I was only seeing random ants and think maybe they were more interested in finding an un-sprayed way out then anything else. I think the centipedes were showing up to eat ants because once the ants were gone I didn't see any more of them either.I have always trusted the Terro brand and now that they have this product that works well and is so easy to use, I will be keeping it ready in case I'm invaded again.

So far this has worked good in killing some ants that were coming into my home.  It comes with a convenient sprayer. You pull the long hose out of the handle and get to work. You have to pump the bottle a few times before the spray will come out though.  If you are doing your whole home, your arm/hand will get tired.  The insecticide is odorless, which is great so that I can use it indoors or outdoors.

Several years ago, we began using Ortho's Home Defense MAX Insect Killer and more recently Terro's T3400 Home Insect Killer, spraying around the perimeter of our home.  We noticed that we had to buy so many different sprays for so many different insects- ants, beetles, carpenter ants, wasps, yellow jackets, bees, bumble bees, spiders, moths, centipedes, flies, mosquitos and several other bugs I don't even know well enough to identify.  I was tired of having to buy so many different sprays, liquids, powders and traps. The one thing I know for a fact is no matter how many insecticides you use, the bugs always return. I was taught in High School Science Class that if the world blew up tomorrow, spiders and possibly a couple other insects would survive. Insects are true survivalists with their indestructible egg casings so well protecting their young and future generations.So, knowing these facts from Science Class, I know you can never get rid of pesty insects completely, but you can keep their populations down. I have found since using both Ortho and Terro Home Insect Killer Gallon Sprays around our home in the warm months- mainly summer, our insect population goes down every year. I'm speaking of a very noticeable difference in insect invasion. If I was killing 100 spiders in a year, I'm now down to a couple dozen after using it for 4 years, and this is no exaggeration. These Home Sprays are that good.  Even though I have used both Ortho Home Defense MAX Insect Killer and this Terro Home Insect Killer, I do not prefer one over the other. Ortho's main insecticide ingredient are 2 natural Pyrethrins- Bifenthrin and Zeta Cypermenthrin. Terro's main insecticide ingredient is Deltamethrin- the world's safest and most widely used Pyrethrin. These Pyrethrins are made from plants which have a natural ingredient which stimulate electrical signals in nerve cells, causing paralysis in the insects.I've found from neighbors and friends who also use both Ortho and Terro, that the Ortho's 2 Pyrethrins are more effective on Fire Ants, and the Terro's 1 Pyrethrin is more effective on German Cockroaches and Bedbugs. I've rarely used these Insect Killers in our home, only on occasion I used them in cracks in the basement, if I notice insects more than just an occasional one here and there. Spraying around the perimeter of our home once a week, or more often if rain should wash the insecticide away, completely keeps the insect populations down and lessens insect activity in the home as well.  Since I don't have fire ants, I prefer the Terro Spray. Terro's main ingredient of Deltamethrin is the safest insecticide in the world and most widely used. It is used on golf courses and ornamental gardens world wide. This Terro kills 65 different insects with either a narrow stream or wide spray. The barrier it sets up on the perimeter of your home lasts a full week or longer without rain.Since Pyrethrins are a natural nerve paralysis agent made from plants, you do not want to spray this where your pets are, or near food, grills etc..  Also don't spray near any water where fish are. Pyrethrins do affect fish like they would your pets. One gallon of Terro Home Insect Killer lasts us an entire summer or longer. We've sprayed every year around our foundation, and bushes where spiders and mosquitos love to live, and after 4 years we actually do have 75% less insects in and around our home. That is a huge difference in our battle with the bugs! Terro Home Insect Killer deserves 5 STARS for making our life more enjoyable with having to kill less bugs in our home year after year, and it is non-staining and odorless making it perfect indoors or out!
summary: SAFEST Insecticide Keeps Insect Population Down

reviewText: And, boy do we have ants :(  Those little buggers that bite and judging by the way they scarf down cat food, I would hate to trip and fall in their wake!Sometimes I think our house and the ones around us were built on a giant anthill because they are always around.  There are no basements either; houses are built on slabs so they have to work at getting in and work they do.  Last month I had 3 invasions in my bathroom and before caulking around the baseboard and tub again, we put down TERRO liquid bait trapsTERRO PreFilled Liquid Ant Killer II Baits  6 Pack  T300.  They do the job, but watching hundreds of ants going to and from into the wall can be a bit disconcerting.  You just have to remember they are eating the bait and taking it back to the nest where they and the others, including the queen, will die. Leave the trap down until no more ants are seen, about 2 days, depending on the size of the colony.  That's for inside the house........there are also larger TERRO liquid ant baits for outside.Two days ago I walked into the back yard and in seconds my slippers and feet were covered with biting ants.  I mean covered, as in some of the old horror movies where the ground is moving with them. There was a Don Johnson movie, A Boy and His Dog, in the 70's about ants taking over the world - looking at my feet I had a flashback of that movie!Our house is up against and above a large grassy park and I don't know if they were migrating there - if ants migrate - or if they were from the house next door that is now vacant, but I have never seen anything like it.We got the TERRO T3400 and sprayed the back and side of the house and all around the ground where they were.  We then got theTERRO 600 1-Pound Ant Killer Dustand put it on windowsills and at the base of the house.  Then the sprinklers came on and we knew the ants would go underground.Late that afternoon we didn't see any ants and the next morning the same thing.  A few here and there, but the moving horde was gone.  They might have gone underground and are planning a new assault on the backyard or they have moved on with the help of the water and the TERRO products.I do know that the TERRO T3400 killed them on contact when sprayed directly on them. It is easy to use and the sprayer has a wide area.We always have the dry and wet cat food on the back patio up on a table (we feed stray/feral cats who pass by) and keep the ground under and around the table sprayed as a preventative measure.All I know is that TERRO products will continue to be a permanent part of our ant control.Based on our experience, I would recommend the TERRO T3400 Insect Killer.
summary: TERRO Products are deadly for ANTS!!!

reviewText: For the last two years I have been using the insecticide that comes with a battery powered spray head wand, which was relatively easy to use.  The squeeze pump trigger spray head on this product is tiring to the hand and about 3 minutes into the application I poured the remainder of the product into a 1 gallon pump-up garden sprayer and that solved the problem. ( however it was then necessary to clean the sprayer, adding to the effort & time needed to do the application )As far as killing bugs, the little critters definitely don't like this stuff.  Spraying into the crack between my garage floor and the driveway and the crack between my patio and the house sent several bugs scurrying out into the open.  I also sprayed the rest of the perimeter of my foundation.  Haven't seen any bugs for a week now, so the product seems to be working as well as the Ortho Home Defense Max Insect Spray used previously.I gave this product 4 stars because it was harder to apply, even though it was comparatively priced.
summary: Kills Bugs, But squeeze sprayer is no joy to use

reviewText: From a distance this basket is attractive but close up the cardboard liner does not appear to be as sturdy or as well-constructed as similar liners I've seen in local nurseries. I think the appearance would benefit from more wiring on the cage too. Also the chain is not as sturdy as I'd have liked, particularly at the points that connect to the planter base.  Frankly for the price I expected a lot more.  I think there are better products on the market with better prices too.  If you're going to use this product I'd suggest  a trailing plant that will cover most of the planter as it grows.  Ultimately this product will do the job but I'd prefer to see the plant and not the planter. (NOTE: Per the description Amazon Vine reviewers were supposed to receive two baskets.  I only received one basket but since that's a shipping issue I didn't take it into consideration for this product review.)
summary: Should be designed better...and less expensive!

reviewText: This goes under "the easiest thing to use" for ease of planting and hanging.  the hooks have a place that is very noticable on the wire bowl, and if you put them there, the whole thing will be easily balanced.  I liked the large drainage hole in the bottom of the insert and the large size made it easy to put several types of flowers in there.  Easily the prettiest hanger in my garden this year!

This is a huge step up from the plastic hanging baskets plants come in from the hardware store; it's very attractive. The chains look like good quality and are supposed to be rust resistant which is great. Mine still look good after some use.The liner is all recycled and even though it is different from traditional liners it looks fine. I like that the plants can be watered less because honestly I sometimes forget to water my hanging pots. So far none of them have gotten too dry.The 14 inch basket is a good size for me. The basket was ready to go out of the box. I really don't think it is too expensive comparatively to other products either after doing some searching on Amazon.Update - 6/18/13:I docked a star from this because the liner got moldy. I wasn't watering this excessively or anything else I can think of that would cause it.

This is a large planter with a 14" diameter. The metal hardware and hanger are incredibly lightweight, as is the pressed board liner. The liner is unusual looking, but I don't think its freakishly horrible or anything, and if you plant cascading plants it will be covered up soon; also it has the advantage of being less porous than a moss liner. There is one small drainage hole in the center, otherwise it seems watertight. It is unusually light for this size hanger, so if you use it with  lightweight potting soil or augment your soil with fillers like Perlite, this large hanger will still be quite light. So far I like this very well, and will update this review further into the season to see if the filter maintains its structure and can be re-used, and if the hardware stays stays rust-free. So far so good! Quick to assemble and very light.
summary: excellent large and lightweight hanging planter

reviewText: This is a great hanging basket. I love the large size, but it's not so big it is overwhelming. The liner looks natural and attractive (I've seen negative reviews on the liner but I'm quite happy with it). The basket and chain are quality, sturdy metal, not plastic. It holds moisture well and the water doesn't drain straight through.The only ding on this review is the chain. Getting it onto the basket and adjusted so the basket hangs level was a bit of a challenge and required some patience and perseverance, but the effort is well worthwhile.

The good things about this hanging basket are that it is:* Reasonably priced, in my opinion; and* Large, I have the 14-inch version.The not so good points are:* The EcoLiner certainly holds water, but doesn't seem to drain!  After planting the baskets and leaving them outside during a rainy night, they were filled with water.  I resorted to using an awl to make three holes on the bottom, yet they still didn't drain.* The construction of the basket and chain seem flimsy.  The planted 14-inch basket weighs at least 15 pounds.  The basket is made of thin metal wire, and the chain is tiny.  I don't have confidence in its sturdiness or its "rust resistance."* This basket is fine if you are using plants that will trail and hide the basket, because the basket, with the EcoLiner, is unattractive.I think that theGeorgian Hanging Plant Basket with Coco, 14" Blackis much sturdier and more attractive, and worth the extra cost.

This is a good, standard hanging basket.  It's more attractive than the plastic varieties that typically come pre-planted at home improvement stores and gardening centers.  But it is still pretty utilitarian looking - while the metal basket is sturdy there's really nothing in the way of ornamentation or decoration.  For me this makes it a good choice for plants that tend to grow down and spread, thereby covering a good portion of the basket.  But if I'm filling it with something less likely to grow down or spread I'd probably opt for a basket that has a bit more style to it.Aesthetics aside it's easy to plant and care for.Overall, it's a solid, standard hanging basket.

This basket is really large compared to the baskets I bought at Walmart, and when filled with dirt are very heavy.I planted strawberries in the coco-lined baskets I had and the strawberries suffered from lack of water although I watered every day but the water ran right through the coco-liners..really was frustrating.  These baskets seem perfect but will have to see how well the strawberries withstand the summer heat.

What I got wasn't quite what I expected. From what I've read in a couple reviews on it I'm not the only one a little disappointed in it. I needed something for a Hoya plant for indoors so I really didn't need something with a hole in bottom of it. As for the liner the recycled paper its made of doesn't look like it would last very long. So for a few touch ups I gave it a couple coats of spray Polyurethane on the inside and a couple on the outside with brown stain in it. Then I used about half a tube of Plumbers Goop to stick the plastic lid from a can of Folgers Coffee upside down over the hole in the bottom. Used most of a spray can of gloss Polyurethane on the outside to finish it off and it looks pretty nice. It's probably not enough to make it waterproof but should be enough to keep it from falling apart. I let it sit outside for 3 days to let the Polyurethane cure out before I put my Hoya start in it. It looks great and I really hope the Hoya plant, or actually its a vine, takes off and grows. My mother had one and it was over 40 years old with at least 150 feet of vine and after she passed away my sister destroyed it. I managed to salvage 3 leaves from the garbage and got them to grow some roots in a glass of water. Now I hope they will take off and grow now that I have them in some dirt.As for the hanging wire frame for the pot it looks pretty good. It looks like its been dipped in some sort of rubber or plastic coating to keep it from rusting. The hanging chains look like they have also been powder coated or enameled to keep them from rusting.If you don't like the appearance of the pot and want to take the time there's a few things you could have some fun doing to it to help it last longer. Give it a couple coats of clear acrylic or Polyurethane or something like that and brushed on would probably work better than the spray I used. Then get artistic with some paints or if you got kids let them have at it with some paints and you could end up with something nice and unusual for your flowers on your patio, deck, or wherever. It wont only make it look a lot better it should help make it last a lot longer. If this one last for a while I think I'll do just that. Get a few more and see what I can come up with. They are cheap enough so if they don't last its no big deal. And like somebody else said, if the paper pots fall apart I can find some plastic ones or clay ones or something else to use in them.
summary: It's OK to start with, after a few touch ups it's pretty good

reviewText: The first thing you'll notice with this planter is that the hole in the bottom is rather large. I put a coffee filter in the bottom before putting in soil, and it was fine. Kudos go to the company for trying to use green materials.If you use this planter for hanging on a porch or in an otherwise relatively lower- to mid-light place, it seems to hold water rather well. I wouldn't put it in an area that gets a lot of light, however, without adding in a self-watering insert of some kind. You won't be able to use it inside unless you can figure out how to rig a drip catcher.The chain is plenty long, the planter itself seems sturdy, and I like the fact that it's biodegradable over time. I haven't been able to find replacement liners, however. If these are available for an economical price, I wouldn't mind getting some more of these, especially since the price seems to have dropped to a more reasonable amount since these planters were first released.

First, I was disappointed when I only received one, because it clearly stated Vine reviewers would get 2 to review.  And this was part of the attraction to review it, but I only received one, like a normal order.It came with no tag, lable or instruction, and the chain was in an attached ziplock bag.  You need help or to be somewhat dexterous to assemble, because the hooks like to come off the chains.The metal part of the basket seems quite sturdy, so this is good.The EcoLiner is what concerns me.  It is grey like paper egg cartons or plantable small starting flower pots that eventually disolve if not planted.  They say it holds in more moisture than the coconut fiber basket lining, and since I never had one, this might be true.  But like the recycled pressed paper flower pots, this became quite soggy, and is easily shapable with a slight touch after the first watering.  I would guess it will disolve and fall apart in less than a year (maybe months), and there was no instruction on how to order a replacement liner or if you need to buy the whole thing again.  When this disolves, I will probably go to a dollar stor to buy a big plastic bowl to replace it which will hold water even better.

This is a nice large hanging basket.  The EcoLiner is very sturdy and more environmentally friendly that the typical coco liner.  In the past, I've filled hanging baskets with ferns and had them grow through the coco liner.  I doubt that will happen with this liner.  Probably best for plants that cascade down naturally.  I might try cutting small holes in the liner and put some small plants in the spaces.  Given the free shipping, the price seems reasonable to me.

This is one of those charming hanging baskets that does its job of holding plants and letting the attention go to your lovely flowers.  The steel chains provide a simple, down home look that will match with any outside decor.  I found this to be an easy set up, comparable with other hanging baskets, and it looks so nice.  The liner is very handy.  This is sturdier than others I've seen and indeed promises to last a season without wear and tear.
summary: Simple and elegant basket with sturdy liner

reviewText: This new 14-inch hanging basket has a new Ecoliner.  Place the potting soil in the liner, add your plants and you are all set with a lovely hanging basket. The sturdy basket base and chain are coated with a black material that seems very sturdy. (This is the company that also does baskets that can hang on the deck rail.  I have used those for two years and they hold up very well. I think this basket will be the same-- wearing well.)  The new basket Ecoliner will hold the water for your plants much longer than moss which can quickly dry out on hot days. Nice new addition for gardeners who love hanging baskets.

The insert is and looks like recycled cardboard. The skeleton of the basket has fewer metal ribs than other hanging baskets I've seen. In fact, when I went to Home Depot to buy a bracket to hang this, I realized that the other hanging baskets were better assembled and had actual  moss instead of the rather ugly cardboard AND that the traditional hanging baskets were MUCH, MUCH less expensive than this thing.The chain and hook seem adequate (don't plan on hanging any heavy plants). I intend to use moss instead of just potting soil to keep the weight down.Overall? Ugly, cheaply made and wildly overpriced -- when you can find a better price at Home Depot than on Amazon there is something wrong with the picture. I cannot recommend this thing. Look elsewhere for a better price and a stronger and more attractive product.---Edit: I see the price has dropped from $25 to $9 -- that's a big improvement for what this is.

Love the shape of this hanging basket.  Although it's specially constructed with water retaining fiber, it looks very natural.  The hanging chain is also exceptional.  To be as pretty as this basket and as  moisture retaining but at the same time, slowly drying and very supportive of the planting it contains, this  basket is a "win-win" addition.  I am very proud to have this basket filled with flowers hanging from my front porch.'

I like the simple look to this basket and its versatile uses. You can remove the chain and use it as a centerpiece for the table on your patio, or attach the chain and use it as a hanging basket. The liner keeps the water from pouring out the bottom allowing the soil to soak up more water and I have found it to be quite effective at holding water. The liner will likely only last a year but the basket can be relined with moss, or other similar basket liners. The chain is sturdy and the basket has a nice weight to it when full. This is a great investment, but I would like to see the price a bit lower.
summary: Quality basket to use for years

reviewText: I am disappointed with this hanging basket. The chain came apart the moment I touched it and although it wasn't broken, I just needed to attach the links together again and tighten them up, it still took some time and was rather annoying considering I had only just opened the box. The frame of the basket is rather minimal; the metal ribs are thin and very far apart from each other. The liner is made of the same biodegradable material that vegetable plants come in, which is fine for when you're planting pots in the ground but terrible for a hanging basket that will be in full view on your porch or deck. If the metal ribs would have been thicker and closer together then you wouldn't notice the liner as much, however it looks very cheap in this bare bones of a hanging basket. Overall I feel as though this product is over-priced and not at all sturdy enough or attractive enough. I'd recommend finding something else.
summary: Not great--look around for something else

reviewerName: Jill Clardy "So many books, so little time...."
reviewText: I replaced one of my unsightly plastic pots with this attractive hanging planter. It was very easy to attach the chain hooks to the edge of the basket and hang it on an existing hook. I planted it with a big pot of purple pansies. The 14-inch size allows you to use plenty of fresh soil to give the flowers room to grow, and will be slow to dry out, so probably will not need daily watering. The biodegradable pot and open design makes the basket lightweight, and does not appear to spill over and leak as easily as the plastic pot after watering. My concern is that the thin cardboard-like substance from which the liner is made will probably last only one season, and I didn't find on Amazon a source for replacement liners. It would be a shame if this hanging basket was good for only one year, as that sort of offsets the ecological benefit of using a biodegradable liner.

Item received quickly and the basket was packed well.  I've never used a hanging basket that had this type of container before that held the soil.  The tag said that it held 50 percent more water and I believe it.  I'm very happy with the look (it's crafted beautifully) and it really does keep the dampness longer than any other container I've used in the past.  The chain link is the perfect length and the basket has 3 sections for the clips on the chain so that the basket stays plumb and level.I will be purchasing a couple for the front porch area.

This basket is nothing out of the ordinary; the structure includes no additional support between the top and bottom supports, though it is quite sufficient to hold the included eco-liner or an aftermarket coco liner.The clips on the chain bend easily. Once hung in place, they will hold fine, but take extra care to ensure they do not fall onto the lawn and get lost while either walking around with or filling it - my clips came bent in an open state, and I was aware they could fall off as soon as I inspected the pieces, so I did alright with it.The basket works, and really that is all that matters. The absence of a midway reinforcement may even be a plus if considering that visibly I get to see more liner and less black bar. This basket, as of July 2013, has been assigned a new, perfectly reasonable MSRP. If you like the exclusively vertical bar look as much as I do, there's really no reason to pass this one by.
summary: Exclusively Vertical Bars Provide a Clean, More Natural Look

reviewText: Love this! It is large enough to hold several plants with room to grow. It is lightweight. The liner allows it to drain easily. Highly recommend.

My wife does a lot of gardening, but has to be cautious, do to our hot and dry weather.  Therefore, she loved the CobraCo PLB14 hanging basket with EcoLiner was perfect in our weather conditions.  The basket's simple lines make it easy to blend with most decors, especially for environmentally conscious people.  The liner is great, because it looks good, absorbs water, yet it has a draining hole to avoid overwatering.  In addition, the liner is solid, so birds will not pilfer through it as they do with other biodegradable hanging baskets.  I highly recommend this product.

Love this pot!It is sturdier than the other coco fiber pots that i haveThe chain is strong and not so plastic looking like in my other potshave been able to add more flowers than i thought in itI like that it looks different than the ones in the storesYes the liner is different .. clearly says so in the descriptionif you buy this thinking it will look like the others in storesyou will be sadly disappointedthe liner is indeed recycled paper product and looks like it up closefrom a distance honestly I do not notice it looks all that differentthan the ones i have hanging next to itthis is a very basic simple pot

There is not a whole lot to these - the iron or steel or whatever metal is used for the frame is fairly sturdy.  The black chains are great and didn't get twisted up but weren't stiff either like some of the ones I've seen.  The eco liners are really just a kind of cardboard to keep the soil in which actually helps keep things out while still allowing the soil to breathe and not get overhot  like the plastic hanging containers would. I gave a set to my mother for mother's day and she planted strawberries inside it which actually turned out kind of adorable.

I am very pleased with this! I love finding quality items made in the USA and this one did not dissapoint. The 14" is perfect for a cascading hanging plant like fuschia or ivy. I like the look of this, very natural and non-plastic. This was easy to put together and suprisingly light weight. Huge bonus, no leaks when watering!I will definitely be searching for more from this company in the future.
summary: Well designed and quality construction--made in USA

reviewText: I am very happy with this. Put it up today with 7 plants (it's a nice size) and it's currently in my yard. Easy to assemble (basically the only thing you need to do is clip on the chain). It's very attractive, very sturdy and well made with quality iron/metal frame and chain. I rated this as a 4 instead of a 5 star simply because I don't care for the eco lining on this. Kind of a light corrugated porous cardboard material. I have others of these in my yard that I bought from Home Depot and I like them better (with kind of a grassy hay lining the basket. One thing that I guess is good with the CobraCo is that the birds won't be swiping the basket grass for nesting materials, but it doesn't look as nice as the others. Guess it's a personal choice with the lining materials. Overall, I am happy with this basket and would recommend to you.

I wanted to mention first to REALLY check your packing materials, because I initially thought I was missing the chains, until I located them wrapped in paper under the pot.Anyway -- this hanging basket is currently swinging on my front porch, and overall I'm very pleased with it.  The metal basket is very high quality -- really nicely made, and feels as thought it'll last for many seasons outside.  It is shiny and well finished -- painted for rust resistance (most baskets like this are not, and will last you one or two seasons).The chains are very nice quality as well, and match the painted finish of the basket.  The hook at the juncture of the chains is heavy and substantial, and is shaped nicely -- open enough to fit over any shape hook or through any eye you have, and bent in a way that should keep it fairly secure (sometimes hanging baskets have a poorly designed top hook that easily slips off, but this one is large enough that it should stay put, at least when the basket is loaded with dirt).The liner itself is designed as an alternative to the fuzzy brown cocoa husk liners, which have a tendency to dry out quickly (if there's no inner liner of another material).  It fits the bill -- it is EXCELLENT at retaining water, unlike the cocoa husk liners -- this one, especially if filled with that "moisture control" potting soil, will actually stay moist for several days after watering.  I have never had a hanging basket retain moisture as well as this, except for plastic ones.  I assume this is why it is called an "eco" liner -- because you'll use less water and no plastic(?)  (Because obviously cocoa husks are sustainable and bio-degradable -- they just dry out quickly.)  Plastic, besides the whole non-eco thing, gets TOO wet in rainy weather -- this one is a very good balance.The only drawback I can find is that it's just not as attractive as a real cocoa husk liner -- it looks a bit like a cardboard box, or those recycled paper packing forms that come around fragile products!  I think next year I will buy a bit of cocoa husk (they sell extra husks at the garden center) and add some to the basket for "camouflage" between the basket and this liner (assuming it holds up for a second year, which it seems like it might).All in all, a very nice product that should hold up for years.  I would recommend it, and I'd definitely buy a product with this liner (I'd just disguise it with a bit of actual cocoa husk for vanity!)
summary: Sturdy & well made; liner is nice

reviewText: This is really a Plain Jane hanging planter. The liner looks just like the cheap pressed cardboard cemetery baskets. The metal frame feels like it is of average quality, but there are no decorations or flourishes at all.  It won't make much of a difference once it is covered with trailing plants, but it looks pretty boring now with my small Juliet tomatoes transplants.My biggest concern, and the reason I am not impressed with this, is that the liner, basically a pressed cardboard, will fall apart after a short while.  I hope it will make it through the season, but I don't expect it will last another year.  Like my coir baskets, I will line it with a plastic bag (with plenty of holes poked for drainage).  This will not only keep it from drying out rapidly, but will prevent the liner from breaking down too quickly.The difference between this and coir is I can patch the coir.  If one basket is way past its prime, I use good sections of the coir from it to repair bad sections of others.  I can also punch holes in the sides of the coir liners for additional plants and patch the holes the next year.  This will not give me those options.  I would not buy another.
These pots are really awesome.  They hang the plants with three hanging chains.  The really thing is that they support the plants with water pots.  They are really stout planters!

This large (14-inch) basket is lined with a thick paper liner.  The outer, metal skeleton is sturdy, and overall the basket is very attractive.  However, according to an email from the company, the replacement of this paper basket is a coco liner basket rather than a water-saving paper.  So, in essence, this basket is good for a year, then it's back to the old-fashioned coco liner.Photos and the written description of the basket indicate that this basket comes with a chain.  No chain was in the box with the basket.  I have asked for a chain to be sent from the company and will update this review when I receive the chain.Three Stars!UPDATE:I contacted the manufacturer to request a new chain.  They had no extra chains but sent me a new basket, chain included.  It's great, sturdy enough to support the heavy basket.  As a result, I have changed the rating on this basket from three to five stars.  If you need help, contact them.  They'll do what it takes to make it right!FIVE STARS!
summary: Nice Basket but No Chain (be sure to see UPDATE)

reviewText: I  bought these containers for strawberries and upsidown tomatoes, and I think they'll be perfect for both.  The container is quite spacious and sturdy, simpler than my other hanging containers, but nice.The best thing to compare the inside material to is the thing that it's meant to imitate, the coconut matting that's gotten popular recently.  That's what my other two hanging containers use.  This material is thinner and, to be honest, not as attractive.  As I have only recently hung and planted these, I don't know how it's going to hold up over the summer growing season, but I'll try to remember to report back, this winter.

This 14-inch hanging basket came in great use for hanging some rosemary from under our balcony where it will get full sun. The basket comes with a chain that snaps into three spots and a large S-hook to hang it from whatever you'd like. The metal frame is sturdy and durable, though the cardboard insert (the "EcoLiner") seems considerably less so. I didn't notice any issues after I gave the rosemary a good watering, but over time or after excessive rains the EcoLiner may break down sooner than I'd like. I don't have any particular issues with the look of the EcoLiner, as some other reviewers do. The basket holds a sizable amount of material in it. My only other issue is that even with the three individual chains connecting to the appropriate parts of the basket (there are three obvious areas where it's supposed to be connected), the basket seems to be slightly off. Not significantly so, but just slightly askew. Other than that, this seems like a great buy.Note that when I ordered it from Vine it told me I would get two baskets and regular purchasers would get one. I only got one, so it may be that purchasers get two? Or maybe I was only given one by mistake.

The Eco Liner hanging basket is made of rust-resistant steel and  is 14 inches in diameter at the top and 7 inches deep.  It comes with a planting liner and a chain for hanging.  This hanging basket is very attractive and accents the décor of any patio or garden area.  Attached to the hanging basket are the INSTRUCTIONS on how to plant in the Eco liner.  The liner is biodegradable and cuts watering down by 50%. It is a big basket and my purple petunias look so beautiful in it!  This is a must buy if you want a steel basket to use over and over again.

I am very pleased with my CobraCo 14-inch hanging basket with its ecoliner. I have another similar basket with a coco liner that doesn't hold up well, so I'm anxious to compare.First off, the ecoliner is more stable and made the planting easier. I like that it uses up to 50% less water as I sometimes fail to water in a timely manner.I decided on an annual arrangement with a red, white and blue theme. I chose lobelia, red impatiens and white wax begonias since it is to be placed in a mostly shaded area. Both the basket and its contents look lovely, and watering has been minimal. I'm very pleased with this basket and will purchase another.

When I unpacked this hanging basket I was disappointed by its appearance.  2 of the chain hooks were lost in the packing, but I was able to find them.  They had become detached from the chain because they were deformed, but were easily bent back into shape.  The basket is very plain and appears to be made to minimum standards.The liner did not fit the basket very well either.  After planting and watering I thought the liner might soften and take the shape of the basket better.  Watering resulted in a stream draining out the hole in the bottom of the liner.  I removed the plants and potting mix and placed 4 layers of newspaper in the bottom of the liner,  then replanted and watered again.  Water drain was slowed and absorbed by the potting mix but the liner did not seem to absorb any moisture or change shape. After a very rainy week ( over 3 inches fell ) I notice the liner has been softened by moisture enough to take the shape of the basket.  The liner is recycled paper, so it is environmentally friendly, but I still prefer the look of coco fiber liners, and coco fiber conforms to basket shape almost immediately.  I have posted a "before planting" and an "after planting & rain" picture at the top of the page.Bottom Line - The hanging basket is functional but lacks eye appeal. If used with cascading plants it should be adequate.

This is a very large hanging basket that is very sturdy and functional.  It's a very simple and utilitarian design, no frills or extras here.  The metal is very strong, sturdy and looks great for any decor.  The liner is some kind of pressed cardboard.  It doesn't leak as much as coconut liner and holds moisture in there longer - better for the plant.  The price may be a little on the high side, but I also don't expect to have to replace this anytime soon either.  The liner would probably need to get replaced with each replanting.  I don't expect the pressed cardboard liner to last for too long through multiple waterings.  If price is not an issue and you want a good, solid, long-lasting product - this is a great one.  Consider using with plants that trail down that will hide the liner.  The liner is the most unattractive part of the setup.

First of all,The wire construction seems strong,smooth and appears resistant to normal rusting.The cocoa brown paper inserts are dense and textured brown.14" is a good size for my farmhouse porch. The water saving insert is a great thing too.The insides are smooth.I received a very nice pair,however the chain for hanging was nowhere in the boxing.I checked description again,and it did state that chain was included.Now it's off to some other store to look for chains for the two.So construction good,insert also a plus,absent chain sort of turned the situation from A to B-.

The two big differences between this unit and other motion-activated sprayers that I've seen are (a) it's solar powered and not battery powered, and (b) it has a water reservoir and doesn't connect to a hose.  Presumably these are to make it more flexible in where you put it, as they don't lend themselves to lower maintenance.  It is indeed more flexible in where you can put it *assuming* that where you want to put it gets plenty of sunlight _and_ it's small enough to fit there.  The reason that I say the hose versions (which are battery operated on the ones that I've seen) might be better for some of you is because they won't run out of water due to an empty reservoir, won't have the water get dirty or grimy because it's been sitting around outside for days, will operate even in very shady areas, and they are smaller.  You do have to run a hose to them, though, and this unit wins out when that's not possible.I wanted to like it, and it's okay, but I don't think that it's worth the current price of $180.  I can understand that it's expensive to make with the solar panels, motion sensor, pumps, and so on - but I think that's a lot more money than this is worth.  So, I don't recommend it, but it might fit your needs, so I'm listing some considerations below.General Comments(*) This thing is a lot bigger than I had envisioned.  I admit, though, that I'm not very good at visualizing volume from dimensions listed on product pages, so you might not be surprised.  I should have realized that the sprinkler on the top is a regular size sprinkler unit, so this thing is sizeable.  It's just way too big and conspicuous for where I had wanted to put it in my front yard.  I learned about it's operation in my back yard, but I can't really speak to its effectiveness.(*) Set up was really easy.  It took about five minutes, then I was outside filling it with water.(*) The range adjustment (min to max) doesn't seem to do anything on mine.  I've even turned the dial a few times around in any given direction, and it doesn't do anything.  The distance is always the same.(*) The sensor sensitivity dial does adjust it, but it might take you a while to dial in a setting that you like (if you can get it).  The sensitivity that you choose is based on animal size and daily temperature, so you'll probably need to tweak it from time to time.  On the max sensitivity on a hot day, it had no problem detecting me about 20 feet away.(*) Moving it around is best done without much water in it.  At full capacity, the water alone weighs about 30 pounds.Solar Panel Considerations(*) Make sure that where you want to use this has plenty of sunlight, or you won't have much power to operate the sprinkler(*) The effectiveness of the panels drops off as the top surface gets dirty, so you'll likely need to clean it periodically.  At least on my unit, the sprinkler leaks a decent amount of water on to the panels when it sprays, so they get a bit of mineral build up.  Also, when my trees are dropping pollen in Spring (and will be the same with the leaves in Fall), the top gets covered...and then grimy when the water leaks on it.Water Reservoir Considerations(*) Obviously, you need to keep refilling this, and how often depends on how much it sprays.  So, you might find that it will run out of water depending on activity and how often you get around to filling it up.  With a hose, you don't have to worry about that.(*) I know that this has a cap on it, but you might want to also consider that the water might get a bit dirty/slimy if it's sitting out for a while (at least in my yard, things start to grow in standing water).  So, the sprinkler might get clogged, or you're just spraying dirty water around your yard.  You can also clean it out, sure, but I wanted to mention the potential for added maintenance.
summary: Okay, but the hose versions might be better for you

reviewText: Where I live, it seems there are more deer around than birds in the sky. We live in very northern Minnesota and are about an hour outside of the areas largest city. In a tiny tourist town that's surrounded by national forests, we live where people come to camp on the weekends. So to say we have a lot of deer and other wildlife locally would be an understatement. The deer walk in herds comfortably through town all day every day. While most people driving through a neighborhood might have to worry about someones pet dog running out into the street, here you can hardly drive to the local post-office without having to dodge groups of white tails.One of the reasons the deer come into town is because of the easy access to food. Everyone has bird feeders, gardens, and some even buy cracked corn and place it outside in the evenings just for feeding the deer specifically. So at any time of day, locals can look outside and usually see the large pests chowing down on just about anything found in their front yard. The deer here are not easily scared. Barking dogs, cars going by and people walking aren't a bother to them at all. A few years back, I opened my front door to let my 3 dogs outside to go to the bathroom, and found a huge deer had walked up onto my porch and was eating the flowers out of my potted plants. In the process of opening the storm door, I bumped it right in the rear, not knowing it was there. It just turned and looked at me, annoyed that I had interpreted it's meal.However one thing the deer definitely don't like is being squirted by water. They walk past the yards that have running sprinklers, and of my neighbors have motion detecting systems installed, so that when a large animal comes into their yard, a sprinkler system goes off. However I''m not looking to spend that kind of money to install such a large setup, just to keep the deer from eating my potted plants. Also I have 3 large dogs, and I don't need something going off every time I need to let them outside. I need something extremely simple. Something that doesn't require being hooked up to my hose all the time. And I wanted something that didn't need power cables run to it. This Havahart Spray Away is just that.This system is exactly what I needed. I am able to put the Spray Away unit right in front of my porch, where my potted plants sit. I love that it's mobile, not affixed to the ground and no need to have any power cables or hoses hooked up to it. If I decide to move my plants to get better sunlight, I can move this unit right with them. The solar panel provides all the power it needs, and inside of it there is a water reservoir for filling so there's no need to keep the hose hooked up to it. You don't even need to hook up the hose to it to fill it. This is a big plus, since I need my hose for so many other things in the summertime.You can change the sensitivity levels, so that it's not going off every time a bird goes by. Or if you're trying to keep birds like crows or seagulls away, you can set it super sensitive so that it goes off when they get within a certain range. There are two light indicators on the side that will flash to let you know if your water in the reservoir is getting low, or if the solar battery is running low. It does need a few days of sitting in the sunshine before the first use so it can get a full charge. Also if the battery completely runs out (days of raining/cloudy weather) it will need some time to charge up again. This does run on sunlight, so it if sits all day in the shade, it will run on the stored solar energy and then need recharged before using it again. If you use this in direct sunlight, recharging time won't be a problem, because it will be able to keep drawing on the solar energy each day.This is the perfect solution for keeping deer away from plants, stray dogs out of your lawn or just about anything else you want to keep away from something. With the adjustable sensor, you can set it to the size of animal you want, and the distance away that it is before the unit spays them. It can be set to keep something out of your yard, but not squirt people as they are waling by on the sidewalk. With the great portability it has (no power cords or hoses), the low-cost when compared to built in deterrent system, and the range of settings it offers, this Havahart Spray Away is just what I was looking for. Love it!
summary: No cords, no hoses and more affordable than built in systems

reviewText: This has many great attributes:  it isn't bad looking, not really that big and tall, black rather than some hideous col0r, lightweight so it's easy to move and of course, best of all you don't have to plug it in or hook it up to a hose.  The only thing is where I want to put it to protect a couple of apple trees I'm trying to espalier against a fence is a place I often walk myself and I then can get sprayed instead of the deer. It does seem to discourage the deer but I need it in many places.  I will try moving it around, easy to do as it's so light, and see how long the effects last from the last time the deer were sprayed.  I guess you could just move it every week or so so the deer would be taken by surprise because there are many different areas in my garden where they like to nibble.

I compared the Havahart to the Scarecrow sprinkler system.  I posted two pictures so people could size the relative size difference because I think it would factor into some people's decision to get one over the other.Now, this is not the most pretty sprinkler out there.  Seriously, it really does look like something you might expect to see roaming the hallways of an Imperial Star Destroyer... but I've never seen a garden inside one of those ships.  A little speaker with droid sounds and this thing could really give your friends a laugh.On to the comparison versus the Scarecrow:1.  Solar powered, never need to worry about batteries.  Honestly, one 9V batt lasted the whole season on the Scarecrow.  So while I really like this feature, it's not a huge advantage.  Also, if you live in an exceedingly cloudy/misty area or the ideal set up place is in a shady area, then this unit will be fairly useless to you.2.  Motion detection is merely okay.  I actually thought the Scarecrow had a more sensitive sensor.  After adjusting the sensitivity to a high number, walking back and forth in front of this unit (and waiting the 8 seconds for it to reset) was not reliable to set the sensor off (but it should be able to pickup a human fairly easy).3.  No hose needed.  Awesome!  This is especially good since a hose has to be constantly moved to prevent the grass underneath from dying.  Also, despite my best efforts, the Scarecrow always had a tiny leak at the plastic hose connection.  This Havahart unit is fairly large, but light, so even with 3.5 gallons of water, it was no problem filling it up, picking up and taking it to its resting place.  (The cap is not water tight though, so it's very easy for water to flow out onto your pant legs if you tilt it...)4.  Sprinkler distance was mediocre.  I was expecting a lot more distance.  But then it occurred to me that this solar unit has to power it's own little pump to eject the water.  With the Scarecrow, since it's hooked up directly to a hose, it can get a lot farther distance.  This would be important for long distance coverage, but if you're only interested in protecting a flower bed, then it's sprinkler throw combined with it's sudden mechanical noise should be good enough to deter animals.So, I think both units are actually quite effective.  They both operate on the same principle of scaring animals away.  But each system has it's advantages and disadvantages in upkeep and requirements.  At their current pricepoints, you could get ~ 3 Scarecrows for one Havahart.  So are the fancy features worth it to you?
summary: My own personal Imperial Droid to watch over my flowers, PICS posted

reviewText: When it comes to humane solutions to common outdoor pest problems, what could be greener than sun and water?The same two elements that nurture my backyard tomato plants every summer now play a major part in keeping birds, squirrels and other critters away from them with the assistance of the Havahart Spray Away Elite II Motion Detector Sprinkler.This is one smartly-devised, cleverly-constructed item.  For starters, it's solar-powered, so there are no plugs or batteries to worry about.  Secondly, it doesn't required an attached garden hose--just fill the 3.5 gallon basin with water and you're good for approximately 35 motion-detected activations triggered by the infrared sensor.And it's good to go right out of the box--you just attach the adjustable sprinkler head with the provided wrench.It comes pre-charged, although it needs a few days in direct sunlight for peak performance.  You just adjust the protection range and spray distance, as well as the sensitivity knob, and then, anything (or anyone for that matter), who crosses in front of the sensor's detection range gets a cautionary blast of water.I'm very impressed with this unit even though I haven't actually seen it in action yet--I've heard it do its thing a couple of times, though.  The ultimate proof will be the state of my tomato crop in a couple of months, but so far, so good!

These days everyone is aware and concerned about chemical deterents, even the non toxic, all natural products can have a nasty smell or pepper burn to them.  A device like this seems to be a good replacement for repeated treatments with constant cost.Setup was fairly simple but you need to get it right in order for it to do it's job properly... After screwing the spray head onto the top with the supplied plastic wrench (wrench designed to slip off when properly tightened)Place unit with the IR position pointing the direction you need based on it's full range of detection, set the amount of sensitivity needed (range) with the knob on the back, set the sprayer head to spray the direction you want. set the sprayer to spray the distance needed at the time, fill with water and turn it on.  That's it, other than you really should place the unit in the bright Sun right off to fully charge the batteries.Of course you will be moving this around as the pests dictate so you'll make the same adjustments over each time.  They advise you to NOT pick the unit up by the top when you move it and to be sure to support it under the base.  Since the item housing is all plastic I understand the concern.One thing that took the first day to get used to working in the yard was moving in front of the sensor by accident.....  when you are not used to it being there it's easy to do and you will get sprayed.Don't forget to turn it off if there will be a lawn party or children/pets over to visit.In case you are wondering, I would like to make note that even though the product description says it makes a noise that helps scare pests away, it's just the natural noise of the pump and water spraying, not a noise maker of any kind.  Does not bother humans in the area at all.I'm thinking some regular yard pests might get used to it and figure out how get around it over time but we shall see.A couple of items I have on wish list is that they had the "low water" & "Low Battery" LEDs on the backside so you had a chance of seeing them come on from the house or porch rather than only from the target zone...  you do need them on the IR sensor side to set the thing up withour spraying water (light come on to indicate you've been detected) but for the price could have had two more to the rear.It would also be nice if the IR sensor would rotate up and down like their other small unit does... this would cover you better for any size animal you had and still keep the water tank level as it needs to be.I"ve uploaded some photos I took of it showing a few things you don't get to see in company product photos if you care to see them at the top of the page.Update 5/24/2013;This unit started activating without anything in the sensor zone, was working well for about three weeks.  On the same #2 setting, it will now repeat fire until out of water or dead battery.Contacted Havahart via their website a couple of days ago about the problem but have not heard back from them yet, will return with resolution when it comesUpdate 6/2013;Customer service was very helpful and talked me through a few diagnostic procedures, then sent a return shipping label and sent out a new Elite II that is now in service and working as it should.Update 7/2013;I really had high hopes for this animal repellent and at first I gave an Amazon 4 star rating for "I like it" but after living with it and seeing animals moving around in front of it without being chased (even with sensitivity all the way up the scale), and also now and then seeing it spray without anything in sight, I have to lower my rating as it just isn't working out for it's intended purpose and price tag. I have tried every setting over and over to get what I needed and have to give up now.... A shame as it's a good idea
summary: Good idea...  Sorry to say, mine is just not dependable in daily use...

reviewText: If you want a water deterrent to protect your garden and yard from pests that this is the one to get. The fact that this thing is solar powered and has its own water supply in the base and is portable makes it the perfect solution. Now I've reviewed a few sprinkler deterrent systems in the past and this one is by far the best. The ones I reviewed in the past you need to hook up to a hose which I find a lot more difficult in placing exactly where you need. Where this thing as long as he gets a decent amount of sunlight is ready to go and can be placed practically anywhere.Most hose type sprinkler systems and cost you anywhere from $80-$120 I think that dropping the few extra dollars on this system will make you much happier. Another thing to note is that you'll be able to tell if it's doing its job by how much water it uses. As wherewith the hose type deterrent systems you won't really be able to tell if the animals haven't been coming around or if the system has been working. Where is simply looking in the basin on this product yield no of it's actually working or not.I really think Havaheart got it right with this product and yes while it is a little bit more expensive the mobility of it is top-notch I highly recommend this.
summary: This thing is great - WORTH THE EXTRA CASH!

reviewText: Seemed like a novel idea at first, but I'm having a hard time adjusting the stream.  Mine sprays more to the right as another reviewer said.  The plastic sprayer has an adjustment but although I tried to move the tabs, it didn't seem to really change anything and I just wasn't too sure what I was doing.  I wanted this motion detector to keep the rabbits away from my car as they were eating the fuel lines...I am not kidding.  However I can't see this helping me as the sensor is not 360 degrees so the rabbit can come in from opposite direction.

Love this things.  It works right out of the box.  As soon as i opened it, I attached the trigger on the top (just screw it in using the tool it came with.  Put water into it.  And Voila!!  I really thought that it had to stay in the sun for awhile before having the power to spray.I put the sensitivity on high and waved my hands over it, and the darn thing shot out water in about a second. At the highest sensitivity, it sprays at anything that moves a bit, even like leaves.  I had to bring it down.  ust left it outside to shoo away squirrels, cats, and skunks in my back yard.
summary: no electric wire, no water hose, no problem!!

reviewText: Out of the box Havahart Spray Away Elite II Hose-Free Motion Activated Sprinkler Animal Repellent is almost ready to use. Attach the spray head with the included plastic wrench, fill with water and you are ready to go as it is pre-charged and ready to use right out of the box.Standing about 2ft tall and about a 2ft round footprint the Spray Away is easily placed anywhere you need it. No hoses to run, no worries about leaking faucets or hoses, just fill and let the sun keep it powered up.The range of spray is adjustable, I have found that just the noise will scatter most animals, a direct hit doesn't seem necessary.So I keep the spray range away from the filler so I don't get wet.There are lights to show low water level and low battery (battery an go low if it discharges too often so you may need to adjust the sensitivity)Unfortunately these lights are fairly dim and worse the are right above the motion sensor so you will set off the device when you approach to see the lights. The device claims "simply look out your window any time you need an update" but this means the sensor would need to be facing the house, it seems to me the sensor would be facing out for approaching animals.4 stars because my tomatos are no longer getting robbed, would be 5 stars if I could see the low water indicator easier, perhaps a blinking bright white led on the top.
summary: Completely portable, use anywhere to keep animals away.

reviewText: Havahart makes a great safe natural Animal Repellant.  This device sprays water from a basin at critters that walk by the motion sensor, and is run on solar powered batteries.  The device is light, and portable.  You just have to fill it up with water and off you go.  It does take a good time to charge the batteries though. Right out of the box, the device was able to give a few shots of water for me to test, but after that, I got the low battery warning and it took about 3+ days for it to charge up.  It is good for about 3-5 shots continuously before the battery will need to recharge.It's ideal for areas where you occasionally get critters that you need to scare away.  I place mine around my raised vegetable garden and it helps to keep the rabbits away.  I really like the fact that it is maintenance free and only needs to be filled with water.  I even left it out in a heavy thunderstorm, and nothing happened to it.  It still operates as normal.However, if you have a high level of animal intrusions, this won't work for you.  The battery life is too short and takes too long to charge.  Havahart makes a plug in hose model for high level needs.I think this is a great device and great idea.  It is a bit pricey but works wonderfully.  If you have a need for a maintenance free water sprinkler, this device is for you.  Just remember that is is NOT meant for high animal activity and you will be happy with this purchase.  I highly recommend it.

Last year, I planted green beans in a garden.  By mid-June, I gave up and let the rabbits have them.  I tried sprays on the plants, fences, etc., but nothing helped for more than a day or two.  This year, I tried the Havahart Spray Away Elite II.  I've had it a few weeks and, so far, so good!  Assembly was a breeze.  Everything is together except the actual spray nozzle that just screws on.  There is even a wrench included that makes it impossible to over-tighten it.  I took it out in the yard and followed the directions to adjust width of spray area, filled it with water, and adjusted how far out it sprayed.  That was the entire setup.  I rarely see it actually work, but the plants aren't eaten down to the ground like they were last year (and we have plenty rabbits around this year too), so I assume it's doing the trick.I haven't had any issues with the solar power not having enough charge which was a big concern of mine.  Overall, I'm very pleased and glad I'm not having to use chemicals to keep pests away.EDITED 6/9/2013I'm sad to say, after a few weeks of use, the unit has completely stopped spraying.  I've done all the troubleshooting I can and nothing will get it to spray anymore.  I'm very disappointed.
summary: Keeps the rabbits out of the garden!

reviewText: I have both the 5268 and 5269, the 5268 is currently unavailable on amazon.com, but here's a link to its page where customers' reviews could still be found.http://www.amazon.com/gp/product/B004VMACA6. I have tried them both, the only noticeable difference to me is the rechargeable battery pack, the 5269 comes with a pre-charged battery, ready for immediate use, whereas the 5268 has to be charged 1st prior to operation.The 5269 comes mostly assembled, it takes little time to set it up and put it into use. I like the fact that it has a tank for water storage, no need to hook it up to a water faucet with a hose. The solar power is a great idea, but it does need to be placed at a place with good sun exposure ot make it work, and the battery strength indicator tells you whether the battery is strong or weak, a great feature. I do wish it had a back-up battery power option such as regular AAs or a charging port for household electricity for rainy days. But overall I am satisified with its performance.

I got this 3 weeks ago and it's had plenty of time to charge and is full of water but the low water and low battery lights flash continuously.  I just called Havahart and they will be sending another one and want this one back so they can examine it to find the problem, so the customer service is excellent, and I'll update this when I get a chance to evaluate the next one.  They say it's on back-order so it may be awhile but the vine program makes you write something within a month of receiving it so here is the evaluation so far.Update: The replacement works fabulous, and I forget it's there until I get sprayed!  You have to let it charge while ON for 3 days, then try it out.  You can set the range and direction it sprays, like a regular sprayer.

We use this to repel deer and squirrels in our garden.  I really like this product as an alternative to the scarecrow version.  What allows this to standout is being solar powered (no batteries needed) and needs no hose.  This is a huge plus.  Of course you have to fill the reservoir on occasion but this is no big deal since it is an infrequent necessity.It took about 3 days of sun to charge the internal battery.  We tried alone away from the scarecrows to check on its effectiveness.  It doesn't have the same power or pressure coming out the nozzle as the scarecrow, but it works just fine.  I recommend this device and look forward to it keeping the critters out of our veggies and flowers.This is the 2nd one that I own and like them a lot more than the type you put hoses and batteries.  Now is the time of year to get one of these right when you plant your bulbs and veggie starts.  Nothing like coming out and finding the squirrels have dug up half your garden or a little later when your garden up and growing finding the deer have neatly pruned everything back.I highly recommend these system over sprays on the plant stuff (which washes away with irrigation or rain), fencing and what other repellents are out there.  These are easy and they work!

The Havahart motion detector animal repellent does a fine job repelling ducks, rabbits, herons and other animals from backyards, gardens, and fish ponds.I tried the "Havahart Spray Away Elite II Motion Detector Sprinkler Animal Repellent 5369" model which keeps herons and ducks away from a backyard fish pond by spraying water and emitting an unexpected noise and motion to scare them away when approaching. A couple years ago herons entered our area in unwanted numbers to swoop down and grab unsuspecting goldfish out of the pond. They are less of a threat now but ducks are the nuisance of choice this year.The Havahart motion detector was easy to set up for use. One thing I really like about it is that the detector is solar operated so does not have to be plugged in or does not have batteries that eventually will have to be replaced.  The other nice feature is that it does not have to be hooked up to a hose. You just add water when you set up the detector and it works fine.Because it is hose-free and does not have to be plugged in to an electrical outlet, the detector is highly portable making it easy to move to different locations to find the best one. Once you find a good location the water basin (which holds 3  gallons of water) can easily be buried in the ground to make it more pleasing to the eye.The device can detect motion within 35 feet and protect an area up to 1,900 square feet. You can adjust the detector to cover a shorter distance so it does not spray water into an area where you frequently can be found walking around to avoid getting wet.In fact getting wet (once) is the only problem I have experienced so far. I am sure with improved memory on my part and some fine tuning adjustments this problem will lessen or go away. The Havahart Spray Away Animal Repellent is a motion detector that does its intended job and performs well over time.
summary: How to Keep Herons and Ducks Away From Your Fish Pond

reviewText: The one thing that has kept us from having a garden at our house is that the wildlife of all sizes would eat it right up, so we would be paying out time and money to feed the critters!This device lets you set up a zone of coverage around your garden so that when it senses the presence of something warm enough to trigger it, it will spray for short period of time and hopefully scare the animal away.This does not require a hose or an electrical line, so you can set it anywhere there is sunlight to charge the battery. You can fill the reservoir with a hose or with a watering can.You can set the sensitivity with a knob - you can also turn it off so you can work in your own garden!you can adjust the spray width - the smaller the better so you don't waste water.

I must admit I was over-the-top excited to receive this unit. I had read about the devices similar to this that attach to your hose and have always wanted one to keep these pesky bunnies from eating my grass and then peeing on it and killing it.Here's my impressions:The sensor isn't very accurate. I turned it to the highest setting and had my kids crawl around. Most of the time they stayed dry, which was disappointing to us all. Also, when it did spray them, the spray was a little weak. I'm pretty confident that it would have deterred the rabbits, but if the sensor only kicks in once-in-a-while, the effects of it would be lessened.Filling up the water will definitely become a hassle. Because mine didn't go off as often as I would have liked it, it never ran out of water. This being said, if you live in a place that will keep this thing busy, and you're like me, chances are you'll get tired/lazy/busy, etc. and let it go.So my advice is:Get one that attaches to a hose. You'll likely get more pressure, and you won't have to fill it up.

I have been doing battle for my garden with the elements and pests for the past 15 years.  I have tried just about everything, excepting pesticide, and I will not resort to that.  Since I built raised beds and routinely add compost, the water problem has been tempered somewhat. My biggest problem the past few years has been pests, of the larger variety.  i have fenced my yard, fenced my garden and even put fencing (hicken wire or hardware cloth) around individual plants.  It's a lot of work and expense and does not always work (animals dig)!last year i tried an earlier version of the Havahart spray away and while I thought it was a great idea, I was not very impressed with it's performance.  The primary issue was power.  It stopped working after a few days of rain and the spray did not reach as far as the infra-red detection.  The new model seems to have solved that problem with a better battery which is precharged so that it may be used right out of the box.  I have only had the new one out for a little while but can already see the improvement.  It is an overcast, rainy day and it is working nonetheless!  Besides that, it does seem to spray to the set range (that is the spray reaches as far as you have the detection sensitivity set).  My complaint with the older model was that it can detect movement at 35 feet, but the spray only reached 5 feet!I know from years of studying behavioral psychology that you get the best results when there is 100% certainty.  With something like this in the garden, an intruder will be sprayed every time it enters and should rapidly learn to stay away.I like that it is safe to people , pets and wildlife (as well as plants).  The reason I gave it 4 stars rather than 5 is that I have some withholds based on my experience with the older model.
