If my garden survives this season without my having to fence every plant or sleep outside, I will come back and rerate.  Thus far I am mor impressed with this model than the old one.  They do seem to have the kinks worked out.  Now if I can only find something which is safe and effective against giant snails we'll be in business (I may have to keep those little fences up... but at least they do not dig ;)-----------------------------------------------------------updated 6/22/2013I am updating this review after having had it in place for a few months.  It does work a good deal better than the prior model.  One of the complaints i had with the old model was that it could dretect at a distance of 15-20 feet but the spray was only 3 feet (not very effective for something 15 feet away).  This model has a longer range, and is somewhat bvetter matched to the detection.I still believe it could use some twesaks and may not be the thing for everyone (it very much depending on the type of pest).  There isa limited spanb to the detection and spray.  That is, it will only detect pests coming from one direction (and they do not always do that ;)  The spray is also at a height of about 3-4 feet, so if you have small pests it would not work very well (for example I do not imagine it would be much heklp to people who have issues with rabbits or gophers).In short it is working better than the last, and my garden has only been attacked once since I put this out, BUT I think it was out of water then.  That said, for me, it is helping some and I find it to be a big imporvement over the older model.
summary: An innovative product and potential problem solver

reviewText: It only takes a minute to install this product.  You just have to attach the sprinkler head to the top of the unit.  There is a sensitivity knob to use depending on the size of animal you are trying to deter (squirrel, rabbit, deer etc).  There are indicator lights to warn of low water or low battery.  The spray can be adjusted to long or short distances as well as  to make it oscillate with a wide or narrow arc.  That's the good news.The bad news is the product is overpriced for what it is.  We have not yet gotten the low battery light to go off  so the sprinkler is still just sending out a short single stream rather than the oscillating arc.  The ideal place we chose does not have full sun but we will see if the strong Colorado sun can still fully charge the device.  We have not used the product long enough to see other problems but other reviewers seem to indicate additional difficulties with long term use.  Ironically we haven't noticed many rabbits in our yard since installing this product so it is difficult to say how effective the product is at discouraging them and other little creatures.
summary: Environmentally Friendly And Humane But Has Some Problems

reviewText: I have a grass area in the back yard near the pool where our dog always likes to go to the bathroom.  I tried almost every technique to get her to go somewhere else, and nothing worked.  I tried dog repellants, crate training, and the motion detector sprays that attach to the hose, and none of those tricks worked.  The motion detection sprayers that attach to the hose are useless because they always end up leaking under the hose pressure and I had to stop using them.  FINALLY this Havahart battery powered sprinkler did the trick!  Our dog stays far away from this thing, she uses a different area of the yard as the bathroom.  We can keep it in the back yard as long as we need, without worrying about causing a major flood.  The motion detector is pretty accurate.  The spray is brief, but it's startling also because of the noise it makes, so it will scare people too if you happen to walk in its path and are not suspecting anything!  I love that we can place this in remote locations where the hose connection is not easily accessible, and not worry about the leaking problem of the hose units.
summary: Finally, a motion detection sprayer that works!

reviewText: I SO wanted to just love this motion detector sprinkler by Havahart, but unfortunately we've had a rough start in using it. I charged it outside for a few days before we began use. The sprinkler is easy enough to set up and fill with water. Though it's fairly large for a motion detection sprinkler, and heavy when fully filled with water.I will say I think this product *would* work pretty well if ours were doing what it was supposed to. With the sensitivity turned all the way up, it missed no motion in our garden. That said, the range and function of the sprinkler head has been disappointing. This product touts a 1900 square foot range, but it barely reaches  across our 900 square foot garden even when it is right against the edge. The last couple feet of our 30 ft wide garden go untouched by the water when it is fully charged and spraying full blast.But what has been the most disappointing is that the sprinkler head on our product only turns to it's right, and it has no problem adjusting toward the right when there is movement in that direction. However, when movement moves back over to it's left, the sprinkler head won't turn back. It just ends up stuck completely to the right, spraying in just ONE spot unless we manually start it over back on the left. (At which point it just eventually ends up stuck directed at the right again.) So basically, this renders the whole thing ineffective unless these pesky rabbits only go for one spot of our garden.I will be calling Havahart, I'm happy to report that they make their customer service line well known when you buy this product. We'll be seeing if this is just a defect with ours and what can be done about it, and I'll be sure to update this review accordingly.As for now, however, I'm sorry, I can't recommend this product. I feel it could be GREAT, if it would just work correctly.

We like the way the Havahart Spray Away works with the exception of the arc of coverage.  We have it set at a fairly wide spray arc and we have observed that when it triggers, it sprays only one half of the arc of coverage in a single shot.  It starts were the head is pointed and goes half the distance of the arc.  This can be a problem because the critter might be on the wrong side of the arc and it won't get wet at all.  It may take a couple of sprays to get hit and some critters will be in and out in that amount of time with some of our veggies gone.  We had to have the sensitivity up at the highest setting to get a good response from the unit.  We are in May and it is only 67 degrees out, so it isn't hot.  I don't know how this will work when the unit gets in the 80's and 90's which is pretty common in Texas during May and June.  The instructions say the sensitivity must be set higher in hot weather but we are already maxed out.I haven't tried the hose and spray type of unit but will do so in the future.  The problem with that set up is that you have to have a hose on at all times.  With this product, it is solar powered and has its own water reservoir.  I like that part about this unit but am really disappointed with the coverage, especially at the price.We've had a variety of critters in our backyard and really wanted this to work.  We also have birds starting to arrive for our strawberries and they will likely come back for tomatoes and peas.  We'll see over time how this performs and I'll update this review once I have more information.Updated:  While the spray still does the half arc, it may be that that is enough.  We have had overnight visitors again (we think it is a bobcat based on prior sightings.)  The first night, the sprinkler almost completely emptied and we found that something had knocked all our potted plants down in an effort to get out of the backyard.  The second night, only about a third of the reservoir was empty but the spot the cat had been doing its business in my veggie garden was dug up but nothing was deposited.  We think the sprinkler scared it away before it could finish.  That might be what the half arc does - if the cat had come in on the side that sprayed first, maybe the damage would have been even more minimized.
summary: Seems to be scaring the critters out of the backyard

reviewText: This thing is HUGE and kind of amazing. It doesn't need a hose, which is good, I guess? Is it? I'm not sure why no hose is a good idea. If it's for use in a yard, hoses are there, so why not use it?Like everything else, it has pros and cons.PROS: It's portable and you don't need to hook up a hose to it. It's solar powered. It's big and stable. It works.CONS: The price. WOW! It must pump the water in the reservoir rather than using a hose pressure so it's less powerful. Pump uses more current than just the detector so after several sprays it could deplete the battery. Since there is no hose, the reservoir can also be depleted and will need to be refilled.One reviewer says he'll use RV antifreeze in it so he can use it in the winter. I hope it's a nontoxic antifreeze. My final thought is this: isn't there a point beyond which complexity becomes a detriment, rather than an advantage? Isn't this getting close?
summary: Self contained, portable and solar powered!

reviewText: The Havahart Spray Away is a good option for deterring deer and critters if you live in an area with plenty of sunlight. Here in central Texas, that's no problem and there's no shortage of animals wanting to eat all our plants. The device is very easy to set up with minimal packaging and assembly and is already charged and ready to fire. You only need to fill the basin with water, set the sensitivity and find a place to scare off the wildlife. Generally this works well for medium traffic areas since the battery will only allow several blasts a day and you don't want to be refilling the machine all the time. For high traffic areas, I would recommend a traditional unit where you can connect a hosepipe. This newer model is definitely an improvement on the previous unit I tried in terms of the battery performance and sensitivity adjustment (the old version really had a mind of its own). In practice it works well at deterring most animals although we've found that the feral hogs don't seem too bothered.
summary: An improvement on the previous model

reviewText: Update - as promised, I'm updating this review. Once again, it has died a pre-mature death with the exact same problem as the prior unit. Light's up to show the battery working/alive. Doesn't spray. Plain and simple, these don't see to last. Given the price, can no longer recommend an item with just over a year average life expectancy.Original Review...I hard the earlier version of this same sprayer and liked it immensely until it suddenly quit working. Given the cost and relatively brief time the unit worked, I was hesitant to purchase one (the prior had been via a Vine review). However, like many people, this seemed to be the most humane way to deal with raccoons that have been wrecking havoc in our  yard. The little buggers have figured out the traps and won't go near them, the dogs go crazy over the little coons and none of the plants are safe after both racoon and dogs go pouncing over them.This works beautifully for both the dogs and the racoons so everyone is happy. It looks almost exactly like the old one and works in the same manner except this one doesn't spray back/forward like the old one but rather in a burst fashion. Personally I prefer the older motion but either way this gets the job done. Simply fill with water, allow to charge in the sun, set the range and leave. It's that easy. Assuming the lifespan of this one is longer than the last, I give this a full 5 stars as an effective yet humane way to deal with critters, keeping dogs out and so forth. I will update if the unit fails too soon.
summary: Fast Death - AGAIN _ Updated Review - Some notable changes from prior look-alike model

reviewText: This unit and similar devices are designed to scare away yard pests who may snack on your plants and/or leave droppings in your yard.I ordered the Havahart Spray away Motion detector sprinkler to replace my Scarecrow motion activated sprinkler. The Scarecrow requires that you keep a pressurized garden hose attached to the unit for it to function. This does not work in cold weather, when the water in the hose is likely to freeze.The Havahart Elite two requires no garden hose. It has it's own 1.5 gallon fluid reservoir which needs to be filled periodically. I say fluid rather than water, because I plan on filing it with RV antifreeze in cold weather to keep the fluid from freezing. Proper placement is a consideration because this device is huge!. It has a 17" diameter basin and the entire unit sits 23" tall unless you bury the basin in the ground-which is a good idea.The Elite also has a solar charger to keep the battery charged.Near the top of the unit are two indicator LEDs to tell you if the battery needs charging, or if the tank needs to be refilled. Great idea!I will update this report after I see the unit in operation.

I am truly amazed at the number of really favorable reviews on this thing.  Although I very much respect the other reviewers opinions, I must say personally I have been nothing but disappointed with it.  I have had it for a while now and been testing it in different situations.  Except for a very small select few, I can't see where this thing would work that well at all, never mind be worth it for the high price they're asking for it.... I'm not going to go into the mechanics of putting it together and how it works for that is well described in the other reviews.  When it is actually working, it does the job quite well.  I particularly like the wide range of sensitivity it has with a 1 to 10 scale dial.  With this you should be able to adjust it to any kind of critter you are trying to banish.  Anything from a squirrel to a deer.  And I love the reservoir feature that doesn't require a hose running across your yard somewhere.  But that about does it as far as its assets.  Basically this thing is a great idea, but unfortunately reminds me of the first cell phone that was big and heavy and had about 15 minutes talk time but was considered revolutionary for its time.  (And also extremely expensive like this is).  Some time down the road, they will get this thing right too...First up on its liabilities is the extremely cheap sprinkler head that comes with it.  It's so cheap feeling that I was afraid of breaking it just screwing it on.  I know that many sprinkler heads are plastic, but I expected something more, perhaps with a little metal in it with the price of this thing.  The smallest bit of manhandling, or runaway baseball hitting it for example is going to snap it like a twig.  Really sad.  My biggest problem with it however is its very short battery life and long recharge.  The basin in it provides about 35 bursts of water, but trust me it will take forever for you to get that many out of it.  The instructions with it stated that it arrives fully charged and ready to go.  Well I managed to use up its first life just setting it up and testing it with different sensitivity settings.  After 6 bursts it was dead.  The low battery light came on and that was all she wrote.  Which brings me to something else I didn't like right away.  Unlike other things like radios and flashlights that still run when the batteries are weak, this thing just dies when the battery light comes on and refuses to work at all.  The low battery light is not a low battery warning at all, but a dead battery indicator.  Once it comes on the thing is totally non functional until you charge it again.  (It kinda reminds me of the old so called idiot lights in cars.  They came on to just tell you that you were screwed for the most part).  After charging it in the bright sun for 3 full days, I set it out to work again.  I know that everyone has different ideas for it as to what they are trying to control.  For me my basic aim with it is to stop cats from going near my bird feeders.  We have a lot of cats around here, and its always a battle trying not to provide them with a smorgasbord.. My feeders are in an area of partial sun and shade, and unfortunately my second attempt with it saw it die before the day was out, and the "low" battery light being on again.  That means another full 3 days in the sun to get another 6 or 7 bursts out of it.  My third attempt with it in a place with more sunshine faired a little better.  But it still lasted less than 24 hours before it was dead again.  That was enough for me.  I am going back to the hose and battery model for less than half the price..In conclusion, all these motion detector water devices are a good, and harmless idea to keep pesky varmints of all manner away from your 'possibles.  And I also realize that having a hose attached with a battery operated unit is not ideal for sure.  But I still highly recommend a hose system over this thing.  In short, if where you have in mind for this is in an area of full sun with little in the way of varmints, you may just get by with never having to see it go dead on you.  But just about any other combination will see it die, with a three day respite in between getting it fully charged again.  A sunny spot with lots of varmints like rabbits, cats, etc., and it will die at around 6 to 8 bursts.  (All three times I charged this fully I never got more than 7 bursts out of it).  A sun and shade area won't see it live past a day or two no matter what the critter traffic, and just getting some cloud cover for a few days under any circumstances will see this be worthless in any scenario.  (It will still go off in the rain or on a day with showers with any movement unless you remember run out and to turn it off completely).  What this thing really needs is a battery backup that takes over when the solar power fails, sorta like a hybrid Havaheart.  Then it would pretty much run non stop between the two.  As it is, the best I can do with this model is 2 stars considering its drawbacks and price.  It just doesn't last, can't be trusted, and in my opinion way too expensive for what you get out of it... : )
summary: Unrealiable And Short Lived Solar Power...Expensive.

reviewText: I wanted this to scare away rabbits and the occasional deer that wander in to our backyard. Rabbits do set it off.  The spray lasts about 3 seconds, which seems to be enough to scare the rabbits that have triggered it.The spray is surprisingly strong.  It seems to spray like any other hose-powered circular pulsating sprinkler.  It sprays out to approximately 25 feet as the instructions claim.  The "travel" and the water spray distance are both adjustable.Test the unit without water first (like the instructions say), as it will save a lot of battery drain while testing.The unit is infrared (IR) so body heat sets it off, not motion like tree branches in the wind, etc.  I haven't had any issue with branches, etc.  setting it off even on very windy days.The area I am protecting doesn't see a lot of action, but it hasn't run low on battery yet.  I can't be sure without watching it for 24 hours, but I would estimate it sprays about 3 times a day max.I like that it's solar so no batteries to change & no hose to drag across the patio/lawn.  I tested it on a perfectly sunny day to see how many sprays in a row it would do; it did 12 & then needed to recharge.  Within an hour, it was charged enough to activate again - Then I got 14 sprays out of it. They were somewhat weaker by the 10th spray but would have chased away a rabbit.  I'd say that's more than enough for my situation.The unit is bigger than what I was expecting but that's mainly because of the water reservoir.  It's black so not obnoxious looking sitting on the corner of my patio and no hose trailing after it.

I have the original Spray Away, and after a few months, it started falling apart and leaking. I was hopeful that many of the seemingly obvious design problems in the original had been addressed, but sadly, this sequel is more of the same.In fact, the only thing that's really notable over its predecessor, is that this works out of the box (the original needed to be left outside for a day or two to charge). Other than that, the top still inexplicably pops off of the base, getting any sort of accuracy out of the spray head is a bridge too far, and the tank empties out much faster than expected.Where it does excel, intentionally or not, is that the noise of the activated sprinkler is enough to scare animals away before a drop of water hits fur. I use this to keep my dogs out of the garden, and they hate the noise more than anything. And to that end, I guess it works as advertised, if you want critters away -- dryness optional.

This is SUCH a great idea!  The solar power, the reservoir, etc.  And it works--mostly.The first few days, we noticed that the reservoir emptied right away, and I had an animal repellent surrounded by bunnies.  (I was going to post a picture of that--it's hilarious!)  We were shocked that it emptied so quickly--but realized that when the sprinklers came on, it sensed the water and sprayed over and over again until it emptied.  Since the sprinklers run 2-3 times a day here, that emptied super fast...Once we adjusted the sensitivity, it has been fine...so be aware--if it's emptying quickly, check that your sprinklers aren't activating the repellent.I do wish it had a continuous water source capability.  Just a float with a hose attachment.  That would make this perfect.As it is, it has indeed kept the bunnies off of the grass.  (Once we figured out the emptying problem.)I would have given it 5 stars if it had an option to hook up an external water source.  We went out of town for 4 days and it was empty when we got home, and bunny poo all over the lawn.  There was nothing we could do about that.
summary: The reservoir empties too quickly, and there's no way to  hook up a water source.

reviewText: I initially wrote a glowing review about the Havahart Spray Away Elite II because its range (50 ft) and spray distance (25 ft) matched my area coverage needs and everything worked well for awhile. Now the solar battery light (indicating low levels) comes on a lot, and it does not spray water until there is enough charge.  Days can pass before operation resumes.The device is placed in the sunniest possible spot in our yard.  It is virtually tree-less, however, Michigan weather can be unpredictable. Apparently our sunny days do not provide enough juice to keep this thing effectively operating.  I keep the solar panels clean, and wonder what more can be done to make it work better.I revised the review and downgraded stars simply because I need an animal repellent that works consistently.  Think twice about purchasing unless constant sunny conditions can be provided.

Havahart Spray Away Elite II is larger than I thought it would be. The base measures approximately 17" in diameter. The Elite II has been working for us, but in our efforts to keep squirrels from the bird feeder, we have scared some birds away too. We need to keep working on this & will have a solution soon. Our yard is mostly shaded, so finding a full sun site to charge the unit isn't easy.Havahart Spray Away Elite II has some good points & some bad points. Because of its portability & solar battery, it is an improvement over the Havahart Spray Away 2 (5266)...but what would be great is if the Elite II  included some features of the Spray Away 2 (5266).  For example, it would be nice if you had the option to hook a hose up to the Elite II; it would also be great if the Elite II had battery back-up for those with shady yards & for those days when the sun just doesn't want to shine. Also, I would love to be able to read the  indicator lights from our house. We currently have the unit spraying away from the house..the indicator lights are on the same side the unit sprays from. I don't think that is very convenient.Despite the fact that the Elite II could use some improvements, I'm going to tell a couple families I know about it. One family is constantly chasing geese away from their pond; the other family has a heron which visits regularly to eat their goldfish. I think either family would like to give the Elite II orHavahart 5266 Spray Away Motion Activated Sprinkler Animal Repellent 2.0a try.Store inside when the temperature drops below 32 degrees Fahrenheit.2 year guarantee
summary: So far, so good...needs to be charged in full sun

reviewText: We've found this sprinkler Repellent dose a good job of scaring away various sizesof problem critters from tearing up our flower beds and garden.It conveniently doesn't require batteries, nor have to be attached to a water hose.It's suppose to be pre-charged & ready to use straight out of the box, (although ours needed charged first)All that's needed is to screw on the sprinkler head, (plastic wrench is enclosed) & it's ready to adjust & use.The unexpected noise stated in product details is simply the quite sound of the mechanism spraying water.The unit doesn't point at the intruder, it just detects that there is an intruder (up to 35 ft away) & goes off.So it isn't a loud noise that scares the animals away, nor water actually hitting the animal,it simply that the water movement & sounds are unexpected.I feel the booklet lacks clarity of how to get started , and exactly what to expect.I phoned Havahart with some questions, and found that this black model is new ~ mid April 2013.The older version of this product is green. The differences are ~The plastic of the new black model is made to withstand the rays of the sun better.And the sprinkler head is a new and improved design, more mobile, and smoother working.Fully charged batteries are good for approximately 2 basins full of water.Customer service said, once the appropriate settings have been found, and with the right conditionsit's possible the battery would keep itself continually solar charger for the entire summer.This gets to be quite tricky, the right conditions mean, how much sun it does/doesn't get ~the number of times it sprays ~ & how hot the temperature gets, etc.One draw-back I'm not found of ~ the unit can't be taken apart, the battery isn't removable,and the battery isn't supposed to be stored where it gets cooler then 32%.For us that means it has to be stored in our house for the winter since our garage is unheated.The unit is light weight, empty it weighs just under 7 lb. (6 lb 13.4 oz)A couple steps about charging are needed to be done exactly as stated ~ or you may go around & around.1. When charging ~ DO leave unit turned ON & sensitivity set on #1.2. When fully charged ~ TURN unit OFF before adding the 3 1/2 gal of water.3. When full ~ Turn on and WAIT 30 SECONDS before waving your hand in-front to see if it's working.(immediate motion after turning unit on only delays the start up)Conclusion ~ This is quality made product, in material and design,but is a bit tedious to get adjusted ~ and requires no-freeze storage for the winter.The unit has a 2 year warranty.

The Havahart Spray Away Elite II is a neat little device for scaring off critters that you don't want in your yard or garden. It works well but requires sun lite since it runs off of solar power. The unit is fully portable, no hose attachments. There is a tank you fill which holds 3.5 gallons of water. You can choose how sensitive you want the machine to be. I found the highest setting to produce false activation's, such as going off from leaves/butterfly, opposed to a raccoon. If you need to use in a shaded area you get about 5 charges from the machine if its been sitting in the sun charging. We keep ours around a level 8 and find its been the best setting. You can also adjust the spray jet up to 25 feet. The LED shows you a low charge or low water basin, though its not super bright. The spray head also rotates and sprays in different directions so that your pesky critters can't "predict" where the water will be.We seem to fill our's up weekly but that would depend on how many critters you have in your garden/yard. The more you have obviously the more water you will use and need to refill.Instructions were a little rough and confusion but we got through them after reading it a few times and learning the machine. My only complaints are if you want to check the LED lights you must shut the machine off otherwise you will become that pesky critter and get sprayed by the machine. And second, we found birds like to leave droppings on the machine which lands on the solar panel since its on the top of the machine - so its alot of cleaning if that happens.So far though, its been very effective keeping rabbits out of the garden and other varmints. I really like that fact you don't need to connect a hose to it, makes it easy to move and setup in different spots - plus you don't have to worry about hose extensions and such. - You do need the sun though as I mentioned, if you have an all shade spot I can see this becoming an issue.
summary: Humanely Safe, Works Well - Portable but needs Sun Lite Area (Solar)

reviewText: So far it seems to work, but maybe TOO well. Where I have a small garden in my front yard, I've set this at one end to try and deter birds, rodents, and other pests from pillaging my veggies. I've not yet observed it work against any animals, but when switched on it fires up any time I walk anywhere near it in the yard, which bodes well. The problem is it also seems to go off at random, or even in response to airplanes (we're right in the flight path) which doesn't make much sense, even on it's least sensitive setting. The instructions say to increase the sensitivity setting for warmer weather, so maybe it well become less touchy with the heat. I love the basin so you don't have to have a water source connected, but it empties quickly when placed where it will activate often. I also love how it's powered by its own solar panels, and it was very easy to assemble. You'd probably need at least two, though, to protect an area from at least two sides. Overall, pretty neat; I just turn it on when I'm leaving or over night--word to the wise, don't forget it's there and stroll through it's path in the middle of the night, unless you don't mind getting your hip soaked!

This is the hose-free version, with a water reservoir under the smarts and the sprinkler head.The unit came in a nice, simple cardboard box with minimal excess packaging. The sprinkler head is a separate piece for ease of shipping and also for potential replacement later (very important if you have hard water for example). A wrench was included to attach the sprinkler. Instructions were short and simple.The sprayer works as advertized, filled with water it activates at motion and sprays water. Simple enough. How effective it is at keeping animals away remains to be seen. We set it up to protect tender shoots from rabbit damage this Spring. Seems to be working. We can test the spraying and it does activate on occasion, but hard evidence of effectiveness is difficult to come by.If you're within range of a water hose, the hose-connected option probably makes more sense, but this unit can be setup anywhere on your land with relative ease. Price seems high for the task, but the unit is quality.

Havahart's Spray Away Elite II Motion Detector Sprinkler Animal Repellent is a nifty resource for your garden or yard.  While I think this would work wonders for deterring rabbits, deer, and other animals from gardens, I have to admit my real purpose was to keep some neighborhood dogs out of the yard.  It's rather pricey, but with that price comes a tool that is adjustable in many ways, offers a hose-free reservoir, and solar charging.Setup is fairly easy, but you will want to take the time to properly adjust the sprayer for not only the size of animal you are wanting to deter, but also spray pattern and distance.  At first I was worried that it would produce false positives, but it actually did an awesome job at recognition.Power/charge hasn't been an issue thus far.  I've placed my sprinkler in an area that gets plenty of sunlight, but those in partial shade might have some issue.  The water reservoir holds more than enough water.  With mine being in the front yard, the dogs have kept it fairly active and I've had to refill it more often than I thought.  However, I suspect that will likely slow with time.The only gripe I have would likely be the size of the unit.  But honestly, given the fact that it's hose free and solar powered, it's worth the extra size.  Overall, I'm very pleased with the unit and look forward to its continued use.

We filled this up after it was charged and promptly got hosed down and the toddlers freaked out, lol.  MAKE SURE YOU HAVE IT AWAY FROM YOU.  I know that is a stupid thing to overlook, but I thought I'd just remind people out there who also may be under-slept.I love how we don't have to keep the hose on with this sprinkler! The solar works great keeping it charged.It has a good motion sensor, but it does not spray the item it detects, it just hoses down the "hot zone" you set up. This is fine, but just good to know.  It would cost much more if it had that kind of sensor capability.This is so much better than buying fencing or using some kind of chemical deterrent.  Our area is raised garden boxes so it is easy to set the hot zone to keep birds off our tomatoes and veggies.  We have it on a lift to sense the birds easier.  We fill it up every weekend, takes a second and is good for days.It's about fifty bucks more than what I would be willing to pay to replace it if it were stolen or broke.
summary: Safe and humane way to keep gardens critter free!

reviewText: I have severalContech CRO101 Scarecrow Motion Activated Sprinkler, which I have been using for many years.  This is better because I can place it where I cannot run a hose.  It is supposed to be activated by heat, not just motion as the Scarecrow is.  There are still false sprays, but I don't think I am getting quite as many with this.  I still haven't figured out the exact placement and settings, but so far am very happy with this. I was missing a part, but one quick call to the company had a replacement immediately coming by FedEx, so I am very impressed with the customer service. The only things I don't like, and the reduction of one star, are that it is so expensive and I needs a better battery back-up so I am not defenseless on cloudy days.  I am happy to have it as part of my arsenal in keeping the deer from eating too much of my garden.
summary: Works pretty good as part of a deer arsenal

reviewText: The Havahart spray Away Elite II is a stand-alone (i.e., no hose required) device that deters garden pests by spraying them with water.  It contains a reservoir that has to be filled periodically, a motion detector, and a PV solar panel that keeps it charged.  It's easy to assemble and set up; although Havahart claims it comes fully charged, I would count on leaving it in the sun for a few days before using it.I had the previous model of this device and wasn't very happy with it.  My biggest complaint was that it wasn't sensitive enough to detect and deter smaller animals.  Apparently I wasn't the only one, because Havahart quickly took it off the market and replaced it with the Elite II.  I'm not sure what other tweaks they made, but the Elite II is more sensitive, and I've been happier with it. (The sensitivity is adjustable.) The previous model worked reasonably well with deer, while the Elite II also is triggered by squirrels and some birds. Every time?  No, but pretty often.The downsides of being more sensitive are that the unit needs to be recharged and refilled with water more frequently.  It holds about 3-1/2 gallons, which keeps it operating in my yard for about four or five days; obviously your mileage may vary.  Because it must be charged by the sun, you have to find a sunny spot for it, especially if it's going to be triggered more than once in a while.  If it's consistently shady it likely will run down; I had that problem only once, however.Let's face it, you can't expect a droid to perform perfectly, but this device is much better than nothing, and offers the ability place it far from any hose, and needs no batteries.

What it does:The Havahart Spray Away Elite II is designed to scare off critters that come to eat your garden vegetables. It does this by spraying a jet of water to startle the creature. When a creature ventures into the field of view of Spray Aways sensor, it activates and fires a jet of water. The intensity is similar to a garden hose with a nozzle being turned on at about 75% of full blast for about 5 seconds. The water jet sweeps a few degrees and makes a startling noise. Spray Away does not directly target and shoot water at animals (unless it gets lucky). It detects heat and motion at a distance of 30 feet from the front of the unit. It covers a 180 degree angle. It can't detect animals coming from directly behind it. The solar powered battery can fire about 5 times a day. There's no need to hook up a hose like some other similar models. It has 2 led lights which flash when water is low or the charge is low. The LED lights are not bright, but are visible even in bright daylight. Maintenance is rather minimal, only requiring twice a week water fill up (but this depends on how many animals cross its path) and wiping the solar panel and detector surfaces clean. Fit and finish quality are high.Set-up:I found the set up very easy. You fill the tank with 3.5 gallons of water. Choose the sensitivity from a dial and turn the unit on. The sensitivity setting is not well defined in the instructions, but I assume it's based on the size of the animal you are attempting to deter (contact with the company confirms that the settings are based on animal size, 9 being most sensitive for small animals). Strangely, instructions do not tell you exactly what a 'large' or 'small' animal is in terms of measurements. The higher the sensitivity setting the smaller the animal the unit will detect. A very high sensitivity may produce false activations. For example, a tree limb moving in the field of view or a butterfly might cause the unit to spray. Therefore, you may need to lower the sensitivity a bit or move the unit to a different location. I have mine set on 8 out of 9 to deter pesky rabbits. I have not experienced any false alarms.  You can adjust the spray jet to travel about a maximum of 25 feet. The spray head also rotates during squirting so that the jet of water is always firing somewhere different. This keeps the unit from becoming predictable to animals and losing its effectiveness.Conclusion:My only major complaints are the instructions and the indicator lights. The manual says to set the sensitivity values based on "small", "medium" and "large". Large what? I assume animals? How big? Not sure. The indicator lights are positioned on the front of the unit. If you forget to turn off the unit and try to read the LED lights, you will get hit with a jet of cold water. Also, the top of the sprayer is a place where birds like to roost and, of course, poop. The poop lands on the solar panels. Hopefully, on the next re-design of this product, the Havahart engineers will make that roosting spot a little pointy so that birds will avoid sitting there.So far Spray-Away has been very effective. Rabbits devouring spinach and lettuce were our problem last season. I have not seen one rabbit (or any other varmint) in our 25' x 30' garden area since placing the unit on the perimeter. They actually seem to be avoiding the garden. We left some "bait lettuce" in the garden for a few days as a test and so far it is completely uneaten. I have had no problems with inadequate charging of the battery. It always seems ready to work.I think the Spray-Away is worth the extra expense. It's actually fun to use and is a much better alternative to applying chemical deterrents (especially in an edible garden). If you have a huge garden, you will probably need additional Spray Aways and of course, this could be costly. Also, if you expect many animals to be crossing through your garden, you may want to get the version with attached hose, as you don't want to have to fill up the unit with water constantly, but remember that animals will eventually learn to avoid the Spray Away's path and therefore, it should spray less and less.I highly recommend this product if you have a garden munching animal problem and a little extra money to spend.
summary: Very Cool, Effective and Well Built

reviewText: I wanted to use this Havahart Spray Away Elite II Motion Detector Sprinkler Animal Repeller for one reason... to keep free-roaming cats away from my bird feeders and squirrels, while at the same time not frightening off my birds and squirrels!From a behavior perspective, the device has a lot going for it.  It provides a sudden, negative sound, visual, and tactile experience for an animal.  The theory of effective animal harassment encourages multiple, unpredictable negative sensory experiences to provoke fear and reduce the onset of habituation.  So the spray of water (tactile, and certainly unpleasant for cats), and the sight and sound of the water, along with the fact that the spray doesn't occur at regular, pulsed intervals, should help in the effectiveness of this device.  And I like that it isn't connected to a hose, and is solar powered.Unfortunately, I am having difficulty in getting the sensors to work for smaller animals like cats. I want it to be like those automated guns in the movie, Aliens.  I will keep trying.
summary: The theories behind animal behavior say this should work...

reviewText: REVIEW UPDATE: After barely over a month of use, the Havahart Spray Away Elite II has developed a leak. The last time it rained, the housing for the motion sensor filled with water, rendering the unit inoperable.Original review:The Havahart Spray Away Elite II is claimed to be an improvement over the previous version, but the only difference I can tell between the two is this version comes precharged, and is black instead of green. As far as function goes, I like the previous version better! Compared to the model this version replaced, this one sprays for a shorter time duration, does not have as powerful of a spray; this particular unit struggles to change directions and many times hangs in one spot and needs the wire direction bail to be manually shifted.Still, the sudden noise of operation is enough to startle most creatures, save for a few stubborn feral cats. The only potential drawback to using this over a garden area is that if it is tripped in the late evening or early night, is I'm worried that the water sprayed can contribute to undesirable fungal growths on plants that could be harmful.

UPDATE 2014-06-10The unit just doesn't charge or work anymore.  Disappointed with the durability of something at this price.ORIGINAL POST:The design and execution is well done.  The instructions are clear, it is easy to fill this up with water and setup the sprinkler.An improvement over their other motion activated sprinkler, is that this one has an on/off switch.  That is important.The sensor works fine and the LEDs on the front are very clear and obvious.  As in, when you've activated it, the 2 bright red LEDs on the front let you know you are about to be doused.  The sudden sound of the sprinkler is definitely surprising.  The power of the spray is mediocre.  But I think that isn't the deterrent... the sound and getting hit by water is the key.My only concern is that the solar doesn't seem to charge up fast.  I let this sit in the sun for days before turning on.  Then overnight, either I had a lot of wild critters to run the charge down, or the charge was just not very good and it ran out quickly. The next day, the charge was run down and indicating low.  (I am sure it wasn't the critters as the ground isn't that wet and the water is still full).Overall.. nicely designed product, the execution of the solar doesn't seem to be perfect.

This product is made of heavy black plastic and does not look conspicuous on your lawn. It is also only a couple of feet in diameter and about 3' high. You put water in the base and forget about it until something goes in its path, then it suddenly squirts water where it picked up motion. It is so funny to see animals react. It will get you too! If you forget to aim it in another direction. The main drawback is that the moles eat my bulbs from under the earth where the repellent cannot "see" them.

This may be scaring away a few animals but not many. The deer seem to get used to it fairly quickly and some actually seem to enjoy it! I don't hear the sound they refer to and I suspect neither do the animals. The reservoir seems to always be empty and I am wondering if even swooping birds are setting it off. Setting the sensitivity is a very inexact process . All in all I cannot recommend this to anyone with a real varmint problem in their yard because it is an expensive repellent that only repels for a short while. I'm thinking about putting soap and towels out beside it in hot weather so the deer can make the best use of it!
summary: Might scare away a few animals

reviewText: This is my third product from Havahart and I'm very happy with all of them. I have problems with stray cats, dogs, racoons, and possums. Havahart animal repellants take care of all of them, and without chemicals or anything dangerous.The Havahart Spray Away Elite II is very easy to use and really does the trick! The unit weighs 11 pounds empty, so it's easy to carry.  I fill it with a bucket, since it's easier to carry a bucket of water than a full Spray Away unit.  Once it's in place, it works very efficiently.The unit is solar powered, so I never have to worry about dead batteries. I love the eco-friendly aspect of it.We had a lot of fun testing it out! It detected our movement every time and gave us a quick blast of water.  This will be perfect to put in the far corner of our vegetable garden this summer, where a water hose won't reach. We won't have to worry about stray animals messing up the garden.If you have a lot of animals to deter, you'll probably want to use the model that attaches to a water hose so you'll have continuous action. The Spray Away Elite works well with occasional problems, unless you want to fill it up every day.
summary: Very efficient! So easy to use.

reviewText: This is a well-designed, self-contained, animal repellent sprinkler.  No unsightly and inconvenient hose connection to mess with.  No extension cord to connect or batteries to change. The only requirements are to locate it where there will be plenty of direct sun to keep the solar power supply charged, and to maintain a water supply in the 3.5 gallon reservoir.A lesser issue I had was that I initially located mine in the corner of a fenced area . . . I immediately learned that I had no way to access the Spray Away (to add water or adjust sensitivity) without getting sprayed. Easily fixed, as the unit is totally mobile and being all black, it easily blends in pretty much anywhere you place it.  A little imaginative landscaping will also pretty much hide it.  The reservoir/base is about 18" in diameter and it stands less than two feet tall.  That wide reservoir/base by the way, with the weight of water in it, makes the unit inherently stable.  It is not going to move under even the most severe wind conditions. The pedestal above the reservoir supports the sprinkler head and contains the battery and electronics.  The four photovoltaic solar power panels are located horizontally on top of the pedestal at the base of the sprinkler head.  The single infra-red motion sensor is on the side of the pedestal near the top, with the control panel on the opposite side.It does come pre-charged and ready for immediate use. Just screw on the sprinkler head to the top (a wrench is provided), add water to the reservoir, and it's ready for service.  The water comes out strong and with a range (adjustable) of up to 25 feet.  The charged power supply will provide only about a dozen activations before depleting.  I've already seen that the unit is sensitive enough to pick up rabbits and even squirrels that come within range. During sunlit conditions, one assumes it will maintain itself during the day.  During night conditions with active animal traffic, it's conceivable that the power supply would deplete.  I imagine this would become less of a problem as the local animal community becomes "trained" to stay away.  And I can't help but speculate as to whether familiar animals might also figure how to defeat the Spray Away . . . either by learning that it is exhaustible, or learning how to circumvent the coverage area.  No matter - this clever device works and will keep away the balance of unwanted animals and certainly without harming them.I already have taken a preventative maintenance measure of adding a little (less than an ounce) of chorine bleach to the reservoir to help keep the water supply clean and algae free (the black color prevents sunlight and will help in this).  This device should be brought in during freezing weather to prevent damage from internal ice expansion (no garden or flowers to protect in the winter anyway, right?).Speaking more on winter considerations - there may be situations where an owner doesn't want to bring in their unit when temps are below freezing.  There may be year round pests to control (stray cats, dogs, coyotes) or the owner may have a rather permanent installation (such as I have done) where the reservoir is partially buried in the ground. So for sub-freezing temps, I plan to install RV (recreational vehicle) anti-freeze in the reservoir, and run it though the unit before turning it off for the winter. The RV anti-freeze prevents freezing, is relatively inexpensive (much cheaper than automotive engine anti-freeze, which is also very poisonous to animals, people, and plants), and is non-toxic (designed for use in RV water systems including the "clean" water systems). And finally, I'm not sure how well winter sunlight conditions will keep the power supply charged.Havahart's Spray Away Elite II is a well-designed, well-built, and humane animal repellent.  It's not magic and it's not perfect, but it does exactly what it promises to do, within realistic limitations.

This is a great concept; watch for animals eating your plants and squirt them.  The self-contained unit is fairly large and holds plenty of water in the base - 3.5 gallons, or enough for about 35 activations.  It recharges itself from the sun so no batteries are needed.  Thus, it can be placed pretty much anywhere.Setup is easy - just screw in the sprinkler head with the included wrench.  The wrench is designed to slip off when the head is tight enough, but if you really try you can force it tighter.  Don't!  Unless water is leaking, it's tight enough.It senses our free-roaming chickens when they get in the garden, and when the sensitivity is set fairly high it can see us 30 feet away.  It responds with a short burst of water that can go up to 25 feet.  There is an adjustment to make the distance less by deflecting the water from a stream into more of a spray if that's too far.Keep in mind that the manual says that the battery may run low if it activates more than 10 times per day; this is for the occasional raider rather than a constant stream of visitors.  There is a light that turns on if the battery runs low; if it does, keep it on (with sensitivity turned down) and leave it in the sun to recharge.  There is another light if the water runs low; if this activates, refill then turn it off and on again to reset.  The clear plastic cover keeps falling off the on/off switch, but it probably isn't that important anyway.It was rather amusing when our neighbors walked too close (about 20 feet away) and screamed when it shot water at them.  With a little imagination, this could provide hours of fun!  It doesn't hurt that this looks a little like a cigarette disposal.Our first unit didn't turn side to side no matter how we adjusted the clips, so it only sprayed an area directly in front of the unit.  The head is supposed to go left and right through a range you can set with the attached clips, and can even be set to go all the way to either side.  Despite the problem, it still chased away the chickens until they figured out it didn't squirt the sides of the garden (because it didn't turn) and started eating everything there.We called Havahart (the help number is on a paper in the box) and a new unit arrived in about 2 weeks.  The new one works great; it turns out there was a problem with the original sprinkler head.  The tiny springs in the head don't look that durable; if we have any more issues I'll update the review.  And unfortunately, they don't sell replacement sprinkler heads at this time.  But for now, it's working fine at keeping rabbits and chickens out of our small garden.
summary: Replacement works great; fun for startling neighbors

reviewText: The Havahart motion detector sprinkler does the same job as theHavahart 5265 Spray Away Motion Detector Sprinkler Animal Repellentbut with several distinct advantages. It gives you more coverage, needs no batteries, and needs no hose. If you can afford to tie up a garden hose full time, or want to disconnect it and reconnect it when you have other uses, you should consider the other model.Aside from not needing a garden hose draped across your yard, and possibly across a walkway or flower bed, you have a great deal more control over where you can put this. As long as it's not blocked from sunlight, it can be used where needed.For example, I have a decorative fish pond where I used to have an egret problem. It's pointless having a decorative and landscaped backyard only to drape a hose across it, especially if the area where you place this is meant to keep it out of sight. This unit is huge with a large base, about 16 inches in diameter. The base itself can be buried if you wand something less obtrusive, but you'd still have to keep the filler hole accessible.Assembly merely requires attaching the sprinkler head with the included plastic wrench until the wrench slips off. There's no danger of over tightening it. There's a single knob to set sensitivity to a number based on distance and whether you want small, medium or large. There's a table that shows you the appropriate settings. If it's not clear what's meant by small, medium or large, the instructions don't say, but it seems that they meant it to refer to animal size.  The sprinkler head itself can be adjusted easily to set a particular range both in terms of distance and size of arc.One disadvantage of this unit compared to one with a hose is that it needs water to be added periodically. But it holds 3.5 gallons. That's a lot of water for occasional activation. If you have a more extreme problem, be prepared to fill it often.The unit has a sensor with two red lights above it. One will tell you when the battery is low and the other will tell you when water is low. They will both flash when movement is sensed, so you can walk near the edge of the desired range and see when you get close enough to activate it. That may not seem necessary, because it should be obvious enough that water is being sprayed at you. but it will illuminate for three seconds when it senses you. That could be an advantage until you get your spray pattern to match your desired distance. But considering that sensitivity is based on the size of the animal, setting it for yourself won't do much to assure that you have it set as desired. I merely used the chart, waved my hand in front of it to assure that the spray was the correct distance, and left it at that.A potential problem with having the lights and sensor on the same side is that you need to be on the side with the sensor to see them. If you have the unit facing away from the house, that won't happen. If you have the unit facing toward you, you'll see the lights but may not be able to get close. And since there's no hose, and therefore no way to turn off the water remotely, you will want to approach this from behind. If that's not practical because of the layout of the area, you'll need to trigger a burst and then use the eight second idle period to dash behind it, or to get to the switch. At startup there's a 30 second calibration period, and you are supposed to wait 30 seconds before going in front of the sensor. I'm not sure what happens if you need that 30 seconds to get out of range, so ideally you will be able to stay out of sensor range and be able to walk away on a path that's outside the range of the arc.I can't consider this a five star product because of the trade offs. You gain a lot compared to a unit with a hose, but you might have to fill it every couple of weeks or more, especially until stray or loose animals learn to avoid the area. I can't blame the manufacturer for the trade offs, since they offer an alternative if that's what you need. And the limitations are unavoidable for this type of product.  If I were rating it on quality alone, I've yet to find faults.

Used it in a hot tub and it seems to have done a decent job cleaning it. Very little was needed so the price seems to be quite reasonable (definitely better than having to call someone for a professional cleaning!). No negative film was observed.
summary: does what it is supposed to do - clean and break down gunk

reviewText: My spa is in-ground and adjacent to my swimming pool.  Both are jointly cleaned and connected to a pump system that automatically adds chemicals.  However I attempted to isolate the spa and added the required measure of Orb-3.  It is my understanding that Orb-3 is designed to work with the pool/spa chemicals to keep the spa clean and not to supplant them. So I will tentatively endorse Orb-3 and may amend my review after a few months of use.

reviewText: There was no chemical odor.  I noticed there was less scum--it was reduced not eliminated.  Supposedly it doesn't need time the circulate before using the hot tub but I was nervous about getting in the water too soon so we waited. No one had any allergic reactions.  Appears to work quite well.

This additive appears to work for a small above ground pool (an Endless Pool). I say appears because we generally keep the pool clean by rising off before getting in and covering it after use even though it is in an enclosed area.Recently, it seemed to be a little cloudy. I checked the chemical levels and everything looked OK, so I decided to leave it alone. As a pond owner, I know that it is better to make gradual changes and just leave well enough alone. When I saw this product being offered, I thought it sounded interesting and might help.I have been using this a few weeks and noticed the water is looking crystal clear again. There was a small amount of detritus that appeared to be released by the Orb-3 spa enzymes, so I was pleased that the pool is as clean as I had hoped and that the spa enzymes appear to work. I like the 2 ounce marks on the label. This makes it very simple to dose the correct amount.I like this product and was looking to buy more. While looking around, I noticed the Orb-3 Pool Enzymes. This looks like a similar product but at one quarter the dosage (one ounce per 2000 gallons). Since I am using this for a pool at lower temperatures (80-86F), I bought that version.

We keep the hot tub clean and change the filter regularly.  However, there is an occasional scum ring issue that has baffled me.  I know it was from skin products and shampoo residue, etc.  But getting rid of it has not always been easy without scrubbing and completely changing the water and filter.  We tried this, in addition to our regular chemicals, and voila!  Within a few hours the water was crystal clear, smelled fresh and the slight scum ring that had kept me from wanting to use the tub was gone.  Water tests showed everything was good to go, so we went in.We will definitely use this in conjunction with the regular chemicals.

I followed the instructions and placed two ounces in my small hot tub.  I could see the grime separate from the enzymes right away, like oil and water.  And yes, after a few hours the water did look clearer.  This stuff does not smell and is safe for our dogs should they insist on drinking the water.  While grime is not really a problem for us as we try to keep the water clear of body lotions and oils, what little grime there was came off easier than before.  This is a well-priced product that works very well.

I used this in my outdoor hot tub a few hours ago, and the water now looks crystal clear. I was able to use the tub soon after adding this. It had no odor and only created a little foam. A little bit of this formula goes a long way. I am very happy with it.

I manage a commercial apartment property, so I was delighted at the chance to try this product.  Since I am not technical on the hot tub front, I had my maintenance manager use it.  He was very impressed with the product, and the hot tub seems to be running as good as ever.  The clarity is nice, and I like that this is a safe, enzyme formula.  So far we haven't had any complaints about smell, skin irritation, or any other adverse effects.We use this with a salt cell hot tub which runs at 104 F year round.  It is approved for use for residential, multi family property in Oregon, and probably in other states.  As always, make sure to consistently check your pH and other levels and adjust if necessary.  And a little of this goes a long way as an additive.

reviewText: We use our tub occasionally.. perhaps once a month now that we have a busy young family.  Our 2002 CalSPA Atlantis has been through the Ohio outdoor challenges,  frozen over due to failed pumps and electricity, etc...  It's been through the war of environment vs tub.  One thing we don't get to do during the winter season is to change out the water as often.  Even with regular chlorine shock, the tub can get s ring of film and feel less fresh.Using Orb-3 initially had a bit of extra debris.. someone called it cheese...  that apparently is the solution deep cleaning your pipes and unseen areas...  after a full water change and regular use, the water is clearer and we feel that its fresher than just water changes, wipe downs, and chlorine... reviewText: The things that happen as a result of lotions on people's skin when using pools or hot tubs are a major problem. It seems like this type of problem cannot be managed without great difficulty. I like this natural way to remedy it by using natural enzymes. One must remember to not put other chemicals in at the same time, or the enzymes will likely get killed before they do good.

We replaced our hot tub this summer. I am familiar with the maintenance aspects of owning a hot tub and keeping it not only safe but clean. I'm pretty good about emptying the tub and cleaning at regular intervals as well as adding the appropriate chemicals. This product is designed to work with the chemicals to keep the spa clean and is not meant to replace them. We came back to our place in Michigan after a two week absence. The water in the tub was a little murky. I followed the instructions on this product and after 7 or 8 hours checked the tub. The water was crystal clear and I hopped right in and kicked back.Since this is an enzyme powered product it worked efficiently. I would definitely buy this product and make it part of my regular maintenance package. I love our hot tub, but am kind of nuts about the clean thing. The visual results made me feel good that this product does a good job of breaking down residue in the water.

The weather has become chillier so it's time to heat up the spa.  Generally there are no problems when only my family uses the spa but when the relatives and friends drop by, additional chemicals are needed to minimize contaminants and waterline scum buildup from body oils, cosmetics, lotions, sunblocks, and other organic substances.  This Orb-3 Solutions Spa Enzymes was exactly what we needed.Likes:>Safety sealed 1 pint (16 oz.) bottle is enough for 8000 gallons of spa water at 1 oz./500gal. per week.>The spa was first checked for proper pH and chlorine levels prior to adding about 1 oz. of this Spa Enzyme.>There was a tiny waterline scum ring that easily dissolved as I circulated the water through the spa jets.>There was less chemical smell and foam buildup as the folks piled into the spa.>Even our salt chlorinated spa water feels a bit more softer/smoother.Dislike:Like all pool chemicals, this Spa Enzyme is priced high at $11.90/16 oz. or about $0.74 per oz.Overall:A good complement to routine spa chemical sanitizing and maintenance especially during high bather usage.

reviewText: After using the product for several weeks I can't say it's miraculous or anything.  Our spa looks clean when we open it, but after the jets run it looks murky again.  I think this product definitely could be working, but I'm going to empty the tub and start over (it needs it anyway).  My perception is that the standard water clarifier we've been using works better, but I hate to base a review of a product on something so subjective.  I honestly think you'd need some scientific testing to be able to review a product like this accurately.  So it definitely could work, but it's not a miracle product.

I've had my hot tub for years and getting the right chemical balance and clean, clear, nice-smelling water can often be a puzzle. The key is having the right combination of products and using them consistently. I think it's also important to change the water and filter regularly, and also to try to limit the amount of contamination the water gets from users who wear lotion, oils, perfumes, bug repellants or whatever into the spa -- along with a suit that may have been washed using soap.That said, I've found this liquid enzyme product to be very effective in controlling organic deposits and in making the water odor free and clear. I add about 15-20 mL (a little over half an ounce) of the liquid in my hot tub along with my brominating tablets andRenew 2.2 lb Leisure Time Spaeach week. I sometimes add a little extra of the spa enzymes after I've had a large party of guests. I maintain the water temperatre at around 100-104F as the product is designed to use in warmer water. I keep my spa open and use it all year long and it seems to make my other sanitizing agents work more efficiently to maintain a good chemical balance. I also like that you can use the spa immediately and that you don't have to circulate the water for long periods after adding in order for it to work. It does not cause skin irritation or dryness. I've noticed less scum along the walls of the tub as well! I'm all about less maintenance and am quite pleased to recommend this item.
summary: Great adjunct to sanitizer system for hot tub!

reviewText: I like the idea to conserve water, and this is made to specifically extend the use of your hot tub water by clearing it up.  I used it on what I thought was a clean tub, but it showed me different.It says it can break up gunk in the filter pump and it sure did.I let it run for 30 minutes and got clear water and a nasty gunk rim, that I removed with paper. I now use this once a month in addition to my regular cleaning to keep away the gunk and keep the spa ring free.
summary: Enzymes to extend life of hot tub water.

reviewerName: Gertrude, the Innocent "Live well, laugh loud...
reviewText: The past ten days or so, some family members have been doing heavy moving work and then jumping into the hot tub after to soothe sore muscles. My favorite offender has been getting in the shower AFTER hot tubbing. reviewText: This stuff works great in addition to the regular sanitizers.  I noticed the first time it seemed to release a film into the water, which I was surprised about because I use a line purging solution between fills, but the film went away after a few hours and hasn't come back with regular maintenance doses. This can actually help clear away some stains and residues that harsh chemicals won't be able to fully address, so anyone seeking a top notch cleaning solution would want to consider using this enzyme formula.

reviewText: As far as spa enzymes go - Orb-3 is a great product that I'd recommend. My friend's hot tub appears really clean despite being used quite frequently. He still uses traditional chemical sanitizing. However when he first used this Orb 3 spa enzyme it foamed up excessively - it found gunk in his pipes apparently. Within a few days the foam cleared. The water felt clean and there was no typical spa chemical odor (his hot tub is outside.) All in all we would both recommend the Orb 3, especially for cleaning out the pipes from gunk built up over time. The first time Orb 3 is used I would definitely recommend using it a few days then dump the water and start over - this will help to clean everything out of the pipes and internal sections then start with a truly clean experience.Another perspective: A few years back we upgraded our hot tub to become mostly chemical free by adding an ozonator and a Nature2 mineral sanitizer in the filter. Now we just use a potassium based shock as needed, usually once a week. Since my hot tub is virtually chemical free and since we shower VERY thoroughly just prior to using the hot tub and do not use lotions or conditioners on our skin, our hot tub is free of requiring enzymes such as this However, if we did not take such care to keep our hot tub clean of these oily products and needed a good quality natural enzyme I would certainly consider using the Orb-3 Spa Enzymes.

reviewText: If you are like me, you sometimes question what a product really is. This one claims to contain enzymes that break down organic matter in your pool, which is certainly a good thing. So I'm envisioning this stuff as digesting the oils, detergents, dirt, pollen, and various substances shed by the human body. This can keep your pool cleaner and help your filter do it's job.This product is biodegradable but that does not mean it has no risks at all. The product safety sheet (MSDS) says: "Avoid contact with eyes. Mild skin irritation." If ingested, it may cause "irritation to the mouth and throat. May cause nausea."  The directions on the bottle say to dilute it in a bucket of water before use. As long as you follow the formula on the bottle, this product is quite safe, as far as I can tell. I would not dump it in your fish pond though!At the time this arrived, our pool was in good shape. I diluted some and cleaned some inflatable pool accessories and it worked well.I read that many people add enzymes to the water before covering the pool in the fall and this helps slow down algae growth. You can also add it in early spring for that purpose.One more thing: the manufacturer recommends storing this out of direct sunlight in a cool dry area, so putting it in your deck box or shed during hot weather is not a good idea.

reviewText: We recently purchased a spa around 3 months ago. We thought this would be a great product to try being new to the hot tub / spa world as we learn our chemical balance needed for the spa. Of course we add chlorine as needed, but the PH certainly controls the rest and no need for this product at all.It recommends it for pool use too.... though I never saw a pool have "foam" in it before? Perhaps checking your water, seeing if the PH etc are off and using proper chemicals to maintain it is all you need then starting to add in an "additive".

reviewText: Works as stated.....Works as stated. Price is good. Can be used in a pool, whirlpool, pond. Can be used on any pool surface...vinyl or concrete. reviewText: I used this in my little pond and it does take care of foam right away.  I didn't notice any smells as some have said in their reviews.  There are no stinky smells from the bottle itself, therefore if others have noticed odors, I am guessing it is something already in their water that is actually producing the smell.  I especially like that it is People, Pet and Plant friendly.  Safety first!

Years ago (decades, actually), there were times I needed something to control the foam in my spa.  This was also the time that people used a mini-chemistry set to check for chlorine or bromine levels, pH, and total alkalinity.My techniques have evolved.  I've learned that water "feel", smell, and clarity are all the indicators I need to make adjustments.  And I haven't had a foam issue for, literally, 15 years.  But I recognize that if others use my spa, or if something gets spilled, or whatever, "da foam" can return.  So an antifoam product is good to have, just to keep on hand.For this test, I mixed dish detergent with water in a clear, tall glass, and got a good head of foam.  I added 3 drops of Orb-3 T422-000-1PT Pool and Spa Antifoam, and... nothing really happened.  This makes sense, because the agent weakens the bubbles, causing them to collapse, but the agent doesn't defy gravity and travel up the glass.  So my next test was to mix dish detergent with 3 drops of antifoamer, then add water.  What a difference!  First, overall, instead of a glass 3/4 full of foam, there was about an inch of foam.  The water was very opaque, and full of tiny, tiny bubbles that all disappeared in about 30 seconds, leaving behind clear water.  Those tiny bubbles reminded me of the foam in a pint of Guinness, which is not a bad drink when you are in the spa!So this product works against foam.  Remember, however, that foam is an indicator of something out of wack.  The best use of your antifoamer is never having to use it.  And if you do use it, and afterwards there are evil vapors and scum left behind, remember that an antifoamer doesn't remove what you put into the spa, it just breaks down the bubbles.  Consider the source of the organic substances that contribute to foam!
summary: When your spa is out of control

reviewText: Okay, so I followed all of the instructions (prepped the soil, planted the pods, watered them every day), planted half of the seed pods, and after three weeks...nothing.  And I mean nothing.  No signs of life whatsoever.  The pods don't look any different than when I planted them.  Based on the stated germination period, I thought that I'd see something by now.So, why in the world would I give them three stars?  Honestly, because they actually got me _excited_ about gardening - and I'm not a gardener at all.  Just the idea of growing my own tomatoes, lettuce, and peas got me jazzed up.  They showed up one work day, and I was out back the very next morning getting everything all ready and getting them planted.  I've been out there every morning to water them.  Heck, I've paid this much money for a movie that I enjoyed for a couple of hours, and these things kept me entertained for longer than that.  Plus, they are remarkably easy to plant.  I'm not going to say that they are economical compared to seeds if you plant a lot - they aren't.  However, if you're like me and either (a) would only use a small number of seeds per variety anyway, or (b) at least sometimes gravitate to convenience (I use K-Cups for coffee, which is similar to using these for gardening), you might just like these a lot.Plus, while it is a disappointment to have none of them grow, my experience seems to be in the minority based on the other reviews here.  I'm assuming that either I did something wrong (always possible) or I got a bad batch (or perhaps they got too hot during shipping to my house in Tucson).  Had I purchased these instead of getting them as part of the Vine program, I'm sure that Amazon would refund my money or ship me another package.  Plus, Miracle-Gro has a satisfaction guarantee.  So, if yours don't grow, you can take them up on it.So, for you experienced gardeners, these probably don't make a lot of sense.  If you want to give gardening a try, or if you know someone that doesn't garden and want a gift idea, then these are kind of cool and really easy.(Note:  I planted these in late July in Tucson, which isn't the recommended timing.  As an explanation, I am required to write a review within 30 days of receipt of the product, so I couldn't wait until next spring.  That said, this is the wetter part of our summer season, and I planted the pods where they'd get sun and shade throughout the day, so they shouldn't have gotten too hot.)

these individually-wrapped pods can be inserted into the soil and planted in your backyard, to bear herbs and vegetables. One pack would be enough for the whole summer season. I am still eating the ones I planted about 1.5 months ago.This a bit pricier than buying only the seeds but it is more beneficial if you don't know what you are doing. This kit is a great idea.  The only thing that I would change is I would buy it sooner.  You get large pods with soil, seed and feed in them and just stick the whole thing into your garden.  I'm still waiting for my plants to pop up, but love whole speil!

Let's start with the good - miracle grow is one of my favorite products, and it does miracles on plants.I love having a selection to choose from, already planted.I appreciate the idea of taking these out and just putting them in the ground.It is a very cute idea, and these pods aren't small, they allow for plenty of growing space.So what is the bad?The price is very high for what you get. You can buy a bag of miracle grow soil, peat pots, and seeds for a lot less. In fact, you can usually buy early plants in four-packs for less.You are stuck with their selection. While it is a nice selection, I am partial to certain varieties and miss having my own varieties.The shape means they have to be started outdoors. Our weather is uncertain enough that I start everything except potatoes and onions indoors. This also protects them at their youngest from the "critters" in the yard who love to eat tender new shoots.If you are a beginning gardener, these might be very nice, but they are an extravagance that you really don't have to have to start your own garden.

When I was offered this, I thought, how cool - all the veggies a family of two will need in a neat little kit.  And yes, if you order early enough, that thought was correct.  By the time I received this (in late May), it was way to late to plant the lettuces and peas (too hot and humid in Arkansas), so those will have to wait until fall.I do like the variety of herbs and veggies tho - unfortunately many of the veggies aren't labeled with their variety name, (especially the tomatoes, so you really don't know what you're getting).We prepared a four by four foot raised garden bed for the remaining veggies (minus the peas & lettuces) and the pots are super easy to plant in prepared soil.  You will need to take care watering in the early days to insure the seed and soil mixture in the pod isn't washed away.  The herbs we planted in containers.My best advice if you are going to purchase this kit is to follow all instructions (what few there are) to the letter.  Space the pods out in your garden space as indicated on the labels.  You should see proof of germination in all the pods within a week - or at least I did.Bottom line, this may be a good kit for the beginner gardener or to get children interesting in growing their own food.  Because each pod includes Miracle Grow fertilizer, these are not organic, so you might want to keep that in mind if that bothers you.For myself - I'll continue to start my own seed indoors and transplant when the weather is right.
