Lettuce and peas will be planted at the right time outdoors.  Even if I have to purchase started plants from the nursery, for tomatoes and cucumbers, at least I'll know exactly what variety I'm getting.

Designed especially for those who have a brown thumb, these planter/seed pods are a heaven sent gift!  They are simple to use, just peel the top, plant, and water.  The directions are right on the pod, if you decide not to read the package directions.  I got 100% sprouted plants within 7 days of planting.  Totally cool, I'd say!With these pods, there is no excuse NOT to grow your own food, I planted most of these in containers and they are flourishing!

I thought this was such a neat idea at first glance - a ready-made herb and salad garden!  We live in a climate that gets below freezing for a few months every winter and it normally takes until late spring for anything to really get up to speed.  I had visions of planting these cute little pots in a sunny window and transplanting them outside when the weather was right.All in all, it's a neat kit, with fertilizer, seeds and a peat pot for each.  After removing the kit, you simply peel the label off the top, pick a nice spot and water.  Of the 18 seed pods, I had good results with 15 of them. Not bad odds really, and the ones that did sprout are doing pretty well right now.  It's a whole lot of packaging for 18 tiny pods though.  We've done starts before with peat pots from the garden store and had just as much luck with those.  I think if you used a soil with fertilizer, it might be better to start them that way at less than half and probably more like a quarter the price of this kit.  This saves getting your hands dirty digging in the soil bag, which really is most of the fun to me.All in all, it's a neat idea.  Peel a label, pop it in the ground, water and wait.  I think it'd make a great gift or a good starter for someone just dipping their toes into gardening.  If you're looking for an economical way to start a garden, however, I'd go with peat pots and a bag of soil from a local store.

It is difficult to accurately review this product as it was just received a few days ago.  The climate and temperatures in my area would not be conducive to planting the cool weather vegetables, particularly salad greens.Starting some of the other varieties of tomatoes could possibly yield a small harvest in early October, based upon harvest schedule.  However, based upon my own past experience, this is not likely.The herbs, dill, basil and cilantro would have a better chance of 'taking off' as they say in the garden world.The concept of the pods is a fun option, and could be a wonderful learning experience with a youngster.Most home gardeners, however, are looking to a plant system that would yield more than one plant of any variety (as seeds in these pods are to be thinned to the one strongest per plant).It would be beneficial if planting sticks identifying each pod were incorporated with this set.Cost wise...an expensive option, for a serious gardener.
summary: Should order for planting beginning after first frost...not in heat of mid summer..

reviewText: This product would rate 5 stars on cuteness alone!  since we are nearly past time to order and plant, I wanted to do this review in real time.June 1st, 2013I purchased 2 raised cedar beds (locally, under $50 each) and filled them with Miracle-Gro Potting soil. I added a center container to each bed to give the beds some height interest.  I planned out my garden by looking at the space requirements for each seed pod and using my basic knowledge of mature plant height.  The estimated mature height is one bit of information Miracle- Gro should add to their literature as many first time growers might not realize certain plants may block sunlight.  My spaces to work with were two 4x4's which it just about right, albeit a little crowded.  The area I chose has full sun 10/11am thru 2/4pm.  My main pest concerns are slugs and ants.June 2nd, 2013Planting day!  The basil was planted in the two containers, however with larger containers you might be able to double up with the cilantro or dill.  The cucumber, which needs 48", I planted to one side of the raised bed.  My thought is to train the plant to grow the length of the rest of the raised bed.  Since both tomatoes take up large space, I put these in with the cucumber.  Staking should be simple because I don't have to worry about the small veggies.I put the remaining seed pods in my second bed, arranged by spacing size and estimated height and trailing size.  Staking will be more difficult if it becomes necessary.Hint: before you rip the top off your seed pods, lay them all out in the beds and rework your spacing if needed. When finalized, take a picture and make a detailed map of what plant is where.  Mark north on your map....but then, I'm a map person....the point is know what you planted where.  I ripped the tops carefully as some seeds were visible, planted the pods, and watered.Updates to come....stay tuned.  Sprouts should be up in 5 - 10 days!June 7th, 2013Torrential rain, but I saw a few 5mm sprouts!  The cucumber and one of the lettuces were first out of the gate!June 19th, 2013I have never had such a rainy June!  All the plants are up; the last one to break thru was the pepper plant.  Some are still very small, like the dill, lettuces, and the basil.  Hopefully a few days of dryness and sunshine will promote rapid growth.I culled the plants as recommended, when they reached 2".  Nearly every seed sprouted.  I did not edit the cucumber or the sweet pea down to a single plant as I have room for both to grow.  I will see whether or not that was a foolish choose later in the growing season.

As a military member, I'm not too big on gardening because we move so often we can't fully enjoy the growing process.  However, as I'm in a good location for about a year, I figured I'd give it a shot.These seed pods are a dream come true for simple gardening.  It's basically the Keurig of gardening.  Take out the pod, stick it in, water, fertilize, and watch it grow!It's simple, effective, and easy to use.

This is a great kit for kids or novice gardeners. It contains a variety of vegetables and herb seed pods and a sample of Miracle-Gro Shake N Feed.  There is a cute little instruction guide that is affixed with a paper measure. It contains the basic information abut the individual pods, including spacing,  whether to plant in ground or containers, whether it should be started indoors, estimated germination and harvest times. There is a recipe for a vinaigrette. I found accessing their website to be a helpful supplement. They have a video on the actual planting as well as additional information including photos of how each plant should appear at different stages of growth. There are specifics for the individual plants and additional recipes.This kit is not going to transform a beginner into a master gardener. The instructions are sparse when it comes to tilling and outdoor ground preparation. Coverage on pests and diseases is minimal at best. The experienced will not need the hand holding and will no doubt be able to select, plant and harvest more economically and efficiently. But it is a fun project for kids and a confidence builder for beginners who long to literally get their hands dirty. Recommended

My initial reaction was that this is a wonderful concept, and it is.  Everything you need for a vegetable/herb garden in one place.  Just peel back the seal on the pod and pop it into a pot.  Easy.  There is a nice variety of pods--romaine, lettuce, dill, cilantro, basil, tomato, bean, spinach, cucumber, etc. It is very well-packaged.  In fact, the packaging seems to have received more attention than the actual product.A close look indicates that each pod will have at least two seeds?  Really? That means that I will, most likely, harvest nothing from most of these pods.  Having gardened from seeds in the past, I know that not all seeds will grow to maturity.Additionally, most people who are interested in seed pods have limited space and/or time.  This brings me to the realization that those people do not have space for 18 pods nor do they have the time to cultivate them. You must actually plant the pods.  If you wanted to start them in a flat container before planting, you won't be able to as they are not flat-bottomed.I will update my review once I see what does and what does not sprout or grow to maturity.  It will be annoying to have gathered enough pots to plant these 18 pods if there is not a good success rate.UPDATE: The cherry tomato pod produced two plants and is growing nicely. Nothing from the spinach.  One dill pod is growing and one produced nothing.  The basil did not grow well--what I planted on my own from seed is flourishing but the pods were not successful.  The cucumber produced one plant.  The bean (one of the easiest plants to grow) did not produce anything.  The lettuce pods did very well.  Cilantro produced one plant that is doing "OK".  Not much was actually harvested from these plants. Seeing results, I think that my initial rating of 3 stars is appropriate, if not, the rating would be a bit lower.

So far, I've had mixed results with this pack. All the plants were extremely easy to plant, and having everything in one little pack that I can just stick in the ground was awesome. I have an existing garden that's doing very well, and used these seeds to round out my variety of plants. But, as I said, I'm having mixed results.By far the most successful of all the plants is the cucumber, followed by both the globe and cherry tomato plants. The cilantro is doing fantastic, and the rest of the herbs are also doing reasonably well. Everything else in the pack seems to not have taken, or is taking very long to grow, despite the fact that they're all in the same garden as the plants that are doing well, with the same soil and the same amount of water. I'm still hoping that the other plants will show themselves in time. I may update this review if anything much changes.

Some of the other reviews are down on the lack of options and small number of seeds available in this set but I respectfully believe that they are missing the point. This is a starter kit for those who want to try to grow their own salad garden. I really like the convenience of the individual pods and how they are ready to plant. I've used Miracle-Gro on plants and in my garden and know for certain that it works very well to boost production and health of plants. So for what this kit says it is I believe this is a good idea. Anyone, even those who live in apartments can grow this stuff in raised or hanging beds on a balcony or in the yard. These will grow and will (hopefully) whet appetites for more gardening in the users.I'm at four stars because of the price. For 18 pods the price is over a dollar a pod and that's too much. The local hardware and garden stores in your area will have similar, but much lower cost, options - even fully sprouted plants - for sale. I like the Miracle-Gro built in, but you could just buy some Miracle-Gro and add it to your garden. Instructions are also lacking with the set. Like others have mentioned there are no instructions for local areas and climates. So when does someone plant these where they live? Bing it because the box wont tell you. A couple minor complaints. Overall the kit is great and I'm very much looking forward to my salad!

Miracle-Gro's Salad and Herb Garden Kit takes a quantum leap in making gardening easy.  The concept which is both brilliant in its execution and simplicity itself, though, I have to admit, a bit pricey for the wallet.  In these Miracle-Gro kits, the seed is put in a biodegradable peat pot with growing mix and slow-release fertilizer.  You remove the label on top of each conical pot, and insert it into the soil  The peat pot is an ideal environment for the seedling to start growing and develop.  As the pot decays, the plants root can burrow out into the soil and continue to grow.  Because of the conical shape of the pot, it is very easy to push into the soil.This particular kit includes vegetables: cherry tomato,  beefsteak tomato, cucumber, bush bean, romaine, loose leaf, and butterhead lettuce, cucumber, snap pea, spinach, sweet pepper and herbs: basil, cilantro, dill.  Hence, the salad name.In addition to the seeded pots, there is a 1 oz sample of Miracel-Gro garden fertilizer, a growing guide (which includes spacing directions), and to help you space the pots in the garden, a paper 12 inch ruler.All these combine to make the easiest garden planting I have done, ever.
summary: Planting a Garden Was Never So Easy

reviewText: This review is for the "Miracle-Gro 170025 Groables Salad and Herb Garden Kit, 18 Seed Pods".The set comes in a nice small box, 14" x 8" x 2.5", wrapped in aluminum.  In addition to the pods, my set included a free sample of Shake n' Feed (1 oz) for Tomato, Fruits, and Vegetables.  Each pod has a label on top of it that provides various information: days to germination/harvest, how to plant, and tips.  There is a separate printed single sheet that contains all the labels as well for quick reference.  Each pod is 2.5" tall and 2.5" wide at the top.  The pods are made of peat, and you have to be careful when removing the labels, or else you will rip the pod.  The plant food and soil are already included in the pod and the seed at the correct depth, so it should be fairly easy to plant, grow, and tend this garden.I planted four of the pods as instructed, and sadly, none of them grew.  I kept the pod moist and in a sunny area, but it didn't grow. I also gave two pods to my brother who lives an hour away and neither of his two pods grew neither.  I did notice some of the plant food (yellow pellets) came up to the top of the pod. So now I will try the remaining set and update as necessary.
summary: Some of the pods didn't grow for me.  Neat kit.

reviewText: I think this is an excellent idea as gift or starter garden for a child. Yes you can certainly buy seeds etc. but if you want a complete starter kit, this is a nice concept.The kit includes 18 "cardboard" type pods which contain the seeds and growing medium. You simply pick a spot in a garden, pot or planter, push the pod into the soil until the rim touches the soil, and then treat it like any other seedling.I used some deck planters to start these. While it is well beyond the start of growing season here in New Jersey (I planted these on 7/28), I have done this before with some vegetables/herbs that can be harvested in a couple of months. So I decided this would be a good comparison test. For my "from seed" plants I generally use a soil thermometer, and as the summer winds down, will remove some plants from the ground and shelter them (sun in the day in a pot, then the garage at night, etc.). In the past I have done this with tomato, cucumber, peppers, etc.My 11 year old daughter Kyleigh and I added several inches of garden (not top or potting) soil to the planters and she planted 4 to 5 pods in each planter. As the plants grow we will repot/replant them.In the box you get 18 Seed Pods, which at this time are (alphabetically):* 2 Basil* 1 Bush Bean* 2 Butterhead Lettuce* 1 Cherry Tomato* 2 Cilantro* 1 Cucumber* 2 Dill* 1 Globe Tomato* 2 Loose-Leaf Lettuce* 1 Romaine Lettuce* 1 Smooth-Leaf Spinach* 1 Snap Pea* 1 Sweet PepperYou also get a small packet of powdered Miracle-Grow fertilizer mixture and a little user guide.I did get almost immediate germination. After just 2 days several plants were sprouting. Now they were two hot days and cool nights, so I am sure that helped the seed crack quickly. But the action time was fantastic, especially since with a child you want them to see some results so they stay interested.We continue to monitor the "garden" and it is doing well, a couple of other seeds have broken through. I will update this review as the plants mature. For now I think this is a really cute idea, and while you can buy seed and have more variety, and save some money, if you do it the old-fashioned way, this is a nice, neat introduction to vegetable gardening.NOTE: like any other seed, these have expiration dates. Also like any other seed, you would generally plan to plant based on your last Spring frost, etc. not in the summer in the Northeast! The expiration date on these were late August  which would have been fine for a Spring planting this year, but obviously you would not buy this now for next Spring.

It's hot here in New Orleans. Still, I planted the herbs and have basil, cilantro and dill. The pods are simple to use, peel off the top and plant. I really just don't see the point or the expense of this item. I can buy a bunch of seed packets, a bag of miracle grow, and even those little plant pods and still be money ahead.This is a pretty standard mix of easy to get seeds, basil, cilantro, lettuce, cherry tomatoes, peas. There is nothing wrong with this garden kit, and the seed pods I planted are growing, but I'd rather just buy the seeds or starter plants, this in between product is unnecessary to my mind.
summary: works but why not buy a packet of seeds

reviewText: I actually really like this kit. It gives you a range of different things to grow, it packs them up for you in advance in a convenient way, and it makes it exceptionally simple to get them into the ground, even going so far as to have a little paper ruler you can use to figure out your spacing.The plants will obviously perform differently depending on where the gardener lives, but most beginners are otherwise probably just going to pick out a bunch of seeds that look interesting and see what happens anyway. This is a good way to get a fair variety of things to try and see what happens without having massive numbers of seeds left over, and then people can refine from there in future years.I can also see this being really nice to use with kids, since it keeps the fuss and mess to a bare minimum and sets you up for a pretty decent probability of success on at least some of the plants.I don't really see this as being useful for experienced gardeners, but I think that's okay. Beginners need products too, especially if they're going to have something to give them a good starting point to become experienced.

I thought this set would be a fun homeschooling experiment with my boys. The only negative is the fact that you're somewhat sacrificing the benefit of actually planting "seeds" as opposed to planting a pod of seeds. It still seems like a fun little experiment. Unless you buy several of these, I can't imagine it would be a great deal of good for something other than a children's project, though! You get 18 seed pods and they are mostly for something different(there are 2 pods for 5 items). That means you won't be getting a huge amount of food from any one plant. It might be a great way to taste test these different kinds of plants, and know if you'd like to buy more of any certain ones.It really couldn't get much easier, though. You peel off the top and put it in the ground, or a container. Then water. That's it. On the package it guarantees at least 2 seeds per pod.*It states in the directions that these plants don't like hot weather. I'm in the HOT south right now, so it's really too late in the year to plant these. Doing so would be a complete waste, so I'm saving them for next spring. I'll try to update on how well they grow at that point.(I do have to admit that it worries me a bit that these aren't allowed for sale in CA!)

I used a plant dibber (do a search for it if you are unsure what it is) to make the right sized hole for the seed pods, plopped them in it, and watered. A little cardboard measuring guide came with the Gro-ables to make it even easier. Planting these vegetables couldn't possibly be any easier than that.I was pleased with the selection of vegetables and herbs, although I probably never would have planted beans. I had to work around really crazy weather in Oklahoma, waiting for the 100 plus degree weather to pass, then the flooding rains. I grabbed my chance to plant and we'll see what happens. I planted them in containers on wheels, so I can move them into my greenhouse later if necessary. All-in-all, this was fun and not too labor-intensive.

My review is going to be somewhat biased, as I a) live in FL (so I have to be careful what/when I plant) and b) already have a real garden.I see this kit as a nifty, convenient way for certain people to be introduced to the concept of vegetable and herb gardens. What types of people? Those with tiny yards (townhouses in planned communities) or balconies (apartments in the city) who have very little experience with growing things.These pods provide seeds, starting soil, and some fertilizer to help you get your vegetables started in large pots, planters, or your garden.There's a pretty wide distribution in here, but it seems geared toward a temperate climate and will produce enough stuff for a few good family-sized salads if planted all at once... plus a meal's worth of beans if you get the single plant to produce heavily. Tomato, snap peas, cucumber, lettuce, snack pepper -- definitely salad material. You're not getting what I'd consider the 'staples' of a real garden -- cabbage, broccoli, peas (normal kind, not snap), potatoes, onions, etc.Since I live in FL, I can't really plant the majority of the items in this kit right now -- I have to wait for fall, as it's too hot and there are too many bugs going around for tomatoes or lettuce to make it anywhere. However, the cilantro and basil work well in the 'strawberry'-type pots I have on my porch and I'm hoping to see the basil re-seed itself after it dies back.I'd like to have seen some warmer weather-friendly varieties in here, as well as some flowers -- marigolds, sunflowers, some fun and easy varieties to add some color to your little vegetable / herb patch.BOTTOM LINE: I like the idea behind this kit -- convenient, reasonable variety, and made as easy as possible for beginning gardeners. What I'm not crazy about is the price (you're getting about $3 worth of seeds / potting soil / fertilizer, if that) and the fact that, if everything in here grows, you're basically getting a few salads out of the deal. The wonder of a real garden is the amazing bounty you can get out of a relatively small bit of cultivated land. It's pretty cool having your own tomato plant or bush bean for the first time, but unless you're limited to a balcony or some kind of really tiny urban backyard, there are cheaper ways to try out growing your own vegetables.I'm giving this 3 stars but may bump it up to 4 if, during the fall, I'm blown away by the productivity of the other pods.
summary: Pricey, but cool introductory gardening kit for some

reviewText: I have some real misgivings about this garden in a box.  First, if you are looking for clean produce, Miracle-Gro seems like a dubious source for organic foods.  Also, if you have visions of pulling bushels of produce from your plot you will need to plant more than one box or mix a lot of other seed in.But what I was hoping for with this kit is to make an engaging introduction to gardening for my kids.  Unfortunately I got a reviewer package long after planting time for Minnesota, but we opened the box and looked at the individual, if overpackaged cone.  My kids are truly excited to plant them come spring.  For introducing children in the simplest of prepackaged kits, I can't imagine a better solution than this.  I can't imagine planting like this every year, but I think it's perfect for the kids first venture.Personally, I feel like it's my duty to free these little guys from their foil and cardboard prisons.  We are hoping for great things next spring.
summary: Perfect for Introducing Children to Gardening, not a great way to fill the table

reviewText: I love growing my own food. It's fun and I know no harmful chemicals or pesticides touched them. For someone who has little experience growing plants from seed, I suppose these pods could be a fun learning experience. You get a pack of 94% bio-degradable paper pots already stuffed with soil and all you have to do is dig a hole, push the pods in, and water. The shipping box is all cardboard and can be recycled. However, I can think of few reasons to buy this when seeds are readily available and the extra effort of digging a hole in the ground, dropping some seeds in, then covering up the hole again isn't really that hard to do. Maybe for a child's first gardening project? But really, it's not hard to plant seeds. We did that as a class project in the third grade with milk cartons and tomato seeds.For serious gardeners, it's much more economical to buy packets of seeds, which can be had for as little as $1-2 for hundreds, if not thousands of seeds. Or visiting farmers markets or nurseries, you can usually buy starters very cheaply. So if your aim is to grow your own food, these Miracle-Gro pods are patently cost-inefficient. Seed depth usually isn't important for most plants, and it's written on the instructions anyway. Most trowels have measurements on the handle, like thisFiskars 7067 3-Piece Softouch Garden Tool Set. Mother Nature has been just dropping seeds on the ground since the beginning of time (or out of a bird or bear's butt) and she seems to be doing quite fine.
summary: Good for a beginner - uneconomical for serious gardeners

reviewText: I love to garden and am always willing to try new things.  In the garden world, there are always new ways to market tools and planting devices.The concept of this package is interesting.  Ideally I'd prefer just a few vegetables to grow a bigger yield of one item.  And then there are climate variations.  I live in southern Arizona.  The monsoon is in heavy swing and gardeners usually plant just days before the first rains in mid June.  Some of these vegetables are cooler weather crops, others require some shade in our extreme sun.This is an expensive starter kit, but Miracle-Gro does work.  The one problem I had was having the seeds pop out of the soil after a heavy rain.I'll update this review in 30 days.

This kit is convenient and easy to use. I would not recommend it for a serious gardener, but this would be nice for someone who has no experience in seed starting, or just wants the absolute easiest way to plant vegetables.This kit contains 18 seed pods. Each pod contains the seed, growing mix and slow-release plant food. The pods were sturdy and firm and they were easy to handle and plant. Just peel of the paper cover, put the pod in the ground and water. That's it. Now you just have to remember to water.So, if you are feeling lazy but want a home-grown garden of vegetables, then this kit may be for you. Now if only it would water my plants too! ;)

I received these a little late in the planting season, so I only planted a select few and will plant the rest next year. I chose one of the lettuces, flat leaf spinach, one dill and two cilantro.The pods themselves are nice and neat. These are decent sized pods and definitely not tiny like Aerogarden sized ones. They are easy to plant. Just add them to your potting soil. I used organic for the herbs and a mix of organic and some cheaper soil for the lettuces. The pods have a label that peels back where you can see instructions on how to maintain the plant. Some of these were stuck, so they ripped, making them unreadable. The pack comes with a sample of plant food and tips on how often to fertilize. I used the sample pack, but I normally use Neptune's fertilizer for my plants.I planted these the evening I received them and made sure to place them in a spot where they would receive sufficient sunlight. The weather had cooled down, so it wasn't too harsh for the plants. They were watered daily and the pots they were in seemed to stay moist. After almost 2 weeks, the lettuce and spinach were growing nicely. In the other pot, the herbs have not sprouted at all. There is a little pathetic looking thing growing out of the pot that could be cilantro, but it is not growing from the pod, so I am not sure what it is. I know cilantro is a difficult herb to grow and maintain. I have grown dill in the past though and am disappointed that it hasn't sprouted at all.This set might be good for beginners, for a kids project, or people who live in smaller spaces who want to grow their own food outside their apartment or condo. I agree with the other reviewers that it seems weird that only one bean plant is provided in the kit, but I guess it could be something to nibble on while harvesting the other plants. I look forward to planting the other pods next season and will most likely update this review with those results.

I was offered this about a month ago in mid-July for review.  Given the time it takes for seeds to germinate and then produce, it meant that I had to sprout indoors without the possibility of transplanting outdoors into my vegetable garden before frost.  (I am in Zone 5-6) So for the purpose of this review, the entire process from germination to harvest will be in containers and  rotated between my sunny kitchen window, the deck and my enclosed sunroom.Pros:+ Biodegradeable individual pods that contain Miracle-Gro plant food, a bit of soil and supposedly a seed or two to produce a plant+ Small easy-read leaflet that indicates how far away to plant them from each other.  Simple, concise and easy to follow instructions.+ A small paper tape measure so you don't have to go and find one.+ A small packet of additional Miracle-Gro plant food for additional fertilization that is the correct quantity for the number of pods in the kit.  There is no need to go out and buy an additional container of fertilizer only to have most of the bottle/bag leftover.+ All-in-one kit is convenient and portable.Cons:- Not practical for the established garden or gardener for economical reasons.- May contain the occasional dud.- Output would be low and is only really enough for a few salads.Perfect for:- Beginners and those who want to try growing their own but have never ever tried growing a thing in their life.- a gift/project for kids interested in beginning gardening to start their own garden alongside mummy or daddy's garden.- Vacation gardening away from home for those lucky enough to have a place to go to for the summer months but would like to garden a bit without having to schlep all their gardening things up to the holiday rental.- Container gardeners or those short of space to store full sized versions of seeds, and fertilizers.- Housewarming gift for a new family moving into their first house for the convenience factor.Experience:So far I have planted the pods according to the instructions on the packet into large terracotta pots.  The lettuce has sprouted as has some of the herbs and a tomato plant.  A few that I expected to sprout have not and may be duds.  I will update this as the season progresses.  The plants have been sprouted in a sunny kitchen window and are going through the hardening process (in and out from the kitchen to deck) before being left on the deck in their pots for the remainder of the growing season here and then will be brought indoors into the sunroom to see how long they are able to produce.
summary: Cute, convenient and makes a good gift.

reviewText: This Miracle-Gro "Gro-ables Salad and Herb" Garden Kit is a clever way to get an instant garden that even a "brown thumb" like my wife can get going in hurry. We have tried our hand at small gardens in the past and have had mixed results since my wife is able kill almost any plant she chooses to give any attention to.Each seed is settled in a self contained pod that includes fertilized soil and is just inserted into the ground. The instructions are very easy to follow and most of the guess work has been removed. This set actually produced results that were rather impressive, in that most everything germinated and began to grow. Sadly for us, we lost just about everything to bunnies since we left these unprotected.We will try these again next year in boxes on the back porch where the critters can't reach them. These would also make good science projects for students as well.Recommended!CFH
Everything is done already. By just placing the pods, peeling and watering, the herbs began to grow.  It was easy to plant and the variety is good.

I planted them in containers on my deck and watered them gently.  Next day it rained and we had pleasant, sunny weather for several days and nothing ever grew...I saw a spindly sprout appear in one of the four but it died and nothing has happened since so I'm assuming it's a loss.  I've NEVER had problems growing from seed before.  I checked it daily to make sure all was well and not dried out.And also the term "kit" is a bit misleading.  These are seeds in tiny starter pots that you plant somewhere, such as a container or in your garden.The kit is really very expensive.  It would be less expensive to buy the seed starter cups and then buy the seeds and you would also know what type of tomato, etc., that you are getting.

Confident gardeners and those with green thumbs may well decide that this bundle of pre-planted capsules of basic herb and vegetable seeds is heavier on packaging than productivity. However, people without gardening experience will find that this product offers multimedia guidance and support along with seeds and growing media.To put this product through its paces, I tried to approach it from the perspective of a beginner -- remembering childhood guidance from my dad, as well as my own attempts to nurture a love of gardening in my own children. The growing guide is a brightly colored flier with basic instructions about how to create an inviting environment for your new sprouts, as well as how to get those little capsules in the ground and tend them. A miniature measuring tape subtly discourages guesswork, and explanations for how and why to space plants and to thin seedlings helps avoid rookie mistakes. In addition, MiracleGro maintains an approachable website (domain name: groables) that includes a planting video, frost maps, and troubleshooting tips. A FAQ page anticipates beginners' questions in a friendly and non-condescending manner. Overall, the positive tone is more cheerful than cloying, and seems well suited to nurturing a positive outlook in the mind of the new gardener, especially if that person doesn't have an experienced person to turn to. Information is basic but does cover the necessary ground.In my garden, everything I've planted thus far except for the peppers germinated reliably, and with care and thinning, each pod brought forth a healthy plant. However, I prepared my soil thoroughly, and although the kit gives information on doing so, I think beginning gardeners could benefit from pods being deeper and thus having more nutritive medium for the seedlings' early growth. At this price point, I also think the number of pods is counterproductive. Why? I suspect that it will be difficult for beginning gardeners to thin the pods willingly, given the likely perception that they are "wasting a perfectly good plant."Is this kit suitable for most gardeners? If you have experience with growing herbs, veggies and lettuces, you will find the kit filled with only basic varieties, and may well be disappointed. However, if you are within the target market for these kits -- and their online support -- you are likely to find this to be a good value.This product is well suited for adults who want to dispel the self-perception of having a brown thumb, or who did not grow up learning about growing edibles. The pods may be easier for arthritic fingers to handle than small seeds, a reassurance to former gardeners who wish for a container or two of homegrown produce. I could also see this as an excellent long-distance gift of affection and tradition to a child from a grandparent or other family elder.

Though I grew up on a farm, somehow I did not inherit the green thumb. Since our family eats so many veggies everyday, I wanted to grow my own. These pods from Miracle-Gro make it very easy to do so. Everything is contained in the pod: the soil, fertilizer and seeds. You simply pop it in the dirt (you don't even need to cover them with more dirt), water and wait for them to sprout.They are all sprouting what appears to be healthy plants. It is way too early to harvest them, but I feel confident I will get great results.This package comes with a nice variety of veggies and herbs (a few are duplicates). There are pods for dill, cilantro, basil, lettuce, beans, tomato and cucumber.It also comes with clear directions for spacing and sunlight and plant food. I have mine in a raised bed, but these would also be great for container gardens.I think this is a great product that can help those of us ease our apprehension about having a successful garden.
summary: Super easy to use and already growing!

reviewText: This is a cool garden kit. Makes a great gift too. Very easy to use and very fool proof. Just water and watch it grow. You get 1 seed of each for a total of 18 seed pods. I started a small garden box with my son and we used these pods since you can dig them up at the right depth each time and plant food is in the pod too. This was our first garden and this helped us to move into bigger gardening projects. This is well worth the price since the pod has the soil and plant food inside already. Might be a more convenient and maybe cheaper route than buying seeds, soil mix and plant food. Plus you will need to know the depth of the hole to plant the seeds. This kit just makes it real convenient.

These are currently selling for $19.  At a $1 a pod, this is a reasonable price to pay for this variety of vegetables and herbs.My brother maintains a 1/4 acre garden almost year round.  He chose these pods and planted them in herb garden.  Ideally they would have been planted months ago but we are having a mild summer and we planted them in a partially shaded herb garden that has rich soil.To be able to identify the contents, he left them in the cardboard frame and placed them on top of the rich soil.  He labeled each pod by writing on the frame and threw away the foil label.  Bad move as the writing quickly faded so we have to wait for the seeds to develop to know what they are.Not planting the pods into the soil didn't work well because they dried out too quickly so I planted them into the soil (still in their pods) a week later.Most of the pods have sprouted.  Others had the seeds sitting on top of the soil (we pushed them back in) and some had lost their seeds entirely.Addendum:  One month later and only half of the plants survive due, I suspect, to the late planting.I suspect that we would have had all the pods sprout and do well if we had planted them correctly in the early spring.  I recommend this package particularly for kids as it makes the planting and selection process easy.  The kids are more likely to eat the vegetables and herbs if they grow them theirselves.
summary: Good Choice for a Child's Garden

reviewText: I live in California and i planted 10 of these in my back yard.  I plant various vegetables in my back year, from tomoatoes to squash to cucumbers.  When I plant these, most of them sprout and i'm able to veggie on them for the summer.  However, out of the 10 that i planted, only 5 were successful.  The description does say it's not for sale in CA, so maybe CA is not rightly zoned for this product?  I dont know.

I didn't pay a dime for this garden kit, so I had to question why I ordered this. The answer was fairly easy. I maintain a small herb garden in the warm months which is usually transplanted to small pots that reside in an insulted and lighted green house window when it gets cold. While this would satisfy my herb garden needs in the most minimal of ways and would be supplemented by other herbs, this would be a great way to get my granddaughter into gardening in a small and manageable way. As it turned out, this was perfect. We cleared and cultivated a small patch of land, ammended and supplemented the soil, dug evenly spaced holes, inserted the seeds and their own pods, and watered and weeded.Since everything in the set was done for us down to the proper depth of seed placement, all we needed to depend on was mother nature. Germination has been quick. My granddaughter is thrilled with her accomplishments and comes over every day to weed and water. Sure, we are not getting a huge yield that will feed the family for all summer or even a few meals. However, this is a first easy step into getting into gardening and green sustainability. On this score, i think this product is a nice approach to introduce a child to gardening or creating an urban rooftop garden. Overall, it simplifies the steps I normally follow each spring when i start prepping my regular garden. Despite being overpriced for what it is, it simplifies gardening for kids and would be gardeners.

If you want to try gardening, this is a simple kit to try it out. It comes with 18 seed pods that you can just put straight into the dirt. Of course, it isn't as easy as that. Some plants like more sun and water than others so if you are going to successfully grow everything, you need to learn more about the individual plants and their needs. But this gives a great assortment of seeds so you can experiment with what grows well if your area.
summary: Fun for a first time gardener

reviewText: I'm all for making any process easier, so this kit seemed like a great idea for me.  I had room in my garden area and several containers ready so I immediately got these planted when I received it.  I watered as I should have, we had plenty of sun and in the end I didn't get nearly as much from them as I had hoped.For me the following items either never produced or produced so little that it wasn't enough to harvest.* Cucumber* Bush Bean* Loose-Leaf Lettuce* Romaine Lettuce* Snap Pea* Smooth-Leaf Spinach* Sweet PepperOn the other hand the following items produced very well and I am still enjoying them now* Globe Tomato* Cherry Tomato* Butterhead Lettuce* Basil* Cilantro* DillOverall I still like the idea of this kit, but depending on your area, weather, soil, etc. you may see better or worse results than I had and because of that it may not be the best option.
summary: Easy to plant, but only a few produced

reviewText: I usually garden with starts, not seeds, so I thought these might be a good way to learn to love seeds, but I was so disappointed. While there is a nice variety, once I opened it up and read the directions, I was a bit aghast at how little food this kit makes, and how much packaging it uses. I think I pictures smaller pods--more like little protective peat bullets--and a lot more of them, 18 types, not 18 total (so that's my fault--but that doesn't make this product any less silly). These are little pointy peat pots, about the size of a tiny Dixie cup, filled with soilless mix and 2 seeds, with a peel off lid like a little tub of coffee creamer.I'd give it 0 stars for me, but if you're a city dweller with only a tiny sunny balcony and a few pots, or someone not concerned with actual yield who just wants a tidy, educational project for small kids, this might be a fun and cute way to grow a bitty bit of food. If you have any space at all, it makes no sense.Seriously, who plants one bush bean plant? That's one dinner. Ditto the lettuce and pepper.Even if your space is limited, if you want one of each plant, buy starts for the herbs and vegetables and a packet of bean seeds. You'll spend about the same, get to pick more interesting varieties, and be that much closer to harvest and with no fussing over tender shoots, which can get knocked off by one hungry bug or especially hot or cold morning. Or if you love seeds, this price tag will get you a good 8-12 packets or more of seeds, giving you a full garden, and probably plenty to save for next year.Germination wasn't spectacular, either. The cups didn't seem to hold any more moisture than just plain soil (but I do have good, sheep poo-enriched soil), and didn't germinate any better than bare seeds. I don't get the rave reviews, unless others are a lot richer and grow vegetables for novelty rather than the table.If this were an herbs-only kit, I *might* be able to see it, since that's more where you'll see spreading and a couple seeds going a long way. But one bean plant? That's just deranged.
summary: A very expensive route to a teeny tiny garden

reviewText: Gardening is as old as humans but for some reason, gardening can be intimidating if you haven't done it before. The Miracle-Gro Garden Kit takes the intimidation out because it has all been done for you. The kit contains 18 grow pods, each already include seeds and Miracle-Gro, all that is needed is for you to plant and water. Miracle-Gro is named rightly because it's great, I have always had excellent results with it and it really does work.The set comes with complete instructions for each plant including germination time and when to expect your harvest.If you are an experienced gardener then you probably don't need this kit because you already know how to garden but if you are just starting or just need a small patio or container garden then this could be a good option for you. This set is just right for herbs and salads.

This is a great product and seems fool proof.  However you still need to tend to the garden and make sure you water enough.  They come in little pods and you just stick them into the soil in your garden.  They were fun to plant and grow but you get so little food out of this pack and it is expensive.  I only planted some herbs, and it is too hot and sunny in my zone to plant others.  Most of the vegetables listed take about 60 days to grow, according to the booklet.The packaging it came in and the packet to teach you how to use them are great.  If you have a big garden, economically you will want to buy seeds as you will get more for your money.  However, for convenience, these make a good choice. It's a good choice for those who want a smaller vegetable garden and just starting out.

This is a fun and healthy project for parents or grandparents to do with the kids.Miracle-Gro is like crack cocaine for plants--they love the stuff. Planting seeds in a peat container (actually a recycled material that looks like a peat pot) full of Miracle-Gro is a nearly foolproof way to grow the plants. The included booklet includes planting instructions and grow times for each of the veggie products, so you'll know when to expect them to mature and be ready for consumption.This is a fun way to entice kids to grow food by hand and eat healthy produce grown at home. There is a great selection of veggie products including a variety of lettuces, etc. What better way to encourage kids to try new foods and to teach them to garden. It's good for their bodies and their souls.I wouldn't necessarily recommend this to adults looking for a robust vegetable garden for feeding their family. The portions are too small and growing vegetables from seed isn't necessarily the most practical way to grow a summer garden. Plus these plants are born Miracle-Gro junkies and need a constant "fix" if you plan to keep them growing very long.

My family enjoys planting, growing, and eating home-grown fruits and vegetables so I didn't hesitate to try this Miracle-Gro Gro-ables Salad and Herb Garden Kit.Likes:>Pre-packaged seed pods consist of specially selected seeds positioned at the proper depth with the appropriate growing materials to maintain seed moisture and slow release plant food.>Simple manual with clear instructions on planting the pods, correct spacing, and whether the pods can be planted both in the ground or in containers, or capable of being started indoors then transplanted outdoors.  Estimated days to germinate and days to harvest.>A recipe on making Fresh Herb Vinaigrette dressing.>A good assortment of garden salad and herbs seeds including Bush Bean (1 pod), Butterhead Lettuce (2), Cherry Tomato (1), Cucumber, Globe Tomato (1), Loose-leaf Lettuce (2), Romaine Lettuce (1), Snap Pea (1), Spinach (1), Sweet Pepper (1), Basil (2), Cilantro (2), and Dill (2).>Includes a 1 oz. packet of Shake 'n Feed for Tomato, Fruits, & vegetables.>Helpful tips for best results, watering, and storage of unplanted pods.>More info available at groables dot com.>Miracle-Gro (Scott's) is well known manufacturer of plant foods and soils, and we've had good results with their products over the years.Slight concern:This is a sample but unfortunately these gardening seed pods are normally not for sale in certain states.Results so far:>The soil in our backyard is nice and fertile.  We already have grown a wide variety of vegetables such as Romaine Lettuce, celery, cherry tomatoes, red peppers, etc.  We carefully selected plots in our garden to insure adequate spacing and good sun exposure for these Gro-ables pods.>We planted all the pods except the vegetables we already have and watered them according to instructions.  This summer in so. Cal. has been exceptionally cool with daily daytime temps around the mid-70s to the mid-80s so we planted the pods anyway in a partially shaded plot.  Ideally, new seeds should be planted in springtime.>After approx. 14 days, most of the pods have germinated and we continued to water them with care.Overall:It will take some time (up to 75 days) before these vegetables and herbs will be ready for harvest.  These pre-packaged Gro-ables seed pods certainly made home-grown vegetables/herbs a simpler and more enjoyable task.  We can't wait to taste the salads and herbs from our garden!
summary: Easy to plant and grow garden vegetables and herbs kit.

reviewText: I have a garden every year and start many plants indoors like tomatoes, melons, things that take longer to reach maturity because int the north our seasons are shorter. I only planted some of these because it is just too late to plant some of the plants plus the fact that the base of them is pointed so they don't stand up on their own so they need another pot to be placed in.The ones I did plant outside have started growing so they are good and will germinate. I don't like the selection of plants that much though, seems it has more lettuce than anything.1 Globe Tomato1 Cherry Tomato1 Cucumber1 Bush Bean2 Loose-Leaf Lettuce2 Butterhead Lettuce1 Romaine Lettuce1 Snap Pea1 Smooth-Leaf Spinach1 Sweet Pepper Plus, the Herb Garden2 Basil2 Cilantro2 DillWhile this kit is OK, it would be much cheaper to get miracle gro soil and some peat pots of your own and then you ca plant any variety of seed you want.
summary: They are OK for starting outside

reviewText: This Miracle-Gro "Gro-ables" Salad and Herb Garden Kit might be a nifty idea. The seed pods are compact and simple to plant. And the instructions are very clear. But the final results--i.e., the "crop" yield--will be the final determining factor as to the quality of this product. So for now, it's 3 stars. I've planted the seed pods and most of them have started to grow. But, again...time will tell. I also have to agree with some of the other reviewers: the cost of these seed pods is pretty high. You can buy a whooole lot more seeds for the cost of this garden kit. And I've never found seeds particularly hard to plant. Buying "straight" seeds might be a more cost effective way to go. Unless these "Gro-ables" produce mass quantities of vegetables and herbs, I'm not sure the product is worth it.

What a great idea. So easy to plant, all you do is dig the little hole and set the plant right in it and water daily until it gets going and it started growing very fast. There is a little packet of Shake n Feed with it too which I used when I first planted them all. Everything started growing very quickly, less than a week, but then it happened, the deer came and ate the entire garden....I mean every single plant, roots and all... This year we've had a lot of problems with deer in town as we live in a rural community, just 86 people. People fed them a few years ago when they came in town when we had such a hard freeze and they were starving to death. Bad idea, now they just keep coming. I had a little fence around where I planted but it wasn't high enough so they got in anyway. These plants came up so fast that I'm sure they would have had a great vegetable production and I only watered them a few minutes each day just once. I'll get some next year and try again with a taller fence around to keep the stupid deer out.. Sorry my review couldn't be much help :(
summary: Miracle-Gro 170025 Gro-ables Salad and Herb Garden Kit

reviewText: The Miracle-Gro 18 pod salad garden is basically for someone who wants to either grow their veggies on the patio or in limited space or someone who wants to sample various veggies. Below I cut and pasted the list of veggies from the Amazon website:Salad Garden1 Globe Tomato1 Cherry Tomato1 Cucumber1 Bush Bean2 Loose-Leaf Lettuce2 Butterhead Lettuce1 Romaine Lettuce1 Snap Pea1 Smooth-Leaf Spinach1 Sweet Pepper Plus, the Herb Garden2 Basil2 Cilantro2 DillAs you can see you get one bean, one snap pea, one pepper, two tomatoes (a cherry and regular size) and a cucumber. Obviously if you are planning to feed a family with the one bean and pea pod you are not going to be able to do it. It will probably be good for one salad. This is a mini-garden for one or at the most two people.This was a review product and I got it in mid-summer. My thinking on this was that I'd be able to utilize it in Denver where I live and Las Vegas where I spend significant time. First off I'm not sure when I started watering the pods if they liked the Denver climate or they knew in their little seeds it was late in the summer. I did get some decent lettuce from the five lettuce pods and some spinach from the one spinach pod. They sprouted quickly as lettuce often does and transferred easily to some long rectangular pots. The lettuce wasn't huge when harvested, but it made a good salad and was tasty.  I brought the sprouted tomatoes, cucumber, bean, pea and herbs with me to Vegas. The heat here fried the poor tomato plants immediately (within a few days). The cucumber, bean and pea are still going--they are in pots and I've brought them in during the hottest part of the day. I don't think any of them will make it here in Vegas. Too hot. The herbs (basil, cilantro and dill) all sprouted, but aren't doing anything much. I do have a rather lethal touch with plants, so it is probably me and not the pod seeds. I was really surprised that the basil sprouted as I've heard basil is hard to grow from seed. It is a tiny thing, but hanging in there. The dill and cilantro probably aren't going to make it. I have put them out in the early morning and late evening to enjoy the sun, but the heat seems too much for them.I don't think this is a bad set, but I do think the beans and peas could be eliminated for something else. What exactly are you going to get from one bean and one pea plant? Not much. I should have poked around in the seed pod to see if there was more than one seed, but I did not. I got one plant from each pod. Same goes for the tomatoes.This would be a fun set to introduce children to gardening and the joy of salad eating! Not sure it will do much for adults. And the Vegas' climate is much too hot for most of these plants!

Other reviewers have pointed out that this won't appeal to serious gardeners, but I think that goes without saying.  It's a cute project for kids or people who just want to dabble in gardening.  It doesn't seem to have a better germination rate than regular seeds, and it is rather expensive for what it is.  It seems to me that you would be better off buying seedlings than buying these if you're truly interested in the outcome, but a major benefit of this kit is that it can be shipped and stored (unlike seedlings). It's also *much* easier for children to handle than seeds.  So really the idea is not that you'd be able to eat off of it or anything, but it does allow kids to experience the whole process from start to finish and can also whet the appetite of non-gardeners.

I'm a little late to Grow-ables and will have a very late crop this year.  I most certainly like the concept, but the price for a Grow-ables mini-crop will be very prohibitive for anyone who wants to grow a large garden.  Perhaps the price will come down in time and if it does, I'll be one of the first in line.  This also comes with a small sample ofMiracle-Gro Shake `n Feedthat you can use on your plants.I do like the simplicity of the Grow-ables.  The directions are as follows:1.  Remove entire lid from Seed Pod.2.  Choose a sunny spot.3.  There is no need to cover the pod with soil.4.  Keep Seed Pod moist.How easy can it get?  There are seed pods for a bush bean, butterhead lettuce (2), cherry tomato, cucumber, globe tomato, loose-leaf lettuce (2), romaine lettuce, snap pea, spinach, sweet pepper, basil, cilantro (2) and dill (2).  There was also a Gro-ables Seed Pod Guide enclosed in the packet.  I really do like the concept and at this price point I could only see that it would be worth purchasing for use in a homeschool or classroom setting.
summary: Perfect for homeschool or classroom use, but otherwise too expensive to make it practical for home use ...

reviewText: I generally don't have a green thumb, although I've been successful planting marigold seeds outside in the past. Generally when it comes to herbs and vegetables, I'm lucky if I can get anything past the two leaf phase of sprout-hood. Perhaps a miracle could occur with these Miracle-Gro pods. On August 28, I planted all 18 in a window box full of soil and mulch. Each seed pod is fitted into the soil with its top showing; then the top is peeled off, you water everything, and things should be good to go. I decided that since the weather is pretty good for growing, I'd leave the box outside for now, then bring it in if we start to get close to a frost. And meanwhile, I'm watering the box daily. I figure if anything actually grows, I'll transplant it into something more appropriate. For now, I'm a little puzzled by the cost of this set, which seems somewhat high given the number of actual seeds included in each pod - most of the expense here is for the little pods that hold the seed, I'd think. For $30, though, you could buy quite a few herbs and vegetables at the market. Well, we'll see. I'll be back in a few weeks to report the kit's progress.Day 5 after planting: 11 of the 18 seed pods have sprouted shoots. So far, so good.Day 13 after planting: 15 of the pods have sprouted....all doing quite nicely. There are 2-3 sprouting plants for each one of these pods.
summary: Waiting to see if they grow

reviewText: At first look this product looks like you just stick it in the ground, water it and you'll have a wonderful herb and veggie garden. It's an appealing idea, but in truth, some of the pods need to be first planted inside and then later transplanted outside. Also, planting times vary from climate to climate. As other reviewers have mentioned, this plants would produce very little actual food. You can get a lot more garden for the money by going with seeds or plants and doing a little research. This is more of a gimmick for the first time gardener. Not recommended.
summary: Not as simple or as practical as it looks

reviewText: My kids love these little garden pods they are easy to plan just dig a tiny hole plop them in and water you are done. I have planted the herbs since it is late in the growing season I could not plant the others till next year. The herbs are up and look great. Fun for the beginner gardener or for kids.

I have a deadline to write reviews so I can only tell you what I have experienced so far!I have most of these growing in a raised garden but have planted the tomato and peas in containers. I've used Miracle Grow planting soil for both and within 1 week, had sprouts and they are now all growing well. We've had hot dry weather, so I've been quite religious about watering them.Time will tell. So far, so good! 6/8/13

I should begin by saying this little set is not a bad idea in and of itself. Heck, this is hardly the first time anyone has introduced a seed kit to the populace and Miracle-Gro is a brand I highly respect.  So little seedpods in their individual biodegradable containers with food ready-to-go should have been a hit, right?  Yet I found myself, even while planting them, thinking "why?"The plants grew about as well as I could hope for, but I could see no difference between them and more traditionally-sewn plants, nor was the containers significantly more convenient.  The same amount of energy and work goes to setting these up than any other seedling or seen, and this kit just costs so darn much.I think I was just excited by the fancy setup, but when all was said and done I would rather go the old-fashioned route.  Kind of fun, perhaps a good gift idea, but not how I would support my gardening full-time.
summary: I considered it gimicky after the fact

reviewText: A lot of home gardeners choose to save money by starting plants by seed inside and then transplanting them to the vegetable garden when the season allows. This is a good procedure if you have patience, otherwise can be tedious and unrewarding.Now Miracle-Gro has made it easy to give plants a head start inside before transplanting with its seed pod products. There are 19 different seed pod varieties to select from, including spinach, several lettuce types, pumpkin, zucchini, squash, watermelon, beans, peas, sweet pepper, different tomato types, and several herbs.I chose the Miracle-Gro Gro-ables Salad and Herb Garden kit which contains 18 seed pods including globe tomato, cherry tomato, cumber, bush bean, loose-leaf lettuce, butterhead lettuce, Romaine lettuce, snap pea, smooth-leaf spinach, sweet pepper, basil, cilantro and dill.The ready-to-plant seed pods contain everything a plant needs to grow - specially selected seed planted at the correct depth, snow release plant food with the right nutrients for root growth.Amateur gardeners as well as green thumbers with more experience will love Miracle-Gro's Seed Pods. It makes gardening easier and much more fun.
summary: How to Garden With Ease and Enjoy it More

reviewText: Depending on your weather and how hot your summers are will determine how well these cute little all in one garden pods grow. Great for a spring garden starter or plant late in summer for a fall garden. See the Amazon video.These are individual little pots that you just push into prepared soil. They can be used in containers or garden, which pmakes them perfect for someone who gardens in a small area. All seemed to germinate well, an drequire a lot of water in my lower south area.
summary: Buy these early to start a great patio, homeschool, individual garden starter seeds and pots in one.

reviewText: I grow my plants from seeds each year and while it's cumbersome, I have good luck with it. This product seems to make that process even easier, though at an increased cost. The nice part is they are already seeded at the proper depth and ready to go. I can see the product being more suited for someone who doesn't have the time or patience to grow plants from seed.I was impressed with all the materials that came with these little pods. Fertilizer, guide, etc. They were well-packed and easy to get started. I planted mine in my Garden Tower and within days, I had sprouts from all of the pods. They are not very big yet, but sprouting is half the battle!I did not use the fertilizer, nor do I plan to. I'd prefer to go a more natural route.So far so good and no complaints!Pros: SUPER easy to use - just stick in soil and water. Kit is easy to understand and comes with all you need to grow a sizable amount of food. Instructions make this almost fool-proof.Cons: Not nearly as cheap as planting seeds yourself, but cheaper than buying already-grown plants. Cups must be planted to grow - will not stand up on their own.

Gardening is a bit of work to begin with and not only did I get a late start, I was going to have to put my garden on the deck, more than likely building something to hold the garden in the first place. Since that would take a while, when it came to the actual planting, I wanted a simple way to get a variety of seeds planted easily and quickly, maximizing the percentage of successful plants without a lot of measuring, thinning, and re-planting on my part. My purchase ofGreenes 4 Ft. X 4 Ft. X 21 In. Tiered Cedar Raised Garden Bedsolved the garden deck problem, and this Miracle-Gro kit solved the effortless, fast planting part.The kit comes with 18 pre-seeded peat pots with twelve different kinds of herbs and vegetables (the herbs and lettuces being what is doubled up), and all you have to do is put the pots into the ground and water until the plants come up and the veggies come out. The kit comes with plenty of explanation about the individual seed pods, as well as a paper ruler to make sure you are giving the plants enough room to grow. They also provide a planting chart which tells you where, when, and everything else you need to know about the planting process. I took a chance and planted the "in the ground" plants in the highest level of my three tier garden, and everything else I just put wherever the spirit moved me, keeping in mind the distances needed between the plants when I put them down. After three days of watering, the cucumbers and bush beans came up (as did my radishes that I planted myself in the extra space around the plants). The instructions said everything would germinate in 7-10 days, and that turned out to be the case. All the plants sprouted, so I guess they really are "guaranteed to grow" (as advertised).I can't vouch for the final, ultimate results, but that is all dependent on the dirt and watering, anyway, so I'm expecting a bountiful, tasty, healthy garden to indulge in later this summer. I really like this kit, both for the variety you get and the ease of planting, I think it is quite decent value. If my results are as good as I'm expecting them to be, there's a good chance I'll be buying these again next year. It's a five-star green-thumb product.
summary: Good eats before too long, I'm sure

reviewText: The Miracle-Grow Salad Kit is a simple and complete system.  All you need to supply is a prepared bed or set of planters.  It has instructions and growing tips for those who have not gardened before.  Honestly there is not much to setting it up.  Push the "pods" into the soil (appropriately spaced,) water and watch them grow.This is a very nice set up for someone who does not routinely garden or want to get down in the dirt.  The "pods" are compressed peat pots filled with growing medium, each containing a seed (and a bit of fertilizer).  The kit also includes a packet of Miricle-gro plant food for when your plants are up.I looked at this kit as my daughter is now in college and wants a window sill garden.  It's a good thing I looked at it first (before sending her one) as this is not the right thing for her.  This set will plant a raised bed of approximately 8x10 feet (not a window box).I am not a novice gardener, having planted an acre in Hawaii for 30 odd years.  I do, in fact, have most of these materials in my garage, generally starting seedlings in plant cells (a tray) in a similar mix.  For those who do not routinely garden, this spares your having to buy soil + additives + fertilizer and seed.There are some positives and negatives here.  Any home gardener knows that after poring over catalogs and ordering seed you wind up with enough for a small farm.  Typically ordering half a dozen varieties of heirloom tomato, I could plant 500 tomatoes... if I had the space (and frequently get carried away, starting way more than I have room for).  This kit gives you one of each (and 2 basil and cilantro).  The downside?  These are not the varieties nor assortment I would have chosen.  It is a bit heavy on the lettuces, and... why 2 cilantro & basil (of the same variety)?  I typically plant a mesclun mix, several varieties of tomato... and at one point had 17 varieties of basil.  That said, this really is a kit for the novice gardener (despite the one size fits all description).  The instructions, pictures, print size all look like they are set up for young children.  I also did not get as much information as I would like about the seed.  I have to assume that all or most are hybrids, but of what sort? Bred for early harvest, pest-resistance...?  Does it contain any GMO stock? (I suspect not because those varieties are expensive).  However not much information is provided on the seed other than how long to germination.  The only other questionable aspect for me is the peat pots.  I have personally not had particularly good experiences with them in the past.  Yes, they are easy and add a soil amendment which is good if you have poor soil or a bed which is not well prepared.  They are easy to handle, BUT in my experience, do not decompose anywhere near quickly enough, frequently impeding plant growth.  I have peat pots which still turn up when I turn my plant beds after 5-10 years (in one of the wettest places on earth)!  I am sure the seeds will be off to a good start, and miricle-gro makes a balanced, reliable fertilizer, the question is how they will perform once ready to grow through the pots?I would recommend this kit for novice or infrequent gardeners or for young children (though it is not as good a teaching tool for kids setting up their first garden, as they will not learn about choosing a finer grade of soil or potting mix to start seeds or choosing varieties suited to their growing area (plant zone)), those who do not want to get their hands dirty and who are not especially picky.  You get 2 non-descript tomatoes, a few varieties of lettuce; the kinds typically seen in the super market, and a very very small selection (2) herbs, also pretty generic.  I planted this kit in addition to half a dozen varieties of tomatoes, peppers, beans and a dozen or so herbs ;)  After a week, they are not yet up but ought to be soon.  I'll report on the progress and post pictures when the plants are established, another few weeks, I suspect.-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------UpdateAfter roughly 10 days not a one of the seeds is up, while those I planted myself mostly are.  I suspect this is an artifact of the shipping process.  The box the pods are in is marked "this end up".  Unfortunately,m that box is shipped inside another box, so the P.O. will not see that instruction, one I doubt they would follow anyway.  The problem is that some seeds ought to be planted at a depth of 1/2 inch, some 1 inch.  If they are jumbled around in shipping (as they inevitably will be) you do not know where in that little capsule they wind up. Does it make a difference?  absolutely!  Seeds contained enough food/ energy to grow through the medium and reach the light.  Small variances will not make much of a difference, but large ones will.  If a small seed which ought to be surface-planted, or planted at a shallow depth is instead under 4 inches of medium, it will run out of steam before it reaches the light.  I can not think of another way to explain this utter failure as I believe the seed is fresh.  For those of you considering this system, I would recommend, instead, Ferry-Morse seed, also sold by Amazon.  The seeds I received from Ferry-Morse all sprouted in a couple of days, much faster than average, in my experience.  The included seedling mix is good, as is the fertilizer.  There is just a problem if you do not know the planting depth, which you will not if it is handled by USPS.  Alternatively, one could dump the contents of each pod, sift through the medium to find the seed, refill the pots and replant, a good deal more effort than if one had planted them themselves.  It looks like others have had more luck... but that is what you wind up with.  If you are lucky, the pods will arrive with the seeds more or less at the correct planting depth, if not, you will have limited success.  Mine have been planted in just about the ideal growing situation, one I suspect few could easily replicate, in a sunny patch in Hawaii, a prepared raised bed which is mostly compost and which has been worked for 10-15 years so the soil is loose to a depth of a couple of feet.  They receive adequate water and light.  Not much can got wrong here (my biggest issue is generally pests).  This is the first time in 30 years I have had issues with seeds sprouting (other than when birds dig up my seed)!  The pots and soil seem undisturbed, and the birds seem to be plenty happy with the cherries we have in abundance right now.  I do not think that is what happened here.  I will update if/ when I see some seedlings, but I doubt I will see a good germination rate if not a one of them is up now, to include the beans, which generally take 2-4 days to sprout.6/18 2 weeks on and the seeds in 1 pod have sprouted (the peas).  I suspect it is because these are larger seeds and so can tolerate a deeper planting depth.  This does not bode well and at this point I would be surprised to get germination from even half.  I will update to report any progress, or note germination rate at the end of a month which ought to be ample time for all the seeds to have germinated.  This is the lowest germination rate I have ever seen, and I can not think of anything besides random planting depth which would have produced such poor results.  I got better germination from seed which is several years old (planted at the same time in amended garden soil and seed trays).I have downgraded my star rating accordingly.  Beyond that, I do not believe I'd recommend it as an activity for kids.  It is less good as a teaching tool than a packet of seed and, because of issues mentioned above, there is bound to be disappointment.  I would rather avoid doing something like this which could actually damped kids' enthusiasm.  When my kids were little, they would check the garden daily (or more ;)  if they had planted, anxiously waiting for their seeds to come up.  I imagine they would have been very disappointed if they never did.-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The plants started to grow in a mini garden after carefully following the instruction. However, if the garden was bigger, it would be more economical to use discarded cardboard egg cartons cut into separate holders, to buy potting soil and seeds separately, to put them into the holders, and to make my own cones at no time.  The key is easy accessibility of gardening store.

It's good that these are "specially selected" to not include GMO seeds...It's good that there's a fair variety of seeds, "pre-planted" into little pods - that you, in turn, plant into actual dirt.  Wait a minute!  That's just weird.So most gardeners have used peat pots or other seedling containers.  Miracle-Gro has...put a seed in said container for you, along with "soil" and nutrients (not organic), and you plant the entire container.  I suppose the draw here is that the seed is planted at the correct depth, but that's such a trivial thing to do on your own, it's difficult to figure out who these little seed pods are actually designed for.If you happen to really want to be able to dig a hole big enough for this entire pod rather than a tiny spot for a small seed, you may be happy in the end - the plants have emerged so there is actually a seed in there.  It hasn't been long enough to see how the plants perform, but at least there's a seed in there!  I'll update this if the rating should change significantly based on how the plant continues to grow.With all that said, I wouldn't personally buy or recommend these.  Some peat pots and packet of seeds gives you more variety and options.  Top Rated seed companies like Territorial Seed Company, High Mowing Seeds, Seed Savers Exchange and others provide much more for a lesser cost.  You likely have an alternate seed company in your region that specializes in seeds that grow in your conditions, as well - rather than a very large company selling seeds that "work anywhere" (and aren't ideal anywhere) or that may not be best suited for you.
summary: Interesting idea, but only for lazy "gardeners"

reviewText: I have planted these in the backyard and time will tell what success will come of this.  The kit comes with 18 seed pots for easy growing but some of these plants need to grow indoors before planting outside.  Checking the growing distance means that some of these can't be planted close together or there will be too much crowding.  Basically garden space needs to be taken into account along with good soil preparation.  This also includes getting the snail and slug bait out or there won't be anything left to grow.  Price is high for what you get.  Some plants in the kit I normally wouldn't grow and for me tomato plants are faster to get starts from the local nursery.  Unless you have a long growing season, time is a large factor here.  This makes growing the seeds inside or green housing more important.  If you have the season and want to watch things grow from seed this will work but I can't really recommend this kit.Addendum Dec. 12, 2013.  Now that the summer is over and the growing season is past, I can definitely say that this garden kit is not worth buying.  Especially if it is grown out in the garden.  My seed pots didn't properly germinated and I only got a few sprouts.  Most of these quickly died or got eaten and only the beans came up.  If you can grow these indoors they may do better.  Better yet greenhouse them where there is better climate control. Either way this kit is way to expensive for what you get.
summary: Verdict is in on the success of this Garden Kit

reviewerName: Gertrude, the Innocent "Live well, laugh loud...
reviewText: In order for me to grow anything in my food garden, I pretty much need to get the stupid proof started plants from the nursery.  I can grow anything flowers but a vegetable planted in my garden is pretty much an invitation to die.This is a great collection of vegetables and some herbs, the perfect beginning for any salad.  I wish I had been smart enough to use the pull off stickers to make a map of where I put stuff.  On the other hand, one spin and they would all be lost again.I purchased 5 Apollo Plastics H012-MOCHA 12-Inch Self-Watering, hoping to be able to put them in my windowsill by the time the first frost arrives to have a year round vegetable garden in my actual greenhouse window above my sink in the kitchen.  Now you would think that is a pretty safe place for a plant to live, it being that close to a water source AND a hose.  This is where the stupid proof part actually comes in.In my defense, I don't actually have to water anything outdoors. Our summertime 75% standard humidity - to 90% on any given day - occasionally explodes into rain.Anyway, these were planted in hanging planters outside on a rainy day and they are hanging in the section of garden my husband tends so they have a much better chance of survival.Until then, I am off to the Farmer's Market.

These are very easy to plant.  Each pod says a minimum of 2 seeds.  You just take the label off of each pod and put them in the soil.
