The directions say that you don't have to cover them with soil, but I recommend covering them with a thin layer because when you water them, the contents stay in place better if there is a thin layer of soil over them.All of the pods that I planted seem to be growing well, I will have to update when the plants get bigger.  If you just want a small garden, this is the way to go.  Everything you need is in the little pod.  I actually used some of these in my container gardens.

The idea is cool, but...it is a lot of packaging for a micro garden.And this IS a micro garden, and not a particularly well chosen one.  The size is only appropriate for someone planting a single raised bed/flower bed or a pot-based garden for their deck or balcony.  With that said, it really would only serve to raise enough for a salad now and again.  I think the idea would be more attractive in a "salsa" or herbs alone collection rather than this salad version.
summary: A lot of packaging for a microgarden

reviewText: I thought this would be a fun idea to make a tiny winter garden indoors. We have a lovely warm sunny spot that is just perfect. So I got some nice planters and planted the seed pods. I read the directions and followed them carefully. I have actually gardened for years but this is the first time I have tried a ready made garden.Only 1/2 of my pods sprouted and one of the sprouted guys looks like he is not long for the world. So there are huge gaps in my planter but these little seedlings aren't exactly hardy enough to move. It is a very fun idea and might be a good way to introduce gardening to kids or adults that don't have room for a full garden. But I have had much better luck just dropping seeds in the ground and hoping the birds don't eat them.
summary: I guess I have a black thumb

reviewText: You're paying for the convenience of having a pre-packed assortment of future edible plants, complete with fertilizer. You plant these pods in soil (in your garden or in a pot) and wait. Since I just planted mine, I won't have results for a while, so I'll write an update here when I get results (or if I don't get them). For now, I would say it's a little expensive and involves a lot of fancy packaging, but it's the price of a shortcut. A the same time, fertilizer is included, and you get variety.Price per pod: $1.50 each.
summary: Sort of pricey, but nice setup

reviewText: This was a great project for my son and I. The little pods were fun and easy to use. We planted everything indie by a sunny window in planter boxes. My son enjoyed opening them up and putting them in the soil. He liked that even after they were planted he could tell where the pods were and knew where to watch for sprouts. It has been a few weeks and things are really starting to grow, even indoors!While I do not think this is a kit for a serious gardner, it is great for a newbie or an experimenter.

We couldn't get these to work much at all. The idea is that the pod is a self-contained herb garden starter kit, including the seed and fertilizer in one. This seemed like a great idea, and as we have had limited success in the past with gardens, we were excited to try this. We had very limited success even after trying to follow the instructions for water, shade, and the appropriate zone (we live in Phoenix, AZ and it is summer).Despite watering according to the recommended schedule, we had very little germination and those that did promptly died. I'm no garden expert, but it seemed like everything just dried out. I wonder if I just needed more than the recommended watering due to the hot and dry climate in Arizona. But it seemed to me that the pod may have actually limited the amount of water that was able to be absorbed and kept in the soil around the seeds.Guess I really don't have a green thumb. I'll just keep going to the grocery store. Too bad, cause I was pretty excited about this.
summary: Seemed to Dry Out Without Germination; I Guess I Do Not Have a Green Thumb

reviewText: I am a home gardener and we grow more than we can eat every year. I wanted to try this kit for the novelty of it. I think this would be a great kit for people with arthritis and teaching kids to garden with visual results. Most the packaging can be recycled, it comes in a box with paper instructions and a paper ruler for spacing (nice touch). The pods themselves come in a foil type package that keeps light and moisture out for long shelf life and better germination chances. A 1oz packet of plant food pellets. Feeds for three months. The pods are about 2 1/2 inches tall and 3 inches wide. Each pod is labeled with how far it should be from its neighbor. The pods are biodegradable, under their label is planting instructions and tips. The longest harvest date is 75 days and that is the sweet pepper. I live in Midwest with mixed weather ranging from super hot days and cold nights and everything in between, I put a small cage around my peppers and garden fabric or bubble wrap with top open. The extra heat really give them a growing burst and protects from whipping winds. Instructions say after 30 days apply the included pellet food, it will last 3 months.Each pod has its own start fertilizer, it really is plant and grow, just water often and keep the weeds down. Since you don't bury the lips of the pods I had a few wash up in heavy rain, I then put straw on top and haven't had issue since, plus straw helps keep even moisture.  Everything is growing, nothing to eat yet so will update at end of season.update 11/13We ended up with tomatoes, peppers, cucumbers, and herbs. The lettuce never did grow, I think we should have watered it more. I would be willing to try a whole herb garden this way.

This kit is great and very easy to use.  It comes with 18 seed pods that are ready to plant. You just dig the holes in your garden and place the pods in the ground. There is also some miracle gro to place on the ground after they have been planted awhile. It includes everything you need to start and plant these except water. It also gives some tips on planting and a little paper ruler to measure between plants to make sure you are planting them the correct distance apart.  Just plant, water, and wait to grow. Lots of good plants to make a great salad.

I received my Garden Kit late in the year.  Not an ideal time for planting but I already had a garden in place and I had some space not being used so I gave it a shot.  Sometimes we don't get a good frost until way late in the year so I felt like it was worth the risk.The kit is a little too "cutesy" for me and I think this is geared more to first time gardeners who really don't want to fuss with all decisions and picking out of seeds... etc.That aside there is nothing wrong with this type of product and I think it's a great intro to gardening because it takes a lot of guess-work out of the equation.I did feel that the information wasn't ideal planting times and the like.  A first time gardener is going to need clear concise information on different times to plant in different growing zones, and they basically tell you to go figure that stuff out, they should have had that covered for a first timer.The seed pods are easy to plant with good direction on how much space to give them.  All you do is place them in and water.Most of the items I planted have sprouted, some aren't up yet but it's still pretty early in the game.  So bonus points there.  They sprouted pretty quickly and so I think this is also really good for the beginner gardener... instant gratification that they have done everything right.I'm giving it 4 stars for beginner gardeners but for seasoned gardeners I'd probably only give it 3 stars because there aren't many seeds for the $$$ and you could easily duplicate this mix on your own for less money per seed/soil as this kit and you'd get a lot more yield.  Maybe not as much variety though.
summary: good for a beginner gardener, a "sampler" garden.

reviewText: First, as part of the Vine program, I received these late in the season. Although one may think growing anything in Florida would be easy, it's anything but...ridiculously high heat combined with absurdly high humidity makes plants wilt away if they even manage to get started. Sadly, that seemed to be the case wit these...either that or they were much older than I realized. In any respect, I really like the idea behind these. Rather than comparing to planting by seed, I compare it more to using starters...at least in cost, it makes this much more feasible. The salad and herb garden is nice although I'd probably prefer more herb selections and less salad. As others have noted, a single pepper or tomato plant is cute but not sufficient. On the other hand, one can never have too many herbs! In any respect, these are super easy, very convenient and an overall great idea. I'd be inclined to try them again especially with a wider variety of pods to select from. Why only three starts? Germination rate left a lot to be desired but again, I suspect that is due to the weather here in Florida this time of the year although I can't be totally sure.
summary: Great idea but so so execution

reviewText: As some reviewers have mentioned there is not much in the way of yield to this small gardening tool, but it is fun and a good to get your feet wet in gardening.  It seems more like a science kit to get someone started.  It is fun and it avoids much of the mess of gardening.  No it is not going to replace many trips to the grocery store, but its concept has some merit, primarily to get more folks involved in raising their own vegetables.

This Miracle-Gro kit is designed to get beginners up and running with a small garden... it contains a variety of vegetables and herbs, which grow from seed pods. The pods are meant to take the guesswork out of positioning/planting seeds, and there is built-in plant food to help nourish the seedlings. The package comes with a guidebook about planting and caring for the plants, and this is easy to read and follow.The challenges here are typically weather/climate (seeds often don't germinate if the climate conditions or season aren't appropriate). Thus, some of these plants might not grow easily in your area, which makes the kit with so many different plants not the best idea if it's meant for beginners. The cost is somewhat high compared to buying seed packs individually and planting them on your own. This kit makes it easy and perhaps fun to get started, but some people may become disappointed if the results don't match expectations. This is nice as a kit to explore gardening as a new hobby, though it has some drawbacks and would not be well-suited to a seasoned gardener who can select seeds and prepare the soil more specifically than Miracle-Gro can do with this kit.It's great that Miracle-Gro is trying to make gardening simple for novices, though the concept may not work as well as desired when put into practice. I am OK with this kit so far, but I would encourage people looking to start gardening to just pick seeds that grow easily in their area at the time of the year they hope to plant.
summary: A kit for novices to jump-start their gardening effort

reviewText: This kit is easy...super easy. Good for children and beginners, but it sure is spendy. You can buy a boat load of seeds and top soil with the same results. But a burning question is why California won't allow it?
summary: Good for a Beginner or Children

reviewText: I have to confess that my primary criticism of this product is one that I knew existed before it arrived. Since this kit is manufactured and sold by Miracle-Gro (part of the Scotts lawn fertilizer company) I knew the seed pods would, of course, contain Miracle-Gro fertilizer.Why does the fertilizer bother me? First, I've been a gardener since I was a kid and a serious backyard gardener (as an adult) for more than 20 years. I know how to grow vegetables and flowers. And I admit that, 15 or 20 years ago, I happily used Miracle-Gro products. But the more that I talked to farmers and other gardeners the more I shifted over to organic gardening--and for many reasons, not just a blind fear of chemistry. Hey, table salt is a chemical, but I eat it every day. But fertilizers like Miracle-Gro have two problems: for one, they work on a feast-or-famine feeding schedule. When you water the plants (at least with the liquid form, less so with time-released capsules) you essentially soak the plants in food. Then they wait two weeks for the next feeding--and they stress more and more as their food source diminishes. Feeding plants organically (primarily with compost or other organic foods such as chicken manure or seaweed) provides a continuous supply of food. Does this matter that much for your backyard tomatoes and lettuce? Truthfully, probably not. For farmers it's a different story, but for a backyard garden, perhaps not so much.A far more immediate and bigger concern is the ingredients of the fertilizers. I am not a chemist and make no pretense to know much about most of the chemicals in Miracle-Gro, but I can't even pronounce half of the laundry list of things found in this fertilizer (and included in these pods), so why would you or I want to ingest that? Look up Ammonium nitrate for example sometime--do you really want to eat that? If you grow your food in it, guess what, it's in your body.OK, that all said. This product is a great concept in terms of planting design. I give them credit for creating a simple, effective and easy system for planting seeds. Tiny seeds are a pain to deal with and you (or, at least, I) end up wasting a lot and planting them in less than an orderly way. These pods solve that problem and that is the ONLY reason that I give the product three stars. All that you have to do is dig a little hole, peel the top off of the pod and stick it in the ground and water it. How great! I start most of my seeds indoors in winter (I'm in New England, starting seeds in February keeps you from jumping off the roof into the snow), but there are some things like lettuce and herbs that will be fun to start directly this way.But why not make these organic??? That's that part I don't get. Why poison your own food? There are organic foods that can be used in a product like this. Read about products like:Jobe's 6028 50-Pack Organic Vegetable Fertilizer Food SpikesBut more importantly, your seeds don't need fertilizer to germinate! In fact, it's very likely the fertilizer will end up burning the roots. Nature gives the seeds all of the energy they need to germinate: all they need (depending on the seed) is water, soil and light--and all three of those aren't always necessary. If these seed pods contained only seeds and a bit of composted manure, they'd be ideal.I am, however, growing these pods. I don't want to contaminate my organic beds (I grow primarily in 4x12' raised beds made from untreated lumber--treated lumber contains arsenic, you do NOT want to eat that), so I'm going to grow these in containers just to see how they do. I will try to remember to update this review just to comment on how they grow.So, three stars for an interesting concept, but please, read about the chemistry before you resort to ingesting it via your foods. I'm not some new-aged anti-chemistry person who has been sold a bill of organic goods. It took me years and many long conversations and the reading of many books to devote my energies to organic gardening, but I'm convinced that many of the rampant diseases today, including things things like ADD, are the result of the chemicals in our foods. I'm an experienced gardener who grows by the motto taught to me by one of Connecticut's oldest organic gardeners: "Take care of the soil and it will take care of you."
summary: An interesting planting concept, tragic that it's not organic

reviewerName: Jeri Zerr "formerly a Road Warrior of the Nth...
reviewText: I very much appreciate the seeds in the Miracle-Gro garden kit are GMO-free, so I added a star.  Otherwise, the Miracle Grow Salad and Herb kit would be a 2 star kit ... or zero stars with GMO seeds.First of all, I'm concerned this kit is NOT for sale in California... makes me wonder why, my first guess is the fertilizer must have a chemical known to be cancer inducing in California (seems like EVERYTHING is known to cause cancer in California, what about the rest of us?!).. but this is not confirmed, in fact I could not find ANY information on the included fertilizer.The pods have begun germinating just fine for me, during an unusually pleasant Midwest summer. During a drought or shortage of rainfall these pods will need to be kept damp with a fine mist so as not to dislodge the seeds from the pods.The pods are fine for an educational experiment for children.  However, personally I would buy the seed packets (and at this price GMO-free heirloom seed packets sound like a great investment!) and plant a few extra seeds to accommodate for the (possibly) lower germination rates. Both the seed pods as well as seed packets should be refrigerated prior to planting to give the seeds a "cold" season for better germination.  The pods are rather large so will take up considerable fridge space during this process.
summary: Maybe good for educational purposes, not practical nor cost effective at all.

reviewText: I've done a little gardening in the past. Not much, but I've grown a few things in a few square feet in my backyard. If you've ever done the same, I'd skip this product altogether and go straight for seeds or starts. They're MUCH cheaper (a single 99-cent seed packet might contain as many individual seeds as this entire kit), and you don't need to buy a set of 13 different plants that you may or may not even like. While this kit does simplify a few steps, there's nothing difficult about putting a seed in the ground. And while gardening is wonderful, I feel that kits like this just serve to distance people from the experience that much more. Add to that the questionability of the fertilizers added (I prefer something a little more natural), the "California won't let us sell this manufactured product there", a little "only 94% biodegradable" (what else is in there that WON'T decompose in my soil?), and the questionable safety record of the Scotts Miracle-Gro company (they eventually admitted to poisoning bird seed they sold with pesticides highly toxic to birds). Not a recipe for success.Anyway, I'd suggest starting with something less commercial. Maybe a packet of seeds (or twenty, which will give you ~50 times the growing potential of this kit, and still likely be cheaper). Or a 4-pack of tomatoes for a couple bucks. Tomatoes are good.
summary: I'm not impressed, but I suppose some might like it.

reviewText: I received this kit the other day and no it's not planted yet but it will be this weekend. As they progress, or die I'll update this review. But I wanted to provide some immediate feedback on the cost and what you receive.The kit itself is packaged in a foil sleeve to keep it from getting moist, you tear it open and  pull out the seed pods which are all in a cardboard holder. Overall the initial impression is good. The price of the kit as of me writing this is at $18, and for that you are getting 18 "plants" (actually seed pods). If you were to go to the grocery store and buy cilantro plant it's going to cost you around $3 or so for a fresh little one. So if you bought all 18 plants grown you would be looking around $54 at least. Now you are paying for convenience as they plants are already grown. But you don't know how they were raised, what pesticides if any, etc. The beauty of this kit is in it's simplicity. You plant the pods and water and let them grow. It contains the food and soil it needs to get started so you don't have to think about it. I like that.Initial impressions are "I like it." I do wish it was a bit cheaper, but when you compare the costs its really not too bad. More to come as the planting of the plants starts.
summary: For $1 a plant its not a bad deal

reviewerName: Joel Avrunin "Electrical Engineer who loves S...
reviewText: Having recently had my kids grow a bunch of vegetables from seeds they purchased, I can attest it is not incredibly difficult.  They dug little holes, threw in the seeds, and watered regularly.  I was wondering if these Miracle-Gro seed pods could be an easier solution that would grow better.  The idea here is that each pod contains fertilizer and a seed to help in germinating the plant quickly.  I thought we could germinate the seeds indoors and then transfer them outside.  First, if this is your plan, make sure you remember what each pod contains.  My kids, in an effort to be helpful, removed all of the labels.  There is no labeling on the pod itself, so once you remove the top label, you need to know what's there.  Second, I tried germinating them inside, but the pod itself started to disintegrate surprisingly quickly.I transported the seeds outside and no surprise, some of them grew and some did not.  There's not much redundancy in the pods, just one or two seeds, so if it fails to germinate you are out of luck.This is a cool idea, but for the price, I'd recommend just buying some seeds and planting them - it's not as hard as it looks.
summary: Seed pods seem okay, but really not a major improvement over just buying seeds

reviewText: I'm just getting into some light gardening and these pods really hit the spot. They come with a planting chart (as far as when to plant and how far apart). The seed are already planted in each pod according to the desired depth, etc. so all you really do is loosen up the soil, plant the pod, water and watch the plants grow. It really couldn't have been much easier.

I think the idea of this is greatand deserves 5 stars. It would make a great gift, especially to abeginning gardener. I really like the selection of vegetables andherbs that it includes. It is a perfect assortment. It would have beennice if the package or product page contained some pictures for ideason arranging the pods in a container and maybe a picture of a fullsize garden using this set of pods. It seemed like there could havebeen a few more helpful tips, but maybe there really isn't much to add.

This set of grow-pods would be a nice educational product for teaching a child about plant growth and basic gardening.  The pods are easy to plant and care for.I thought the set would work well for me because most of my gardening is container gardening.  And I am having limited success.  Some of the pots have made nice little seedlings, healthy and doing well.One of the advantages of this set is that the seeds are supposed to be planted at the right depth in the pot.  I have a tendency to plant too deeply when I use plain seeds.  But I had seeds showing at the top of both my tomato and bean pods.It would be nice if there were a more complete gardening guide included.  The pots come with a lid that can be peeled back to show additional information, but at least half of those I opened stuck together, and then tore so as to obliterate the information.  Not helpful.Only one bean pod is just silly.  I had one bean sprout come up, and the top was promptly eaten by some garden-invading critter.  That is not the fault of the set, but there goes my whole bean crop.The salad and herb kit really doesn't work as such.  They can't all be planted at the same time because, for instance, tomatoes are not going to be happy planted during the cool weather the lettuce wants.  Even if all could be planted at the same time, they wouldn't mature at the same time.  I planted some of the warm weather pods but the rest have to wait.Even for my small container gardening, I think I am better off buying packets of seeds for the items like lettuce and beans, and buying small tomato and pepper plants.  So, consider this for a first garden for a child, but not so much if you want a real garden.

I live in an apartment, which has a small deck.  I've always wanted to grow something out there - and these things have been a great opportunity to try it!  So far - these little things have been great!  I bought some pots and soil, and planted some of these to see how they'd do.  It's pretty idiot proof: you just peel off the top label (which isn't all that easy, actually), and stick them in the soil.  Water and wait.  I get crazy sun on my deck, this being Texas and it being summer, so I check every day to see that the soil is moist.  I planted the snap peas which grew, and the romaine lettuce, which has yet to blossom.  Still - it's interesting and fun to check on these and hopefully they will grow into something stable and edible!  I think it's a real neat idea and fairly idiot-proof.  I'm a little concerned that the romaine has yet to grow - but that could be operator error on my part.  If these, and others, continue to work for me I'll kick this up to five stars.  It's a fun option for beginner "garderners" like myself!
summary: Great idea for someone with limited space who wants to grow stuff!!!

reviewText: Miracle-Gro 170025 Gro-ables Salad and Herb Garden Kit, 18 Seed PodsI'm an experienced organic gardener, but when all one wants is to plant a simple vegetable/herb garden, selecting vegetable and herb seeds, soil, fertilizer, peat pots for starting (some plants) indoors -- and remembering to fertilize -- etc. can be a daunting experience -- so many choices, so many things to do -- and, it can be quite time consuming.reads highlights of the Miracle-Gro 170025 Gro-ables Salad and Herb Garden Kit, 18 Seed Pods:* An entire garden, in one simple kit! Includes 18 Seed PodsSalad Garden1 Globe Tomato1 Cherry Tomato1 Cucumber1 Bush Bean2 Loose-Leaf Lettuce2 Butterhead Lettuce1 Romaine Lettuce1 Snap Pea1 Smooth-Leaf Spinach1 Sweet Pepper Plus, the Herb Garden2 Basil2 Cilantro2 Dill* Each ready-to-plant Seed Pod contains everything seeds need to grow* Specially selected non-GMO seed, placed at the proper depth* Slow release plant food gradually delivers essential nutrition to promote root developmentOkay, I'll try it! Into my Shopping Cart it goes! :)Quick and Easy! 1st, select a nice sunny spot for your plants to reside.  after amending the space with enriched garden soil, just dig a small hole in the soil (planter, garden, flower bed et al) with digging tool, tear top off vegetable or herb pod, place in hole, cover with a small amount of dirt, tamp soil gently with gloved hands, water. Keep watered and wait for vegetable and herb plants to emerge from soil.  That's it! :)  *sips espresso*Everything one needs is already in the peat pod - except the surrounding soil, water and sunshine.There is a handy paper spacing ruler on back of packaging band to help with spacing of seed pods.  The fold out instruction pamphlet is extremely useful, and loaded with tips and tricks. ...even includes a Fresh herb Vinaigrette recipe one can quickly make and enjoy over home grown vegetable salad.Some vegetables need to be started indoors, and then planted outdoors.  Not a big deal, just an extra step to insure that that particular plant safely emerges into this world!  The cardboard pod holder makes a wonderful stand for starting indoors.  Just leave pods in place, place stand in waterproof dish (like an old cookie sheet with sides), peel off seed pod label, water.I found that the peel off tops of the pods (info labels) are laminated (to a certain extent) and can be used as plant markers -- so one knows what-is-where.  I used wooden chopsticks and just threaded label onto the stick and stuck it in the soil beside the planted pod.  Even after a couple of torrential rains I am still able to read the label.In less than a week, my cucumber and bush bean had emerged, I kid You not! :)Does the Miracle-Gro Gro-ables Salad and Herb Garden Kit sound like what you may be looking for? :)  Would make a Fantastic Gift, or project!  Highly Recommended!  --Katharena Eiermann, 2013

Miracle Gro really has a great idea here with the Gro-Ables Salad and Herb Garden.  Each pod contains seed, growing mix, and plant food, so all you need to do is stick it in the ground and water.  Each cup of dirt and seed is like a compostable K-Cup. However, you're really paying a lot for the cost of "semi-convenience" here.Buying the starts for a globe tomato, cherry tomato, cucumber, pepper, basil, cilantro, and dill will probably set you back anywhere between $7-21 at a nursery, BUT you'll be guaranteed a live plant that is a couple of weeks old.  You'll also get more varieties of some of the plants (such as heirloom tomatoes like Yellow Jubilee, Black Krim, etc).  Also, you can bypass buying plants you simple won't use.  I personally have no use for dill or cilantro, and would rather grow a yellow variety of tomato instead of the cherry tomato.Some of the plants listed here simply need more than a single plant to do well/yield well.  A single bush bean will not feed a single person, let alone a family.  Five heads of lettuce won't last long either.  That said, the bush bean, lettuce varieties, snap pea and spinach plants just don't make sense to have as single plants.  You'd be better off spending the buck each to buy full packages of these seeds to plant yourself.  You'll be ahead of the game in case one of the seeds in the Miracle Gro batch doesn't sprout.  Offhand, the Miracle Grow pea I planted faired about as well as the full package of peas I planted in the garden.That said, yes, this set does offer an almost fail-proof method of growing your own food.  If given the choice however, I would sooner purchase starts, or full packages of seeds instead of paying for the convenience of these seeds.  You'll have more variety, a good jump start with starters, and better luck with a seed in a cup of dirt - and if that seed should fail, at least you'll have a package more to test with.
summary: Great Those Just Starting in Gardening - But Expensive!

reviewText: Seriously...two seeds (at least) per pot? They'd better be some darn good seeds! That aside, I can only report.on the planting experience, which was pretty nifty.I haven't had the best experience growing veggies from seed so I decided that I wasn't going to try anymore. Then I saw these pods from MiracleGro and my interest was revived. I can't imagine an easier way to plant except for paying someone else to do it for you.Simple instructions and everything all ready to go in the ground make quick work of the job.I'll let you know how it works out.

I am a novice gardener. I've grown tomato plants from seedlings but not much else. I get way too distracted to give them the daily devotion for watering and care. We also live in the woods and the deer munch on our yard daily. So I decided to try in 'indoor' garden. This is a great way to start a garden, even when the start of the growing season is slightly off.There are 18 seed pods, some are repeats, with a wide variety of seeds. They are really easy to plant after preparing soil. Just remove the top and push the pot in. They require daily (gentle) watering and it is recommended to remove all but one 2" seedling from each pod growth. The kit comes with some basic directions and a small portion of Shake 'n Feed plus Calcium fertilizer.Seeds will take from 40-75 days before they can be harvested, depending on the vegetable (and how well you take care of them!).My daughter was really excited to start working with this. I see it as a great way to encourage a child or gardening newbie to try their hand, especially since it is so easy to start.
summary: A Cute Way to Try Beginner Gardening

reviewText: Just received these today July 27th. The instructions are great this couldn't be easier to follow. Mine are in Earthbox containers that I always grow veggies in but had not this  year. I filled with good container mix pushed the pods in after removing the top. You have to water gently the first time so I used a small hand sprinkler. They are in full sun but 2 full months late going in. This may be a review of just ease of planting and not salad on plate but one never knows. I will be back when there is anything to report.August 5, 2013 UPDATE all the pods are growing about an inch tall now I am surprised and delighted. It is still way late in the season but it proves it is an easy set to plant and they do grow.
summary: I am very late in testing this set I will have to come back in Sept. to update.

reviewText: What a fun little kit to get you into everything you need to start gardening. With prices going up and pay going down it's time to find ways to save yourself some $. This i a fool proof way to start you off in gardening very easy to use starter pods will have you reaping some useful product.Very happy with the end results and look forward to planting the rest of them when the season starts next year.

These are individual pods of seeds.  Each pod is to be a part of your herb and salad garden; there's dill, basil, tomato, peas, etc. Well, it's cute in theory but nothing grew. I had a couple of the tomato seeds sprout but they died a short time later. I had thought you start them inside in these pods and then transplant outside but you're suppose to plant the whole pod in the garden right from the start. The pods dry out quickly so you do have to water everyday. Once the seeds sprout you then pull out the extra seedlings leaving only one or two to let grow. It's very difficult to pull seedlings out by the roots without disturbing the other seedlings since all the seeds were dropped right in the middle of the pod. Just go buy packets and do it yourself. This was toooo much trouble.
summary: It didn't grow....a tomato plant I think

reviewText: I planted these a month ago- I live in New Mexico.. The herbs are growing, the tomatoes are but the lettuce didn't grow.. My expiration date was 8/30/13 so I was close to that date, so not giving a horrible review based on that- Was easy to grow and plant.. Instructions easy to follow- Put in soil and wait about two weeks to see growth- Water as instructed- I think next summer I might give these a try again if the price is right.. Easy to follow.. Hopefully we won't get a early freeze and I will get full use out of my vegis

So far, so good.  I just planted the pods and won't know if I have "success" for about 60 days, but I'm optimistic!I have brown thumbs.  I usually by starts and bring them along, not seeds.  These pods are a cross between seeds and starters.What I like best about this is how easy it is to use, and I mean EASY.  The most frustrating thing about beginning to try to garden is that everyone else seems to "know" how to plant thigs.  The tiny directions on the packet of normal seeds are of no use, and gardening books assume I already "know" how to do basic gardening.  This product has the seeds in disintegrating containers, pointy on the bottom.  Plant in the container, the pointy container makes it easy to get the right depth.  The directions that come with the kit are so very easy.  A chart, a ruler, a booklet... there is NO GUESSING AT ALL about how to plant this stuff. I KNOW I did it right.I'll post an update in a few months...let you know if the seeds were good, and grew.  All I know for now is that if they don't grow, it wasn't because I didn't plant them correctly!Recommended so far!UPDATE:  Fall is here, we've had our frost.  Garden is done.  How did these perform?  Well, I've got a brown thumb, and not much of my garden did very well.  However, I only had one container of these "work."  The rest grew, and then stopped a little past the seedling stage.  I'm not sure if my soil wasn't good enough, but looking at the ground now -- you can still see the containers.  I live in a very dry climate, and we had to water 2x a day.  Not sure if it works well elsewhere, but I won't be getting these again unless I do some containers inside or something.... bummer, I really wanted these to work.
summary: So far so good - but an update

reviewText: This is a kit that includes vegetable and herb seeds (cold AND warm weather which did make me wonder), pods, and soil mix. It is expensive, so if you're into saving money and want to grow your own vegetables, this is probably not the route you want to go.I got this kit because of the Miracle-Gro name. MG is a great product, but anyone who's seriously gardened in the past will not like this kit.It's so simple and simplistic, I think it might be best for kids or someone who has never gardened before.
This is a very clever little kit - very easy to use, with a nice selection of seeds.  Overall it is incredibly convenient and easy, but quite expensive for what you get.

Easy to Use, ideal for Kids, Beginners or limited space.  My first thought I had when I saw these pods were for a container garden.  I've seen so many inspiring gardening ideas on Pinterest that I thought I'd give it a shot.  I've started the spices in little pots and I'm going to make some sort of wall or fence hanging. reviewText: These seed pods are designed to make gardening simple, even for those with a black thumb.  You open the packets, plant, and water.  Keep moist while germinating and presto, you have plants.  Each pod contains seeds, growing medium, and fertilizer.  A separate fertilizer also came with the set. These pods can be started indoors and planted outside, a good idea if insects tend to attack seedlings.  While these would be cost prohibitive in a large plot, these are ideal for a small plot, container gardening, and as a project for children.  We planted these after our last average frost day (mid May in the midwest).  There was germination in each pod (within 10 days) and growth looks promising.  We glued the labels for each pod to a Popsicle stick and used them as markers.  So far, everything looks good.  I have some conventionally started seedlings and it will be interesting to see how growth between the two compare.
summary: Nice for the patio gardener or for gardening with children

reviewText: The Miracle-Gro 170025 Gro-ables Salad and Herb Garden Kit reminds me of a cross between those chemistry sets we used to have as kids in the '60s and those Kuerig coffee packs that are all the rage these days.The kit is sealed inside aluminum wrap and at first glance looks like something one might want to bake. It contains 18 seeded peat pots and a dozen different vegetables and herbs. There are extras of the herbs and lettuces to allow for staggered and companion plantings (still too much dill here for my tastes, though).The selling point is ease, convenience, and instructions. Put the Kuerig-like pods into a container, raised bed, or garden; space the plants as directed; water them; thin seedlings and transplant extras when possible; fend off the various critters that will come to enjoy your work; and let the sun and rain do the rest save for weeding and feeding.It's almost everything one needs for a garden, and it makes the planting process quite easy.The growing process, however, is another matter. I've heard and read the idea of putting a 50 cent plant in a five dollar hole more than a few times. If you have not prepped your soil with amendments for drainage, air, and nutrition, then you plants may lose their initial enthusiasm after sprouting and either be stunted or just die. Keeping them feed and pest free is vital, so learning about fertilizers and companion planting with other herbs and flowers should be the next step. Light and drainage and soil depth are also important.My point is just that aspiring gardeners may think the whole process is a bit simpler than the reality of getting from seeds to harvest. The presentation of this kit suggests a science experiment more than a horticultural exercise to me. So it is a great way to get started---but what's here needs to be augmented by trying things out and learning more about the whole process of growing vegetables and herbs.Meanwhile, I will be seeing how my plants do in the coming weeks and hoping the various bugs and chipmunks leave something for the table.  I learn something from every garden and am still trying to figure out what killed my tomato plants in my other raised bed that were poised to deliver my first-ever fruits by July 4th.Update: It is September, and as I look back, I have to say this garden kit failed to produce. Pretty much everthing we planted either died despite plenty of water and light or was consumed by squirrels and chipmunks who must have found the little peat cups full of seedlings to be tasteful appetizers. I think the term failure to thrive applies.
summary: Failure to thrive---worse than I originally thought

reviewText: This is a cute idea, but really, is quite pitiful. You only get a couple of seeds packed into each tiny peat pod.The kit is great for getting your feet wet in the world of planting with seeds but don't expect to grow anything resembling a plentiful herb and veggie garden with this tiny little kit.For the price I have to say Miracle-Gro could have done A LOT better. Nice idea, poor execution. Your money would be much better spent buying seeds and soil (or if you like the idea of the peat pods, some empty pods and a few seed packets would yield a lot more herbs and veggies for a lot less money). I really wanted to love this product but I just can't recommend it. Very disappointing.
summary: More of a science project than an herb garden

reviewText: I enjoy gardening.  I plant A LOT of different crops and when I have pest problems or nutrient problems, I feel comfortable enough to find answers online.  When something dies prematurely, I view it more of a learning experience and feel better prepared for the next planting season.This product is an interesting concept - I can't help but smile when I look at it.  Inside the foil packaging is a 14" (L) x 8" (W) x 2" (H) cardboard container that opens up to display 18 ready to plant pods.  The literature is simple and tastefully done.  They include plant spacing (with a paper ruler), recipes, tips for growing, and websites for additional information.  You basically take the cover off of the biodegradable pods (there is more nutrient literature under each paper lid - I was unable to view this as my paper lids stuck together), push the pod into your soil, and then remember to water.  You could plant most of the pods indoors (close to a light source) or outdoors.  You could also plant in pots or right into ground that has been properly tilled.The variety of vegetable and herbs provided with this kit are the "easy to grow" varieties.  You'll receive Basil, Cilantro, Dill, several varieties of Lettuce and 2 different Tomatoes, a Snap Pea pod, Cucumber pod, and a Bush Bean pod.  Basically, you provide adequate water and it grows.  Each pod has Miracle-Gro plant food in the tip of the pod and at least 2 seeds in each pod.  If you get more than one seedling in each pod (and you probably will), you could carefully separate the seedling but for the novice gardener, it would be easier to simply pull out the weaker/smaller seedlings once the strongest seedling is at least 2" high.  You're guaranteed to have a plant grow - They claim satisfaction guaranteed or your money back.  I suspect more information is available on-line to exercise the guarantee (there was nothing specific in the included literature).I couldn't help but think that kids would LOVE this product.  What a great Birthday present for the child who has a Spring Birthday - Seed Pods that just need pushed into soil and perhaps some small gardening tools.It's a cute product but if you're an experienced gardener - I rather doubt you'd see any economical benefit in this product.  Seeds are incredibly cheap and even if you were to plant each of the varieties in this kit with seedlings bought from a nursery, you'd likely pay less than what this kit costs (and the seedlings would produce a fruit/vegetable faster since it's weeks ahead of a newly planted pod).
summary: Rather Expensive But Might Be GREAT For The New Gardener Or To Introduce Children To Gardening

reviewText: I'm a gardener and for the last several years I have been practicing the "art" of gardening with varying degrees of success.  I buy heirloom seed and raise my seedlings before planting which for me, is fun but still work.  I wanted to try out these seed cups by Miracle-Gro and so far I kind of like them. I won't be changing to these from what I've been doing, but for someone who has a very small area to grow vegetables/herbs or just want a small patio garden I think this is a great way to accomplish that.You won't be raising a large garden with numerous plants of each kind, but you will get a small sampling of some fairly popular vegetable garden plants.  I'm sure the seed used in these seed cups are NOT heirloom, so I wouldn't bother trying to save any to use the following year because they most likely will not produce any vegetables.  Plants yes, but no produce.  And I wouldn't mix them with plants that are heirloom if you're planning on saving any seeds because they will cross pollinate and could sabotage your heirlooms.However, for children, school classroom projects, or the micro gardener I think these are perfect.  They are very easy to plant, I just made a small hole in one of my raised beds and pushed the entire container into it after peeling off the lid. Sprinkle with some water and wait.  It's too early yet to report on the quality of the produce, but so far I have only planted the herbs. I already have a lot of the other type plants growing and don't want to risk cross pollination. I always get excited when I see the new plant babies breaking the surface of the soil - never gets old for me!I'm looking forward to some fresh herbs though, and each seed cup will produce several seedlings.  I don't like to waste seedlings so I carefully separate them and replant.  Most people will choose one or two of the healthiest seedlings and discard the remaining ones, but I like to give everybody a chance if I have the room.  I think these seed cups are an excellent way to introduce gardening to children and for those who just want to start out with something very easy and not much of it.  Some plant food granules are included along with very good instructions.4.19.14 UPDATEThe plant pots I planted never amounted to anything, and this year while getting my raised bed ready for new plantings I found a pot I planted from last year with it's seeds still in it, buried underneath the soil that didn't germinate.  The pot didn't even decay much.  I wouldn't waste my money on these things but buy fresh seeds instead or seedlings that have already been started. I have a few more pots left over and I'll try them again somewhere in the garden, but I'm not expecting them to do anything.
summary: Miracle-Gro 17002S Gro-Ables Salad and Herb Garden Kit

reviewText: The Miracle-Gro Gro-ables salad and herb garden seed pod kit contains 18 individual seed pods, supposedly to create a salad with.  Eight of the seed pods require starting indoors using the included cardboard shipping container and transplanting, while the remainder can simply be pushed into the ground and watered.I saw the Miracle-Gro Gro-ables salad and herb garden seed pod kit, and thought it would be a cool and simple way to grow a garden.  I live in Texas in a house with minimal yard and received the kit at the end of July.  I was unaware the kit required at least 18 square feet of treated soil and a cool season, preferably within 2-3 weeks of the last spring frost.  I'm not sure where to plant the kit and even then, according to the instructions, it's too hot anyway.The kit appears to simplify the process of growing a garden.  However the only real difference is the seed pods replace seed packets.  The 94% biodegradable seed pods are guaranteed to grow, since they contain mulch, seed, and fertilizer.  It really doesn't seem to be any easier, just cute.If you're looking for a simplified gardening kit, the Miracle-Gro Gro-ables salad and herb garden seed pod kit misses the mark.  This is nothing more than a cute garden to salad marketing idea which completely missed the mark for me.PROS:Guaranteed to growCONS:One month shelf lifeAttempt to simplify doesn't
summary: No Gro For Me: A Miracle-Gro 170025 Gro-ables Salad and Herb Garden 18 Seed Pod Kit Review

reviewText: This is lovely in concept for a small starter garden and/or a project with kids. Its a nice assortment of compatible plants for lovely salad fixings. The kit and information is befitting the Miracle-Gro name and quality so you can't go wrong in MOST cases. With the weird weather across the country and the timing of getting your kit you really CAN GO WRONG and produce NOTHING.Before purchase, visit the groables(dot)com website - PLANT area specifically- to make sure you have: 1. enough days until harvest at the ideal soil temperature after Spring frost and until Fall Frost to produce a harvest for each plant type. 2. the ideal soil temperature during that time frame to support plant growth. 3. The watering freedom to compensate for drought or other issues. 4. a fighting chance to bring the plants to maturity.I share this information because I DIDN'T do the research until the kit was selected and on its way to me. Although using planters, containers and sprinkling can for discrete watering (to avoid drought-restriction fines of $200 and up) AND to grow some of these plants, I cannot control the Texas heat and the soil temperatures. We're having 100+ degree days and rarely below 80 degrees at night. SEE GROW areas of the website which are helpful as well.I've opted to wait until the summer heat breaks and see which plants may have a chance before the Fall frost and update you on my findings. I'm giving this kit a temporary 3-star rating UNTIL I can actually put it through its paces and evaluate it thoroughly.

UPDATE (october 2013): got this kit in june. not a single seed sprouted all summer or fallOriginal review:=======right out of the box, i tried the cucumber, tomato, and sweet pepper. i'm going to try some of the other ones inside (as per instructions), so after 3 weeks not a single sprout on the first round.last year at the local farmers market, for $10 we bought a whole flat filled with a variety of 15 starts. i think 13 of the 15 were producing within a matter of week. that was a much better deal.additionally, the miracle-gro are not local seeds, so there's no way to know if they will acclimate to your particular climate zone. and this kit is incredibly expensive compared to just buying starts from a local supplier. if you can find organic non-gmo starts that are native to your local climate, then even better.
summary: nothing grew (3 weeks later, still nothing)

reviewText: I got the Miracle-Gro Seed Pods late in the season (early July) and planted them immediately.  They are really easy to plant; just stick the hand shovel in the ground, twist to make a small hole (which is just about the same shape as the pods), and the pods drop right in.  They have a lip, to keep them at the correct depth.  I presume the seeds are already at the right depth within the pods.  Then peel off the label, water, and that's it!As for the growing... well, I've had mixed results.  The tomatoes grew like crazy, which is typical here in Maryland.  Anyone who can't grow tomatoes here should quit gardening.  We've separated several tomato plants out of the two pods.  The lettuce has sprouted and is growing well, even through the hottest part of summer when leafy stuff typically bolts.  A couple of the other pods sprouted and got eaten by our aggressive non-pet wildlife (i.e. deer, rabbits, groundhogs, or others).Several other pods didn't sprout at all.  I don't totally blame the pods, though - I only watered them three or four times, planted them in mid-summer (90+ deg F weather) instead of spring, and really didn't pay any attention to them.Another benefit is that it's an easy SET of different plants, as opposed to buying a whole package of seeds of each type.  Seriously, does anybody really plant a whole packet of cilantro seeds?  Three or four seeds provide all the cilantro a household can use in a season!I will likely try the pods again, because of their ease and convenience, but I will get them early in the season and plant each at the right time of year.
summary: Very easy to plant, nice mix of plants, indifferent growth

reviewText: This was fun for my step-daughter to use with her five-year-old stepdaughter to grow a small garden on the back patio.  The success of the seedlings has been iffy at best.  However I blame that on the five-year-old and my step daughter, who hasn't taken much better care of the plants than the child has.This isn't for a serious gardener.  The cost of the kit is far too high for a couple of seeds and the crop would be much much cheaper to buy organic at the local farmer's market.

I'm in a Zone 9 and received these Mircale-Gro pods in the middle of summer. Not a good time to start seeds. But this isn't my first rodeo and I wanted to see how they would do. The sun is for growing and we certainly get a lot of sun here. No humidity though, unless you count that day a few weeks ago. Drippers are what gets us through the hot times. Given what I know of my area I have been able to successfully grown lots of things and decided that despite the time of year I would try them. They did wonderfully. Naturally they were thirsty for water (who isn't) and the sun helped them grow fast. A little on the costly side but performed wonderfully.I received this product free from Amazon Vine for my free and honest review.

There are not enough seeds here to start a backyard garden, but it is great if you want to have a few pots sitting around with herbs and tomatoes or if you want to start an urban garden.  We have a few small pots on our back patio and these mini-planters with seeds have started to grow already.  The kids love watching them take off.  It will be a while before we have anything big enough to eat, but it has certainly been a major hit so far with the limited space we have around our house., for
summary: Fun set of seeds, but buy it for window sill growing, kids, or a patio garden

reviewText: I was interested in trying these because I wasn't sure I would actually use all of the types of veggies included so I wanted to just grow a small amount to start and help me plan for future gardens.  These little packets were perfect for that purpose.  I was able to try a nice variety of lettuce, herbs and tomatoes as well as beans, peas and cucumber.I really appreciated that the seeds were non-GMO, which is important to me and difficult to find.The packets were simple and easy to pop into a small container and they yield wasn't so much that they overgrew the container I planted them in.  I didn't have to go back and dig them up for spacing later, it was already planned for with each packet.If you're interested in growing a small garden for whatever reason (small space or just want samples like I did) this is perfect.  All you need is the containers and the dirt, everything else is done for you.  It would be great for growing a small garden on a balcony or patio.  I will buy these again and give them to my daughter for her apartment as she loves to garden & cook with fresh veggies.
summary: Perfect for container gardening or small/starter gardens

reviewText: When these arrived I was thrilled! We purchased our first home towards the end of last year so this is the first summer we have been able to have a garden. These were so easy to plant - honestly it couldn't get any easier unless I hired someone else to do it. If you are looking for an easy way to start growing yummy vegetables and herbs this is the kit for you!

These pods make growing from seed much easier than the real thing. They are also about 20 times more expensive than buying the seeds themselves, so you hope you are getting something from it. I'd give it 3.5 stars for the reason below.I will update in the next few months as the plants grow/die.For now (first month):- About 80% started growing without issue- About 60% made it thus far. (granted it's hard to tell if the slugs are to blame)Pros:- Easy, just put in soil and water. (don't need to take them out of their pods or anything)- comes with plant food (fertilizer)- easy to open- You don't have to worry about planting seeds at appropriate depths, etc.Cons:- $30 dollars for 18 seed pods. (due the math, that's almost 2 dollars per pod, with those 2 dollars you can buy 100+ seeds)- Almost more expensive than buying lettuce/tomato startersThe description claims it's for gardening experts and new ones alike, but I have to disagree, It is easier for new ones, but a gardening expert will be better off with seeds.If you enjoy growing items from scratch, and want a quick starting point, this is probably a good kit.The cost though, makes me more hesitant to give it a solid 4 or 5 stars. I can buy lettuce starts (6 lettuce heads about 3-4 inches tall) from local garden stores for around $4 dollars. It means, I could get 18 heads of lettuce, that are already healthy and growing, for about half the cost of these 18 pods. Granted a tomato starter and other of the varieties included here are more expensive, but chances of your pod making it into a full grown plant vary, and pretty much never would be 100% rate.
summary: Easy, most have started to grow

reviewText: This review will be a little different as it will be a while before I can actually plant these. Why? Look at where I live. Yes, we now hold the record for widest Tornado ever recorded. My garden is a swamp at the moment. But since I received this as part of the Vine program, I am required to review it. So I will start with a review of the product alone and will update it as I am able to plant the pods and continue updates through harvest.The pods themselves are an ingenious design; Peat pots containing your seeds, fertilizer and growing mix. Just peel off the paper cover and literally stick them in the ground. If you have ever planted seeds, you know just how small some are, how difficult it can be to get them at just the right height and how frustrating it can be to see birds in your garden digging them back up.The biggest negative with these is that I don't know what I am planting. I want to know what kind of tomatoes I am growing. Different types have different disease resistance, grow to different size and produce different types of tomatoes. The name alone tells me all I need to know; Celebrity=Disease Resistant, Super Fantastic=Set fruit in Hot Weather, Brandywine=Heirloom with Great Flavor. Not including the name of each plant also means I do not know how long it will take till harvest, how big the plant will eventually get and if it needs any special care. Brandywine tomatoes have no disease resistance will need to be protected from common tomato diseases.Also keep in mind that even though the pod has fertilizer, different plants have different needs when it comes to micro-nutrients. Tomatoes need calcium and magnesium to develop properly and this will need to be amended to your soil with bone meal and add some Epson salts as they grow.I will continue this review when my swamp is a garden again and I can plant these.

Ever year I resolve to start my herbs and vegetables from seed using tiny compressed peat pellets in a plastic grow tray, and every year I end up buying plants a few months later. The pods have a lot of theoretical advantages, but never seem to work out in practice for me, mainly because I don't really have a good indoor growing space; just a few windows with decent exposure to the sun.These pods are suppose to give you most of the advantages of the compressed peat pellets, other than being able to start your planets before the last frost. They eliminate having to measure out the right number of seed, the right amount of starter fertilizer, and the right planting depth. They also provide a protected environment during germination and initial growth.But at a dollar each, they're a lot more expensive than growing from seed, and some close to the cost of hearty plants that have already grown strong enough for outdoor transplantation. I think these are really intended for the person with no particular gardening knowledge or skills who is looking for a fairly fool proof method of growing a small garden, and for that person, they might be just the thing. Serious gardeners and those looking to grow food to save money or improve the quality of the produce they eat or perhaps want to supplement their diet should probably look elsewhere.Aside from that, though, do they actually deliver what they promise in terms of easy plant starting? Well... it's almost August here, which means it's way too late to think about starting plants in the garden, let alone starting them from seed. Amazon Vine program requirements mean that I can't wait two months before writing my review. So in the light of that, but still wanting to do something of a scientific evaluation,  I've planted a few of these pods in a large  pot in front of my house, and if I get some decent growth before the front comes, I'll add that to this review.

The seed packets arrived as described and included each of the varieties as listed in the product description. The instructions for planting the seeds are simple enough, and the kit includes a separate fertilizer to aid in the growing process. While the overall price is a bit high, this is a solid kit that is heavy on the lettuce side and not so much on other types of vegetables, so make sure to pay close attention to the product description to make sure the variety is what you're looking for to add to your garden.

These pods are awesome; they're fun, they amaze kids and adults alike... fast-growing, incredible results.  But don't let me plant them outside.  For I am veggie death, destroyer of plants.My wife had these growing like mad inside, on the kitchen counter under the fluorescent lights, and when I told them we needed our counter space back, we planted them outside, and they died painful deaths in early June.  If I had been there to support them, I would probably be climbing bean stalks to the sky by now, but instead, I plant-slaughtered them.  I put them out in the garden where we'd planned them to be -- we'd weeded it and got everything ready days before -- and then we had a heat wave when we were both very busy and no watering plan in place.  My fault.But before this fatal faux pas, these pods really were incredible.  Follow the instructions and these things will germinate by the next time you look at them.  The trays they are laid upon are smart, orderly, and certainly effective.  I just didn't have my act together on the outside end to give these little guys a chance.  This is a great product, and you need to be a complete green buffoon (like ME) to ruin the chances of having a nice little salad and herb garden.  I mourn what I have done, and hope Miracle-Gro doesn't ban me from trying their excellent and cost-friendly product again.
summary: It was all going so well 'til I got my hands on it

reviewText: Ok, so I did get this set from Vine. I live in a townhouse with a yard where I am not allowed to dig to plant (I can only use planters). So, I have several 2 foot long rectangle pots that I used last season to grow herb seedlings I had bought at Home Depot. This year, I decided to use these, planting them from scratch in the planters. Of course, it's only two weeks so I can't give you an ultimate review on these (not enough time). I will say that they are super easy to use and to plant (even someone without a green thumb could not go wrong). As of today, the plants are growing and hardy and it looks like I may have some basil within the next few weeks. I really have no complaints with this except for the price. Honestly, the seedlings I bought from HD last year were a lot cheaper and already half grown. I guess it's more the fun in growing these from scratch and maybe a great learning tool for families with children. That being said, the plants are hearty and I think they will work out just fine. I have never grown lettuce before, so I am curious as to how it will turn out. I wish there were more herbs in this pack (and less lettuce) but I have to rate this a 4 star just because it does deliver what it states. I would wait for a Lightning Deal to get these a little cheaper if you are really interested in buying.
summary: Easy, works well expecially for a condo/apt dweller but a tad extravagant

reviewText: I recommend this easy, quick starting garden to both kids and adults with one proviso: if you want it to grow and astound you, take care of it from start to finish.This is a neat idea.  Americans like ready to go, time and mind saving ideas.  Fast food direct from the garden, well, not quite.  They provide 18 seed pods, basically, lettuces, herbs, tomatoes, peas, and cucumber.  There are very simple planting instructions for both ground and pots, planting indoors to start, a paper measuring tape to space the seeds, estimated time to germination and harvest.They include a sheet of label info listing each plant and fertilizer used and planting instructions. One needs a magnifying glass to read that sheet.  Just follow the growing guide.Steps: Plant pod, water and wait.  One removes the pod cover, pushes it into loose soil level, and keep it moist. They provide a packet of fertilizer.The secret to any garden is daily care: weed, water and fertilize.  Don't miss a day- especially early on.  Miracle-Gro offer suggestions on the guide and at their website. I plant some pots, some in the ground.  Less issue with weeds in the pots.  Out where we live, dry, high plains, if you water and provide any kind of semi-fertile soil, the high praire grass/weeds think it's just for them.  So do the deer.  Will work nice on a patio as well, but don't let the sun burn them out.The best part on this system, it's easier to plant and control; seeds don't wash off; the depth is just right.  Not organic, if that matters, you'll have a great garden if you just stick with it.  Happy gardening!

reviewerName: Modern Blue Argonaut "No I do not have a shoe...
reviewText: I used to have a beautiful garden, ten years ago! This kit makes it so easy to get back into gardening without the hassle of picking individual seed packets and researching/selecting what you are going to grow. I am a busy person and this really got me back into gardening! I live in Florida so I started my seeds inside and will move them out once Oct 1st hits or I feel the weather is appropriate for outdoor growing. Also, unlike growing in the ground, I have these in pots so I can bring them inside in case of a freeze. I planted these in mg soil as well and results so far have been good. I can't wait for ripe products ready to eat! I expect this will save me a bunch since produce is expensive here (anyone traveling to FLA knows how expensive produce is even though so much is grown here).

This is a SUPER deal for the beginning gardener, someone older who likes a lot of single (one tomato, one bean) plants, kids' project, homeschool families, folks who live somewhere with not-too-much land etc. You get these snazzy, inventive cups with foil over each pod. Lots of great things to try, one of each. This would make a great gift for someone moving into a new home or out on their own. Get to know these veggies and what you like, what grows well for you etc. NOTICE..DO NOT BUY IN JULY. I got these in July and am going to wait until next spring (in Virginia) because lettuce etc will not grow in a hundred degrees heat!Sheri Gill - Writer, Mom, Mage!
summary: AWESOME...but you might want to buy in early, early spring,.

reviewText: I am a novice gardener. I wanted something that would be easier to work with. The Miracle-Gro 170025 Groable Salad and Herb Garden Kit is about the easiest way to accomplish this goal. The Pods that I planted are already growing. I live in Texas, so I planted these in pots and keep these inside. I saw results in a very short time. I am very pleased. These Pods make Gardening very easy.

I have watched my herb garden grow very nicely. I live in florida and it has been raining a lot here. This is how I did mine. I placed them first into planter pots  set them outside and made sure they did not get too much Sun (unshaded here}. After about three weeks I made a bed and put them into the ground. They are doing well since I added drainage to the bed. I love having fresh herbs and this is a great way of doing it. The lettuce is starting to come up. The kids like seeing the progress of them as well. Overall great way to have fresh herbs.

I haven't planted any vegetables for a long time, but when I did, I had a hard time sometimes evenly spacing them. The pods are great and make things easy - and they're biodegradable! It really doesn't get any easier than peeling off the lid and pushing it into your soil... then watering. Mine are already growing. Such a cute little garden and kids would have fun doing this and seeing their seeds grow. Highly recommend!

This is a pretty cool idea.  Good for beginners and others who don't want to put too much effort into gardening (which is not a put-down; if you have a small yard or know you're not great at gardening, this would be nice year after year), I like that the set gives you a variety of vegetables in bio-degradable containers.  This is cool because you can start them in their very small containers and transplant them safely into a bigger pot or the ground without having to do the risky part of transplanting!You'll soon want to have more things planted, but this will give you a good idea of how easy it is to grow certain things and what time of year they'll pop up.These are supposed to be started soon after the last frost of winter, so plan accordingly.

Okay for someone that wants an "instant" garden this is a great idea and works nicely.  The seed pods are easy to plant and with proper care and attention should grow you a nice salad.  This is a great no brains way to make a simple little garden spot.  (while your at it I'd add in a few other plants as well but that is just me).

I love these little gardeny things so when I saw the new Miracle-Gro Gro-ables kit for salads and herbs it was a no-brainer.I've been a Miracle-Gro user since I can remember; back when my mom used to feed it to her Pine trees.Now, you still have to do some of your own research, they can't do it all for you, to find out what is best to plant when and where for optimal results.Look at this as more of a starter pack for the beginning gardener. It has 1 or 2 of each plant to help get your feet wet. You can learn what you're good at growing this year and plan for the next. Well, at least that's what I'm doing.It's really an enjoyable set and would recommend to anyone looking for a varied, yet small, setup.
summary: Miracle-Gro 170025 Gro-ables Salad and Herb Garden Kit, 18 Seed Pods (Not for Sale in CA)

reviewText: I am very interested in seeing how well this kit works.  It is a great idea for beginners who want to make sure their first garden is easy to plant and guaranteed to produce. It would make a nice housewarming gift for people who have room/desire for a small garden.  The packaging and included media are well designed and easy to read, they look pretty sharp too.I took a half star off for the price, which I felt was high for what you get after all the flashy packaging is removed.  I also took a half star off for the very limited herb variety, you get 2 each of 3 herbs instead of 6 different herbs which I felt was redundant -- especially since parsley didn't make the cut but somehow cilantro did, parsley is much more versatile than cilantro and many people even hate cilantro so I felt that was a bad call.Updates will be made to this review as things sprout and grow: initial review is 4 stars.
summary: Nice starter set, wish the herbs were better

reviewerName: Nathan Andersen "Gadget lover and author of S...
reviewText: While it's not all that difficult to grow plants the usual way if you have the right soil, fertilizer and climate, these little seedpods make the planting stage a little less messy and take out the guesswork of figuring out how deep to plant the seeds.What you need is a small plot of land that gets some sun but isn't scorched, and a bit of good soil (if you aren't sure about your soil a bag from the local hardware and garden store should do the trick).It couldn't be simpler to plant these seeds -- just space them out according to the instructions and dig little holes to lay them in. There's fertilizer and soil in there with the seeds, and they are already at the right depth and ready to go. After a few days of watering, the peat container dissolves into the soil.It would have been nice if they came with sticks to identify which was which. The labels are on top, and once you remove the label you can't tell which is which unless you label them somehow or until they come up.This would be a nice way to start a small garden and build up a little confidence before planting more. I agree, though, with other reviewers that this is a bit of a gimmick, since you need a larger soil bed to plant these in, and once you have the soil, all you need are seeds and water, and you can get a bag of most of these seed types for not much more than the cost of a single one of these pods (that contains only a few seeds). Still it would be a great gift for someone who hasn't even done a garden and is afraid to try, and if it motivates them to keep it up the next season and buy their own seeds it's more than worth it.
summary: An easy way to grow a small salad garden -- tomatoes, cucumbers, beans, lettuce, peas and herbs

reviewText: I had hopes that surely I'd have luck with these groables, but my general lack of luck growing stuff extends to this kit with zero results.  Very disappointed.
summary: I admit to not being a great gardener, but...

reviewText: Miracle-Gro Gro-ables take much of the challenge from gardening by packaging the seed with everything it needs for a strong start.  My approach to planting from seed has devolved into pure laziness, which means a terrible germination rate, but these Gro-ables sprout quickly with almost no TLC.  I planted them, which means shoving them in the dirt rather than digging deep holes, and added a little water.  In short, growing them is as simple as planting purchased plants, but with the fun of watching them sprout from seed.  Everything needed is in the box, including a paper tape measure for proper spacing.Unlike seeds, Gro-ables are not cheap, and probably too pricey for use in a full garden.  I suggest this kit for kids just learning or for someone with limited space.  My hope is that the idea will pick up and breed more competition, which would bring down the price and increase variety.  If so, I will purchase more for next year.

This year I only had one thing I planted from seeds actually grow at all, so I decided to give the Groables salad and herb kit a shot at saving my attempt at a garden. These pods are very easy to plant, just place in the soil with the top flush with the surface of the soil, and water daily. All of these plants had germination time frames included and so far all of my plants have sprouted within the time frame and have skyrocketed. Once they have been growing for two weeks the package recommends removing all but one seedling and we are just about at that point.After my experience so far I would recommend this system hands down for the gardening-impaired and those looking for the easy way out.

This is a very easy way to start a garden. All you have to do is open the package, dig the hole, and place the pods into the ground. I love how easy it is to start a garden this kit. It has all the different Plants that you would need to start a basic garden.
summary: Fun and easy way to start your garden

reviewText: I haven't had a chance to try all of these yet because I'm going to wait until next spring to plant most of them, but I did try out the cilantro and the dill and both are growing really well!  The little pods are easy to use and so convenient!  I just popped it into a bigger pot, added some soil, watered it and let it go.  Within just a few days there was sprouting!  These would be great fun for kids too.  A nice little assortment.

Most Amazon customers, myself included, tend to write reviews within a few weeks after receiving a product, and are most likely to do so if they are highly motivated by an extremely positive or negative experience.  The challenge?  How to review plant seeds.  I can tell you that they were delivered in a box marked "This end up".  The delivery person, of course, left the box lying on its side in the hot sun.  Inside the box the contents were well protected in a sealed foil bag.That ends part one of my review.  It is well past the outdoor planting season, so I have decided to create an indoor garden.  I will update these comments in a few months after the plants have had a chance to grow.  There will still be a bit of a challenge for one user to recommend or not recommend something like plant seeds to other users because of the incredible difference in how they can be planted, climate variances, what kind of soil they are planted in, how much they are watered, etc.At this point I believe they earn 4-stars due to the convenient form-factor and how easy Miracle-Gro has made it for people like me who don't have a natural green thumb. At $1 per pod the convenience is worth the cost.
summary: Easy and convenient and only $1 per pod

reviewText: Miracle Gro has come up with a biodegradable paper seed starter.  The cone shape of the starter and the biodegradable paper make this a winner in my book.  It's easy to fill, although these cones are already filled with starter mix and seeds.  The shape makes it easy to plant in the ground while protecting the growing seeds and seedlings.  A great idea, except . . .What I don't like about this kit is that the seeds are preselected and already planted for you in the paper cones.  While the selections are ok for a sampler kit, they may not be appropriate for a particular area of the country, and they may contain veggies that do not appeal to your family.  Here in hot Texas, fall gardening is within a month or so away, but that doesn't mean that we won't still have scorching days that will fry tiny lettuce or spinach seedlings.  Not enough time is left to get tomato and cucumber plants to the production stage before the cold winds of winter make their appearance.All in all, I like to choose seed varieties that are known to produce well in our often harsh climate, so I'd like to see these valuable paper seed starters available as a separate product, not preplanted with seeds I may not be able to use.Four stars!
summary: A Great Idea for Seed Starting

reviewText: This seemed like and interesting concept so I thought I would give it a try.  Here is what I liked about the product:1.  Each herb and vegetable start is in its own individual peat like container with soil, fertilizer, and seed already inside.  As well, each peat planter is sealed to keep the contents inside until you are ready to plant it.2.  Each Seed container is clearly labeled.3.  Clear planting instructions and a paper type ruler is included to help you plant your garden correctly.4.  Extra fertilizer is included.5.  The entire seed collection is sealed in aluminum type foil.Here is what I did not like:1.  No geographical region consideration is used in putting together this collection;  So, depending upon where you live this may work or it may not.
