I decided to give the Rat Zapper a chance and found it works well.  The pros are that it works well, is small, easy to "load" (I use dry dog food pellets), and very easy to "unload" and clean.  Cons are few, it does use 4 D alkaline batteries - expensive, but long lasting.  It also needs to be kept clean, or the electronics will fail.  Just clean it quickly after a catch. (no big deal).  The main problem or possible problem is that the machine needs to be kept in a dry location.  Rain will ruin it very fast.I leave it under a shelter where the pack rats seem to survive, even then I put a cardboard over the top.  The electronics are on top, so be careful.  Keep it dry!  If not you will find it was an expensive experiment.I recommend it for mice and larger critters.  It would be too small for squirrels I think.  Very useful in the Tucson area, for sure!  It is a great idea and works well.

For several years I've used the little brother of this product with great success.  This unit is larger and more refined.  It's super simple to use - drop some bait in, place it, and turn it on.  The green light turns on for a few seconds to let you know that it's operable.  If there's a path for electrical current flow (a short) the red light will start flashing.  This probably means that it's wet or that it needs cleaning.  Usually it just needs to dry for a while.  When a rodent enters the unit, a series of high voltage pulses are applied and the rodent is quickly killed.  The red light flashes to let you know to empty the trap and reset it.  You never need to touch (or for that matter even see) the rodent - just dump it out in the trash.  The smaller version uses AA batteries and this one uses D batteries.  Unless the unit gets wet, the batteries last through many kills.  The instructions say that it's for indoor use only, but I've used it outdoors with great success.  The only issue that I've encountered is that, when it rains, the unit has to be taken to a dry area and allowed to dry.  So far, and I've used the smaller ones for years, they always come back to full function after they dry out.  They work on mice, rats, chipmunks and squirrels.  I can finally grow a garden without having the vegetables eaten before I can harvest anything.  The only downside is that they aren't discriminating.  If it will fit in the trap, it will be killed.  That hasn't been an issue so far because I bait it with vegetables and that entices the critters that eat my vegetables.  Highly recommended.
summary: Effective, Humane, Easy to Use - Fantastic!

reviewText: I received this for free as a Vine item primarily to deal with the chronic mouse infestation in our older but otherwise very lovely house.  Fortunately for us our mice seem to have moved outside for the summer so I can't say how effective it is. Hopefully this trap will be ready for them when they return with the colder fall and winter weather.  On consideration,I would have preferred a smaller trap targeted at mice instead such as theVictor M2524 Electronic Mouse Trap.  This Rat Zapper trap requires four D batteries which I did not have on hand. To save energy it doesn't have any sort of on light so I will check it once in a while both for any kills and to be sure it is working.  A light comes on briefly when you cycle the on-off switch.  I am slightly concerned that a child could  put a hand in it and get an unpleasant shock.  Similarly it is large enough that a small kitten sized animal could potentially crawl in and receive a fatal shock.  The manual says that the trap will shock for two minutes which seems like it should be enough to both kill and cook a mouse.
summary: My mice moved out for the summer

reviewText: This takes 4 D batteries and is easy to put together...we have put it in an area that is known for mice...it all seems to be working correctly, I will come back to post about if it works...

I will freely admit that I don't like killing animals.However, a few years ago, we realized that our house was gradually being invaded by mice. They would typically move in at the end of Summer, and keep us company during the long Winter evenings. The occasional cache of seeds, or scattering of mouse droppings, gave us the first clue. Then we noticed holes gnawed in our bags of bird food (stored in the basement in the winter). Not good.The last straw was when I saw a little shadowy reflection pattering across our wooden floor, its owner hidden by the sofa, while we were watching TV. The clincher came a few days later when I looked into our kitchen waste bin, and saw two little beady eyes looking back at me.We looked into a number of options. We tried an electronic mouse repellent thingy, which didn't work at all. We considered and rejected the crueller traps, particularly those nasty adhesive ones. We even tried a 'humane' trap, which malfunctioned and broke the poor little guy's back. Traumatic for all concerned.Finally, we bought a Rat Zapper. It worked perfectly, as advertised: the only sign of a kill is a flashing red light. Within a few weeks, we had killed, and disposed of over a dozen mice. As far as we can tell, it does the deed quickly and efficiently, and you can inhume the deceased by taking the device to the end of the garden and shaking it with the open end downwards. If you don't want to look at the poor little chap, you don't have to.There were only a couple of shortcomings in the Rat Zapper, both of which seem to be addressed by its replacement, the Ultra.The original Zapper used four AA cells, which meant that it was somewhat picky about the type of batteries. The makers recommended Duracell Ultras, and strongly recommended against any lesser breed. The new device uses four D cells, and although the documentation still recommends Duracell Ultras (which aren't available in D size, by the way) it grudgingly admits that good quality alkaline batteries will be perfectly adequate. There is also some talk about using the much more expensive Lithium cells, but I suspect this has got more to do with shelf life than actual performance. We're using standard Duracells.The original Zapper tried to use a singe LED to indicate multiple events, including both low battery and successful euthanasia. This could get confusing at times. The new one uses separate LEDs to denote system functionality and 'mission accomplished'.I'm not sure why, by the new device has a rather attractive retro 'streamlined' design. My son thought that it looked like an Airstream camper, or perhaps even the 20th Century Limited, ready to leave Grand Central. Charming thought, but I can't imagine that the mice will notice.Very effective for mouse control (and chipmunks).

Setup involves installing 4 D batteries (not included).  Place bait into the trap, and then, turn on the power.  As the manual suggests, one must put in a "Freebie" for the rat to first get attracted to it.  However, I don't have a rat problem.  I do get occasional field mice in the house when contractors leave the door open, though.  They do like nuts so that's what I put into the trap.  Most of the time, I don't even need bait.  I've caught a couple.  Hopefully, with the end of contractors leaving the door open all of the time, I don't have a recurrent issue.The indicator light will flash when you have a catch.  The beauty of this device is that you don't need to see or handle the furry creature.  I do recommend cleaning the interior after each "kill".  I have had false alarms where it's blinking red, signifying a "kill" with an empty trap.  I just proceed to reset it.  It's likely a visitor who wasn't in all the way.I find this to be a humane and less messy way of dealing with a rodent issue.  Between finding a dead mouse in the skimmer and this trap, I don't really have an issue.Two thumbs up.
summary: Ingenious little gadget for Mice, too

reviewText: This is my 2nd rat zapper. We use them to kill chipmunks in our small back yard.I initially tried to use this when temps were 30 degrees and below and it just doesn't work. I have changed the batteries this spring and have already caught two pests in one week - a mouse and a chipmunk. We have chipmunks and I'm starting to see new holes in the yard. I initially struggled using this product since I am an animal lover, but my yard is getting wrecked and I'm tired of having all my hard work get destroyed. I also also tired of large amounts of poop in my garage, all over my shelving.This unit is very easy to use - though I really wish the back had an opening. I'm always so paranoid to stick my hand in there to load the bait, even with the item turned off. I take out a battery when I load the bait, just to be sure I don't get zapped. LOL A "back door" that opened for easy bait loading would be much appreciated! I'm using peanut butter as bait, which seems to be very effective.I do like that this kills the pest quickly, humanely and cleanly. There's no blood, etc. Just tip the device into a yard waste bag and load bat again. I was doing the catch and release method with Havahart, but got tired of giving chipmunks a ride to the local park, wasting gas and time.There are times when a chipmunk will get a free meal and the red light indicates a kill, but there's no chipmunk inside. I attribute this to batteries needing to be replaced.Easy to use, easy to set and works well. Love the blinking red light telling you you've got a catch!
summary: Stellar product that gets the job done.

reviewText: Thus far my rat zapper has not caught anything.  I can not actually say that I am looking forward to when it does, in fact would much prefer they just went away.  That doesn't usually happen, hasn't yet or I would not have this.  There are not a lot of good solutions.  Move back to the city ? Maybe.  I understand they live there too.I have kids and pets, and am not fond of pestacides./  They are poisons, non-specific.  I do not want to add them to the environment.We've tried patching vents with chicken wire and hardware cloth.  They come back, eat through it.  I tried glue boards.  They don't work.  Honestly you do not want the details, but trust me...you do not want the details.I have a garden I work very hard on.  My neighbors grow landscape plants.  I grow fruit and vegetables.  It likely contributes to the appeal.  I do not, however, tend that garden to feed rodents, nor do I want to give it up.  It is why I moved to the country to begin with.  All that said, this is part of the battle.The rat zapper is essentially set up on arrival.  Just add 4 d cell batteries, bait with pet food and leave by base boards, or where they have been seen in your house.  It is easier to handle/ dispose than something like a glue board but I) still do not look forward to it.I have had mine out for 2 weeks and have not yet caught anything.  On the other hand I have vegetables undisturbed on the vine.  It is summer, and maybe they are in someone else's yard.  Though I have not caught anything I have no reason to believe it is not working.  The test circuit lights, and I have no damage.  Maybe they just took it as a warning that I am getting serious and moved on..One can always hope.I will update this review to note that it is either working, or not.  For now I have no damages, which is nice, but suspect they will be back.  Provisional star rating based on perceived ease of use as compared to other solutions, and the equipment itself seems solid and well made.---------------------------Updating my review as promised. They are back :( and do not seem to have found the rat zapper much of an obstacle. (They got the last of my tomatoes and first of my peppers!)  If we are doing something wrong I do not know what it is. This has been out for months and so should not be something novel or suspicious in the environment. (Included instructions note that they may be suspicious of novel objects).  I is placed along the baseboard where they run from attic vents :( :( to my vegetable garden :(  :(  :(It is back to the drawing board, so to speak, for us. Thus far the only way we have interrupted the flow without poison is when we accidentally caught one in  humane trap provided by the SPCA (meant for larger quarry).  At the present time I have cages around every single plant in my garden.  It is ridiculous what it takes to grow things here without poison.  Many go to building a greenhouse, which may be where we wind up when we move. As of now, I am still looking for a non-toxic way of ridding my house and garden of pests.  This was easy to set up and use, but ultimately not effective. I have downgraded the star rating accordingly.
summary: Easy to set up, easy to use (updated 12/15)

reviewerName: Gina Pera "Is It You, Me, or Adult A.D.D.?, a...
reviewText: Update:Now that our trap has seen "action," I am updating the review to 5 stars.Each year, I await the Blenheim apricots. A farmer at our local market grows them, and they are highly sought after. I left a few sitting on a little table in our kitchen, to ripen. But the next morning, I saw that several contained divets, of the type made by small creatures chewing on them.First of all, gross. A rodent in my kitchen. Second of all, I moved the trap from the attic to the table, inserting a chunk of apricot (sitting on a small plastic cap), and only hours later, we had our Blenheim napper. My husband cleared the trap, and I re-set. We had barely left the room when we heard it "activated" again. No doubt there are more.At the market, I told the farmer about the popularity of his apricots among the rodent population (I always keep fruit on this table, but there's never been sign of rodent activity until the Blenheims arrived). A lady overheard me and said she had the same thing happen in her condo. Apparently, the scent of the apricots (which, honestly, aren't that aromatic, compared to other fruits) lured some mice up through the pipes into her unit.Some people might balk that the old-fashioned traps are much cheaper. Yes, that's true. But do you want a mouse going "splat" on your kitchen table? I don't. We also tend to throw out the trap, not wanting to get into the details of extrication.This trap is great. Well worth the money. Effective, clean, and convenient.---I've given this trap only 4 stars for now. The reason is that we're not sure it's in the right place or if our mouse problem is already resolved. I will revisit in a few weeks as news develops.For now, I can say that this is vast improvement over the previous method: climbing the ladder through the closet into the attic and setting an old-fashioned trap.  (My husband actually gave me a headlight, as worn by splunkers, to assist in this process. He is too big to negotiate this tight spot in the closet, so I am the designated "mouser.")I had to visit YouTube to find a non-finger-damaging way to set the trap (you use a fork!). And even though the method works fine, it's a giant hassle. Especially when precariously perched. Then you have to dispose of the entire trap (unless you are less squeamish than I am). Try this a few times, and the cost adds up. Not to mention, it's still gross, maneuvering the thing into a bag for disposal.With this Rat Zapper trap, you simply add batteries and peanut butter, set it in the desired spot, and wait. When it "zaps," you need only slide the occupant out into a waiting bag.We haven't spied an "occupant" yet, but it could be because our past weeks of effort took their toll. I will update when/if that happens.
summary: Much easier than conventional traps, especially in hard-to-reach areas

reviewText: I wasn't quite sure what to expect from this product... I had never used an electronic rat killer before.  Our property adjoins woodland and occasionally rats wander over to check out our garbage etc.  Our cat kills a few but I wanted to give Hudson a break (and keep his 20 pounds from going even higher) so decided to try this.  After inserting 4-D batteries (not included) I set it out and per the instructions put a little dry cat food in there but did not turn the trap on.  This allows the rats to feel safe and they "scent" it to let other rats know it's a good place to hang out.  After a couple of "free" feedings, I turned it on and the next morning voila, dead rat.  I shook it out and set it back down.  Next morning, another rat.  I like this thing!For those that have used this and said that the red light (indicating a kill) flashes without a rat inside, the directions say that this is ALSO an indicator of a low battery, so before you throw the thing out, replace the batteries.  They recommend Energizer lithiums and say that type of battery will provide 100 plus kills and more than a year of battery life.  Normal Duracells are rated at 9 months and 60 kills.Overall, I like this much more than rat bait (which can harm beneficial creatures) or disposable conventional rat traps.Highly recommended.
summary: Rats check in but they don't check out....

reviewText: I have a rat that lives under my deck that is driving my dogs crazy. Because of having dogs, I was reluctant to put out poison. This trap is just the right size to squeeze under the low deck. I looked at Home Depot and Lowe's and couldn't find anything locally that I thought would work for me -- and this is perfect. I'm only giving it 4 stars since I haven't actually caught the rat yet. I'll update my review with more details later.

Killing mice is always gross, but we get them under our kitchen cabinet (who knows how they come in) every year. This is about the size of a shoe box and works on batteries with little 'dead mouse contact'. Still takes a while to catch them, but works well.

... as a feeder, that is.  For a week now I've baited the trap and turned it on each night, confirming the green light shows briefly, only to find the trap exactly where I left it and the bait gone.  I've verified each morning that the switch was in the "on" position.  When I ordered it I did not realize this was for "indoor use only" and have been using it outside in my vegetable garden, but I have been very careful to put it raised on a cement paver and in a very dry spot.  Not so much as a drop of water has gotten on or near it!  Each morning I've put it up on a chair off the ground where any possible moisture would air-dry (even though we have very low humidity here), so I'm not sure why it *wouldn't* work.  Nonetheless, since I'm not using it *exactly* as intended I'll give it 2 stars instead of only 1.  But in the end, instead of getting rid of the little rats that are eating my vegetables, the Rat-Zapper has only served to attract more to the garden.  No more - I'm going back to wooden snap traps.

reviewerName: Joel Avrunin "Electrical Engineer who loves S...
reviewText: The Rat Zapper Ultra is essentially a long dark chamber with an electrocution plate inside of it, powered by four D batteries.  You put the bait in the very end, and your hapless rat or mouse will hobble along to the bait, getting electrocuted as they cross over the plate.  I've had it setup for awhile now and haven't  caught anything, but I'm not too surprised since my last round of snap traps seemed to have killed most of the mice in the house.  Time will tell when winter comes and the little animals scurry back inside.The device itself feels high quality, and is large enough for rats to make it inside.  The trap measures 12"x4" and is 5" tall.  An indicator light lets you know if the zapper is on and if the batteries need replacing.  A nice feature is that there is a wired remote that looks like a mouse (not included but supported) so you can put the trap in a secluded spot and easily tell from the remote if there is a dead rat inside of it.The instruction manual is quite useful, and even helps by explaining ways to acclimate a rat to the trap and entice them to go deeper into it.  The only downside is that you have to deal with cleaning out a dead rat (including feces) and then put the trap back out in your home.  Snap traps are nice because you can throw them out.  The electronic trap is nice because it seems a bit safer with kids around and it features the remote monitoring feature.Recommended so long as you are okay with a reusable trap!Update: Updating this to 5 stars!  Last night I put the trap in a new spot because I found mouse droppings all around a field of snap traps I setup in a corner cabinet.  Somehow a mouse had made it into the cabinet and flaunted my snap traps.  I could even tell he had nibble some bait off of one.  He was apparently quite cunning!  I put the Rat Zapper in there at 9 PM.  We don't keep peanuts in the house due to allergy, so I baited it with a Ritz cracker covered in a dollop of soynut butter.  I pushed it to the back of the trap with a bamboo skewer. At 6 AM my kids woke me up to let me know they heard a ZAP.  Sure enough, there was a huge mouse inside.  I suppose he got go big by being quite smart and avoiding snap traps, but he didn't know what he was doing with the Rat Zapper!  I'm a little grossed out by having to keep this reusable trap in the house that has now killed a mouse, but who can argue with success?  I set it up again.  I suspect after awhile I may throw it out and buy a new one, but I am quite happy.
summary: Good alternative to snap traps as long as you know what you are getting

reviewText: We unpacked this unit, added the 4 D cells, and deployed it in an outbuilding. We had a rat two hours later. We'll have to wait to see how it works out long-term but right out of the box it's a rat killer. How I wish, though, that the folks who make these could use a cheaper load of batteries! We have another unit from a different vendor that also uses 4 D cells, while we have a 500,000 volt stun gun that's happy on one 9-volt battery. I'm certain the stun gun would kill a rat - if we wanted to get that close! - so why do these things need a pound of pricey batteries to do the job? Still we're totally pleased with this unit and may buy a few more if it holds up.
summary: It kills rats! What else really matters?

reviewText: It WORKS!!!  IF you would like to see it in action, go to youtube and search "Ratcam + Ratzapper Ultra = slight remorse + satisfaction".  It's shocking ... pun intended! This video is what convinced me it's the "better mousetrap" compared to other options available I've tried. Furry, beady-eyed creatures  give me the heebie-jeebies, their destructive tendencies and unhealthy messes anger me. Eradication became MISSION CRITICAL... enter the RAT ZAPPER ULTRA.When the Rat Zapper Ultra works, there's about two minutes of buzzing as it shocks the free-loading critter to the great beyond. It sounds like a Bug Zapper, just 2 minutes worth. The red flashing light indicates "GOTCHA". The ease of disposal is THE BEST, you simply tilt the unit to slide the deceased etc into the trash bin. I'm not fond of grabbing the decedent by the tail to dispose of it to save a few kibbles.  The bait kibbles can go with the critter to it's next destination - NO PROBLEM.Only 4 STARS for now. I had a Rat Zapper Ultra Infrared that was inconsistent from the start and tended to indicate there was a successful ZAP when there wasn't a victim. So I'm reserving the last star for a couple of months to assess product consistency/longevity and will update this review accordingly.UPDATE 7/24/2013:+ 7 GOTCHAS + 1 Flashing Red Light with NO VICTIM!+ Today, I've experienced the turned-on-it's-side Rat Zapper with flashing Red Light and no victim inside with my dog hovering over something. As best I can determine, my dog decided to pull the electrocuted varmint out the Rat Zapper and shake/play with it like one of his toys. The Rat Zapper is on my back patio, but I was in the side yard weed-whacking and missed the encounter. I've moved the RatZapper out of my dog's reach.UPDATE 7/25/2013:- Another Flashing Red Light with NO VICTIM! Is this the beginning of the end of this Rat Zapper? This is how the other one started to die ...UPDATE 7/27/2013:= TOTAL 11 GOTCHAS AND 3 Flashing Red Lights with NO VICTIM!UPDATE 8/20/2013*** Lost count of the Flashing Red Lights with NO VICTIM...UPDATE 8/23/2013:Been moving the Rat Zapper around following the Rat Trails ... Found my Rat Zapper turned on it's side, red lights flashing BUT NO VICTIM or so I thought. My pooch was doing a walk of shame, so I looked around and found the VICTIM about 6 feet from the turned over Zapper. I'm still wondering HOW the dog got the rat out of the Zapper without getting zapped. Well at least I know the Zapper is still working!
summary: Pow, Zip, Zap, Zoom to Critter Heaven... With UPDATES!

reviewText: I have had this set out for about two weeks.  It hasn't caught one rat or mouse!  However, the first night I had it out, something did try to eat the bait (dog food).  When I got up the next morning, I discovered the Rat Zapper turned upside down, with the battery cover dislodged and the batteries (and bait) strewn a couple feet from the trap.  Apparently, it has enough of a zap to royally tick off whatever critter wanted the bait, but not enough to kill it.I put the batteries back in and re-baited (and reset) the trap.  Two days later, the kill light was flashing, and I eagerly looked inside.  The trap was empty.  Not only was there no critter in the trap, but the bait was gone.I gave it one more try.  Put more dog food (and peanut butter smeared in a soda pop top -- you can't put wet bait directly on the bait tray), and then I reset the trap.  It has been almost two weeks, and except for the bait, it sits empty.  I guess the critters learned their lesson, and they've decided to leave the trap alone, but still infest my property.I can't recommend a trap that merely annoys its intended victim, but doesn't kill it.

Pros:- You don't need to touch the dead rat- Looks good...Cons:- Silver scary? We haven't caught anything- In the instructions it specifically says never to use rechargeable batteries. I really don't like wasting or throwing away batteries so I have a bunch of rechargeables. Well, this product specifically says not to use them. It also recommends against using regular batteries, only fancy alkaline ones (names on subset of energizer batteries as the best)I'm going to try it for a little longer before making up my mind, for now, I am giving it 3 stars, but it's trending down, unless the critter gets caught.
summary: Does it work? Doesn't work with rechargeable batteries

reviewText: So I had a rat and a couple mice roaming around my attic and in the backyard...however now they are gone...and NO not thanks to the rat zapper...more like the heat/weather kind of ran them away. I have not seen or heard any rodent activity and neither have my dogs.I followed instructions and used the trap but without mice or rat can't really say how effective it is so I am just leaving as a 3 star.However, it did zap 2-3 roaches and the light let me know to clean up the trap...so it doubles as a insect zapper...and effective at it as well.So far will recommend but will update review if I catch any rodents.
summary: No rats zapped...but it got something else...

reviewerName: Mr. Deeds "Opportunity is limited only by ima...
reviewText: We don't have rats (thankfully) but living out in rural Ohio we have plenty of little field mice. They are cute enough but I don't want them living in our basement.We do have a lot of mice activity in our basement's utility room - judging by all of the mouse droppings.I've used traditional mousetraps - some still in place there - with no results. I did have a different electronic mouse trap that worked well but it had this little drawer you had to remove and then dump. It was pretty gross to see the zapped mice, especially if they were in there for a few days as I don't check it too often.I like the Rat Zapper's design because I don't have to look at the dead mice - I just take the entire unit outside to our trash can and dump them in.The directions suggest placing a couple pieces of dry dog food inside and at the back of the zapper, which is what I did. Within a week I noticed that the red light was flashing, indicating a tenant (I posted a photo of the unit with the red light on).In a nutshell, I like this mouse/rat trap because it's easy to use, it works great, and I don't have to see the dead mice (yes, I am a wimp about that).I recommend the Rat Zapper Ultra Rodent Trap RZU001!
summary: Caught a mouse the first week!

reviewText: This is my second Rat Zapper Ultra.  The first one I bought in 2008 and it successfully killed dozens of mice for 4 years before it started flashing without a mouse being caught (often, the bait would still be in the trap).  This was probably somewhat to blame on me because I only cleaned it once or twice in the 4 years I had it, and you could see where mouse pee had damaged and corroded the electric plate inside.So, with this new Rat Zapper Ultra, after each kill I am removing the batteries and wiping out the inside of the trap to keep mouse pee from ruining it.  So far, so good.  I love it just as much as my old one, it works very well and it's a trap I can use without being squeamish.  The batteries will kill a lot of mice before needing to be replaced.

On the back side of my house is nothing but cattle grazing green belt. I loved the idea when I bought it that there would be no neighbor over my back fence. Well there ARE neighbors. Little furry ones. And they love the attic.This device sounds like the technical marvel to come to the rescue. It isn't quite that, though it does do what the box says it does. Mostly.In addition to what you read in the advertising copy you should know four things before making your decision:1. You can only use electric traps in try areas or you will short out your device.2. A regular trap will be more productive. I just don't think rodents want to go into a suicide box. Or any new box that just shows up. They like the bait around it but they don't want to "check in" to Hotel California. Two so far...3. Multiple kills per charge...no. My numbers are low because I had a kill then just bait being taken then I changed the batteries and got another kill, and back to bandits eating for free.4. Clean up is...well imagine a bug zapper if the bugs weighed a few ounces and were covered in fur. GAH! It's a bit on the messy side. If you like Friday the 13th movies, you might like this feature. I think rodents must be full of gravy or something.Well that's it. It works to a degree but makes more work than it saves. However the one good thing about it is absolutely indisputable. If used properly it will kill rodents.
summary: It is what it says but is more restrictive than you might think...

reviewText: I tried using this for three weeks and never caught a single anything. I re-set it and baited it every night and the bait was gone every morning and the red light was on but nothing in the trap. Still have rats in the ceiling going back to poison I guess. Wish this worked but it was useless.

Ooooo. This works! We have an RV set on wooded property. The mice are very active. We have used several different types of mouse trap. None have worked as well as this trap. It is a big (for rat size critters) and heavy and large (more difficult to place in tight places). Nevertheless, we are pleased with the trap because IT WORKS. Each time we have caught a mouse the light on the trap has alerted us. The mice have been dead, dead, dead. This trap has an easy dump-it-into-the-trash disposal. Easy to work: set tap where mice may be, turn on the switch (don't look at the light because it is bright), and leave it. Check it daily and if you see a red light on, you have got one (mouse). Tip it over the trash and voila! mouse is gone. Very good product and much easier (and safer) than setting a snap trap.

I have several mice that try to make a living in the backroom of my garage every single year around this time and I get them every single year-I dont know if they talk or what but it has always been a problem. I never get them in the house thatnk God for that. So I set this out for a few nights to no avail and one the third night was a bingo-caught two of them ready to make their winter break home back there. Easy cleanup and done til next year! I hope! Lol This is much nicer than the old traps-no cheese and I dont slap my hand in the wires which I always seemed to do!

This seems like a simple enough process.  Basically you just take it out of the box, make sure it's turned off, install 4 D size alkaline batteries (not included).  Put some bait for the rats and mice in the far end.  Set it where you think there be some rodents, Don't turn it on yet, let them get used to the free food first.  After they have eaten food, refill it and turn the unit on.  Then you should be able to get a kill. The light will blink on and off once you have one dead inside. Then you just dispose of the body, (turn the unit off first) and reset it for the next one.  So far I haven't been able to get one, I guess I don't have any mice.

I have rodentia eating my tomatoes! !#@$#$%^%!~ This means WAR. So I get this... put in some peanut butter and crackers and a few hours later... dead rodents!There are a few detractions... one is size... there are some big rats out there and this won't take them. This will only accommodate the small rats, which is fine by me, I have the small rats from fields, not wharf rats.The second one is is that there are specific battery needs... read that before you put the batteries in.Other than that, it sure works better than the old traps and the BF thinking he can blowgun them! :D

The Rat Zapper seems to work well and to get the job done. It functions in much the same way as a Sherman trap, except when the rat steps on the panel the trap doesn't spring closed...it shocks the rat to death. This results in a reasonably humane and clean way of disposing of the rodents, as all you really need to do after the trap catches one is pick up the trap and up-end it into the trash. The flashing light on the trap lets you know when you've caught something. I have had one false positive when the red light was flashing and I looked inside and not only was there nothing killed inside, but neither the peanut butter that I put in back nor the almond that I had in front had been moved. Not sure what happened that time but otherwise this has functioned just fine.However, this does have one big limitation, and it's a big problem if you have a yard similar to mine, with lots of produce growing in it. That's that this unit, as you may have guessed, cannot be used near water. Why is this a problem? Because outdoor rats in a yard like mine are most likely going to be hanging around the produce trees eating it up at night; here they like the avocados and the peaches. If you have an automatic sprinkler system set up to water these fruit trees, that means you either can't use the trap there, where the rats are most likely to be, or you're going to have to keep removing the trap each time the sprinklers are set to go off. If you can deal with this, you may be good. But be aware that this is probably best used inside or along the exterior walls of houses, and not anywhere in your irrigated yard where you may otherwise be able to place manual traps.
summary: Works well with one big limitation

reviewText: I was very excited and happy when I saw the Rat Zapper Ultra offered on Amazon Vine. Living in Southwest Florida, we have always had problems with large river rats eating some of the wiring in our cars' engine compartments. I have used traps and poisons with varied success. Most rats seem to be smarter than the standard traps and the poisons disappear without leaving any evidence of their effectiveness.When the Zapper arrived, I put on surgical gloves before taking it out of the box. I learned a long time ago that human scent is easily detected by rats and mice and acts as a deterrent. The unit looked efficient and well-made. Once I put the required batteries in, the light came up green indicating a good charge. Then I put 10 pieces of dry dog food in it and set it up outside at a likely spot, covered to protect it from any rain.I went out to check it the next morning not really expecting anything to have happened yet.  However, the trap had been moved a few feet, was upside down, and all the bait had been removed. In other words, whatever got to the bait was not disuaded by the promised shock. In fact it must have reached in several times in order to get all the small pieces of bait. Or possibly the charge plate isn't working properly even though the light shows green.So I reset it. The next morning I had to search a twenty foot area to find the trap. This time the red light was flashing but nothing was inside. Once again all the bait was gone with no kill. Something, like a raccoon, must have long legs that allow it to reach the bait without touching the hot spot. Or it holds the trap up and shakes it. Or a feral cat is messing with it. So I reset it again, and again, and again with the same results every time.So then I looked closely at the instruction sheet. FOR INDOOR USE ONLY. Oooops. Knowing that the Rat Zapper seems to be working properly, even though set up outdoors, only two things can be happening. Either rats and mice are entering the trap and not getting schocked hard enough to kill them, or some other animal is adept at robbing the trap. I will set up some classic Victor traps to see if I can determine what is really happening.

I've seen the mouse so I know there is one. After about a week we finally got the beep and red light but apprently they got away or something else caused it to go off.I like the design, shape and ease of use. It takes 4 D cell batteries. Has a convenient on and off switch plus 2 LEDs. Green comes on for a second after you turn on the switch to let you know it is on. Red is supposed to be when you have a catch.If we ever catch one I'll update this review.
summary: No catch for over a week

reviewText: If you check my past reviews you will see I have bought & paid for almost every trap at every price on the market. I just returned a set of 4 of theVictor M240 Electronic Rat Trap. I also want to commend Victor (bought direct for a buy 3 get 1 free deal)for being as wonderful as Amazon on returns. A real surprise. I only tried one and it fails horribly, found a broken wire. They had me just return the 3 I never baited for a full refund.I have 2 of the earlyRat Zapper Classic RZC001and 1 of theRat Zapper Ultra Infraredmodels. I have also most likely bought several of EVERY brand of non electric and finger snapping old school traps. in 22 years in our home we never had ANY rodent problem. Then we removed the grass and replaced with drought resistant succulents that we found out are rodent heaven....It has been a non stop assault every since. I may be a USMC Combat Vet, but fighting rats is a REAL war and one I never bargained for. I have given up being squeamish and hoping to do things easy with electronic traps at this point. Why, well that will be my review for this particular electronic trap as well as all the others.With any brand or model of electronic trap, you have to use it in dry areas so you don't short it out. Baiting may be easy as pie but cleaning will generally NOT be. Especially if there is fried fur etc left behind. And you need to CAREFULLY clean with alcohol q tips or similar to remove traces of feces and urine from any kill. In the end? Trust me, a regular old trap is less disgusting to deal with after multiple kills! Where these MAY be of an advantage is your attic? If you buy the optionalRat Zapper Rat Tale Remote Monitor With 12-Foot Cord - RATT001to hang down from that attic access door, it will make your life a LOT easier. I am becoming badly disabled and to deal with our ladder, climbing up to check & reset traps became an actual nightmare. BUY the rat tail if it works with your model! And then do what I did, buy your loving wife a GOOD staple gun, some wire mesh (1/2 inch), send her up there and close off any and all entry points. Once I did this it has now been 8 months without a single attic entrance. I never would have figured it out if we hadn't been in our hot tub and watched a family of rats simply cruise across the top of our cedar fence in mid afternoon, and scurry straight up 10 feet of stucco and into an air vent opening! I though I had been drinking too many beers but the wife saw it too. I had no idea that a mouse or rat could climb straight up a wall. NO idea.  The next weekend we did the wire mesh with steel wool and in the next week got our final kills. Using every type of trap in existence, we have only had a total of 4 kills with all of our electronic traps combined. With manual old fashioned traps, over 40-50+ now. I will give this and any/ALL electronic trap 3 stars only since in a dry and controlled environment they MAY be of some benefit IF you utilize the "rat tail" option to see if you got lucky without the need to climb into that attic to manually check? But do yourself a favor and replace the batteries after every SINGLE kill or you will really get massive failures which in turn, lead to the rats playing poker in your trap and laughing at you when you peek in to look at them..... I actually think 3 stars may just be too kind?What do I now use? I use the Snap E Rat Trap 6 Pack I bought here at Amazon. I have never ever had a SINGLE trap ever trip without the victim stuck in that trap waiting for me the next morning. Not once. I no longer even bait them! I just use fishing line and place them along that fence we saw them proudly walking along that wonderful day in the hot tub am BAM! Next day (sometimes same day) I have dead rats. It has taken a few months since my review of the Snap E Rat Traps by Kness Mfg that I wrote a year ago this month. But we now have less that 1 kill a month or so as they have moved on to easier picking. Know that with this trap however you need to somehow cover it so birds don't land on it and die. Sadly I killed 2 before I figured that out and broke my heart....If you want proof of just how deadly these Snap E brand traps are, go to my review here at Amazon for all the pictures I posted. I have much more gruesome ones of them hanging from these traps on my fence but they may just be too distasteful for some? My advice is buy the Snap E traps and they are a breeze to bait, set, and dispose of the rats with. I PROMISE.______________________________________________________________________________________________________________Final thoughts, true confessions:How do you tell if your trap is working?1-Electronic-Is there a body? Signs of urine or feces?2-Old School Spring Loaded Trap (whatever brand)=is there a body? Is it sprung?3-Answer is SIMPLE! Electronic you just may never know....spring trap is OBVIOUS, every single time period.4-How did I know? Well n a 4 week period I placed 3 electronic traps, and 2 old school spring traps in my attic. Next day I had 3 kills from spring traps & NO evidence of activity in electronic traps. Same results for next 3 days!. Switched locations of old spring traps with electronic traps. Result? SAME! ALL 3 spring traps had kills, NO evidence of activity in electronic traps. What would YOU think at this point?Baiting:DISCLAIMER-Do NOT listen to me. I am a combat veteran who most likely has MAJOR brain damage! If not from combat, from 30+ years of marriage! I am an idiot,I know NOTHING. If you listen to be you will probably pay a horrible price.-1=Read the directions-2=THROW AWAY those directions!-3=What I do (remember to NOT listen to me!) is this. If you do as instructed, eventually all your bait, peanut butter etc)will harden and become next to impossible to clean, even if you have tiny GIRLY type hands that can reach inside to do it. So what I do it this  and remember, do NOT listen to me! I take a little twist cap of a bottle of pop, or water. NOT metal you idiot! Plastic lid OK? Still alive??? OK, GREAT! Now, take some peanut butter and place it into that PLASTIC cap.Now, (ask me how I know, I DARE ya!) turn the power OFF. REMOVE all those batteries! Take an item, any item and push that bottle cap (PLASTIC) all the way to the other end of the trap. Re-install the batteries and put the trap where you choose. Turn it on (amazing but actually turning it ON seems to help?). Still alive? GREAT!-4-=Now wait till your wife can help YOU check that trap....-5=Don't say I didn't warn you.Confessions:Are you a tough guy? A MANLY MAN? Have you ever promised your girly girl wife you would "take care of it" while checking that electronic trap? Told her to "stand aside" while you flexed yer muscles and began your trek? Climbing up that LONG ladder while she held it steady, holding your feet to steady everything while you checked and then spoke all that tender/sweet encouragement while you made that fateful climb? Was she holding you tight while you checked, as you looked into that trap in that dark, HOT attic, all ALONE, only to then have her GRAB & CLUTCH your ankles while SCREAMING to scare you for all the "tricks" you ever played on her for 30+ years? Did you fall DOWN that ladder screaming like a girl, maybe having a flashback or two while your loving wife was on that same floor right next to you laughing so hard she wet herself???? Well DID ya? Would you ever, EVER tell another living soul? Well I sure as heck wouldn't :-)! Don't YOU either!!!!!!!But know this, it could happen to you......ESPECIALLY if you married a DINGBAT like I did.________________________________________________________________________________________________________________And in the end:I have nothing against electronic rat traps. I find them NOT worth the effort for ME based upon the above. However, know that IF I were to pay for another one, it would ABSOLUTELY be this brand. Why? Because they are the pioneers in this field. Because they stand behind their products. Because they RESPOND to you is you ever attempt to contact them. They respect me, I respect them. All attempts at humor aside. they CARE about customer satisfaction in my experience. To me, that is worth something in this "throw away" society we seem to now live in.

I like everything about this trap but we haven't "trapped" anything yet!  It hasn't been 30 days of continuous use, so I have to be fair and give it longer to work.  We are using it outside and since it isn't waterproof, we have to be mindful of where it is placed. Am using it by our chicken coop, trying to kill rats/mice and avoid skunks/armadillo/raccoon/squirrel at the same time!  Any bait you use must be placed so it is not all the way at the end where the smaller rodents can reach in and just take some.  I don't know about where I would place this in a home with cats since they are so inquisitive, probably a basement with no access to them?  Same with children of course. I am going to try a different, more attractive bait now and will update with progress. I really do like this and it's not a lightweight flimsy contraption that's going to fall apart easily..I think trying this in my situation is just more difficult than a normal "home" situation!

I noticed a couple of rat dropping in our garden, so I thought this would be the perfect opportunity to try out the zapper.  We have many fruit trees on our hillside below our house, so it is not uncommon for us to have critters wander our flower gardens around our house during the warm months.  I followed the instructions and baited the trap with dry dof kibble in the back of the trap and left it off to lure the rat into feeling comfortable about the trap (apparently they are very skittish). After checking daily I found the kibble was eaten (it took about 10 days), so I reloaded the trap and turned it on.  After another three weeks there has been no activity in the trap, also the low battery light is on.It is unclear if we still have the rat or if it moved on.  We are blessed to have many raptors in our area (hawks, owls, turkey vultures) so it is possible the varmit succumbed to the Circle of Life.  Either way, I am disappointed that the batteries went dead.  As far as the idea that there is no mess; I have doubts about that.  There have been times when we have caught critters with the snap trap (still my favorite method) and they have oozed their bodily fluids.  If that happens in this trap will it not short itself out? There is still clean up of the inside of the trap after a kill.  You need to wipe it down once you dump the body.  This is where the snap trap excels.  Yes you have to see the body, but the snap trap is less than a couple of bucks, so i just toss it.I have not given up hope on the trap and if I ever catch anything in it I will edit this post.  But at this point I prefer the old fashioned snap trap. Sometimes you just have to get you hands dirty.
summary: Critter only went in; when unit was off

reviewText: Over the last five years, we've used three different brands of electronic rat traps.  They've all worked...you bait them, set them out without turning them on (to let the rats get used to their presence) and then turn them on.  From then on, you check them every morning and see what you've caught.  It's kind of like fishing, except the fish have four legs, a tail and aren't exactly edible.The battery life has been good.  The D-cells store a lot more charge compared to the C-cells used in some competing versions.  I haven't caught thirty rats yet, so I don't know if it meets the spec and I'm not about to act (as has been suggested) like a surrogate rat and stick my hand in there.Rat disposal is trivial...you pick the entire thing up, hold it over a trash can and the dead rat will slide out.All in all, I strongly recommend the Rat Zapper.  It's not as much fun as a 12-gauge, but it's a lot less messy.

I'm a fan of the Rat Zapper Ultra, and use it to zap mice in our home.  I already had a Rat Zapper Classic, and found it performed admirably, but was excited about the Ultra because of the extra kills you get from the batteries.  With the Classic I found I'd get a few mice, but then the juice would wear down quickly and I'd hear it go off but then not find anything within.  So, that's not cool.  But, with the Ultra, I don't have to change the batteries as often, and it's still nice and easy to kill & dispose of the critters.  The indicator light is also a nice plus.  Now, to be clear, this isn't perfect - cleaning it can be a pain when it gets, um, messy (mostly from food), and it does still miss some mice, but on the whole, it's better than a lot of other products out there, and is much cleaner / safer than snap traps or glue traps in my opinion.All in all, I like the Rat Trapper Ultra, and expect to use it for a long time to come.
summary: Mice go in, but they don't come out! (usually)

reviewText: This is no small device. While you may not have to move the coffee table to fit it in, you won't forget it is there. ;)Past that, it is big enough for both mice and scary big rats. You won't have to worry about it being too small for larger rats like many mice/rat combo devices.It kills anything that fails to read the warning sticker on the sides and continues inside. It also easy to dump the dead guys when zapper is done with them.Show your unwanted house guests you mean business and get the zapper for your house or garage.
summary: Not only does it kill them,  it looks serious.

reviewText: Works as indicated, but does not kill 50 rats on one set of batteries. We have this in use at our family property in NewDelhi, India where there is a significant rat population. In our experience, it is more like 3-5 rats on one set of batteries. Still, this is much better than the conventional rat killing contraptions we have tried. Overall, we like this product and would buy again.

This is a hand held bug zapper that is useful for short hikes. It has a red light that shows up on both sides to show that it is on. It can be used by both right and left handed people. There is a little switch that must be held in place for the racket to be activated. I took this with me in an area where there are many annoying bugs like mosquitos and gnats. The grating was a bit large for gnats, but I got to zap a few other insects, though I wish I could have killed more. The racket fits comfortably in the hand, though can get tiresome after a while, having the hold the button down with your finger.The zapper seems to sometimes kill bugs with making a zapping noise. You can remove the dead bugs by shaking it. I think the racket is relatively safe to use, when used as instructed. You cannot activate it without manually pushing the button on the side, so there is no risk of leaving it on when it is not in use. The racket takes 2 C batteries which go into the handle. I would take the necessary precautions using this near children or pets.

reviewerName: Clark Isaacs "Clark's Eye on Books by Clark I...
reviewText: This bug zapper works, but is fairly heavy and seems like a racket ball racket more than a bug zapper.  It works and the flat edge in front is ok but the configuration is such that it cannot be put flat on the bug, you have to hold it away from it.  The energy produced is quite strong so you can get the bugs from the distance of about 2 inches.
summary: Is a bit cumbersome, but does the job!

reviewerName: Dr A "A reader of biographies, history, and o...
reviewText: This bug zapper takes two C batteries.  It is solidly made, but feels heavy, making it less maneuverable than the old lighter, flimsier models.  Those bugs are fast, and this thing feels like chasing them with a baseball bat.  I liked the corner feature, but then went back to an old light model, which yielded many more hits.
summary: The weapon of mass destruction? Way too heavy...

reviewText: The Stinger Bug Zapper racket does an excellent job of killing bugs without a lot of unnecessary swatting or force. I was able to test it on moths, a couple spiders, and a stink bug and it worked every time for me. The design is good. Sturdy feeling, and the squared edges make it easy to kill a bug that's hanging out in a corner. This is great when you are indoors and a bug finds its way into your house. Just grab the racket and the thing will be dead in seconds. The design doesn't allow humans to get hurt but I still keep my racket away from kids just in case they do something stupid like stick their tongue in it and turn it on. I don't even want to know what would happen, but it can't feel good.Overall, this is a safe and easy way to kill bugs and I will be looking to purchase this model as well as more "pro" versions in the future for different areas of my home.

It works! It works! Every insect I've managed to touch with the energized filaments of this racket have died quick deaths.  Some of them even sparked and smoked. So: does it do what it claims to? Thats a resounding yes.However:  it is rather large and unwieldy.  Also, its not always easy to get the insects to touch the filaments.  Waving it about when they are in the air doesn't work well - it works best on bugs that have landed, because when they try to take off they bite the dust.  Or bugs on the ground that can't fly, although if they are too small you won't be able to touch them with the mesh.So if you are looking for something convenient, there are better bug solutions out there, even though this one works as promised.

Unfortunately, I've had plenty of opportunity to try out this zapper this summer, as it's been a bug-filled adventure!I admit my first trials didn't go so well... I have a cricket problem, and I thought this might work if I put the racket over the cricket-- when the cricket jumped, it would get zapped. And that happened... it got zapped and zapped and zapped some more, but all that did was knock it out temporarily and then the cricket came back to life a minute later and hopped off like nothing had happened. (I tried twice.)But it's a joy at mosquito hunting. So far, I've been successful every time, though it's taken a few swipes sometimes. I worried that it would be messy to clean out the racket, but bugs have never stuck to it. I just go to the trash can and give the racket a smack or two over the top of the can and the bug disappears into the bag. No more squashed bugs on my walls... love it!

This zapper rocks.  I have owned one of these before and always had trouble with others being flimsy, getting an occasional shock from, and most of all, having to clean dead bugs out of its grill.  This Stinger is very well constructed with a thick insulated handle.  Its grill area is big enough to easily run it into a fly or anything else buzzing around that refuses to land, and, it is also flexible so you can lay it flat onto a bug in the wall and just bend it to zap them.  It works on two C batteries, (not included) and is operated with a push button that self releases when you let go of it.  A really nice touch that prevents anyone from accidentally leaving it on.  And a red power light illuminates on both sides when the power button is pushed.  Lastly, the mesh on this is very well designed.  The inner part is very tightly webbed so nothing can really slip passed it, and an outer grid is big enough that hardly ever does a bug get stuck in it.  Most of the time there is just a spark and a zapping pop and the moth, bug, etc, just falls away.  When it doesn't a quick little rap on it usually dislodges it..A to the safety of this thing, it should of course be kept away from children.  There is a hook at the end of the handle for hanging it in a closet or something high enough away. And remember that the power button has to be pushed to activate it, and self releases when you let go of it.  But even if a child was to pick this up and push the button, it will really do nothing more than scare them a little. I have touched the grid a couple of times and all you feel is a slight tingle of a shock, and a zapping sound with a spark is seen that will certainly make any little one drop it. A few tears maybe and some whining, but that will be about the extent of the episode.  Truly, I can't imagine anyone with children being afraid to have this in their house.  (The instructions state that with bigger bugs you may have to zap them two or three times.  We're not exactly talking about the electric chair here.  But keep it away from the kids anyway).A really cool and useful device that is quality built, very nicely thought out, and reasonably priced.  Highly recommended.. : )

This is just the awesomest! (Not a real word but spellcheck let me get away with it!) It feels like a real racket, has some weight to it once the batteries are in. I think that is a good thing, because it's kind of pricey for an alternative to a rolled up newspaper. The best part is the satisfying ZAP it sends out when you kill a bug. Personally, I'm against violence, but when I see a spider, I grab my racket and sneak up on that ba*tard and BZZZT!!! It's dead!!!! There is nothing more disgusting than crushing a spider, that sickening :::cruuunnch:::: makes me woozy. But with the Stinger Bug Zapper Racket, you feel like you have final justice!! BZZZT! BZZT! Would make a great gift. Super fun to pull out at parties or to keep the kids busy in summer! BBBZZZT!!!Sheri Gill - Writer, Mom, Mage!

The audience for this product is someone who wants to be proactive in their pest-control, and take a full role in the stalking of various buzzing and annoying insects.That is different than me; I'll swat an insect that's bugging me, but I'm not one to go out of my way to smash them. As for wasps, I'll use bug spray so I can stand far away. But I figured I'd take a shot at this product and see if there's a different way.This Bug Zapper behaves as advertised - it produces a pretty satisfying and intense 'zap' that few bugs will walk away from. I was a little surprised watching the flash obliterate a spider who got a little too forward.I think the price is acceptably inexpensive, and the two batteries make it cheap to use and maintain.Ultimately, it's three stars for me because it's not going to make me change my habits. I can't see worrying about where I've put the zapper, then following some bug around hoping I get in range to zap it. If I'm outside, I'm not devoting time or energy to do this - I'll swat them if they land on me, but I'm not chasing them around.So the buyer for this product should be somebody who is fed up, and isn't going to take it anymore, and is ready for open war between yourself and the flying bugs. And you want to do the work and take the fight to them - not just sit there and wait for the bugs to come to you. Good luck and get zapping.
summary: So it works, even if I don't quite buy into the concept

reviewText: This summer the bugs have been awful in my yard even with citronella candles and lanterns so I thought I'd give this a whirl. It runs on 2 C batteries (not included) and activates when you slide and hold the button. This product is junk! It doesn't kill large bugs like bees and wasps or really small ones like gnats and believe me I've tried. A wasp got stuck in the mesh but it didn't zap it! It flew away - defeats the purpose of the racket and the gnats just flew right through it, so basically the bug has to be a perfect size in order to kill it. Also, the bugs have to essentially fly into it in order to kill them; because of the bulk of this racket and how thick it is, you can't smash a bug on a flat surface. Waving the racket around to try to kill the bug gives it ample time to fly away and you look crazy in the yard swinging this thing with no results. The head of the racket is not flexible at all either. So to me, this is a waste of $13. You can buy a 99 cent fly swatter at Target that's much more effective than this.

This is my second bug zapper.  It works good killing and frying bugs that come into the path of the bug zapper.  It is larger than my other zapper.  Both feel to weigh about the same. I wish  that they were a little bit lighter.  The problem with these bug zappers are that you don't want to be swinging your arms all night zapping bugs. You also don't want to smack the person sitting next to you in the face, that would hurt.  So, it works good to zap an annoying flying insect, but you would want bug spray if you're sitting outside for awhile with many biting insects.

This bug zapper works great.  It zapped flies with an audible pop, that got the whole family involved.  In order to test this swatter I enlisted most of the family.  First, I needed flies.  Well we don't have any around the house, usually. To alleviate that dilemma I fed our Bassett Hound a large breakfast and instructed my kids not to pick up his droppings (they were heart broken about that).With ample test locations, I set out the next day to test the swatter.  Having never used an electric swatter I did not know what to expect.  I admit I jumped a little at the sound of the "pop" of the first fly I made contact with.  Within a couple of minutes I had rid our backyard of the dozen or so flies that had inhabited our dog's droppings (I mean test locations). It so impressed my 9-year-old son that he wanted to run around the yard in search of new victims. Fun for the whole family.I love this zapper and would reccomend it to anyone trying to get rid of flies.  The construction is sturdy and we have not had any issues with it.

The device is operated by two C batteries which go into the handle of the "racket".  It is a bit clumsy to use because it is a little heavy and very rigid.  It is tough to catch a fast flying insect with such a device.  I was able to zap the very small flying insects but a bee or a wasp appears to be too large for the current to kill.  For several times, I was able to get a bee which became stuck to the mesh but it did not kill them.  In one instance, once the bee recovered from being shocked, it just flew away.  I would not recommend this as an effective way to kill flying insects.  I think an old fashion fly swatter would be just fine.
summary: Clumsy to use and only half way effective

reviewText: This is quite an interesting hose. At first the hose is rather flaccid, small and wrinkly. When you turn it on, it expands to its full length, and works just like a normal hose. Then, when you are done, the hose drains and becomes small and soft, and easy to put away. It's rather a brilliant idea.So far, I have been very happy with using this hose. I love the beautiful coloring and the way that it feels in my hand. Keep it clean, and out of the sun (not a good idea with this type of hose), and you will get years of fun use out of it. What can I say? I love it!(Review of Rumford Gardener Expanding Hose)
summary: What can I say? I love it!

reviewText: I am a gardener and this hose saves me no end of work.  It is a colorful as a pansy but as tough as a fireman.It will "fluff "up the moment I turn on the water and shoot a steady stream of water easily controlled.  It even has an off and on attachment so that if you are using a nozzle without that function the hose will let you control the on off function.When I am done I turn off the water and watch the hose come shrinking back to me where I place the nozzle up so the water just flows back into the pipe.As I use this several times a day that it is lightweight and durable are important; and so far I am wonderfully delighted.I make sure to drain this well when frost is predicted and secure it away from the ravages of the weather for next year.

The Rumford Gardener Expanding Hose is an easy to use garden hose that through the magic of modern plastics doubles in size to 50 feet when engorged with water.  When the water turns off, it contracts back to its original length.  This makes it easier to store and wrap up (it comes with its own bag).  The purple color is also a nice change from the usual greens or blacks that populate garden or big box stores.  Another advantage to this hose is a ball valve at the end that lets you turn or shut off the flow.  This turns out to be very important if you don't have a nozzle attached.  At my water pressure (which is pretty good, but I have not measured the flow rate, and it does appear to be a notch lower than my neighbors), the Rumford Gardener will start contracting because the water flow is not enough to keep it filled out.  The contraction is quite forceful and counterproductive to watering.  So, it is important to be able to modulate the water flow so that does not happen.If you need an extra, or rarely used hose, the Rumford Gardener Expanding Hose is quite convenient.  But as other reviews have mentioned.  With something that has all plastic parts it is simply a question of when, not if, it will break.

The hose works but does have some issues.  First problem I had was the connectors were to deep so I had to use an extra o-ring to make a good seal on my sprayer.  The second and more important issue was the water flow was significantly less that with a normal hose.  I suppose the diameter is smaller accounting for this but I was a bit surprised by the lack of strong water flow.  I did not have any kinking issues and once I doubled the o-rings I had no leaking problems.  Since these are so new, its maybe worth a try just to try something different...if the price is right.

This hose is pretty neat! It's super lightweight, and takes up very little space when there's not water in it. It's almost hard to imagine it turning into a regular hose. Once the water starts going through it, it will expand(which feels really weird, but cool). As soon as there's not water running through, it shrinks right back.It *seems* on the delicate side. I keep expecting a leak, but so far, so good!It's also fun that it's purple! It can add a bit of color in place of the plain old black or green hoses.We like it! For our yard, a longer one would be more beneficial, and I was thrilled to see there is a 75 ft. version, too. If this one holds up, we may add more to our yard.

I've been tempted to buy an expanding hose for awhile now but put off doing so because of all the "horror" stories I've read in reviews and from people I know who have used them. However, my temptation won out when the Rumford Gardener Expanding 50' Hose in Passion Purple was offered for free from Amazon Vine.In the 2-3 weeks that I've been using the Rumford hose I am pleased that I selected it, as the hose has performed exactly as described in its product description. It quickly and easily expands to its full 50 feet when supposed to and folds back to being a small hose when supposed to, making it easy to put back in the storage bag that is provided. Plus, the Passion Purple color is attractive and, believe it or not, an attention getter from neighbors who see it being used.Up to now, the Rumford hose has done everything I need it to do without encountering any of the types of problems I've heard about with other expanding hoses. I have to admit, however, that because of the criticisms expressed by many others about these hoses ripping/leaking/breaking, I am still anticipating experiencing a similar problem. Hopefully, this will never be the case and, as I said, to-date I have been very satisfied with the Rumford hose.

I have been using this hose for about a week, and so far no problems. It works exactly as described - it's small and lightweight when it's empty, but expands to its full 50 feet when the water is turned on. I also love the color - makes it easy to find.The connectors are plastic, so I'm very careful when attaching it. I do feel that I have to be careful with this hose as I see that in many reviews this hose ripped. We haven't had that problem here, though I do make sure that I don't use a very high water pressure when using this hose.

First, if someone is going to sell me a "50 foot hose", what I get better be a 50 foot hose. This isn't. I'd say it comes out to half the length at best.Second, the exterior of this hose is a fabric. If you are going to use it around a driveway (dragging on rough concrete) or there is any chance of it snagging on roots or branches near the spigot, it is simply going to wear through at some point. With your normal rubber garden hose, that isn't an issue.Third, the fittings on each end are just cheap plastic ... not the solid brass fittings you get on better garden hoses.It's cool to watch this thing expand and contract, but that makes it a toy of very limited interest, not a real tool.Sorry, give this one a very wide pass.

reviewerName: Clark Isaacs "Clark's Eye on Books by Clark I...
reviewText: We are were satisfied with this hose until it broke!  Problem was not the hose so much as it is not very sturdy to haul around the yard to water in the desert.  We have cactus in our yard and when we went to water near the cactus it seemed to jump out at this hose and put two tiny holes in the hose.  The hose worked fine for a time and then when I was watering some tomato plants I heard this pop!  The water had been flowing just fine until then.  It broke and there was no way to repair.  We bought the one from TV as it is designed for a little more rough use.  The problem as I see it is that the covering has to be a stronger mesh.  Be sure when you order one of these hoses for the yard, that it will work for you.  There are instructions on the other hoses which say that you should not stop the water without turning the faucet off first and then let the water run out.  Also, keep it out of the sun when storing!  Keep it in the container in which it came when storing as well.  The price of this hose is a bit high compared to other hoses on the market and its reliability! Updated 6/6/2014.
summary: The quality of this hose is questionable compared to others.

reviewText: This hose was even more compact than I expected, very light, and very easy to move from place to place, especially when contrasted with the usual hoses I buy. I loved the purple color, and the nice little carry bag it came with.  First of all it seemed to work pretty well, although getting all the water out to have it contract and put it back in the bag was a little tricky.  One could only expect that however given the nature of the beast, I expected this to be less compact because of the picture shown, but it is much smaller in person. It took about 2 minutes to fully expand when I turned the water on low, and for full expansion it seemed to be required to close the valve on the end.I did note some defects in the hose, most had that scrunched together appearance, but there were a few places where it was not like that, and I would put this on quality control.  These places did not automatically scrunch back when the pressure was off, so they are defects in construction.  I also would have chosen metal fittings for this hose, I often have this in the driveway, and the car safely runs over most metal fittings, but these would definitely break.  This is not a hose I could just leave outside connected, because of it's construction, but it's useful when wanting to extend my other hoses to the non-attached garage, or the back of the property, without having to reel out another heavy duty hose.I used it to water tomato plants I have by the back fence. I found it was easy to manipulate and attach, but unlike the hose I have there halfway to the back of the property, I would not want to just leave this one out.  It appears too flimsy to leave out in the heat, or to be run over by the car.  I would recommend this as a quick to connect extension hose, but not a replacement hose for your gardening needs.  If they made one a little more heavy duty with metal fittings, I might amend that judgement.
summary: Not a bad product, some correctable defects!

reviewText: For the amount this item costs, I would say its a good purchase. Comes in a nice bag, I would not say this would replace a standard good garden hose. However if you live in an apartment or such and want an easy way to have a hose and wash your car or such, I would say buy it.

I rated one of these other expandable hoses (Pocket Hose) a 1 star as it broke within a week.  This is on week 2 and while I have no leaks or tears, the hose now sprays half force and to the right even when the water valve is open all the way.I'm convinced this is going the way of the trash can within a week.As I stated in my other review, resist the temptation to buy these hoses.

We have a large lot and lengthy hoses in both the front and back yards.I've invested in decent hoses because they kink less, last longer and are easier to roll up than the cheaper ones.Given the composition of this hose, I would not expect it to hold up under heavy use for very long.  We're using it as an extension to existing hoses when we need to go further than usual for a specific purpose and then storing it away when not in use.So far it has worked fine for short term use, but I doubt it would hold up to heavy use or exposure to the elements.Since it's so lightweight and easy to store, it might make a nice gift for someone who has a patio or balcony container garden.  It's also handy for the way we're using it, but I wouldn't rely on it as my primary or only hose unless I seldom used one.

We have 11 planting areas around the house, some 200 feet away, so we use a lot of hoses and in summer have to water a lot.  I'll attempt to compare this hose to both traditional garden hoses and other shrinkable hoses, i.e., The Pocket Hose.First, it does have plastic connectors but all shrinkable ones do, the picture of the product does seem to make this clear, IMHO.  It also comes with a pouch for storage and carrying.  Compared to the Pocket Hose, the connectors are much, much sturdier, about 50% thicker.  As for the hose itself, the fabric is also much thicker than a Pocket Hose, seems less flexible but more solid.As for use, I first tried the hose directly on the faucet.  The end of the hose connected to the faucet quickly became smooth for about 2-3 feet, like a normal hose.  After than the hose stretched out but not as smooth, it still had some of the folds you see in these hoses.  It did take longer to fill a two gallon watering can, maybe 25% longer.  It did not leak.  I found that to make the hose contract all the way, leave the nozzle open so water is flowing through when you shut the faucet.  It did shrink enough to fit back into its pouch.We have traditional hoses on reels connected to our faucets but need to connect other hoses to them to reach all our planning areas, so I tested this way also.  Obviously this hose was easier to carry, than a traditional one.  Way easier.  With the water pressure being less it did not expand as much, just a few feet less.  I had to shut the nozzle numerous  times after filling watering cans and walking to the really far planting areas but no leaks or bursting.Finally on my first use I shut the nozzle and let the hose sit for 15 minutes to see if it could take the pressure since others have had trouble with bursting.So far so good, I really like this hose, makes life a little easier.  A little less flow than a normal hose and doesn't quite expand to the full 50 feet.  I will update if there are problems with bursting or leaks, etc.
summary: Seems to work fine, no problems so far.

reviewText: I've never been particularly happy with garden hoses. If they are long enough to reach from my spigot to the target plants or car, they usually kink in the middle of my work, leading to my walking back, unkinking the hose, and then continuing with my work - over and over again. Or after a year or two, they develop multiple pinhole openings in the hose material, resulting in my getting soaked every time I water the plants. They're inevitably heavy, difficult to reel back in, and overall just a pain in the neck.Now meet the Rumford Expanding Hose. This is a truly lightweight hose that weighs about a pound when empty. It reaches its full length when there is some pressure build-up in the hose. That is, if the opening is wide open, the hose is fractionally shorter than its full length, but if you close it down a bit (and there's a built-in control if you don't want to get a separate nozzle), you get the full length of the hose.The hose doesn't kink, doesn't leak, and quickly returns to its starting length and weight once you've turned off the source and allowed the water to drain out. A tiny carrying case comes with the hose and rather amazingly holds the hose once emptied. You no longer need to leave a big hose sitting outside your home, nor do you have to schlep a heavy hose in and out of your garage or toolshed.

This is the "cutest" hose ever.  I never dreamed I would own a purple hose!  It is light, delivers just as much pressure as my expensive rubber hoses and far more than the hoses I own that claim "no more kinking".  The only thing it is not good at is use with a sprinkler.  Apparently the pulse action of my sprinkler heads affects the hose pressure and the hose tends to creep back to a smaller length dragging the sprinkler along.  The first time I used it to water my veggie garden it ended up squirting in my back window because of that movement.  Not good!Otherwise, it is so much easier to use and to store and to carry around wherever needed.Highly recommended
summary: Fun to watch, great for moving around the yard

reviewText: This hose is perfect it works great it looks great it Is very light and easy to store. My kids love the magic trick when we spray all the water out of it and it shrinks. The purple is just as pretty as pictured. Watering has never been this fun.
summary: I could not love this more.
