reviewText: We had a ""pocket" hose from a big box store - I LOVED it until the inner lining burst after a few weeks of daily use. I've only used this nightly on our garden since receiving and so far, so good. Will update if anything changes. It comes packed in a small bag, which, I suppose will come in handy for storing during the winter. It does not come with a spray nozzle (just to be clear!). When you first take it out of the bag, if you've never used an expanding hose before, you may think you've been sent a smaller hose, but trust me, it does expand. There were no directions or tips on how to take care of it...which is fine as common sense SHOULD dictate don't tug on it and turn it off then "empty" it by continuing to spray until the hose shrinks. I don't think it would be a good idea to keep the hose full all the time as it would cause the inner bladder to weaken quicker.I truly love expanding hoses, love that it takes up virtually no room. It does have a tendency to "curl" when watering, but it has never kinked.So far, I'm in love!
summary: This Girl Loves An Expanding Hose

reviewText: My first impression of this hose was that it looked more like a kid's toy than a garden maintenance tool, but I was pleasantly surprised.  It's bright purple and resembles a toy snake if you aren't using it.  Attach it to an outdoor water outlet, though and turn it on, and it will likely surprise you. As it fills with water, the hose firms up and expands, and eventually, reach 50 feet.  Applying pressure at the hose's mouth will let you control the force of the water flow and even temporarily turn the water off (at least that's what happened when I experimented). The length was such that I was easily able to water all my backyard flowers and plants.I just received and started using the hose, so it remains to be seen how hardy it is, but so far I am satisfied.

This hose has a lot of great things going for it. It's super lightweight, the fabric is gorgeous and it is very stylish to look at and comfortable to pick up and carry, and I loved the concept of an expanding hose. If I had a patio or townhouse garden and needed a hose, this would be among my top picks.However, the issue here is one of quality. The fittings are plastic and feel like a flimsy plastic to boot, the fabric is not heavy-duty by any means, and other reviewers have noted problems with its longevity. It also is not meant to be safe for drinking out of, which is fine, but should certainly be noted as that was a major factor for me the last time I bought a hose. If you have kids around the house that drink from hoses despite being told not to, that's a feature you'll want to look for.Overall, this is a stylish and attractive hose, and the expanding action is fun to watch each time I water. If you just need a hose for occasional use on a patio or deck and don't mind a lack of longevity, then this might be the hose for you, as it won't break or scratch anything and it is soft and easy to carry and use.
summary: Good patio hose but not good for actual gardens

reviewText: This hose works fine and is very easy to store. I love the purple color, makes watering flowers more fun. And I don't have to reel it up like a traditional hose!

I tested this hose on my regular outdoor spigot and it worked fine. The hose expanded and it was fine to use.I also tested it on both my solar water pumps on my rain barrels which is where I really wanted to use the hose. The solar water pumps just did not have the water pressure to expand the hose. It didn't matter to me but it would matter if you needed that extra length. The water stills flows out just like on any hose you hook up to the pump but the size of the hose stays put.But I love the color and i'm going to use it on my rain barrel any way.Obviously the hose not expanding is the fault of the pump and not the hose.
summary: Tested on Solar Water Pump on rain barrel. Did NOT expand.

reviewText: While my yard is not as big as many homes, it is still 7500 square feet.  I hate to sound lazy, but unreeling 100 feet of hose, weaving it amongst the flower beds, dragging it around to water the flowers on the far reaches of the property, and putting everything away again is not exactly fun.  By the time I drag the hose around, water the flowers, and try to reel it back into the hose reel, I tend to be wet and full of dirt from guiding the hose and the water flying about when I reel the very end into the hose reel.  I thought that an expandable hose like the Rumford Gardner Expanding Hose might make life a bit easier.The hose is quite easy to operate as I show in the video.  The "female" end of the hose is like any other hose.  The male end of the hose is the same as well, but it comes with a plastic shutoff valve to attach to the end.  To get the hose to expand, the shutoff valve must be closed and then the hose needs about 10 seconds to expand to its full length.When the hose is unexpanded, it measures in at right about 17 feet long.  Once allowed to expand and with the shutoff valve remaining in the off position, I measured the hose to be about 48 feet long including the connectors.  It might not be a full 50 feet, but I will call it close enough as the two feet might have been lost due to measuring error.While the hose does seem to work just like the DAP Xhose did on TV, it just is not the same as a regular hose.  Once you open the shutoff valve, the hose starts contracting again.  Another issue is that if you are trying to fill something like a bucket or a pool, the hose is so light it really does not stay in place and the end will start flailing wildly about.  On the plus side, I found the hose was much easier to drag around and put away when I was doing regular watering duties of the gardens.After using the hose for about 6 weeks, the hose is still operational  My main complaint is the cheap plastic fittings always seem to be coming loose, leaking, or spraying water everywhere.  Also, the screw holding the shutoff handle in place on the valve is already showing a significant amount of rust.  I am wondering how long it will take before it rusts through.Overall, I felt this was just an OK product.  If hauling 50 or 100 feet of standard rubber garden hose is something that is difficult to do, then this product very well might be something worth trying.  I did like the lightweight of the expandable hose.  However, to me the product seems to be cheaply made and while after 6 weeks I have not had the product fail, I do question how long the hose will last.Update #1:  The host did make it through the summer.  I drained the hose to the best of my ability and put it in my deck box for the winter.  I tried to use it a few days ago and found that the hose suffered a massive leak.  There does not appear to be any damage to the external wrap of the hose, so I am not sure what caused the leak.  Regardless, I am updating the title of the review and I recommend staying away from this product.

Rumford Gardener expanding 50 foot hose is a lightweight hose that is easy to move around your garden and yard.  When contracted, the hose is very compact compared to other garden hoses.  This nifty hose expands when the water is turned on and contracts back down to an easily manageable size when the water is turned off.  The hose resists kinks better than other garden hoses I've tried.  Additionally, the smaller diameter of the hose allows for greater water pressure, which allows gardeners to spray the water at greater distances without the use of a spray nozzle.The Purple Passion color of the hose is vivid and adds a nice accent to your garden when stored in an open garden hose "pot".I particularly liked the weight of the hose.  I get tired of lugging heavy hoses around my yard when watering, so the lighter weight of the Rumford Gardener Expanding Hose was a nice change.  And, at 50 ft, the hose is a nice length, allowing me to water in almost all areas without having to connect it to another hose.All around, this expanding hose is a nice, convenient addition to my garden.

I'm a gardener and a purple girl and fell all over this hose.  Who doesn't need a purple hose?  Plus, the thing came with a carrying case. Seriously.  Wallet?  Check.  Sunglasses ? Check.  Garden hose? Check.  OK, dear, I'm ready to go.  You'll be ready for anything, from a thirsty garden, to a brush fire, to a smallish riot.  There must be thousands of reasons for including a carrying case with a purple hose.  The most obvious reason, that the hose needs protection, doesn't bear thinking about.  Hoses are made to be used outside, right?That said, this hose is really, really easy to attach to an outside faucet.  I like that the connectors are plastic with some give, unlike metal that if you don't get it right it's possible to wedge the connector on the faucet crooked so that water spews out and it's impossible to fix unless the water is off, but then you don't remember to fix it until the next 100 degree plus day and you're trying to water...but I digress.  The plastic is fine, and I really appreciate the extra connector with the on/off valve, which is also very easy to attach.My yard is weird and there's not the space to stretch the hose to its full length before turning on the water.  It works fine, anyway. In fact the hose is perfect in every way but one.  I'm a bit suspicious of the fabric casing, as it doesn't seem to be durable. I'm hoping that if the hose does spring a leak, duct tape will fix it, and I have a roll standing by.  I'd hate to lose this purple gorgeousness from my garden!
summary: Love the color and the concept.  Fingers crossed on execution.

reviewText: Some time ago I had purchased a similarly advertised gardening hose - one made of the same type of material and stored easily compared to standard garden hoses. The first one I bought broke the first time I tried it, after which I replaced it with the same thing. The second one didn't break, but leaks near the on/off switch and sprays a fine mist all over me when using the hose.I recently received the Rumford hose and used it for the first time in my garden. When I first turned it on I waited for the leaks or for the on/off switch to break, but nothing happened. It worked very well and does not leak at all. However I did notice the water pressure seemed to be less than I would prefer, but perhaps I hadn't adjusted the on/off switch appropriately. There has been considerable rain where I live, but the next chance I'm able to wash my car I will try it again to see if I can adjust this correctly. My only other complaint might be the color - purple would not be what I would normally choose in a garden hose. But it's not that critical of a feature for me and am fine with it.I would certainly recommend this hose over the standard rubber ones I've had in the past. Even the rubber hoses advertised as free from tangles would still gather into knots. I also love that it stores in a very small container and can be easily hidden from view in the garden (except for the color!). All-in-all I can't wait to use it to wash my car!

reviewerName: K. Salinger, MSN, FNP, RN AHN-BC
reviewText: We really need to conserve space and don't have room for one of the regular hoses all wound up, so we decided to try one of these. Honestly, I was skeptical and thought it was going to be a piece of junk. However, I've been pleasantly surprised at how well it works for us.This hose does roll up really small - a little bigger than a softball size. And it really does reach 25 feet - providing you have the water on enough so that there is good pressure. When it's not in use it's all wrinkly and shriveled up, and when you turn on the water it stretches out until the purple is tight and smooth and feels/looks a bit like the stuff a firehose is made out of. I'm able to stuff it behind a big planter when not in use, then stretch it to it's full 25 ft. length to reach all the areas I need to water.The primary downside that I see is that the connectors on each end are plastic instead of metal. I figure this is where the fail will occur whenever it does end up having problems. In addition, at low pressure the hose doesn't work well at full length, so you need a sprayer on the end that lets you adjust the pressure so that you can have the hose on full pressure in order to reach wherever you need to reach without blasting whatever you're watering.If the ends weren't plastic I'd give it 5 stars.
summary: I was skeptical, but it really is pretty great and works well

reviewText: I was really excited to try the water hose, since I've seen so much about this type on TV and in stores. When I got it in, I decided to go try it out. I had the water pressure on normal (as I always do) and within 10 minutes the hose had busted. So within an hour of receiving the hose, it was in the trash. I wouldn't go with this brand, for the price, it's just too risky!

I have to change my initial review of this hose. I thought it was truly a great hose, but now I have changed my mind about the quality of the hose. I gave it 5 stars in my first review, but I can't do it now. I only used this hose about 4 times, and it finally broke from the hose attachment. I believe the manufacturer needs to make the attachments stronger with brass attachments.

I read the negative reviews on this hose, but so far I don't see anything negative I can write about. It is compact and fits tidily in my small one car garage (takes up a heck of a lot less room than my old rubber house). It appears fairly sturdy to me (see complaints about the plastic nozzles and the tearing). I am not a 'gentle' person and I have been dragging this around my yard almost daily for the last two weeks without any incidents. I will say it is lightweight and a real pleasure to set up. I have nothing bad to say and rated this as 4 stars only because I am thinking that maybe, over time, something might happen? But, for now, I highly recommend this (particularly to older seniors who love to garden but don't want the weight and mess of your typical garden hose).

The first thing I noticed about the Rumford hose is the weight. It is featherlight. The second thing is the strong chemical smell. That dissipated quickly.I was a little worried about using the hose. What if I didn't need 50 feet of hose? What if I just wanted to stand right next to the faucet with it? No problem. Just turn it on and let the water come out gently.Getting it to expand to fifty feet requires the opposite. Increase pressure by opening up the faucet and closing the nozzle so that it sprays. It has to spray. Let the water out to lower the pressure and the hose shrinks.Therein lies the drawback: If you want to stand at fifty feet and dribble water, it cannot be done. If you want a strong spray next to the faucet, be prepared to have fifty feet of hose unwind at your feet.The good thing is the hose does not kink. I pulled hose off and dragged it around, paying no attention to how it was wound. When it expanded, the loops came apart. I did not have to struggle with a kinked hose.The bag is cute, but I don't use it. My hose just hangs around the faucet. I mostly use it to water dead patches of grass and it's been great for that. I haven't challenged it with more pressure than it takes to make the hose expand, because it feels like it might not be able to handle very high pressures, but I don't need extreme pressure. I like it, and I'm contemplating getting the 75 foot hose for my front yard.

Updated: Bummed! At time of first review, I loved this hose, but it turns out it is a fail. After less than three months of use, the cloth completely detached from the coupling that attaches to the faucet. Not repairable. Useless.Previous Review Title: Makes My Daily Watering Easier And QuickerMother's Day is the beginning of the outdoor growing period in our area of the Rocky Mountains. Once winter's passed and there is little chance of snow, we begin transforming our barren, uninviting, expansive wood deck into a our own little summer oasis.From out of the basement, we move the barbeque, patio furniture, awnings, umbrellas, a gazebo, a fountain and a chimenea to make the deck an attractive outdoor living space. Dozens of planters and flower pots get arranged in groupings on the deck and in multiple hanging baskets.The job of planting and maintaining the annual flowers is happily all mine. Every morning I water and joyfully watch hundreds of blooms proliferate as summer heats up. Two heavy 25' traditional garden hoses are attached together to make one long hose. The length is necessary to zig zag my way back and forth across one thousand square feet of deck. The hose is heavy. Sometimes I have to stop and use both hands to swing it up, over and/or around the furniture, etc.About a month ago I received the Rumford Gardener Expanding Hose. I'm never going use my old traditional type again. The Rumford weighs about two thirds less. It takes me much less time maneuvering it about, plus it delivers better pressure than my old hose.My Rumford Hose has not ripped despite me dragging it up, down, across and around everything on our wooden deck. As I swirl it to collapse inside our hose pot it naturally drains and is protected from direct sunlight. From what I've read in other reviews, that might be the reason my Rumford Hose hasn't ripped. My hose pot isn't available here, but it is very similar to this Liberty Garden Products 1913 Hammered Bell Garden Hose Pot - Copper.The Rumford Gardener Expanding Hose has made my daily routine tons easier and given me more time to enjoy my hard work. I'd say I have more time to stop and smell the roses, but I don't grow them :)
summary: Updated Review: From 5 Stars To 1, Didn't Last Three Months

reviewText: This hose is amazing.  We had fun just watching it stretch and shrink when you turned the water on and off.  But then, we live in a small town and not much exciting goes on here.  I was skeptical, but this little hose surprised me.  It is lightweight, packs small in its own little bag and really does get to be a full size hose.  I think it will be perfect for camping when we need to hook the up camper or just hose off something at the site.  It's so small it won't take up much space at all.It got four stars instead of five because the pressure isn't great, but it's cool for what it is.  Also, I think it will be good for watering plants because you can adjust it to a fine mist.  It's so light you can hang it from a post or a decorative gnome in the garden.Next time we get bored, we'll just get out the hose.  Oh, the dog liked it too.  She thought it was fun to chase.  When you turn off the water, it shrinks really fast.  I'm not sure how long it will last, but we like it so far.

I love this hose so much!  First of all, it's an awesome color.  The color looks pretty much exactly like the picture.  It's a fun and vibrant plum color.  Secondly, it's a 50 foot hose but it's so light I can carry it with one finger!  And lastly, the thing works, and it works well.  It expands and contracts just like it promises and it reaches all around my deck so I can water all of my flowers and veggies.  I am so happy to have this.  It the most convenient hose I've ever had.

I love the color of this rumford hose, makes it easy to find in the garage where I hang it to drain.It works fine to water my small back yard tomato patch. It is easier to handle than my long hose that I have had for ages. I have not had any issues with it so far. I hope it will last a few years. It is fun to watch it fill and I love anything in Passion Purple. It is very convenient for my use and no problems have come up yet.

I get a big kick out of this thing and it hasn't failed on me yet, but it has some obvious limitations.  It is much lighter than a regular hose, so it can't be hung over a barrel and left to run; it is so light the water pressure will twist and flip it up, i.e you can't leave it alone, especially if you try to leave it open while turning off the water; it will shrink out of, say, a bucket...  However it comes with a neat optional cut-off valve that I am very happy to have.  Still, it is a little demanding for a hose.It is obviously made from material far less puncture-resistant than a regular hose; I don't hold that against it.  I would only use this outdoors in emergencies; for indoor use it's light and compacts to a size that will fit in a gallon freezer baggie - very convenient.If this doesn't split on its own, I'd give it high marks for a limited range.

The first time I tried it, it worked exactly as the ad claims.  Turned off the water, it coiled up, and all was well.  The second time I used it, 2 days later, the hose sprung a geyser a couple of minutes after I turned off the water.  Oh well.  Never again.
summary: Broke second time I used it

reviewText: This is a great idea especially if you don't have much room. It does expand a good amount and we've used it successfully a few times. But we can tell the quality isn't that great and the material seems thin. I think it will break for sure after some use. So what we have done is to turn on the water at a very low pressure and it has been fine. But even then, we're not really sure how long this will truly last.
summary: Works well if at a low pressure but sure to break

reviewText: This product is made for light-weight duty, judging from its light covering material and light plastic fittings.  I have several plastic faucet fittings in my home for outdoor use, and their quality is much better than the ones that came with this hose.  The hose does expand to its full 50', but it does not retract as it does on TV until the water is removed.  So far, the hose is functioning well, even when I ran the water fast.  When I retract the hose, grass shavings get caught in the hose covering which is messy. I like the color. The expanding hose is a novel idea.  I hope that it can hold up for the long haul.

I have only had this a short time, but I love it.  It does the job, is nice and long and I didn't spring any leaks right away.  i am keeping it out of the sun to prevent deterioration as the reviews said, and not drinking out of it because of potential mold.  Great color.  Looks good next to my purple bush1

To be honest, after reading some of the other reviews and handling this lightweight hose with its plastic connectors, I've expected something to go wrong, but I've used it every day for two weeks so far and there's no sign of imminent tears or breaks.  Our water pressure is neither low nor especially high; perhaps this has something to do with how well it is working for us so far.  We also keep in in the shade and always make sure  it's not pressurized when we turn it off.That said, I absolutely love this bright purple hose.  I use it to water the vegetable garden and surroundings every morning and, as often as not, turn it on my car to get the nightly droppings of silk tree flowers unstuck. The hose pressurizes quickly and easily and shrinks quickly back from up to 50 feet to its original 17 feet when turned off. Though it comes with a bag for storage, we just let it hang on a wrong iron gate. Since we're in SoCal, we won't be storing it away for winter either, but if I lived elsewhere, I'd really appreciate the bag.One caveat - be careful to make sure you don't turn the hose off too close to your plants.  As it contracts, it can wrap itself around an unsuspecting tomato plant before you realize what's happened. (Fortunately, turning it back on releases plants, but it could damage a seedling badly.)I'll report back if the hose stops working well, but I'm hoping it continues to please! So far, I love it.

I have tried two of these hoses at this point....first of all I would like to say that they do indeed work as advertised.  When no water is running to them they can be made very compact and stored almost in a cargo shorts pocket space...when you turn the water on you get a nice thin, lightweight 50ft hose.  All great...  Rumford even includes a carrying pouch so you can store the hose when not in use.I started using these as someone normally would...for light duty yard work, cleaning the deck, etc....nothing major.  The hose was always around a wooden deck or a soil filled flower bed...never near brick or concrete.  The first hose ripped after about 3 weeks and the Rumford after about 4 weeks.  Disappointing.It should be duly noted that I live in a home that has WELL water with very little pressure.  Yes it was enough to expand this hose...but not enough to make it rip apart.Personally I feel that this is a great product that may need a bit more work before I would recommend it.  I give it 2 stars because it does work and because Rumford is the only company that includes a carrying pouch.2/5....
summary: Second one I have had - lasted 4 weeks in total...

reviewText: The Rumford Gardener Expanding Hose is a great concept with a few execution problems.The bright purple color is just downright fun.  And the three-quarter-inch diameter does concentrate the pressure and create a high spray.  Add to that it's truly light-weight and does expand to the full fifty feet.  So it's great for patios and container gardening - easy storage and long enough on its own for patio gardening and light light light.However, when we attached a plastic sprinkler to the hose and attempted to water our herb garden, the combination of light weight and the force of the water gave us a sprinkler careening across the backyard.  In the yard it works best for those who water from place to place themselves and hold the hose.The light expandable hose is an idea whose time has come, however, this particular model has limited use.  It's best, in my opinion, for porches and patios.  The light weight and small size when stored will make it quite useful for many gardeners, but it has yet to earn a place in our backyard gardening.

This is not a true 50 foot garden hose. It only expands to 50 feet when it is filled with water and under pressure. So if you have it attached to a sprinkler or something else it may have the inclination to retract it self. It seems to work better and it stretches easier than the 75 foot one.It also isn't good for things such as draining tanks because it relies on a fairly heavy water pressure to operate. I tried to use it to drain the expansion tank on my coal boiler and it would not work because the water pressure was not nigh enough.Pros: it is light. It also does not take up a lot of space. Very good for people who have limited room to store a hose. Would be good on a boat or camper.

UPDATED REVIEW: 9/29/13The hose popped in the center!!  What do they make these hoses out of these days!!!  The reason why I chose this one was because all the other hoses we had also popped.  They don't make hoses like they used to.  We took care of this hose to great lengths.  We would drain the hose and never leave water in it when we were done.  We'd disconnect from the faucet and put it away after each use.  It still popped!!!  You can read my original review when I got this hose, but now that it is of no use, I'm altering my review.ORIGINAL REVIEW:I was so frustrated that we bought a standard hose and then one day, it just popped and water sprayed out of the hose.  We had been looking to buy a replacement, but hoses are expensive and the one we had was the second hose we bought.Then came the Rumford Gardener Expanding Hose.  I'm glad I held off buying the standard hose.  I like this expanding hose for the following reasons:A) Very lightweightB) No need for a hose box you have to wind up to put the hose awayC) Comes with a carrying/storage caseD) Expands as the water runs throughE) Comes with a fitting to allow you to shut the water off at the end of the hose to change fittingsWhat I thought could've been better is:1) Water pressure was not as forceful as with the standard hose.  I think this is due to it's size2) Plastic fittings instead of metal3) Would not be easy to replace the fittings4) End that connects to the water faucet is hard to grab in order to tighten.  Water was coming out and I had to tighten moreOverall, it may be a bit more than a traditional hose, but I like the weight and ease of storage.  When it is time to replace my other hose, I will consider replacing it with an expansion hose.

I think we can all agree that this is a very cool concept.  This hose is very capable, very light, very portable - it's just about perfect in the whole concept department.  The only problem is that it has no lasting power.  The fittings are all in plastic and hardly durable.  The hose itself can't be left out in the sun - the sun will break it down.  Then it's not even durable because even when you are super careful with it, it can still develop leaks.  The outer covering is a strange, crunchy material that fades in the sun - none of it seems up to par for durability.  I think this is useful maybe for times when you need a portable hose - this has to be the most portable hose around...but you can't rely on it, so I'm not sure if the convenience of the portability is worth not knowing if it will last for you and when it will break for no reason at all.  I cannot recommend this item.
summary: Very cool concept, Very poor quality/execution

reviewText: I just spent a couple hours playing with this washer.  I cleaned two cars (water only), sidewalk/driveway, house siding/gutters, and a very moldy outdoor wood railing.I've never had a pressure washer before, so wasn't exactly sure what to expect.  I thought it would be a bit more powerful.  It's not terribly underpowered, but I thought it would be more.Cleaning cars:  This is the main reason I bought the washer for.  I had a ton of really baked on bugs on two cars, I thought it would be a good test.  I used the 25deg head for this.  The first car I soaked with water and let sit for a while to loosen the bugs a bit.  From about 12" away I got about 50% of them off, at about 4" away I got another 30% off, and at 1" I got another 15% or so, leaving a very stubborn 5% left which I had to break down and use a textured sponge to remove.  Not too bad I guess.  This was on the whole front end obviously, windshield, bumper, and hood.  I found some tar in a few places and was able to remove the majority of it, but I think a sponge and some solvent would be needed to do a proper job.  The second car I manually sprayed on a strong bug remover chemical and let sit for 30sec, then sprayed with the washer.  This time I used the 15deg head and I was able to get nearly all of the bugs off with the washer.  I just had a few places where I used the sponge.  Not bad.  I have newer cars and the paint is intact and strong.  I might not be so inclined to get so close with older cars/paint.  I could see it getting under a chip or bubble in the paint and removing a bunch of it.  I've ordered a foam cannon attachment to soap the cars properly, seems like I'll still need to use that sponge quite a bit as the washer doesn't get the fine dirt on the paint, even at close range.  I feel a bit neutral about the unit for cars, I was hoping for it to work better.Cement sidewalk/driveway:  I live where there is a lot of moisture around and my sidewalks and driveway turn black every year.  I was spraying watered down bleach to get rid of it but that is not very environmentally friendly, and some of my plants would die!  I didn't really buy the pressure washer for this but since it's a popular thing to use it for I gave it a shot.  I used the 15deg head and had to be about 2-4" from the cement to fully clean it.  This means cleaning a 2" strip at a time, it takes a while to do a large area!  I was very surprised how well it cleaned cement, very nice!  I'm more excited to use it for this than washing cars.House siding/gutters/wood railing:  My house has an aged latex stain on it.  The paint is very easy to remove with pressure, so I had to be careful.  I used the 15deg head but really should have had a wider one on.  I just moved back 3-4 feet or so when cleaning the siding so as not to damage the paint.  I think I'll stick to the joe-max/bleach for this task in the future due to my sensitive paint.  My plastic gutters where terribly moldy!  I got 2-4" from them and it cleaned pretty well.  If I was super anal I could have used a brush to get every last bit, but the washer did a decent job.  I have a raw cedar wood railing on my porch which is extremely moldy!  I had to get within 1" and use a few passes to clean it fully, but the wood looks new now!  Quite amazingQuality:  The build quality of the unit seems ok.  It feels/sounds kind of cheap.  Some of the parts fit loose and it sounds like it's really working hard when in use... reminds me of what a vacuum sounds like when it binds on a rug end or string.  My unit seems to have a variable output, at times it backs off the pressure for no apparent reason.  Sometimes it doing more of a pulsing type thing and other times it's more continuous.  It also acts very funny if you release the trigger and press it again before it has stopped moving... it fails to start back up properly and you have to stop and wait a few seconds then start again.  Strange!Leaks:  I was careful to check for leaks after reading all the reviews about them.  At first there was a slight leak where the hose adapter (for connecting your garden hose) connects to the unit itself, this seems to be common.  It's very hard to hand tighten due to the tight space.  The screw part also comes to a sudden tight spot so you don't get the feeling it's really going to hold.  For my first round of cleaning it was fine being hand tight.  However, some side pressure was applied to the garden hose and therefore the adapter it started leaking a lot!  I tried to hand tighten again, but it wouldn't be.  Now understood the frustration people had.  I used some channel locks to get it a little more snug, but it was leaking worse.  I've seen this before, the rubber o-ring gets bunched up and fails to seal.  The supplied o-ring is not very wide and I suspect it's not sealing the landing surfaces correctly.  I put in my own rubber o-ring which was 50% wider than the supplied one and it worked as I had supposed.  Pretty simple fix.Quick disconnect.  I decided to get one of these to make connecting the garden hose easier.  I stumbled upon Gardena connectors.  Wow, super cool.  They're just plastic but work awesome, highly recommend, they are worth the price.Overall I'm pretty happy with the washer, it's not exactly what I was hoping for, but I can definitely make use of it in a few different ways.  I'm happy with the purchase.

My dad and I have been using gas pressure washers for 20+ years. Craftsman Briggs/Stratton Honda etc...they were all great and served their purpose well. I bought this for my dad for Christmas this past year and also put it together for him. He has now used it for a month and is in love with it. He wakes up early an can now wash his cars without bothering anyone. The unit is well built (based on my first-hand knowledge putting it together; it does have some plastic parts, but as long as you don't leave it outside in the sun for years I do not foresee any issues). It is very compact, meaning it has a much smaller footprint that all of my gas ones and is much easier to operate. No heat generated from the unit, so cant burn your leg or hose on the heat shield or block. I have a 7.5hp gas PW now, and once it craps out I will be buying this unit as well. Will update if and issues arise...GREAT value also, needed to mention that

For being electric it has good power. Enough to take a little paint off. I put it close to wash a piece of tar off and it took it off allright and the paint with it. Seems to leak a bit where the garden hose connects, but I can live with that, or probably try to find a brass connector and replace it..

New upgrades make this an even better purchase. The Pressure Washer now comes with a very comprehensive manual with very clear directions and drawings to help you through the assembly. The company also has added a video on You Tube which takes you through the assembly and also is excellent. See the link below. Also purchased a brass fitting which attached to the machine which does NOT require a quick connect fitting as most are suggesting here. One end of the female to female fitting attaches to the machine and the other can be quickly attached to your hose end.  You can purchase this on Amazon - Gilmour 7FPS7FH Double Female Swivel Brass Connector, 3/4-Inch by 3/4-Inch.SPX3000 - Sun Joe 2030-PSI Electric Pressure Washer - Let's Open the Box - How to Assemble and Start -https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wucog5E5eDE

Snow Joe has a two year warranty.  You can put car wash in one tank and another cleaner in the other tank and switch easily between the two with simply turning the switch.  It is easy to change heads they just pop out and snap back in.  I put a quick disconnect with a water shutoff on between the unit and the hose.  I remove it every time I move the unit and do not have to shut off the water and the hose does not put pressure on the connection.  After reading all the reviews I used a Claber 8983 that is plastic instead of metal and it works best. reviewText: Good quality hose connector.  Many hose connectors seem to need Teflon tape to keep from leaking.  This one was machined well enough that it connected leak-free to my hose bib without any need for tape, as did the hoses I attached to it.  It came with "instructions" and follow-up emails - on the one hand excessive, but on the other reflective of a company invested in its product.  Certainly skip the plastic ones from Orbit.  The couple of dollars you'll save initially will quickly evaporate when you realize they don't hold up, and in many cases aren't very good from the outset.  (My recommendation in using any brass faucet connector is to first try it without Teflon tape rather than putting it on automatically.  Brass is a soft metal and the threads are vulnerable to distortion, so use tape only if you need it).
I hooked this up easily. There's good water flow and no leaks, and the two shutoff levers give you control over where the water is directed. No problems.

Well crafted and made out of solid brass, except for the plastic levers to turn the valves and the part you screw onto your faucet.  This second piece covers the brass and actually makes it easier to grip and turn.  There are no leaks whatsoever.  The plastic levers directing the flow are sturdy and easy to turn also.  Four star because the opening valves that control the water flow in each arm are smaller than seems appropriate and end up restricting water coming out of each arm.
summary: Very handy connector for multi tasking water distribution in your garden

reviewText: Okay, I just love this! Is has allowed me to have two hoses on one faucet, so I don't have to attach and then detach hoses one after the other, depending on my needs.This unit is very high quality and you cannot go wrong. I really am impressed, and will be replacing a couple more with these around my place.Now I have 2 hoses on one faucet and it is grand.A couple months ago, the water company came over to tell me that I have a water leak, we looked all over and the water link was just from a hose that was dripping a drop at a time. I could not believe that little drip could have caused so much water leaking out (and a very large bill). This faucet, with the plastic unit connect levers have solved my problem. When you finish using the hose, just make sure the plastic lever is in the "off" position. Now I have no more leaks and I am very happy. Try it, it works.
summary: Very good, well made double faucet...

reviewText: I had a plastic 2-way hose connector on our back water tap last year.  No surprise that it broke.  Green Thumb was great in sending me detailed instructions on how to loosen up the levers using WD40.  It was worth the time to read those instructions so I recommend you do the same if you order this item.  It is strongly made and I anticipate getting more than one season out of it!  If I don't I will be back to change my rating.  But right now, I am one happy camper!  Great item!

I have trouble finding products made in the USA, as everything is either made in China or elsewhere and the materials just don't add up. I only hope this 2-Way Connector meets the bill. It looks good and I have put in service, so we will see how this product works. I got great service from Amazon and in fact, anything I order from them is great and the service is superb. Thanks much for all the good things you supply. JB
summary: Looks great and is well mad for a China product.

reviewText: I was having to remove my hose to putting something else on so I finally decided to get a 2-way connector. All the connectors on Amazon seemed to have a few negative reviews; I decided on this one as the best of the lot because it was all brass. By that I mean the main body, the switches and ring are still plastic, as opposed to some which are all plastic.The vendor seems to be very concerned at my experience because after I bought it, he sent me an e-mail plus directions to a website with a video on how to use it.I got it within a few days by mail. It is pretty hefty and sturdy. The switches were initially quite stiff but I added a drop of oil (as per instructions) and they loosened up. Once installed all the connections fit well and does not leak. So far so good. But the complaints are of the connector failing in time, so if it fails at any time, I'll be sure to come back and update this.
Unable to use this. Gave it 4 stars to be nice. One thing that IS p!ss!ng me off is that I've now received my 3rd review reminder. These maggots are relentless!

I don't really go through a lot of nozzles, but I have grown tired of the lower quality ones that I get at the hardware stores.  After taking a step backwards while washing the car and snapping the handle off of one that I liked (probably cost ~$15) because it was just plastic, I started looking around and found these.They sure look sturdy in the pictures, but my concern was functionality.  I'm used to the nozzles that swivel and let you choose between various types of sprays (full, shower, jet, and so forth).  Plus, I'm used to nozzles with pull handles.  So, I was nervous that I wouldn't like them, but I took a gamble - and won!  I'm writing this review to say that the various types of sprays available are pretty decent just from a rotating nozzle.  You can do a pretty gentle wide spray, to a more powerful wide spray, to an ever increasingly concentrated jet.  The outer cylinder turns so easily and quickly that you really don't have to worry too much about spraying everything down as you turn it closed and pass through the wide spray setting.  Plus, the water pressure is outstanding.  Granted, that depends on your supply, but it sure seems like these nozzles flow a lot more water than my other nozzles did.I put one of these on both of the hoses (front and back yards), and I find that I go out to water just to use them.  True, the plants do need the water :D, but I just like using them.  They have such a great feel to them.Quality-wise, they're very good.  One of them had some surface marks on the outside cylinder, but seeing as how my yards are mostly rock, I knew they'd get scratched up pretty quick anyway.  The extra washers are a nice touch, but those are pretty inexpensive at the hardware store - I wish that they would have put in some spare o-rings instead.  Not a gripe, mind you, as I think it was pretty cool that they put in spares of anything.So, while pretty darn expensive (they were over $44/pair when I ordered), I'm really happy with them - highly recommended.
summary: Awesome nozzles - they make watering fun!

reviewText: I am really tired of plastic hose attachments that crack, break and leak. This brass nozzle is the solution to those problems. Avoiding frustration and aggravation enhances my pleasure in outdoor projects and gardening. These nozzles are a bargain for the outdoor enthusiast.

I've been in this house for 40 years, and in that time, I must have bought a dozen nozzles. I have them on stems with 5 different sprays. I have just the grip with 6 different sprays. Every single one of them broke, I suppose because of plastic parts. Finally, I decided to go back to a brass nozzle from my childhood, a time when there was ONE nozzle.Well, this is it. It's perfect and goes from a forced stream to clean the patio to a gentle spray for watering flowers. I should have done this years ago. Couldn't be happier.
summary: Back to Basics: All Sprays in One Brass Nozzle

reviewText: Works great. After buying a new spray nozzle each year I splurged and bought this set.  Has a really nice heavy feel too.

Amazing item made in the U.S.A. I have this hooked up and it does what it supposed to do. It waters my yard and I foresee many good years of usage as compared to the gun type sprayer that eventually breaks down and need replacement. This is why I bought this sprayer.The company even sent me an email on how to take care of this sprayer. This company cares about there products.
Ill be honest.. I bought these and I would do it again. Yes it is a little more money but these JUST WORK. They are beautiful and give you lots of pressure.Just. Buy. It.
No need to go on and on.  Simply stated, these are the best you can buy.  They are finely machined and the fittings ensure smooth adjustment.
These are first ever nozzles that I have had that "do not" leak.  I highly recommend them.  I use mine for hosing down a couple of patio covers.  My other nozzle always gave me a bath.

Unit is nearly identical to Dramm 12380 which I have for a long time. Seem to be from the same OEM. The knurl on World's Best is tiny bit more aggressive, easier to turn but most people would not notice the difference. See picture for reference.Its also came with extra washers(made in usa) which will useful, as washer will wore out in couple year. Make this unit a even better value.2 pieces solid brass design with o-ring should last a life time, once a while should open the nozzle to clean out the water corrosion. We got very bad hard water in Southern CA. I got about 7-8 different type of nozzles, I left them outside, most material won't last only brass can take a beating.Fast communication from seller, and good service, I have no worry buying more made in usa product from small business.

I finally starting shopping for an quality injector after going through so many crummy ones.  In addition to the usual Texas BBQ use most weekends, I cook whole pigs a couple of times a year so I needed a good injector this time because after one 50 - 60 pounder it's usually time to throw away the injector I used because the needle broke, the seal broke or both.I used this injector on a 75 pound pig a couple of weeks ago and it is still like new! This thing is solid! The big plus with the Epica is that is cost less than comparable ones but I really can't see another one being built better than this one is.  I big "would buy again".

This kitchen device looks like something out ofLittle Shop of Horrors, but it's actually a fantastic way to inject flavors and moisture into large cuts of meat.This comes with two large needles (6" long).  One needle is solid with a hole in the angled tip (just like a syringe) and one with a series of holes throughout.  You insert the needle into the meat and then press the plunger down as you slowly withdraw the needle.  To fully infuse the meat, you need to inject it over and over, from different angles.  It really is a great way to make an incredibly moist turkey or chicken.  It's also an easy way to get marinades under the skin of the bird if you like to season your poultry that way.  Just be careful not to inject it too many times, because you'll damage the meat.The injector comes apart and is pretty simple to clean.  If your needles are clogged with chunks of seasoning (herbs, garlic, etc.), then just fill the body of the injector with warm soapy water and squirt it through the needle until it's clean.Remember that the #1 most important factor in retaining the juices in your meat is to let it rest after you cook.  Letting the meat rest for at least ten minutes lets the muscle fibers in the meat relax, and the juices are soaked up from the cells in between the fibers back into the fibers themselves.  With the juices soaked back in, the juices stay in the meat after you cut it.  Otherwise, the free juices in between will just spill out when you cut it.If you love to cook, try something different and give this injector a try.I was provided this item for review.

This is one solid marinate and seasoning injector I can definitely live with.  For one thing it's stainless steel, easy to clean, and won't absorb any odors or flavors of any previous ingredients used.  It's very well-designed and easy to handle with the 3-ring handle and, unlike its plastic counterparts, will last for a long time.  Once you are through using it, it will come apart totally for cleaning.  Simply unscrew the top beneath the two rings and then pull the plunger out.PROS:~  Easy clean~  Holds up to 2 ounces of marinate or seasoning~  There are markings on the flat side of the plunger you can use to gauge your liquid from 1/2 ounce to the full 2 ounces~  Stainless steel, a solid material that will hold up for years~  Designed to use high pressure to inject your meats~  The package includes two needles, one for liquid marinade, the other for chopped solids such as garlic and onionCON:~  It's so solid, it's a bit difficult to press down the plunger.  You'll need to use one hand to balance the body of the injector and the other to use the plunger.I do love this seasoning injector, partially because I love kitchen gadgets, but mostly because it's of very good quality like some of my old-time collectibles.  The body of the injector and needles are definitely stainless, but the top appears to be a composite.  No problem if after you wash it you let it dry thoroughly before reassembling so it won't start to flake off in the interior.  All in all, this is a great little seasoning injector that should last for years.  The feature I especially like is the fact that there is the second needle that will accommodate solids such as chopped garlic in olive oil, something that's especially nice when seasoning a pork roast.Sample provided for review.
summary: This is a nice multi-use marinate and seasoning injector ...

reviewText: It is a goodly size.  Well made.  The 2 needles (included) allow one to approach seasoning in 2 different ways.  One needle is full of holes down the sides.  After you have inserted the needle FULLY and press down, a liquid flavpring will come out of the holes and distribute the goods all along the length.  (Comic aside - if you do not get the needle far enough into the meat, you will take an aromatic bath when you press the plunger.  I know - I oopsed.)  The other needle is open at the end and allows you to shoot smushed flavorings of a more solid nature into the heart of the meat.  (Think pulverized garlic, oil, sage, salt and peppers deep into pockets of a big piece of pig.)About the 3 rings.  The one in the center gives you a good soild hold when you need to retract the plunger.  Greasy fingers will not hinder your hold.  In the same way, the 2 on the sides give you a great grip when you push to force your goodies into the meat.Plastic would not do so good a job.  If you like Q - low and slow and juicy - you'll want this.  Yes, you will.

this thing is of high quality. I use it to inject chicken wings. Haven't used the needle with multiple holes but the other one is sharp and pierces through meat no problem. Just keep an eye on the little o-rings on the threaded part of the needle they temp to fall off.

This marinade injector from Epica is made of stainless steel, which I much prefer over a plastic syringe.  It's also very heavy-duty and weighs about eleven ounces with the needles.  It has a comfortable triple ring handle for accurate and easy injection and aspiration and holds a full 2 oz. of marinade.There are two needles, one with a larger bore and a single large end opening that is about 5 in. long and one with nine peripheral openings at about 5 1/2 in. long.  Both have knurled grips and silicone gaskets to prevent leaks under high pressure.  To clean, just immerse in hot soapy water.If you have never used a marinade syringe, you will be surprised at what a difference it makes in both flavor and moistness, especially for grilling and smoking outdoors.  There are simple instructions and tips included on a reference card.  Use the search term "injection recipe" to find wonderful flavor combinations for marinades. Any recipe with butter will be remarkable and it's fun to experiment with wine-based marinades and even plain beer for chicken.This injector can also be used to make spiked watermelons for summer parties—but please don't say I said so!A sample was provided for unbiased review.

It came with two kinds of tips.  One with the hole on the tip and the other doesn't have a hole on the tip but has three holes around the tube.  Don't use the later for marinades with bigger chunks like garlic or herbs, it won't fit on the smaller holes.  Both have pretty shart tips so it goes easily through the meat.My wife loves to use it for poultry and pork.  It produces much better tasting dishes especially for baked chickens and pork loins.  She uses mainly butter and garlic.  If you want to use different kind of herbs, it is better to grind them very fine first using a food processor.It is made of stainless steel.  Sturdier than most injectors that is made of plastic.  It is much easier to push in because the needle feels very solid. The finger holes are very comfortable.  You can really apply pressure  to push the marinade.  It is not too tight, it works very smoothly.  A great tool for anybody who loves to cook.  Dishwasher safe.Sample item provided by the distributor for evaluation review.

This is pretty neat. In full sunlight (this is late November, so the sun is still weak) it charges my Galaxy SIII about 18% / hour.Five hours in full sunlight to charge my phone isn't great -- but then again, this is SOLAR power. Taking that into account... and considering that this only has the surface area of a couple sheets of notebook paper, it's really impressive. I was not expecting this kind of performance from a tiny little solar cell.This unit comes in a nice canvas binding, sorta like an old-school trapper keeper. Its two solar cells fold together and are held in place by a magnetized tab. The backside has a mesh zipper pocket which contains the charging ports, including a USB and a 12V DC.This unit has a bunch of loops which can be used to secure it to your backpack, or dashboard, or boat console, etc. for security. It can also be used inside a bag or other transparent sealed container -- perfect for aquatic situations.I'm most excited about being able to combine this with theGoal Zero 21004 Switch 8 Silver Solar Recharger, which I'll be reviewing soon, for better charging.I own, have reviewed, and regularly use rechargeable battery packs and those are cool for recharging your devices on the go. But, if you're going to be camping or kayaking or whatever for several days, those will eventually run out of juice also. The idea of having an unlimited (if somewhat slow) power source at hand is really neat.BOTTOM LINE: it's not as fast as a wall AC or car DC charger, but this little package is pretty impressive. I can get a full charge on my SIII phone in 4-5 hours in the winter sun. I imagine it'd be faster in summer months with the sun at a much more favorable angle in the sky. If you are going to be spending multiple days 'off the grid' but still would like a reliable power source to charge your phone, camera, etc... this is a great product. I'm very impressed at the performance and rugged construction and can see myself using this for years to come. 5 stars.
summary: Small, rugged, and surprisingly powerful solar charger

reviewText: This Goal Zero "Nomad 7 v2" is perfect for gadget heavy campers! I have used solar chargers for quite awhile, and this one covers all of the charging needs we have.What's Included:* Nomad 7 Solar Panel; has USB output and can charge the Guide 10 Battery Pack (not included) or power devices directly* Ultra Charge Solar Cord* 12V cigarette adapter; used to power device with Car Accessory plugs* Manuals & Warranty+ Quality; these are well made components that will hold up while camping or hiking+ Power When You Need It; can charge directly from the Solar Panels or from the Battery Pack+ Powerful; tested both on a power hungry HTC EVO 4G, Kindle Fire, and iPhone 5+ Portable; the solar panels connect nicely to a backpack for use on the go+ Convenience; everything fits nicely into the mesh storage section of the Nomad 7Overall, I am very impressed with this solar charger!Highly Recommended!CFH
summary: Very good Solar Panel - Highly Recommended

reviewText: Spent a week without power in North Carolina during an ice storm and my son spent about two days without power during Nemo in Boston.In both cases we were able to say warm with gas heat but had no way to charge a cell phone or lap top for communication or keeping up with the status of the storm.My son has the Nomad in Boston now.  It works great on sunny days but the sun is noticeably absent during snow storms.  As others noted, it requires direct sunlight to charge.  On the other hand, they often go camping and this device is easily portable and keeps their phones charged.
summary: Great for Camping - Not So Useful During Snow Storms

reviewText: Note: I got this solar panel as an ADDITION to the Guide 10 plus recharging kit, which comes with one another Nomad 7 solar panel. My review will be based on how this product performs when paired with the Guide 10 Plus solar charging kit. For my full review of that solar charging kit, see that product's page.Pros:-The size profile makes it very easy to pack. You will always be able to find room in your backpack to shove this in. It uses built-in rare earth magnets to keep the panel closed when it's folded up.-Adding this solar panel (in a daisy-chain configuration) to another Nomad 7 panel will provide LOTS of juice! I was able to charge my Samsung Note 3 using ONLY the 2 solar panels (without a battery pack), while facing the panels towards the sun from indoors behind a glass window, in the same amount of time as my normal wall charger.-Each panel is 7 watts, making the total 14 watts if you use 2 of them. You lose some efficiency when you don't have perfect conditions (noon sun in the summer on a cloudless day), but with 2 panels you should still be able to easily get roughly 2 amps of power at 5v, the same amount as a standard iPad USB charger.-As you can see in the pictures, it has parachute cord loops all around the panel. I suggest carrying a few small carabiners so you can hang the panels from your backpack/tent/tree/whatever.-Very well made! You can see that the engineers put a lot of thought into form and function. I can tell this solar panel will survive years of use and abuse.Cons:-As a standalone solar panel, and without a rechargeable battery pack, you will probably find that this solar panel doesn't charge your device very well. Goal Zero recommends that you use rechargeable batteries (not included with this solar panel) as a "buffer" between the solar panel and your device, so that your device receives a consistent charge no matter what the environmental conditions are. Without a "battery buffer", your device will likely toggle between charging and not charging frequently.-Weight. This might be a concern for backpackers like myself. The solar panel by itself, without the extra cables, weighed 17oz on my scale. On short journeys, it would probably be more efficient just to carry spare batteries.-The cord that connects 1 panel to another panel is too short in my opinion - the panels have to be pretty much touching one another, you won't be able to space them apart. You could possibly go to Radioshack and make some extension cables, but the existing cable is built-in and not easily replaced.Overall impression:I would not recommend using this solar panel as a standalone power system, and it is probably too heavy to be worth carrying on short outings. So why the 5 stars? When paired with a battery charger (and especially when paired with a second solar panel, both included in the Guide 10 Plus kit), this becomes a serious power solution for long trips where carrying loads of disposable batteries isn't a good answer.
summary: Recommend pairing with battery pack and/or 2nd solar panel

reviewText: We live in an area that loses power frequently, and when there's a big storm we can lose power for days at a time, so we have quite a collection of solar lanterns and chargers.  This Goal Zero Nomad 7 has become one of my instant favorites.  The craftsmanship and attention to detail are excellent.  The case has nine hanging loops, which provides a lot of options if you're using it while camping, and the case seals with a magnetic closure, which I find more convenient and less bulky than velcro.The Nomad 7 has two standard panels, each about the size of a half sheet of notebook paper, so it's about the size of a pad of paper fully opened.  It has three different outputs on the back:  A USB port, a dedicated cable to feed into a Guide 10 battery charger, and a 12v DC female socket (i.e., a "cigarette lighter" socket like in your car).  The 12v DC out is not included on any of my other portable solar panels -- it's a nice addition.  The panel also has an input to chain it to other Nomads.  The output/input connections are all in a single block, which is covered by a zippered mesh pouch on the back of the panel so you can keep all of your charging cables neatly stored with the panel.  The port labels are printed right on the case so you can't lose them -- a handy and smart detail.The Nomad 7 can charge some devices (like my phone) directly, but it won't charge my iPad directly.  To charge an iPad, you need to use the Nomad 7 to charge a battery pack (Goal Zero recommends the Guide 10 battery charger; I use an Anker 5V/2A external battery, which doesn't have removable batteries but is smaller and works great), then dump the charge from the external battery pack to your iPad.  This isn't just because the Nomad 7 doesn't pump out enough power, it's also because the iPad doesn't like power that fades in and out, which happens frequently as clouds cross the sun.  My Instapark 10w solar panel also needs an intermediate battery to charge my iPad reliably, even though the 10w panel is sufficient to charge the iPad directly on a completely clear, sunny day when the panel output doesn't fluctuate.Because it has two panels instead of three, the Nomad 7 is a bit smaller and lighter than the Instapark, and the 7w output seems to charge up an external battery pack very quickly.  During outages around the house, I'll use both, but for camping I would probably take the Nomad 7, both because it's a bit smaller/lighter and also because the build quality seems top notch.
summary: Excellent Quality Solar Panel for Mobile Devices ... Will Also Need a Battery

reviewText: Because I live in earthquake country, I love owning this GOAL ZERO NOMAD 7 ULTRA-LIGHT SOLAR PANEL.  I hope that I'll never REALLY need to use it, but it's a wonderful addition to my emergency-preparedness equipment and supplies.  When unfolded and placed on a window ledge with the solar panels facing bright sunlight, it charges my Android smartphone quickly (adding a 15% charge in about 30 minutes).The NOMAD 7 is very light in weight, and is suitable for backpacking.  The device does NOT store a charge--the panels must be unfolded and exposed to sunlight for it to operate to charge any device.  How fast it charges depends in part on how much sunlight is reaching the panels.  It works best in direct sunlight, but it also worked for me on partly cloudy days.The built-in power port has connectors for charging 12V devices (Sherpa and others) and USB devices (cellphones and others).  You will need to supply the USB cables to connect your USB devices.The literature says that the panel will charge cellphones,  iPods, and tablets.  It works well with my Android smartphone; however, an iPod Touch (4th gen) delivered a message that the solar panel was incompatible, and my Kindle Paperwhite (2nd gen) repeatedly froze after beginning to charge (requiring a full reboot to be operational again after each attempt).  So I would recommend using the NOMAD 7 with care (stay with the newly connected device) until you find out which of your devices are completely compatible.  But it's still a great piece of equipment to have on hand for charging cellphones in emergency situations.
summary: Valuable Addition to Earthquake Preparedness Kit

reviewText: Here in North Texas, we've recently had a significant power outage from a ferocious ice storm, and it would have been helpful to use this solar charger to recharge both phone and iPod.  Earlier in the week, I used it to recharge my cell phone; however when you're hit with an ice storm, you are most likely not in a sunny day, so you're out of luck for recharging using solar power.What I found when I successfully recharged my phone is that I need to be patient.  Recharging is somewhat slower than recharging using the house power.  In addition, I discovered that I could not use this recharger to charge my iPad.Lesson Learned:  When you're informed that a storm is on the way, use this to completely charge your cell phone before the storm hits and while you still have sunshine.  Put two in a chain to have enough power to recharge an iPad, or just use the power in your house or apartment.
summary: Handy Charging Before the Storm Hits

reviewText: This Goal Zero 11800 Nomad 7 Solar Charger is a well put together solar charger that charged my iPhone in about 3.5 hours in winter sunlight.  I think it will probably go much faster in the spring and summer when the sun is more direct and intense. This device is compact with two solar panels which together are about the size of a sheet of notebook paper. It has t has three outputs on the back of the unit. There is a USB port, a dedicated cable to feed into a Guide 10 battery charger, and a 12v DC "cigarette lighter" type socket like the type you'll find in a car.  The ports are on the back of the panel and there is a mash zippered pouch back there to hold the connectors and device you're charging. It also has several loops for hanging it or fastening it to a tent or backpack or in the car where it will get sunlight.This is an excellent solar charger to take along with camping or backpacking because of it's convenient size and low weight. It is also weather resistant and pretty rugged looking. It would also be a good addition to an emergency kit for use when the power goes out. As long as there is sun you would be able to charge a phone or other small device that can be charged with a USB plug. It can be paired with other Nomad devices or used to charge an external battery pack.
summary: High quality solar charger for smartphones and more

reviewText: After opening the box, I was looking for the manual.  Turns out that the small pamphlet inside is actually the manual -- that's how easy it is to use this device.You can often tell a quality device by the small things.  In this case, I noticed instantly that the zippers to the pocket that holds the cables run smooth and have a nice extender to grab.  The panels come in a small folder about the size of a computer tablet (e.g., iPad) and everything you need is all in the folder including the cables.  There is a nice strong magnet that prevents the tablet from opening on its own.Below are the results from my little test.  I took a smart phone and ran down the battery to 54%.  I then connected it to the charger and angled the panels at the sun.2:04pm - 54% (start)2:38pm - 78%3:28pm - 98%The device was probably near 100% around 3pm to be honest but I forgot to check sooner.  After the test, I decided to place the device in the shade while still connected to the phone out of curiosity.  After 30+ minutes, the device was at 90% so I am not sure if the panels drain the device if connected during long periods of shade or if my phone was acting up.Note the panels have a plastic film over them when shipped that you peel off -- and that is a good thing.  However, I was surprised to see a lot of scuff marks on the panel after I pulled the protector sheets off but thankfully the scratches didn't seem to impact performance.Overall, this panel lives up to the claims.  It's made with high quality and is super easy to use.
summary: Solar Recharger all in a Mini Folder

reviewText: The outputs are a 5v USB, which you will need to provide your own cable forA 12v to charge devices that are usually charged by the 12v output of a vehicle (car/truck/etc)and a Guide 10 output that can be used to charge the Guide 10 Plus Recharger which you would need to buy separately.From what I can tell from the product information on Amazon and on the Goal Zero website, you might be able to charge  the Goal Zero Switch 8 from the Guide 10 output, but I am not 100% sure about the Zero Switch 8 as I did not have that device on hand to test.The charging times for devices that you can charge from this are extremely optimistic, as predicted by the manufacturer's estimates, as they give a shorter time to recharge using this as compared to a consistent charge from a USB port. Realistically it would be extremely difficult in most situations to obtain maximum charging power from using the Nomad 7 since it was frequently difficult to get full sun even in Texas over the last couple of months.To gain full use of this solar panel, you would really need to buy either or both of the charge packs that work with this.It can charge the Rock Out 2 Rechargeable Speaker and the Lighthouse 250 Lantern, but for non Goal Zero devices you really need to be sure that they are compatible with 5v. The highest voltage cell phone that my extended household owns takes a 2 volt input, so you would need to have the Lighthouse or the Guide 10 plus the Goal Zero USB Smart Adapter to charge the average cell phone.My recommendation, take it with a very large grain of salt, realize that without accessories you might not get as much use out of this panel as you might think from reading the product blurbs.

With 7-10 day backpacking trips, finding options for powering my cell phone which doesn't work where I go, but can still be used for GPS navigation), is more and more difficult. I have resorted lately to bringing along 4 or 5 flash batteries, which helps, but adds for additional clutter and weight in my pack, and are just more items that must be stored in waterproof containers. The Nomad 7 is an interesting idea for resolving this problem. I tried it out over a 2 day trip, by strapping it to the outside of my pack so it would be in direct sunlight while I hiked. It did not work out as well as I thought it might, since I was under tree canopy during most of my hikes, but once I reached a campsite I was able to get a few hours worth of charge in direct sunlight. At 1 lb, it isw a bit heavier than I would like, but probably worth the extra weight in my pack for what it can provide. Actual charguing worked fairly well. I thought 7 watts would be inefficient to provide any real charging, but as long as I made sure it received several hours of sunlight, that was enough to give me a decent charge on my cell phone to keep it going through the day, and ensure that I could use the Nomad on extended hikes in the future without having to bring along a bunch of extra batteries. The Nomad 7 is fairly rugged and I didn't have to worry too much about damaging it while strapped to my pack. I'll definitely use it again for future hikes.

compact and convenient, this lightweight solar panel can handily assist you with lightweight charging needs and can even run a few accessories without an attached battery(for example, i use mine with a lightweight fan for a cooling breeze while sitting on the beach; any USB-based fan or an 'O2Cool' fan [found in local drugstores or box-marts] will do)i have to credit w/goal zero; there is at last a clear, concise and comprehensive online product guide to help a solar newbie with making proper choices for one's panel and accessory needs - BUT, simply clicking on the accessories page will not help you decide on what to buy for your panel - and more pertinent to this product, there is no clear and concise information to show what you need in order to or what you need to 'chain' several of these smaller panels together (i make my own cables to bump up the USB amperage for charging my handheld radio transceivers, or to run small high-frequency transceivers via the solar output port)i like the compact size and versatility of the Nomad 7, but if you have an older version you should know a few things:1. the regulator and ports have been moved to the back of the panel - this is an improvement, as heat from the sun has been a known problem w/the original2. the pouch area is now larger, on the back, and uses a mesh3. all cables are attached, so nothing can be lost, but you will need to construct a female and/or male adapter if you want to do custom cabling4. dimensions of the panel are the samei took off one star for failure of the manufacturer to offer any comprehensive chaining or cabling information for this panel, despite chaining being touted as a feature, and a marked port on the panel itself 'Chain input' - the included instructions state: "Can I chain multiple solar panels together? Yes. Chaining additional solar panels is a great way to charge your device from the sun in less time." - well thanks for that, but there are NO pictures, NO schematics, NO info or name of a required accessory cable to chain this panel - this is a MAJOR omission on the part of goal zero - sorry folks!all in all though, i think you'll be pleased with this product, and if you have an older Nomad, this updated version... if you have the acumen to do your own cables you may be able to chain this panel with your older one - but don't expect to easily find any info from the manufacturer on doing so - get out your volt meter and soldering iron!

reviewerName: Y. R. Wu "The will to win is nothing without ...
reviewText: Summary: If you are going to be off the grid for a good couple of weeks, this might be a good way to keep your devices charged.  Otherwise, I'd seriously consider one of the larger battery packs (see suggestions at the end)I just spent a week in San Diego so I had a chance to see how this performs in decent sun. (even though it's just after the winter solstice)  Although the panel is rated for 7 amps, but this must be full sun with the panel properly aligned.  You're not going to see anywhere near that output except between 10am and 2pm and I certainly never got anywhere near this in practice (Summer or near the equator?  You'll be getting a lot more power).The difficulty is that the loops on the side help you hang this, but there isn't an easy way to position this for optimal sun exposure.  I ended up laying it flat on the table on our balcony.  I was able to charge aNew Trent iCarrier 12000mAh Portable Dual USB Port External Battery Charger/Power Pack for Smartphones, Tablets and more (Now w/Micro-USB charge port)perhaps one bar over the course of two days.  This suggests that it captured perhaps about 1500 mAh eacy day - enough to keep your average smartphone charged up (as long as you didn't use it too much) but not much more.Here's the rub.  My 12000 mAh battery weighs 10 oz and is enough to do a full charge of my phone about 10 times.  If I were off the grid, it would provide enough power for about 20 days assuming I was careful with usage.The Goal Zero weighs 17 oz.  To properly use the solar panel, I'd really recommend some type of battery pack, so you could easily be up to 20 oz.  The advantage of course is that you'd be good indefinitely (assuming you've got some decent sun)Design and fabrication were very nice, though my panel came with plastic protective sheet on both panes with some sort of chemical haze or "bloom" on the epoxy.  I cleaned it off with some polish (Simichrhome) and elbow grease.I've had my New Trent battery pack for about a year and use it regularly on long flights and day hikes, etc.  Anker also has some excellent reviews.  I have a smaller Belkin pack, but it's a lot more dough and as far as I can tell, it hasn't been any more reliable or functional than the New Trent.
summary: Good option if you *really* can't be near an outlet for a while......

reviewText: My Weber grill cover couldn't make it 2 years in the Chicago winter and summer. After reading reviews and taking measurements I ended up going with the large size (the color was the closest matching for my patio).  It doesn't fit like a glove but it isn't too loose (Maybe 1-2" too big length wise). I was worried about the depth not being enough but there isn't an issue there. It hangs about a 1/2 inch off the ground (lower than the Weber cover). Towards the first snow I'll tighten up the bottom strap. It has survived a few normal rain/thunderstorms without blowing off and protected the grill.I'll update my review in the future.[Update April, 2014]The cover survived a harsh cold winter, and more importantly my grill survived.
summary: A replacement for a weber genesis

reviewText: I've owned several grill covers in my lifetime, and none of them quite stacked up to the quality, durability, and design of this one.  Yes, it is heavy weight, which one would expect of a premium grill cover.  But the quality does not stop here.  It is sewn well with stitching that seems to be built to last.  But what really makes this grill cover stand out to me are the unique features that you will not find in most grill covers.  First, the straps that can be secured around each leg of your grill are ingenious.  This means no more improvised inventions to keep the cover on your grill in storms or high winds.  You need not secure the cover on all 4 corners, but even one or two corners will ensure that it's not going anywhere when the wind starts blowing.  The zippered pocket that faces the front is pretty cool.  I am not sure what I will keep in there, but it's a neat feature.  Lastly, though I have seen them on some other covers, too, the sturdy handles for lifting and positioning the grill cover are great.  Again, they seem to be built with longevity in mind.  One quality that is too early to test is whether the cover will fade or discolor in the sun so badly, like other grill covers I have owned.  My only minor complaint is probably my own fault.  I own a Char Broil grill with a griddle on one side of the fire box and a shelf on the other side.  I thought for sure I should get the XL cover, but it actually seems a bit TOO LARGE.  I can live with it, though.  You might want to actually measure your grill, rather than guessing, as I did.

The Ravenna Grill Cover is impressive in its construction and seems a good value for the price. Over the years, I have paid the same amount and more for grill covers with nowhere near the quality of this one. The package states that the main body is 100% woven polyester with laminated polyvinyl chloride backing and a hem casing of 100% polyester.
